events.title: test: gate key injection on the program-entry stop, not a media frame
events.message:
test: gate key injection on the program-entry stop, not a media frame

The readiness signal was the guest's blue start frame, but the media
stream is change-gated and drops a frame that cannot go out whole, so
that one early change can be missed and the gate times out even though
the program ran — it failed on macOS, and flakily on Linux. Use the
session's own signal instead, exactly as debuggerStopsAtProgramEntry and
mediaDisplayFeedsThePanel do: arm the program-entry breakpoint, wait for
that stop, resume, then inject. An entry stop cannot be missed, and
injecting only after it keeps the early presses that make EmuTOS abandon
the autostart (PLAN.md §9) from happening at all.

events.title: release: don't tilde-expand the pre-release separator
events.message:
release: don't tilde-expand the pre-release separator

`PV="${V/-/~}"` expanded the literal "~" in the replacement to $HOME,
so the v0.9.0-alpha tag produced "0.9.0/home/runneralpha": the deb/rpm
version, and the check against it, would have been garbage. Only the
tag-triggered Release runs this, so a green CI run cannot catch it.

Take the tilde from a variable instead: "0.9.0-alpha" -> "0.9.0~alpha",
numeric tags unchanged.

events.title: test: make the media readiness gate and panel compare race-proof
events.message:
test: make the media readiness gate and panel compare race-proof

Follow-ups from the fork's frame path: a frame that cannot go out whole is
dropped ("never queue two"), so comparing the panel to the newest
received frame races a repaint and cannot converge while the guest's
screen keeps changing. Compare only after the stream is quiet — no new
frame for 400 ms — so the panel has caught up.

The key-injection readiness gate now accepts any blue frame, not only the
newest: the guest paints it once and then blocks in Cconin, so a later
non-blue frame must not hide that it was up.

events.title: fix(loader): count LEA abs.L into any An when inferring a raw binary's load address (#739)
events.message:
fix(loader): count LEA abs.L into any An when inferring a raw binary's load address (#739)

InferRawBinaryLoadAddress only counted LEA abs.L,A0 ($41F9) as an absolute
reference.  PlaySFX V1.0 is a headerless BJL image linked at $4000 whose
startup uses LEA abs.L into A1-A7 (library base in A6), so it scored 2 for
$4000 against the minimum of 8 and fell through to the sub-1 MiB headerless
cart fallback.  HLE then took cart+$404 ($00004436, mid-instruction-stream)
as the entry point and the 68K slid through zeroed RAM until its PC left RAM
(pc_escape, final_pc=$200002) by frame 19.  Matching (op & 0xF1FF) == 0x41F9
scores it 14 for $4000 and 0 for the other bases; it now loads at $4000 and
plays its sounds on keypad input.  Across the 155-ROM private corpus this is
the only file whose inferred load address changes.

events.message:
release: order the pre-release package version before the final

Passing the tag version to CPack fixed the deb metadata, but
"0.9.0-alpha" is not a pre-release to Debian or RPM: both read the
hyphen as a package revision, so the alpha would sort *after* a later
"0.9.0" and hide the final release from upgraders. Encode it as
"0.9.0~alpha", which both order first; asset names keep the readable
form. Mark a hyphenated tag a GitHub pre-release too — the release
action does not infer it, so otherwise the alpha becomes "Latest".

events.title: test: wait for the running guest before injecting keys
events.message:
test: wait for the running guest before injecting keys

keyInjectionReachesTheGuest injected scancodes from t=0, while the guest
was still booting. TOS flushes those presses, so the guest reached the
program's Cconin and the test passed; EmuTOS instead abandons the
autostart when a key arrives during boot, so the program never ran and
the test failed on every EmuTOS run — CI's ROM — while passing on real
TOS. It was the only tst_emulatorhost failure in CI.

The program now paints blue before its Cconin, and the test waits for
that frame before injecting: proof the guest is actually running, with
no input during boot to cancel the launch.

events.title: test(disk_control): pitch guard checks alignment; case 5 needs no --disc
events.message:
test(disk_control): pitch guard checks alignment; case 5 needs no --disc

vid_cb() reads rows as uint32_t, so reject a pitch that is not a multiple of 4 and a framebuffer base that is not 4-byte aligned, in addition to pitch < w*4 (unaligned uint32_t loads are UB / SIGBUS on strict-alignment targets). Reword the usage text so --disc is clearly not needed for case 5.

Version 0.4.8: keyboard "as printed" for a US or a UK TOS

The ST's layout depends on the language of the TOS, and the EmuTOS in
the release zip is UK. The single option becomes a choice in
"Controllers & ports" -> "Keyboard": ST keys (positional, default) /
As printed, US TOS / As printed, UK TOS. UK differences (EmuTOS
keyb_uk): " = Shift+2, @ = Shift+', # and ~ on the US \ key, \ and |
on the ISO key. OPTM_SIZE 99 (stcfg 99 bytes), C_MENU_* from 58 on +4.
GHDL keyboard test covers the UK mapping.

events.title: Leap once per side-touch button press; both sides held stand still
events.message:
Leap once per side-touch button press; both sides held stand still

Saul: holding one side and then holding the other leapt over and over.
He wants a press on the other side to leap once, further taps to leap
again, and two holds to stop all movement.

- A button finger now taps fire once when it lands (or when the chord
  window resolves) instead of holding fire until it lifts.  In the air
  the tap waits for the landing read as before.
- Once that tap has been read, the held side stops supplying its
  direction while the button finger stays down; lifting either finger
  walks the side still held.
- Behind the figure, the button tap waits until the turn has been read,
  so the turn and the leap stay separate reads.
- A held button no longer holds fire in the air.  The glide still opens
  from the steering side alone, as fireFree tries it with any sideways.

The off-picture Pointer sidebar keeps its held trigger.

events.title: New option "Keyboard as printed" (issue #6); docs for 0.4.8
events.message:
New option "Keyboard as printed" (issue #6); docs for 0.4.8

Controllers & ports -> "Keyboard as printed": digits and symbols give the
character printed on the MEGA65 key (US ST layout) instead of the ST key
at the same position. keyboard.vhd presses or hides the ST's Shift key
as needed; the symbol key follows 20 ms after a change of the Shift
state, so the IKBD never sees it with the wrong Shift. Extra characters:
Shift+: ; @ * = [ ] { }, Pound = \ |, Shift+- = _, Arrow left = ` ~.

The menu has one more line (OPTM_SIZE 95): C_MENU_* from 57 on shift by
one, /atarist/stcfg must be the new 95 byte file. GHDL keyboard test
checks the mapping and that no symbol key is ever seen with the wrong
Shift state.

README/VERSIONS: 0.4.8 changes (issues #6, #7), stcfg size 95.

events.title: Cold boot after changing the machine type or memory size (issue #7)
events.message:
Cold boot after changing the machine type or memory size (issue #7)

TOS keeps memvalid/memctrl/phystop in RAM and trusts them at the next
reset, so after a change of the machine type or the memory size in the
menu the ST crashed until a TOS was loaded again. tos_loader now watches
these menu bits: on a change it keeps the core in reset, clears the
system variables (like a TOS load from the menu) and lets the ST make a
cold boot. GHDL test: tb_tos_loader -gMEMCHG=true.

events.title: Give the glTF figure's trunk cloth the skin weights of the body beneath it
events.message:
Give the glTF figure's trunk cloth the skin weights of the body beneath it

Stooped, the elder women's wraps showed skin through at the belly: the
cloth kept the code-built weights, measured to the code-built bones, and
the bent chest moved it otherwise than the MakeHuman-weighted skin under
it. Cloth from the hips to below the shoulders now takes the nearest
trunk vertex's weights (arm bones left out, faded over the band's edges);
the hem and the shoulders keep the weights that fold a robe with the legs
and the arms. The clearance test now also skins body and cloth with the
elder's stoop.

events.title: Fade the screen in and out from the power button press
events.message:
Fade the screen in and out from the power button press

The fade no longer waits on the power clips: power-on lifts the dark
screen at the press, and power-off fades the frozen last picture over
200 ms starting at the press.  Speaker.clip() no longer returns the
clip length, since nothing times against it.

CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION came from PROJECT_VERSION, which CMake requires to

the workflow's own metadata check — and the asset name — say

pushed.

Pass the tag-derived version through to CPack. Debian accepts the
pre-release suffix verbatim; CPackRPM rewrites the '-' to '_', the only
form RPM's Version field allows.

events.title: A landing stops on the platform; a hen draws at its own x
events.message:
A landing stops on the platform; a hen draws at its own x

Two alignment fixes carried over from the working repo.

A landing: AirPhysics replays PHYSICS_STEPS Spectrum main-loop iterations for
one GB frame, and on the iteration he lands CheckBelow clears PlayerInAir --
the Z80 takes the ground path from the next iteration on. Replaying the fall
regardless carried him up to 3 px into the platform he had already landed on
and left PlayerInAir clear at a y that is not y+1 % 8 == 0, a state nothing
recovers from except a jump: on screen, Harry sunk into the platform he had
just dropped onto, and a jump shook him out. The replay now re-reads
PlayerInAir (and PlayerDead) after every step and stops when he lands. Sink by
frame phase was +3 +1 0 +3 +2 +1 0 +2 on two platforms; it is 0 in all eight
phases now. tools/verify_player.py section 11b drives the drop from all eight
phases of the falling counter, which is what makes the sink deterministic --
section 7 lands him on the floor, where an overshoot has almost nothing to sink
into and the frame usually ends first, so it passed throughout.

A hen: climbing hens drew 4 px right of their ladder. The Z80's hen art is
shifted 4 px inside its cell and the game compensates in the draw; the port was
applying the shift to the wrong frames, so frames 2/3 and 4/5 are now
de-shifted at extraction, with a generator refusal and a sprite-sheet check to
keep it that way.

events.title: Fit the dress round the glTF body's measured trunk sections, and let each dress station cover the girth up to its neighbours
events.message:
Fit the dress round the glTF body's measured trunk sections, and let each dress station cover the girth up to its neighbours

Skin showed through the glTF women's bodice (worst on the heavy Hausa
build) for two reasons. The dress envelope was the code-built profile with
the trunk's widest and deepest extents plugged into an ellipse — but a bust
or a belly off the front line, or a square flank, lies outside the ellipse
through those two extents. And a wrap's stations sit ~0.055 of stature
apart, the cloth running between their girths, so it cut the chord through
the bust and the belly between them.

The glTF body now measures its trunk every 0.01 of stature from crotch to
neck as ellipses that enclose every point of each cross-section, and the
dress follows those sections; the code-built body keeps its profile. Each
wrap station takes the largest girth as far as its neighbours, so the
cloth falls straight from the bust. A new test casts rays from the trunk
axis through every trunk vertex of every sex, age and build and asserts
each people's dress layer lies beyond the skin.

events.title: hardware: Leave Gary timeout mode unchanged during SCSI probes
events.message:
hardware: Leave Gary timeout mode unchanged during SCSI probes

Fat Gary's timeout register reads status rather than the programmed
mode, so saving and restoring it can leave short DSACK timeouts active
for unrelated hardware accesses.

Use guarded reads for NCR and SDMAC detection and configuration. Keep
controller writes conditional on accessible, idle hardware and restore
the saved transfer count before handling a failed readback. Check WD
register access before entering the timed diagnostic section.

Update identify to use guarded NCR detection and remove the unused
Gary timeout definitions.

events.title: grm-mej.13: registers a callee provably preserves keep their value across the call
events.message:
grm-mej.13: registers a callee provably preserves keep their value across the call

StoredValueScanner.resolveStoredValue and constantValue no longer treat every
call as clobbering the register being resolved: a plain JSR to one resolved,
disassembled, non-banked target whose CalleeRegisterSummary preserves the
register is stepped over (CalleeRegisterSummary.summarizeCallSite; per-program
memo invalidated on modification number).

The register surviving does not mean the BANK survived -- the callee may switch
it. So resolveStoredValue resumes with hooks.stateAt(call) after the crossing,
exactly as a call-crossing PHA/PLA pairing does (resumeStateAfterPairing); with
no state there the walk goes blind: it may still finish on a state-free
definition (immediate, transfer, immediate AND/ORA) but stops at any read that
would consult the in-state WITHOUT asking the hook (the ironsword rule).
constantValue was already safe: it resolves loads under BankState.unknown().

banktest2 C5 (LDA #$35 / JSR sub / STA $01, sub = bare RTS) now resolves to
bank 5; criterion C5 updated (it asserted the old clobber warning) and the
generator comment with it; golden re-blessed. No real-ROM row moved (check nes:
wizwarr held + shenlong/dragonpower symbol flaps only).

CalleePreservedRegisterScanProgramTest: 13 tests, incl. the bank-state hazard
(mutation-checked: both fail without the at-call resume / blind guard).
Unplumbed, future: HelperArgumentRecovery prologueOutcome, reload walk,
inboundArgumentCell.

events.title: Steer touch glides with the newest finger and treat a leap as airborne
events.message:
Steer touch glides with the newest finger and treat a leap as airborne

Three side-touch fixes for leaping and gliding on the sky platforms.

- Gliding: the newest side finger steers, so a press on the other
  side turns at once with the first thumb still down, and lifting it
  turns back.  The fall rule from deb5eb5 (a second side is the
  button) now applies only before the glide opens; in the glide the
  button does nothing until landing, and holding back the turn until
  the first thumb lifted was the long press it took to change course.
- A leap now counts as airborne.  A finger landing mid-leap took the
  ground route: a lone press waited 120 ms to tell a tap from a hold,
  and a two-thumb press waited up to 250 ms to rule out the menu
  chord.  Either could miss the single landing read, so a re-leap
  worked only sometimes.  In the air every press is live at once.
- Lifting the steering finger hands the steer to a remaining button
  finger on the ground too, not only in the air, so the figure walks
  whichever side is still held instead of holding fire alone.

events.title: Drop taps made during a knock-down when the figure gets up
events.message:
Drop taps made during a knock-down when the figure gets up

The player step reads no input for the 2.75 s knock-down, so presses
made meanwhile queued for the first read after it.  A button tap made
during the fall's last row or while lying down then joined a held side
in that read and leaped, where the player expected a walk.

The step that ends the knock-down now flushes queued presses through a
new `flush` on the input.  Held keys and fingers stay held, so the
figure gets up doing what is held at that moment.  Playback reads its
recording and ignores the flush.

# SMS Game Designer

*Formerly "SMS Game Maker"; renamed because another tool already had that
name. Projects and autosaves from before the rename open as they are.*

A no-code environment for making Sega Master System games: Blockly for logic,
pixel editors for art, a compiler running as WASM, and an emulator to play
the result. Everything happens in the browser — no server, no accounts, no
install.

Ported from [`vcs-game-maker`](https://github.com/haroldo-ok/vcs-game-maker),
built on [CVBasic](https://github.com/nanochess/CVBasic) and
[gasm80](https://github.com/nanochess/gasm80), with the browser toolchain
from
[`CVBasic-emscripten`](https://github.com/haroldo-ok/CVBasic-emscripten).

## The idea

The Atari 2600 has five movable objects, so `vcs-game-maker` can name them
all: `player0`, `player1`, `missile0`, `missile1`, `ball`. The Master System
has 64 sprites, and a modest shmup has 25 things on screen at once. Naming
them is hopeless.

So this tool changes the unit of authoring:

> You author **types** — a Ship, a Bug, a Shot. The runtime owns the
> individual copies. Interactions are declared between **groups**, not
> between individuals.

Everything else follows from that. Scripts are written from the point of view
of one instance, so blocks say *set my x* and never name anything. Collision
is `on collide with enemy` on a type, and the tool derives the matrix — four
specialised tests for the worked shmup, not the 300 a named-object model
would need. Bullets and explosions can come and go, because lifetime finally
has somewhere to live.

## Why this backend

Everything must run in the browser, so the real question is not "which
console" but "which compiler can ship as a WASM blob, and which emulator can
ship next to it". CVBasic and gasm80 are two small, portable, file-in
file-out C programs — the same property that makes this kind of tool possible
at all. And the Master System needs no BIOS, so Play is one fetch lighter and
one caveat shorter than the alternatives.

The same project also builds for the SG-1000 — genuinely the same project,
with the instance counts brought inside the smaller machine and one line
changed. `examples/shmup-sg1000.json` is the worked shmup on a TMS9918: half
the pool, one 16x16 hardware sprite per actor instead of two 8x16 ones, one
colour per sprite instead of per pixel, and not a single change to any actor,
script or collision rule.

ColecoVision and MSX share that renderer and should be close. They are not
tested, so the roadmap says so.

## Getting started

```sh
npm install
npm run serve         # the compilers are already in public/wasm
```

The in-browser compilers ship prebuilt in `public/wasm/`. To rebuild them,
you need Zig, which installs from PyPI - no Emscripten SDK:

```sh
pip install ziglang==0.16.0
npm run wasm          # make -C toolchain wasm
```

To work headlessly — no browser, no WASM — you only need the native tools:

```sh
make -C toolchain native        # builds ./bin/cvbasic and ./bin/gasm80
npm run sample                  # writes examples/shmup.json
npm run rom                     # project JSON -> .bas -> .asm -> .sms
npm test                        # the whole suite: codegen, blocks, UI, playtests,
                                # and an end-to-end walk through the built editor
```

`npm test` also runs the block layer headlessly: Blockly works fine without a
DOM as long as nothing is injected into a page, so the tests build real block
trees, lower them, and compile the result to a ROM.

The suite does not stop at "it compiled". `tools/sms.py` is a headless
Master System — a real Z80 core plus enough VDP to render a frame — and
`tools/playtest.py` runs the built ROM on it and checks what a player would
notice: that the cast is on screen, that the pad moves the ship, that holding
fire spawns shots, that clearing a wave advances the room.

```sh
pip install z80 pillow
python3 tools/sms.py out/shmup.sms --frames 40 --png out/frame.png
python3 tools/playtest.py out/shmup.sms out/shmup.sym
```

That exists because the shmup once compiled cleanly, reported 91% of a frame,
passed every source-level test, and drew its entire cast as thin vertical
slivers.

`npm run rom` prints the whole accounting:

```
  out/shmup.bas  (705 lines)
  27 slots, 16/96 sprite defs, 42 collision checks/frame
  Frame 91% at worst case (sprites 34%, behaviours 24%, collision 31%)
  RAM 509/7966 bytes (6%)
  ROM out/shmup.sms  32768 bytes
```

## Layout

```
engine/          the CVBasic kernel, hand-written and versioned
  core.bas         entity pool and declarations (no executable code)
  kernel.bas       movement, animation, reaping, rendering
  terrain.bas      tile collision (only included when a room has a tilemap)

src/ir/          project model -> intermediate representation
  schema.js        project shape, target profiles, migration
  build-ir.js      slot ranges, collision matrix, VRAM and RAM planning
  lint.js          rules that run on every edit
  budget.js        frame budget, from measured cycle counts

src/generators/  IR -> CVBasic text
  blockly-lower.js          blocks -> statement AST
  cvbasic/emit-program.js   assembly and emission order
  cvbasic/emit-*.js         actors, collision, behaviours, rooms, assets

src/blocks/      Blockly definitions and the scoped toolboxes
src/components/  actor editor, sprite editor, Blockly host, budget meter
src/views/       Game / Actors / Rooms / Play / Code
src/workers/     the compiler Worker
examples/        a shmup, a platformer, an SG-1000 cut of the shmup, and a
                 coverage sample that uses every block in the language
tools/           headless build, sample generators, tests
  sms.py           a headless Master System, for looking at the screen
  playtest.py      runs the ROM and asserts what a player would see
  cycles.py        static Z80 cycle counter, for the frame budget
docs/            measurements and porting notes
```

## Budgets, not surprises

On this hardware the limits *are* the design, so they are visible while you
edit rather than after you wonder why the game crawls:

```
 Sprites  ████████░░  22/64 hw      RAM    ██░░░░░░░░   509/7966 B
 VRAM     ██░░░░░░░░  16/96 defs    ROM    ██████████  32.0/32 KB
 Slots    ███████░░░  27/40         Frame  █████████░  91%
```

Everything except ROM size comes from the IR with no compile. RAM comes
straight out of CVBasic, which prints its own accounting on every build. The
frame figure comes from cycle counts measured on the real generated Z80 —
see [docs/MEASUREMENTS.md](docs/MEASUREMENTS.md).

The same idea applies beyond performance. A platformer actor reports what its
jump actually reaches, because nobody can eyeball that from "jump strength
5":

```
 note  Hero jumps 33 px (4 tiles) and covers 54 px (6 tiles) in the air.
       Keep ledges within 3 tiles of each other.
```

When something is over budget the tool says what to do about it, with a
button that does it: *"enemy vs player_shot is 48 checks a frame. Checking it
every other frame halves that, and at these speeds it is not noticeable."* A
user cannot act on a number alone.

## Examples

**Open → Examples** in the editor offers three working games: *Bug Blaster*
(a shooter), *Cavern Run* (a platformer with tile terrain) and *Bug Blaster
SG* (the same shooter on the SG-1000). Their scripts open as real blocks you
can read and change. They are the same files the test suite builds and plays
on emulated hardware, so anything offered is known to work.

## What you get without doing anything

A new project already has the parts that make something feel like a game
rather than a demo: a title screen that waits for the button, a game over
that returns to it, five sound effects, and three tunes. Music takes two of
the four sound channels and effects take the other two, so they never cut
each other off.

None of it needs a tracker or an envelope editor. All of it is plain,
commented CVBasic in the exported source.

## Escape hatches

- **Export the ROM** and run it on real hardware or any emulator.
- **Export CVBasic source + engine** as a zip that builds standalone. The
  generated code is commented and meant to be read; that is the answer to
  every "can it also do X".
- **Export a playable HTML bundle** — ROM plus emulator plus a page.

## Credits

`vcs-game-maker` by haroldo-ok, with contributions by AbstractPolygon.
CVBasic and gasm80 by Óscar Toledo G. (nanochess). EmulatorJS for the player.
Blockly by Google.

events.title: emu: widen the owed-tail drain window to outlast scheduling
events.message:
emu: widen the owed-tail drain window to outlast scheduling

The drain that absorbs a timed-out command's late tail capped at 200 ms,
and the assertion that depends on it flaked on the macOS runner where a
shell's sleep 0.05 overshot that cap under load (the same race already
lost there once at 20 ms). The window is a cap, not a delay — the drain
returns on the first byte — so a tail that arrives promptly costs nothing;
only a genuinely late one waits it out. Widening it to 1500 ms gives the
test's 50 ms gap real margin against scheduler overshoot.

Same code passed macOS at the branch; the flake was load-induced timing,
not a regression.

project.notes: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof.

events.title: grm-mej.11: CalleeRegisterSummary -- per-callee A/X/Y preservation over p-code
events.message:
grm-mej.11: CalleeRegisterSummary -- per-callee A/X/Y preservation over p-code

A state-free forward fixpoint per callee entry over raw instruction p-code:
A/X/Y in {bot, Entry(R), top}, SP as Entry+k, stack slots by offset. A register
is preserved when every reachable RTS returns it holding its own entry value
with SP == Entry+2. Nested JSRs compose summaries recursively (recursion guard,
nesting cap 8, 2048-instruction cap); unresolved or banked-from-outside callees
clobber all registers. Abandons on TXS, join stack mismatch, caller-frame or
stack-aliasing stores, RTI/BRK/JMP(ind), undisassembled code, no return.

Chosen over SymbolicPropogator (does not track 8-bit parentless registers), the
p-code emulator (single concrete path) and the decompiler (runs after
BoardBankAnalyzer; no per-function unaffected inference). Design and rulings on
the bead.

Named assumptions, recorded in each Summary when relied on:
- StackDiscipline.CROSSED_CALL_IS_STACK_NEUTRAL (owner ruling O4)
- StackAssumption.INDIRECT_STORES_DO_NOT_WRITE_STACK_FRAME (owner ruling O3)

No production consumer yet (grm-mej.13 will be); full gate byte-identical.
CalleeRegisterSummaryProgramTest: 34 tests x 3 languages, incl. blmaster's real
e61b bytes (preserves X and Y, not A).

events.title: fix(sandbox): the harvest returns what the CPU stored into I/O space
events.message:
fix(sandbox): the harvest returns what the CPU stored into I/O space

Symptom: `trx64cli sandbox` harvested $D800-$DBE7 and $D018/$D020/$D021 as
all $00 under $01=$37, although writtenRuns listed those ranges. With $01=$34
the same stores were captured correctly. (C64RE issue #37, item 7.)

Cause: the harvest sliced the raw 64K `ram` array. A store to $D000-$DFFF with
I/O banked in lands in a chip and never reaches `ram`.

Fix: Observer gains `on_io_store(addr, value, pc)` (default no-op), fired from
the write path only when FullBus::wr_land == LAND_IO. The sandbox observer logs
the last value per I/O address (armed at entry, like writtenRuns). The harvest
overlays those values on the raw RAM slice: the CPU's value, no chip read-back,
low nibble for colour RAM $D800-$DBFF. Unwritten addresses and RAM under I/O
keep raw RAM; stores with I/O off were already right. JSON: each harvest (and
the back-compat `harvest`) gains `ioWritten: [[lo,hi],..]`; text output adds an
ioWritten note. Existing fields unchanged.

Retarget the Quaternius clips onto the villager skeleton and author the shovel clips

The walk, sprint, idle and the kneel transitions come from the Quaternius
Universal Animation Library (CC0 1.0, quaternius.com; pinned GitHub mirror
J-Ponzo/gltf-universal-animation-library @ e24c23cf), retargeted by world

events.title: Hold a button tap made in a short fall until the landing, to leap from it
events.message:
Hold a button tap made in a short fall until the landing, to leap from it

A leap that comes down lower than it took off ends with a fall of a
row or two.  The fall reads input every row, so a button tap queued
during the leap was spent on a fall read that ignores it, and the
landing walked a step instead of leaping.  On touch, a tap on the
other side during the fall was also taken as steering, which with
both sides down released the held side.

- The player step reads with a new `falling` policy while the fall
  would ignore the button: no shuba glide yet, and short of a
  knockdown fall.  It moves as `continuous` but leaves queued button
  presses for the landing read, which then leaps.  Recordings store
  what the game read, so replays are unaffected.
- SideTouch: while airborne, a finger on the other side from a held
  side is the button and the held side keeps steering.  Lifting the
  steering finger hands the steer to a remaining button finger, so
  thumb-to-thumb glide turns still work.

events.title: The OAM image is cleared at boot and at every level load
events.message:
The OAM image is cleared at boot and at every level load

Two reports off a physical DMG, one class: a byte the ROM reads before it
writes. An emulator powers OAM and WRAM up as zeros, so every check here
passed; a DMG powers them up with whatever the cells held.

BlitOam copies OAM_BYTES out of wOamShadow every VBlank and OAM_BYTES
stops at the duck, so entries 32..39 are never written on any level, and
the draws skip the slots a level does not use. OAM is in screen
coordinates and nothing scrolls it, so a leftover entry is a sprite pinned
to the screen -- the stray glyphs of the first report. wOnNotice was the
second and worse: HandleVBlank tests it with the front-end flags and skips
the whole draw pass while it is set, and the title's START reaches the
first level without going through ShowNotice, so that level ran on the
powered-on byte: no camera, no sprites, no status row.

Start now zeroes the shadow, all 40 OAM entries and wOnNotice with the LCD
off. Then the second report showed the same bug one level later and not a
power-on bug at all: only Start ever cleared the image, so a level that
used fewer slots than the one before it inherited its birds and platforms
for good -- a game over at level 3, and level 1 came up with level 3's
third hen and a lift. The clear is now the routine ClearOamShadow, called
from LoadLevel, which every level arrives through, and DrawLifts' hide path
hides both platforms instead of one (four entries, not two).

tools/verify_init.py checks all three against a machine that powered up
dirty; tools/sweep_wram.py (make sweep) is the tool for the next one of
these.

events.title: feat(minigl): composite plugin frames from imported dma-bufs (#2382)
events.message:
feat(minigl): composite plugin frames from imported dma-bufs (#2382)

* feat(minigl): composite plugin frames from imported dma-bufs

When AMIBERRY_MINIGL_ZEROCOPY=1, the MiniGL plugin (companion PR
amiberry-minigl-plugin#3) exports each presented frame as a dma-buf
instead of encoding it into the Picasso96 span. The transport
registers the optional image sink after plugin load; the OpenGL
renderer imports the fd on its own EGLDisplay (resolved from libEGL at
runtime - no new build-time dependency) and composites the frame
directly, so the per-frame surface upload and the plugin's glReadPixels
both disappear.

The imported image is cached until the plugin announces a change, the
surface path remains the fallback whenever no image is live, and the
path is skipped entirely for non-RTG screens. With the flag off the
build is byte-identical in behavior; shader stacks (preset, external,
crtemu) still run for RTG screens without a live export but are
bypassed while one is showing.

Measured on the RPi4 rig (GLQuake timedemo1 640x480, same binary):
57.7 fps with the flag off vs 70-73 fps on, +22-26% guest frame rate.

* fix(minigl): review fixes for the dma-buf composite

- The imported EGLImageKHR handle was never stored, so cleanup never
  destroyed imported images; backing buffers leaked per handover.
- The registry now duplicates the dma-buf fd while the sink callback
  holds the plugin's serialization, closing the window where the next
  handover could close or recycle the descriptor between the snapshot
  and eglCreateImageKHR. The renderer imports from the owned dup.
- The sink is only registered when the OpenGL renderer is live: with a
  software or SDL backend, registration would make the plugin skip span
  updates that nothing would display.

Also removes the diagnostic back/front buffer probe used to verify the
scanout during bring-up. Re-verified on the rig: both buffers carry
live frame colors through a full timedemo, 71.7 fps zero-copy vs 57.5
flags-off on the same binaries.

* fix(minigl): renderer-published importer gate, owned snapshot dup, libretro link

Review round two plus CI:

- The renderer now publishes once, under its own current context, whether
  dma-buf frames can actually be imported (an EGL display with
  EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import and the entry points). Sink registration
  is gated on that flag instead of the C++ backend type, so a GLX or
  SDL-only window system keeps the plugin on the span path instead of
  exporting frames nobody can show.
- minigl_display_current() returns a fresh dup taken under the registry
  lock; the renderer closes it after the import attempt. The registry's
  own descriptor could previously be closed by the next handover between
  the snapshot and eglCreateImageKHR.
- libretro builds compile service_transport.cpp without the OpenGL
  renderer, so the old get_opengl_renderer() gate broke their link; the
  flag removes the dependency and libretro/Makefile gains
  minigl_display.cpp. Verified: full libretro core builds and links on
  aarch64 Linux again.

* fix(minigl): define destroy_minigl_import on non-Linux platforms too

It sat inside the __linux__ guard while destroy_context() calls it
unconditionally, which left FreeBSD, macOS and Windows builds with an
undefined symbol at link time. The definition now lives outside the
guard with its body still Linux-only.

* fix(libretro): compile gl_context_ladder.cpp in the core build

The ladder lookup from the KMSDRM context fix (a4efa20c) was added to
CMake's source list only. libretro's Makefile never compiled it, and
while GNU ld drops the unresolved reference with section GC (the core
never calls set_opengl_attributes), mingw's lld reports it - so the
Windows libretro job has failed since that merge. Adds the translation
unit next to the other osdep sources; the Linux core build is verified
to still link with it.

* fix(minigl): review round three - fd leaks, probe strictness, sink lifetime

- The import-failure return skipped the snapshot fd close; every retry
  leaked another descriptor. All exits from render_minigl_dmabuf close
  the owned duplicate now.
- The capability probe requires EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import_modifiers
  (the import attributes carry a modifier) and GL_OES_EGL_image on the
  GL context (resolved via SDL_GL_GetProcAddress, enumerated with
  glGetStringi), so a context that cannot bind the imported image never
  stops the span updates.
- Importer capability is reference counted per renderer instance and
  re-probed when the context is rebuilt: amiberry recreates the window
  context during startup, and the previous static/global flag handling
  left registration seeing no importer (observed as a silent fall back
  to span mode). When the last capable context goes away the image is
  dropped and the sink unregistered, so the plugin resumes span updates.

* fix(minigl): retryable sink install, RTG-scoped importer references

- Context recreation unregisters the sink when the last capable context
  goes, but the plugin stays loaded and the installation guard stayed
  set, leaving zero-copy off for the rest of the process. Installation
  now retries from the dispatch path whenever an importer is ready, and
  the registry allows reinstalling after the last reference drops.
- Importer references are held only by renderers presenting the
  Picasso96 screen, so a native-screen monitor staying capable cannot
  keep the sink installed while the RTG display falls back to SDL and
  the plugin keeps skipping span updates nobody consumes.

Verified on the rig: both boot contexts publish capability, the sink
installs once the RTG importer is live, 72.1 fps timedemo.

* fix(minigl): serialize install, reconcile the transport flag, probe after make-current

- maybe_install_zero_copy now runs under the plugin mutex the same way
  every other plugin interaction does; the trap workers in indirect
  UAE-board mode could previously race the first install and the sink
  state.
- The transport's sink_installed flag is reconciled against the
  registry: a release that removed the sink no longer leaves the flag
  latched, so a recreated context can reinstall.
- The capability probe moved after SDL_GL_MakeCurrent and is taken only
  by renderers presenting the Picasso96 screen: the one-shot verdict
  previously described whatever context happened to be current, and a
  capable native-screen monitor could keep the sink installed while the
  RTG display fell back to SDL.

Verified: capability published once the RTG context presents, sink
installs under the mutex, 73.0 fps timedemo on the rig.

* fix(minigl): failed-import memo, registry install/release locking

Self-review findings before merge:

- A runtime eglCreateImageKHR rejection retried and logged on every
  presented frame while the plugin kept suppressing span updates. The
  rejected export's sequence number is now remembered: no retry, no
  repeat logging, the span fallback simply stays for that export.
- Sink install/release mutated g_installed and g_set_image_sink without
  the registry mutex, and install could race the release path's
  uninstall into a dead sink with the flags claiming active (or install
  with zero importers, freezing span updates). Both now decide under
  the mutex with the plugin setter invoked outside it (the plugin holds
  its own mutex around the sink callback; opposite orders deadlock),
  and install refuses when no importer reference exists.

72.4 fps zero-copy, 57.7 flags-off on the rig.

* feat(minigl): zero-copy on by default with minigl_zerocopy option

The dmabuf composite no longer needs AMIBERRY_MINIGL_ZEROCOPY=1: the
new minigl_zerocopy config option defaults to true, and the env var
becomes an explicit override ("1" on, "0" off) for one-off runs and
troubleshooting. Registration still requires a verified importer, so
builds and window systems without one keep the span path untouched.

Closes the two blockers that kept it opt-in:

- create_screenshot() refreshes the Picasso96 span through the plugin's
  optional minigl_plugin_materialize_all before reading the surface, so
  screenshots capture current pixels while image mode holds. The
  actionable-screenshot path gets the same refresh.
- The composite is claimed by one renderer: on hosts with several
  Picasso96 monitors only the claiming monitor shows the plugin's
  image; the others keep their own span content instead of receiving
  the plugin's frame.

Verified on the rig: 72.8 fps timedemo with no environment variables,
opt-out via env yields span mode (no imports), 223-check plugin suite
green.

events.title: Merge branch 'demo-feedback': what a demo asked of the library
events.message:
Merge branch 'demo-feedback': what a demo asked of the library

A demo built on STDL measured where the library cost it frames and
what it had to write for itself; this is the library's answer, tested
in Hatari and on a real Mega STE at 8 and 16MHz.

- The gcc 4.6 multiply trap, durably: stdl_math.h (16-bit multiply and
  divide on the 68000's own instructions, and STDL_FixDiv), and the
  build's libcallcheck, which fails on any new libgcc arithmetic call.
- STDL_FillPolygon: convex polygons set, XORed, ORed or cleared into a
  colour's planes, shared edges tiling exactly; inside the clip, a
  68000 path from vertices to rows. Within 12% of the demo's own
  filler at full vertical resolution, at the same frame rate.
- Rasters on Timer B (STDL_OpenRasters and family), sharing the timer
  safely with the borders; palette staging (STDL_StagePalette); music
  from memory, seekable, with its registers readable for meters;
  STDL_BlitSprites and STDL_DirtyWholeGroups for scenes of bobs.
- Faster pre-shifted sprites, whole-group fills, aligned text, chunky
  conversion, pre-shifting and dirty restores.
- Fixed on the hardware: a program that inited without a video mode
  left the machine at 60Hz on exit (since v1.10.0).

events.title: fix(net): gate the RX ready count on firmware 2.1 and cover review cases
events.message:
fix(net): gate the RX ready count on firmware 2.1 and cover review cases

Firmware before 2.1 maps register 0x8C to the zzdebug test counter, not
the RX ready count, so the repeated-serial rule now reads it only when
FW_VERSION reports 2.1 or later. A repeated serial 0 always waits:
firmware never starts a post-restart sequence at 0 and handshake
firmware rejects an ack of 0, so delivering it would loop on a corrupt
slot.

The status register and firmware version now come from the shared
include/zz9000_hw.h map instead of a second definition in rx.h. The
known limit of serial reuse (a restart during a payload copy can let
the ack consume the new frame) is documented at the model contract.

The firmware model now covers 2.0.x, 2.1/2.2 and 2.8 behaviour; new
tests pin the 2.1 serial-1 restart, the version gate, the re-read
mismatch, the ready mask width, serial 0, bad-size drops and the
large-gap BadData path. Also drops the unused zznet_read_word and adds
the shared headers to the device's make prerequisites.

events.title: fix(net): detect RX restarts from the firmware ready count
events.message:
fix(net): detect RX restarts from the firmware ready count

The previous rule only treated a repeated serial as new after the framer
had read an empty slot. A firmware restart and its first frame can land
between the framer's ack and its next header read, so the cleared slot
is never seen and the RX livelock remains.

The serial ack completes on the bus only after firmware handled it, so
a header still carrying the acked serial is either a stale slot on
firmware that never clears slots, or a new frame after a restart. The
ETH_RX_STATUS ready count separates them: the frame is new when
firmware reports frames waiting and the header is unchanged on re-read.
Firmware before 2.1 has neither restarts nor that register (reads 0),
so it keeps the old behavior.

events.title: STDL_Init: a program that never sets a rate leaves the sync alone
events.message:
STDL_Init: a program that never sets a rate leaves the sync alone

A Mega STE came back to its desktop at 60Hz after a test program.
stdl.old_sync is -1 for "never changed", but STDL_Init zeroes the
state and only STDL_SetVideoMode set it to -1 again, so every program
that inited without a video mode wrote 0 into $FFFF820A on its way
out: 60Hz. Games set a video mode, which is presumably why no port
noticed; probes and tools do not. In since STDL_SetRefresh (v1.10.0).

STDL_Init sets it to -1 after the memset. SYNCCHK is the check, on
the machine because tests/host does not link video.c: init and quit
alone, a video mode, and STDL_SetRefresh to the other rate, each
against the rate before. Hatari, plain ST: sync 2 before, 0 after all
three without the fix; 2 after each with it.

expandFrame's comment said it widened a 32-pixel frame to 64; it does
not.  Each 16-pixel chunk of a resident frame is stored as two
bitplanes and written into planes 0-1 (the body: colours 1-3, the
clothes in palette slots 1 and 2) or planes 1-2 (the head: colours 2,
4 and 6, slot 6 the skin) of the four-plane compositing buffer.  So
flipV, which never flipped anything vertically, is lowPlanes; flipH is
mirror; m1/m2/mmask are planeA/planeB/mirMask.  setDogSprite's flipH2
is mirror too.

documents whose Ghidra names it decodes, and the README lists it.

events.title: fix(net): deliver the first frame after a firmware RX restart
events.message:
fix(net): deliver the first frame after a firmware RX restart

Since rev 2.2 the framer keeps old_serial across empty slots. A firmware
DMA restart (Amiga reset, MAC update, TX-timeout recovery) resets the
frame serial to 2, so when the last frame consumed before the restart
was also serial 2, the next frame looked already consumed: the framer
never acked it and re-armed the IRQ, which firmware raised again for
the pending backlog, forever.

After an empty slot, the next non-empty header is a new frame even if
its serial matches: firmware clears a slot before its read cursor moves
on, so a consumed frame cannot reappear after an empty read.

The slot classification moves to net/rx.c so the host suite can drive
it against a model of the firmware backlog ring.

events.title: cp_asm.s: document the copy protection in detail
events.message:
cp_asm.s: document the copy protection in detail

A header explaining the idea (two contradictory gap measurements of
track 79 within one attempt's reads), the flow, every hardware
register and 1772 command it uses, and the encryption; comments on
each step of the code, including the FDC/DMA sequence, the drive
select through YM2149 port A, and the gap-measuring routine.

Four routines were described wrongly and are corrected: cpseek issues
$03 RESTORE (not a seek), cprd issues $13 SEEK to track 79 (not a
sector read -- the read is $e4 READ TRACK in cpsec), cprest2 issues
$d0 FORCE INTERRUPT (not a restore), and cpfdcw waits for the motor
to stop rather than for the controller to go idle.

Comments only: instruction lines unchanged, byte-identical.

events.title: cp_asm.s: write the encrypted track check as decrypted code; encrypt at build
events.message:
cp_asm.s: write the encrypted track check as decrypted code; encrypt at build

checkCopyProt's 96 encrypted bytes were carried as .dc.b.  They are
now the instructions they decrypt to: the routine that scans the raw
track for the $a1 sync run and the $fe ID mark of track 79, then
counts the $ff gap bytes before it (fewer than 15 sets d3 bit 0, 80 or
more bit 1; both are needed to pass).

The key is $1567: cpsetp clears d0 and calls the cpsum chain, which
only adds constants.  The header's 'keyed by the current drive number'
was wrong and is corrected.

tools/cp_encrypt.py runs in alcyon_link.sh right after as68: it finds
cpenc..cpencend through the object's symbol table, checks the block is
the 48 words cpsetp's dbf covers, and adds the key to each word.  It
refuses to encrypt twice.  as68 reproduces the decrypted bytes exactly
(cmp.b #$4f,d6 stays the immediate cmp, not cmpi), and nothing in the
block is relocated.

Clean build byte-identical; reloc_audit and stx_check unchanged.

Fix the A key: work around a Vivado synthesis bug in keyboard.vhd (issue #1)

Vivado 2026.1 turned the first call of the process-local procedure
map_key (which wrote the process variable m and read key_pressed_n
implicitly) into a constant: the ST matrix key A (column 4, row 5) was
always pressed, so the IKBD never saw a new press of A. There was no
warning, and GHDL/Verilator simulate the code correctly. Moving another
key to the first call broke that key instead.

map_key now takes the matrix and the key state as explicit parameters.
A standalone synthesis of keyboard.vhd shows that only matrix bit 37
changes (it is a register again); confirmed on a MEGA65 R6.

Also add the JTAG keyboard probe used to find this (USER3: ST matrix,
the last bytes the CPU read from the keyboard ACIA, press counters;
tools/probe3.tcl + decode3.py) and A/S cases in the GHDL keyboard test.

events.title: hardware: Handle probe faults on 68010 and later CPUs
events.message:
hardware: Handle probe faults on 68010 and later CPUs

The existing guard assumes a 68000 exception frame and a vector table
at address zero. Extend it for hardware probes on later processors.

Use the active VBR on 68010 and later CPUs and recover through a saved
supervisor stack pointer instead of modifying the fault frame. Mask
interrupts while the handlers are installed and restore the vectors
before returning. Flush the 68060 branch cache on prediction errors,
retrying when no other fault is present.

Add a longword probe alongside the byte probe and publish results only
after successful reads have left the protected supervisor section.

events.title: v0.3.1: runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel)
events.message:
v0.3.1: runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel)

### New: macOS
CPCSyntaxError now builds and runs on Macs, both Apple silicon (M1 and later) and Intel. A user's build compiled, but then stopped at start-up with "Failed to initialize OpenGL loader!". macOS only gives a modern OpenGL to a program that asks for a 3.2 Core Profile context, and the emulator now asks for one. The README has a new *Building from source → macOS* section:

```
xcode-select --install
brew install cmake ninja sdl2
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
./build/cpcse
```

Other things that work on a Mac now:
- **CSL scripts window:** it runs scripts (it finds its own program file without Linux's `/proc`).
- **"Open screenshot folder":** it uses `open`.
- **GDB server and command API:** a debugger that disconnects mid-reply no longer ends the program.

If a computer's graphics driver can't provide OpenGL 3 at all, the program now explains this in a message box instead of stopping with an assert.

Windows and Linux are unchanged.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.3.1.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. On Linux and macOS, build from source (README, *Building from source*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

events.title: Polygons: a 68000 path from vertices to rows, and only the colour's planes
events.message:
Polygons: a 68000 path from vertices to rows, and only the colour's planes

STDL_FillPolygon was about 2.3x one demo's own glenz filler. Most of
the gap was per polygon and per row in how the library did it, not in
what a library has to do:

- XOR, OR and CLEAR now write only the planes the colour has. A colour
  with nothing in planes 0-1 is a pair from the third plane's word,
  and an XOR into one plane - each face of a glenz object - is eor.w
  and not.w on that plane's word alone, where it was four words a
  group, three of them XORed with zero.
- A polygon inside the clip's columns, no taller than 256 rows, SET or
  XORed onto a surface with no mask, goes through stdl_poly_fast: the
  vertex scan, the clip, the winding and the walk down both sides in
  68000, each edge stepped in 16.16 in registers inside the row loop.
  No column tables and one call a polygon. 16.16 is exact at that
  height (the step falls short by under t/65536 after t rows, and the
  true position is never within 1/dy of a column, so t*dy < 65536 is
  enough): the same pixels as the table path. test_fixed_point checks
  that for every edge up to 256 rows and the first one it gets wrong
  at 257; triangles built on such edges fail if the limit is raised.
  Anything else - clipped columns, taller, a mask, a tie in the
  winding, OR and CLEAR on the machine - keeps the column tables.
  The C walk (fill_traps) is the host's twin; PGCHK runs the suite on
  the 68000, where a broken clipped-top multiply fails it.
- The row set-up finds a column's group with a mask and one shift,
  where it took two shifts of four and one of three.

PRIMCOST, plain ST, the old polygon.c against this in one library
(A and B passes identical):
  24 one-plane glenz-like triangles   85.0 -> 49.1ms
  22-row triangle, one plane           2.29 -> 1.27ms
  22-row triangle, colour 5            2.29 -> 1.55ms (spans 2.26)
  160-row diamond, XOR                15.08 -> 12.58ms (spans 23.9)
  160-row diamond, SET                15.23 -> 12.81ms
  22-row triangle, clipped (tables)    2.75 -> 2.58ms
polygon.o is 6092 bytes, from 4172, and outside the pixel budget: only
a program that fills polygons carries it.

PGCHK had outgrown run.sh's two-minute wait with the new tests and
looked like a hang; its surfaces are filled a plane word at a time
now, 82 seconds. AGENTS.md records the ceiling.

events.title: fix: the undo ring records the byte a store overwrites, not the ROM above it
events.message:
fix: the undo ring records the byte a store overwrites, not the ROM above it

The pre-write `old` byte (undo ring + trace) came from a CPU-view bus read, only
for $0002-$CFFF, and undo wrote it back into RAM. Stores that do not land in plain
visible RAM therefore corrupted RAM on reverse-step:

1. BASIC in, STA $A000: store lands in RAM beneath; old was the BASIC ROM byte,
   rstep wrote ROM into RAM.
2. Read-only cart ROM at $8000-$BFFF: same, with the cart ROM byte.
3. KERNAL in, STA $E000: old was 0, rstep zeroed the RAM byte.
4. $D000-$DFFF with I/O off (char ROM / RAM): old was 0 and undo went to the
   I/O shadows, leaving the stored byte in RAM.
5. A store a flash cart consumes (EasyFlash, EF3, GMod2/4 ...): RAM unchanged,
   but undo wrote `old` into RAM.

FullBus::write now reports where the store landed (wr_land: RAM / port / I/O /
cart / none) and, for RAM, the byte it replaced (wr_old, read from the RAM array:
no bus read, no cart read accounting, no side effect). write_raw / write_raw_dummy
use that report; cart-consumed and dropped stores are not recorded in the ring;
restore_byte undoes a $D000-$DFFF store into RAM when I/O is off. The RMW dummy
write to $00/$01 now records the port's pre-write value too. Ring dump format
unchanged. Regression tests: trx64-core/tests/delta_ring_under_rom.rs.

Found by the TRX64-Ultimate session.

events.title: windows: report installer failures and install shares from the real path
events.message:
windows: report installer failures and install shares from the real path

Under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with ErrorActionPreference Stop, the first
stderr line of pip, python or git becomes a terminating
NativeCommandError. The installer died on that line, showed only
"error: subprocess-exited-with-error", and never reached its own exit
code check. Run native commands through Invoke-Native, which streams
both streams and returns the exit code, and run git describe with
Continue so a repo without tags falls back to 0.0.0 as intended.

install.bat recorded the PowerShell exit code but returned pause's 0, so
a caller saw success. Return the recorded code after the pause.

setuptools_scm 10 lists tracked files even when the version is
pretended. It resolves them to their real path, so a checkout on a
mapped drive or behind a symlink yields \\host\share\... paths, and
relpath against a C: or U: working directory fails with "path is on
mount". Install from os.path.realpath of the checkout so both agree.
Take Resolve-Path's ProviderPath so a script started from a UNC path
does not hand "Microsoft.PowerShell.Core\FileSystem::\\..." to git.
events.author: tbdye

events.title: windows: install development checkouts with their dev version
events.message:
windows: install development checkouts with their dev version

The installer pretends the version so setuptools_scm skips its own
derivation, and it took the latest tag (git describe --abbrev=0). Every
development install therefore reported the release it descends from,
v0.6.0 thirty commits later, while pip install -e without the installer
reports 0.6.1.dev30. Derive the version as setuptools_scm does: the tag
on a clean tagged commit, otherwise the next patch release as .devN.

On a share owned by another account git refuses the checkout with
"detected dubious ownership" unless a global safe.directory entry
exists, and the installer fell back to 0.0.0 without a word. Trust
exactly this checkout for this one git call, ask git only when the
folder has its own .git so a ZIP download inside another repository
does not take that repository's version, and say so when the version
falls back to 0.0.0.

events.title: windows: let other accounts read files below the mount root
events.message:
windows: let other accounts read files below the mount root

WinFsp builds each file's ACL from st_mode and grants the "other" bits
to Everyone. Amiga entries rarely carry GRP/OTR protection bits, so
files report 0600 and directories 0700, and any account other than the
one that mounted (a global drive letter, a second logged-in user) can
list the 0777 root but cannot open anything beneath it.

On Windows, mirror the owner's read and execute bits into group and
other. Write stays owner-only unless the Amiga GRP/OTR write bits grant
it, and an Amiga file without the read bit stays unreadable for every
account. macOS and Linux keep the plain Amiga protection mapping.
events.author: tbdye

events.title: grm-fekc: recover select-data helpers whose sites store from different registers
events.message:
grm-fekc: recover select-data helpers whose sites store from different registers

MMC3 helpers commonly write the select from a constant in one register and the
bank from the caller's argument in another (tmnt3 FUN_8705: LDY #$47 / STY $8000
/ STA $8001). findHelpers' register-agreement check nulled argReg for that, so
recovery never ran. HelperModel.recoversPerSiteWithoutArgReg() now routes such a
model (depositsPerSite strategy, null argReg) through foldDeposits under the
caller's registers, offering no face-value argument to any site.

Two latent foldDeposits defects surfaced and are fixed:
- primary (the max-address site) seeded the fold, so EARLIER sites overwrote it.
  rcransom FUN_ff29 claimed select=7 though its last write restores select from
  $fb; nesmmc3mirrortest's ModeOne/SaveRestore/VaryingWindow summaries were wrong.
- each site saw the CALL's in-state, not the state the helper's earlier sites
  built, so a mirror read inside the helper answered the caller's bank
  (nesmmc3mirrortest CrossCopy: r6 now 4, per the generator's MM4 truth).

Re-blessed: tmnt3 (instrs.inOverlay 1405->3425, bankComments 49->119, warnings
37->56 -- more code reached; remaining warnings filed as grm-mej.9, grm-mej.10,
grm-lwvc), rcransom (f21d wrong select=7 removed), megaman3 (c0b8 wording),
nesmmc3mirrortest. check nes otherwise: wizwarr (held floor) + shenlong 97
(pre-existing flap; HEAD reproduces the identical dump in ab-test).

events.title: Unmount the interpreter behind a Windows venv launcher
events.message:

A Windows venv's python.exe and pythonw.exe are launchers that run the
base interpreter as a child with the same command line. Mount discovery
kept the launcher and dropped the child as a duplicate, but only the
child creates the PID-named unmount events, so `amifuse unmount` and the
tray failed with "cannot find the file specified" for every venv
install, including the one the installer creates. Keep the innermost
process of a duplicated chain instead.

The native cross-process unmount test signalled Popen.pid, which is the
launcher in a venv; it now uses the PID the child reports.

events.title: boot: Reduce animation overhead during floppy loading
events.message:
boot: Reduce animation overhead during floppy loading

The loader animation competes with DOS and decompression for CPU time
and holds off task switching across a full batch of plasma blits.

Shift scrolltext with word-wide carry operations and copy precomputed
horizontal Copper WAIT bytes in groups of eight. Skip vertical plasma
updates when the phase is unchanged, and release the blitter and task
switching exclusion after each column while checking the display map.

Lower the loader task priority after splash setup so background plasma
work yields to loading. Keep scrolling and horizontal wave movement in
VBlank so they continue while the foreground task is busy.

events.title: morepork conform and morepork final: an adapter's behaviour as Mammet facts
events.message:
morepork conform and morepork final: an adapter's behaviour as Mammet facts

Mammet checks the adapters, and its rules judge what a runner reports.
`morepork conform` runs an adapter through fixed probes (profile, trigger
instruction/mcycle/tcycle, boot-rom skip, version, beside itself) and states
each as adapter::honoured, refused (exit 2, with the adapter's reason) or
broke (with what differed), plus the columns the profile probe asked for and
wrote. A finer trigger whose trace has no more entries than the instruction
trace is broken even when the header claims it. `morepork final` runs an
adapter over ROMs and states each trace's last entry as adapter::ended
facts, or a failed check::outcome when the run fails. Both exit 0 whenever

events.title: SameBoy and missingno adapters: out-of-tree builds that refuse what they can't give
events.message:
SameBoy and missingno adapters: out-of-tree builds that refuse what they can't give

Mammet builds the adapters as checks from pinned, read-only source trees and
checks what they do. Each adapter now builds into OUT and writes nothing into
its sources, stamps its version from the build, and exits 2 naming what it
won't give instead of giving something else.

SameBoy: built from SRC (a patched tree; cloned at SAMEBOY_PIN and patched
when absent) with SameBoy's own Makefile into OUT, linked statically against
libsameboy.a, so it no longer needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH. SameBoy's boot ROMs are
assembled from SRC into OUT/boot_roms, where the adapter looks. Its
emulator_version is SameBoy's VERSION plus PIN (it said 0.16.x for v1.0.3).
It refuses --boot-rom skip (SameBoy has no skip; the panel had taken its
boot-ROM run for a skip), triggers other than instruction and tcycle (mcycle
was silently traced per instruction), columns it can't fill (they were
skipped with a warning), unknown models and unknown flags.

missingno: the Makefile copies the adapter and the crates it needs into
OUT/tree and builds there with its own Cargo.lock; with MISSINGNO_DIR, every
missingno crate comes from that tree. missingno-vcs is a git dependency like
the others, not a path to a sibling checkout. The GB adapter now honours the
profile: missingno's tracer writes its full scope to a work file, and the
adapter keeps the profile's columns (it wrote all 130 whatever was asked).
It gives the gbmicrotest block at instruction granularity, read beside each
capture, and refuses it at tcycle, where capture happens inside missingno.
Its emulator_version is missingno's version, +PIN and, for a git checkout,
the short commit. An instruction trace now ends with one more entry, the
state after the last instruction, which carries a stopping write such as
gbmicrotest's verdict. It refuses mcycle (it labelled per-instruction
entries mcycle), a boot ROM file, and unknown models.

events.title: make: build the CLI and FFI into OUT

Mammet runs morepork's builds as checks against a pinned, read-only tree, so
the build has to land elsewhere: `make OUT=<dir> cli ffi` builds with
`cargo build --release --locked --target-dir <dir>`, writing nothing into the
tree and never rewriting Cargo.lock. OUT defaults to target, so `make cli`
and `make ffi` work as before. cargo, not file lists, decides what is out of

events.title: v0.3.0: drives in the file picker, any file name on Windows, a Save dialog that browses
events.message:
v0.3.0: drives in the file picker, any file name on Windows, a Save dialog that browses

### New: the file picker switches drives
The Open dialog has a button for each drive (C:, D:, E: ...), with the one you're on highlighted. You can also type a drive (`D:`) or a folder, absolute (`D:\games`) or relative, into the name box and press Enter or Open to go there. A typed file name opens as before.

### New: the Save dialog browses
Saving (the assembler's source, DSK images, screenshots, snapshots) now uses the same folder view as Open: drives, `[..]`, folders to go into, and the files already there. Clicking a file takes its name.

### New: file and folder names in any script (Windows)
Files and folders whose names use accented letters, CJK or emoji now open. That includes discs, tapes, snapshots and ROMs you pick, drop onto the window or load from the command line, and running the program from a folder such as `C:\Users\José\Downloads`. Before, such a name could be listed but not opened. This needs Windows 10 version 1903 or later.

### New: typing the characters BASIC lines need
The command API's `type` and the headless `--type` now press the keys the CPC's own keyboard map gives. `[ ] { } ! ' `` and `@ |` all type correctly. On the French and Spanish keyboards, letters and digits now go to the right keys.

### Also in this release
A second full audit of the code. If you use the GDB server or the command API, the most important fix is this: a web page you visited could make your browser send commands to the API port. Both servers now refuse that. The audit also fixed crashes from crafted or mistaken input: symbol files, snapshots, CSL scripts, tapes, settings values and breakpoint conditions. Saves are now written whole or not at all, and the Symbiface II's clock is switched on with the board (it never was before). Unused code was removed.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.3.0.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. On Linux, build from source (README, *Building from source → Linux*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

made it tinny.  A synthesized click was tried first and rejected by ear.

silence() and suspend() leave them ringing, which lets power-off reset

events.title: Sprites in a batch, and restores of whole groups for scenes of bobs
events.message:
Sprites in a batch, and restores of whole groups for scenes of bobs

One demo's bobs, fourteen pre-shifted 16x16 sprites restored from the
background every frame, cost about twice its own loops through the
library, and most of the difference was per call. Two additions:

- STDL_BlitSprites(spr, list, n, dst) draws one sprite at many
  places from a list of STDL_SpriteAt {x, y, frame}. What does not
  change between entries is worked out once. Each one wholly inside
  the clip, drawn by the aligned four-plane loop on the CPU, goes
  straight to that loop, now a static inline in stdl_internal.h so
  both files share it; sprite.o is unchanged at 5304 bytes. Anything
  else is handed to STDL_BlitSprite, so the pixels match
  (test_spritebatch, SBCHK). SPRCOST, plain ST: fourteen bobs 13.1 ->
  11.1ms. Its own object.
- STDL_DirtyWholeGroups(1) rounds each restore out to the groups it
  touches, a plain copy where exact edges are merged. That is right
  only where everything on the page is background or pushed, and the
  header says so. Sixteen 16x16 restores at x & 15 = 5: 12.7 ->
  7.9ms.

A bob is now about 10.6k cycles drawn and restored, against 14.9k on
the version the demo tried and 7.5k for its own loops.

events.title: Polygons: an edge's columns stepped in 68000, when nothing needs clamping
events.message:
Polygons: an edge's columns stepped in 68000, when nothing needs clamping

Profiled on a glenz-sized triangle, about 30 rows, the side walkers
cost about 150 cycles a row a side, more than the edge set-ups: two
clamp compares every row, in a loop gcc kept in C. A polygon whose
vertices all lie within the clip's columns cannot have an edge
outside them, so it needs no clamping. One that is also under 32768
rows tall keeps every edge value in sixteen bits. Such polygons now
step their edges in a five-instruction 68000 loop (C twin on the
host); the rest keep the clamped C.

PRIMCOST on a plain ST:
- the 22-row triangle 2.71 -> 2.29ms, level with STDL_XorHSpans
  (2.27);
- the 160-row diamond 17.3 -> 15.1ms, against 23.9 as spans.
PGCHK passes on the machine.

Also tried and dropped: a direct path for triangles, sorted into two
trapezoids sharing the long edge, with no walk round the vertices.
It came to the same 24k cycles a triangle as the general path. The
walk was not the cost; calls and set-up spread through the function
were, and the extra path was a kilobyte for nothing.

- The general two-register handler fetched the second register's
  address and saved a register to hold it, a third dearer an
  interrupt than the demo's handler with the address written in.

events.title: Review fixes: polygon edges at int16_t's ends, staged SDL palette, and more
events.message:
Review fixes: polygon edges at int16_t's ends, staged SDL palette, and more

Three reviews of this branch (the asm, the C, the docs against the
code) found these.

Polygons:
- A column off either end of int16_t wrapped when it was narrowed into
  the edge tables, and a row drew 32000 pixels (ASan reproduced it on
  the host). Each side is now held within the clip plus one before it
  is narrowed.
- The divs.w fast path took edges up to 32767 columns wide but any
  height, so an edge taller than 32767 rows divided by a negative
  number on the target.
- Orientation comes from the top vertex's cross product, compared
  rather than subtracted; the signed area it replaced overflowed for
  big polygons.
- A clipped top from the far ends of int16_t steps in 64 bits.
- The fill now ignores the surface origin, as the contract says draw
  primitives do. SET takes STDL_TRANSPARENT as STDL_FillRect does.
- test_polygon gains these extremes, and PGCHK on the target fails
  without the divs.w fix.

Palette staging: SDL_SetPalette(SDL_PHYSPAL) wrote through
STDL_SetColour, which is never staged, so TPALETTE -stage did nothing.
A raw-word hook now stages it. Staging marks registers one by one, so
a staged physical write changes only the register it names, and
leftover state cannot reach a later STDL_Init.
tests/hatari/palstg.c, counted by palsplit.py, measures 99 and 100
frames of 100 split unstaged, through STDL_SetColours and the SDL
shim, and 1 and 2 staged (the switch-over frames).

Music:
- A voice handed back by an effect during a pause stays silent; it
  used to drone the held note.
- A seek is playing again before it writes the state, so an effect
  ending meanwhile restores its voice rather than muting it.

Rasters: reopening after a later Timer C hook no longer saves the
prefix as its own successor, which would loop on the first tick.

libcalls.sh:
- It stops when objdump fails or yields no disassembly. Before, it
  passed on anything.
- It now finds the float conversions (__floatsisf, __fixdfsi) and the
  64-bit helpers.

Docs: corrected wherever the reviews found them wrong, and every
measured figure now has a probe in the repo:
- PRIMCOST gains polygon and aligned-text cases;
- IXCHK times the pre-shift;
- RASTCHK measures the general handlers too and, built
  -DRASTCHK_NOPREFIX, the hold without the Timer C prefix, counted by
  rstill.py: 2 of 144 frames late with it, 16 without.

POLYDEMO's star is now a fan of triangles that really share edges.

events.title: Rasters: STDL_OpenRasters, Timer B shared safely with the borders
events.message:
Rasters: STDL_OpenRasters, Timer B shared safely with the borders

Programs wanting rasters (colour registers changed every few lines)
wrote their own Timer B handler. Two things went wrong that the
library can prevent. Nothing stopped it running while an open border
also used Timer B. And the terminate path did not know about it, so
an abnormal exit left the Timer B and Timer C vectors pointing into
freed memory.

STDL_OpenRasters(lines, reg1, reg2) changes one or two colour
registers every `lines` lines from a table:
- STDL_RasterTable is the table to fill and STDL_ShowRasters shows
  it from the next frame.
- There are three tables, so the program never writes one that this
  frame or the next VBL reads. A new one starts as a copy of the last
  shown.
- A VBL callback restarts Timer B from entry 0 before each picture.
- A Timer C prefix, as the borders use, lets Timer B in during TOS's
  200Hz handler.
- Colour 0, which is also the border, has its own quicker handlers.
- stdl_timerb_owner in video.c makes rasters and borders refuse each
  other.
- The teardown is vectors and registers only, on the terminate path.

Measured on a plain ST:
- with colour 0 first, every second line costs 11% of the machine
  (15% with a second register) and every line 22% (29%);
- with a fixed table and the program idle, a stripe edge is a line
  late in 6 frames of 186, 13 with the general handler, and 184
  without the Timer C prefix;
- RASTCHK aborted with rasters open, and the desktop came back in its
  own colours.

test_raster covers the refusals, the open state, the VBL arming, the
tables (never the shown or the armed one handed out) and both
teardowns, against host stand-ins for the MFP and vectors. RASTCHK
measures the cost and checks the two refusals on the machine. The
new RASTERS example draws copper bars in colour 0 and a gradient in
colour 15. AGENTS.md records the ownership lesson.

events.title: Polygons: STDL_FillPolygon, set, XOR, OR or clear into a colour's planes
events.message:
Polygons: STDL_FillPolygon, set, XOR, OR or clear into a colour's planes

A filled polygon meant building a span list for STDL_HSpans or
STDL_XorHSpans, which clip and find the row for every span on its
own. One demo measured over a thousand cycles a span drawing a glenz
object. STDL_FillPolygon fills a convex polygon directly:
- each side's edges are stepped exactly (an integer and a remainder,
  so nothing drifts) into a table of clipped columns;
- 68000 fills the rows from the two tables, for SET and XOR at either
  plane pair;
- OR and CLEAR use the C, which is also the twin.

Coverage follows the rectangle's rule, top and left edges in, bottom
and right out. Faces sharing an edge then tile with no seam, which
XOR needs, and a rectangle's corners fill exactly STDL_FillRect's
rectangle. The ops take a colour's planes, so a glenz draws each
face into a plane of its own.

Measured on a plain ST:
- a 160-row diamond XORed: 16.8ms, against 23.9 through
  STDL_XorHSpans;
- a 22-row triangle: 2.6ms against 2.3. Each edge's set-up is a
  divide, about 1000 cycles, so faces of a few rows are cheaper as
  spans, and the header and skill say so.

test_polygon checks random convex polygons against an exact rational
reference (every op, budgets 4/2/3, clips, origins, masks), plus
split polygons XORed seamlessly and the rectangle case.
tests/hatari/pgchk.c runs it on the machine; it passes, and a broken
XOR fails it. The new POLYDEMO example XORs three turning shapes into
three planes, its rotation through STDL_MulS16. Its own object, so
programs that never call it do not carry it.

events.title: Text: 8-pixel fonts on their own grid through movep
events.message:
Text: 8-pixel fonts on their own grid through movep

An 8-pixel glyph at x & 7 == 0 is one byte of each plane per row,
the bytes two apart, and movep.l reads or writes all four in one
instruction. stdl_glyph8_rows doubles the row out to a long mask and
merges with d ^= (d ^ c) & m. Its gain is less in the row than
around it: five asm operands where the general glyph rows take nine,
which gcc reloaded for every character. That overhead was about 135
instructions a character, measured with the profiler, against about
140 for the eight rows themselves.

STDL_DrawText takes it for a whole line when the font is 8 wide and
x is on the byte grid; glyphs cut by the clip still take the general
rows. STDL_DrawChar takes it for an uncut cell. Each lives in its own
out-of-line function, because as a test inside the general loop it
made unaligned text 5% slower through register allocation. Measured
on a plain ST, 8x8 font, colour 5:
- a 39-character line at x = 0: 13.9 -> 9.55ms;
- one character at x = 0: 552 -> 520us;
- STDL_DrawChar at x = 8: 497 -> 447us;
- unaligned text: +1-1.4%, the cost of the test that chooses.

The C twin works in plane words, since the host keeps them in its
own byte order. PIXCHK full passes on st, test_text_model included.

events.title: Fills: whole groups as rows of stores, four groups to a movem
events.message:
Fills: whole groups as rows of stores, four groups to a movem

A fill of whole groups that was not a full-width block went through
the edge-merge row loop. That loop read and rewrote the first and
last group of every row, about 100 cycles each where a store costs
24. fill_groups stores each row from its end down, four groups to a
movem.l of eight registers and the rest a group at a time, or at a
plane budget of 2 a long a group with planes 2-3 left alone. Full
rows still take the single memset or fill_longpairs.

The branch sits where fill_block was called for those fills, and
nowhere else. Written in ahead of the other paths, or moved out of
line with them, it changed fill_rows' register allocation and made
a 1x1 fill 2-3% dearer (148 instructions became 165). As it is, the
1x1 path is the same 148 instructions it was.

SPRCOST on a plain ST against the previous commit:
- 64x32 whole-group fills 0.54 (2031 -> 1089us);
- 16x16 0.87;
- unaligned fills and the 1x1 fixed cost unchanged;
- 86 cases 0.973, floor 1.002.
BLITCHK on an STE passes at every budget, and its CPU timing at
budget 2 goes 1330 -> 1260ms. PIXCHK full passes on st. Pixel-path

events.title: Dirty: restore by offset when the background is the page's shape
events.message:
Dirty: restore by offset when the background is the page's shape

STDL_DirtyRestore replayed each rectangle through STDL_BlitSurfaceEx.
That set-up clips both surfaces, asks the BLiTTER's rules and
dispatches on phase and masks, and it was most of the cost of a
sprite-sized restore. Restoring a page from a background of the same
size and stride, with no origins and no masks, a rectangle is an
offset into both, two edge masks and a run of whole groups. With no
BLiTTER and the default plane budget, DirtyRestore now does exactly
that:
- the rectangle is clipped to the page's clip;
- the edge groups are merged as longs;
- the rest goes through the asm row copy;
- nothing is rounded out.
Anything else takes the general path as before.

SPRCOST on a plain ST, 16 restores of 16x16:
- at group edges (a new case), 9.9 -> 6.3ms;
- at x & 15 = 5, 18.6 -> 14.9ms; the edges' merges, about 160 cycles
  a row each, are most of what is left.
Over all 86 cases 0.993 (floor 1.002). test_dirty compares the
direct path with STDL_BlitSurfaceEx byte for byte over random
rectangles and random page clips, and breaking its clip or its right
edge fails it.
