events.title: Music: play from memory, position, seek and register read-back
events.message:
Music: play from memory, position, seek and register read-back

STDL_MusicFromMemory plays an STM linked into the program in place,
so a demo can be one file. STDL_MusicFrame is the music's own clock
to sync to, STDL_MusicLength the range, and STDL_SeekMusic jumps
there. STDL_GetMusicRegisters copies out the stream's 14 registers
for VU meters without reading the chip.

The stream is delta-coded. A seek replays the deltas from the
nearest key, and the loader keeps a key every 256 frames: the frame's
offset and the registers before it. It then writes the whole state
to the chip, every voice rather than just what the next frame
changes. The keys replace an offset per frame, 4 bytes a frame (21KB
for a two-minute song), of which the player only ever used the
loop's.

Resuming after a pause now writes that state back too. Before, pause
silenced the voices, and a note held across it stayed silent until
the stream next changed it.

test_music replays a 700-frame stream alongside the player, checking:
- the clock;

events.title: Palette: STDL_StagePalette, and STDL_HW444 for constant tables
events.message:
Palette: STDL_StagePalette, and STDL_HW444 for constant tables

A palette written from the main loop lands wherever the beam is, and
that frame shows the old colours above it and the new below.
STDL_StagePalette(1) converts each change when it is made and writes
it in the next vertical blank. The changes it covers are
SetPalette, SetColours, the SDL shim and FadeTo. Measured in Hatari
with a colour switched at mid-screen every frame: 300 of 300 frames
split unstaged, 0 of 305 staged.

Overscan already staged its writes while a border was open. It now
shares the mechanism, in a new palstage.c, each user holding a bit,
so opening and closing a border no longer clears a program's own
staging. The pending flag drops before a stage is converted, so a
VBL landing midway cannot write half a palette, which the border's
copy could. release_hardware clears the hook with the VBL slots, so
staging reinstalls if the program inits again. STDL_SetColour stays
immediate for raster tricks.

STDL_HW444(0xRGB) converts a constant with four bits per channel to
the rotated hardware word at compile time; a raw 0xC72 shows green.

TPALETTE gains -stage. test_palette covers the staging cases (both
users, off writing what waits, a full queue, reinstall after release)
and HW444 against the run-time conversion.

events.title: Arithmetic: stdl_math.h, and the build fails on a new libgcc call
events.message:
Arithmetic: stdl_math.h, and the build fails on a new libgcc call

gcc 4.6 turns any multiply or divide it cannot prove 16-bit into a
__mulsi3 or __divsi3 call, and what it can prove moves with the code
around the expression. Measured, the calls come from mixed widths
(two bytes, s16 by int, s16 by u16), from a loop counter that ivopts
rewrites as a 32-bit variable whatever its casts, from every product
at -O1, from any divide or % by a non-power-of-two, and from a
difference of pointers to a 6-byte struct. On a plain ST a call costs
about 350 cycles against 40 for muls.w, and 630 against 140 for
divs.w (MATHCHK).

stdl_math.h makes the instructions public as STDL_MulS16,
STDL_MulU16, STDL_DivS16 and STDL_DivU16, inline asm with C twins.
It adds STDL_FixDiv, a 16.16 (a << 16) / b in two chained divu.w
(420 cycles against 630). test_math checks them against wide
arithmetic, and tests/hatari/mathchk.c runs the same cases on the
target and times them.

tools/libcalls.sh lists every libgcc arithmetic call per function
from the objects' relocations. With an allowlist it fails on any
that is new or more frequent. The cross build runs it as
libcallcheck against tests/libcalls.allow, where each of the 59
remaining sites says why it is not hot. Ports can run the same
script on their own objects.

Four per-frame sites are fixed:
- the music tick's volume scaling (u8 * u8);
- STDL_FrameLimit's 200 / fps;
- the ring pump's half offset;
- STDL_FadeTo, which spent 48 multiplies and 48 divides a step after
  the blank. It now works each step out before the blank and writes
  it straight after, with test_palette checking every step against
  the old formula.

The skill's profiler recipe gains a demo's Hatari findings:
- `symbols prg` loads the program's own symbols;
- a save must happen while profiling is on;
- the saved call graph carries per-function cycles, and is where the
  libgcc calls show up.

events.title: v0.2.7: external debugging with DeZog, a tape deck, assembler syntax colours
events.message:
v0.2.7: external debugging with DeZog, a tape deck, assembler syntax colours

### New: external debugging and code loading
Work in VS Code (or any editor) and let the emulator follow your build. Everything is off until you turn it on in *Settings → External debugging* or on the command line. The servers listen on `127.0.0.1` only.

- **GDB server** (`--gdb`, port 12000) for [DeZog](https://github.com/maziac/DeZog)'s `mame` remote: source-level debugging with breakpoints (conditional ones too), step into/over/out, pause and continue, watchpoints, and memory and register views and edits. DeZog's breakpoints also show in the emulator's Debugger window. Plain gdb clients work too, along with MAME's `monitor` commands.
- **Command API** (`--api`, port 6128) and the new **`cpcse-ctl`** program beside `cpcse.exe`, for build scripts. It can load a `.bin`, `.dsk`, `.sna`, `.cpr` or tape and run it, type on the keyboard, press keys, read and write memory and registers, set breakpoints and watchpoints, disassemble, step, wait for a stop, and take PNG or BMP screenshots. Requests are one line each, as JSON or a short form (`cpcse-ctl load build/game.bin 0x4000 entry`).
- **Auto-reload** (`--watch`): your build's output is loaded again and restarted every time it changes. That works for a `.bin`, or a `.dsk` with a command typed after it.
- **New command-line options:** `--gdb[=port]`, `--api[=port]`, `--load file[@addr]`, `--watch file[@addr]`, `--run entry|addr`, `--reset`, `--command "RUN\"GAME\n"` and `--symbols file`. Symbols can come from RASM, sjasmplus, pasmo or WinAPE files, or `EQU` lists, and addresses can be given as labels.
- **Documentation:** `docs/external-debugging.md` has a DeZog `launch.json`, a VS Code build task, and every option and command.

### New: tape deck
In the Media window, *Media → Tape* and *Debug → Chips → Tape*:
- a **tape counter** with a reset button
- the tape's time position, and which block it is in out of how many
- **rewind to the start, back a block, play, pause, stop, fast forward, eject**
- a list of the tape's blocks to jump to
- a MOTOR light

### New: assembler syntax colours
The assembler's editor colours each part of the code in its own colour: instructions, registers and conditions, directives, numbers, strings, comments, label definitions and the labels they use. **Colours...** lets you change each colour or switch the colouring off, and your choice is saved.

### New: Eject for cartridges and snapshots
Cartridges and snapshots now have an **Eject** button in the Media window and the Media menu, like discs and tapes. Ejecting restarts the same machine without it. The Snapshot section shows which snapshot is loaded.

### New: windows that fit when they're narrow
Rows of buttons, toolbars and text now wrap to the window's width in every window, so a narrow or docked window shows everything instead of cutting it off. This covers the Machine, Media, Settings, debugger, Chips, Memory, GFX9000, DSK editor, assembler, CSL and printer windows.

### New: GFX9000 VRAM image as the display shows it
*Debug → GFX9000 → VRAM image* now colours VRAM the way the picture does: each layer uses its own palette offset, sprite patterns use their sprite's palette, and transparent dots show the backdrop colour. In P1, **layers A and B are shown side by side**, and hovering over a dot shows which layer it belongs to.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.2.7.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. `cpcse-ctl.exe` and `docs/external-debugging.md` are in the zip too. On Linux, build from source (README, *Building from source → Linux*). The build includes `cpcse-ctl`. The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

events.title: fix(kmsdrm): GLES-first context ladder and runtime-matched ImGui GLSL (#2379)
events.message:
fix(kmsdrm): GLES-first context ladder and runtime-matched ImGui GLSL (#2379)

* fix(gui): pick the ImGui GLSL version from the runtime GL context

The backend's hardcoded desktop default (#version 130) does not compile
on GL 2.1 contexts, so opening the GUI with F12 while emulation ran
aborted with a shader-compile IM_ASSERT on Raspberry Pi 3 (vc4 via
KMSDRM, where the context ladder lands on its GL 2.1 Compatibility
tier). The startup GUI was unaffected because it renders through the
SDL renderer path; only the F12 re-entry routes ImGui through the
emulation GL context.

Derive the version from the live context instead: GL 2.x gets
"#version 120", GLES2 "#version 100", GLES3+ "#version 300 es", and
desktop GL >= 3.0 keeps the backend default (130/410, 150 on Apple).
The overlay's duplicated version detection now uses the same helper.

* fix(gfx): match SDL3's lowercase kmsdrm driver name and keep desktop GL as the KMSDRM ladder fallback

set_opengl_attributes() classified KMSDRM with a case-sensitive
strcmp(drv, "KMSDRM"), which never matches SDL3's lowercase "kmsdrm",
so KMSDRM silently walked the plain desktop ladder. Fixing the
comparison alone would regress RPi3: the ES-only ladder tier requests
GLES 3.0, vc4 only has GLES 2.0, and both attempts failing demoted the
monitor to the software renderer.

The ladder selection now lives in a pure, unit-tested table
(gl_context_ladder) with three profiles: Desktop (unchanged),
GlesPreferred (KMSDRM: ES 3.0 first, then desktop Core/Legacy tiers so
vc4 keeps hardware GL 2.1), and GlesOnly (Android/iOS/USE_GLES3,
unchanged strict ES ladder).

Legacy layout migration runs before logging_init() opens the log, so its
write_log() output was discarded and the log was then truncated. The
"Migration Review Needed" notice told users to check a log that held
nothing about the failure.

Buffer messages logged before logging_init() and replay them into the
log once it opens. The notice now names the log file path, or explains
how to enable logging when it is off.

* fix(log): re-arm startup log capture on every amiberry_main run

libretro can run amiberry_main() again via retro_load_game() without
reloading the core. Capture was disabled after the first logging_init(),
so a second run lost its migration messages again. Re-arm the capture at
the start of each run, and end it on the logging_init() restart path.

* fix(log): reopen a closed log and report when it cannot open

logging_init() skipped reopening the log on its third and later calls,
even when logging_cleanup() had already closed it after a libretro core
run. Only skip while the file is still open.

The migration notice pointed at the log file even when fopen() failed
and the buffered details were discarded. Say the log could not be opened
in that case.

events.title: feat(crash_detect): inframe_hang signature for absurd blits (#740)
events.message:
feat(crash_detect): inframe_hang signature for absurd blits (#740)

The blitter runs synchronously inside one register write, so a garbage
B_COUNT can keep retro_run from returning for hours -- the per-frame
watchdog never gets a turn and the frontend sees a hung core with no log
line. Check at blit dispatch (both engines, memo and compare paths):
when B_COUNT asks for more than 2^24 pixels, log [CRASH-DETECT]
inframe_hang with the counts, the command, A1 base and all three
processor PCs, then run the blit as before. Log-only, latched like the
other signatures, one multiply per blit.

Pixels are counted the way the accurate (default) engine runs them:
outer 0 = 65536 lines (JTRM BLIT_COUNT), inner 0 = one step (<= 64 px;
BlitterMidsummer2 stops on the bit-15 crossing). Counting inner 0 as
65536 per the JTRM flagged Troy Aikman, Double Dragon V and Brutal Sports
Football, which write B_COUNT=0 at boot and run fine.

Reproducers: Music Demo (ScatoLOGIC) --bios writes B_COUNT=$2710826D
(334M pixels) at frame 158; DEMO1 (bin) in HLE freezes at frame 400 on
the accurate engine.

The issue proposed sampling PCs in the JaguarExecuteNew slice loop. That
loop advances emulated time on every iteration, so the frame always ends
unless a single call inside it never returns -- and a sampler there never
runs during such a call. Every in-frame hang sampled (Music Demo, DEMO1,
DEMO1B, Painter) was inside BlitterMidsummer2.

cart_boot_matrix.sh now lists inframe_hang among a timed-out row's
signatures (cd_boot_matrix.sh already reports the first CRASH-DETECT line).

grm-rr5p: RUNTIME_SOURCE for loads of RAM cells nothing in the program stores to

StoredValueScanner.neverStoredTo: a load of a writable, non-volatile cell is

store targets it, no absolute-indexed store's base..base+$FF window covers it,

events.title: fix(display): correct smart horizontal centering offset (#2377)
events.message:
fix(display): correct smart horizontal centering offset (#2377)

* fix(display): correct smart horizontal centering offset

Compute the display window position from the line renderer's own pixel origin and use the correct sign and scaling for the offset. Keep the previous offset only when the whole window stays visible with it. Mirrors tonioni/WinUAE#518.

* fix(display): undo the line's centering shift when latching the origin

internal_pixel_start_cnt is latched after get_line() applied linetoscr_x_adjust, so on shifted lines it already contains the previous offset. Feeding it back into center_image() made offsets beyond the hysteresis alternate between frames (e.g. 9 and 49). Record the shift each line was drawn with and remove it; ignore lines whose origin never latched.

events.title: fix(native): zombies do not count as running; a stop waits for the leader's exit; unknown monitor output is an error
events.message:
fix(native): zombies do not count as running; a stop waits for the leader's exit; unknown monitor output is an error

In a container whose PID 1 never reaps, as GitHub's job containers, an
orphan stays a zombie, and kill(pid, 0) and kill(-group, 0) called it
running: stops waited out their grace period and then failed. On Linux the
supervisor now reads the state from /proc and treats Z and X as ended. A
group of zombies counts as gone before Node reports the leader's exit (macOS
too), so a stop now also waits for that exit: right after a c64_window move
the old VICE was still listed as running.

A profile or memory map that VICE prints in another form read as empty
(found on macOS); it is now an error that quotes the lines.

Tested: the process tests and the full live suite in a Debian 13 container
with tail -f /dev/null as PID 1 (448 pass, 50 skipped); full live suite
here, 498 of 498.

internal_pixel_start_cnt is latched after get_line() applied linetoscr_x_adjust, so on shifted lines it already contains the previous offset. events.title: fix(jit): handle shift counts 32-63 in ARM register shifts (#2376)
events.message:
fix(jit): handle shift counts 32-63 in ARM register shifts (#2376)

A 68k register shift count is taken modulo 64, but the ARM64 32-bit
variable shift uses the count modulo 32, and LSL_wwi/LSR_wwi encode only
five bits. With flags not needed, LSL/ASL Dx,Dy therefore kept bits it
should have shifted out: for .w, counts 32-47 left the low word
unchanged or partly shifted (VirusCheckerII crashed with a Line-A error).

- jnf_LSL_{b,w,l}_reg: shift in 64 bits, so every 6-bit count is exact;
  .l clears the upper half afterwards.
- jnf_LSL_l_reg, jnf_LSR_l_reg: the constant-count shortcut compared the
  register number with 31 instead of the count, so constant counts
  32-63 reached the immediate shifts and were encoded modulo 32.
- jff_LSR_l_imm: clear the result for counts 32 and above instead of
  encoding them modulo 32.
- jnf_LSL/LSR_{b,w}_imm: limit the count before folding a constant
  operand, which shifted a 32-bit value by up to 63 bits in C.
- jff_ASL_{w,l}_imm: CLS cannot exceed 31, so for constant counts of 32
  and above V was set even for a zero operand. V is now set when the
  operand is non-zero.

The ARM32 midfuncs had the same constant-count and folding mistakes and
get the same fixes; their register shifts already use eight count bits.

Fixes #2375

The whole workflow ran on two releases of Bruce Lee from corpus/, through
the MCP and every skill script.

  real 64 KiB image was refused. The listing parser accepts both.

events.title: fix(host): complete drive stops at the computer's next instruction (D22); fix Windows CI
events.message:
fix(host): complete drive stops at the computer's next instruction (D22); fix Windows CI

A drive 8 checkpoint makes VICE enter the monitor from inside the drive CPU,
with the computer's CPU halfway through an instruction, and makes drive 8
the text monitor's default device. A computer register write was then lost,
the first frame count ended one frame early, and load, disassemble, search,
memmap and the stopwatch acted on the drive. The session now runs the
computer to its next instruction after such a stop, and every
device-dependent text command selects the computer first.

The Windows CI job failed because the fake Ghidra installation in the test
had no analyzeHeadless.bat, which discovery looks for on Windows.

Tested: a new live regression test fails without the fix; full live suite
with real VICE and Ghidra, 489 of 489.

events.message:
grm-46ch: second-tier helper recognition crosses a proven-safe branch (megaman2 c78d)

findSecondTierHelpers no longer needs a straight-line [entry, relay) prefix.
New HelperDiscovery.inboundRegisterOrigin is a forward dataflow over every path
from the wrapper entry to the relay call, labelling A/X/Y by the inbound register
they hold (TAX/TAY/TXA/TYA relabel, other writes -> LOCAL, disagreeing joins ->
LOCAL). It declines on any call, terminal, computed jump, flow override,
mechanism write, undisassembled byte, or exit from the wrapper body. It subsumes
traceInboundRegisterOrigin and the zero-length-prefix special case.

FUN_c760 is one contiguous function; its BCC/JMP c783 is an internal diamond on
which X is never written, so it is now admitted.

megaman2 golden: c78d warning -> SECOND_TIER_ARGUMENT note; callers 91c4/91d7/
931b/932e resolve prg_bank=13 via FUN_c760; c7a0 moves mirroring.0 known ->
assumed, matching sibling restores c640/c71f (stale mirroring no longer leaks
through the now-modelled relay, same as grm-ylm6's c71f/c725/c743).

events.title: fix(input): map magic-mouse pointer against the presented crop (#2374)
events.message:
fix(input): map magic-mouse pointer against the presented crop (#2374)

Manual Crop and the full-window nominal crop present only a sub-rect of
the native surface, but getgfxoffset() fed the renderer's crop rect to
the pointer mapping only for Auto Crop. With a manual crop the guest
pointer moved at surface/crop speed and lost the crop offset, drifting
away from the host cursor.

Map every native frame against the source rect the renderer actually
presents, clamped exactly as the presenters clamp it, and share one
render_quad-to-source formula between the OpenGL, Vulkan and SDL
renderers. Vulkan previously applied the letterbox offset unscaled (and
with the wrong sign on RTG); the SDL renderer assumed a 1:1 logical to
source scale, which is wrong under any crop stretch or NTSC 6:5
correction.

Fixes #2367

events.title: fix(crash_detect): cd_seek_wedge only while the drive still owes data (#741)
events.message:
fix(crash_detect): cd_seek_wedge only while the drive still owes data (#741)

cd_seek_wedge counted every frame with frozen FIFO drains. Under
cd_boot_mode=bios it fired 15 times across Baldies, Battle Morph,
BrainDead 13, Highlander, Primal Rage and Myst (+ both Myst demos), all of
which go on to run: the transfer had simply finished.

Measured at each fire (temporary dump, not committed): BUTCH low byte $02
every time -- the game's CD ISR clears the master interrupt enable to
signal completion. Philia (bios) ends its transfer the other way, leaving
BUTCH $03 but clearing I2CNTRL bit 2 (FIFO data enable) while it waits for
a button (it responds to B). The real IMASK-stuck transfer wedge
(7c98e16 re-broken behind an env flag as a control) has both still on:
BUTCH $03, I2CNTRL $05. fifoDataReady / cdPlaying do not separate them --
both are 1 in the false fires and in the wedge -- so the issue's proposed
"FIFO idle" test would not have worked.

A frame now counts only if a seek is outstanding (seek_starts !=
seek_dones), or the transfer is still open: BUTCH bits 0+1 armed AND
I2CNTRL bit 2 set. The predicate is CrashDetectCDSeekWedgeFrame(), pinned
by test/test_crash_detect_cd_wedge (measured rows from both sides, runs
in make test). test/tools/cd_seek_wedge_regress.sh checks the 8 titles
against the private corpus (SKIPs without it) and asserts on the log line,
not [PASS] -- test_cd_bios_boot reports [PASS] on the real wedge too.

Controls on the final code: Primal Rage and BrainDead 13 with the
delay-slot fix disabled still fire (butch_int=$03 i2s_ctrl=$05).

The log line now prints butch_int= and i2s_ctrl=.

events.title: feat(892): EasyFlash 3 cartridge
events.message:
feat(892): EasyFlash 3 cartridge

CRT type 90 (mnemonics ef3/easyflash3): one 8 MB MX29LV640EB, eight slots of 64
banks, the $DE00-$DE0F registers, the cartridge lines and boot flag from $DE02,
the IO2 RAM, the $DE0F mode register (EF with/without reset, off; modes 2/4/5/6
act as off and are reported notEmulated), generated resets (8 PHI2 cycles, then a
warm reset the cartridge knows is its own), and the Menu/Reset/Special buttons:
RPC cart/button, monitor `cart button`, FFI cartButton; a cartridge without
buttons refuses by name.

The chip gets non-uniform sectors (8 KB boot blocks + 127 x 64 KB), a 24-byte
erase mask and DQ7/DQ6 polling during a program; values from the Macronix
MX29LV640E T/B datasheet rev 1.7. State rides checkpoints and .c64re (ef3State),
the flash is the writable image, savecrt writes a type-90 CRT in the CHIP layout.

ef3_gate: one test per acceptance item, including skoe's boot menu built from his
sources and his MX29LV640EB EAPI driver run unchanged.

feat(host): heartbeat between clients and the Host Runtime (D18)

A half-open connection (container network, sleep) or a hung client kept its
VICE session forever. After ready the client now pings every 10 s; the host
closes a connection that sends nothing for 30 s, with its session and
emulator, and the client fails a silent host like a closed one. TCP keepalive
on both ends. Protocol version 2, so mixed releases fail the handshake.

VICE itself is never pinged: any monitor command stops its CPU.

events.title: Address Copilot review: stale fallback on reset, negative in_ptr accepted
events.message:
Address Copilot review: stale fallback on reset, negative in_ptr accepted

resource_write only kept HostCtx::resources (the live store's cache)
coherent with a successful write, not WasmRuntime::resources (the
load-time snapshot reset() falls back to when a reopen fails). A file
that became unreadable after a successful write would resurrect the
pre-write bytes on reset, the opposite of the point of reopening.
Fall back to the live store's cache instead.

checked_wasm_window clamps a negative ptr to 0 rather than rejecting
it, so resource_write(..., in_ptr=-1, len=1) silently read from
address 0 instead of returning RESOURCE_WRITE_BAD_PTR. Reject a
negative in_ptr explicitly before calling the shared helper (left
unchanged, since its other callers don't use the clamped value).

Both covered by new test cases: a reset after a successful write with
the backing file removed still sees the written byte, and a negative
in_ptr returns RESOURCE_WRITE_BAD_PTR without touching the file.

feat(host): DXA adapter for dxa.analyze

dxa runs with -a dump, all NMOS opcodes and skip-scanning, so only reachable

labels (not authoritative) and the listing as an attachment.

events.title: fix(blitter): fast phrase-mode Gouraud lane order and Z saturation (#793)
events.message:
fix(blitter): fast phrase-mode Gouraud lane order and Z saturation (#793)

The JTRM p.81-82 worked example (jtrm_gourz_strip) exposed two fast-path
bugs in phrase-mode computed data:

- Lane order. Fast started every strip at lane 0, the right-most pixel
  (z_i[0]/gd_i[0] come from bits 15-0), whatever the pixel's x, and
  advanced only the lane it had just drawn. Hardware picks the lane by
  position -- lane 3 is the left-most pixel (JTRM v8 p.130-131; netlist
  BLITGPU Dec4 maps B_Z0-Z3/B_I0-I3 to lanes 0-3) -- and adds the
  increment to all four lanes once per phrase write. Phrase mode now
  selects lane 3 - (x & 3) per pixel and advances all lanes when a pixel
  ends its phrase. Pixel mode is unchanged.
- Z saturation. z_i wrapped; JTRM p.81 says Z saturates like intensity.

Fast-vs-accurate per-blit disagreement, test_blitter_compare on in-game
states: Cybermorph 155,314 -> 0, I-War 11,315 -> 0; AvP, Doom, Super
Burnout, Checkered Flag, Tempest 2000 BIOS boot unchanged at 0; Hover
Strike unchanged at 1.

jtrm_gourz_strip now runs under both engines. The fast golden rows of
gourd_single/gourd_second, which recorded the old reversed lane order
as a known divergence, now equal the accurate rows.

events.title: fix(blitter): accurate computed Z writes the seed first, then adds ZINC (#791)
events.message:
fix(blitter): accurate computed Z writes the seed first, then adds ZINC (#791)

* fix(blitter): accurate computed Z writes the seed first, then adds ZINC

The accurate engine ran the GOURZ ADDARRAY before forming srcz, so the
first pixel of every computed-Z strip got seed + ZINC and every Z was
one step ahead. The blitter netlist (jag_sim) says otherwise: in the
dzwrite state zpipe[0] latches srcz into srczp on atick[0] (INNER.NET,
the 15/10/92 "move zpipe[0] up a tick" fix), Srcz1add lands on
atick[1] (DCONTROL.NET), and the Z write data Srczo is srczp one stage
later (DATA.NET). The value compared and written is the pre-add one,
which is also how the JTRM v8 p.81-82 worked example seeds a strip.
Move the add after srcz is formed so it feeds the next write.

The fast engine already had this order. With #790 the two engines now
agree on PolyEngine: 0 of 268,258 blits differ, frames identical.

Under Accurate the Z buffers of GOURZ titles shift by one step but no
displayed frame changed across 12 in-game savestates and Hover Strike
attract (Cybermorph/I-War run ~596k/~407k GOURZ blits there).

New test_blitter_cmd vector gourz_seed_first (hand-derived, both
engines) fails on the old accurate path.

Closes #789

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(blitter): JTRM p.81-82 phrase-mode Gouraud Z strip vector

Copilot review on #791: gourz_seed_first covers pixel mode with uniform

events.title: Trace the boxed poster into a vector map without its grid
events.message:
Trace the boxed poster into a vector map without its grid

tools/trace_poster.py redraws iso/map.jpg as assets/box/map.svg
(viewBox 0 0 2656 976, cells at x = 48 + 80c, y = 80 + 40r, as
assets/box/map.png places them).

Geometry: poster_image.grid_lines seeds each rule; every rule is then
traced along its length in the photo, rules that bend away from both
neighbours are replaced, and a Coons-patch lattice (4 points per cell
edge) follows the traced rules between crossings.  A robust B-spline
displacement field, fitted to where the warped rules actually land,
refines the lattice twice.

Grid removal: each warped rule's centre is found by a Viterbi path held
near the cell edge, so a trunk or branch beside the rule is not taken for
it.  The rule's cross-section is divided out of the ink (ink composes as
1 - ink = (1 - rule)(1 - drawing)); strokes crossing it are bridged from
the band edges, preferring straight crossings; stretches where the core
stays dark past the longest dash keep their ink, since a drawn line runs
along the rule there.  The horizontal fold crease is removed the same way.

Drawing: the cleaned ink, normalised by its local peak so faint thin
lines trace at their half-height width, is outline-traced (marching
squares, Douglas-Peucker) into one even-odd filled path.  Specks, marks
lying wholly on a rule, and grainy shadowed paper are dropped.  Outline
tracing was chosen over centreline tracing so ladders, trunk shading,
houses and the title keep their printed weights and shapes.

Redrawn from tools/trace_poster.json: frame, credits box, spirit-limit
box and title underline as straight rules; grund labels (Cinzel), item
names, credits and copyright (Jost, added with its OFL), and the
spirit-limit table and BTR mark (Michroma), each line fitted to its
measured ink extent on a straight baseline; erase boxes for the redrawn
lettering and the empty margins and right-hand columns.  The title, TM,
legend icons and grund tick marks are traced.

python3 tools/trace_poster.py regenerates the SVG byte for byte;
--preview DIR renders full.png and compare.png through Chromium.

events.title: Repaint the paper map only while it is showing
events.message:
Repaint the paper map only while it is showing

Saul saw a 300-400 ms freeze at every screen change on his phone, fine
on desktop and new since a few days.  Diagnosed by a Fable
investigation: since 4a69cfa the frame loop repaints the paper map
whenever the visited path or room changes, open or not, and drawMap
re-renders every visited room in software and rebuilds the grid.  The
cost grows with rooms seen, so fresh test sessions showed nothing.
With 250 visited rooms at 4x CPU throttle, each room change was a
220-236 ms long task; with this change it is an ordinary 17 ms frame.

paintPaperMap now returns unless the desk shows the map; opening the
map already resets the key and paints fresh.  Opening the map late in a
long session still costs one full drawMap; making it incremental
(cache each room's thumbnail) is a separate follow-up.

events.title: Add resource_write: a capability-gated import for WASM board plugins
events.message:
Add resource_write: a capability-gated import for WASM board plugins

resource_len/resource_read already let a board plugin read a manifest-
configured file resource; there was no way to write one back. Boards
that need to persist changes to external media (e.g. a virtual disk
image) had no path to do so.

Add WasmCaps::resource_write (opt-in per board, same pattern as dma/
net/host_sockets) and a resource_write(name, off, buf, len) import
gated on it -- an ungranted module fails instantiation rather than
silently no-opping. Writes address a resource by its manifest name
only, never an arbitrary path, matching resource_read's existing
boundary. Write-through to disk per call; HostCtx now retains each
resource's source path so there's somewhere to write to, and reset
reopens resources so a cold reset doesn't resurrect pre-write bytes --
consistent with file resources already being documented as live
external state outside the save-state/replay guarantee.

Covered by three new tests: capability gating fails instantiation
(not a silent no-op), persisted writes round-trip through a fresh
read and survive a reset, and out-of-range/bad-pointer/missing-file
cases return negative error codes without faulting the board.

events.title: feat: add an SAA5050 character-rounding upscaler
events.message:
feat: add an SAA5050 character-rounding upscaler

A new WebGL upscaler (scaling mode 6) applies the Mullard SAA5050's
character rounding to any machine's output. Each source line becomes two
half-lines and, where two lit pixels meet diagonally, the half-dot between
them is filled; "lit" is the brighter of the two colours. Output pixels that
cover both half-lines (1x) blend them for anti-aliasing; from 2x each half-line
is its own row, at any integer scale.

Checked in headless Chromium against Saa5050.characterRounding: 0 of 9600
pixels differ for 20 glyphs at 2x; 1x blends and 4x is crisp.

With the upscaler selected the BBC supplies the plain teletext dots (Saa5050
.rounding off, one line per glyph row) in the 1x layout at every scale, and
the display does the rounding. The Display pane applies settings on change so
machines see the selection.

fix: show the BBC hi-res layout at half the display scale

The hi-res layout has two buffer lines per scanline, but it was displayed at
the full UI scale, so 2x looked like 4x of the normal picture (and Mode 1 at

the descriptor's screen geometry carries it so the TEXT overlay stays aligned.
The hi-res layout is used at even scales from 2 so the halving is pixel-exact;
odd scales keep the 1x layout at an integer multiple.

events.title: feat: add BBC Micro Model B (#31)
events.message:
feat: add BBC Micro Model B (#31)

* feat: add BBC Micro Model B (WD1770 DFS, Mode 7)

New 6502-based machine: the BBC Micro Model B. Boots the real MOS 1.2 /
BASIC 2 ROMs to the Mode 7 banner and BASIC prompt, with the Acorn 1770 DFS.

Commodity cores:
- m6502: cycle-counted NMOS 6502 (official + stable undocumented opcodes).
- m6522: 6522 VIA (timers, IFR/IER, ports, CA1/CA2/CB1/CB2 handshakes).
- saa5050: teletext generator with character rounding, emitting the doubled
  12x20 cell the BBC's video hardware produces.

Machine (src/machines/bbc/):
- 32K RAM, OS/BASIC ROMs, 16 sideways sockets and the ROMSEL latch.
- Sheila IO decode: CRTC, Video ULA, ROMSEL, System/User VIA, 1770 DFS, Tube.
- IC32 addressable latch; keyboard matrix + option links (boot mode selection);
  column-based CA2 for the MOS's scan.
- Mode 7 (480x500) rendering plus a generic bitmap path for modes 0-6.
- Acorn 1770 DFS interface, .ssd/.dsd codec and disk service, DFS ROM loaded
  through prepare().

Also adds the m6502 debug family (disassembler + DebugService), registry /
model / menu registration, and unit tests for the CPU, VIA, SAA5050, SSD
codec, IO decode and Mode 7 rendering.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): character-based keyboard layout and SN76489 sound

- Route printable keys by the character they produce (event.key) so the BBC's
  own layout types correctly on a PC: its shifted symbols differ (e.g. '*' is
  Shift on the ':' key, not Shift+8; the number row is `! " # $ % & ' ( )`).
  Letters stay positional; the host's physical Shift is no longer mapped, so a
  shifted host key presses the BBC key that actually yields that character.
- Drive the SN76489 from System VIA port A writes (gated by IC32 latch bit 0)
  through the shared AudioMixer, with the anti-alias strategy read from the
  Sound panel, and expose the PSG activity LED.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): hardware-pane DFS toggle, on-screen keyboard, palette/charset

- Hardware pane: fit/remove the Acorn 1770 DFS interface. The DFS ROM is
  fitted at build time, so toggling rebuilds the machine; the drive service
  hides its drives while the interface is absent.
- On-screen skeuomorphic keyboard (red function strip plus the QWERTY deck)
  driving matrix cells directly, with live key highlighting; BREAK resets.
- Display pane gains a 'bbc' palette family (PAL / Measured), and the Memory
  pane a 'bbc' ASCII glyph table (pound sign at 0x60).

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): render modes 0-6 with the cell-major layout and ULA palette

Modes 1-6 rendered as garbage. The hi-res display memory is cell-major, not
linear: one 6845 MA unit is a byte-wide column of eight scanlines, so the byte
for a cell is (MA << 3) | RA and the row address advances by R1. The renderer
now follows the beebwiki address-translation formula, including the IC32 C0/C1
hardware-scroll wrap when the address overruns the top of RAM.

The ULA palette register's logical-colour field also depends on the mode's
colour count (2, 4 or 16), which follows the chars-per-line and clock bits.
Decoding it by the top nibble alone mapped the foreground to black on the
2-colour modes, so modes 0, 3, 4 and 6 came out blank.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): decode multi-bpp bitmap pixels with the ULA's bit interleave

The video ULA interleaves pixel bits across a display byte rather than
packing them contiguously: the top `bpp` bits hold the most-significant
bit of each of the `n` pixels in the byte, then the next group, and so
on. Reading contiguous bit pairs split every logical-1 pixel in modes 1,
2 and 5 into an alternating 1/2 (red/green) pair, corrupting the image.

Decode pixels with the interleave and add regression tests for the 2bpp
(0b01100101 -> 0,3,2,1) and 4bpp (0b10001001 -> 10,1) cases.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(debug): stop repeating PC/SP in the generic register panel

GenericRegisters renders the whole RegisterSnapshot.regs list and then a
separate PC/SP line, but the Z80 and 6502 family services both list SP and
PC among their registers, so every non-Z80 machine (the BBC's 6502, the
CPC's Z80 uses its bespoke panel) showed each of them twice. Filter PC/SP
out of the listed registers — the dedicated line already draws them.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): selectable disc system (8271/1770/none) and sideways ROM pane

Replace the Acorn 1770 on/off checkbox with a "Disk system" dropdown
offering None, the original Acorn DFS (Intel 8271) and the Acorn 1770 DFS,
and expose the Model B's sixteen sideways ROM sockets in the ROM pane.

- Add an Intel 8271 FDC core (command/parameter/result phases at FE80-FE84,
  data-register DRQ handshake, NMI on completion, DskImage-backed) plus the
  Acorn 8271 peripheral. Semantics cross-checked against BeebEm's
  disc8271.cpp: the interrupt is asserted only for Seek/Read/Write/Verify/
  Format/ReadID (never for READ DRIVE STATUS or READ SPECIAL REGISTER), the
  drive-status result is 0x80|drive1|drive0|track0|wp, and "sector not found"
  is 0x1E.
- Fit the DNFS ROM (Acorn DFS 1.20 + NFS 3.60) for the 8271 option; mirror an
  8K sideways ROM across both halves of its 16K socket.
- Route the floppy window (FE80-FE87) to whichever controller is fitted; the
  disk service and the frame probe go through a common BbcDiscController, and
  the Drive pane hides the drives when no interface is present.
- Decode the whole 0xFE20-0xFE2F Video ULA window (A0 selects control vs
  palette): Acorn DFS probes 0xFE28/0xFE29 with a write/read-back.
- ROM pane: new SidewaysRomSlot SPI. The BBC exposes all sixteen sockets (13
  = disc interface ROM, 15 = BASIC); the shell persists per-socket overrides
  in IndexedDB and applies them at build time, and the pane renders them.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): give the 8271 a delayed command completion (busy phase)

BeebEm's 8271 holds BUSY for a short interval (SetTrigger) after a command
finishes, only then raising the result and the interrupt — it does not
complete the instant the last parameter is written. Model that: a completed
command enters a BUSY phase with a queued result that a cycle countdown
applies.

- Add `tick(cycles)` to BbcDiscController; the machine drives it at the
  1 MHz disc clock from the per-instruction VIA tick (the WD179x has no such
  timer, so its tick is a no-op).
- The 8271 queues the result/idle transition and holds BUSY (0x80) for
  COMPLETION_CYCLES before delivering it. Seek/Read/Write/Verify/Format/ReadID
  use the delay; READ DRIVE STATUS / READ SPECIAL REGISTER still return a
  result immediately and without interrupting, and SPECIFY / WRITE SPECIAL
  REGISTER finish immediately.
- Extend the core tests with a `done()` helper that advances the disc clock.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): Mode 7 OCR overlay, BASIC listing, 5.25" drive sound

The BBC was missing the two pull-on-demand UI features every other machine
has, plus two smaller nits.

- Add a Mode 7 screen-text OCR engine (src/ocr/bbc.ts): the teletext field
  is read straight from the 40x25 SAA5050 codes rather than recognised from
  pixels, mirroring the renderer's MA-to-address mapping and its
  colour/mosaic state machine. Wired as the frame probe's transcribe driver
  (blanking matched cells to their paper colour) and as the machine's
  ocrScreenForMcp, so both the TEXT overlay and the MCP ocr tool work.
  Bitmap modes 0-6 are not transcribed yet (they would need the OS font).
- Add a BASIC II detokeniser (src/basic/bbc-basic-parser.ts) and expose it
  through the probe's basicListing, so the BASIC Listing pane fills in.
- Publish the 5.25" floppy-sound profile — BBC DFS drives are 5.25" units.
- Make the "Disk system" hardware row span both columns (as the Ace's does).

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): BASIC variables pane, aligned like the register panels

Add parseBbcBasicVariables(): BBC BASIC II keeps variables in a heap indexed
by a first-character chain table at &0480, plus a separate resident-integer
block (A%-Z%) and a fixed FOR-control stack at &0500. Decode number (float
and integer), string, array and live for-next variables and wire the result
through the frame probe's basicVars.

Reformat the BASIC Variables pane into two aligned columns (name, value) so
the "=" lines up down the pane, like the Z80 register panel, instead of the
ragged `name = value` text.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): transfer 8271 data one byte per disc-clock interval

BeebEm drives the 8271 data register off a per-byte timer
(TIMEBETWEENBYTES): each byte is offered a fixed interval apart and
re-raises the interrupt. Our core delivered a whole sector the instant a
read/write command started, so the Acorn DFS's per-byte NMI handler ran an
arbitrary number of times and its byte counter (READNO) barely advanced —
the DFS then read far past the end of the disc and aborted with a
"Disk fault 1E at 50/00".

Arm a byte countdown on the 1 MHz disc clock: beginRead/Write queue the
first byte, `tick` offers each subsequent byte (re-raising DRQ) and
completes once the last is serviced. The DNFS now boots a disc — the
Plotmate Welcome Disk's !BOOT runs — instead of faulting.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): drive the Acorn 1770 from NMI and fix its control latch

Make the Model B 1770 DFS work end to end:

- The Acorn 1770 interface wires DRQ and command completion to the CPU's
  NMI line; Acorn DFS 2.26 transfers each sector byte from an NMI handler,
  so give WD179x an optional onInterrupt with a per-byte cadence on the
  1 MHz disc clock plus completion edges for Type I/II/III commands (and
  for commands that fail before transferring). BbcMachine wires it to
  cpu.nmi(); the polled hosts (+D, Beta Disk, Einstein) are unchanged.
- The drive-control latch at &FE80 is write-only and floats high. The DFS
  presence probe reads it and requires a bit set, so stop echoing the
  written value (it previously concluded no controller was fitted and the
  machine fell back to the ROM/tape filing system).
- Drive select is bit 1 = drive 1 (not a binary number) and reset is
  active low.
- List the disc-interface and language (BASIC) ROMs first in the ROM pane.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* test(bbc): cover a read across a track boundary on the 1770

Pin the Citadel 2 loading case: its CitBits file runs from LBA 137 to
142, so the DFS reads track 13 sector 9, STEPs onto track 14 and then
reads sectors 0-2. The test drives the peripheral the way the DFS does,
including waiting for the completion edge on the 1 MHz disc clock before
issuing the STEP (otherwise the still-busy controller drops it).

* fix(bbc): disc boot, sound, bitmap-mode OCR, border and keyboard

Discs
- Default to no keyboard links (*FX255 = &FF): a plain BREAK no longer

- Loading a disc into drive 0 performs a SHIFT+BREAK auto-boot, and the

events.title: fix: make the CPC CAS READ trap replace the read, not the setup
events.message:
fix: make the CPC CAS READ trap replace the read, not the setup

The instant-load trap hooked the routine at os464 0x2873 / os6128 0x29E3
and resumed at entry+0x0D, treating it as the block reader. It is only
the shared read/write/verify setup (stash sync, motor on, PPI setup,
RET): the bit-level read happens back in CAS READ (0x2836 / 0x29A6)
after it returns. So after each instant-loaded block the firmware went
on to pulse-read the NEXT block into the same buffer against a stale
sync byte; on the 464 that surfaced as "Read error a" (1942 at block
21, 180, 10th Frame), and only ever worked on the 6128 by accident.

Now the CAS READ entry, its shared sync/record-read block and teardown
tail are located by signature scan (identical shape in os464/664/6128).
The request (A/HL/DE) is captured at the entry, the firmware's own setup
runs, and at the record-read block the CRC-checked block is delivered
and control resumes at the teardown with the reader's success result
(A=0, C+Z). Only fires while the lower ROM is paged at 0x0000.

With the trap on, every CAS READ now returns the same result and bytes
as pulse loading on 464, 664 and 6128 (1942, 180, 10th Frame, 1943,
2048, 3D Starstrike), and whole files (data too) instant-load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: model the Z80 CTC daisy-chain in-service latch and RETI unwind
events.message:
fix: model the Z80 CTC daisy-chain in-service latch and RETI unwind

The CTC cleared a channel's pending interrupt on acknowledge with no
interrupt-under-service tracking, so an ISR that re-enabled interrupts
before RETI could be re-entered by the same or a lower-priority channel,
or by a device further down the daisy chain.

Per the Zilog CTC manual, acknowledge now sets the channel's IUS latch;
while it is set that channel and every lower one are inhibited (a higher
channel may still nest), and a new ieo getter reports the CTC's IEO for
downstream devices. reti() clears the highest-priority channel under
service. The Einstein and MTX wire Z80.onReti to it, and the Einstein's
keyboard/ADC/fire and 256 VDP interrupts wait for the CTC's IEO. RETN
does not unwind the chain. Also drops the per-instruction closure from
interruptPending.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat: notify daisy-chain peripherals when the Z80 executes RETI
events.message:
feat: notify daisy-chain peripherals when the Z80 executes RETI

Add an optional Z80.onReti hook, called after ED 4D (RETI) executes.
Zilog-family IM 2 peripherals decode RETI on the bus to clear their
interrupt-under-service latch; the ED 45 RETN and its ED x5/xD mirrors
do not trigger it. The check sits only on the RETI/RETN path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: test: add a headless CPC 6128 boot and AMSDOS save/cat smoke test
events.message:
test: add a headless CPC 6128 boot and AMSDOS save/cat smoke test

Boots the 6128 firmware through the real frame loop, checks the sign-on
banner and frame length, then saves a BASIC file to a blank Data-format
disk and finds it in CAT. Skipped when the firmware ROMs are not cached
in mcp/.cache.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: feat: stretch CPC Z80 bus cycles to the gate array's 1us wait-state grid
events.message:
feat: stretch CPC Z80 bus cycles to the gate array's 1us wait-state grid

The CPC gate array holds /WAIT low for 3 of every 4 CPU clocks, so each
Z80 memory, I/O and interrupt-acknowledge cycle waits until its WAIT
sample lands on the one free clock of the microsecond. Internal cycles are
never stretched. Model that in the CPC's memory/port hooks (memory cycles
start on phase 0, I/O on phase 3, INT ack on phase 2) and on the Multiface
NMI, which gives the published CPC NOP timings: PUSH 4, EX (SP),HL 6,
OUT (C),r 4, LDIR 6/5, CPI 4, IM 1 ack 5 (4 after an instruction ending in
internal cycles), IM 2 ack 7, HALT 1 per re-fetch.

Frames now also start where the previous one was scheduled to end, so the
last instruction's overshoot no longer lengthens every frame and line
boundaries stay on the microsecond grid.

The Z80 core is untouched, so other machines keep identical timing.
Table-driven tests check every main/CB/ED/DD/FD/DDCB/FDCB opcode against
Caprice32's CPC cycle tables and the CPCWiki microsecond table.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat: LOAD and SAVE on the ZX80 through ROM traps
events.message:
feat: LOAD and SAVE on the ZX80 through ROM traps

Extend the cassette traps to the ZX80 ROM: SAVE ($01B7, after it drops
the command's return) records $4000 up to E_LINE, and LOAD ($0207, and
the bit wait at $0222) reads the next program there, both resuming at
$0283 as the ROM's LOAD/SAVE end test does. A SAVEd program is left
unplayed so a following LOAD reads it back, as after rewinding.

events.title: fix: drop the .tap suffix from the Saved tape menu entry
events.message:
fix: drop the .tap suffix from the Saved tape menu entry

The MSX now offers its BIOS-saved cassette through the same Save entry,
but downloads it as .cas; the machine picks the filename, so the label
should not promise a format.

events.title: fix: clock MTX CTC channel 0 on VDP /INT edges, not every frame
events.message:
fix: clock MTX CTC channel 0 on VDP /INT edges, not every frame

The VDP's /INT is a level (F AND IE) on CTC channel 0's trigger input,
but the CTC was triggered every frame F and IE were set, even when F was
never cleared. Sample the line where F or IE can change (frame flag,
status read, control write) and trigger only when it asserts, so a
pending F gives one edge and enabling IE over a set F gives one.

events.title: feat: save MSX cassette output through TAPOON/TAPOUT traps
events.message:
feat: save MSX cassette output through TAPOON/TAPOUT traps

CSAVE/BSAVE/SAVE to CAS: now record. The BIOS TAPOON and TAPOUT entry
points are trapped (with the BIOS paged in) to build a .cas stream:
each block starts with the 8-byte sync ID on an 8-byte boundary, then
its bytes. The Save menu offers the result as a .cas download; it is
cleared on reset.

events.message:
fix: strobe the MTX SN76489 from its port 6 latch on a port 3 read

OUT (6) wrote straight to the SN76489. On the MTX it only fills a latch;
a read of port 3 strobes the latched byte into the chip (MAME mtx.cpp
sound_lach_w / sound_strobe_r). Port 3 still reads back 0x03.

events.message:
fix: fire debugger memory and port watchpoints on the Lynx

The Lynx bus hooks never consulted the watchpoint lists, so memory and
port watchpoints were silently ignored. Check them in read8/write8 and
the port handlers (only while any are set) and stop the frame on the
instruction that trips one, as the Spectrum does.

events.title: fix: sound the MSX key click from PPI port C bit 7
events.message:
fix: sound the MSX key click from PPI port C bit 7

The mixer's 1-bit path was fed a constant 0 with zero gain, so the BIOS
key click was silent. Port C bit 7 now drives it, mixed under the PSG.

events.title: fix: size standard DSK sector data by the Track-Info N
events.message:
fix: size standard DSK sector data by the Track-Info N

Standard (MV - CPC) tracks were laid out using each sector's own ID N, so
a sector whose ID claims another size desynced every following sector's
data. The CPCEMU format stores every sector of a standard track at the
Track-Info sector size (0x14); only EXTENDED records per-sector lengths.
Use the Track-Info N, falling back to per-sector N only when that N is
evidently unset (the sector sizes exactly fill the track and it doesn't).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix: run the Lynx 128K Z80 at 6MHz
events.message:
fix: run the Lynx 128K Z80 at 6MHz

MAME camplynx.cpp clocks the 48K/96K Z80 at 24MHz/6 = 4MHz but the 128K
at 24MHz/4 = 6MHz; every model ran at 4MHz. The clock is now per model
and drives the frame length (divided across the CRTC's lines), the tape
pulse scale and the audio mixer.

events.message:
fix: clear MSX 8255 output latches on a mode-set write

Any 8255 mode-set control word resets the output latches, so a write
to 0xAB with bit 7 set now returns the slot select (port A) and port C
to 0 instead of being ignored.

events.message:
fix: limit the Lynx 48K/96K cassette input to keyboard line 0

With the motor running the tape level replaced bit 0 of every keyboard
line, not just line 0 (MAME camplynx.cpp port80_r), so keys in column 0
of lines 1-9 read as the tape signal during loads.

events.message:
fix: resume MCP-loaded .z80/.szx snapshots at their saved frame position

The MCP loader bypassed the snapshot service, so .z80 v3 and SZX loads
still fired an interrupt immediately instead of tpf - offset T-states
later. Call resumeAtFrameOffset as the service does.

events.title: feat: add ASCII8, ASCII16 and Konami MSX mega-ROM mappers
events.message:
feat: add ASCII8, ASCII16 and Konami MSX mega-ROM mappers

Cartridges over 64KB (or 64KB with an AB header) now bank-switch
through the ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami or Konami SCC mapper. The mapper is
guessed with openMSX's heuristic of counting LD (nnnn),A stores to each
mapper's register addresses. Banks reset on machine reset, and the
memory-map pane shows the chosen mapper. SCC sound is not modelled.

events.title: feat: read zip64 archives
events.message:
feat: read zip64 archives

A Zip64 archive stores an all-ones entry count and central-directory offset
in the classic EOCD, so the parser walked nothing and silently returned no
entries. Follow the Zip64 EOCD locator to the Zip64 EOCD record for the real
count and offset, and take overflowed per-entry sizes and local header
offsets from the Zip64 extended-information extra field.

events.title: fix: overlay the PCW keyboard matrix on block 3 reads
events.message:
fix: overlay the PCW keyboard matrix on block 3 reads

The gate array presents the keyboard at &3FF0-&3FFF of block 3 as a
read-side overlay (MAME pcw.cpp installs a read handler there); writes
reach the RAM underneath. The matrix was instead copied into RAM six
times a frame, clobbering anything software stored there. Reads now see
the live matrix; the per-tick scan only flips the heartbeat bit.

events.title: fix: re-encode HFE tracks re-formatted in the emulator on save
events.message:
fix: re-encode HFE tracks re-formatted in the emulator on save

serializeHFE only patched data fields into the retained cells by index,
so a track formatted in the emulator (new IDs, sizes or sector count), or
a cylinder/side the image never had, was saved with its old layout or
dropped. When a side's decoded IDs no longer match the image, MFM-encode
the track afresh (gaps, syncs, marks, CRCs, keeping deleted marks and
deliberate bad CRCs). The patch path now also rewrites a data mark that a
write changed and lays a good CRC over a rewritten bad-CRC field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix: classify .z80 hardware modes per the WoS spec
events.message:
fix: classify .z80 hardware modes per the WoS spec

v3 hwMode 11 (Didaktik), 14 (TC2048), 15 (TC2068) and 128 (TS2068) are
48K-class but were treated as 128K. Decode the byte-37 'modify hardware'
flag (48K->16K, 128K->+2, +3->+2A) into a sourceModel, and save hwMode
13 for the +2A, 12 for the +2 and the modify flag for the 16K instead of
writing 7 (+3) for every 4-ROM machine.

events.title: fix: decode legacy zip entry names as cp437
events.message:
fix: decode legacy zip entry names as cp437

Entry names without the UTF-8 flag are IBM code page 437 per the ZIP
APPNOTE, but they were decoded with TextDecoder('ascii'), which the WHATWG
encoding standard maps to windows-1252. Accented and box-drawing names came
out wrong. Decode them through a CP437 table instead.

events.title: fix: swap Jupiter Ace ArrowUp/ArrowDown to SHIFT+6/SHIFT+7
events.message:
fix: swap Jupiter Ace ArrowUp/ArrowDown to SHIFT+6/SHIFT+7

On the Ace SHIFT+6 is cursor up and SHIFT+7 down (the reverse of the
Spectrum), as the on-screen legends and the ROM agree: booting it,

fix: type Jupiter Ace symbols with SYMBOL SHIFT, not SHIFT

Host characters ! @ # $ % & ' ( ) _ and " were sent as SHIFT + key, which

fix: skip encrypted zip entries instead of failing the archive

An encrypted entry (general-purpose flag bit 0) was handed to inflate as if
it were plain deflate data, which threw and lost every other entry in the

fix: pulse the PCW 300Hz timer interrupt for 100us

The gate array pulses /INT for about 100us (MAME pcw.cpp) instead of
holding it until the CPU responds, so a tick that lands while

fix: decode HFE sectors whose data field straddles the index

decodeHfeTrack stopped scanning at the end of the revolution, so an ID
field near the end whose data field lay past the index lost its sector.
The track is circular: while an ID is pending, keep scanning past the
index for its data mark (up to a gap-2-sized window), stopping if the
track's first ID comes round first.

events.title: fix: place MSX cartridges by their AB header
events.message:
fix: place MSX cartridges by their AB header

Plain cartridge images are now laid out where their header says, using
openMSX's RomPlain location vote: a 48KB image with its header at file
offset 0x4000 maps at 0x0000-0xBFFF, and BASIC cartridges (TEXT in page

mega-ROM mappers need, and the memory-map pane labels only the pages the
cartridge actually decodes.

events.title: fix: list microdrive print files and all no-autorun programs
events.message:
fix: list microdrive print files and all no-autorun programs

The MDR listing treated RECFLG bit 2 as "record in use", but on the IF1 that
bit is reset for PRINT/OPEN# data files, so those files vanished from the
listing. Judge occupancy by RECLEN instead, and don't parse a SAVE* header
out of a PRINT file's raw data. Also treat any autostart line with bit 15
set as no auto-run, not just exactly 0x8000.

events.title: fix: scale tape pulses to the 128K-class CPU clock
events.message:
fix: scale tape pulses to the 128K-class CPU clock

TZX/TAP pulse lengths are T-states of a 3.5MHz reference clock, but the
128K/+2/+2A/+3 run at 3.5469MHz and the Spectrum deck left pulseScale at
1, so tapes played ~1.3% fast. Set pulseScale = cpuClock / 3.5MHz as the
other machines do (still exactly 1 on the 48K).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix: merge SCP revolutions by full sector ID and good-CRC reads
events.message:
fix: merge SCP revolutions by full sector ID and good-CRC reads

mergeRevolutions grouped readings by R alone, folding distinct sectors
that share an R into one fake weak sector, and flagged a sector weak
whenever any revolution differed - including a plain bad-CRC misread of a
sound sector. Key readings on C/H/R/N plus occurrence within the
revolution, and judge weakness only among good-CRC readings when any
exist; a sector bad on every revolution still gets its differing readings
as weak copies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: carry leftover tape t-states across block boundaries
events.message:
fix: carry leftover tape t-states across block boundaries

When a pulse, direct-recording sample or pause finished partway through an
advance() step, the overshoot was discarded: beginBlock zeroed the pulse
clock and an expired pause's negative remainder was dropped, so every block
boundary stretched the tape by up to one step. advance() now feeds the step
through consecutive elements and blocks, carrying each overshoot into the
next. A data block with no pause now starts the next block on its last edge
instead of via a zero-length pause.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix: rebase the Spectrum tape advance point when the deck restarts
events.message:
fix: rebase the Spectrum tape advance point when the deck restarts

When the loader detector auto-starts the tape mid-frame, or the tape
service plays/resumes it, tapeLastAdvanceT still pointed at the frame
top, so the deck was handed every T-state since then (tens of pilot
edges) in one go. Add Spectrum.resetTapeAdvance and call it on restart,
as the Jupiter Ace and Lynx already do.

events.message:
test: update the emulator Spectrum stub for snapshot frame resume

The stub lacked contention.timing and resumeAtFrameOffset (used by the
snapshot service since frame-position resume), and its +2A-origin SZX
mock needs sourceHas1FFD now that 128K-origin snapshots are remapped.

events.message:
fix: end WD179x multi-sector writes in record not found

A multi-sector WRITE SECTOR that ran out of sectors ended with a clean
status, unlike the read path. The controller keeps searching for R+1 and,
not finding it, terminates with RECORD NOT FOUND; do the same for writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
