events.title: fix: raise the Jupiter Ace frame interrupt after the active display
events.message:
fix: raise the Jupiter Ace frame interrupt after the active display

The ULA asserted /INT at line 0 and then drew scanlines 0-191, so the
ROM's frame work raced the beam. MAME raises the IRQ at scanline 248,
directly below its display window: assert the 8-line /INT pulse once the
192 active lines are done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: treat PCW port &F6 as the roller RAM start entry
events.message:
fix: treat PCW port &F6 as the roller RAM start entry

&F6 selects which roller RAM entry scan line 0 reads, walking 256
entries and wrapping within the 512-byte table (MAME pcw_v.cpp). It was
modelled as a raster shift of the picture inside the border, so screens
scrolled through &F6 showed the wrong lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: disable WD179x side compare on the WD1770/1772
events.message:
fix: disable WD179x side compare on the WD1770/1772

Type II bits 1 and 3 were always taken as side-compare enable/select. Only
the FD1791/1793 compare sides; on the 1770/1772 those bits are write
precomp and spin-up disable, so a +D command with them set could
fail RNF on a valid sector. Side compare now defaults on for the 1793
(NOT READY) parts and off for the 1770/1772 (MOTOR ON) parts, with an
explicit sideCompare option to override.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: flush the beam before shadow-screen changes
events.message:
fix: flush the beam before shadow-screen changes

The beam was only flushed for ULA-port OUTs and writes to 0x4000-0x5AFF,
so a 7FFD bit-3 screen flip, or writes into the displayed bank through
0xC000 (bank 7 while shown, or bank 5 aliased there), rewrote pixels the
beam had already passed. Track which slots map the displayed bank
(SpectrumMemory.slotIsScreen) and flush before those writes and before
a screen flip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: keep the last edge's level for 1ms when a pause block follows
events.message:
fix: keep the last edge's level for 1ms when a pause block follows

A Pause block (and a Direct Recording's own pause) forced the level low the
moment it began, so the final edge of a preceding pulse sequence, tone, CSW
or zero-pause data block lasted zero time. TZX 1.20 requires at least 1ms of
that level before the pause goes low, and a pause always ends low. Route every
pause through one helper that holds the level for 1ms (or the whole pause,
if shorter) and then drops it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: let WD179x verify match any ID field on the track
events.message:
fix: let WD179x verify match any ID field on the track

Verify compared only the first sector's cylinder with the track
register, failing a track whose first ID happened to differ. The
controller reads ID fields until one matches TR with a good CRC; do that,
and set CRC ERROR alongside the seek error when only bad-CRC IDs match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat: LOAD and SAVE on the ZX81 through ROM traps
events.message:
feat: LOAD and SAVE on the ZX81 through ROM traps

Trap the ROM's LOAD ($0347, and IN-NAME $0366 while it waits for a
signal) and SAVE ($02FB) after NAME has parsed the filename, and move the
.p image (VERSN up to E_LINE) directly, resuming at SLOW/FAST as the
ROM's LOAD/SAVE end test does. Mounted programs form a tape: LOAD ""
reads the next one, LOAD "NAME" winds to a matching name, SAVE records
onto it, and a program mounted while LOAD waits is played into it
instead of resetting, so multi-part programs load. Traps are enabled
only for ROMs carrying the standard routines. ZX80 is not trapped yet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: decode CPC FDC ports on A7=0 and ignore status-port writes
events.message:
fix: decode CPC FDC ports on A7=0 and ignore status-port writes

The FDC is selected by A10=0 and A7=0; A7 was unchecked, so OUT &F8FF
(expansion peripheral reset) switched the drive motor. A write to the
read-only main status port &FB7E was also fed to the data register.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: report the last sprite checked in TMS9918A S0 bits 0-4
events.message:
fix: report the last sprite checked in TMS9918A S0 bits 0-4

With no fifth sprite on a line, S0's sprite-number field now holds the
last sprite examined (the Y=0xD0 terminator, else 31) instead of stale
data, per the TMS9918A data manual.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: leave CPC FDC ports unanswered on the 464 and GX4000
events.message:
fix: leave CPC FDC ports unanswered on the 464 and GX4000

Without a disk interface the uPD765A is not on the bus, so reads of
&FB7E/&FB7F float to 0xFF and motor/data writes do nothing. The port
decode ignored config.hasFDC.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: make WD179x SEEK step relative to the track register
events.message:
fix: make WD179x SEEK step relative to the track register

SEEK set the head to the data register value outright. The datasheet has
the controller step, updating TR, until TR equals DR, so the head moves
DR - TR tracks from its real position. Model that (clamped at the track-0
stop, and setting the step direction), which keeps a STEP-without-u
TR/head desync intact across a seek.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: resume SZX/.z80 snapshots at their saved frame position
events.message:
fix: resume SZX/.z80 snapshots at their saved frame position

SZX dwCyclesStart (and the .z80 v3 T-state counter) record how far into
the frame the snapshot was taken, but runFrame rebased the frame to the
load point and fired an INT immediately. Add Spectrum.resumeAtFrameOffset
so the first frame starts in the past and the next INT lands
tpf - offset later (INT taken at once only inside the INT window). Load
and save the .z80 v3 T-state counter, and save the frame offset relative
to the current frame's INT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: hold the last tape edge for 1ms before a pause drops low
events.message:
fix: hold the last tape edge for 1ms before a pause drops low

After a data block the deck dropped the level low 945 T-states (a 3.5MHz
figure scaled by pulseScale) into the pause. TZX 1.20 requires at least 1ms
of the opposite level before the signal goes low. Hold for 1ms of real time,
derived from the CPU clock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: ignore RAM banking commands on the 64K CPC 464/664
events.message:
fix: ignore RAM banking commands on the 64K CPC 464/664

The 464 and 664 have no banking PAL, so Gate Array &C0-&FF commands
must leave the base 64K mapped 0-1-2-3. Configs wrapped modulo four
instead, remapping e.g. config 3 to banks 0-3-2-3.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: return a centred reading from the Einstein TC-01 ADC
events.message:
fix: return a centred reading from the Einstein TC-01 ADC

Port 0x38 (ADC0844, mirrored to 0x3F) returned 0xFF, a stick pinned to
one extreme. With no analogue joystick attached it now converts a
centred input (0x80).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: size uPD765A formatted data fields by the command N
events.message:
fix: size uPD765A formatted data fields by the command N

FORMAT TRACK sized each sector's data by the N in its CPU-supplied ID
tuple. The datasheet writes every data field at the command's N; the
tuple's N only goes into the ID field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: decode Einstein port mirrors as MAME's I/O map does
events.message:
fix: decode Einstein port mirrors as MAME's I/O map does

The TC-01 VDP decodes only A0 (0x0A-0x0F mirror data/control), the
WD1770 and AY ignore A2 (0x1C-0x1F and 0x06/0x07 mirror), the 8251
decodes A0, and any access to 0x00/0x01 (and mirrors) resets the PSG,
returning its port A to input.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat: load Plus ASIC state from the v3 SNA "CPC+" chunk
events.message:
feat: load Plus ASIC state from the v3 SNA "CPC+" chunk

Parse the standard CPC+ chunk written by WinAPE and other v3 emulators:
sprite bitmaps and attributes, palette, PRI/split/scroll/vector, DMA
channel registers and internals, RMR2 and the ASIC lock state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: hold a seek-end interrupt per drive on the uPD765A
events.message:
fix: hold a seek-end interrupt per drive on the uPD765A

A single ST0/PCN latch meant a seek on one drive overwrote another's
pending result, so seeking two drives returned only the last one. Keep
the seek-end status per unit and have each Sense Interrupt Status hand
back one drive's result until none remain; INT stays up while any is
pending.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: resume the tape after a tzx stop-the-tape block
events.message:
fix: resume the tape after a tzx stop-the-tape block

A zero-length Pause (or Stop-if-48K on a 48K machine) parked the deck idle
with playing still true. Every resume path only clears paused, and advance()
returned immediately while idle, so the tape stalled forever. The deck now
remembers it was stopped and, once unpaused, starts the block after the stop.
A stop found by the ROM-trap peek parks the deck the same way, so resuming
no longer replays the stop a second time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat: model Einstein keyboard, ADC and fire interrupts
events.message:
feat: model Einstein keyboard, ADC and fire interrupts

Ports 0x20/0x21/0x25 now mask the keyboard, ADC and fire interrupt
sources (bit0 set = disabled, all masked at reset). A 50Hz scan raises
the keyboard request for a key down on a selected line and the fire
request for a held button; an ADC0844 conversion raises INTR ~40us after
a write to 0x38. They follow the CTC on the daisy chain in MAME's order
(keyboard, ADC, fire) with IM 2 vectors 0xF7/0xFB/0xFD. Reading 0x20
clears the keyboard request and reading 0x38 the ADC's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: report the datasheet CHRN when an MT transfer runs off EOT on head 1
events.message:
fix: report the datasheet CHRN when an MT transfer runs off EOT on head 1

With MT=1 the result after the second head reached EOT was the last
sector's own CHRN. The uPD765A result table gives C+1, H complemented and
R=01 for MT=1 HD=1 at EOT; apply it. A TC landing on that last sector
still rewrites the result to the sector transferred, now restoring H too.
The TC CHRN convention itself and MT=1 on a single-sided image are left
as documented.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: restore Gate Array interrupt state from v3 CPC snapshots
events.message:
fix: restore Gate Array interrupt state from v3 CPC snapshots

Load and save the v3 header's GA vsync-delay counter (0xB2), 52-line
interrupt counter (0xB3) and pending-interrupt flag (0xB4), and write
the CRTC type (0xA4). CRTC counters stay unrestored: the frame loop
restarts the raster each host frame.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat: play tzx 0x19 generalized data blocks
events.message:
feat: play tzx 0x19 generalized data blocks

The parser skipped Generalized Data Blocks, so tapes that use them loaded
nothing. Decode them per TZX 1.20 - pilot/sync symbol table with its
run-length stream, bit-packed data symbols, and the per-symbol edge / no-edge
/ force-low / force-high flags - and expand them into the deck's existing
pulse-sequence, set-level and pause blocks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: honour DTL as the transfer length when the uPD765A command N is 0
events.message:
fix: honour DTL as the transfer length when the uPD765A command N is 0

cmdBuf[8] (DTL) was never read. The datasheet makes DTL the data length
when N is 0: read and write only DTL bytes of the 128-byte sector, with
the controller zero-filling the rest of a written data field. DTL of 0 or
above 128 transfers the whole sector.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: mask CRTC registers to their implemented widths
events.message:
fix: mask CRTC registers to their implemented widths

R4/R6/R7/R10 are 7-bit, R5/R9/R11 5-bit and R12/R14 6-bit on the 6845;
types 1/2 have a fixed 16-line VSYNC (no R3 high nibble) and cannot read
back R12/R13. The .SNA loader now restores R0-R15 through the write path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: model the +2A/+3 gate array floating bus
events.message:
fix: model the +2A/+3 gate array floating bus

The +2A/+3 is not fully pulled up: ports of the form 0000 xxxx xxxx xx01
return the byte the gate array last fetched from screen memory (latched
through the idle half of each 8T fetch block, 0xFF in the border), but
only while 7FFD paging is unlocked. Other unattached ports (e.g. 0xFF)
still read 0xFF.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: show ZX81 FAST-mode picture while the ROM runs the display
events.message:
fix: show ZX81 FAST-mode picture while the ROM runs the display

FAST mode was blanked whenever CDFLAG bit 7 was clear, so the screen
stayed empty even while the ROM ran its display loop awaiting a key or
in PAUSE. Blank only frames in which no opcode was fetched from the
display echo.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: compare CRTC row/raster counters to R4/R9 for equality
events.message:
fix: compare CRTC row/raster counters to R4/R9 for equality

The 6845 ends a character row when RA equals R9 and a frame when VCC
equals R4. The >= compares ended them early when a register was written
below the live counter; now RA runs on to 31 and VCC to 127 and wrap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: drive Einstein CTC CLK/TRG0-2 from the 2MHz clock
events.message:
fix: drive Einstein CTC CLK/TRG0-2 from the 2MHz clock

Channels 0-2's trigger pins are fed the 2MHz system clock (MAME's
ctc_trigger_callback), so counter-mode channels and trigger-started
timers now advance. Edges are delivered in bulk through a new
Z80Ctc.triggerEdges to keep the run loop cheap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat: decode z-rle compressed csw blocks in tzx files
events.message:
feat: decode z-rle compressed csw blocks in tzx files

A TZX 0x18 CSW Recording may store its pulse stream Z-RLE (zlib-compressed
RLE), and the parser threw on it. The TZX parser is synchronous and called
synchronously by every machine, so add a small synchronous zlib/DEFLATE
decoder under media/tape and inflate the stream inline, capped at five bytes
per declared pulse.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: update the data mark and CRC state when the uPD765A writes a sector
events.message:
fix: update the data mark and CRC state when the uPD765A writes a sector

A write replaced the sector bytes but kept the stored ST1/ST2, so WRITE
DATA over a deleted sector still read back as deleted, WRITE DELETED DATA
left a normal mark, and a rewritten bad-CRC sector stayed bad (and weak).
The write lays down a new mark and a good data CRC: set or clear the
deleted mark per command and drop DD/DE and MD/MA. Write results also no
longer report CM for a mark the write overwrote rather than read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: start CPC VSYNC on the R7 line and clock the GA at HSYNC end
events.message:
fix: start CPC VSYNC on the R7 line and clock the GA at HSYNC end

The CRTC tested VSYNC onset after drawing the (R7, RA=0) scanline, so
PPI port B bit 0 read 0 throughout it and the Gate Array's post-VSYNC
re-sync fired on the 3rd HSYNC instead of the 2nd. Onset is now tested
on entry to each scanline. The frame loop also clocks the Gate Array at
the CRTC HSYNC trailing edge (R2 + width characters in) rather than at
the end of the line, drawing the display portion just before it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: latch Spectrum border colour on 8-pixel boundaries
events.message:
fix: latch Spectrum border colour on 8-pixel boundaries

The ULA / gate array samples the border colour once per 8-pixel (4T)
character period, so border OUTs take effect on character boundaries,
not at 2px/1T resolution. Floor the high-accuracy renderer's beam
position to a multiple of 8 pixels (aligned with the display cells).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: test: cover 128K-origin snapshots in the +2A snapshot service
events.message:
test: cover 128K-origin snapshots in the +2A snapshot service

Mark the +2A-origin SZX mock as sourceHas1FFD and add a .sp case: a
128K snapshot's 7FFD bit 4 must page ROM 3 (48K BASIC) on a +2A.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: drive ZX81/ZX80 INT from refresh address bit 6
events.message:
fix: drive ZX81/ZX80 INT from refresh address bit 6

/INT is wired to A6, so it goes low when the M1 refresh address (R) has
bit 6 clear. The ROM loads R so each display scanline lasts 207T however
short the row; raising INT as soon as a row HALTed made collapsed 1K
display files run ~66% fast (FRAMES advanced 166 per 100 frames, now 101).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: match sector C and H as well as R in uPD765A ID searches
events.message:
fix: match sector C and H as well as R in uPD765A ID searches

The sector search looked up R alone through sectorMap, so a sector with the
right R but a different cylinder or head was read, and on duplicate-R
tracks the first R always won. The controller compares its ID register
against each ID field: search for C, H and R together (H complemented on
the MT side-1 pass), report No Data with ST2 WC/BC when the track's IDs
carry another cylinder, and write back into the exact sector found. N stays
uncompared so the undersized protection-sector handling keeps working.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: defer Z80 CTC time-constant reloads and honour timer trigger
events.message:
fix: defer Z80 CTC time-constant reloads and honour timer trigger

A time constant written to a running channel now waits for the current
count to reach zero, as the Zilog manual specifies; only the first load
after a reset starts the channel. Timer-mode channels with control bit 3
set now wait for a CLK/TRG edge before timing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: skip unknown and deprecated tzx blocks instead of rejecting the tape
events.message:
fix: skip unknown and deprecated tzx blocks instead of rejecting the tape

Since TZX 1.10 every block ID the spec does not define is followed by a
DWORD length so readers can step over it. The parser threw on any unknown
ID, refusing otherwise-playable tapes. Skip unknown blocks by that length,
and skip the deprecated 0x16/0x17 (DWORD length), 0x34 (8 bytes) and 0x40
(24-bit length) blocks by their documented sizes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: skip 0/1-byte tap blocks instead of truncating the tape
events.message:
fix: skip 0/1-byte tap blocks instead of truncating the tape

A TAP block shorter than 2 bytes cannot carry a flag and checksum, but its
length field is still valid framing. The parser stopped reading at the first
such block, silently dropping every block after it. Step over its bytes and
continue instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: test: cover SN76489 counter continuity and period-0 handling
events.message:
test: cover SN76489 counter continuity and period-0 handling

Adds the regression tests missing from the previous SN76489 commit and
repairs two comment em-dashes that were written in the wrong encoding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: report missing address mark for unformatted tracks on a ready drive
events.message:
fix: report missing address mark for unformatted tracks on a ready drive

Read/write/Read ID/Read Track on a missing, out-of-range or empty track
returned ST0 NR (0x48) even with a disk in the drive. NR means the drive is
not ready; a ready drive that never sees an ID address mark within two
index pulses ends with IC=01 and ST1 MA. Keep NR for an empty drive only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: page the 48K ROM for 128K snapshots loaded on a +2A/+3
events.message:
fix: page the 48K ROM for 128K snapshots loaded on a +2A/+3

128K/+2 snapshots (.sna, .sp, .z80 non-+3 hwModes, .szx 128K/+2 IDs) carry
no 0x1FFD. Their 7FFD bit 4 selects the 48K BASIC ROM, which on the 4-ROM
+2A/+3 is page 3 and needs 1FFD bit 2 too; loading paged the +3 syntax ROM
1 instead. Mirror 7FFD bit 4 into 1FFD bit 2 via a new
SpectrumMemory.selectSnapshot128KRom (analogue of selectSnapshot48KRom).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: use the full data-bus byte as the IM 2 vector
events.message:
fix: use the full data-bus byte as the IM 2 vector

interruptWithVector() forced bit 0 of the vector low, but the Z80 builds
the IM 2 table address from I and the whole byte on the bus; even vectors
are only a convention of Zilog peripherals. All current callers (CTC,
PIO/AMX, CPC ASIC, Einstein VDP) already supply even vectors, so they are
unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: Record the seven cross-vendor review passes over the detailed animal models
events.message:
Record the seven cross-vendor review passes over the detailed animal models

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix: keep SN76489 tone counters running across period writes
events.message:
fix: keep SN76489 tone counters running across period writes

Writing a tone period no longer reloads the divider: the running count
finishes and the new period is picked up at the next zero, as on the
real chip. The discrete TI part now treats period 0 as 0x400 like the
MTX model; only Sega's integrated PSG holds periods 0/1 constant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: apply M1 wait states to interrupt acknowledge cycles
events.message:
fix: apply M1 wait states to interrupt acknowledge cycles

The INT acknowledge (M1 + IORQ) and the NMI response are M1 cycles, so
board WAIT logic keyed on /M1 stretches them just like an opcode fetch.
m1WaitStates (MSX: +1T) was only added to opcode, prefix and HALT
fetches; now IM 0/1/2 acknowledges and NMI include it too, and
interrupt() reports the stretched length.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: load the flat memory dump in v3 CPC snapshots
events.message:
fix: load the flat memory dump in v3 CPC snapshots

A v3 .SNA still carries the flat dump sized by header bytes 0x6B-0x6C;
chunks (MEMn, device state) follow it. The loader parsed chunks from
0x100, so v3 files with a flat dump loaded no RAM. MEMn blocks beyond a
64K machine's RAM no longer alias onto base RAM.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: format head 1 onto a new side instead of overwriting side 0
events.message:
fix: format head 1 onto a new side instead of overwriting side 0

FORMAT TRACK with HDS=1 on a single-sided image clamped the side index to
0 and replaced the side-0 track. A double-sided drive writes head 1 to the
other surface, so grow the image to two sides and store the track there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix: reset P/V when an interrupt follows LD A,I or LD A,R

On NMOS Z80s the IFF2 copy into P/V made by LD A,I / LD A,R is lost if a
maskable interrupt is accepted immediately afterwards: the flag reads 0
even though IFF2 was 1. Latch that the previous instruction was one of
these and clear PF when interrupt() accepts right after it.

events.title: fix: contend the accessed HL during CPIR/INIR repeat cycles
events.message:
fix: contend the accessed HL during CPIR/INIR repeat cycles

The 5 internal T-states of a repeating CPIR/CPDR/INIR/INDR keep the
address of the memory access that preceded them on the bus (WoS
contention tables: hl:1x5); HL is stepped afterwards. The core had
already incremented/decremented HL, so it probed HL+/-1. Latch the
address before stepping, as LDIR already does for DE.

events.title: fix: mix ULA EAR and MIC as weighted speaker levels
events.message:
fix: mix ULA EAR and MIC as weighted speaker levels

The ULA drives the speaker from bit 4 (EAR) and bit 3 (MIC) through
different resistor paths, so the pin voltage is a weighted sum (Issue 3:
0.39/0.73/3.66/3.79V), not an OR. The 48K ROM BEEPER holds MIC=1 and
toggles EAR, so the OR was a constant 1 and BEEP/key click were silent.
Feed the mixer a normalised level via a new AudioMixer.accumulateLevel.

The old code waited for a fresh R44 write, dropping byte one and

events.title: fix(tape): don't restart the machine when mounting a tape
events.message:
fix(tape): don't restart the machine when mounting a tape

The Spectrum and CPC tape mounts each bracketed themselves in
stop()/start(). The pair is unnecessary -- parsing allocates and mountBlocks
swaps the list in one synchronous step, so the frame loop has nothing to trip
over, which is why the disk mounts shed theirs in d65ed23 -- and both
also ran start() on the failure path. Since the shell returns early on !ok
without unpausing, a tape that would not parse quietly restarted a machine
the user had deliberately paused.

Drop them, as the Jupiter Ace's mount already did. Resuming after a
successful mount stays the shell's decision; it already calls unpause() for
tape targets.

The CPC's cartridge path keeps its pair: inserting a .CPR power-cycles the
machine, so that one is doing real work.

events.title: Camputers Lynx: 48K, 96K and 128K, with cassette, floppy and keyboard (#28)
events.message:
Camputers Lynx: 48K, 96K and 128K, with cassette, floppy and keyboard (#28)

* Camputers Lynx 48K, 96K and 128K support

An eighth machine: a Z80A at 4MHz with a Motorola 6845 sequencing the
raster over three one-bit colour planes. All three models boot their real
ROMs to the BASIC prompt and take keyboard input.

Banking is the unusual part, and there are two schemes. A write lands in
every enabled bank at once, and a read comes from whichever bank the
decode selects, as one of a handful of fixed eight-page layouts. The
48K/96K take that on port 0x7F with two bits of port 0x80 joining in; the
128K moves it to port 0x82 with both nibbles bit-reversed and swapped end
for end, adds a fourth RAM bank, and drops port 0x80 from the decode.
Their write paths differ too: the 48K/96K video banks leave A13 and A15
out of the decode, so one store lands at four addresses, while the 128K
decodes in full.

Video follows from that. Each board keeps its planes elsewhere and steps
rasters by its own stride, and the 128K programs the 6845 for 64 columns
rather than 32 - so it is 512 pixels across, with pixels half as wide.
Rows are counted from the CRTC display region rather than a fixed border,
and the frame takes its line count from the 6845 with the interrupt
driven off VSYNC.

The keyboard has no select register: the line number rides in A8-A11 of a
read at port 0x80, so the port decode takes the whole 16-bit address.

Tape and disk are not fitted yet - the media service says so rather than
mounting something that would not load - so the 96K and 128K do not claim
built-in drives, though their FD1793 answers the bus.

Verified headless against the hosted ROM sets: all three reach the prompt,
draw their sign-on, and echo typed keys.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01USAgYedo5mR5nC7pur8DQa

* Lynx cassette support, and put the Lynx in the model menu

Two things, one of which should never have shipped.

The Lynx was registered but had no entry in the model menu, so it could
not be selected at all - the machine booted, passed every test, and was
unreachable. MODEL_LABELS is exhaustive over MachineModel so the compiler
catches a missing label, but a missing menu entry was invisible. The menu
now lives in its own module beside the pane, held against the registry by
a test that fails if a registered model cannot be reached, or the menu
offers one the registry does not have.

Cassettes now load. Lynx .tap shares an extension with the ZX Spectrum's
and nothing else: no length prefixes and no checksums, just entries whose
size is implied by a type letter and a 16-bit field inside them, with the
leader tones left out of the file entirely. The parser puts the leader and
sync byte back and hands the shared pulse deck a pure-data block per entry,
because on the wire each byte is eight bits MSB first with no start or stop
bit, and a bit is one square-wave cycle whose width alone says which bit it
is. The 128K runs its tape at twice the speed, so its cells are half as
wide. Sizes and encoding are MAME's camplynx_cas.cpp, checked against the
TOSEC images.

The transport needs none of the CPC's cadence guessing: the Lynx has a
real motor relay on port 0x80, so the deck runs when the ROM spins it. The
deck is advanced on each cassette read rather than once a frame, since the
ROM measures the gap between edges and has to see the level at the T-state
of the read. A Spectrum .tap is refused by name rather than played as noise.

Verified by loading real software end to end on the 48K: Lynx Invaders,
3D Monster Craze, Gobble de Spook, Mazeman, Mined Out and Deathball all
load from tape and run, in colour, through to gameplay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01USAgYedo5mR5nC7pur8DQa

* The Lynx Save menu offered saves it cannot produce

The Save menu was keyed to a coarse 'spectrum'/'cpc'/'vdp' family, so the
Lynx declared 'spectrum' and offered .szx/.z80 and .scr entries despite
having no snapshot or screen-dump service. Replace the family with a
per-machine list of entries (SaveMenuItem[]), so a machine names exactly
what it can write. The Lynx now lists Screenshot (.png) and RAM (.bin); the
raw .bin dump is universal, backed by LynxMemory.ramSnapshot() (256K on the
48K/96K, 320K on the 128K, matching MAME's RAM device). A capability test
holds every declared entry against the service that must honour it, and
requires every machine to offer .bin.

Non-square pixels (pixelAspectX < 1 — Lynx 128K, CPC, Einstein-256) are
squeezed by the CSS box. With image-rendering: pixelated, the compositor's
2:1 nearest-neighbour downscale dropped every other source pixel at 1x
(missing columns); 2x was unaffected because each source pixel is then two
backing pixels. Let the compositor filter that axis instead — vertical is
always 1:1, so nothing else changes.

* Lynx tape display, turbo loading, and reload restore

The Lynx's .tap name entry and typed data entry now carry their file
identity, so the tape pane lists them as a Spectrum-style load line
(BASIC / CODE) and pairs the name header with the data block that follows.

Turbo while loading now engages on the Lynx. The machine has a real motor
relay, so the loading signal is the motor plus cassette-port reads rather
than the CPC's read-cadence guess; a 25-frame cooldown rides out the gap
between blocks, and the frame probe drives the TURBO lamp.

A model switch rewinds a tape carried across to its first block.

The persisted-model whitelist is now derived from the registry. It had been
hand-listed and omitted lynx48/96/128, so an F5 reload rejected the saved
model, cleared it, and fell back to the Spectrum.

* The Lynx tape pane listed a file's data entry twice

Format-tagged tape blocks (the Lynx's quoted name entry and its typed data
entry) showed the same file line on both the name header and the data child,
so uncombining them produced two copies of `LOAD "NAME"`.

Uncombined, the data child now lists as the raw `Data N bytes` entry — the
same header/data split the Spectrum's TAP blocks use. Combined, it still
hides behind its name header.

* Lynx floppy disks: .ldf raw dumps on the 96K and 128K

The FD1793 and its DOS ROM were already wired, but the machine had no disk
service, so the Drive pane never appeared and .ldf images were refused. Add
the missing pieces:

- media/floppy/ldf-image.ts parses, serializes and blanks the headerless
  Lynx dump: 512-byte sectors, 10 a track, cylinder-major with heads
  interleaved. 200K is 40 tracks single sided, 800K 80 tracks double sided
  (MAME's camplynx_dsk.cpp).
- LynxDiskService drives the two internal units.
- LynxMediaService mounts .ldf into A: or B: on disk models and still refuses
  it on the 48K.
- The descriptor now claims builtinDisk (so the Drive pane and floppy sound
  appear), adds the dsk LED and persists disks; the Drive pane offers blank
  Lynx disks instead of the +3 DSK/HFE set.
- The frame probe ticks the FDC (format latch, latch decay) and feeds the
  drive-sound fields.
- The DOS ROM is exposed as the Memory pane's `rom-dos` region.

* Lynx: the DOS ROM gets its own socket, and an FD1793 toggle

The DOS ROM was the fourth entry of the concatenated system image, so the ROM
pane showed one combined "System + DOS ROMs" socket. Split it out: every Lynx
ROM socket is one 8K image — two system images on the 48K, three plus the DOS
ROM on the 96K/128K — and each is independently overridable through the shared
MTX-style multi-slot machinery (a Lynx branch in romPageSlotCount/romSlotSize).

Add a Hardware-pane "Disk interface (FD1793)" checkbox. Switching it off
rebuilds the machine with the interface removed: the DOS socket disappears
from the ROM pane, .ldf media is refused, the FDC ports and drive LEDs go
away, and the Drives pane hides. The Lynx 48K has no interface to toggle, so
the checkbox is not shown for it.

* The Lynx FD1793 addresses four drives (A-D)

The FDC was modelled with two units, so only A:/B: existed. The FD179x drives
two select lines and the Lynx DOS manual says up to four drives (A-D), so widen
it:

- WD179x core: four-wide disk/head/write-protect/dirty arrays and `& 3` unit
  indexing, plus `selectDrive` over 0-3. Transparent to the Beta/MTX, which
  use at most two.
- Lynx port 0x58 decodes both drive-select bits.
- LynxDiskService exposes A-D, and the descriptor declares `builtinDrives: 4`
  (the pane reads that capability, so the extra rows appear before the machine
  is built — the live service is not reactive at first render).
- The shell disk transport is generalized to four units through a DISK_UNITS
  table, and `restoreMedia` restores `ui.builtinDrives` of them.
- The Drive pane renders C:/D: rows for machines with more than two built-in
  drives, and the Hardware checkbox is relabelled "Floppy disks" to match the
  other optional-disk systems.

* The Lynx tape deck did not restart after running off the end

`cassetteInput` advances the deck by the CPU time since the last read, but it
returns early while the deck is not playing — so `tapeLastAdvanceT` froze once
the tape ran off the end. A later rewind + play then advanced by the whole idle
gap (hundreds of millions of T-states) and jumped straight back to the end.

Re-base the advance clock whenever the deck (re)starts — `resetTapeAdvance()`
on mount, play, resume and rewind. The motor-on path already did this via
`setTapeMotor`.

* A Camputers Lynx keyboard, traced from a 48K

The Lynx was the last machine with a key matrix and no on-screen keyboard.
The deck is 16u wide and every row is centred on it, which is what produces
the staircase: the SHIFT row runs the full 16u, the A row 15u, and the number
and Q rows 14.5u, so each row above starts a quarter unit further right than
the one below. Row widths, the 1.5u caps and the stagger are measured off a
photograph, where a cap top is 63px against a 94px pitch. Caps sit 2 units
apart and the wells clear them by the same 2, so every gap on the face is the
one measurement.

Two cells the host key map had wrong. SHIFT LOCK is [0,3], which MAME leaves
unnamed and the MiSTer Lynx48 core identifies; between them the matrix
accounts for every cap on the deck but BREAK, and every cell but [9,4], which
no cap reaches. The old map pointed the host End key at that phantom cell, so
it carries CapsLock instead.

BREAK gets no cell at all. It is not a matrix key: it pulls the CPU's
interrupt line, which this machine already asserts once a frame, so the cap
depresses under the pointer and reaches no switch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Each machine declares the drive it sounds like

Every probe published floppyProfile its own way. The Spectrum carried an
inline copy of the capacity test that profileForDisk already does, the
Spectrum's +D path used a bare 1, and the machines with no drive a
bare -1, so whether a machine was fixed or adaptable was implicit in each
call site rather than stated anywhere.

A drive path now names itself once, at the top of its probe: fixedDrive for
the machines that only ever shipped the one kind of unit, byCapacity for the
+3 and the CPC, which shipped a 3" CF2 but were routinely fitted with a 720K
3.5". It is per interface, not per machine -- the Spectrum's +3 controller
adapts while its +D/Beta path is always 3.5" -- so the per-frame line becomes
one uniform call. fixedDrive closes over its code at module load, so sample()
still allocates nothing.

The Lynx moves to 5.25" with it. Camputers shipped the machine with 5.25"
drives, and its 800K format is 80 tracks double-sided: past the capacity
where the shared test would have called it a 3.5" had it been adaptable,
which is exactly why the choice belongs to the machine and not to the disk.

The two emulator tests that stub floppy-sound.ts now spread importOriginal
and stub only FloppySound, which reaches for Web Audio. Listing the pure
exports by hand is what broke them here.

events.title: grm-lb54: clobber proof survives a branch after the argument is lost for good
events.message:
grm-lb54: clobber proof survives a branch after the argument is lost for good

rcransom FUN_ff07 (call site f1d0) defines A at entry (LDA #$06), so it
takes no inbound argument, but grm-jqt0's widened clobber span runs to the
select-data switchSite, the second of two $8000 select restores behind a
BNE-split tail (ff1d BNE ff25, decoded from the pinned ROM). That branch
cleared straightLine, and the proof fell back to INDETERMINATE and the old,
false "could not be recovered" wording.

prologueOutcome now LATCHES the loss: once reg loses the caller's byte on
a straight-line prefix with no copy anywhere (nothing pushed, no tracked
cell, no other instruction read reg while it held the byte), no later path
can restore it. A later branch keeps DEFINITELY_CLOBBERED unless some flow
can leave [entry, valueSite] (a target outside it, or a computed jump). The
stack-page tripwire still covers the whole span, so fed1/fe56 keep the old
wording. The span is left alone, so the fix doesn't depend on MMC3 register
parity, and a tail PLA / STA $8000 is not hidden from the proof.

Only the wording moves (argumentDefinitelyClobbered's sole consumers are the
noInboundArgument text and restoreSourceCell, whose one-instruction span
cannot contain a branch). SURVIVES is unreachable after the latch.

Real-ROM (check nes): re-blessed rcransom (f1d0) and ultimaav (f35f
FUN_f34b: LDA #$0E, then a branch-always BNE over its $f34f alt entry before
the MMC1 serial write), one wording line each, warning to warning, no count
moved. contra/tmnt/wizwarr fail at their held signatures, unchanged. Full
synthetic gate SUITE OK. Six new predicate tests in
HelperNoArgumentRestoreProgramTest (ff07 bytes, plus PHA, TAX, branch-out,
stack-relative and branch-before-clobber controls).

events.title: A formatted disk kept its old geometry on the MTX and Einstein
events.message:
A formatted disk kept its old geometry on the MTX and Einstein

Only the Spectrum consumed the format latch. Everywhere else a completed
WRITE TRACK left formattedUnit sitting on the controller, so the drive panel
went on showing the geometry the image had when it was inserted, and the
latch was never cleared. The MTX even had diskImageForSlot ready for it —
the half the bridge needs to re-detect an image — with nothing ever
publishing a slot to use it.

The MTX and the Einstein tick their own controllers from runFrame, so their
frameTick consumes the latch and does nothing else; ticking the FDC here as
well would decay its display state twice. The Einstein was two pieces short
rather than one and gains diskImageForSlot, without which the bridge skips
the refresh however the slot is published.

The tests drive a real format stream through each controller — an ID field
and a data field per sector, at each machine's sectors-per-track — rather
than poking the latch, since the point is that the path from WRITE TRACK to
the panel is joined up.

events.title: Drive sounds for the MTX, CPC and Einstein, and the CPC's drive panel
events.message:
Drive sounds for the MTX, CPC and Einstein, and the CPC's drive panel

The synth only ever ran for the Spectrum: every other machine
with a drive published floppySlot = -1, so the Drives pane offered a sound
toggle that could not make a sound. The MTX also had nothing to play — its
FDX drives are 5.25" half-height units, and the two profiles modelled the
3" CF2 and the 3.5".

The new profile carries the two things that make a 5.25" recognisable, both
optional so the existing profiles are untouched: a belt-driven spin-up, the
hum sweeping 42Hz up to 72 over the gain ramp, and a low sine thump under
each step, where the band stepper lands as a clack rather than a click. Its
seeks are slower to match — 12ms a track against the 3"'s 10 and the
3.5"'s 6.

The FDX's profile is fixed rather than read off the disk: an 80-track FDX
image is past the capacity where the +3's test would call a drive 3.5". The
CPC and Einstein do take that test, since a 720K drive alongside the built-in
one was common on both. It moves to floppy-sound.ts as profileForDisk, with
the profile codes and driveTypeForProfile, so the mapping lives in one place
instead of an if/else in the bridge.

The CPC's drive panel goes with it. Wiring the LEDs meant ticking the FDC:
the uPD765A latches its read/write state for 25 frames and decays it in
tickFrame, which nothing on the CPC called, so the first access would have
pinned the LED on read for good. That is the Spectrum's frameTick block, so
the CPC now takes the rest of it too — the unsupported-SCAN warning, and the
FORMAT latch that refreshes the disk metadata, which needs diskImageForSlot
on the probe or the bridge skips the refresh.

events.title: Stop taking the function keys off the browser
events.message:
Stop taking the function keys off the browser

F1-F12 belong to the browser and the operating system — F5 reloads, F11 goes
full screen, F12 opens the developer tools — and an emulator has no business
hijacking them. They are now dropped at the browser boundary before anything
else looks at them, joystick bindings included, so nothing calls preventDefault
on one.

The machines that have function keys of their own keep them in their matrices:
the Einstein's F0-F7, the MTX's F1-F8 and the MSX's F1-F5.
Those maps also drive the MCP key tool, which runs headless with nothing to
hijack, so deleting them would have cost automation for no gain. They stay
reachable on the on-screen keyboard.

events.title: A floating pane moved while it was being resized
events.message:
A floating pane moved while it was being resized

The resize grip is the browser's own, drawn by the resize property rather than
by an element, so there is nothing to hit-test and nothing to stop propagation
on. Pressing it lands on the pane, and since the whole case had just become the
drag handle, the same press started a move as well: the pane wandered off under
the pointer as it grew.

Its corner is now reserved by hand — a press within 18px of the bottom-right,
against a grip of about 16, does not start a drag. The check sits in panes.ts
rather than the component because the test environment is node, where importing
a compiled JSX module runs delegateEvents against a window that is not there.

events.title: An undocked keyboard is the case alone, dragged by itself
events.message:
An undocked keyboard is the case alone, dragged by itself

Out of the layout, the pane drops its chrome: no title bar, no border, no pane
background. What floats is the machine's case and nothing else, which is the
point of taking it out of the column in the first place.

With no title bar to grab, the case is the handle — a press anywhere that is
not a key or a control starts the move, so keys still type. The resize corner
stays where it was. The dock toggle leaves the title bar for the pane's own
top-right corner: docked it lands where it always did and floats the pane,
undocked it stays invisible until the pointer comes to the keyboard.

Docked panes are untouched, title bar and all.

events.title: Keyboard cases fill the pane, and floating panes scale the face
events.message:
Keyboard cases fill the pane, and floating panes scale the face

Resizing a floating pane now works in both axes and scales the face with it.
The scene publishes the two candidate scales — what the display-scale setting
asks for, and the largest the frame can take — and the stylesheet picks: docked
takes the smaller of the two as before, floating takes the fit alone, so
dragging the pane makes the keyboard bigger as well as smaller. A floating pane
therefore carries an explicit height: its frame has to be a size container for
that fit to mean anything, and a size container without a definite height
resolves to none at all.

The 48K's legends were the last ones sized from the display-scale setting
rather than the scale the scene is actually drawn at, so they kept their full
size on keys shrunk to fit a narrow pane — and stayed small on keys enlarged in
a floating one. Every other face was converted at some point; this one was
missed.

Every case — its colour, edges, bevels and moulded grooves — now paints on a
full-bleed backdrop rather than a centred strip, following the CPC's existing
50cqw idiom instead of the second background this had grown. That needed the
container-type and the overflow clip off each scene, or the backdrop was
clipped back to the box it was trying to escape. How far it bleeds is one
variable: width only when docked, both axes when floating, where a pane taller
than its keyboard was showing the pane's own colour as bands above and below.

events.title: Let the keyboard pane float free of the layout
events.message:
Let the keyboard pane float free of the layout

The keyboard sits under the screen in the main column, which is a poor place
for something far wider than it is tall — and its scale is set by the width it
is given, so where it sits decides how big it is. Drag its title bar and it
tears out where it stands and follows the pointer; the title bar also carries a
toggle to send it back. A floating pane resizes from its bottom-right corner,
horizontally: the height is a consequence of the width, so there is no second
axis to drag.

Position and width persist per pane, and a pane whose stored position falls
outside a window that has since shrunk is pulled back into view on mount and on
resize. Floating is a per-pane opt-in — only the keyboards ask for it, and
sidebar panes keep the HTML5 drag-and-drop reordering they had.

events.title: Keyboards were DPR times too big on a high-DPI screen
events.message:
Keyboards were DPR times too big on a high-DPI screen

The display-scale setting counts physical pixels — one emulator pixel maps to
exactly that many, which is what keeps the picture pixel-perfect — so both
renderers divide by the DPR when they size the canvas's CSS box. The variable
the on-screen keyboards size themselves from carried the raw setting instead,
and CSS is what lays them out. The two only agree at 1x: on a Retina Mac the
canvas halved and the keyboards did not, so every cap and legend came out twice
the size relative to the screen, and the scene's own width clamp then pinned
the keyboard to the pane. Windows at 125% had the same fault at a quarter the
size, small enough to pass for right.

--display-scale now carries scale / dpr. The DPR signal moves out of Screen.tsx
into state, since two places need it and it has to re-run the CSS variable when
the window moves between displays; Screen.tsx reads the same signal it always
did. A test pins the invariant the regression broke: the CSS scale handed to
the keyboards is the one the canvas measures itself in.

events.title: Memotech MTX keyboard addition
events.message:
Memotech MTX keyboard addition

The MTX500, MTX512 and RS128 share one deck, so there is one face and only the
badge's model name changes with the model. Everything sits on a 1u pitch and
no cap is under it: the typing block staggers 0.5u / 0.25u / 0.5u behind 1.5u
modifiers, the number, Q and A rows finish flush at 15u with BS, LINE FEED and
RET, and the numeric keypad and two-column function block stand off to the
right in their own recessed wells, their four rows on the main block's row
lines. The MEMOTECH rule runs across the top.

Every cap and both its legends come from MTX BASIC's own key tables — one entry
per matrix cell at 0x1729 unshifted and 0x177A shifted — which settles the caps
the host key map never named: LINE FEED is [3,6], the keypad's 8/EOL is [1,7]
and its 9/BRK is [0,8], and ENT/CLS is [7,7]. The two unlabelled caps flanking
the space bar are the one guess: the ROM gives the spare cells on their sense
line no character at all, so they are presented as further space bars.

events.title: Einstein 256 TEXT overlay sat one character left of the text
events.message:
Einstein 256 TEXT overlay sat one character left of the text

MOS 2.1 sets the V9938's R18 display adjust to 0x0A, which shifts the whole
picture six source pixels right — a full character cell in the 6-pixel MOS
font. The renderer honours it, as the hardware does; the overlay and the cell
blanking did not, because both positioned themselves against the border origin
alone. So the transcribed text read correctly but sat a character to the left
of the glyphs it was covering.

The V9938 now exposes the adjust it is already applying, and the Einstein's
field box adds it. Blanking takes its x from that same box, so the two cannot
drift apart again.

Sizing: ESC and GRAPH become 1u, and each left-hand modifier grows to meet its
own row's first key (CTRL 1.5u, ALPHA LOCK 1.75u, SHIFT 2.25u) instead of
stopping a quarter unit short; BREAK widens to 1.5u to meet the double-bar cap.
The legend card is cut to the span of the eight function caps rather than
overrunning F7, and its eight cells now divide evenly whatever their text — the
long RST:BCOL4 was stretching its own cell. The cursor cluster comes up and in.

Tones: the caps are the machine's beige rather than white, the function strip
with them; the modifiers are darker and nearly flat; and every gradient is
vertical, with the top-left sheens gone. The case now fills the pane instead of
stopping at the scene box. The POWER lamp and label are dropped.

The cursor wedges print outline arrows, and the ALPHA LOCK lamp moves onto its
own cap, so it lights with the latch and travels with the key.

events.title: Einstein 256 TEXT overlay sat over the wrong box
events.message:
Einstein 256 TEXT overlay sat over the wrong box

The overlay stretches the transcribed grid across the descriptor's active area,
which holds for every machine whose text fills it. The 256's does not: MOS 2.1
runs GRAPHIC 2, so a 42x24 grid of 12x8 buffer cells is 504x192 centred in a
512x212 window. The overlay was starting ten lines high and stretching 212/192
too tall, so it drifted further off the text with every row down the screen.

A transcribe driver can now report the field its grid actually occupies, in
buffer pixels, and the overlay sits over that when given; machines whose text
fills the active area say nothing and are unaffected. The Einstein reports the
same box blankCells paints into, so the two cannot drift apart.

events.title: Einstein 256 display was drawn twice as wide as it should be
events.message:
Einstein 256 display was drawn twice as wide as it should be

The V9938 buffer is 512 pixels across the active window because the chip has
genuine 512-pixel modes; the 256-pixel modes — including the GRAPHIC 2 the MOS
boots in — double into it, the same trick the CPC's gate array uses.
Those machines then set pixelAspectX to 0.5 to present the buffer at its true
width. The Einstein 256 was left at 1, so every 256-mode screen reached the
canvas stretched to twice its width, its 6-pixel MOS glyphs 12 wide.

events.title: Tatung Einstein 256 keyboard addition
events.message:
Tatung Einstein 256 keyboard addition

A second Einstein deck, picked by model the way the CPC picks between its
three. The 256 is a squarer, charcoal machine: the four left-hand modifiers
share a margin and grow rather than stepping (ESC 0.75u, CTRL 1.25u, ALPHA
LOCK 1.5u, SHIFT 2u) while the typing block staggers by the usual
0.5u/0.25u/0.5u and every row finishes flush; the function keys are their own
1.25u strip under the printed BASIC legend card; ENTER is an L across two
rows; and the cursor keys are four wedges on a detached pad out past the deck.
The POWER lamp, the ALPHA LOCK lamp and the cursor well come with it.

The cursor pad needed its wiring settled. MOS 2.1 decodes shifted [1,5] and
[2,5] to the same codes as unshifted, so the TC-01's trick of reaching the
upper legend through SHIFT gives down and right again, not up and left.
Sweeping every cell and modifier against the real ROM found left on [0,1] —
the cell MAME marks unused, and which the TC-01 has no key for — and no single
cell for up at all, so up goes through CONTROL+K, the only route to 0x0B in
either MOS. Host arrow keys follow the same per-model chords.

Caps now press a chord rather than one cell, since neither deck's cursor keys
are one switch apiece, and both faces share one layout, one geometry module and
one controller.

events.title: Tatung Einstein TC-01 keyboard
events.message:
Tatung Einstein TC-01 keyboard

An on-screen key deck traced from a UK TC-01: the eight function caps, the
deeply stepped typing rows whose leading modifier widens with each step, the
twin-arrow cursor caps, the red ENTER and the offset space bar. Cap legends
are the machine's own glyphs, not the ASCII behind them — the codes MAME
labels [, backslash, ], ^, backtick, {, |, } and ~ draw as left arrow, half,
right arrow, up arrow, pound, quarter, double bar, three-quarters and division
sign in the MOS font, and the caps are printed accordingly. Front-face
block-graphic legends are omitted.

MOS 1.2's key-decode table (0x10C5) also settles what MAME's matrix guesses
at. There are only two cursor caps, each carrying two arrows: [2,5] decodes
to cursor-right unshifted and left (0x08) shifted, [1,5] to down (0x0A) and
up (0x0B). The cells MAME calls LEFT, RIGHT and UP are the arrow *character*
caps, and its TAB cell is the cursor cap — the deck has no TAB key. Host
arrows now land on the right cells, with the two upper legends asserting
SHIFT while held.

SHIFT, CONTROL and GRAPH are not scanned rows, so the keyboard exposes them
as a ninth synthetic line carrying the status byte's own bits, letting the
pane press them as ordinary cells.

- tests/machine-capabilities.test.ts holds every registered model to the

events.title: fix(blitter): fast-path Z reads on DSTENZ alone, 32bpp Z addressing (#790)
events.message:
fix(blitter): fast-path Z reads on DSTENZ alone, 32bpp Z addressing (#790)

* fix(blitter): fast-path Z reads on DSTENZ alone, 32bpp Z addressing

Two fast-blitter Z bugs, both needed for 42Bastian's PolyEngine to draw
(either alone leaves 35-37% of the frame wrong; together 0.02%):

- DSTENZ is its own memory-cycle enable (JTRM v8 p.73). With DSTEN
  clear the fast path read the DSTZ register instead of the Z buffer,
  so Z tests compared against a constant. Now DSTENZ reads memory and
  its absence selects the DSTZ register (p.68) in both directions,
  matching the accurate engine's dzread state machine.
- READ/WRITE_ZDATA were hard-wired to 16bpp. PolyEngine clears its Z
  buffer each frame with a 32bpp phrase copy (DSTWRZ, SRCZ1 = ones);
  the 16bpp addressing scattered those writes, the Z buffer was never
  cleared, and later Z tests rejected the water. Z is now addressed
  and sized like the pixel for 32bpp.

Two new test_blitter_cmd vectors, expected bytes derived from the JTRM
(not recorded), fail on the old fast path and pass on both engines.

Left alone: computed-Z order in pixel mode (accurate adds ZINC before
the first write, fast after). Pixels are identical and the JTRM does
not settle which is right.

Closes #786

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(blitter): WRITE_ZDATA as do/while; cite the JTRM's 16bpp-only Z rule

Copilot review: wrap the two-way WRITE_ZDATA in do { } while (0) so it is
one statement in every context. Review: the JTRM limits Z-buffering
(compare, computed Z) to 16bpp pixels (v8 pp.68, 81). The comment claimed Z
'is as wide as the pixel'; it now says what is defined (the Z memory cycles
move a whole phrase at any depth, which PolyEngine's 32bpp clear relies on)
and that a 32bpp Z compare only mirrors the accurate engine. No behavior
change.

Refs #786

events.title: grm-mej.7 (increment 2): proven-membership rule + per-game identifying-offset hint
events.message:
grm-mej.7 (increment 2): proven-membership rule + per-game identifying-offset hint

Owner ruling 2026-10-03: a shift-encoded read-back (rcransom $BFFF,
bank = 2*byte+1) is RESTORED only when the live bank at the read is
PROVEN to be in the encoding's verified set. BankMirrors.restoreMembership
returns NOT_NEEDED / PROVEN / HINTED / UNPROVEN ("not contradicted" is
UNPROVEN). It gates both read-back retention (readBackMatchesReload) and
the annotation (restoreDetail), including the existing caller-side and
direct-site restore paths. A non-identity encoded read-back is kept only
where the helper was proven to apply that encoding.

New per-game key banking.bank_identifying_offsets (grm-hb6.11 vocabulary),
compiled by GameCompiler, published by NesRomLoader, applied through
BankMirrors.withMembershipHints. It licenses ONLY the membership premise:
an entry is accepted only if the ROM bytes already derived that offset
ROM_IDENTIFYING with the same shift/low and a window field; otherwise it
is refused with a logged reason (seed, do not inject). The note says
HINTED and names the descriptor.

machines/games/rcransom.yaml: the first user ($BFFF, shift 1, low 1).

notes 2 -> 6: c08e, c0f4, c7db, fa61 become hinted RESTORED notes).

HLERawStreamAlignOffset returned shift 0 whenever no sync run sat near
the requested LBA. Continuation reads into the middle of a file have

2 bytes off, the movie player aborted, halted the GPU whose PIT ISR

events.title: fix(cd): deliver $03nn/$14nn TOC words after the DSA turnaround, not on write
events.message:
fix(cd): deliver $03nn/$14nn TOC words after the DSA turnaround, not on write

The TOC commands raised dsaResponseReady on the command write itself, and
every DS_DATA read synthesized and consumed the next word regardless.
The Atari CD library's TOC reader (Ocean Depths' own driver) does
`tst.w DS_DATA` right after writing $14nn; that dummy read consumed the
$60nn track word, the collector only saw $61..$64 and waited forever for
the rest of the entry (stuck on the loading screen). Arm the first word
after DSA_RESPONSE_DELAY_TICKS like other responses, and let reads made
while bit 13 is low return the latched word without advancing.

events.title: fix(core): detect 2-9 block jagcrypt carts as GPU-only
events.message:
fix(core): detect 2-9 block jagcrypt carts as GPU-only

Byte 0 of an encrypted boot block is the negated RSA block count.
JaguarCartNeedsBIOS only accepted 0xFC/0xFE (Tursi intros), so
42Bastian's PolyEngine demo (0xFD, 3 blocks, data at $802000) stayed
in HLE and jumped into vertex data: black screen.

Accept 0xF7-0xFE. 0xF6 (Atari's standard 10-block block) is on all
127 commercial carts in the corpus, several with entry opcodes the 68K
check misses, so it stays excluded. Corpus sweep old vs new
JaguarCartNeedsBIOS over 1272 files: only polygon.j64 changes.

pre-script fills the rest of the 64 KiB with uninitialized memory so I/O
references resolve, then applies the knowledge seeds (labels, data ranges,

events.title: feat(host): NMOS 6510 Ghidra language and headless runner
events.message:
feat(host): NMOS 6510 Ghidra language and headless runner

A complete 256-opcode SLEIGH language for the C64 CPU, with its own id so it
cannot clash with Ghidra's documented-only 6502. Deterministic undocumented
instructions have full p-code, the unstable ones (ANE LXA SHA SHX SHY TAS)
compute their value with opaque pcodeops that keep inputs and addresses,
JAM is a terminator, and ADC/SBC plus RRA/ISC/USBC/ARR follow NMOS decimal
mode; D is tracked as 0 at function entry. The runner finds Ghidra
(C64RT_GHIDRA or analyzeHeadless on PATH) and gives each run its own
settings directory with the language as an extension and a disposable
project, so the user's Ghidra stays untouched. Real-Ghidra tests check all
256 lengths, the 105 undocumented mnemonics, JAM flow, the opaque ops and
27 emulated instruction cases.

events.title: v0.2.6: GFX9000 P1 layers A and B no longer mixed up
events.message:
v0.2.6: GFX9000 P1 layers A and B no longer mixed up

A fix release for the GFX9000's P1 mode.

### Fixed: P1 layers A and B mixed up (since 0.2.4)
A user reported that in P1 mode, layers A and B looked like they were in the wrong priority order, which wasn't the case in 0.2.3. Two changes made in 0.2.4 caused it:

- **Drawing commands put layer B's graphics into layer A.**
  - The V9990 manual (11.2, p.51) says bit 9 of the command's X coordinate selects layer B. Tests on a real V9990 found that a Y of 2048 or more selects it too.
  - 0.2.4 wrongly concluded from those tests that the X bit does nothing, so a program drawing layer B the manual's way drew into layer A instead.
  - Now either way selects layer B.
- **Single-colour fills (LMMV) came out striped.**
  - 0.2.4 alternated the fill colour's low byte with a remembered high byte, which is 0 after a reset.
  - Colour 0 is transparent, so the other layer showed through every other pair of dots.
  - Following the hardware tests ("the low byte of FC is always read for the colour"), every dot now uses the low byte.

New automated checks cover both. One draws layer A and layer B at the same spot and checks that the picture shows A in front. On 0.2.5 it shows neither layer's colour; on 0.2.6 it shows layer A.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.2.6.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. On Linux, build from source (README, *Building from source → Linux*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

Everything else is as in [v0.2.5](https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/releases/tag/v0.2.5): the DSK editor, the regrouped interface and the logo.

feat: c64_cpu_history, c64_backtrace and c64_timing

CPU history comes from VICE's chis, oldest first; each C64 entry gets the
raster position it started at, mapped back from its cycle distance to the
current stop. The backtrace is rebuilt from JSR return addresses on the
real stack: VICE's bt keeps stale entries across resets and interrupts and
missed the current call in live tests. The stopwatch counts VICE's cycle
clock from session start or the last start, as a decimal string.

events.title: feat: c64_vicii, c64_sprite, c64_cia and c64_sid
events.message:
feat: c64_vicii, c64_sprite, c64_cia and c64_sid

Chip state is decoded from raw registers read through VICE's I/O bank
without side effects, so it holds whatever the program banked in and a
read never clears interrupt flags. The VIC-II addresses include the video
bank CIA 2 selects; sprite data addresses come from the pointers in the
RAM the VIC-II reads; CIA time of day becomes hours 0-23; SID registers
read back as last written. Decoders are pure and unit-tested; live tests
cover each chip.

events.title: feat: advance-frames and c64_run_until
events.message:
feat: advance-frames and c64_run_until

Frames are counted without a wall clock: one internal exec checkpoint over
all of memory alternates between an arming raster window half a frame away
and the window at the start raster position, so frame k ends at the first
instruction at or after that position (live: exactly N x 19656 PAL /
17095 NTSC cycles, at most one instruction late, repeatable). run_until
adds an address, memory or raster target checkpoint to the same clock and
reports target, breakpoint, watchpoint, jam or timeout. VICE now starts
with -jamaction 2 so a JAM stops the machine instead of hanging it; a stop
on a JAM opcode with no checkpoint is a jam. A text command whose line VICE
drops is sent once more (all text commands are idempotent).

events.message:
feat: c64_autostart, c64_program_load and c64_disk_attach

The private protocol carries binary attachments: a message announces their
sizes and the bytes follow as raw frames of at most 1 MiB, up to 16 MiB per
message (D1). The host-client reads project-relative files, refusing paths
that leave the project, also through symbolic links (17 §4), and sends only
bytes and the file type. The host stages them in the session's scratch
directory: program load uses the text monitor's load and finishes stopped,
autostart uses the binary autostart with -autostartprgmode 1, and disk
attach uses the text attach and keeps the run state. Fixtures build the
test PRG and a D64 in TypeScript.

events.title: Judge request deposits by a fail-closed textual rule instead of a shell parser
events.message:
Judge request deposits by a fail-closed textual rule instead of a shell parser

The confirming review found further bypasses of the executable-position
parser (if/then, env -u, bash -lc, multi-argument pwsh -Command, a
PowerShell backtick+CRLF continuation) and a false positive. Instead of
extending the parser, any command whose words mention finding.mjs and the
exact --request flag is now judged; every --request is a deposit needing
its own --approved, and one without a readable title is denied. The
wrapper, executable-position and -c recursion logic is gone; a flag inside
a quoted command string is still found by re-tokenizing that word. A
backtick or backslash before a newline is read as a line continuation.

The hook header documents the accepted false positive: a command that
merely mentions finding.mjs ... --request is judged too and must be
rephrased. The subprocess test now uses its own all-malformed fixture and
asserts transcript-unreadable. Records the confirming review in the ledger.

events.title: feat: c64_execution, c64_reset and c64_warp
events.message:
feat: c64_execution, c64_reset and c64_warp

pause/resume/step/next/until-return run through the session, which now
reads warp from VICE for c64_status and sets it with the text monitor.
A reset without run stops at the first instruction of the reset vector:
VICE skips a breakpoint at the PC it resumes from, so the reset is sent
while running and only that breakpoint's own stop counts. Reads no longer
resume a machine a breakpoint stopped meanwhile: a ping orders the binary
events before the session decides. Stock VICE resumes the machine when a
temporary checkpoint is set, so none is used. A fake VICE testkit mirrors
the probed behavior for unit tests; live tests cover the real thing.

events.title: Close the request-approval guard's bypasses found in cross-vendor review
events.message:
Close the request-approval guard's bypasses found in cross-vendor review

- Every finding.mjs --request deposit in a command is judged; one that
  fails denies the whole call, so an approved deposit can no longer carry
  an unapproved one chained behind it.
- The script is found anywhere after node, so value-taking node options
  such as -r fs or --import cannot hide it (fail closed).
- PowerShell commands are tokenized as PowerShell: backslash is a path
  character, the backtick escapes, and a here-string is one word.
- A transcript with malformed lines and no readable human message is
  denied as unreadable instead of passing as headless; only a torn last
  line without its newline is forgiven.
- node counts only in an executable position (after assignments and
  wrappers such as env, timeout, npx, a pipe, $( ) or bash -c), so
  echo node ... is no longer a deposit.

Records the review in the mechanism-review ledger.

events.title: dos buffered I/O and the command line in Input() as on AmigaOS 3.1
events.message:
dos buffered I/O and the command line in Input() as on AmigaOS 3.1

- FGetC/FGets/FRead read 196-byte blocks (SetVBuf: at least 196), so an
  unbuffered Read() continues behind the block; Seek/Flush/SetVBuf give
  read-ahead back and report the logical position; reading flushes the
  handle's pending output.
- FPutC/FPuts/FWrite/VFPrintf/VFWritef/WriteChars are buffered until the
  buffer is full, Flush/Seek/SetVBuf/Close or a read; consoles in line mode
  flush at '\n', files never do; Write() bypasses the buffer.
- VFPrintf writes RawDoFmt's output up to its final NUL (keeps the stray NUL
  after %05ld of a negative number) and has no 1 KB limit.
- RunCommand(), CreateNewProc(NP_Arguments), SystemTagList() and the
  bootstrap program put the argument line into Input()'s buffer; ReadArgs()
  reads it from there; an error skips the rest of the line.
- IsInteractive() is TRUE for CON: windows; CON: windows run in LF/NL mode
  and keep their title.
- lxa's C: commands and shell no longer mix Write() with buffered output.

Probes dos/cmdline and dos/bufblock and the interactive-conbuf golden
compare with the reference.

events.message:
clipboard.device: any unit, 3.1 clip ID rules and read/write hold-off

An unfinished read (started with io_ClipID 0) now holds off the first
write of a new clip, CMD_UPDATE without a write and CBD_POST; a write in
progress holds off reads; obsolete IDs (below the write ID) fail with
CBERR_OBSOLETEID; clip size is 8 + the long at offset 4 (no padding);
non-clipboard commands return IOERR_NOCMD; every unit number opens.
Held requests are queued and AbortIO() ends them.  iffparse's clipboard
stream starts reads/writes with clip ID 0 and ends unfinished reads in
CloseIFF so writers are not held off.  Probe clipboard/clipboard equals
AmigaOS 3.1.

events.title: grm-mej.7 (increment 1): stack-reload read-back survival, NOTE path, X1 caps
events.message:
grm-mej.7 (increment 1): stack-reload read-back survival, NOTE path, X1 caps

FUN_fed1-style helpers reload their argument stack-relative (PHA ...
TSX / LDA $01nn,X), so argumentSurvivesPrologue is false and the grm-oj20
discard dropped every proven RESTORED read-back. argumentReloadTransform
now proves, straight-line through the helper's own body, which push the
reload reads (via StoredValueScanner.stackRelativePush) and the transform
from the caller's A to the stored value. readBackMatchesReload keeps a
read-back only when that transform matches a write-through shadow
(identity) or a ROM-identifying cell's identity encoding on exactly the
deposit's field. argumentSurvivesPrologue, the jqt0 tripwire and
argumentDefinitelyClobbered are unchanged.

BankAnnotationAdapter: a call site carrying restore text on the
warnDespiteKnowledge path now gets a NOTE, not a WARNING.

X1 crossBlockMatchingPush caps raised to 384 nodes / 32 joins (owner
approval 2026-10-03; grm-3jzn measured 79-317 nodes, up to 24 joins).

Shift-encoded identifying cells (rcransom $BFFF, bank = 2*byte+1) are
still refused: accepting them produced false notes on nesmmc3idtest
(e28d R7=4, e2cd R7=15). Zero output change: build-and-test check OK,
realrom check nes byte-identical to baseline on all 34 rows.

events.title: Sprint 13: save, load and quit from the disk icon
events.message:
Sprint 13: save, load and quit from the disk icon

- The disk icon on the character sheet opens a game menu built from DM's
  dialog art (graphic 0): SAVE | LOAD, QUIT | OPTIONS (for later), CANCEL.

  magic text, version and header; loading only accepts the game's and
  the JDK's classes, and saving goes through a temp file.
- QUIT asks SAVE AND QUIT / QUIT / CANCEL in DM's own 3-choice layout;
  results show in DM's 1-choice layout with OK.

  sheet. Loading swaps in the saved party and resets the screen state.

events.title: grm-aemp: make the two residual real-ROM races order-independent
events.message:
grm-aemp: make the two residual real-ROM races order-independent

dodge (refs 2480<->2477) and dragonpower (symbols 152<->168) were the only
rows still nondeterministic on check nes. Neither was the competing-decodings
class the bead assumed; both were analyzer-ordering races driven by timing.

JumpTableBoundAnalyzer: the decompiler follows flow past the listing, so a
real function can yield a table for a switch no function owns -- often one
not disassembled yet (dragonpower a546, reached from NMI). The override
always threw "Switch is not in function body" and stock switch analysis
over-read the table to 91 cases. Treat that like the undefined-function case:
pin by references, disassembling the switch first when needed.

MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer: stock analyzeLocation walks a function from its
entry, restricted to its body, so a body range entered only by fall-through
from outside is never evaluated. dodge's 9000 island got its table refs only
when the not-in-a-function sweep reached 8ffc before FUN_8030's body absorbed
it. Also walk each body range the entry walk never reached.

check nes: 34/34 byte-identical across 3 pinned runs + 1 unpinned.
dragonpower now matches its golden; smb3 re-blessed (+1 ref, b460 LDA
$b34d,Y base); dodge moves to a new deterministic state (+295 instrs of
8445 case code) and stays unblessed pending the owner read in grm-q1bi.

events.title: console.device input as on AmigaOS 3.1; raw_events_unit/idcmp_console validated — v0.11.19
events.message:
console.device input as on AmigaOS 3.1; raw_events_unit/idcmp_console validated — v0.11.19

console.device forced IDCMP_RAWKEY|NEWSIZE (and the raw-event classes)
onto its window and read the window's UserPort, stealing the
application's IDCMP messages. Verified on AmigaOS 3.1 with the new
Tests/Console/idcmp_console: with IDCMP_RAWKEY/VANILLAKEY the keys go to
IDCMP only and the console gets none; without, the console gets them;
with IDCMP_MOUSEBUTTONS the console gets no mouse reports.

Now Intuition passes the input events a window's IDCMP does not request
to the console unit's own port (registered per window, Intuition-owned
reply port); the console never touches the window's IDCMP, notices
resizes by itself (csi_unit: bounds follow even when the application
takes IDCMP_NEWSIZE) and reports the window address in the x;y fields of
size-window raw events. CON: windows open without IDCMP.

raw_events_unit and keymap_unit open their windows without IDCMP (as
3.1 requires); raw_events_unit's size-window check reads what 3.1
reports. Both interactive programs have reference scenarios + goldens.
The DPaint startup scenario waits for the 4 s ownership splash (3.1
shows it too; the old snapshot was taken while it was still open).
