events.title: Phase 222c: layers refresh probe; contents, backfill hooks and scrolling match AmigaOS 3.1
events.message:
Phase 222c: layers refresh probe; contents, backfill hooks and scrolling match AmigaOS 3.1

tests/probes/layers/refresh.c (reference output from 3.1): backfill hooks
(layer and Layer_Info, LAYERS_NOBACKFILL), SIMPLE/SMART/SUPER layers through
create/move/depth/size/delete, BeginUpdate/EndUpdate, EraseRect and
ScrollRaster in layers, ScrollLayer, SyncSBitMap/CopySBitMap; prints the
hook calls (as regions), the damage state and screen hashes.

layers.library:
- arrangement changes keep layer contents (ArrangeBegin/ArrangeEnd): the
  image of every layer is saved and written back through the new
  ClipRects - a simple layer only where it was visible before - so moving
  a layer moves its pixels; damaged parts are backfilled with the layer's
  hook and uncovered background with the Layer_Info hook;
- backfill and DoHookClipRects() call custom hooks (CallHookPkt) with the
  3.1 message (Bounds in the target bitmap, OffsetX/Y in layer coords),
  including SMART backing store; new layers are backfilled the same way;
- SUPER_BITMAP layers keep obscured parts in backing store;
- InstallClipRegion() keeps contents and adds no damage;
- EndUpdate() leaves LAYERREFRESH set (Intuition's EndRefresh clears it).
graphics.library:
- EraseRect() in a layer calls the layer's backfill hook (pen 0 without);
- ScrollRaster() in a layer clips to the layer and scrolls visible parts
  and backing store;
- SyncSBitMap()/CopySBitMap() include backing store ClipRects;
- BltTemplate() fast byte path and clipped runs (was per pixel).
intuition: window layers use LAYERS_BACKFILL (as 3.1) instead of none.
Tests: devpac_settings expects the uncovered editor area clean (it relied
on stale Settings imagery); sigma waits for the frame text instead of a
fixed cycle budget.

events.title: grm-9nxj.19: SNES interleaved / small-chunk-first image layouts
events.message:
grm-9nxj.19: SNES interleaved / small-chunk-first image layouts

Add a "ROM layout" loader option (Auto default / Off / Force; headless
-loader-romLayout). SnesImageLayout is the single logical-cart-offset ->
file-offset mapping used by both the header search and block creation, so
they cannot disagree. Two independent axes:

- interleave (32 KiB halves of each 64 KiB unit swapped). Auto applies it
  only when the stored image has no checksum-valid, location-matching
  header, the +0x7FC0 candidate declares a well-formed HiROM/ExHiROM map
  mode ((mapMode & 0xE0) == 0x20), and the de-interleaved parse yields a
  valid, location-matching header.
- ExHiROM chunk order (snes9x-style): swap when the stored order has no
  valid pair at logical 0x40FFC0 and the swapped order does.

Blocks stay FileBytes-backed with true file offsets: a de-interleaved unit
becomes two 32 KiB blocks, nothing is copied. Mirrors are built per logical
unit. Canonical images are byte-identical (snestest/snestestcopier/
snestbltest unchanged).

Header tie-break (owner ruling): equal-scoring candidates now prefer the
one whose map type matches its location, in every layout. This moves
Mario's Early Years off its checksum-valid "SNES Kernel" decoy at $7FC0 to
the real header at $FFC0, which also corrects its NMI/IRQ vectors.

Corpus (921 images): Auto transforms exactly one, tofphant.smc
(interleaved + small-chunk-first), now EXHIROM@0x40FFC0 matching.
WWF Super WrestleMania was a near-miss false positive, excluded by the
map-mode well-formedness guard.

Goldens: new snestestinterleaved fixture (8 criteria, pins swapped file
offsets); re-blessed tofphant (header 0x40ffc0, 96 blocks split in two) and
marioearlyyears (real header, title, vectors). Gates: build-and-test.sh
check OK; realrom-test.sh check snes 13/13; snes-rom-corpus OK.

events.title: deps: TRX64 v0.12.3, the C64U turbo as measured (Spec 890)
events.message:
deps: TRX64 v0.12.3, the C64U turbo as measured (Spec 890)

The pin moves from v0.11.0 to v0.12.3, which brings the U64/C64U turbo as measured on the device: $D031 bit 7 is
"no badline stalls", top speeds 47/63, IRQs at the turbo clock, the measured I/O leads, last write wins between
program and menu, the reset readbacks and the 2^22 PHI2 post-reset hold.

`set_u64_turbo` is the menu now, and the firmware's reset task re-runs setCpuSpeed after every C64 reset
(u64_config.cc:1035-1045). On a C64 Ultimate that strobe leaves the reset state alone, so the bridge drops the
first strobe after a reset when it repeats the applied values; a strobe with new values is a menu change and
applies. Measured here: registers mode at 16 MHz reads $D031 = 0 after boot and after REST machine:reset (9
before), a program's POKE 53297,131 holds, a menu change to 32 MHz reads 12.

Workspace tests and scripts/gate.sh pass (441 s); mandelbrot-upic shows its picture in 30 of 30 frames.

events.title: dos Open("*"), CLI entry stack size, console handles keep host fds (Phase 232)
events.message:
dos Open("*"), CLI entry stack size, console handles keep host fds (Phase 232)

From the Fred Fish mass run (programs crashing at PC 0xfffffea4 =
AutoRequest() through a NULL IntuitionBase in old C startup code):
- Open("*") opens the current console in every mode (it was resolved
  as a relative file: MODE_OLDFILE failed, MODE_NEWFILE created a host
  file named '*'); verified on AmigaOS 3.1.
- The launched program is entered with the AmigaOS CLI convention:
  4(sp) holds the stack size in bytes; Lattice/SAS startup code derives
  its stack-overflow bound from it (YachtC & co. reported a false stack
  overflow).
- Closing a console handle never closes the host's fd 0-2 (with "*"
  working, programs closed lxa's own stdout; the next opened file got fd
  1 and lxa's log was written into it).

events.title: v0.2.5: DSK editor; grouped, easier-to-read interface with a logo
events.message:
v0.2.5: DSK editor; grouped, easier-to-read interface with a logo

### DSK editor (new) Open it from **Tools → DSK editor**, or **Media → Drive A/B → Edit** for the disc in a drive. - **Discs:** - Make new discs in any CPC format: DATA, SYSTEM, IBM, 42- and 80-track, ParaDOS, ROMDOS D1–D40, Vortex, Dobbertin, or a geometry of your own. - Open standard and extended `.dsk` images, and save as either. Standard is used only when the disc fits that format. - Work on the disc in drive A or B while the CPC uses it: the drive and the editor share one disc. This also means a disc the CPC has written to can finally be saved. - **Files:** - The AMSDOS / CP/M directory, for any of those formats. - Import a file, with an AMSDOS header (type, load and exec addresses, user) if wanted. - Export a file, with or without its header. - Delete, rename, change the user number or the read-only, system and archived flags. - Look at a file as hex, a BASIC listing, text or a Z80 disassembly. - **Tracks & sectors:** edit every track's header fields, and every sector's ID (C, H, R, N), status bytes, stored size and weak copies. A hex editor shows each sector's bytes. Sectors can be added and removed, and tracks formatted or unformatted. - **Map:** which file owns each block, and every sector in its place on its track. - **Checked:** - Against the DSK specification byte for byte. - Every test disc reads back identically after saving. - Against the CPC's own AMSDOS: - it LOADs a 20 KB file the editor wrote; - the editor reads back what AMSDOS SAVEd; - `|ERA`, renames and the read-only flag behave the same on both sides. - **Fixed on the way:** the disc reader took each track's number and side from the wrong header bytes, and saving lost weak-sector copies, the gap length and the filler byte. ### Interface - **Grouped windows:** - **Debugger:** the run/step buttons; the Z80's registers, flags and stack beside the disassembly; breakpoints and watchpoints below. - **Chips:** CRTC, Gate Array, monitor, Plus ASIC, PSG, PPI, keyboard matrix, disc controller and tape, as tabs. - **Memory:** a hex editor and the memory map. - **GFX9000:** its picture and the V9990's state, registers, palette and VRAM. - **Less clutter at start:** only the screen, Machine and Media are open. The other windows open from the menus. The first time, they dock with their group: the debugging windows as tabs to the right of the screen, the tools below it. - **Easier to read:** the interface font is now DejaVu Sans Mono (smooth edges instead of ImGui's pixel font), with more spacing. **Window → Interface size** goes from 90% to 200%. The dark theme, square windows and orange accent are unchanged. - **A logo:** a new logo at the top of the Machine window (above). - **Media window:** one line per drive, with Insert, Eject and Edit. - **Layout reset:** the window layout resets once on the first start of this version. ### Other - **SymAmp's slow SA2 songs are SymAmp, not the emulator.** I traced its player from a RAM dump: - it ticks at 50 Hz and turns a song's BPM into a speed (750 ÷ BPM); - a speed the song sets later in its pattern is taken as it stands; - so 60/70 Hz songs that do that play about 1.4× too slowly. A real CPC plays them the same. - **New debugging aid:** `CPCSE_TRACE_IO=` (with `CPCSE_TRACE_IO_FROM=`) logs accesses to the expansion ports with the PC that made them, plus PlayCity NMIs. ### Known issues - **SymAmp:** MP3 playback isn't available; it needs an MSX MP3 cartridge, which isn't emulated. - **GFX9000:** - Intermittent command faults reported from real hardware are not reproduced. - LMMV's colour order with DIX=1 is approximate. - **CRTC 0/2:** the C-HSYNC width is a fraction of a microsecond longer than the Compendium's table. ### Download `CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.2.5.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. On Linux, build from source (README, *Building from source → Linux*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed. events.title: feat: add an SAA5050 character-rounding upscaler
events.message:
feat: add an SAA5050 character-rounding upscaler

A new WebGL upscaler (scaling mode 6) applies the Mullard SAA5050's
character rounding to any machine's output. Each source line becomes two
half-lines and, where two lit pixels meet diagonally, the half-dot between
them is filled; "lit" is the brighter of the two colours. Output pixels that
cover both half-lines (1x) blend them for anti-aliasing; from 2x each half-line
is its own row, at any integer scale.

Checked in headless Chromium against Saa5050.characterRounding: 0 of 9600
pixels differ for 20 glyphs at 2x; 1x blends and 4x is crisp.

With the upscaler selected the BBC supplies the plain teletext dots (Saa5050
.rounding off, one line per glyph row) in the 1x layout at every scale, and
the display does the rounding. The Display pane applies settings on change so
machines see the selection.

Set the game on a desk: box, manual, curator's note, map and disk

Play is one front view: a dark wall, a cutting mat as a desk strip
tilted 60deg in perspective along the bottom, and the chosen item held
up above it where the monitor stands.  The strip holds Box, Game

angle variable (--desk-tilt) flattens it.

The box opens like a book: front alone, the inside lid facing the
inside of the box, then the back, turned with the side arrows, the
arrow keys or a click.  The manual reads two pages at a time as
printed, cover and back cover in their spread slots.  Both share
book.js, each book a list of spreads with null for a blank page.

The map held up from the strip is the zoomable map itself: drag, wheel,
double-click and WASD/arrows pan and zoom it, with - and + beneath; M
and Tab toggle between map and monitor, and /map opens straight to it.
Seen map screens show at 75% opacity.  About becomes the Curator's
Note, a two-page reissue booklet spread.  Escape steps back from an
item to the desk, and from play once menus are closed.

This replaces a run of intermediate layouts (a column beside the
monitor, header buttons, a wooden bench, a top-down mat) that are not
kept.

events.message:
Fit CRT scanlines to the device pixels they land on

A scanline is half a game row dark; under 4 device pixels a row its
edges land between pixels and beat into uneven bands.  Below that, the
scanline period is the row height rounded to whole device pixels at
full strength, and only a 2-pixel period drops to faint single-pixel
lines (FINE_SCAN).  The pattern is shifted by the canvas's fractional
device offset so each line lands on a whole pixel row.

events.title: grm-hb6.5: ExportGameDescriptor -- the human annotation layer out as game YAML
events.message:
grm-hb6.5: ExportGameDescriptor -- the human annotation layer out as game YAML

ghidra_scripts/ExportGameDescriptor.java is a thin front-end over
GameDescriptorExporter: identity + board from program properties,
banking.initial_state carried from the descriptor in force, and USER_DEFINED
global labels (kind label/entry, EOL comment, block: for banked addresses)
as an inline symbols: set. Output passes both GameCompiler.compileOverlay
and the curated build path and compiles to identical documents.

To make the round trip real, the game tier now consumes symbols:
GameCompiler compiles them (provenance required, include/source rejected),
applySymbolSet honours block:, and DescriptorAnnotationAnalyzer re-resolves
the game descriptor each run and applies its symbols. Re-applied labels
come back IMPORTED, never USER_DEFINED.

Also adds DescriptorSupport.programInfoString: Options.getString(name, "")
registers the option, which stamped an empty Game Identity onto every CBM
import and failed GID1-3 on five C64 goldens. All Program Info reads in the
descriptor analyzers/exporter now go through it.

events.message:
grm-hb6.15, grm-hb6.16: headless fixtures for the descriptor overlay and re-analysis

New `descriptors` chunk. descoverlaytest plants a valid and a malformed
overlay YAML under the isolated settings dir, imports, and removes them:
the overlay's prg_mode hint wins and the bad sibling is logged and skipped;
descoverlayctltest re-imports the same bytes with nothing planted. cache_key
gains GRM_KEY_INPUTS so a changed overlay cannot be served stale.
descannotationtest mutates labels and the recorded symbol-set choice, then
runs DescriptorAnnotationAnalyzer one-shot (AssertDescriptorReanalysis):
a disabled set restores nothing, a cleared choice restores PPUMASK, a
USER_DEFINED rename survives, and a third run is idempotent. SCHEMA.md
documents the analyzer and the "Retro Machines.Symbol Sets" property.

events.message:
grm-eawl: realrom-test.sh coverage -- per-row "ran at this build" from the cache

Read-only mode that computes realrom_cache_key() for each selected row and
reports whether build/realrom-cache/<key>.dump exists. Stages the build
first like check (honours --no-build) so EXT_ID is the build a check would
use; uses the manifest's pinned sha256 so no ROM is located or hashed.
Wording is "ran", never "passed": failing rows are cached too. No state
file, never fails. Also corrects the NES/all row counts (34/47 since the

events.title: Phase 222b: graphics probes for lines, areas and blits; lxa matches AmigaOS 3.1
events.message:
Phase 222b: graphics probes for lines, areas and blits; lxa matches AmigaOS 3.1

New conformance probes (tests/probes/graphics, reference outputs from 3.1):
lines (pixels, Move/Draw, line patterns, PolyDraw, RectFill modes and area
patterns, DrawEllipse, SetRast, ScrollRaster), areas (AreaMove/AreaDraw/
AreaEllipse/AreaEnd, outline mode, patterns, vector table limits, Flood)
and blits (BltBitMap minterms/masks/overlap, BltClear, BltTemplate,
BltPattern, BltBitMapRastPort, ClipBlit, BltMaskBitMapRastPort,
BitMapScale, ScalerDiv, chunky pixel functions).

graphics.library fixes, each observed on the reference:
- Draw(): LinePtrn and linpatcnt (pattern continues across lines),
  COMPLEMENT shared-vertex rule via FRST_DOT; Move()/SetAPen()/SetBPen()/
  SetDrMd()/SetABPenDrMd() restart the line state; fast path for
  horizontal/vertical lines; ClipRect cached per line.
- DrawEllipse(): 3.1 rasterisation (minimum-residual trace), every pixel
  once.
- Area patterns anchored to the bitmap, multicolour patterns (negative
  AreaPtSz, was a division by zero), INVERSVID and Mask honoured.
- AreaEnd(): blitter-style mask in the TmpRas (one-dot edges, exclusive
  fill, even-odd across polygons and ellipses, full edges added), drawn
  with pattern/mode; outline only with AREAOUTLINE, in AOlPen; the JAM1 +
  4-row pattern quirk; -1 when the table cannot be closed, 0 without TmpRas.
- RectFill() draws the AREAOUTLINE frame; SetOutlinePen() sets AREAOUTLINE.
- Flood(): builds the mask first, then draws it with pattern/mode; no
  longer gives up when its span stack is full.
- ScrollRaster(): no-op when the distance is not smaller than the area.
- BltTemplate(): INVERSVID inverts the template, layers and Mask honoured.
- BltPattern(): complete (area pattern, mask, modes); LXA_UNIMPLEMENTED
  removed.
- BitMapScale(): 3.1 pixel mapping and destination size.
intuition: restoring AOlPen no longer sets AREAOUTLINE on the window RastPort.

events.message:
CPU faults: interrupt-code faults halt (Guru), held tasks get a sane stack, bounded logging

  interrupt server) is a dead-end alert on AmigaOS: the host records it
  and stops the run instead of 'holding' the interrupted task while the
  interrupt keeps re-faulting (Fish MyCLI, Ash).
- A held task continues on the top of its own allocated stack (tc_SPUpper):
  programs that faulted with a corrupt SP faulted again in _exec_TaskHeld
  forever (Fish MuchMore: 580 MB of log).

events.title: feat(minigl): load an optional renderer plugin through uaelib trap 120 (#2369)
events.message:
feat(minigl): load an optional renderer plugin through uaelib trap 120 (#2369)

* feat(minigl): load an optional renderer plugin through uaelib trap 120

Guest software can reach an in-process renderer plugin (minigl_plugin from
the plugins folder) through uaelib trap 120 when Native Code is enabled.
Amiberry passes guest buffers through unparsed, within fixed size bounds;
the plugin owns the command protocol and its own GL context. Replies can be
written straight into a locked RTG bitmap, and those writes are marked
dirty so the display picks them up. Without the plugin the trap reports
unavailable.

* fix(minigl): reach guest memory through the trap accessors

- Use the TrapContext for the request descriptor and for staged copies, so
  indirect UAE-board mode (uaeboard=full+indirect) goes through the
  emulator thread instead of touching guest memory from the trap worker.
  In that mode nothing is handed to the plugin in place, and the in-place
  request reports unavailable so the guest falls back to its p96 copies.
- Only expose a direct output pointer for memory that may be written that
  way: directly writable banks, RTG VRAM (marked dirty afterwards), and
  banks without a direct mapping that vouch for the range through
  check()/xlate(), such as ZZ9000 VRAM. ROM is staged and written with
  put_byte(), which honours its write handlers.
- Mark RTG memory dirty for every in-place output, not only the in-place
  request, so a readback into VRAM also refreshes the display.

* fix(libretro): resolve capsimg only for the CAPS plugin

Under libretro, uae_dlopen_plugin() tried {system_dir}/capsimg first for
every plugin name, so with capsimg installed the MiniGL (or qemu-uae)
plugin lookup opened the CAPS library instead and never reached its own
file.

* fix(minigl): serialize plugin calls across trap worker threads

Indirect UAE-board mode dispatches traps on several worker threads. The
staging buffers were shared, so a concurrent call could resize a buffer
another call had just handed to the plugin. They are now per thread, and
loading, reset and every plugin call run under one mutex. The mutex is
never held across a trap accessor, which waits for the emulator thread,
so a reset on that thread cannot deadlock against a worker.

* fix(minigl): write in place only to memory that accepts raw host writes

A bank without a direct mapping that accepted the range through check()
and xlate() was treated as writable, but some, like filesys_bank, filter
writes in their put handlers. In-place output now goes only to RTG VRAM,
banks that map writes directly, and ZZ9000 VRAM, which declares through
zz9000_host_writable() that raw writes there are equivalent to its put
handlers. Everything else is staged and written through the handlers.

* fix(minigl): drop plugin dispatches that a reset overtook

In indirect UAE-board mode a worker stages guest memory before it takes
the plugin mutex, so a reset on the emulator thread could run in between
and the worker would then submit a pre-reset handle to the reset plugin.
Each reset now bumps a generation that a dispatch records first; the
plugin call and a staged copy-back return SERVICE_TRANSPORT_ERROR_LOST
when a reset happened since.

* docs(minigl): note why a staged copy-back cannot land after a reset

* fix(minigl): use only known raw mappings in place; reset after the trap drain

- A bank without a direct mapping that passes valid_address() only vouches
  for the range through its own check()/xlate(), which need not bound it
  (soft_check() accepts any size). Guest memory is now used in place only
  for directly mapped banks, bounded by their allocation, and ZZ9000 VRAM
  (zz9000_host_vram()). Everything else is staged through get_byte() and
  put_byte() in direct mode, since trap_get_bytes()/trap_put_bytes() would
  memcpy from the same unbounded pointer, and through the trap accessors
  in indirect mode.
- devices_reset() reset the plugin before reset_traps() drained the trap
  workers, so a queued pre-reset trap could start after the reset and be
  accepted. The transport is now reset after reset_traps(), which also
  discards queued traps. Turning Native Code off resets it after the flag
  flips; a dispatch already in flight is dropped by the reset generation.

events.title: grm-rnf0: resolve cross-window inline jump-table targets through the JSR's bank state
events.message:
grm-rnf0: resolve cross-window inline jump-table targets through the JSR's bank state

A JumpEngine table in one window can point into another switchable window.
InlineJumpTableDispatch resolved such a target in base space, which holds only
that window's HOME bank, so it either disassembled the wrong bank's bytes or
trimmed real entries as implausible.

Table side: a table now also ends where a flow reference from before the table
lands on an entry position (Cut.RAN_INTO_CODE; zelda's e691 BEQ e6b8 ends the
e6a6 table at its true 9 entries). A cross-window entry is laid as a pointer
with a base DATA reference but is neither disassembled nor judged by the tail
trim, since its bytes belong to whatever bank is live.

State side: BoardBankAnalyzer resolves those pointers against the states live
at the dispatching JSR, through resolveWindowOccupant/resolveComputedBank/
resolveModeBank (factored out of retargetForState unchanged). Fully known and
not home: overlay reference, plausibility checked in the overlay, disassembly
and a function; the base reference is retired when every arm resolved. Fully
known home: disassemble the base target. Unknown: plant nothing. Each table
logs one summary line (placed / home / unresolved / implausible).

zelda: the fixed-bank enemy dispatch tables fbb4 (106 entries, CMP #$6a) and
fd82 (95, CMP #$5f) now resolve into bank 4 -- instrs.inOverlay 5966 -> 11395,
refs 1364 -> 2561, bankComments 89 -> 91; handlers spot-checked from the ROM.
tmnt3: warning 8443 -> 85e4, counts equal; A/B shows it deterministic, and 8443
was reached only through fa00 targets decoded in the wrong bank. Both re-blessed.

zelda e6a3 itself stays unresolved (state not fully known at that JSR):
grm-f0di. smb3 a054 is not cross-window ($8000 is fixed in its layout; the
trimmed tail is a byte table).

build-and-test.sh check: SUITE OK. check nes: fail=8 = zelda + tmnt3 (now
blessed) + the six baseline rows at their documented signatures.

events.message:
grm-ujj5: wrap MMC3 bank numbers to the image (bank_wrap: image)

tmnt3 writes R7 = $3A = 58 at seven sites on a 256 KiB (32-bank) cart, which
the analyzer declined loudly as an out-of-range bank index. The value was
right: R6/R7 are 6 bits and the cart wires 5 bank lines, so the hardware maps
bank 26. The game's own bank-ID bytes say so too (each even bank starts with
bank+32; bank 26 starts with $3A). 8776 writes R6 = $2F = 47 -> 15, the same
convention.

Turn on the existing grm-p25h mechanism for MMC3, as MMC1 and MMC5 already
do. tmnt3 re-blessed: refs.intoOverlay 0 -> 410, instrs.inOverlay 0 -> 1405,
bankComments 37 -> 49, warnings 43 -> 37 ("r7=58 (wraps to 26)"; the calls
into WA000_B26 resolve). check nes: the other six failures are the
documented baseline. build-and-test.sh check: OK.

events.title: grm-3er5: follow split dispatch tables through a shared JMP (P) stub
events.message:
grm-3er5: follow split dispatch tables through a shared JMP (P) stub

rcproam's NMI path dispatches object handlers with the table load in the
caller and the computed jump in a shared stub:
  LDA $bb89,Y / STA $1e / LDA $bb8a,Y / STA $1f / JSR $8068   ; 8068: JMP ($001e)
The decompiler recovers a switch only when the load and the JMP (ind) share a
function, so nothing reached the handlers: bd15 and the bd2e switch behind it
were unreached once grm-eyn removed the over-read that used to hit them.

SplitDispatchTableAnalyzer (new, CODE_ANALYSIS.after(), after the constant-
pointer analyzer it would otherwise hide stubs from) matches the five-
instruction shape, walks the interleaved table and stops at the first entry
that runs into code, starts another site's table, or targets non-code,
another banked window, or mid-instruction (cap 128, >= 2 entries). The table
must sit in the caller's own block: dbz_datach's far-call reads a per-bank
header at $8001 right after switching, and took 9 bank-dependent targets
until that guard. Targets get COMPUTED_CALL refs from the stub's JMP,
disassembly, a scheduled function, and an EOL comment at the call.

rcproam: bb89 21 entries, bb5f 21 (ends at bb89), b350 26; ReachProbe shows
bd15 = FUN_bd15 containing bd2e/bd39/bd4f. Its golden moves only in the 818a
primary label (deterministic, re-blessed): W8000 is not an overlay, so the
dump's counts cannot see the payoff. check nes: the other six failures are
the documented baseline, byte-identical. build-and-test.sh check: OK.

events.title: v0.2.4: GFX9000 blitter in real time with /WAIT, the Powergraph notes, scroll fix; Memory map and GFX9000 internals
events.message:
v0.2.4: GFX9000 blitter in real time with /WAIT, the Powergraph notes, scroll fix; Memory map and GFX9000 internals

### GFX9000 (Yamaha V9990)
- **The blitter runs in real time.** Commands now take as long as they do on the chip, using openMSX's measured speed for each command, screen mode, colour depth and sprite/display state. CE and the command-end interrupt arrive when the command really finishes, and the screen builds up while the blitter draws. Before this, every command finished instantly. LMMC, LMCM and CMMC have no published timings, so they borrow the speed of the closest measured command (LMMV, BMLX and CMMM).
- **/WAIT on the CPC bus.** The V9990 now holds the Z80 while it is busy, as the real chip does, instead of letting data be lost:
  - writing P#2 during LMMC/CMMC waits until the engine has taken the previous byte;
  - reading P#2 during LMCM/POINT waits until the next byte is ready;
  - reading P#2 while any other command runs waits until that command ends.

  The wait is whole microseconds (the Gate Array's grid), and it always lets go once the V9990 is done.
- **Vertical scroll fixed (the tearing).** Writing scroll Y (R#17/R#21) while the display is on now restarts that layer's line count from that line, as on the real chip. Before, the scroll was added to the absolute display line, so any write during the display put the picture off by that many lines. The high bits (R#18/R#22) now take effect at the start of the next field.
- **Behaviour measured on a real V9990 on a CPC** (the Powergraph hardware notes):
  - Register bits: R#7, R#15, R#26 and R#27 keep all 8 bits; R#9 keeps &87, R#22 &C1, R#25 &CF.
  - With the soft reset held, status (P#5) and the interrupt flags (P#6) still read, P#1 reads 0, and the other ports return the bus value.
  - VRAM reads through P#0 go through a one-byte buffer, which is refilled from the current read address.
  - The palette pointer's counter at 3: reads give 0 and writes are dropped.
  - During LMCM, a write to P#2 counts as reading the byte.
  - VRAM size (R#8 VSL): at 128K/256K writes land in every mirror, and `11` acts as 512K. The image-space height follows the VRAM size. **Note: VSL is 00 (128K) after a reset**, as on the chip.
  - P1 addressing: lines are 128 bytes, X wraps at 256, and layer B starts at Y 2048. In P1/P2, commands draw at R#6's colour depth.
  - POINT at 2/4 bits a dot fills its low bits from the last 16-bit POINT.
  - SRCH reports the end of the line block when nothing matches (forwards), or &7FF (backwards).
  - LMMV takes FC's low byte, then its high byte, from each line's start. In P1 it uses the high byte latched by the last bitmap-mode LMMV.
  - PSET/ADVN/LINE work on an internal X/Y: X is reloaded from DX only when AXE=AXM=0, and writing DY sets Y immediately.
  - CMMK works with no kanji ROM (font bytes &FF, &FF, then BC's low byte).
  - BMLL reads two bytes ahead, which shows in overlapping copies.

### Debugger
- **Memory map** (Debug menu): one 64K block at a time, chosen from a list of the RAM fitted (the base 64K and every expansion bank, with the `&7Fxx` value that pages it in and where the CPU currently sees it).
  - One pixel per byte, coloured by what the Z80 did there: opcode fetch, operand, read, write, read and write, and optionally code that was also written.
  - The legend counts the bytes of each kind, and the CPC's screen area is outlined.
  - Hover a byte for its details; click it to open the Memory window, double-click for the Disassembly window.
  - It records only while the window is open, so it costs nothing otherwise.
- **GFX9000 internals** (Debug menu): the V9990's mode, raster position, ports, interrupts, command engine and internal pointer; all registers named from the Yamaha manual; the 64-colour palette; VRAM as the picture the display would make, and as bytes at the CPU's addresses.
- The two new windows reset the window layout to the default once.

### Since v0.2.2, not mentioned before
- **DigiBlaster / AmDrum:** the DAC output is AC-coupled, so the firmware's idle value no longer leaves a full-scale DC offset.
- **OPL4 tracing:** `CPCSE_TRACE_OPL4=<n>` logs the first n accesses to the card, with timestamps, and `CPCSE_TRACE_OPL4_FROM=<T-states>` starts the log later.
- **Linux (v0.2.3):** builds from source with the system SDL2. Paths in Windows-written CSL scripts are matched case-insensitively, and drive/keyboard sounds are also looked for in the working directory.

### Known issues
- **SymAmp (SymbOS):** some SA2 songs written for 60/70 Hz play too slowly on the OPL4. MP3 playback isn't available, because the MSX MP3 cartridge it needs isn't emulated.
- **GFX9000:**
  - Intermittent command faults reported from real hardware (a command reusing DY or NX/NY can go astray or hang) are not reproduced.
  - LMMV's colour order with DIX=1 is approximate.
  - A report that P1 scrolling is slightly slower than on real hardware is still open, pending the program it was seen with.
- **CRTC 0/2:** the C-HSYNC width is a fraction of a microsecond longer than the Compendium's table (see the README).

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.2.4.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. Linux: build from source (README, *Building from source > Linux*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they are needed.

events.title: grm-2m07: bound a jump table at an adjacent table's load-table start
events.message:
grm-2m07: bound a jump table at an adjacent table's load-table start

Dispatch tables are laid end to end, and a neighbour's entries are valid code
addresses by construction, so no extent rule can see where one table ends and
the next begins. dbz2's cb97 (table dd47) runs straight into the table the IRQ
handler's cbfd reads (dd65): its true count is 15, the decompiler walked 44,
and every existing rule declined (handlers below both switch and table).

JumpTableBound.boundByNeighbourTable, the last fallback: cut at the lowest
OTHER moving load-table start strictly inside this table's extent, on one of
its entry boundaries, keeping >= 2 entries, and only if every kept entry
targets initialized non-volatile memory. That last guard is load-bearing:
without it dbz2 and dbz_saiyan picked up zero-page/PPU case labels from a far
neighbour past an over-read.

JumpTableBoundAnalyzer now decompiles every function first and bounds second,
since the neighbour is often in another function.

check nes: the rule cuts exactly one table corpus-wide (cb97 44 -> 15);
dbz2 re-blessed (symbols 51). The other six failures are the documented
baseline, byte-identical to clean HEAD. build-and-test.sh check: OK.

Phase 220 (Exec): exec/expansion/utility/locale test programs pass on AmigaOS 3.1

Reference-verified lxa fixes:
- exec: AllocSignal(-1) hands out the highest free bit; Wait() records its
  mask in tc_SigWait (also when a signal is pending) and leaves it set;
  RawDoFmt %X prints lowercase digits; SumKickData starts at -1 and sums
  every MemEntry; AddResource leaves ln_Type alone; MakeLibrary rounds
  lib_NegSize to a longword; no blitter.resource; INTB_VERTB server chain is
  now run every VBlank; SetIntVector stores is_Data in iv_Data for handler
  vectors; cia.resource SetICR/AbleICR dispatch the ICR handler.
- mathffp SPSub = d0 - d1; mathieeedoubtrans IEEEDPPow edge cases.
- utility: CheckDate rejects leap seconds / >2114; unpacked bit fields = ~0.
- locale: built-in US/English default locale names, OpenLocale(name) is a

events.title: exec: AmigaOS trap convention, task held on CPU exceptions; host bounds fix
events.message:
exec: AmigaOS trap convention, task held on CPU exceptions; host bounds fix

- CPU exceptions (vectors 2-11) and TRAP #0-#14 push the exception number
  on the supervisor stack and jump to ThisTask->tc_TrapCode (SysBase->
  TaskTrapCode = exec's default) - the RKRM convention; the old path
  returned to the faulting instruction (runaway tasks, thousands of
  repeated exceptions) and used a private jsr convention for traps.
- exec's default trap handler logs the fault and holds a task that faulted
  in user mode (_exec_TaskHeld: Wait(0) forever) - 'Software Failure';
  held tasks no longer keep the emulation alive.  Traps no longer stop
  the emulator.
- tests/exec/traps (+ expected.ref.out): divide by zero, TRAP #5, CHK via
  tc_TrapCode, and a faulting process being held - identical output on
  AmigaOS 3.1.
- Host: 16/32-bit RAM/ROM fast paths used 'address + 3 <= END', which
  wraps for 0xFFFFFFFD..: a read at 0xFFFFFFFF segfaulted the emulator
  (Fred Fish MyCLI, MicroEMACS).
- tools/rdd/massrun.py ('python3 -m rdd massrun crawl|lxa|ref|report',
  Phase 232); lxa-one results go to a file, not stdout (suite-ref too).

events.title: Real-A500 speed and sound by default (calibrated against cycle-exact vAmiga)
events.message:
Real-A500 speed and sound by default (calibrated against cycle-exact vAmiga)

tools/amiga/emu gives the 68000 every bus cycle and blits in zero time, so the
CPU/blitter-bound loops ran too fast there and in the port. Measured tick-locked
on identical games with vAmiga (new tools/vamiga: driver, pinned build script,
timing_check.py): jungle/village 2.77-2.79 frames/tick (emu 2.00), final jungle
1.96 (emu 1.00), flare ~2.5 (emu ~2.0), tunnels unchanged.

- CPU-time model: cpuLine 426 Musashi cycles per line, each blit charges its
  cycle-diagram DMA time x 2.72; port vs vAmiga within 0.3 %.
- Paula: one audio DMA word per channel and line (short periods capped), A500
  4421 Hz RC filter, LED filter driven by CIA-A PRA bit 1 (the loader turns it
  on after every disk load; re/audio/NOTES.md corrected).
- referenceEmulator=1 restores the emulator timing/Paula: regress_all.sh and
  wavcmp.sh set it (ALL PASS 62/62, 9/9 IDENTICAL); platoon-headless defaults to
  it; practice drills are prepared with it; format-1 replays play with it.
- platoon-headless --tickinput; replay format 2; snapshot Paula trailer;
  roundtrip.sh A500=1.

events.title: fix(bsdsocket): ignore CloseLibrary() of a base that is already closed (#2370)
events.message:
fix(bsdsocket): ignore CloseLibrary() of a base that is already closed (#2370)

* fix(bsdsocket): ignore CloseLibrary() of a base that is already closed

A program that closes its bsdsocket.library base twice made Amiberry abort
with "free(): double free detected": the second Close read the socketbase
pointer still left in the freed library memory, freed its descriptor
tables again and released the guest's library memory a second time.
GLQuake's Amiga port does this when it quits.

Each socketbase now records the library base it was opened as. Close
ignores a base whose socketbase is no longer open, and logs it.

* fix(bsdsocket): claim the socketbase under the lock before closing it

Close checked that the socketbase was still open, then released the lock
and unlinked it only at the end of free_socketbase(), after several calls
into the guest. A second Close of the same base in that window, from
another task or another trap thread, passed the check too and freed
everything again. Close now unlinks the socketbase while holding the lock
and reads its library base there, so only one Close can clean it up.

events.message:
fix(gfx): skip the GL_EXTENSIONS query on desktop OpenGL contexts (#2368)

glGetString(GL_EXTENSIONS) is invalid on core-profile contexts: it returns
NULL and leaves GL_INVALID_ENUM pending, so the next glGetError reports an
error the caller did not cause. The desktop capability classifier only
reads the version string, so query the extension string on OpenGL ES only.

events.title: feat(documents): download a game's manuals, feelies and maps from IFDB (SQ-1680)
events.message:
feat(documents): download a game's manuals, feelies and maps from IFDB (SQ-1680)

Shift-D in the browser (story menu row, info-panel button) and
/download-documents in a running game open a multi-select chooser over the
non-game links of the game's IFDB record, and save the picks into its SQ-1679
documents folder through documents::import.

- ifdb_documents: parse_document_options (extension decides; isGame, setup,
  .hqx, audio, html, .inv and /games/ source are out; /solutions/ and /hints/
  are flagged spoiler), title matching, safe_entry_basename (zip-slip), a
  worker for resolve/probe/list/preview/download, a 50 MB cap judged by the
  declared size and again while reading, and nothing written until a download
  is whole.
- Zips are read over HTTP Range without being downloaded: one request for the
  tail (EOCD + central directory), then two per entry actually taken. Written
  by hand, not through zip::ZipArchive, whose open() seeks to every entry's
  local header and so costs a request per entry. A server that does not answer
  Range: bytes=0-0 with 206 gets "contents unknown" and whole-file only.
- SearchSource grows probe_range / fetch_range / fetch_capped; ResolvedGame
  carries the documents from the same viewgame response.
- documents_chooser: the state machine, renderer and DocumentsSession shared by
  the browser and the game (an overlay with Action::Documents*, polled in the
  loop). Space marks, -> opens a zip, p previews text, Tab/Shift-Tab walk the
  focus, one request in flight, a size probe only for the row under the cursor.
- One registry command, download-documents, which both worlds apply
  (slash::in_both_worlds); an unlinked game gets the button and menu row
  disabled with "Link to IFDB first" and the same line on the status line.
- Styles documents_checked / _spoiler / _title_match / _preview.

events.message:
Fix undefined behaviour reported by UBSan

Mask RLC to 8 bits so an int register no longer grows until it overflows when rotated repeatedly (draw_road's fill pattern). Replace left shifts of negative values with multiplies in the vibrato offset, rm_cycle_buffer_offset and scale_curvature_or_height, and mask NEG results in update_road_level.

Give the row above the backbuffer ($EFE0-$EFFF), which sprite, tunnel and overhead row walks reach when they step past the top, a scratch row rather than indexing backbuffer[] out of bounds. Pad exit_fork's tables with a leading byte so the road pointers no longer point before their arrays.

events.message:
feat(documents): per-game documents folder named <Title> [<IFDB id>] (SQ-1679)

A game linked to IFDB gets a folder for its manual, feelies and maps under
<user_dir>/documents, shared by every release and player. It is found by the
bracketed TUID only, so a title change never renames or duplicates it.

- documents module: sanitise_title, find_dir/documents_dir/ensure_documents_dir
  (race-safe), locate, and the host API list/import/remove (temp+rename,
  suffix on clash, traversal-safe remove).
- DataRoots carries the documents root; the shared config.toml's documents_dir
  moves it and create_documents_folders (default off) opts in to automatic
  creation, both ignored in a player's own file.
- Created at library scan for linked games and wherever a TUID is written
  (fetch_worker::write_fetched: fetch, IFDB-search download, metadata import).
- Story info panel shows the path (file:// link), the would-be path with a
  Create documents folder button, or a link-to-IFDB hint; new command
  create-documents-folder (key m, story menu), styles
  story_info_documents / story_info_documents_button.

events.title: Measure only the reasons a page actually draws
events.message:
Measure only the reasons a page actually draws

Review follow-up on both counts.

The draw path filters its row list through `row_on_page`, so a row this
machine leaves off has no reason on screen at all --
`every_greyed_reason_fits_the_column` measured every row in the table,
hidden ones included, and would have failed a wording that cannot
overflow because it cannot be seen. It now applies the same filter.

That filter costs the two boot-ROM reasons their coverage, since those
rows are hidden outright while no SCSI controller is fitted and the
sweep only ever named a model. They are drawable -- a fitted-but-
unsuitable controller is what draws them -- so the sweep now cycles
`ScsiController` through its values on every model, putting those rows
on a page in the state that shows their text. Eleven reasons are
measured where they render, against twelve measured before of which
three never reach a page. The one legitimately gone is the floppy bays'
"drive off": `Df0Image` is hidden on the same condition that produces
it, so it is never drawn.

The guide quoted "needs A600/A1200/A4000" where the launcher returns
"needs A600/A1200/A4000; Lide has its own". It is quoted UI copy, so it
now reads as the launcher says it, the CD rows' text with it. Both sit
on one line of prose rather than broken across the wrap, so a grep for
either finds the guide as well as the source.

game: both screens are cleared left of the panel when a game begins and when one is over

Something of an attract mode's game was seen left on the playfield in the next.
Rather than find what drew it, VideoClear clears both screens at once at those

events.title: Phase 220 (Graphics): reference-validate 18 graphics test programs (WIP)
events.message:
Phase 220 (Graphics): reference-validate 18 graphics test programs (WIP)

Real AmigaOS 3.1 is the oracle; lxa fixed to match it:
- InitBitMap/AllocBitMap leave BitMap.Flags 0; InitRastPort leaves
  Flags/PenWidth/PenHeight 0
- solid primitives (WritePixel/Draw/RectFill): COMPLEMENT inverts all
  planes in rp->Mask, JAM1|INVERSVID draws nothing, JAM2|INVERSVID uses
  BPen; rp->Mask honoured
- ReadPixel returns -1 outside a layer / in obscured simple-refresh areas
- PixelLine8/PixelArray8: 16-pixel padded row stride, pens copied
  independent of DrawMode
- BltMaskBitMapRastPort: XOR/mask/XOR minterm semantics
- WaitBlit does not wait for the blitter owner; queued QBlit before QBSBlit
- SetRGB4/LoadRGB4 replicate nibbles, SetRGB32CM blue quirk,
  ObtainPen never shares by number, AttachPalExtra without BitMap has no
  free pens, SetChipRev never lowers chip bits
- RPTAG_DrawBounds implemented; CloseFont keeps fonts public; ExtendFont
  matchword/no FSF_TAGGED
- MonitorList holds only the native pal.monitor; Open/CloseMonitor
  semantics
- Regions store RegionRectangles relative to bounds and keep them disjoint

Tests fixed where they asserted lxa guesses or passed invalid input.

events.message:
Phase 230: app corpus manifests & compatibility database

- apps/<App>.json for all 36 apps in ../lxa-apps (16 existing + 20 installed
  from the user's FS-UAE system), plus alias manifests for the case-variant
  symlinks DOPUS/SYSINFO/KP2; old app.json files migrated.
- tools/rdd/corpus.py --check: schema validation, every corpus dir has a
  manifest, executables (hunk files) and assign targets exist, aliases resolve,
  case collisions flagged (exit 77 without LXA_APPS); ctest corpus_check.
- tests/scenarios/apps/*.yaml: one launch scenario per app (titles from a
  discovery twin run on the reference).
- tools/rdd/compat.py + `rdd compat` / `rdd dashboard`: ratings derived from
  twin runs (platinum/gold/silver/bronze/garbage/untested), divergences linked
  to phases (cluster/golden owners, else triage Phase 231); apps/compat.yaml
  generated; dashboard at build/rdd/dashboard.html.
- `rdd loop` runs the app scenarios, refreshes compat.yaml and fails on a
  rating drop (app scenario failures no longer fail the loop by themselves).
- Runner fixes: pylxa and refctl honour LXA_APPS (worktrees); backend_ref
  quotes program paths with spaces and assigns the app root without a
  trailing slash; pylxa wait_window also matches titles set after OpenWindow
  (Intuition tree), like lxaprobe's WAIT_WINDOW.

events.title: Address review: opener failures, greyed-button focus, SPDX header
events.message:
Address review: opener failures, greyed-button focus, SPDX header

An opener that starts but then fails, such as xdg-open with no browser
to run, used to count as success because only the spawn was checked.
open_in_browser now reports the opener's eventual exit on a channel,
which the window polls, and a failure falls back to putting the page's
address on the clipboard. The footer does not wait on that answer,
because xdg-open running a browser itself does not exit until the
browser closes.

While a check is out, the greyed Check for updates button is kept out
of the keyboard and controller focus map, as control_live does for the
configuration screen's dead buttons. It stays in the map if the focus
is already on it, having just pressed it: taking it away would settle
the focus on the close gadget, where a second press closes the panel.

app_update.rs gains the SPDX header its sibling modules carry.

The hi-res layout has two buffer lines per scanline, but it was displayed at

the descriptor's screen geometry carries it so the TEXT overlay stays aligned.

odd scales keep the 1x layout at an integer multiple.

events.title: Add a Check for updates button to the About panel
events.message:
Add a Check for updates button to the About panel

The About panel gains a footer with one button that asks GitHub's
releases API for the latest Copperline release, on a worker thread, and
compares it with the running version by semver precedence (so 1.0.0 is
newer than 1.0.0-rc.1). If a newer release is out, the button becomes
Open release page and hands that release's GitHub page to the host
browser (ShellExecuteW, open, or xdg-open); if no browser opens, the
address goes on the clipboard instead.

Nothing is sent until the button is pressed, and the answer lasts only
for the session. The request carries only the Copperline/<version> user
agent, and the page URL is built from the validated tag rather than
taken from the reply.

The check sits behind a new default-on update-check feature, so builds
without it, such as player, web and libretro, have no button. The shared
HTTP agent moves from gamelib to src/http.rs so the check does not
depend on the game library. semver was already in the dependency tree
through wasmtime, so the Flatpak vendored sources are unchanged.
Windows gains the Win32_UI_Shell windows-sys feature.

events.title: fix(tests): harness refuses an --option key the core never registered
events.message:
fix(tests): harness refuses an --option key the core never registered

The harness applied --option through GET_VARIABLE and silently ignored a
key the core does not register: a typo, a renamed option, or one missing
on this branch measured the defaults and reported a confident null.

Record every key the core registers (SET_VARIABLES, SET_CORE_OPTIONS[_INTL],
SET_CORE_OPTIONS_V2[_INTL]) and, after retro_init, exit 2 naming any
--option key not among them. VJ_HARNESS_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_OPTIONS=1 downgrades
it to a warning for an A/B against an older core. --option without '=' and
options past HARNESS_MAX_OPTIONS were also dropped silently; both fatal now.
The resolved option set prints to stderr on every run, even under --quiet.

A static audit found one casualty: the vj-debug skill's own A/B example used
virtualjaguar_dsp, which does not exist, so that recipe compared two identical
runs. Fixed, along with the same example in harness.h.

Fixes #742

events.title: Treat a real floppy drive as a source
events.message:
Treat a real floppy drive as a source

The Greaseweazle and floppy-controller read routes existed but nothing in
the interface reached them, and the write dialog carried capture fields it
never sent. A disk in a real drive is now opened like any image file:
"Read floppy disk" on an empty pane and in the File menu lists every
Greaseweazle drive and floppy controller, and the capture opens in the pane.

A sector capture takes its geometry from the disk's own boot sector, read
from one track first, falling back to the high-density rate for a 1.44M
disk. A disk without a usable boot sector is refused rather than guessed.
This also replaces a default geometry id that was never valid.

IPF is no longer offered as a capture format, because gw has no IPF
writer. The write dialog drops its stray capture fields and offers a
floppy controller as a destination for a plain .st.

The HDDRIVER distribution floppy ships its driver as AUTO\HDDRIVER.PRG,
so that name is now recognised and installed as HDDRIVER.SYS.

events.title: feat(cia): the C64's CIAs run on ciacore (Spec 888)
events.message:
feat(cia): the C64's CIAs run on ciacore (Spec 888)

CIA 1 and CIA 2 are VICE's core/ciacore.c now, with the c64cia1.c /
c64cia2.c glue ported into c64cia.rs: the keyboard matrix solver
(read_ciapa/read_ciapb, ghost keys included), the joysticks, the POT
selection on port A, the VIC bank and the serial bus on CIA 2's port A,
IRQ from CIA 1, NMI from CIA 2. cia.rs is gone; there is one CIA core.

ciacore.rs grows what the C64 needs and the 1581 did not: VICE's BCD
TOD on its own mains alarm (the deterministic #else branch of
ciacore_inttod's drift correction), the model switch (6526 / 6526A,
from the model row, as c64scmodel.c gives it), write_offset 0 (x64sc),
the read_ciaicr / read_sdr / pulse_ciapc hooks, a side-effect-free
peek. The 1581 keeps its 8520 event counter as a TOD variant. The
snapshot module now writes ACK/NEW_IRQFLAGS with SMW_DB (8-byte
doubles) and reads them with SMR_B, as VICE does.

The CPU core replays the CIAs' cia_set_int_clk calls into IntStatus at
their own clocks (clk_inc and PROCESS_ALARMS), instead of sampling a
level each cycle; the run loop's CIA restamp is gone. The cia_alarm_check
switch is gone with the second path it selected.

Checkpoints store the whole ciacore context (CiaSnapshot v3, alarm
clocks included) and restore exactly; a v2 record converts with a note
in Machine::restore_notes. VSF CIA modules (c64re-own and real VICE)
read and write VICE's ciacore 2.5 layout; the old 48-byte record
converts with a note.

Issue #3: a mask-only write to $DC0D/$DD0D no longer acknowledges —
cia_icr_latch_gate reproduces it on the booted machine (IRQ re-enters,
main loop starves; CIA 2's NMI stays one edge). The iso CIA corpus
replays record-for-record against its goldens (iso_cia_gate).

Re-blessed: cia_alarm_check_gate digests (the chip changed: 6526 IRQ a
cycle late, ICR ack through the IFR line, intta's alarm skip, VICE TOD).
TOD gate checks moved by at most a cycle per mains tick (VICE's drift
correction) and the time-equals-alarm flag VICE raises on a write. The
6526A block exists now: c64c rows are refused for their glue only.

events.title: fix(887): a silent socket holds nothing; only an A/V subscriber or a trace does
events.message:
fix(887): a silent socket holds nothing; only an A/V subscriber or a trace does

The first build counted every connection as holding the idle clock. C64RE's MCP
keeps one WebSocket open for its whole life, so any open Claude window would
have held the daemon forever — the leftover 887 exists to remove.

Now an A/V stream subscriber or a recording trace holds the clock; a plain
connection only resets it with what it sends. Streaming daemons subscribe every
connection to the A/V push on connect, so an RPC-only client connects with
?av=0: no binary frames, no pacing loop started on its account, not a
subscriber. --headless has no A/V stream, so no connection holds it there.
idleExit.holding is "subscriber" | "trace" | null. When the daemon ends, an
open socket is simply closed.

Tests: a silent RPC socket does not hold it, keep_alive and null do, and the
daemon ends under the still-open socket; an A/V subscriber holds a streaming
daemon while an ?av=0 socket does not; a recording trace holds it. daemon 500,
cli 115, 7-game 7/7. Spec, archive decision, README, FEATURES and the play-API
doc (with ?av=0) updated.

events.message:
feat(daemon): --idle-exit and daemon/keep_alive (Spec 887)

C64RE starts the shared daemon detached so it survives a reconnect, and nothing
ever ended it: every closed or killed session left one running.

--idle-exit <s> (default 0 = never) ends the daemon with exit 0 and
"[trx64] idle for N s — exiting" once, for the whole window, no request
arrived (ping counts), no client was connected and no trace was recording. A
connected client or a recording trace holds the clock at now, so the window
starts when the last of them ends. Before exiting, the cartridge and both
drives' disks are persisted exactly as eject does.

daemon/keep_alive {seconds | null} holds it at least that long, null = never
on idle; it replies {armed, armedSeconds, deadlineMs, keptAliveUntilMs,
keptForever, holding}. ping and session/state carry the same idleExit object.

The clock is a pure IdleClock (src/idle.rs) unit-tested for the window, a
request resetting it, keep_alive, null, and holds; tests/idle_exit.rs runs the
binary: nobody there -> exit 0 with the line; a connected client holds it,
keep_alive reports and outlasts the window; a recording trace holds it with
nobody connected. daemon 499, core 731, cli 115, 7-game 7/7.

Spec archived with its decision; README, FEATURES and the play-API doc
describe the flag and the RPC (the ping row and healthcheck said {}).

events.title: fix(daemon): take the port before booting; the .c64retrace grows while recording
events.message:
fix(daemon): take the port before booting; the .c64retrace grows while recording

Two findings from the C64RE test audit.

Port race. Several C64RE servers warm-start a daemon on :4312 at once and the
design has the losers leave quietly. The bind came after the machine boot and
was an expect(), so a loser booted a whole C64 and then panicked (exit 101).
The port is now bound first. EADDRINUSE prints one line — "port N already
owned by another runtime — exiting cleanly" — and exits 0; any other bind
error exits 1 with the OS error; an unparsable --bind exits 2. No panic.

Trace authority. A trace held the whole run in session.trace.buf and wrote the
file only at trace/run/stop: 0 bytes on disk while recording, the daemon's
memory growing with every frame (measured 148 -> 334 MiB over 500 frames of a
c64-cpu+drive8-cpu+iec+memory trace), all of it lost on a crash — against the
rule that the .c64retrace is the authority. TraceState::spill appends the
pending frames once they pass 4 MiB (the first spill creates the file, later
ones append) and once more at stop. The same run writes the same file —
139,529,065 bytes, 7,725,761 events, as before — growing while it records,
memory growing 58 MiB instead of 186. trace/status adds bytesWritten (on disk)
next to bytesBuffered (pending); the stop reply's bytesWritten is the file.

Tests: tests/port_owner.rs holds a port and starts the binary on it — exit 0,
the line, no PANIC, no ROM load or boot. A recording trace has bytes on disk
before stop, holds less than the spill threshold in memory, and stop's
bytesWritten equals the file. daemon 486, core 731, cli 115, traceindex 179,
trace 10, 7-game 7/7.

events.title: fix(sandbox): a sandbox daemon dies with its caller; four smokes onboard again
events.message:
fix(sandbox): a sandbox daemon dies with its caller; four smokes onboard again

The sandbox budget was a timer in the process that started the daemon, so a caller that
died — killed, crashed, its session closed — left the daemon running under PID 1. One
reel daemon ran for a day (2026-10-01). The file's header said the daemon "dies … with
the process"; it did not.

- A keeper (node -e) now sits between caller and daemon. It holds the budget itself
  (plus 5 s, so the caller's reaper can still say why), and polls the caller — ppid
  changed, or kill(parent, 0) failing, since Windows does not reparent. When the caller
  is gone it ends the daemon and removes the scratch dir. close() also kills the daemon
  by the pid the keeper reports, so a platform where killing the keeper cannot forward
  the signal still ends it.
- smoke:sandbox-orphan 5/5: a caller SIGKILLed mid-sandbox → daemon gone within
  seconds, scratch removed; a 3 s budget with the caller alive ends it and says why.
- smoke-859/860/858/863 were red since the onboarding gate: they never onboarded, and
  859/860/858 wrote a `{}` phase-plan.json that project_init rejects as a schema error.
  They now make real projects (project_init, or the service where top-level media must
  stay put) and onboard. All green again.
- Regression: sandbox-prg-start 6/6, d81-drive 5/5, smoke-900 12/12, smoke-814 82/82,

events.message:
feat(sandbox): a .d81 gets a 1581 at drive 8 (#33)

A private machine always had a 1541 at drive 8, so runtime_sandbox_run and
runtime_scene_reel refused every D81 ("a D81 does not fit a 1541: D81 media go into a
1581"). TRX64 0.11.0 has the 1581 and `session/drive_type`; nothing on this side asked.

- The runtime's refusal names the board a medium needs, and that sentence decides: the
  runner switches drive 8 off, sets the board, switches it on, and opens the medium
  again (`openFittingDrive`). C64RE keeps no second opinion about what a medium is.
  Both runners, the starting medium and a disk a step inserts. Private machines only —
  the shared session's drive is never refitted behind the human's back.
- `drive_type: "1541" | "1581"` on both tools fits the board from the start, for an empty
  drive or a D81 that only a later step inserts.
- INSTALL.md: a 1581 needs dos1581-318045-02.bin among the ROMs.
- smoke:d81-drive 5/5: a generated D81 (checked against VICE c1541: dir, read-back,

v0.2.2: PlayCity, speech synthesisers, LambdaSpeak 3 + MP3 module, drive and keyboard sounds; CRTC 1 fixes; DigiBlaster/AmDrum fixed

Sound devices
- PlayCity (TotO): two YMZ294 (six more AY channels, one chip a side) and a Z80 CTC --
  the programmable YMZ clock, CURSOR-driven raster NMIs and IM2 timer interrupts.
- Speech: Amstrad SSA-1 (&FBEE) and dk'tronics (&FBFE), General Instrument's SP0256-AL2 on
  MAME's SP0256 core (BSD-3, third_party/sp0256). Its 2 KB ROM is not shipped; the ROM

- LambdaSpeak 3: its SSA-1 mode, and its serial mode driving a Catalex (YX5300) MP3
  module that plays MP3 files from a folder on the PC (01/001xxx.mp3 ...), decoded with
  minimp3 (CC0, third_party/minimp3). DECtalk/Epson modes are not emulated.
- DigiBlaster and AmDrum were silent (the DAC was never mixed in); fixed and measured.

Machine noises
- Disc drive (motor, head steps, insert, eject) and keyboard clicks from real recordings in

events.title: --clock-mhz: report native-handler call counts at exit (issue #109) (#110)
events.message:
--clock-mhz: report native-handler call counts at exit (issue #109) (#110)

Native library handlers run in zero emulated cycles -- documented, but
previously invisible: a benchmark had no way to see how much of its
work bypassed the cycle count. Found in the wild via
AmigaPorts/m68k-amigaos-gcc#89, where GCC codegen patches were A/B
benchmarked on a real A3000 vs volamos --clock-mhz 25 and a memcpy
benchmark improved 5.3% on hardware but 49.1% under volamos -- the
signature of copies vanishing into exec's native CopyMem.

LibraryTable::dispatch now counts every dispatched call per slot (one
integer hashmap bump; names resolved only at report time) and
accumulates the CopyMem/CopyMemQuick pair's D0 byte size, read before
the handler runs. Runtime::native_call_counts exposes both under the
same clock-rate gating and top-level-run-only boundary as
emulated_cycles. The CLI prints a third report line under --clock-mhz:

  volamos: 183 native library calls ran in zero emulated cycles:
  exec.library/CopyMem x120, ...; CopyMem/CopyMemQuick moved 491520
  bytes natively

Omitted when the guest made no library calls. Docs: CLI-Reference
--clock-mhz section, the zero-cycle warning bullet, --help text, and a
Changelog 0.8 entry.

events.title: Migrate CLI argument parsing to clap (fixes #101) (#108)
events.message:
Migrate CLI argument parsing to clap (fixes #101) (#108)

* Migrate CLI argument parsing from a hand-rolled parser to clap (derive)

Replaces main.rs's ~120-line hand-rolled parse_args_raw loop and ~200-line
hand-maintained print_usage with a clap 4 derive Cli struct. Every flag
keeps its exact spelling and semantics; config::Overrides's Option<T>-based
"explicitly set on the CLI vs. left at a built-in default" merge contract
is unchanged -- clap is never given a default value for anything, and
cli_to_raw() converts the parsed Cli into parse_args_raw's existing
(Overrides, InstrumentationOptions, Option<f64>, String, Vec<String>)
return shape, so resolve()/main's config-file layering is untouched.

Key implementation points:

- --fpu/--no-fpu, --jit/--no-jit, --defaults/--no-defaults each use two
  ArgAction::SetTrue flags with bidirectional overrides_with, so the last
  one given on the command line wins (matching the old parser), then
  collapse to Option<bool> by hand in cli_to_raw.
- --sanitize-uninit implies --sanitize, applied in cli_to_raw rather than
  via clap (clap has no simple "set this other field" action).
- Existing value parsers (parse_byte_size, parse_cpu_type, parse_clock_mhz,
  split_name_value, the 0x-hex ignore-pc parser) are reused as-is via thin
  per-flag wrapper functions passed as clap value_parsers, so their unit
  tests keep exercising the real logic.
- Help text carries over print_usage's full prose (including the two
  trailing "SYS:/C:/S:/... resolve out of the box" and "~/.volamos
  supplies defaults" paragraphs via after_long_help), grouped into
  Logging/Filesystem/Machine/Execution/Instrumentation/Networking
  help_headings. print_usage is deleted.
- Added --version (long-only; clap's auto -V short alias collides with
  our existing -V/--volume, so disable_version_flag + a manual
  ArgAction::Version field).

Trailing-args semantics (requirement: `volamos prog -v --stack` must pass
-v and --stack to the guest verbatim, not re-parse them) turned out to
need more than trailing_var_arg + allow_hyphen_values: empirically, clap
4.6's trailing_var_arg only stops an *unrecognized* token from erroring
once the variadic positional starts consuming -- it still matches a
flag clap knows about (e.g. --stack) anywhere in the whole argument list.
Fixed with a small hand-written split_program_boundary() that finds the
<program> boundary before clap ever runs (using a VALUE_FLAGS table to
know which flags consume a following token), feeding clap only the
option-prefix + <program>, and setting guest_args on the parsed Cli by
hand afterward.

Intentional behavior change: an unrecognized --flag before <program> is
now a clean clap error, instead of the old parser's silent fallback of
treating any unrecognized token as <program> itself. One related edge
case this changes: a program file whose name itself starts with a `-`
would previously have been accepted as <program>; it's now treated as an
unknown flag (an extremely unlikely real-world name).

-h/--help and --version now go through clap's own ClapError::exit() in
main() for the real binary (full formatted help, exit 0), while the
test-only parse_args_raw/parse_args wrapper keeps the pre-clap contract
of Err(String::new()) for help so the existing test suite's plumbing
needed only minimal adjustment (error-message substring assertions
updated to match clap's wording; the exact-string "missing <program>
argument" assertion loosened to a substring check against clap's
standard required-argument error).

Added tests: unknown flag before <program> errors; flags after <program>
reach the guest untouched even when they look like recognized flags
(the specific case split_program_boundary exists for); --fpu/--no-fpu
last-wins in both directions; -V/-a repeated-flag order preservation.

cargo test -p volamos: 171/171 passing. cargo clippy -p volamos
--all-targets -- -D warnings: clean. cargo fmt -p volamos: clean.
Manually smoke-tested --help, an unknown-flag error, --version, and
fixtures/echoargs end-to-end (plain and with -v).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GNNXMtYaZVHe8ihLL2GsrY

* Honor clap's -- escape at the program boundary; derive value-flag spellings from clap metadata

Review fixes on top of the clap migration:

- split_program_boundary() now treats a standalone -- as clap's
  end-of-options escape: the next token is <program> no matter how
  flag-like it looks, and everything after it is the guest's argv.
  Previously the scanner pushed a dash-leading program into the half
  clap parses and mistook the first real guest argument for <program>,
  so 'volamos -- -prog one two' ran -prog with argv 'two' -- 'one' was
  silently dropped (and clap's own unknown-flag error actively
  recommends the -- spelling, so the escape has to work).

- The hand-synced VALUE_FLAGS table is gone: value_flag_spellings()
  derives the -X/--long spellings of every value-taking flag from
  clap's own Command metadata (CommandFactory), so the boundary scan
  can never drift out of sync with Cli's flag declarations. A test
  pins the current set so an unexpected change is still visible.

- New regression tests: the -- escape (with and without preceding
  flags), the spellings pin, and --clock-mhz=25/--stack=256K =-form
  values (a user-reported failure of the old hand-rolled parser, which
  treated '--clock-mhz=25' as the program name).

CLI-Reference: sync the usage block with the full current flag surface
(--defaults/--no-defaults, --volumes-dir, --dirty-heap, --net were
missing even before this branch), document --version, the --flag=value
spellings, the unknown-flag error + ./-foo / -- -foo escape for

Four previously-working command-line behaviors change: a bare
dash-leading program path is now an unknown-flag error (./-foo or

events.title: Make Amiga mice work and let the mouse port be chosen in the menu
events.message:
Make Amiga mice work and let the mouse port be chosen in the menu

Optical Amiga mice jumped around and lost movement. Two causes, both
fixed and tested on a MEGA65 R6:

- The framework discharges the paddle lines (pins 5 and 9) about 2000
  times a second. That upset the mouse, so pins 1-3 toggled on their
  own. The discharge now only runs when the 1351 mouse is selected.
- The IKBD polls the mouse pins in software and misses steps of fast
  mice. quadmouse.vhd decodes the Amiga mouse in hardware and passes
  the movement to the IKBD as mouse events, like the 1351 does.

The right button of an Amiga mouse (pin 9) now works as well.

"Controllers & ports" now has a mouse type (Atari, Amiga, C64 1351)
and a mouse port (port 1 or 2, the other one is the joystick). The
1351 also works in port 2. The menu has 93 items, so stcfg must be
recreated with 93 bytes.

events.title: - Atari ST/Amiga: Comlete combat rewrite. Player and AI now uses same front/aft shields, energy banks and energy recharges. Unified player and AI shields, energy banks, recharge, weapon resistance, maximum speed, turning limits and missile capacity for all purchasable hulls. AI ships currently spawn without Energy Units.
events.message:
- Atari ST/Amiga: Comlete combat rewrite. Player and AI now uses same front/aft shields, energy banks and energy recharges. Unified player and AI shields, energy banks, recharge, weapon resistance, maximum speed, turning limits and missile capacity for all purchasable hulls. AI ships currently spawn without Energy Units.
- Unified laser and guided-missile damage for player-versus-AI, AI-versus-player and AI-versus-AI combat. Removed the random AI damage multiplier while preserving existing aiming, hit probabilities and rating-based laser selection. Guided missiles now use 60 base damage.
* Rebalanced hull durability relative to C64 Elite: Unbound, using Cobra Mk III as the reference. Separate missile resistance reproduces the reference missile hit counts.
* Cougar and Constrictor now have finite laser resistance derived from their Military laser ratio. All laser classes can damage them during their vulnerable mission phases.
* Preserved fractional damage so weaker lasers remain effective against heavily protected hulls.
* Added a one-frame light-blue flash when an active front or rear shield is hit, including AI combat, missiles and surviving collisions. Distant spheres flash; dots and crosses do not. The effect expires off-screen and is suppressed when a collision destroys the ship.
* Fixed missiles disappearing without an explosion when their target survives the impact.
* Missile indicators now show zero to four slots according to hull capacity. Larger magazines display at most four loaded indicators while retaining their actual ammunition capacity.
* Removed shields from the Worm / Escape Capsule while retaining energy recharge. Without recharge between hits, a fully charged capsule is destroyed by the sixth Pulse laser hit.
* Added a green identification square while an I request is pending, including views without a laser. Successful identification clears it; U cancels identification and unarms the missile. Adjusted the square one logical pixel upward.
* Remapped Planet Data ship miniature colours to the closest available original shades without changing the planet or inhabitant palette. Supports Planets ON/OFF and scaled Amiga displays.

events.title: Landscape goes fullscreen on first touch; second-finger tap jumps
events.message:
Landscape goes fullscreen on first touch; second-finger tap jumps

Browsers refuse requestFullscreen outside a user gesture, so rotating
into landscape play arms a one-shot request that fires on the next
tap or keypress.  Leaving fullscreen by hand stays out until the next
rotation into landscape, so it doesn't fight the player.

While one finger holds a direction, a second finger presses fire for
as long as it is down, so direction plus fire leaps (or glides) as on
the joystick.  A second finger before the hold registers is ignored,
and its lost capture or cancel no longer cancels the hold.

events.title: Add native virtual keyboard typing for touch-first browsers (#364)
events.message:
Add native virtual keyboard typing for touch-first browsers (#364)

Touch-first browser users can now open their device keyboard from the
emulator sidebar and type into C64, VIC-20, Oric, or Apple II. Committed
text becomes timed presses and releases at the emulated keyboard matrix
or encoder, so input also reaches programs that read the hardware
directly.

The Keyboard button is hidden in native desktop apps and mouse-first
browsers, where physical and accessibility keyboards already use the
existing input path. Browser availability follows the primary pointer
capability and updates when it changes. Focus loss, Pause, Stop, and
monitor opening cancel queued text; the browser bridge handles
composition, paste, Return, and Backspace without duplicate input.

Browser frame processing also yields to the browser event loop after
each frame, preventing an overrun loop from starving input and painting.
A regression test reproduces the starvation before the fix.

## Known limitation

The native keyboard is intended for typing. Each character is held for
three emulator frames, followed by a two-frame release gap. It cannot
reliably provide continuous holds or simultaneous controls for games,
including WASD keyboard joystick movement. Dedicated touch controls and
machine-specific Avalonia keyboard layouts remain separate future work.

## Validation

- Browser and Desktop Debug builds passed with no warnings or errors.
- Systems suite: 1,548 passed, 18 skipped; keyboard lifecycle, machine
input, and browser scheduling regressions passed.
- All 14 browser JavaScript tests passed; native keyboard script has
100% line, branch, and function coverage.
- Independent build/test CI and Sonar branch analysis passed; no open
Major-or-higher Sonar issues.
- Beta publish completed successfully. User verified native keyboard
typing in C64 BASIC on iPhone Brave and ordinary macOS accessibility
keyboard input.
- Agent live UI verification was blocked by browser site permissions and
desktop automation permissions; other machines have automated input
coverage but have not been manually verified on an iPhone.

events.title: Say what a greyed storage row actually needs
events.message:
Say what a greyed storage row actually needs

Two of the launcher's `disabled_reason` strings spliced "achievable
elsewhere" into "this control needs X", and both sent the reader to a
dead end:

- The IDE bay rows said "needs A600/A1200/A4000 or Lide", but
  `has_ide()` is Gayle or an A4000 and nothing else. A Lide board
  carries drives in its own `[lide] drive0..3` fields on its own
  sub-page; these rows never enable for one, however it is configured.
- The CD rows said "needs CDTV/CD32 (or SCSI/IDE/Lide)", but
  `[cd] image` only ever feeds the machine's built-in CDTV/CD32 drive.
  A CD-ROM on a bus is a drive slot holding a CD image -- which
  `is_cd_image_path` attaches as ATAPI -- and these rows never reach it.

Both now state the row's own enable condition, with the pointer to
where the other thing is done after a semicolon rather than inside the
condition as another way to turn the row on. The remaining `reason(...)`
strings were swept for the same shape and describe only their own row.

A greyed row of the `GreyedAs::Reason` kind draws its text free from the
control column's left edge, unboxed and untruncated -- unlike the
dimmed-value kinds, which pass theirs through `truncate_to_width`. So
the string is the limit, and a longer one simply runs off the panel's
right edge: the first wording tried here was 568px against the 422px
the column has. `every_greyed_reason_fits_the_column` now walks every
model against every page and fails on one that does not fit, rather
than leaving it to be noticed in a screenshot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: The side shows, looked at and played: sets, counts, and a swing that lands
events.message:
The side shows, looked at and played: sets, counts, and a swing that lands

Each of the seven shows was photographed on both of its floors
(tools/shots.py --shows walks in through a real doorway and plays it
with scripted keys) and driven by the harness.  Every change below is
held by a check in verify_minigames.py that fails on the old binary.

All of them: briefing cards centred, three or four rules, a green
SPACE prompt and an ESC line; the verdict is one still picture, green
for good news and red for bad, that takes a key after its first
second; the top line is the count beside its icon on the left, energy
and lives in the shaft's own glyphs in the middle (repainted only when
they change), the clock on the right.  Every set is now built into the
hidden page, and a reloaded shaft forgets the range and drill rules.

Canteen: doors the queue walks out of, a service ladder, a shelf of
twelve rations that empties one tin per serve, SPACE serves like Z,
a wasted tin is heard.  A guard served inside his doorway (x 0-1) used
to wrap to 255 and stride on, drawn past the screen's end and over
the sprite code at #8000 -- the harness crashed on it; he now leaves.

Rat shift: red rats with yellow eyes (they were navy on black), the
count's rat turns white the moment the white one is hit, a bell at
fifteen, walls and a pipe manifold around the hatches.

The Hook: a claw cabinet -- lid, bulbs, posts, rail -- a cable down to
the claw, the mechanic facing the machine, drops left on the left
berth with a hook beside them, and prizes that say what they paid.

Black market: the whole ceiling main turns red when the Eye opens,
with half a second's grace to stop; catches counted beside a bundle.

Boiler: the whip is tested on every frame the rope is out and any aim
bats a falling pellet, the diagonal included.  The slag is red-hot in
fixed pens on every floor (it used to take the crust's colour), the
drum has a crown and walls so it no longer climbs the side gutters,
and the spare pellets are counted.  Its pace is unchanged.

Firing line: the sheet's light, a salvo you hear, and a height that
no longer follows from the last salvo's side.

The manuals (and their PDFs) and docs/minigames.md describe the cards
and the top line as they now are.

events.title: Speed up the entry phase and the common blitters
events.message:
Speed up the entry phase and the common blitters

Entry-phase passes drop from about 126% to 98% of a frame (28 -> 34 fps);
the game overall goes from about 31 to 38 fps.

- DrawSprite16x16 walks the line table in the shadow registers and copies
  with LDI.
- ClearBitmapRect jumps into an unrolled clear instead of a byte loop with
  memory counters.
- In-play stars use a dedicated loop with the line table lookup inlined.
- CheckAndRestoreDockedEnemies only checks the one or two formation rows a
  footprint can touch, and returns early below the formation.
- The entry phase folds its marking pass into the move pass and the
  all-docked check into the restore pass.
- line_tab now lives on the dead load-image copy of the relocated disk
  code, freeing 544 bytes.
