events.title: Make Avalonia Browser usable on small screens with zoom and panning (#362)
events.message:
Make Avalonia Browser usable on small screens with zoom and panning (#362)

The Avalonia Browser app previously clipped its desktop layout on small
screens, making emulator controls and enlarged displays difficult to
reach. This change fits the complete canvas to the available window and
provides zoom, Reset, scrolling, and touch panning while keeping the
toolbar at a stable size on iPhone.

- Measure the Avalonia content dynamically so larger emulator Scale
settings remain reachable; hide the collapsible toolbar when the
unscaled app fits.
- Center overlays, including nested acknowledgments, within the visible
canvas area and route scrolling into an open overlay.
- Offer manual orientation switching where supported, with dismissible
guidance when the browser cannot lock orientation.
- Fix Safari Download & Run by leaving browser User-Agent selection to
the browser, guard zero-duration timing measurements, and revise the
Safari compatibility notice.
- Run browser behavior checks in independent CI and Sonar, import
JavaScript coverage, and verify manual Sonar analyses against the
requested branch and commit.

Validation: Browser Debug build passed without warnings; browser
behavior and instrumentation checks passed; branch build/test, Sonar
analysis, and beta publishing workflows passed. The published beta's
zoom controls were manually verified by the user in Brave on iPhone.
Automated browser checks model the DOM and browser APIs; physical
orientation locking and older Safari compatibility remain
device-dependent.

events.title: Add dependency vulnerability checks (#361)
events.message:
Add dependency vulnerability checks (#361)

High- and critical-severity package advisories do not currently block
pull requests. Add two independent, SHA-pinned checks: GitHub Dependency
Review rejects newly introduced vulnerable dependencies, and a
full-solution NuGet restore audits direct and transitive packages with
high/critical advisories treated as errors. Audit-source failures also
fail the NuGet job, while the existing build/test job remains
independent.

The NuGet audit uses nuget.org's vulnerability-data source and runs with
the SDK pinned by `global.json`.

Validation: full-solution `dotnet restore -p:AuditPipeline=true --force`
passed locally using the available .NET 10.0.201 SDK; the CI job
installs the repo-pinned 10.0.401 SDK. The XML and workflow YAML parse,
and the audit MSBuild properties evaluate as intended.

After these checks pass on this PR, add their observed GitHub Actions
check names to the existing strict `master` ruleset.

events.title: Load in black and redraw the title logo with ordered dithering
events.message:
Load in black and redraw the title logo with ordered dithering

The loader blacks out all inks before loading the splash screen and sets its
colours once loaded, then blacks them out again before running the game.
The game starts with an all-black palette and sets its colours only after
the title screen is drawn, so leftovers in video RAM never show.

The title logo is regenerated from the HD arcade art: regions are reduced
with outline-weighted voting, inner outlines become black gaps between the
letters, stars and the white border are dropped, and regions are filled
with solid pens or a 4x4 ordered dither.

events.title: GEMDOS HD : un opcode magique n'est plus rejoué au retour d'interruption
events.message:
GEMDOS HD : un opcode magique n'est plus rejoué au retour d'interruption

L'appel hôte ($0008-$000A) était servi AVANT execute(), qui pouvait alors
prendre une IRQ en attente au lieu du NOP : le PC empilé désignait encore
l'opcode, rejoué au rte (Fread servi deux fois, bloc sauté — TOSFC Verify ;
même cause pour le défaut --fastfdc de fastfdc_format.py).

Comme Hatari (OpCode_GemDos), l'opcode est désormais traité dans son
gestionnaire d'instruction : délégué Moira illegalOpcodeHook appelé par
execIllegal (patch vendorisé documenté dans NEOST_VENDOR.md).

Garde : auto-test série gemdos_irq (tools/make_gemdos_irq_test.py) —
3000 Fwrite + 3000 Fread contrôlés sous VBL/Timer C, et gdforced (IRQ
prenable pile à la frontière de $0008). Les trois verdicts échouent sur
l'ancien code.

events.title: Check release prerequisites before changing the VSCode changelog (#360)
events.message:
Check release prerequisites before changing the VSCode changelog (#360)

The VS Code release helper could rewrite the changelog and then fail
during its commit because pre-commit needed a Python version that was
not installed. It now checks required tools and GitHub access, verifies
the installed hook's configured Python versions, and prepares hook
environments before changing the changelog. `--check-tools` runs the
same preflight without starting a release.

Validated with `bash -n`, `release.sh --check-tools`, and 22 isolated
success/failure checks covering missing Python, hook setup, GitHub
access, and startup ordering. The repository's pre-commit hook was also
run for the changed files (no matching docs-requirements files to
check).

events.title: fix(app): scroll through a standing top-anchor continuously, not in one jump (SQ-1666)
events.message:
fix(app): scroll through a standing top-anchor continuously, not in one jump (SQ-1666)

window_wrapped_rows had two unrelated windowing formulas: an exact
[anchor_row, n) pin at scroll == 0, and a totally unrelated "last `rows`
rows of the whole array" slice at any other scroll. The first unit of
scroll past 0 jumped from "the anchor's own couple of rows" to a window
sliced from a completely different part of the transcript — reported
after returning from Anchorhead's full-screen picture (and confirmed to
reproduce after any game-driven clear while scrollback is still short).

anchored_window_bounds (crates/app/src/render/transcript.rs) replaces the
cutover with one continuous formula: while the anchor's own content still
fits the viewport, each unit of scroll grows the pinned window backward by
exactly one row (bottom edge pinned at `n`) until the window fills the
viewport, then hands off to the ordinary backward slide from exactly where
growth left off. anchored_max_scroll is the matching fix for every caller
that clamps a scroll offset (page/half-page scroll, the mouse-wheel step,
apply_frame's post-frame clamp): the old `n - rows` cut the reachable
range short by the anchor's own growth padding, which would have stranded
the oldest rows unreachable by scroll even after the jump itself was fixed.

The v6 raster path (render::screen::build_main_text) had hand-duplicated
the exact same two-formula cutover (anchor_row looked up only behind a
`scroll == 0` gate) — fixed the same way, sharing the same two helpers,
so the bug's shape can't drift back in on one path while the other is
fixed.

pager.rs's top_anchor_fits/follow-ease logic only ever looks at scroll ==
0, which this fix leaves untouched, so no change was needed there (full
pager test suite reverified).

Updated the existing unit tests that pinned the old jump as "expected"
(window_wrapped_rows_windows_and_top_anchors,
an_anchor_at_the_end_is_an_empty_screen_not_an_absent_one) to the
mathematically correct continuous values, and added
sq1666_continuous_anchor_scroll.rs driving real Anchorhead frames through
the real render pipeline, falsified by temporarily reverting the fix and
confirming it reproduces the exact reported jump.

events.title: fix(app): make /reset-game's "Delete saved progress" actually delete saved progress (SQ-1665)
events.message:
fix(app): make /reset-game's "Delete saved progress" actually delete saved progress (SQ-1665)

Two bugs, both in host::reset::reset_game's delete_data arm:

1. It deleted default.lanthorn without flushing the background
   archive-writer first. The per-turn auto-save the player's last move just
   enqueued can still be mid-flight on that thread; delete_auto_persistent
   racing ahead of it only looked like a deletion, and the background write
   landed moments later and resurrected default.lanthorn with the old
   game's data. host::persist::write_save_state already flushes before its
   own synchronous write to the same path (SQ-1184) — reset_game's delete
   path was missing that same ordering.

2. "Delete saved progress" never touched the quick-save slot
   (quick-save.lanthorn), even though it's an explicit, player-confirmed
   request to wipe everything the host could resume from — a different
   concern from the ordinary per-turn auto-save that quick_save_state_path
   is deliberately protected against clobbering.

storage::delete_quick_save is new, called alongside delete_auto_persistent.
The quick-save itself is always written synchronously (via
write_save_state), so no flush-ordering race applies to it.

Regression tests: reset_game_with_delete_data_flushes_a_pending_background_
write_before_deleting falsifies deterministically (enqueues a job with
several MB of incompressible bytes so its Deflate pass reliably outlasts
the synchronous delete, then forces the race to resolve before asserting);
reset_game_with_delete_data_removes_auto_sidecars and two new storage.rs
unit tests cover the quick-save deletion scope.

Add a two-player mode and fix collision loop register clobbers

Press 1 (or FIRE) for one player, 2 for two players. Players alternate on
every lost life and resume exactly where they left off: per-player state is
one block swapped with a copy kept in undisplayed video RAM. The HUD shows
HIGH, 1UP and 2UP with the active label blinking; a player out of lives sees
GAME OVER while the other plays on. At the end a results screen compares
both players and names the winner before each qualifying player enters
initials.

Also fix two collision bugs that corrupted memory: killing a tractor-beam
Boss clobbered the missile loop's IX/DE, and shooting a captured fighter
clobbered the missile counter, zeroing data up into the enemy table.

events.message:
fix(zztop): resync interlaced parity cadence and fall back to default monitor

Address the sampling-calibration review findings by mirroring the ZZCapture
patterns:

- vcap_sampling_measure: when an interlaced run repeatedly lands on the same
  field parity (snapshot polling + Zorro reads can skip an even number of
  fields), call WaitTOF() to break the cadence, matching ZZCapture
  measure_phase. The bounded comparison cap is retained.
- vcap_sampling_open_screen: when the explicit PAL/NTSC monitor driver is not
  loaded, fall back to the unqualified native monitor key and validate its
  standard, lace, and 24-bit palette before declaring the sampling mode
  unavailable, matching ZZCapture open_screen.

Experiment 6: the arcade sound driver on Paula

A 68000 port of the sound driver, called at 121 Hz from a CIA timer, with
the three tone voices on Paula channels 0-2 and the fighter explosion as a
noise loop on channel 3. A scripted run in FS-UAE logs what it sends to
Paula and matches the arcade model on all 6,774 ticks. Measured cost: 5 to
19 raster lines per frame depending on how much is playing.

events.title: fix(gate): only an orphaned temp daemon is a leak
events.message:
fix(gate): only an orphaned temp daemon is a leak

The leftover-daemon guard counted every trx64-daemon on a temp project that appeared
during the run, so another session's reel sandbox, started mid-gate and alive under its
own MCP server, blocked a push on 2026-10-01. A leak is a detached daemon whose parent is
gone — parent PID 1 — and that is now the only kind counted. Checked both ways: a live
sandbox under its MCP server is ignored, an orphan named trx64-daemon --project /tmp/… is
still caught.

release: 0.5.1

Patch: no MCP tool schema changed since 0.5.0 (the generated surface is identical).

events.title: ZZTop: redesigned Capture window, sampling calibration and live geometry
events.message:
ZZTop: redesigned Capture window, sampling calibration and live geometry

Rebuild the Scandoubler Capture window around one Automatic action plus
live manual fields (phase, crop, capture window) seeded from current
card state. Add the 'Calibrate Sampling' flow: a 256-colour pattern
screen drives a 64-bin C28 phase sweep that selects the cleanest eye,
with Enter persisting the phase and Esc restoring the entry phase, plus
a live phase-eye readout and fine/coarse nudge controls. Expose the
firmware's capture-window geometry (request/applied readback and
serial-ACKed apply) and input-standard display. Wire the new vcap
sampling and client sources into the ZZTop and ZZCapture builds.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Add acknowledged native-video calibration and geometry-ACK client
events.message:
Add acknowledged native-video calibration and geometry-ACK client

New shared register client (zz_vcap_client) driving the firmware's
native capture-phase and capture-window features through ordered 16-bit
MMIO, with stable-read, phase check/apply and a capture-with-geometry
helper. Adds the geometry-ACK client (request/applied serial pairs so a
write is only trusted once the firmware echoes the matching serial),
the live-value edit model (a field only becomes a saved override when
actually edited), and the phase-domain live helpers. Host suites cover
the client, geometry, edit, sampling-sweep screen and lifecycle paths.

events.title: Amiga version: tdport-amiga, the whole game
events.message:
Amiga version: tdport-amiga, the whole game

A faithful C/SDL3 port of the Amiga release in tdport/src/amiga, built with
-DTDPORT_AMIGA=ON. td is loaded into a big-endian 68000 memory image with
the globals at their D:xxxx addresses; the custom chips and the parts of
graphics.library the game uses are emulated (Views and copper lists,
sprites, the blitter, a four-channel Paula mixer), and the game runs from
the .adf directly. All of the game is ported: title and car selection,
the drive (simulation, renderer, sounds), the gas station, results, high
scores and the ending.

Timing is NTSC (60 Hz, drive frame 12 Hz). The original's bugs are fixed
by default; --original-bugs restores them. High scores are saved beside
the disk image, which is never written to. Text uses the CC BY
"Amiga Topaz" recreation (licenses/amiga-topaz), as topaz.font is in the
Kickstart ROM.

events.title: fix(app): rescue a closed primary window's undrained text instead of losing it (SQ-1663)
events.message:
fix(app): rescue a closed primary window's undrained text instead of losing it (SQ-1663)

Counterfeit Monkey rebuilds its whole window tree the instant its opening
Q&A's first answer completes, closing and reopening windows 1-3 under the
same ids. `AppGlk::window_close` removed the old window's `BufBuf` outright,
discarding whatever it had printed and the host had not drained yet — so the
reply to "Can you hear me?" and the lead-in to "Do you remember our name?"
were silently destroyed, surfacing one turn later as what looked like a
missing line of story text.

Rescue a closing PRIMARY window's undrained log into a new
`orphaned_primary` bucket and prepend it on the next `take_transcript`/
`take_transcript_elems` drain. `orphaned_primary` also has to ride along in
`DisplaySnapshot`: `GlulxSession::silent_look`'s own internal "look" probe
triggers the same one-time window rebuild, and without restoring this field
too, the probe's own (meant-to-be-discarded) output leaked into the next
real turn past its own snapshot/restore.

Confirmed via a real headless trace of every put_text/window_close/
window_open call against CounterfeitMonkey-11.gblorb, and falsified by
reverting the fix and watching the new regression test fail with the
originally reported shape.

Completes: SQ-1663

events.title: feat(scenario): Then lines a runner decides, and `c64re scenario run` (Spec 900)
events.message:
feat(scenario): Then lines a runner decides, and `c64re scenario run` (Spec 900)

A .feature file's Then lines were parsed, classified and never read, so a project that
tests its builds with scenarios (LN_Engine: 25 files, real carts) had an agent judge
every run, and nothing make or CI could call.

- The check notation is the `wait until` predicates said as facts: `$8EF2 is $01`,
  `$40 is $26 $40 …` (bytes in order), `is not`, `is one of`, `@lens` (cpu/ram/io/rom/
  cart, as read_memory), `the CPU is at $XXXX`, `the screen shows "…"`. A line that
  starts like a check and does not parse is a parse issue, not prose; prose is
  UNCHECKED, never a failure.
- A Then is decided where it stands: each criterion records its line and the number of
  steps before it, and the sandbox runner decides it right after that step.
- `Feature:` lines are read as Gherkin writes them (every LN_Engine file starts with one).
- `c64re scenario run <files|dirs> [--scenario] [--json] [--project] [--jobs N]`: a fresh
  private machine per scenario through runtime_sandbox_run's runner, one line per scenario
  (PASS/FAIL/UNCHECKED/SKIP/ERROR), a FAIL names line, expectation and actual bytes;
  unparsed lines are reported and fail the run while the rest still runs; exit 1.
- runtime_sandbox_run takes `Then …` entries in steps, decided in place, reported in a
  `checks:` section; prose there is refused.
- Gates: e2e:900-checks (hermetic, in gates.yml) 23/23; smoke:900 12/12 against a PRG
  gated on joystick fire, so a check decided in the wrong place gives the wrong answer.
  smoke:814 82/82 and smoke:sandbox-prg-start 6/6 after the parser change. On
  LN_Engine's carts, read-only: 25 files → 39 scenarios; no file in the project touched.

Numbered 900, out of sequence: 885 went to PR #31 (large-project load), opened against
a master on which this was not yet pushed.

events.title: perf(885): a large project loads in seconds, not minutes
events.message:
perf(885): a large project loads in seconds, not minutes

Measured on a 23k-entity project (D42 Analysis): the workspace UI took
about a minute to be usable and agent_onboard / project_status cost
25 s / 8 s on every call. TRX64 started in under a second.

- D1 syncWorkflowState writes workflow-state.json only when the state
  changed apart from timestamps. Rewriting it on every read changed a
  file in the audit fingerprint, so the audit cache never hit
  (/api/audit 9.2 s -> 1.2 s).
- D2 the workflow phase gates read counts (records.counts() plus a new
  SQL groundedFindingCount(), equal to the projection: 7226 = 7226)
  instead of projecting every entity and finding.
- D3 workspace server: compact JSON, gzip for JSON/text bodies
  (/api/workspace 185 MB -> 7.4 MB on the wire).
- D4 /api/workspace cached per project until a file in knowledge/ or

events.title: fix(core): charge a 68K long write's bus cycles before the GPU/DSP sync
events.message:
fix(core): charge a 68K long write's bus cycles before the GPU/DSP sync

The 8/16-bit write paths charge the bus cycle, then sync, then write.  The
long-write path synced first and let its two word halves charge afterwards,
so the catch-up was computed from the pre-access timestamp.  Charge both
cycles up front and run the halves uncharged.

No behaviour change today: the 68K's charge for any $F00000+ address is 0
(I/O bus is faster than its own bus cycle), and those are the only addresses
the sync acts on.  This keeps the three paths in the same order if that
cost ever becomes non-zero.

reported shape: session one locks the avatar via a confirmed pickup and
persists the sidecar, session two reuses the same home dir with zero

events.title: fix(app): skip the pager's follow-ease while a top-anchored clear still fits (SQ-1661)
events.message:
fix(app): skip the pager's follow-ease while a top-anchored clear still fits (SQ-1661)

An ordinary command right after a game-driven screen clear (Anchorhead's
intro sequence is the report) briefly jumped the story screen back to
whatever the clear's top-anchor was hiding, then scrolled quickly back
down to the fresh line.

Root cause: `pager::apply_frame`'s follow-ease (SQ-1595) measures its
FROM/TO values against the transcript's FULL wrapped-row count, a
coordinate space `render::transcript::window_wrapped_rows` abandons the
moment a top-anchored view is showing its content in full (`scroll == 0`
is reinterpreted there as "N rows back from the bottom of the WHOLE
transcript" instead of "the anchor"). Arming an ease while the anchor
still holds eases `transcript_scroll` through non-zero intermediate
values, and every one of those frames renders through the wrong branch
and can reach back into whatever scrollback sits above the anchor.

Fix: thread whether the current frame is showing a top-anchored view in
full (`render::transcript::top_anchor_fits`, shared by
`window_wrapped_rows` and the new callers so the two can't drift again)
through `TranscriptRender`/`StoryPaneMetrics`/`RasterMetrics`/`PaneRects`
into `pager::apply_frame`, which now skips arming the ease in that case —
the new output just appends below the still-pinned content, so nothing
needs to move. The raster (v6) path gets the same fix for free, sharing
the one helper rather than re-deriving the condition.

Falsified: reverting the `!top_anchored_fits` guard reproduces the bug in
both the new pager unit test and the new real-game Anchorhead regression
test (crates/app/tests/suites/sq1661_topanchor_followease.rs).

fix(app): scroll old content off the top on every game-driven clear again (SQ-1660)

SQ-1656 made a preserving game-driven screen clear (SQ-1654's
is_screen_reprint said "different screen, don't truncate") skip the
render-facing top-anchor pin, so the fresh content fell back to
ordinary bottom-sticking scrollback instead of being pinned to the
top. In practice this stacked unrelated screens together in one
viewport with zero visual indication a clear had happened — reported
on Anchorhead's intro/quote sequence.

Revert the render-facing behavior: apply_game_driven_result now always
calls state.mark_screen_clear() (collapse or preserve alike), so
top_anchor moves in lockstep with clear_anchor on every game-driven
clear, instantly (no scroll animation) and without affecting
truncate_transcript's own collapse-vs-preserve decision (SQ-1654's
data-preservation guarantee is untouched — state.transcript still
keeps every preserved screen in full, reachable by scrolling up).

Removed the now-dead mark_screen_clear_preserving_top_anchor and its
direct unit tests; rewrote sq1656_preserve_clear_top_anchor.rs's
Anchorhead case to assert the restored per-clear top-anchor behavior
(only the latest screen in the default render, prior screens still in
state.transcript, no scroll_anim armed) instead of the "all screens
visible at once" behavior this reverts. Falsified by temporarily
restoring the old preserving branch: the rewritten test reproduced the

events.title: fix(app): show the inventory dock's registry name, not the live word-join (SQ-1659)
events.message:
fix(app): show the inventory dock's registry name, not the live word-join (SQ-1659)

render::inventory_dock::carried_line already cross-references a carried
item's mapper registry record for its "found Room, turn N" clause, but
built the row's NAME from the live `name` parameter regardless —
grammar_model::ObjectWords::display_name()'s raw joined-words fallback,
the right source when there's nothing better but exactly the word-salad
shape session::item_tracker_display_name (SQ-1648) exists to avoid for
player-facing text. The registry's own rec.name is already that resolved,
clean name, stamped by apply_item_observations from the same per-turn
observation — carried_line just wasn't reading it. Anchorhead's umbrella
(no hardware short name) showed "umbrella things green handle brolly
bumbersho" instead of "umbrella" once seen at least once; SQ-1655/1657
recently made Anchorhead's avatar resolvable at inventory time at all, so
this latent bug had nothing to render until now.

Fix: carried_line prefers graph.item(key)'s rec.name over the passed-in
name whenever a registry record exists, falling back to the live name
only when there's no record yet (the very first frame). No timing gap:
apply_item_observations runs synchronously in turn processing before the
next render, so the clean name is already in the registry by the time the
same turn's frame draws.

Checked the other two render::transcript::display_name() callers this
quest's brief flagged: inventory_items (no keys) has zero production call
sites today — only tests — so it isn't reachable. inventory_click_words'
fallback to display_name() can only fire when ObjectWords::words is
empty, and display_name() itself returns None in that case too, so the
fallback is dead code for this shape; its real path (crate::vocab::
typeable_name) already picks a single stored word, never the joined list.
Neither needed a fix.

Falsified: reverted the one-line fix, confirmed both the new unit test
and the new real-game test fail reproducing the exact reported text
("... — found Outside the Real Estate Office, turn N"), restored it.

events.title: fix(app): snap the transcript to the bottom on the player's own command submission (SQ-1658)
events.message:
fix(app): snap the transcript to the bottom on the player's own command submission (SQ-1658)

In inline-prompt mode, submitting a command while scrolled up into
history left the view scrolled up, so the player couldn't see the
result without scrolling back down manually. A command submission is
an active "show me what happens now" signal, unlike passive output
arriving while the reader deliberately scrolls through backlog
(SQ-1595, which this leaves untouched).

AppState::snap_scroll_for_own_submission resets transcript_scroll to
0 before the turn's output arrives, so pager::apply_frame's existing
at_bottom check sees the reader as already at the bottom and takes
its normal follow path for the new output. No-op when already at the
bottom. Called from the one SubmitCommand/BandQuickPick arm in
main.rs, ahead of the slash-command branch, so it covers ordinary
commands, slash commands and band quick-picks alike.

events.title: fix(app): stop a preserving screen clear from top-anchoring like a destructive one (SQ-1656)
events.message:
fix(app): stop a preserving screen clear from top-anchoring like a destructive one (SQ-1656)

window_wrapped_rows top-anchors post-clear content to hide pre-clear
history that a clear actually destroyed (menu redraws, typed-command
clears). SQ-1654 made mark_screen_clear() also run on game-driven clears
that PRESERVE the prior screen (Anchorhead's intro/quote sequence,
Counterfeit Monkey's accessibility Q&A), so legitimately-surviving
scrollback got hidden above the fold exactly as if it had been wiped —
the first Q&A question scrolling off, and the view briefly jumping
backward then snapping forward early in a game.

AppState::top_anchor is the new render-facing anchor: mark_screen_clear
moves it in lockstep with clear_anchor (every typed-command clear, and a
game-driven clear that collapses) exactly as before; the new
mark_screen_clear_preserving_top_anchor leaves it untouched for a
game-driven clear that preserves the prior screen, so that content falls
back to ordinary bottom-sticking scrollback instead of being pinned.
clear_anchor itself still moves on every clear — apply_game_driven_result
still needs it as the next clear's own comparison baseline.

Reset alongside clear_anchor at every site that replaces the transcript
wholesale (archive restore, auto-resume, history rewind, game reset,
launch resume) so a stale index can't mis-anchor a replaced transcript.

Adds render-level regression/non-regression coverage against real
Anchorhead and Counterfeit Monkey archives, a focused wrap-cache unit
test, and a state-level unit test — falsified by temporarily reverting
to the old unconditional mark_screen_clear() and confirming the new
Anchorhead test fails with the reported symptom.

events.title: Release 2.4.4 (#61)
events.message:
Release 2.4.4 (#61)

* fix(asm): INCBIN searches the -I directories

INCLUDE searched the source's directory and then every -I directory;
INCBIN only the source's own, so binary data kept next to the include
files was not found. Both passes of INCBIN now resolve the file the same
way INCLUDE does.

* fix(floppy): every repeated write option is applied

--add-file, --rename, --set-comment and --set-protection collected all
their values into one flat list of which only the first pair was read,
so a second --add-file was dropped without a message. --make-dir,
--delete-file and --delete-dir could not be repeated at all.

All write options can now be given more than once and every occurrence
is applied: directories first, then files, renames, comments, protection
bits, and deletions last, each kind in the order given.

* ci: run the fuzz targets in parallel

The fuzz smoke run took eight minutes by running each target for 60 s
one after another, and was the slowest part of every pull request. Each
target is now its own matrix job; a job still named fuzz-smoke (the
required status check) passes only if every target passed. The
floppy_amigados_write target, which existed but was not run in CI, is
included.

* Release 2.4.4

Version bump, together with the fixes it releases. fuzz/Cargo.lock is a
separate lockfile and is updated too, since the fuzz crate is built with
--locked.

multilibs twice: t-amigaos tells the driver which directory a set of
flags selects, MULTI tells this Makefile which directories to build
libraries for. Nothing kept them in step, so a change on either side
would show up as a library built for a directory the driver never
selects, or a directory the driver selects with nothing in it.

check-multilib derives the directory set from MULTI and from the built
driver's -print-multi-lib and fails, naming the differences, if they
disagree. `check` runs it first. Against the current t-amigaos (after
AmigaPorts/gcc#44) the 11 directories agree; with a libm040 added to
MULTI and libb32/libm060 removed it reports exactly those two.

events.title: fix(asm): PC-relative displacements measured from their extension word (#59)
events.message:
fix(asm): PC-relative displacements measured from their extension word (#59)

A PC-relative displacement is added to the address of the extension word
that holds it. encode_ea expects that address plus 2, which callers only
supplied correctly when the extension followed the opword directly and
the caller passed instruction + 4. Many did not, and assembled operands
2 or 4 bytes past their target without any message:

- JMP, JSR, TST, MOVE <ea>,CCR/SR and FRESTORE passed instruction + 2;
- BTST #n (bit number), MOVEM (register mask), MULU/MULS/DIVU/DIVS.L,
  DIVSL/DIVUL, CHK2/CMP2, CALLM, the bit field instructions, the FPU
  instructions and PMOVE put a word before the displacement and did not
  account for it.

Every caller now passes the right value, and encode_ea documents the
convention. The single-operand and MMU forms that cannot take a
PC-relative operand are aligned too, so the rule holds everywhere.

tests/pc_relative.rs assembles each form that accepts (d16,PC) or
(d8,PC,Xn) on the 68000, 68020, FPU and MMU, decodes it again and checks
the decoded target is the label; 32 of them failed before.

events.title: agent: scale pointer warps by mode resolution over monitor MouseTicks, not HIRES/LACE
events.message:
agent: scale pointer warps by mode resolution over monitor MouseTicks, not HIRES/LACE

PR #7 (mightym) found the real bug: IECLASS_POINTERPOS is not in screen
pixels, so on a 640x256 hires screen a click at y=170 landed at 85. Its
fix doubled X/Y when ViewPort.Modes lacked HIRES/LACE, but a Picasso96
screen reports Modes 0x7100 (neither bit), so it would have doubled both
axes on every RTG machine, where warps were already 1:1. SuperHires (no
HIRES bit, needs X halved) and dragged-down screens were also off.

Measured on the Amigo guest (OS 3.2, native PAL modes + P96 RTG):
MonitorInfo.MouseTicks is 22,22 on native monitors and 11,11 on the P96
one, and landing = asked * ticks / Resolution on every mode. Scaling by
DisplayInfo.Resolution / MouseTicks per axis, plus the screen's own
LeftEdge/TopEdge, now lands on the pixel asked for on RTG 1280x720, PAL
hires, hires-lace, lores, SuperHires (nearest even X) and on screens
dragged down 40/60/100 lines. Before: hires Y halved, lores both halved,
SuperHires X doubled, dragged screens off by their offset.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: thomas-luebker

events.title: agent: no DOS requesters in plain builds, GETRANGE clamps at EOF, clear the planar temp bitmap
events.message:
agent: no DOS requesters in plain builds, GETRANGE clamps at EOF, clear the planar temp bitmap

Three bugs reported by xmies23, each with the cause already found:

- #6 pr_WindowPtr = -1 was only set in ssl_init(), which a plain build
  never runs, so a path on an unmounted volume put up "insert volume"
  and parked the accept loop (and the ARexx QUIT) until someone clicked
  Cancel at the machine. Now set at the top of main() and restored on
  exit, since from a Shell this is the Shell's own process. The command
  process inherits it: shell commands naming a missing volume now fail
  instead of waiting.
- #5 GETRANGE announced the requested length and sent only what the file
  held, leaving the client stuck mid-frame. The length is clamped to the
  file; a short reply means EOF. PROTOCOL.md says so, and the fake agent
  now implements GETRANGE so it has test coverage.
- #4 The ReadPixelArray8 temp bitmap was not BMF_CLEARed, so on a planar
  screen shallower than 8 the unused planes came back as noise in the
  high bits of every pixel. Also masked client-side in amiga.py, which
  fixes screenshots from agents already deployed.

Refs #4, #5, #6 (closed when 0.13.2 ships).
Reported-by: xmies23

--release, and therefore install-bcc.sh and the package builds, failed.
rdgen-codegen-rust now writes a field-by-field #[inline(never)] PartialEq for
each rule enum. Debug builds were unaffected.

events.title: agent: LIST reports soft links as L, not D
events.message:
agent: LIST reports soft links as L, not D

do_list derived the type letter from fib_DirEntryType > 0, and ST_SOFTLINK
(3) is positive whatever the link points at, so every soft link came back as
a directory: on the Amigo, RAM:Disk.info (a link to ENVARC:Sys/def_RAM.info)
listed as D. A client that recurses into D entries (amifleet68's copier)
would descend into links.

Soft links now get their own letter, L. Hard links stay as DOS presents them
(ST_LINKDIR -> D, ST_LINKFILE -> F). PROTOCOL.md documents L; older clients
that test for "D" treat it as not-a-directory. The Python client gains
DirEntry.is_link, the MCP list tool shows "(link)", AmigaKit gains
AmigaDirEntry.isLink and the amifleet file panel a link icon. The fake agent
emits L for symlinks, with a test.

Verified on the Amigo with a second agent (68000 and 68020 builds) run from
RAM: on port 7950, fleet agent untouched: LIST RAM: returns
"L 23 ----rwed ... Disk.info"; Clipboards/ENV/T stay D.

events.title: amifleet: pace VNC update requests instead of request-on-arrival
events.message:
amifleet: pace VNC update requests instead of request-on-arrival

The RFB run loop sent the next incremental FramebufferUpdateRequest the
instant a frame arrived. AmiVNC answers at once even when nothing changed,
so this was a tight request/reply loop: the same loop in amifleet68 ran ~37
round trips/s against the real AmiVNC on the PiStorm and crashed it ~25 s in.

RFBClient now schedules incremental requests itself (pumpStreaming): never
sooner than 100 ms after the previous update, 250 ms when that update had
zero rectangles (lastUpdateRects). Pointer and key input is still written
immediately. RFBView and amitest rfbdrive use it; RFBView also skips
re-rendering empty updates.

Against amifleet68's fake_amivnc.py --eager on loopback:
before ~24,500 req/s, after 6-7 req/s; 410 pointer events in 10 s all
delivered, 0 protocol violations.

events.title: Unpack record string fields with the stdlib ltrim/rtrim methods
events.message:
Unpack record string fields with the stdlib ltrim/rtrim methods

MBASIC/BASCOM have no LTRIM$/RTRIM$, so the record lowering built an inline
LEN/MID$ loop and always right-trimmed, leaving RSET fields with leading
spaces. It now calls com.bascal.stdlib rtrim for a left-aligned field and
ltrim for a right-aligned one, splicing those libraries in when a string
field is read. Add com.bascal.stdlib.strings (ltrim, rtrim, trim$), drop
trim from the BASIC passthrough builtins, and teach the docs checker to
leave the auto-loaded library text out of generated samples.

events.title: fix(app): find a Glulx avatar find_player can't, by watching confirmed pickups (SQ-1655)
events.message:
fix(app): find a Glulx avatar find_player can't, by watching confirmed pickups (SQ-1655)

gvm::objects::ParseNames::find_player's static scan refuses any story whose
Understand grammar for the player compiles to a parse_name ROUTINE instead of
a static word array — Counterfeit Monkey and the full commercial release of
Anchorhead both hit this (confirmed directly against both stories.gblorb
files), leaving GlulxSession::player_addr() permanently None and every
carried item silently missing from TurnResult.items for the whole session.

crate::glulx_playerlock::PlayerLock is a new fallback learner, ported from the
same idea crate::glulx_roomlock::RoomLock already uses for the `location`
global: find the RAM word by observation instead of by name. The player
global almost never changes, so instead of RoomLock's turn-over-turn
correlation, the signal is a single confirmed pickup — a command the story's
own grammar resolves as take-shaped whose target visibly leaves the room and
lands on a validated avatar-plausible object (a real, situated object of the
story) locks the holding RAM word immediately, with the lowest-address
tie-break RoomLock already uses for aliases (`player`/`actor`). A later
contradicting pickup rejects the stale word and relocks the same turn.

The take-shaped gate (GlulxSession::learn_player_from_pickups, reusing
session::take_command_target) exists because the first version without it
false-locked on nearly every early Anchorhead turn: `climb on garbage can`,
`enter window` and similar containment-shuffling commands also make an
address leave the room's direct children, and without the gate the garbage
can itself got mistaken for the avatar.

Purely a fallback: GlulxSession::player_addr() only consults the learner
after find_player's static scan has already answered None, so no story where
the static scan already works changes behavior. The learned address persists
in a per-game `player-global` sidecar, mirroring room-global's format and
image-identity check exactly.

Real-game regressions added for both motivating stories (CounterfeitMonkey-10
and the full Anchorhead.gblorb), unit tests on the learner in isolation, and
a sidecar persistence round-trip — all in crates/app/src/glulx_playerlock.rs
and crates/app/tests/suites/item_tracking.rs. Falsified by temporarily
disabling the fallback and confirming both regressions fail with the
originally-reported symptom.

Confirm: SQ-1655

Anzeige: Werbung und Stadion wie im Original (#143)

Werbung:
- Der Bildschirm öffnet ohne gewählte Seite (0x28EF1 setzt die Auswahl auf 0xFF): kein
  weißer Rand, der schwarze Kasten leer, das Logofeld nimmt noch keinen Klick an. Der
  Rahmen ums Foto entsteht erst beim Wählen (0x286D4).
- Beim Wählen füllt das Original den Kasten (217,60)-(313,90) schwarz und setzt OK/NEIN
  in der grauen Form darunter (0x2954C).
- Alle Texte in Farbe 1 ohne Schatten. Beträge wie der Formatierer 0x76b:0x681 im Feld von
  zehn Zeichen, links mit '^' aufgefüllt: Einnahmen und Ausgaben ab x 240 (Ende bei x 297),
  Zeilen eine tiefer; im Kasten Text und Betrag drei tiefer, "KEIN INTERESSE..." ab y 74,
  "VERTRAG: 2JAHRE" ohne Leerzeichen (0x288EF).
- Feld- und Randfarben mit den gespreizten 6-Bit-Werten.
- Palette: der Bildschirm schaltet über 0x28FE2/0x39924 auf den zweiten Block von
  PIC/1.PAL um (Farben 22-26, 30, 31: Trikot weiß statt gelb). tools/vga.py setzt 46.CP,
  31.VGA und 32.VGA jetzt damit um - wirksam erst nach neuem Erzeugen von assets/pic.

Stadion:
- Beträge der Stufenliste ab x 216 im Feld von neun Zeichen (0x0FAA): "380.000 DM" endet
  bei x 268, "1.140.000 DM" bei 265.
- Die Restwochen im Feld von zwei Zeichen (0x1FA7), eine einstellige Zahl steht eine Ziffer
  weiter rechts.
- Die große Beschriftung unten bleibt nach dem Klick beim gewählten Eintrag, auch wenn der
  Zeiger wegfährt oder über eine andere Zeile geht; sie steht mittig über x 133 ab y 219.
- Nach ACH NEE leert das Original den Kasten und hebt die Auswahl auf (0x1655); die
  Bausperre setzt weiterhin der Server.

Punktvergleich mit tools/bildvergleich.py gegen DOSBox (TEST2, Manager 0, mit neu
erzeugten Werbebildern): Werbung beim Öffnen, Trikot, Bande mit und ohne Vertrag und alle
zehn Sponsoren 0 Abweichungen; Stadion leer, Flutlicht angeklickt, Maus weg, Maus über
anderer Zeile, nach ACH NEE 0 Abweichungen (Mauszeiger ausgenommen); Stufenliste mit
1.140.000 DM gegen die Aufnahme aus #142 ebenfalls 0.

events.message:
Saisonwechsel und Rekorde wie im Original (#128)

Audit 2, Befunde G1-G3, B12-B16, H2 samt Nebenbefund 0x0D615, D2, E6:

- G1/G2: Vereinsrekorde über die Argumente von 0x2DBDF (p, q, Modus):
  "kassiert heim" (k = 3) und "erzielt auswärts" (k = 6) im unteren
  Halbbyte, 8 Bit ohne Grenze auf 15; leerer Rekord zählt als 0, ein
  torloses Spiel schreibt weder Byte noch Gegner.
- G3: Serienrekorde aller Manager nach der Buchung jeder Liga
  (0x2D812), nicht nur für die Vereine eines Spiels.
- B12/D2: Torschützenkönig je Manager vor Ewigkeitspunkten und
  Auf-/Abstieg mit der alten Liga (0x1E199); 0x16515 schreibt die
  Kadertore in Spielerbyte 34 - am Saisonende und beim Öffnen der
  Bestenliste (neuer Endpunkt /api/bestenliste).
- B13: Positionsart der Neubelegung geht an Spieler -0x7c (6 nach
  Aufstieg, sonst der letzte Jugendspieler), ohne Ziel kein Schreiben.
- H2: Karriereende würfelt random(0,3) für die Meldung (0x0D55E);
  sie erscheint nur als Kasten (Server: Hinweis statt Meldung).
- B14/B15: Jahrgangswechsel löscht Byte 12/24 im Kader von Manager 0
  am neuen Platz; Aufschieben mit Länge nach Platz == 4 (0x1FDBE).
- B16: Spielerpool zieht höchstens 1001 Mal, dann Spieler 255.
- E6: Spieltagzähler 225A läuft über den letzten Spieltag hinaus
  (35/39/39 wie in KP-RELEG1/2 und KP-SAISON-START).

Tests: history, saisonende, pool, season; europa- und Leihtest an das
Verhalten des Originals angepasst. Doku: SPIELMECHANIK.md, Zweigbücher
0CB62 und 2D144.

events.title: Anzeige: Tabellen, Spielplan, Pokal, Bestenliste, Spielerinfo, Zeitung (#138)
events.message:
Anzeige: Tabellen, Spielplan, Pokal, Bestenliste, Spielerinfo, Zeitung (#138)

- Verlegte Spiele zeigen den Nachholtermin "T.M. (N)" statt "verlegt", auch in der
  Ligaübersicht der Konferenz an ihrem Platz (0x2BBD2, G5)
- Spielplan: Blättern über den Rand, Start bei Spieltag 1 nach Saisonende (0x2BF6B, G6);
  Platz auf zwei Stellen "^5." (0x2C139, G10)
- Info-Tafel: Mindestbreite 2 für Platz, historische Ergebnisse und Ewige Punkte, bis ein
  nicht leerer Rekord sie auf 1 setzt (G9); aus der Pokal- und Europapokalübersicht per
  Klick, ausländische Vereine mit dem Späher-Text (0x1A2FD, 0x2A56B, G12/D5); aus der
  Tabelle auch im Spieltagsablauf (G13)
- Tabelle vor dem ersten Spieltag "1.SPIELTAG" (G11)
- Stärketabelle sortiert wie das Original durch Tauschen, nicht stabil (0x2DF80, G15)
- Zeitung: Aufstellung nach Kaderplatz, Verein als eigener Baustein, jedes Tor ein Baustein
  mit Umbruch, zwei Leerzeichen ohne eigenen Schützen (in DOSBox nachgemessen); leere
  Wörter bleiben Lücken, der letzte Artikel läuft ganz durch (G16, G20)
- Bestenliste: SPIELER bis zu 20 Managerspieler aus der ganzen Liga (D3); LIGA mit Lücke und
  Punktlinie hinter Sortierplatz 12, danach geht es wie im Original erst weit unten weiter
  (in DOSBox gesehen, D4); Klick auf eine Zeile zeigt die Spielerinfo (D5)
- Pokalübersicht: im Europapokal alle deutschen Vereine hervorgehoben (D11), "n.V."/"n.E."
  hinter dem Ergebnis, Gastwert ungekürzt, Ergebnis und Hinspiel an den x des Originals (D12)
- DFB-Finale: Auslosung ohne Abfrage (0x17C77, D8)
- Konferenztafel: ab zehn Toren nur die Einerstelle (D13); Tafel Manager gegen Manager als
  Abweichung eingetragen (D14)
- Spielerinfo: "VERLETZT (ART)" ohne Zähler (C3); drei Spalten mit Saison(Gesamt) (C4)
- Bestenliste der Diskette: Europapokal-Zuschlag nur mit DFB-Siegerbit, Saisonzahl aus
  4cb3:07E2 (H5); Einordnen ohne Punktevergleich, Tauschsortieren, beim Öffnen aus dem Menü
  mit dem jetzigen Stand, im Endlosspiel gleich in die Datei (H6, in DOSBox gesehen)

Nicht umgesetzt: D10 (Kaderbyte 21 ist Spielstand), G18 (in DOSBox nicht mit vertretbarem
Aufwand herbeizuführen), H6 Punkt 3 (die Hervorhebung trifft alle Einträge, wie hier schon).
Ein Komma hinter dem letzten Spieler der Aufstellung zeigt das Original nicht (DOSBox).

Test mit 1,9 Mio. Kontostand.

events.title: YM: Mask interrupts across each register write, and silence the bell
events.message:
YM: Mask interrupts across each register write, and silence the bell

TOS's Timer C plays Dosound sequences (the bell, an accessory's sound)
on the YM2149 and outranks the VBL tick, so landing between selecting a
register and writing it sent the value to the register it selected.
stdl_ym_write() and stdl_ym_mix_update() now mask interrupts across the
select and the write (and the port-bit readback): a few stores, under
8us, about 40 cycles a write. The service also clears the bell bit in
conterm with the key click, and test_tone checks both are restored.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: stdlconv: Reduce General MIDI to the three voices by instrument
events.message:
stdlconv: Reduce General MIDI to the three voices by instrument

`stdlconv midi` kept the three newest notes and played every drum as
the same noise burst. It now shares the voices one per instrument
before any gets a chord, going by General MIDI program (the bass, then
melodic instruments, then pads), a part playing its lowest note if a
bass, else its highest, and a note keeping its voice. Notes below C2
play an octave up; notes get an accent, melodic ones settle, pads
swell, plucked and struck ones fade, and held ones get a vibrato;
levels follow each program's perceived loudness by octave; drums are
eight kinds of noise or falling-tone burst over a free voice, else the
bass or the least important note. The synth runs at 120Hz and the
stream samples it at 50Hz; drums start on a frame so short ones keep
their attack. Program changes, expression and the notes-off
controllers are read, and event times round to the nearest tick
rather than down.

The demo tune gains General MIDI programs (square lead, fingered bass)
and DEMO.STM is regenerated; the skill, limits and STDL_Tone header no
longer describe the old policy.

events.title: Time replay code in vAmiga; SoundMon's note start measured
events.message:
Time replay code in vAmiga; SoundMon's note start measured

tools/timing.py runs code taken from a replay's annotated listing on an
emulated Amiga 500 (vAmiga, pinned as a sparse submodule), from chip RAM
under a boot ROM in tools/timing/boot.asm. Data files in data/timing/
name the code, the memory writes by record field, the spans to measure,
and the bitplane loads. SoundMon's DMA wait and note start become 647
and 442 CCK, so the restart limit moves from period 547 to 544, and to
771 with 6 bitplanes.

setup/Makefile now builds IRA, vasm, vlink and the timing driver, keyed
on content, so activate costs almost nothing on a set-up checkout; CI
caches the venv and vAmiga's objects. m68k-formatter lays out *.asm, and
mypy type-checks tools/.

events.title: Add the Disk Inspector
events.message:
Add the Disk Inspector

View > Disk Inspector shows what is recorded on a floppy in either
drive, the same way for every format (DSK, DO, PO, WOZ bit and flux
tracks), because each image hands over its tracks as the bit cells the
drive would read (DiskImage::inspectQuarterTrack).

core/disk-image/disk_inspection reads those cells as the drive's latch
does and names every nibble: sync, address and data fields and their
marks, checksums, well-formed bytes in no standard field, and noise. Two
exports carry it to the host: _getDiskOverview (the whole disk in arcs
per ring) and _getDiskTrackDetail (one track in full). The window
re-reads only when DiskController::getRevision moves.

The window has a platter that turns under the emulated head and zooms
down to single flux transitions, a zoomable track strip, the sectors in
the order they pass the head with their decoded bytes, and the raw
nibbles. Timing mode colours flux tracks by cell time, which is how a
track written at more than one speed shows itself.

Documentation and release notes cover the Disk Inspector, WOZ flux
images and disk links.
events.author: mikedaley

events.title: Start a disk link with only the disks it names
events.message:
Start a disk link with only the disks it names

A link that names any image (?disk=, ?disk2=, ?hd=, ?hd2=) no longer
restores the floppies and hard drive images from the last visit into the
other drives. A disk left in drive 2, or a SmartPort image the machine
boots ahead of the floppy, changed what the link did.

The persisted images are not cleared, so they come back on the next
plain visit. skipRestore is kept apart from urlOwnedDrives, which also
stops a drive being persisted: a drive the link left empty is still the
visitor's to use.

events.message:
Play WOZ 2.1 flux tracks back by time

A WOZ 2.1 image can hold tracks as flux timings, mapped by a FLUX chunk
over TMAP. They are now played to the Logic State Sequencer as pulses on
its own clock, one per tick, and the sequencer takes a pulse on whichever
tick it arrives rather than one bit at phase 4.

Converting them to bits is not enough: Sirius's Bandits writes parts of
each track at 3.7us a cell and parts at 4.1us, and its loader times its
reads to tell them apart. As bits every flux track failed its checksum
and the boot retried track 1.5 for ever; played by time it boots.

Flux tracks are saved as flux (a FLUX chunk on a block boundary, named by
INFO), so a save state of a flux disk comes back bootable. Writing to a
flux track turns it into bits, and the head keeps its angle crossing
between the two kinds. The export's TRKS chunk now covers its track data.

events.title: cpu: 68030 MMU — without data cache emulation, retried accesses go to memory
events.message:
cpu: 68030 MMU — without data cache emulation, retried accesses go to memory

An access error RTE in the pipelined tables resumes a split (misaligned)
access through read_dcache030_retry() and write_dcache030_retry(). These
use the emulated data cache whenever the guest has enabled it in CACR,
even when data cache emulation is off. In that mode nothing else fills
or updates those cache lines, so a retried read could return a line
filled by an earlier retry, from before later writes.

With data cache emulation off, read and write memory directly, which is
what table 32's RTE (mmu030_get/put_generic) does. With it on, nothing
changes.

Same change as tonioni/WinUAE#511 (commit 2).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: slaapliedje

events.title: cpu: 68030 MMU — split misaligned MOVES accesses when the data cache is off
events.message:
cpu: 68030 MMU — split misaligned MOVES accesses when the data cache is off

Without data cache emulation, MOVES in the pipelined tables (34 and 35)
reads and writes through mmu030_get/put_fc_word() and _long(). These
call mmu030_get/put_word() and _long(), which translate only the address
of the first byte. A misaligned MOVES that crosses into the next page
therefore reads or writes the rest in the physically adjacent page, and
the page it belongs to is never faulted in.

Unix kernels do exactly this in copyin()/copyout() when a user buffer is
at an odd address. Under AMIX (Commodore's Amiga UNIX) in cycle-exact
mode, bytes of received network data read back as zero (the bytes went
elsewhere), TLS certificate chains fail to parse, and the kernel panics
in kmem_alloc() on free lists overwritten by the stray bytes.

Split them the way table 32 does (dfc030_put_long() and friends) and the
way the data cache path does (uae_mmu030_*_fc()): is_unaligned_bus() ->
mmu030_*_unaligned(). Aligned accesses take the same path as before.

In Hatari this path runs with --mmu on --data-cache off (with the
default --cpu-exact or --compatible); with the data cache on, the cache
path already splits.

Same change as tonioni/WinUAE#511 (commit 1).

events.title: fix(cd): search 16 sectors for the boot header, not 1
events.message:
fix(cd): search 16 sectors for the boot header, not 1

CDIntfExtractBootStub looked for "ATARI APPROVED DATA HEADER ATRI " in
the first 2352 bytes of the session-2 boot track only. Ocean Depths and
Simone open that track with a silent sector and carry an intact header
at LBA +1 (+0x2B6 / +0x1DE); they were refused as "zero-filled" bad rips
and fell back to the diagnostic screen. The BIOS scans the stream for
the sync run, so widen the window to 16 sectors -- the 32-byte magic
keeps it from matching anything else.

events.title: fix(cd): rebuild the 'ATRI' sync run a CHD virtual pregap truncated
events.message:
fix(cd): rebuild the 'ATRI' sync run a CHD virtual pregap truncated

Atari's mastering header (10 zeros, 'ATRI' x16, "ATARI APPROVED DATA
HEADER ATRI ") can start inside a track's pregap. When the CHD stores
that pregap as virtual silence, INDEX 01 keeps only the tail of the run
(Vid Grid USA/Alt track 3: 9 and 10 of 16). Drivers that match 16
consecutive 'ATRI' longs then retry the boot read forever (black, silent
screen). The missing bytes are fully determined by the header format, so
rebuild them at the end of the pregap's last sector, only when the data
sector starts with a truncated run followed by the header text.

events.title: Pads: STDL_PadRumble, and xpad v1.1.6
events.message:
Pads: STDL_PadRumble, and xpad v1.1.6

int STDL_PadRumble(uint8_t low, uint8_t high, uint16_t ms) pulses an
Xpad pad's heavy (low) and light (high) motors, 0-255 each.
- A new call replaces the pulse that is running, and 0,0 or a zero
  length stops it.
- It returns 0 when the provider offers XPAD_CAP_RUMBLE and a request
  area, and -1 otherwise, so a game can call it unconditionally.
- A refusal stops a running pulse before it returns. A provider drops
  the cap when its last rumble-capable pad leaves, and a pulse already
  written would otherwise never end.
- The pump ends the pulse when its time is up. stdl_events_remove()
  also ends it, from STDL_Quit and from the terminate path alike; that
  is memory writes only.
- TJOY's shoulder buttons pulse each motor for 300ms.

Written in a port's session and reviewed here before committing. The
review found one real gap: the magnitudes and the seq bump were
written through a plain pointer, and the provider reads the area from
an interrupt, so gcc was free to move seq ahead of a magnitude. Both
writers now go through a volatile XPAD_REQ, and the disassembly
stores the two magnitudes before seq on every path.

lib/xpad moves from 12683cc to v1.1.6 (6ce9a10). The core files STDL
compiles (xpad.h, xpad.c, xpad.inc, xpad_gas.inc, xpad_provider.c) do
not change between the two, so the ABI holds. The new upstream
commits are the STE driver, XPADEMU, the viewer and CI.

The skill's joystick bullet had been split mid-sentence by the
controllers bullet some time ago, which left the key-mapping sentence
stranded. That is fixed on the way past.

XPADSTUB offers the cap and a request area now. XPADPROB checks start,
the pump's timeout, stop, refusal and the stop at quit, taking
snapshots and printing afterwards. Its output is identical on emulated
st and ste:
  before 0/0 seq=0; start 200/60 seq=1; 50ms 200/60; 150ms 0/0 seq=2;
  stop 0/0 seq=4; refused ret=-1 0/0 seq=6; after quit 0/0 seq=8
The existing axis, merge and key-emulation lines are unchanged.

The cross build has zero warnings, pixel-path size is unchanged at
34272, and the host tests pass. New public API, so the next tag is a
minor version.

NVMBiosHook served the call and relied on our RTS stub at $2404 to

CD_read treated any LBA before the session-2 boot track as a misdecoded
MSF and redirected it to the session-2 game-data track. Homebrew discs
(Fast Food 64, Frogz 64, Saucer Wars) keep their program on track 2 in
session 1: the loader reads TOC entry $2C10, subtracts 6 frames, and
expects a 'TRAK' run there. The redirect found another 'TRAK' file on
track 4, the loader jumped into it and the 68K crashed (black screen).
Keep the requested position when the D1 run is within 16 sectors of it.

events.title: TPALETTE: -flip draws into a second page and flips
events.message:
TPALETTE: -flip draws into a second page and flips

TSPRITE has had -flip since it was ported. TPALETTE had nothing
like it, and without it the boats are erased and redrawn on the
page being displayed. On a real Mega STE they flashed on and off
whenever the beam passed between the two.

With -flip the screen is double-buffered. Both pages get the
background at the start. Each frame repairs the page it is about to
draw where that page last had its boats, two frames back, since the
previous frame went to the other page. It then draws the boats and
shows the page with SDL_Flip. The FPS overlay goes on every frame,
so both pages carry it. Without -flip nothing changes.

In Hatari as a Mega STE, recorded to AVI, the flip build has all
five boats whole in every frame and leaves no trails. The
single-buffered build (and v1.13.2) show the boats missing or partly
drawn in about 40% of frames. A frame of five boats takes a little
over three vertical blanks, so the flip holds it to 12.5fps. Rename
to TPALETTE.TTP to pass the option from the desktop.

events.title: fix(cd): treat an HLE CD_read with end <= dest as a seek, not a 367 KB copy
events.message:
fix(cd): treat an HLE CD_read with end <= dest as a seek, not a 367 KB copy

When A1 was a RAM address at or below A0, byteCount fell through to the
$5BC00 unknown-size default and the stream overwrote 367 KB past A0. The
BIOS GPU ISR stores only while its write pointer is below the end, so
such a call transfers nothing and just leaves the drive playing at the
target. World Tour Racing starts its title music this way (A0=$12ECDE,
A1=$12EC88, then CD_I2S_enable); the copy clobbered the GPU program it
launches from $133AB0 and the title screen froze.

events.title: Voices: one or two mix straight into the ring, chunks step by pointer
events.message:
Voices: one or two mix straight into the ring, chunks step by pointer

Two fast paths in the voice mixer, suggested by a look at AGT's
audio (which, it turned out, has no software mixer at all):

- One or two voices cannot overflow a byte. Every volume row is half
  scale, -64..63, so their sum is -128..126. They now mix straight
  into the ring, the first storing and the second adding bytes,
  without the 16-bit block or the clamp pass. Three or four still
  sum in 16 bits and clamp once.
- A voice at the device's own rate steps exactly one frame. Every
  SDL_mixer chunk does, since it is converted to that rate at load.
  It now walks its sample with a post-increment instead of the 16.16
  index and fraction.

Each of the eight loops (word or byte, store or add, one-frame or
resampled) is 68000 with the C twin voice_run_c beside it. They sit
in four small functions chosen once per voice per block. With all
four kinds in one function behind a switch, four resampled voices (a
module) mixed 2% slower than before.

VOICECHK, which compares asm and C byte for byte, now picks the
device rate for a third of its voices and times 1, 2 and 4 voices at
both rates. On an emulated STE, 400 blocks:

                  resampled         native rate
  1 voice         680 -> 415ms      680 -> 305ms
  2 voices       1140 -> 860ms     1140 -> 630ms
  4 voices       2060 -> 2070ms    2055 -> 1610ms

On an emulated Mega STE the same shape: one voice 370 -> 240 and
170ms, and four resampled 1130 -> 1165ms, within that machine's
layout noise. 0 of 120 random cases differ on either machine.

MIXBENCH, the whole SDL_mixer path in a game-like loop, on an STE:

                  6258Hz      12517Hz
  1 chunk         9% -> 5%    18% -> 8%
  2 chunks       15% -> 9%    29% -> 16%
  3 chunks       20% -> 16%   40% -> 32%
  4 chunks       26% -> 20%   51% -> 40%

The skill, porting.md, README and SDL_mixer.h quote the new figures.
Host tests pass under ASan.

events.title: BLiTTER: keep drawing onto a single-buffered screen off the chip
events.message:
BLiTTER: keep drawing onto a single-buffered screen off the chip

On a real Mega STE, TSPRITE and TPALETTE flashed, tore and lost their
sprites throughout. Both are single-buffered. This branch had started
sending shifted keyed blits and sprites to the BLiTTER, which draws a
keyed blit as three passes over the whole rectangle a plane at a time
(XOR, AND, XOR) and a sprite as two (AND, OR). On the page being
displayed, the beam shows the rectangle between passes.

An AVI of TSPRITE on an emulated Mega STE shows the same. The frames
with the fewest lit pixels hold white outlines and striped sprites,
the XOR state. v1.13.2 and a build with the BLiTTER refused only
clip sprites under their neighbours' erase, as single buffering
always does.

stdl_drawn_visibly(dst) is true for the screen surface when the
program is not double-buffered. There stdl_blitter_wants now declines
masked and shifted blits, and spr_blitter declines sprites, so they
go to the CPU as before the BLiTTER could shift. Unmasked same-phase
copies and fills, which v1.13.2 already gave the chip, are unchanged.
A double-buffered program draws into the hidden page and keeps every
BLiTTER path.

The fixed TSPRITE shows no XOR states in its worst frames and runs at
20.0fps on the emulated Mega STE, against 20.8 for v1.13.2. It was
35.1 with the garbage.

- SPRCOST on st, all 85 cases: geometric mean 1.0000 against the
  previous commit, same-binary floor 0.18%.
- BLITCHK passes on ste, and the host tests pass.
- Pixel-path text +28 bytes (34272).

limits.md, porting.md and the skill now say that the BLiTTER's
shifted sprites, and the advice to pre-shift only without a BLiTTER,
assume STDL_DOUBLEBUF. AGENTS.md records the lesson with the
live-scene rule.

events.title: PIXCHK: seconds on hardware, not hours
events.message:
PIXCHK: seconds on hardware, not hours

A full pass of the host pixel suite on the target took 11,288s on an
emulated plain ST - three hours - and 6,207s on a Mega STE. Nobody
knew, because it had only been run natively or under Hatari's
fast-forward. A tester found out on a real Mega STE.

The time was the suite's own checking, not the library. Timed per
helper on an emulated ST:
- a STDL_GetPixel call and a 32-bit multiply per pixel compared;
- STDL_PutPixel with rnd() % maxcol per pixel filled, a libgcc
  division each;
- rnd() itself was a 32-bit multiply, 440 cycles a call, and 900
  more with % n.

Now:
- surf_row decodes a group through a table, four plane bytes to
  eight pixels each, checked against STDL_GetPixel in test_putget.
  ref_cmp and surf_to_ref, and the inline compares in the sprite,
  tile and text tests, use it and skip matching rows.
- randomise writes plane words directly when the surface is
  unclipped, with the budget's colour mask and the mask upkeep
  STDL_PutPixel does, and only a clipped surface still goes a pixel
  at a time.
- rnd() is a shift register returning 16 bits, so rnd() % n narrows
  to divu.w.
- The reference fill, XOR and blit walk row pointers.

The full pass is now 950s on an emulated plain ST.

PIXCHK's default build samples three cases of each test, spread at a
stride coprime to 6 so the budget and mask variants still come
round; every test runs, and each starts at its first case. A pass is
about 20s on a plain ST, 18s on an STE and 10s on a Mega STE. It
prints that at the start. -DPIXCHK_FULL runs every case and prints
each test's time as it goes; -DPIXCHK_VERBOSE adds those times to
the sampled build.

Host tests pass under ASan. Sampled PIXCHK passes on emulated st,
ste and megaste; full PIXCHK passes on emulated st.

onto the CPU-only core, so no key was ever scanned, and the mount's queued RUN was

  never runs, not a ?SYNTAX ERROR.
- The log reports the outcome from the PC: still in the editor's key wait
  ($E5CD–$E5D4) is "the program did not start", anything else names where it runs.
- A type step waits for the keys it typed: 160 000 cycles each (the daemon's 80 000
  hold + 80 000 gap), where max(4, len*2) frames cut "RUN\r" short.
- runtime_media_persist's description names the reply TRX64 now gives: role, the
  absolute path written, or the reason nothing was.
- smoke:sandbox-prg-start: BASIC autostart, run=$C100 and a typed POKE, each proven by

- Workflow: Read Disk presets flux device -> image file, Write Disk image
  file -> flux device. Nothing starts; "Start" stays a deliberate press.
- The second "Protection Analyzer..." entry triggers the connected one.
Disabled with the reason in tooltip and status bar: Verify Disk (no
disk-versus-image comparison exists; verification runs after a
conversion), Checksum Database and Check for Updates (not implemented),
the four language entries (translations/*.ts exist, no QTranslator loads
them).

Same class, same pass: the Workflow tab showed "Repair", "Compare" and
"Create Blank" visible and enabled without a single connect(). They now
lead into the Tools window the same way.

Gate: scripts/audit_menue_aktionen.py, category "Menueeintrag ohne
Wirkung" in check_consistency.py. Every <action> of forms/mainwindow.ui
must appear in src/mainwindow.cpp as connect/alsFenster/menueKnopf, or
as abschalten() with a non-empty reason (a literal, or an identifier the
file assigns a non-empty tr()). Comments and bare mentions do not count.
Red first: 20 -> 0. Self-test 10/10, plus two planted cases in
audit_selbsttest.py (79 green, 0 red). What the gate cannot see: whether
a handler does what its label says — the tests of the pressed buttons'
tabs cover that.

Making the GUI checkable at all: the CMake app build (UFT_BUILD_APP=ON)
had never linked locally, and measured there were two causes:
- scripts/verify_build_sources.py --emit-cmake-sources handed the ten
  opt-in dtc_components sources to CMake, which compiled them without

  names; `contains(CONFIG, uft_dtc_components) {` (MF-1100) slipped past.

  adds X to CONFIG — what qmake does without a command-line CONFIG, no

- the app target did not link zlib, mandatory since MF-1070: exactly one
  undefined symbol, `uncompress` (uft_mfi.c). Same MinGW hint as
  src/core and tests; ZLIB::ZLIB and UFT_HAS_ZLIB on the app target.
After both the app builds and links (82 MB). Headless run with
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen and QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 for 12 s: no

events.title: fix(daemon): one cart path, one write door; a loaded PRG hears the keyboard (C64RE #29, #30)
events.message:
fix(daemon): one cart path, one write door; a loaded PRG hears the keyboard (C64RE #29, #30)

#30 — media/persist role=cartridge wrote the parsed image's bare NAME, so
fs::write put a new .crt in the daemon's cwd and left the mounted file alone.
The cart's backing file now has one record, session.cart_path: the path field
on ParsedCartridgeImage is gone, and media/persist, bare savecrt, swapcrt's
persist of the old cart, eject and auto-persist all read the session's path.
swapcrt now moves it to the new cart (eject after a swap used to write the new
flash into the old file). media/persist cart takes eject's gate (dirty and a
persisting mapper) and replies {written, role, path: <absolute>, bytes} or
{written:false, role, reason}; disk replies the same shape.

host_write_target is the one door for a caller-supplied write path: absolute
as given, relative against the bound project, refused with no project —
never a raw relative fs::write. Routed through it: media/persist cart+disk,
savecrt, swapcrt, snapshot/dump, snapshot/undump (its sidecars), recorder/dump,
vsf/save, audio/export, trace/start_domains output, the ring trace output and
ringbuffer/dump. media/ingress resolves its path as media/mount does; the
monitor ringdump/ringload resolve against cd/pwd like every monitor file verb.

#29 — media/open's PRG branch, runtime/run_prg and media/ingress latched
session.injected, so with no disk and no cart full_machine_gate sent bounded
runs to the CPU-only core: no CIA, no IRQ, no keyboard scan, READY. forever.
A load into a booted machine no longer latches it. The mount autostart pushed
RUN into a type_buffer nothing ever read; the buffer is gone and autostart
types through the keyboard as run_prg does, as "RUN:\r" (text left on the
logical line becomes a following statement, not a ?SYNTAX ERROR — as VICE).

run: a number, $0840, 0x0840 or 0840 — on media/open, session/load_prg and
runtime/run_prg (which read only a number) — starts the loaded program there.
media/open also sets VARTAB after a $0801 load, as run_prg does.

Tests: persist writes the mounted file and never cwd, clean persist is a
no-op, swapcrt moves the backing file, relative paths never go raw, run
parsing, a $0801 stub autostarts under bounded runs with no media (red with
the latch put back), typed SYS reaches a PRG-only machine, run starts without
the keyboard. daemon 481, core 731, cli 115, 7-game gate 7/7.

events.title: Refuse conflicting manifests and bound upload staging
events.message:
Refuse conflicting manifests and bound upload staging

A manifest naming a path and a file beneath it, an unwritable upload
directory, and a stalled sender could each fault or hang a transfer.
Manifests with such paths are refused, directory failures return a
refusal, a grant may stage a bounded number of slots, and a silent
sender is dropped after an inactivity limit.

events.title: Keep peer-driven faults from stopping the broker and fix launch lifecycle
events.message:
Keep peer-driven faults from stopping the broker and fix launch lifecycle

Handlers that run from socket events now log and continue: request
dispatch, release and host-tool end, incident write failures, and the
transfer promises. The per-line size cap replaces the per-chunk cap.
The startup reap runs only after the control port is bound, and acquires
wait for it, so a losing second broker no longer kills a live broker's
emulators. A crash respawn of a granted instance stays granted and its
grant follows the new pid; a respawn waits for a busy launch slot. Ports
and config directories are freed after the kill settles, and a busy port
is no longer blocked for good. The launch log descriptor is closed after
spawn, spawn errors are handled, a missing VICE binary refuses the
acquire by name, wildcard VICE_BROKER_BINMON_HOST is refused, and the
Ghidra projects root is checked before use.

events.title: Bound text-monitor commands and flush banners ahead of a command
events.message:
Bound text-monitor commands and flush banners ahead of a command

TextMonitorClient.command() ignored its timeoutMs option, so a monitor
that never sent a prompt hung the call and held the channel lock. The
command now rejects at timeoutMs (default 30 s), drops the connection,
whose stream can no longer be matched to commands, and the lock is
released as the rejection unwinds. A command also waits until partial
banner output has gone quiet and emits it as a banner first, so it no
longer becomes the head of the command's response. The prompt tail scan
decodes as utf8 like the payload.

Delete the tests that read the source text of the textmon parsers,
text-protocol and text-capability-probe (import counts, forbidden
calls, declaration shapes).

events.title: fix(workspace-ui): the page talks to its own workspace's runtime, not :4312
events.message:
fix(workspace-ui): the page talks to its own workspace's runtime, not :4312

The workbench page hard-coded ws://127.0.0.1:4312, the server read only C64RE_WS_PORT,
and the launcher resolved C64RE_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT (and started the daemon there) without
passing it on. A workspace started against another endpoint therefore showed a page
attached to whatever held :4312 — another workspace's runtime — and offered "Switch to
this project" as the default action, which ends the session running there.

- launch.ts passes the resolved endpoint to the HTTP server as C64RE_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT.
- server.ts takes C64RE_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT, then C64RE_RUNTIME_WS, then C64RE_WS_PORT, and
  reports it as runtimeWsUrl / wsUrl and uses it for the probe and the monitor route.
- ws-client.ts asks /api/config for runtimeWsUrl before its first connect; the constant
  is gone. No answer = no connection (error + retry), never a guessed port.
- ProjectMismatch: "Leave it" has the focus and the weight; "Switch" stays disabled until
  "End the session serving <project>" is ticked. The dialog names the runtime endpoint.
- smoke:workspace-runtime ran on :4312 itself; it now starts the workspace against its
  own endpoint (4396) and proves /api/config reports exactly that one.

Reported by the trex64.dev session, 2026-09-30.

before the arming reply is processed. VICE wraps each command on a
running machine in a stopped/resumed pair, which the wait ignores
unless a checkpoint was reported.

Every entry of a directory sector reports that sector's next pointer, so
the audit flagged any disk with nine or more files as cyclic. It now
treats the same pointer on consecutive entries as one sector. An
unreadable or empty dir/bam listing is refused instead of reported clean.

c1541 and petcat print the one-line JSON result on every path; petcat
treats an absent entrypoint as a decline. The SKILL.md files no longer
describe a common-ancestor path rule the code does not have.

ending past $FFFF made it walk billions of addresses. It now clamps
ranges to $0000-$FFFF, cuts them at block boundaries and classifies once
per interval. argvDigest refuses an argument with a NUL byte, the
separator it joins on. The source-scanning tests are removed and the
stale comments are corrected.

events.title: feat(plan): the settings tab's "adaptive clock recovery" switch reaches the flux decoder — measured on a wobbling AmigaDOS track (MF-1625, P3-711)
events.message:
feat(plan): the settings tab's "adaptive clock recovery" switch reaches the flux decoder — measured on a wobbling AmigaDOS track (MF-1625, P3-711)

Of the 27 settings fields still marked "not wired", each was measured
against reachable readers (sub-agent, at 981f2f91). Exactly one has a
carrier of the same meaning with a reader an operator can trigger:
"Adaptive Taktrueckgewinnung" -> flux_decoder_options_t.use_pll, read by
the Amiga flux decoder on the path SCP -> ADF. With use_pll off the cell
period stays frozen and the phase correction is skipped
(uft_flux_decoder.c, `if (pll->use_pll)` at both steps).

- uft_convert_options_t gets decode_fixed_clock, mirrored in
  uft_convert_options_ext_t (both appended, as MF-484 did for
  reverse_decode); the dispatcher copies it.
- uftc_apply_decode_options() sets use_pll = false for a flux source and
  warns for a clocked bitstream (HFE), where there is no time axis for a
  PLL — same rule as the cell-time nudge.
- uft_copy_plan_t gets fixed_clock (appended; false = adaptive, the
  default). uft_copy_plan_to_convert_options() passes a set true; the
  JSON names "fixedClock" only when set.
- The tab sets it only while "Erweiterte Optionen" is on and the switch
  is unchecked. Setups store the switch as an effective value and restore
  it. 26 fields stay marked.

Measured that it works, not only that it arrives:
tests/test_convert_fester_takt.c writes a real AmigaDOS track
(tests/flux_gen/amigados) to SCP with every flux interval scaled by
1 + A sin(2 pi t / 20 ms) and counts the sectors that come back
byte-identical. UFT_MESS=1 prints the table: adaptive 22 of 22 up to
A = 30 %; fixed clock 22 of 22 up to 10 %, 2 of 22 at 12.5 %, none from
15 % on (0.5 cell of slack on a 4-cell interval). Before the option was
applied the fixed-clock column read 22 of 22 at 15 % — the red proof.
The test asserts at 15 %: adaptive all, fixed not all, and fixed on a
clean track all (the switch does not break the normal case).

Deliberately NOT wired although a carrier with a reader exists:
"Bei Fehler erneut lesen" (checkRetryOnError). decode_retries in SCP ->
D64 is not a retry on error but the number of revolutions ALWAYS decoded
and voted, which also confirms good sectors against the 8-bit checksum
(MF-566); switching it off would switch off the confirmation, and the
switch does not say that. The measurement is recorded in P3-711.

Tests: test_convert_fester_takt (new, 3), test_copy_plan_taktkorrektur
9 (4 new), test_decode_options_reach (new case: fixed clock on a
bitstream explains itself and changes nothing), test_format_tab_bindung
15 (new case). Mutation matrix 12 of 12 red (decoder not told, bitstream
silent, dispatcher drops it, plan not mapped, JSON never/always, tab
never sets it, ignores the group, sets it when checked, setup forgets
it, setup cannot load a checkbox, still marked unwired); tree restored
green.

Docs: OPEN_ITEMS P3-711 NACHTRAG.

events.title: fix(core): sync GPU/DSP to the 68K before a local-RAM write, not after
events.message:
fix(core): sync GPU/DSP to the 68K before a local-RAM write, not after

M68KGPURAMSync ran after the write landed, so the RISC catch-up executed
the cycles that precede the write with the write already visible. A short
GPU job posted by the write could finish and raise its CPU interrupt
before the 68K reached its next instruction. Myst's movie decoder posts a
job then runs `stop #$2000` with only the GPU interrupt enabled: the
interrupt was serviced before the STOP, so the 68K slept forever (black
screen after the Cyan logo). Syncing before the write keeps the #138
guarantee (each later write still flushes the GPU first) without letting
the GPU see a write earlier than it happened.
