events.title: fix(app): stop a bolded page title over a list entry from minting a phantom room (SQ-1653)
events.message:
fix(app): stop a bolded page title over a list entry from minting a phantom room (SQ-1653)

Superluminal Vagrant Twin's `map` and `prospects` commands stack two own-line
`Subheader` runs in one turn — a page title ("VISITED WORLDS") detached by a
blank line, then a list entry ("Other Worlds\nBoony (not yet landed)") joined
immediately to its one-line status. The entry is styled and shaped exactly
like a real Inform 7 room heading joined to its description (SQ-1625's rule),
so `StoryScan::capture_heading` had no way to tell them apart, and the map
minted "Other Worlds"/"Other Opportunities:" as a room every time the player
checked their own status screens.

Two existing corroboration signals don't help here: `AppGlk::status_room_name`
never names a room for this story (its status line reads "Credits: 0k ...
Fuel: 2/5"), and `RoomLock` never locks for it even after several real
land/launch moves.

The fix tracks the first own-line `Subheader` candidate each turn settles
(`StoryScan::heading_seen_this_turn`) and exposes whether the turn's final
answer differs from it (`AppGlk::heading_is_a_later_distinct_entry`). The
decision to refuse is made in `GlulxSession::finish_turn`
(`refuse_a_later_distinct_entry_in_a_list`), not in `glk_backend` itself,
because a game's OWN title banner joined to its credits block legitimately
precedes the opening room on the turn a title menu is dismissed (*King of
Shreds and Patches* is exactly this shape) — refusing is only safe once a
room is already known, a fact only `GlulxSession` has.

Adds real-game regression coverage (stories/Superluminal_Vagrant_Twin.gblorb.blorb)
and five glk_backend unit cases isolating the mechanism.

events.title: fix(app): stop one item's own vocabulary bleeding onto another in the item tracker (SQ-1652)
events.message:
fix(app): stop one item's own vocabulary bleeding onto another in the item tracker (SQ-1652)

item_tracker_display_name's tier 1 was called once per currently-tracked
item against the SAME turn-wide prose string, with no awareness of what the
OTHER items being resolved that turn looked like. Examining Anchorhead's
umbrella ("x umbrella") prints only the umbrella's own description, but the
unrelated "clothes" item's own vocabulary also has "green" (from its own
separately-described "tasteful ensemble"), so tier 1 wrongly relabeled
clothes to "green" too, from prose that never mentioned it at all. This is a
correctness bug in an embeddable, host-facing API (TurnResult.items), not
merely a TUI cosmetic glitch.

Fix: item_tracker_display_name now takes every OTHER item being resolved
the same turn, and a stored word is only trusted as tier-1 evidence when no
other item's own vocabulary also claims it — otherwise it keeps searching
that item's own word list, falling through to tier 2 (its own first stored
word) if nothing unambiguous is found. Both call sites (zvm_item_observations,
glulx_item_observations) now materialize every item under consideration
before resolving any single name, so each call can see the full turn's set.

Verified against the real AnchorheadDemo.gblorb repro (falsified by
temporarily reverting the fix and confirming both "umbrella" and "clothes"
relabel to "green" again), plus a focused unit test proving the
disambiguation rule directly.

events.title: fix(app): stop a game-driven screen clear from wiping unrelated scrollback
events.message:
fix(app): stop a game-driven screen clear from wiping unrelated scrollback

apply_game_driven_result (host/turn.rs) unconditionally truncated the
transcript back to the previous clear_anchor on every game-driven
erase_lower — correct for Counterfeit Monkey's arrow-navigated help menu
(SQ-0407, same menu reprinted every keypress) but wrong for a totally
different screen taking over: Anchorhead's intro/quote/game-start sequence
of "press any key" screens, and clicking an inline picture then returning.
Because clear_anchor is sticky (only ever moves forward), the second shape
was worse than "lose the screen right before a clear" — the FIRST
game-driven clear in a session planted a landmine that the NEXT one
detonated, discarding every real turn played in between.

is_screen_reprint now gates the collapse on whether the new content
actually looks like the old screen redrawing itself (>=50% of its
non-blank lines matching the discarded ones) rather than collapsing on
every clear. Proven against three real fixtures: Anchorhead's three-screen
intro survives fully in scrollback, a picture click + return no longer
wipes three intervening real commands on a later click, and Counterfeit
Monkey's real in-game HINT menu (yes/andra/''/tutorial off/hint, then an
arrow key) still collapses as SQ-0407 intended.

project.title: UnifiedFloppyTool
project.display_title: UnifiedFloppyTool — Amiga/Atari disk preservation
source_language: floppy disk formats and flux data
project.notes: Forensic floppy toolkit covering Amiga, Atari and other disk/flux formats. Current work raises A2R from T2 to T1, fixes Apple 5.25-inch seam/checksum handling, pairs verification sectors by ID, and wires effective settings into the conversion plan: retry count reaches SCP→D64 and clock correction reaches the SCP→ADF flux decoder only when advanced options are enabled. Encoding remains visibly unconnected because no live conversion path reads its carrier. The earlier G71 bridge and documented real-hardware bench gaps remain open.

project.title: NESRecomp
project.display_title: NESRecomp — 6502-to-C static recompilation framework
project.notes: Translates NES/Famicom 6502 ROM code into C with a hardware runner. Beyond its FDS LLE/HLE support, the cycle backend now exposes opt-in game-mod packages with instruction-boundary hooks, isolated guest-routine calls, mod save-state records, presented-width control and game-owned frame rendering. CSB requires a nonzero source-rendered viewport hash after authenticated handoff, proving renderer execution rather than pixel/audio parity. DM2 Amiga reaches its initial real-GDAT M11 frame with zero core fallbacks while broader input, save, display/audio and dungeon parity remain open. Theron's current labeled suite passes 53/53 tests, but public status was corrected to keep original presentation, stair/exit, pickup/use, combat and chapter-completion consumers explicitly open. Captured controller input was observed only in the System Card poll loop, not the title/menu route. Nexus remains active real-data bring-up and full-suite parity is not claimed.

events.title: feat(app): dim the inventory panel's per-item metadata clause
events.message:
feat(app): dim the inventory panel's per-item metadata clause

The "found Room, turn N" / "last seen Room, turn N" tail of each
inventory row now draws in a new muted `inventory_panel.meta` style,
distinct from the item's own name — a user request to make the name
stand out from its metadata.

`carried_line`/`elsewhere_line` now return the CHAR count of the
name-prefix alongside the row text, threaded through `ItemDockRow`'s
new `meta_start` field so the renderer draws two style runs per row
instead of re-parsing the string for " — " (which an item's own name
could itself contain). `[vanished] ` stays at normal weight — it's a
status flag, not metadata.

`inventory_panel.meta` takes `room_panel.aliases`'s treatment (muted,
no italic) rather than `room_panel.description`'s (muted + italic),
since this is host-authored metadata, not quoted game prose.

Also gave `style_example_matches_generated_template` the same
LANTHORN_REGEN_DOCS regen path `docs_reference.rs`'s checks already
have, so `style.example.toml` and docs/reference/style.md can be
regenerated together as intended.

events.message:
fix(app): name the Mac/Amiga colour picture archive's machine when it's known (SQ-1650)

A colour AmigaMac picture archive (Pic.data/CPic.data, EF_MONO clear) always
labelled itself plain "Amiga" in the launch dialog and story-browser info
panel, even when the story was mounted out of a known Macintosh HFS disk
image — the codec alone can't tell Amiga and Mac colour art apart, but the
medium it came off can.

rendition_label now takes the caller's known machine (from
blorb::medium::DiskImage::machine) and resolves the ambiguity to "Mac" or
"Amiga" when it has one; with no known medium in scope it now says the
honest "Amiga/Mac" instead of guessing "Amiga". Threaded through
discover_art_candidates and resolved_default_art, and wired up at every
caller that already knows its disk image: LaunchOptionsState::new/
on_disk_entry (from the disk_image field already passed in), and picker.rs's
resolve_aux (reusing the InterpreterProfile it already resolves for the
info panel's font row, rather than mounting the medium a second time).

events.title: fix(formats): a recorded sector ID 0 stays 0 in FDI, NFD, STX and TD0 — before, R = 0 and R = 1 both came out as 1 (MF-1623, P3-549)
events.message:
fix(formats): a recorded sector ID 0 stays 0 in FDI, NFD, STX and TD0 — before, R = 0 and R = 1 both came out as 1 (MF-1623, P3-549)

Four plugins passed the recorded R through `R > 0 ? R - 1 : 0` into
uft_format_add_sector(), which adds 1 again. For R >= 1 that is the
identity; for R = 0 it yields 1, so a track carrying R = 0 and R = 1
came out with two sectors named 1 and the first one's real name was
gone. Copy protection uses exactly such IDs. MF-1017 fixed the same
shape in jv3.

P3-549 listed six plugins, read only (MF-1344, "NICHT an Abbildern
gemessen"). Measured now, red first: tests/test_sektor_id_null_bleibt_null.c
builds one track with R = 0,1,2 (FDI, NFD) or sets the first R of a
corpus file from 1 to 0 (STX, TD0) and reads it through the plugin
itself. Before: two sectors named 1 in all four formats ("1,1,2";
"1,2,3,..."). After: 8 of 8.

- fdi (data path and no-data fill path), nfd (data path and truncated
  fill path), stx, td0: uft_format_add_sector_with_id(track, R, ...).
- d77 was already fixed (its own comment, test_d77_spur_nach_kopf); the
  P3-549 list is corrected there.
- edsk is NOT touched. It loses more than ID 0: its read_track drops the
  ST1/ST2 findings its own parser decodes (CRC error, deleted, no data,
  weak), takes C/H from the physical position and N from the data
  length. The tested reader of the same format, dsk_cpc, does all of it
  right, and both tie at 95 on samdisk_edsk.dsk. Whether edsk is fixed,
  withdrawn or kept is a removal question, so it stands as P3-713 with
  the three ways and their costs, for the owner.

Mutation matrix 6 of 6 red (each site back to the old shape). The first
run left two mutants alive — the fill paths of FDI and NFD, which the
test did not enter; the two cases were added before commit.

The constants gate refused the first version of the test: its TD0
builder copied the header/track/end byte arrays of test_td0_error_marks
(three new copies of known families). STX and TD0 now take a committed
corpus file (hxcfe_pc160.stx, libdsk_uftk_pc720.td0) and set the first
sector's R from 1 to 0, with the 1 asserted as the anchor.

The same gate reported family 75bc6d286ade (uft_ipf_air.c::buf /
test_air_cross_validate.c::ipf_trunc) as gone — a consequence of the IPF
cleanup in MF-1617 that the manifest never followed. The ratchet only
shrinks: konstantenfamilien_grundlinie.json 56 -> 55 families, 16 lines
removed, none added.

Docs: OPEN_ITEMS P3-549 closed for the four, P3-713 new.

events.title: fix(triage): a blank sector is not a damaged one — a clean xdftool ADF no longer comes out "severely damaged" (MF-1622, P3-708)
events.message:
fix(triage): a blank sector is not a damaged one — a clean xdftool ADF no longer comes out "severely damaged" (MF-1622, P3-708)

uft_triage_analyze() judged each sampled sector of a sector dump by a fill
check: a sector of nothing but 0x00 (D64: also 0xFF) scored 50 and counted
as BAD. That is exactly how an unused sector of a sparse disk looks.
Measured on free, undamaged corpus dumps from foreign tools, before:

  xdftool_dd_ofs.adf     9/100, 30 of 33 "unreadable", RED
  vice_c1541_35trk.d64   3/100, 55 of 57 "unreadable", RED
  mtools_fat12_720k.img 33/100,  2 of 3  "unreadable", RED

and the recovery wizard turned the first into "SEVERE damage ...
Professional data recovery may be required". A blank ADF and a blank D64
were additionally reported as "Copy protection detected", because a blank
bootblock / BAM failed the "DOS" check.

The fill check measured emptiness, not damage. A sector dump records no
read status; what it can show is data MISSING from the file and, for a
D64 with the trailing error block, the 1541 error bytes — which the
triage ignored.

- One blank test (sector_blank) replaces the three fill checks; blank
  sectors are counted and named in the summary, never scored.
- A sampled sector is bad only when it is missing from the file or, in a
  D64 with an error block, its error byte names an error.
- The D64 error-byte rule (0x00/0x01 = no error) stood as a literal in
  the D64 plugin; it now stands once, as uft_cbm_error_byte_ok() in
  uft_cbm_geometry.h, and the plugin and the triage both call it. Its
  comment says what is sourced: Schepers' D64.TXT lists 0x01 as "no
  error"; 0x00 has no entry there, and the plugin's reading of it as
  "no error" is kept, not decided.
- A blank bootblock / BAM is no protection finding.
- For a sector dump the summary no longer says "good condition" or
  "sectors unreadable": it names present / missing / blank and says that
  a dump records no read status. A D64 with error bytes says so instead.
- The recovery wizard's good band said "Disk quality is good ... standard
  imaging should work" — a statement about the disk that a sampled dump
  cannot carry. It now says "No finding in the sampled sectors".
- Left alone, named: src/formats/d71/uft_d71_parser_v2.c:316 counts D71
  error bytes by the same rule as its own literal; the file is an orphan
  (docs/orphan_baseline.txt), nothing reads it.
- The comment "track 18 counts double" was false (the code never
  weighted) and says what the score is.

Tests: tests/test_triage_leer_ist_kein_schaden.c (new, 19 cases),
red first against the old code: 16 of 19 red; after: 19 of 19. Case (4)
(a cut-off ADF keeps its 11 missing sectors bad) is a guard that was
green before and must stay green.
test_recovery_wizard_ohne_prozente gains one case (the advice on the
clean ADF names neither damage nor a disk condition), 5 of 5.
Mutation matrix 12 of 12 red: blank counted bad (ADF, D64, IMG each),
missing ADF sector not bad, D64 error bytes ignored, error-byte rule
accepting all (caught by the triage test AND by the plugin's
test_crc_befund_erreicht_modell), blank bootblock / BAM as protection,
dump summary not written, error-byte summary lost, wizard claiming disk
quality; tree restored green.

The first suspicion in P3-708 ("reads a headerless Amiga image by a PC
geometry") was wrong and is corrected there; the geometry was right.

Docs: OPEN_ITEMS P3-708 closed.

events.title: feat(plan): the settings tab's clock correction reaches the flux decoder — a carrier the field mapping had not seen (MF-1621, P3-711)
events.message:
feat(plan): the settings tab's clock correction reaches the flux decoder — a carrier the field mapping had not seen (MF-1621, P3-711)

Owner answer 2 (2026-09-29): wire the fields whose value has a carrier.
After MF-1619 I measured which fields of uft_convert_options_t are read
at all. decode_cell_adjust_pct (MF-480, "percent nudge for the decoder's
cell time, 50..200; 0 or 100 means unchanged") has 7 read sites, and
uftc_apply_decode_options() puts it into the decoder's media profile on
the SCP -> ADF path (an HFE source is refused with a warning, because its
cells were clocked when recorded). Nothing in the user interface set it.
That is exactly the draft's "Taktkorrektur (50..200 %)". The field
mapping had listed it as "no reader" because it searched for the widget
name, not for the meaning of the carrier.

- uft_copy_plan_t gets cell_adjust_pct (appended; 0 = unset).
  uft_copy_plan_to_convert_options() sets decode_cell_adjust_pct only when
  it is set, so the dispatcher's default of 100 stays otherwise; the
  converter checks the range itself and says when it does not apply it.
  The JSON names the value only when it is set.
- The tab sets it only while "Erweiterte Optionen" is switched on (the
  checkable group disables its fields, and a disabled field contributes
  nothing) and only when it is not 100. The label's tooltip says where
  it acts.
- Setups now store only EFFECTIVE values, as the draft's README demands,
  plus whether the advanced group was on; loading switches the group
  before applying values. The hidden-value test now enters its value
  explicitly, as an older or foreign file would carry it.
- 27 fields stay marked. The other carriers with readers
  (decode_vote_confidence_pct, reverse_decode, use_multiple_revs) have no
  field of the same meaning in the draft; mapping one would be invented.

Tests: tests/test_copy_plan_taktkorrektur.c (new, 5 of 5, red first:
the field did not exist), test_format_tab_bindung 14 (new case:
the value reaches the plan only with the group on, 100 stays unset, a
setup restores both), copy_plan 28, capability_gating 7, retries 6.
Mutation matrix 9 of 9 red, each by its own case (value ignored,
written unconditionally, JSON omits / always names it, tab never sets
it, sets it while the group is off, sets 100, setup forgets the group,
setup writes ineffective values); tree restored green.

events.message:
feat(plan): the settings tab's retry count reaches the conversion, the default plan is fully initialised, and the encoding field stays marked because nothing reads it (MF-1619, P3-711, P3-712)

Owner answer 2 (2026-09-29): wire the fields whose value has a carrier
in the core. MF-1618 left two such fields marked until this commit.

1. Retries — wired.
   uft_copy_plan_t gets two appended fields, read_retries and
   read_retries_gesetzt (zero = unset, same pattern as caps /
   caps_bekannt). uft_copy_plan_to_convert_options() lets an explicit
   count win over the read strategy; unset, the strategy decides as
   before. The JSON names the count only when it is set. The tab sets it
   only when "Max. Wiederholungen" is visible and free: when the
   strategy forces read.retries, the parameter gate locks the field and
   the plan carries no count of its own. The effect is real but narrow,
   and the label's tooltip says so: decode_retries is read in the
   SCP -> D64 conversion, where it bounds the revolutions tried.
   Setups (.uftsetup) now store the count.

2. Encoding — NOT wired, measured.
   The carrier flux_decoder_options_t.encoding has exactly one reader,
   flux_decode_track(). Its callers outside its own file are
   uft_otdr_adaptive_decode.c (no caller, MF-767) and uft_diag_gw.c
   (names only itself). No conversion and no read job reaches it; the
   converters pick their decoder from the TARGET. Wiring the field would
   be a promise without a deed, so it stays marked, and the comment that
   said "carrier in the core, no path yet" is BERICHTIGT. 28 fields are
   marked now.

3. A defect found on the way: uft_copy_plan_default() declared
   `uft_copy_plan_t p;` and set ten fields; caps and caps_bekannt
   (appended in MF-1311) stayed uninitialised. uft_copy_plan_gate_caps()
   reads both to choose between DENY and NEEDS_MEASUREMENT, and the
   settings tab builds every plan from this function. Red first: the test
   dirties the stack, then calls it; before, caps = 0x00001000. Now the
   struct is zeroed first, so every future appended field is "unset" too.
   Not measured: whether the garbage ever produced caps_bekannt = true
   and so a wrong verdict — that depends on the caller's stack.

Tests: tests/test_copy_plan_wiederholungen.c (new, 6 of 6),
test_format_tab_bindung 13 (new case: the count reaches the plan only
when the field is free; unwired count 29 -> 28), copy_plan 28,
capability_gating 7. Mutation matrix 8 of 8 red: default not zeroed;
explicit count ignored; count written unconditionally; JSON omits it;
JSON always names one; tab never sets it; tab sets it while locked;
field marked unwired again.

Docs: OPEN_ITEMS P3-711 NACHTRAG and BERICHTIGT (the tab has 1322 lines,
not "about 1000"; its mutation matrix was 15 of 15, not "14+"), P3-712
(new).

c64os-llvm: ship as a .car, C64 OS's own app archive

C64 OS apps ship as a .car: copied into //os/applications and
double-clicked, C64 OS's extractor makes the app's folder. `make car`
writes build/unoc.car with tools/mkcar.py -- the ega trek project's, which
measured the format against the third-party archives on a C64 OS volume --
and reads it straight back, checking every record and the CRC32 trailer.
The release zip now holds unoc.car and a README.txt in an uno-c64os-llvm/
folder, as egatrek-c64os.zip does. The archive date and the zip's
timestamps are fixed, so both rebuild byte for byte.

`make install-car` / `run-car` test the release path on a second, fresh
copy of the C64 OS disk: only unoc.car is installed (verified byte by
byte by the same BASIC installer, now a template for either layout), and
C64 OS is left to unpack it. Done in VICE: unoc.car double-clicked, the
unoc folder appeared, and the game played from it. main.o is unchanged --
the binary played before.

tools/build_all.py now skips install-* targets as emulator launchers, as
it already skipped run-*; without that the sweep would have opened VICE.
No other port has an install-* target.

events.message:
feat(gui): the settings tab rebuilt from the owner's design — what reaches an operation is wired, what does not says so (MF-1618, P3-711)

Owner request 2026-09-29: "setze alles um und verbessere es wenn
möglich … nimm dann das alt gui überall raus und ersetze es mit dem
neuen, verdrahte alles mit abhängigkeiten", with his four answers of the
same day:
  1. the copy-plan axes are their own section, editable only in the
     mode "Benutzerdefiniert"; findings always visible in the help column
  2. fields without a reader: wire where the core has a carrier; the
     rest visible, disabled, marked "noch nicht verdrahtet"
  3. a tab that takes effect immediately: no Apply / Close
  4. only this tab is replaced

Measured before building (git grep per objectName): the old tab had 129
input elements, 79 of them without any reader; its only product readers
were copyPlan(), leseUmdrehungen() and the plan source.

forms/tab_format.ui is the owner's Qt Designer draft, with the old
objectNames where the meaning is the same (btnModus_*, comboPlan*,
comboSystem/Format/Version, spinRevolutions, checkSHA256/checkHashSha512/
checkCRC32, labelProfileText, labelPlan*), plus: the copy-plan section,
the hash set under "Prüfen", a group for the IPF / CT-Raw helper paths,
the help column with findings / forced values / capabilities. Apply and
Close are gone (answer 3). Two corrections to the draft: its help text
said only effective options are shown, which answer 2 makes untrue, and
"Slicepunkt" is "Splicepunkt".

src/formattab.cpp is new: 3255 -> 1322 lines. Carried over with
their reasons: the named modes and axes (MF-1233/1235/1237), the JSON
view (MF-1238), the hidden-field rule (MF-1306), the capability gate and
the parameter gate (MF-661/1234/1320), variants from the plugin
(MF-1231/1308), the plan source (MF-1265). The old hand-kept format
database and its variant list are gone: their values flowed into fields
without readers.

New:
- 29 fields without a reader are disabled, marked "*", and carry the
  hint "Noch nicht verdrahtet". No gate re-enables them; gates only
  decide whether they are seen. Retries and encoding are among them
  until their own commits wire them (they have a carrier in the core).
- "Nach dem Wandeln nachprüfen" is a view of plan.policy (verify_after),
  not a second truth (MF-1177): it follows the policy and sets it.
- the system list is filtered against the registry; every registered
  format without a group appears under "Weitere Formate".
- .uftsetup (JSON): load order as the draft's README demands (mode,
  system/format/variant, visibility, values); a value for a field that
  is hidden or not wired is NOT applied, and it is named.
- the old presets.json is taken over once as .uftsetup files, untouched;
  what had no reader is listed under "nicht_uebernommen", not dropped.
- IPF / CT-Raw: helper and library path, stored in QSettings, effective
  through the environment uft_ipf_helper.c reads; status line.
- the header shows the connected hardware (MainWindow connects the same
  two HardwareTab signals that feed the LED and the workflow tab).

Two defects surfaced on the new tab, both fixed:
- MF-1320's "unknown hides nothing" lifted EVERY hidden/forbidden state
  for an unknown format, including the level's own: at "Automatisch",
  read.revolutions stayed visible on the file level. The gate now asks
  with all capabilities when the format is unknown, so level rules hold.
- at "Automatisch", 5 of 18 mode buttons were locked, because "unknown"
  counted as "can do nothing"; with a known format they lock as before.
  Findings at "Automatisch" invent no capability failure and say that
  the check follows once the format is known.
Four old tests had silently relied on the old tab opening on D64; they
now select D64 explicitly.

Tests: test_format_tab_copy_plan 28, test_format_tab_bindung 12
(rewritten: its witnesses went with the old form), test_format_tab_
capability_gating 7 (witnesses re-anchored, formats chosen from the
registry at run time). Mutation matrix on the tab: 15 of 15 red —
unwired fields not marked; either gate re-enabling them; unknown format
as caps 0; the verify view not following / not setting the policy; hash
set always visible; a setup applying values to hidden fields; migration
dropping "nicht_uebernommen"; helper path not reaching the environment;
the flux anchor removed; custom mode not freeing the axes; unknown format
locking modes; unknown format inventing capability findings; the device
name not shown. The last-but-one survived at first; the case
unbekanntes_format_erfindet_keinen_befund was added for it. And the
first run of the matrix measured nothing: Qt tests on Windows do not
write to a pipe, so every mutant looked green — including the unmutated
baseline, which is what gave it away. The runner now reads -o file,txt.

Smoke test (DoD for GUI changes): the tab rendered offscreen in three
states (start, EvidenceCopy + SCP + hardware, custom + file level); the
layout follows the draft, disabled fields are grey, the plan axes are
locked outside "Benutzerdefiniert". Offscreen has no fonts, so the text
itself was not read from the images. mainwindow.cpp and formattab.cpp
compile in the CMake app target; the full CMake app build stops at a
pre-existing GLOB issue (src/dtc_components without its include path),
unrelated to this change. qmake is canonical; CI builds it.

The test CMake block loses three sources only the old tab used
(flow layout, GW2DMK panel, protection API).

Docs: OPEN_ITEMS P3-711 (new), P3-528 NACHTRAG. BACKLOG C1: "called
from outside" of the protection catalogue drops 9 -> 8 (gate
audit_protection_claims.py caught it). The ninth call was
uft_prot_config_init() from FormatTab::getProtectionConfig() — a method
with 0 callers itself. It counted a connection from dead code; no path a
user reaches has changed.

events.title: fix(asm): each pass starts in the text section, re-entered sections continue (#57)
events.message:
fix(asm): each pass starts in the text section, re-entered sections continue (#57)

Two section-tracking defects, both present since sections were added:

- Pass 1, the relaxation recount and pass 2 reset the location counter
  but not the current section, so everything before the first SECTION
  directive went into the last declared section. A source opening with
  code and declaring SECTION gfx,DATA_C later came out as a single
  chip-RAM data hunk holding the code, and LoadSeg() entered data.
- Only the encoding pass saved a section's location counter when leaving
  it. In the sizing pass a second SECTION code restarted at the section's
  origin, so labels after it got addresses inside the first part, and
  references to them encoded the wrong offsets.

Each pass now restarts in the text section with every section back at its
origin, and SECTION saves the counter of the section being left.

events.title: fix(app,zvm): stop the item tracker showing "it"/"thing" or raw Inform identifiers (SQ-1649)
events.message:
fix(app,zvm): stop the item tracker showing "it"/"thing" or raw Inform identifiers (SQ-1649)

Two distinct, previously-unexplained symptoms from SQ-1648's own diagnosis,
each traced to a different root cause:

- HHGG's own avatar object (#31) prints the header short name "it" and its
  only parse word is "protag" ("PROTAGONIST" truncated to a v3 dictionary's
  6 characters) -- nothing zvm::location::find_player_object_with checked
  for recognised it as the player, so it was NEVER excluded from item
  tracking: it followed the player into every room as a persistent fake "it"
  item for the whole 605-turn walkthrough, and -- the bigger half of the same
  gap -- the story's carried inventory was never tracked at all (0 of 3,319
  item observations were ever Carried), because the room-exclusion and the
  carried-inventory walk share the same unresolved player_obj. Fixed by
  adding "protag" to PLAYER_WORDS, the same precedent Lost Pig's "me" already
  set.

- HHGG's rose bed, wash-basin, wallpaper/chair and birdcage objects, and Lost
  Pig's "(missingOutside)"/"(whistle)"/"(missingBR)"/"(key)" placeholders and
  six auto-multiplied "Brick_1".."Brick_6" instances, are genuine per-object
  data -- verified not a decoding bug (neighbouring objects decode sane text;
  zvm::objects::printed_name, the SQ-1372-aware reader, returns the identical
  text on Lost Pig, ruling out a wrong-property read there too). They are
  real objects whose author gave them no player-facing name at all.
  item_tracker_display_name now treats a bare pronoun ("it", "thing", ...) or
  an Inform-identifier-shaped printed name ("(whistle)", "Brick_1") the same
  as an absent one, falling through to the existing word-list tiers instead.

Both real-game walkthrough suites gained regression assertions, and both
fixes were falsified (reverted, confirmed the original symptom reproduces,
restored) before landing.

events.message:
fix(ipf): every record read by its own length, what is skipped is counted, and the duplicates are out (MF-1617, P3-710)

Owner request 2026-09-30: "uft_ipf_air.c verbessern, so dass es wieder
zum Tool passt; falls doppelt, dann weg". An inventory by git grep per
identifier found four things.

1. INFO and IMGE were read by a FIXED advance (84 / 68 payload bytes);
   the length in the record header was never compared. Red first,
   tests/test_ipf_air_satzlaenge.c rebuilds the free disk-analyse IPF
   with a changed INFO record (CRC per Louis-Guerin, IPF Documentation
   V0.0 ch. 2.1): an INFO of 100 bytes gave 0 tracks instead of 168, an
   INFO of 60 bytes read on into the next record and said TRUNCATED.
   2 of 4 failed. Now every record is read by its own length, and a
   record shorter than its fields (INFO 96, IMGE 80, DATA 28) is
   refused as BAD_RECORD.

2. Duplicated or called only by tests, removed:
   - ipf_air_print_info (printf dump) and ipf_air_platform_name
   - the IPF_AIR_TEST self-test, never built (docs/selbsttest_baseline.txt
     line removed; the gate reported it as resolved)
   - ipf_air_get_track_raw: decoded bytes instead of cells (P3-360),
     superseded by uft_ipf_zellstrom; its only callers were two tests,
     which now check the unread-record count and the cell count
   - the file's own big-endian reader and the plugin's copy: the tree
     has uft_read_be32 (uft/uft_endian.h)
   - include/uft/profiles/uft_ipf_format.h: a second IPF parser with 0
     callers, whose INFO check would have refused a real 96-byte record;
     the plugin included it and used nothing from it
   1268 -> 1031 lines.

3. CTEI/CTEX were parsed into structures that only the printf dump read;
   a second CTEI leaked the first; unknown records vanished without a
   trace. Now they are skipped by their length and COUNTED
   (ipf_air_get_unread_records), and the plugin names the count.

4. In uft_ipf_air.h, `extern "C"` closed before ten declarations; a C++
   caller would have got C++ linkage for them. It now closes at the end.

Test 8 of 8. Mutation matrix 6 of 6 red, each caught by exactly one
check: INFO fixed advance; INFO length unchecked; IMGE fixed advance;
DATA length unchecked; CTEI counted as unknown; unknown not counted.
All 11 IPF tests green. On the four real IPFs (two SPS-encoded, two
local), the reader delivers unchanged 88 / 1760 / 1570 / 1600 sectors,
0 tracks differing from the capsimg helper. None of the six corpus IPFs
carries CTEI/CTEX, so no new warnings appear and nothing measurable is
lost by dropping the CTEI/CTEX structures.

Kept on purpose, and named in P3-710: the SPS gap elements are parsed
but have no reader (the cell stream uses gap_default only); the fixed
84x2 track table stays, what lies outside is counted (MF-1372).

and NACHTRAG (helper built, reader replaceable, not replaced); PROTOCOL.md
and uft_ipf_helper.h note the removed function.

fix(app): resolve a no-printed-name item's tracker display to a real word, not a joined list (SQ-1648)

ObjectWords::display_name() joins every parser word into one run-on string
when an object has no printed name (correct for its other callers, which
need every word the parser will accept) and leaves a Glulx dictionary word
exactly as truncated ("proprieto" for "proprietor"). The item tracker used
that string verbatim as ItemObservation::name, producing entries like
"proprieto men old portly shopkeepe man himself person" for Anchorhead's
shopkeeper.

Add item_tracker_display_name (session.rs), shared by zvm_item_observations
and glulx_item_observations: prefer the first of ow.words this turn's own
printed text actually used, matched with the same truncation comparison
ObjectWords::refers_to applies so the untruncated prose spelling is
returned for free; fall back to the first stored word, unspelled, when the
turn's prose gives no evidence. Scott Adams needs no change — its items
always carry a real printed_name.

Confirmed against stories/Anchorhead.gblorb: replaying the committed
walkthrough script to the Curiosity Shop resolves the proprietor to
"proprietor" (spelled out from the arrival prose) rather than the old
joined list; falsified by reverting to display_name() and confirming the
exact reported symptom reproduces.

Updated three item_tracking.rs assertions that depended on the old
joined-list substring shape (Cragne's coffee cup/wristwatch, King of Shreds
and Patches' walking stick) to match the new single-word names and match
by ObjectWords::refers_to instead of a name substring.

events.title: fix(verify): sectors are paired by ID, not by position — every real recording failed against its own correct sector image (MF-1616, P3-709)
events.message:
fix(verify): sectors are paired by ID, not by position — every real recording failed against its own correct sector image (MF-1616, P3-709)

Found through CT-Raw -> ADF (MF-1615): the IPF -> ADF converter wrote a
full, correct 901 120-byte ADF from sq1_amiga.ctr (local only, through
the capsimg helper), and verify_after then reported 125 of 160 tracks
as differing and took the success back. Measured against the written
file: 35 tracks happen to be in ID order, and exactly those 35 passed;
by ID, 1760 of 1760 sectors are equal.

uft_generic_verify_track() compared the s-th reference sector with the
s-th sector of the target. A sector image lists ID order; a recording
lists DISK order, which starts wherever the index fell. The same pairing
stood in uft_weak_bit_verify_track(), in the sector fallback of
uft_flux_verify_track() and in the per-sector counting of
uft_disk_verify(). A false alarm is as expensive as a silent loss
(MF-1307): it sends someone to the wrong place, and here it discarded a
correct result.

One pairing now, uft_verify_find_partner() (uft_format_plugin.h,
additive): the first unused sector of the target with the same
id.sector, so duplicate IDs (copy protection) pair in their order. All
four places call it (MF-1177). uft_disk_verify_self() stays positional:
it reads the SAME disk twice with the same reader.

tests/test_verify_nach_sektor_id.c reads the free xdftool ADF through
the ADF plugin and rotates the sector list, which is what a recording
delivers. Red first: 4 of 8 failed (the three track verifiers and the
disk-level count). The three guard cases (flipped bit, duplicated ID,
foreign ID) were green before and after. Mutation matrix 6 of 6 red:
partner ignores the ID; partner never marks used; generic, weak-bit,
flux fallback and disk count each back to position.

After, on the real image: sq1_amiga.ctr -> ADF rc 0, and the ADF is
BYTE-IDENTICAL to greaseweazle 1.23's `gw convert` output (md5
7de2c108d3014e473f0f78435c04079a). gw reads through the same
CAPSImg.dll but decodes itself. Workbench 1.3 and Lemmings stay refused
as incomplete, without a file (1749 and 11 of 1760 AmigaDOS sectors).
The 11 Workbench sectors UFT misses are the same 11 gw misses (h/s/c
lists compared), and the 1749 present ones are byte-equal to gw's ADF.
Whether the gaps are in the recording or in the revolution capsimg
delivers is NOT separated: both readers go through the same DLL.

events.title: fix(asm): hunk relocations and memory types, stricter operand and DC checks (#52)
events.message:
fix(asm): hunk relocations and memory types, stricter operand and DC checks (#52)

* fix(asm): emit HUNK_RELOC32 in hunk executables, keep text as hunk 0

Hunk executables carried no relocation table, so every absolute
reference (lea label,a0; move.l #label,d0; dc.l label) kept its
assembly-time address and pointed at garbage once LoadSeg() placed the
hunk anywhere else.

The relocations are recovered by assembling once more per section with
that section moved by RELOC_PROBE: a longword that moves by exactly the
probe is an address in that section. Any other change, or an overflow in
the moved run, means an address was used in a way a 32-bit relocation
cannot express, and is reported at its source line.

The default text section and the first declared section both had
order 0, so which became hunk 0 (the entry point) depended on HashMap
iteration order.

* feat(asm): --linedebug writes LINE debug hunks

Hunk executables can now carry source line info as HUNK_DEBUG blocks in
the LINE format, one per source file with absolute paths. Lines expanded
from a macro map to the invocation. The hunk reader parses these blocks
into Section::lines, so a debugger can map addresses back to source.

* fix(asm): plain absolute paths in line debug info on Windows

fs::canonicalize returns verbatim paths (\\?\C:\...) on Windows, which
no editor uses, so a debugger could not match source breakpoints
against the line table. Line debug info now records std::path::absolute
paths, which also keeps symlinked paths as the editor sees them.

* fix(asm): carry chip/fast memory requirements into hunk headers

SECTION name,DATA_C (and _F, or a separate CHIP/FAST argument) was
parsed for its type but the memory requirement was dropped, so the hunk
size table never had bit 30/31 set. LoadSeg() then allocated such hunks
in any memory, and bitplanes, sprites or samples could land in fast RAM
where the custom chips cannot reach them.

The section now records its memory type and the hunk writer sets bit 30
for chip and bit 31 for fast. An unknown memory argument is an error.

* fix(asm): undefined symbols inside operand expressions are errors

Pass 2 rejected an undefined symbol only when it was the whole operand.
Inside a displacement or expression the evaluator's pass-1 fallback of 0
stayed in place, so GM_HEIGHT(A2) with GM_HEIGHT never defined assembled
to 0(A2), and likewise (d,An), d(An,Xn), d(PC), and sums such as
SYM+2(A2), whether read or written.

Pass 2 now checks every identifier of an operand with the expression
evaluator, skipping register, control register and cache selector names,
so defined symbols, forward references and local labels behave as
before.

* fix(cli): deterministic order in symbol table and listing output

Symbols were sorted case-insensitively only, so names that differ just
in case (a label err_exist and a constant ERR_EXIST) kept hash-map order
and the symbol file changed between identical runs. Ties are now broken
by the exact name.

* fix(asm): multi-character constants, DC range checks, quoted DC.B expressions

Character constants in expressions yielded their first byte only, so
CMPI.L #'Hell',D0 compared against 'H' and MOVE.W #'ab',D1 loaded 'a',
without a message. Up to four characters are now packed big-endian and
right-justified ('ab' = $6162); five or more are an error. DC.W and
DC.L take a quoted literal as such a constant instead of rejecting it
as a DC.B-only string.

Two silent defects in DC found along the way:
- Values were masked to the element size: DC.B 300 emitted $2C and
  DC.W $12345 emitted $2345. A value now has to fit its size, read as
  signed or unsigned; symbols stored as 32 bits (X EQU -1) are read as
  negative so they still fit a byte.
- Any DC.B operand starting with a quote was copied as text, so
  DC.B 'x'+1 emitted the five characters of its source. Only a single
  complete literal is a string now; a doubled quote inside one is an
  embedded quote character.

* feat(asm): warn about word and long data at odd addresses

Instructions are padded to an even address; DC/DCB/DS data is not, since
moving it would shift every label after it. A word or long access to an
odd address raises an address error on the 68000, so DC.W/DC.L, DCB.W/L
and DS.W/L starting at an odd location counter now produce a warning
naming the address. The layout is unchanged.

* docs: hunk-exe relocations, memory types, --linedebug and DC rules

---------

events.title: 68030 MMU: split misaligned MOVES accesses when the data cache is off
events.message:
68030 MMU: split misaligned MOVES accesses when the data cache is off

Without data cache emulation, MOVES in the pipelined tables (34 and 35)
reads and writes through mmu030_get/put_fc_word() and _long(). These
call mmu030_get/put_word() and _long(), which translate only the address
of the first byte. A misaligned MOVES that crosses into the next page
therefore reads or writes the rest in the physically adjacent page, and
the page it belongs to is never faulted in.

Unix kernels do exactly this in copyin()/copyout() when a user buffer is
at an odd address. Under AMIX (Commodore's Amiga UNIX) in cycle-exact
mode, bytes of received network data read back as zero (the bytes went
elsewhere), TLS certificate chains fail to parse, and the kernel panics
in kmem_alloc() on free lists overwritten by the stray bytes.

Split them the way table 32 does (dfc030_put_long() and friends) and the
way the data cache path does (uae_mmu030_*_fc()): is_unaligned_bus() ->
mmu030_*_unaligned(). Aligned accesses take the same path as before.

everything. The other shm blocks are released as before.

master (13 of 13) and passes with this (11; config-roundtrip needs the

events.title: 68030 MMU: without data cache emulation, retried accesses go to memory
events.message:
68030 MMU: without data cache emulation, retried accesses go to memory

An access error RTE in the pipelined tables resumes a split (misaligned)
access through read_dcache030_retry() and write_dcache030_retry(). These
use the emulated data cache whenever the guest has enabled it in CACR,
even when data cache emulation is off. In that mode nothing else fills
or updates those cache lines, so a retried read could return a line
filled by an earlier retry, from before later writes.

With data cache emulation off, read and write memory directly, which is
what table 32's RTE (mmu030_get/put_generic) does. With it on, nothing
changes.

events.title: A2065/Ariadne: a receive buffer error doesn't stop the receiver
events.message:
A2065/Ariadne: a receive buffer error doesn't stop the receiver

When data chaining runs into a receive buffer the host still owns, the
emulation cleared RXON and wrote BUFF|OFLO into that host-owned
descriptor. On the real chip RXON is only cleared by STOP, RESET, a
memory error, or INIT with DRX (Am7990 data sheet, CSR0 RXON; only the
transmitter is turned off by a BUFF error, CSR0 TXON). The error status
goes into the last buffer the chip used, and RINT is raised.

A driver that never re-initialises the chip after an error, which
matches real hardware, had no network after the first BUFF error.

Now ERR|BUFF|OFLO go into the last descriptor of the frame, RINT is
raised, the receiver stays on, and the host's descriptor is not
touched. QEMU's PCnet (pcnet_receive()) does the same.

Until now the helper branch of the IPF plugin delivered cells and ZERO
sectors per track. The sector block (uft_ipf_sektoren() plus its

CT-Raw images through the helper: 84x2, 168 tracks, 0 sectors each.

branches call it (MF-1177: one rule, one place). No new decoder:

has accepted against foreign hands.

Reference: UFT's own AIR reader on the same file.
tests/test_ipf_helfer_sektoren.c sends the cells of the disk-analyse
IPF (free corpus, Keir Fraser's writer, independent of AIR) across a
real process boundary; the test binary is its own protocol-v1 helper.
Red first: helper 0 of 88 sectors. After: 88 of 88, equal to the AIR
path in ID, bytes and status on every track.

Mutation matrix 3 of 4 red (no decode in the helper branch; half the
cells; no decode in the AIR branch). The fourth, "cells shifted by one
byte", is equivalent on this input: the track starts with gap, and the
sector layer records no position (uft_ipf_sektoren.c sets no bit_offset).

Measured with the REAL capsimg (greaseweazle 1.23 CAPSImg.dll):
  IPF, helper vs AIR, per track (ID, bytes, status):
    disk_analyse_uftk_amiga.ipf     88 sectors, 0 tracks differ
    disk_analyse_uftk_amiga_80.ipf  1760 sectors, 0 tracks differ
    sps_lethalxcess_a.ipf           1570 sectors, 0 tracks differ
    sps_lethalxcess_b.ipf           1600 sectors, 0 tracks differ
  CT-Raw, helper only (the AIR path does not read CT-Raw):
    sq1_amiga.ctr             1760 of 1760, all checked and clean
    amiga-wb132d_blaurot.ctr  1749, all checked and clean
    lemmings_amiga-pal_disk1  11 sectors on one track
Where the 11 missing Workbench sectors sit is NOT measured. That
Lemmings uses its own track format fits, but is not established.

the existing IPF -> ADF converter writes SQ1 as a full 901 120-byte ADF,
but verify_after reports 125 of 160 tracks as differing and takes the
success back. The ADF is right: 1760 of 1760 sectors equal BY ID.
uft_generic_verify_track() compares by POSITION, and exactly the 35
tracks whose disk order happens to start at sector 0 pass.

events.title: 68040/68060 MMU: debug memory reads select instruction or data space by FC bit 1
events.message:
68040/68060 MMU: debug memory reads select instruction or data space by FC bit 1

In get_byte_debug(), get_word_debug() and get_long_debug(), the non-68030
branch used the instruction-fetch path (mmu_get_iword/mmu_get_ilong) when
debug_mmu_mode & 1, i.e. for the DATA function codes 1 and 5, and the data
path for the program codes 2 and 6. The 68040 and 68060 match instruction
and data accesses against separate transparent translation registers
(ITTx/DTTx), so a debugger read of data could translate differently from
the CPU's own data accesses. get_real_address_debug() and debug_safe_addr()
already pass debug_mmu_mode & 1 to mmu_translate() as its data argument;
the readers now agree with them: FC bit 1 (program space) selects the
instruction path, everything else the data path.

Verified in Hatari (which shares this code) with Linux booted on an
emulated 68040 and a user-data read of $2000: with DTT0 matching and ITT0
off the read now returns the memory (it returned the $FF of a failed
page-table walk), and with ITT0 matching and DTT0 off it now fails as it
should (it returned the memory).

events.title: fix(ipf): CT-Raw is named instead of called invalid — and capsimg's "flakey" on CT-Raw is no protection finding (MF-1614, P3-707)
events.message:
fix(ipf): CT-Raw is named instead of called invalid — and capsimg's "flakey" on CT-Raw is no protection finding (MF-1614, P3-707)

CT-Raw (.ct/.ctr, SPS raw dumps) is the IPF's CAPS record chain with TRCK
records instead of IMGE. Measured on three images from archive.org
(collection flux_floppies, local only): CAPS 1, then DATA/TRCK pairs,
168 of each, and the chain ends exactly at EOF.

Two defects, both measured before the fix:

1. Without the capsimg helper, open() answered UFT_ERR_FORMAT_INVALID
   (-25) for a valid CT-Raw file. That is a false statement about the
   file. Now it answers UFT_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED (-40) and names the path
   that reads it (UFT_IPF_HELPER). CT-Raw is recognised only from a
   COMPLETE chain: CAPS, at least one TRCK, no IMGE, every length
   consistent, ending at EOF. A broken IPF is never passed off as CT-Raw.

2. Through the helper, capsimg sets CTIT_FLAG_FLAKEY on EVERY track of
   all three images, including an unprotected Workbench 1.3 disk and its
   unformatted tracks. The plugin turned that bit into
   UFT_TRACK_PROTECTED and copy_protected, so 168 of 168 tracks were
   reported as copy-protected, a protection finding nobody made. On
   CT-Raw the bit is now named once in the log and makes no claim. On
   IPF the meaning is unchanged: there the SPS marks weak bits itself.

Measured after the fix, on the three real images:
  without helper: rc -40 (each)
  with helper:    84x2, 168 tracks, 0 copy-protected, 0 fuzzy (each)

tests/test_ipf_ctraw.c, red first: 2 of 7 checks failed before the fix,
exactly (1) the refusal and (6) the protection claim. The test binary is
also its own protocol-v1 fake helper, so the plugin runs through a real
process boundary. The fixture is built from the measured layout
(structure only). Mutation matrix 6 of 6 red, each caught by exactly
one check:
  open without refusal; flakey still protection on CT-Raw; flakey
  dropped for IPF too; detector accepts a broken chain; accepts a DATA
  payload past EOF; ignores IMGE.
The last three needed three extra inputs. The first fixture ran into
the length check before any of those branches, so all three mutants
stayed green at first.

Still open (P3-707): sectors from the helper's cells (0 per track today).

events.title: fix(app): close the exit-save-flag race in lifecycle.rs's other tests (SQ-1641)
events.message:
fix(app): close the exit-save-flag race in lifecycle.rs's other tests (SQ-1641)

exit_auto_save and exit_clear_resume_save both unconditionally construct
crate::ExitSaveGuard, which flips the process-global EXIT_SAVE_IN_PROGRESS
atomic. Four tests called one of those functions without first taking
exit_save_lock() — the Mutex meant to serialize every test that touches the
flag — so under cargo test's shared-process, multi-threaded model any of
them could flip the atomic out from under
exit_auto_save_publishes_its_progress_to_the_termination_watchdog's own
"nothing running before" assertion, intermittently panicking it on CI
(seen 4 times this session: macOS x2, Windows x1). nextest is structurally
blind to this, since it runs each test in its own process.

Added `let _flag = exit_save_lock();` to the four tests that were missing
it, so every test in the module that can flip EXIT_SAVE_IN_PROGRESS now
holds the one lock that serializes them, making the race unreachable by
construction. Updated the two doc comments describing the discipline to
match.

test(app): exercise SQ-1627 item tracking across the 7 full walkthroughs (SQ-1647)

The item-tracking machinery (mapper::graph::MapGraph::items()/item(),
ItemRecord, ItemLocation) has only ever been driven by short synthetic
fixtures and a few-turn real-game snippets. Wire apply_item_observations
into all 7 walkthrough suites' turn loops (mirroring host::turn.rs's real
per-turn order: apply_turn, then apply_item_observations) and add sanity
assertions at each walkthrough's real ending — deliberately no exact
item/count pinning, since this repo's own synonym_groups.tsv precedent
shows pinned lines break on unrelated changes.

Per game (all thresholds derived from an actual run, not guessed):
- Photopia: asserts an EMPTY registry (0 items) is the expected shape,
  mirroring its existing empty-room-graph assertion — no location or
  player-object signal reaches this narrative work at all.
- HHGG, Lost Pig, The Lurking Horror, Zork Zero, Adventureland: a
  non-empty floor well under the observed count (106/99/79/111/27), plus
  a "Vanished entries aren't the overwhelming majority" check (<90%,
  comfortably above every observed specimen's high-water mark of ~31%)
  and an orphan check (every Vanished item's room is one the graph
  actually mapped).
- Anchorhead (Glulx): the same three checks, plus an SQ-1640
  scenery/door-exclusion regression exercised across the whole 629-turn
  script (the alley is revisited 16 times) rather than item_tracking.rs's
  single-turn case. Confirmed the ~47% Vanished rate here (highest of any
  lane) is genuine inventory churn — keys, clothes, tools — not scenery
  leakage.

No production code changed. Adventureland/Scott Adams gets no scenery
filter check: gvm::objects::ParseNames::is_scenery_or_door is Glulx-only
and crates/scott has no equivalent (a possible follow-up, not built here).

events.title: feat(ipf): the capsimg helper exists — the other side of the process boundary, measured against H1-H5 (MF-1613, P3-190)
events.message:
feat(ipf): the capsimg helper exists — the other side of the process boundary, measured against H1-H5 (MF-1613, P3-190)

Owner decision 2026-09-29: capsimg is used under its own licence, the
SPS DECODER LIBRARY licence v1.02 (non-commercial), and only through the
helper process that PROTOCOL.md v1 has described since MF-917. UFT's
side had been built and measured since then; the program behind it was
missing.

tools/capsimg-helper/uft_capsimg_helper.c (MIT, ~250 lines) loads
CAPSImg.dll / libcapsimage.so at run time from a path the user gives
(UFT_CAPSIMG_LIB). Nothing of capsimg is in the tree or compiled in; the
declarations are interface facts from the public CapsAPI.h, declared
anew. The two programs talk through files only.

Measured with the CAPSImg.dll shipped with greaseweazle 1.23 (win64):
- CAPS-encoder IPF (free corpus, 4 cyl): rc 0, 84x2, 8 tracks with data
- the same source at 80 cylinders (local): 160 tracks with data
- two SPS-encoder IPFs (local): 82x2, 160 tracks each
- the hollow hxcfe_ibmdd.ipf (P3-358): rc 5, ERROR, no TRACK line (H3)
- three CT-Raw images from archive.org (local only): 168 of 168 tracks
- H2: index and blob byte-identical on a second run
- H4 needed a correction: an IPF cut to 20 000 bytes keeps every track
  header, and capsimg answers CAPSLockTrack rc 2 for 163 of 164 tracks.
  The first version listed those as empty and ended with END, which is
  exactly the partial answer H4 forbids. A lock error is now rc 5.
- H5: rc 6, ERROR, no TRACK line
- H6 NOT established: the flakey bit is passed through, and capsimg sets
  it on every track of all three CT-Raw images. Whether they carry weak
  bits is unmeasured.

Cross-check against UFT's own IPF reader: 160 of 160 tracks carry the
same cell count, on two images. Writer, capsimg and UFT are three hands.

CI: the consistency job compiles the helper with -Werror on Linux and
checks that, without the library, it answers rc 3 with an ERROR line
and no TRACK line. CI has no capsimg and gets none. Run the same way
under WSL: PROBE OK rc=3.

Docs: PROTOCOL.md line "nach stdout: den TEXT-Index" BERICHTIGT (the
index goes to the file argv[2], as uft_ipf_helper.c reads it); §5 gets
the measured H1-H6; §7 Stand. OPEN_ITEMS P3-190 and P3-707 NACHTRAG.

Not done here, and named: sectors from helper cells; a named refusal for
CT-Raw without a helper (today rc -25); whether uft_ipf_air.c goes. That
removal needs an owner decision (MF-1077), and P3-353 is NOT settled by
this.

events.title: paula: keep the host output volume out of save states
events.message:
paula: keep the host output volume out of save states

Paula's output_volume (the status-bar slider) was serialized with the
machine, unlike its neighbouring host preferences. Loading a state set
the volume to whatever it was at save time, a rewind or netplay rollback
past a volume change undid it, and because netplay checksums digest
netplay_snapshot(), peers at different volumes reported a desync (and
computed different machine identities) even though the netplay guide
says volume stays local.

Skip it in serialization with a default of 1.0 (a bare skip would give
an f32 0.0 and mute every Paula decoded without a live one), and carry
it, together with mono, stereo separation and the filter override, in
Paula::adopt_host_preferences, called from Bus::adopt_host_resources.
That runs inside adopt_state, so every restore path shares it: state
load, rewind, run-ahead, netplay rollback and libretro frontend states.
The three hand-written carries in Emulator go away; only the uaelib file
root remains there.

This also fixes netplay_restore, which never carried mono, separation or
the filter override: each rollback reset them to stereo, full width and
Auto, and with a non-Auto filter a rolled-back peer's effective filter
could diverge at the guest's next /LED write.

Old states that still name output_volume keep loading: the chunk

events.title: fix(cd): CHD virtual pregaps are stored in FRAMES, not beside it
events.message:
fix(cd): CHD virtual pregaps are stored in FRAMES, not beside it

chdman counts a virtual (PGTYPE=V*) pregap inside the track's FRAMES
and writes it as zero frames at the head of the track. ParseCHD treated
it as unstored: it read INDEX 01 at chd_frame0 + 0 (still inside the
zero pregap) and added PREGAP to lengthLBA a second time, shifting every
later track by ~149 sectors cumulatively.

Myst (USA).chd (tracks 3-10 VAUDIO pregap 148/149) booted its stub from
track 2 (no pregap) then read zeros and sat on a black screen forever.
After the fix every track's first data sector matches the chdman
extractcd CUE/BIN, and cd_visual_verify shows video + audio (RMS 2809).

events.title: grm-j2kl: follow JSR-inline jump tables (the SMB JumpEngine idiom)
events.message:
grm-j2kl: follow JSR-inline jump tables (the SMB JumpEngine idiom)

A dispatcher that pops its own return address and JMP()s through the
word table laid out after the JSR (smb 8e04, db3 803a) was treated as a
returning call: Ghidra decoded the table as code (smb 8218 AND) and
never reached a target. smb recovered 1067 instructions for a 32 KB
game. A byte scan finds the idiom in 60+ corpus titles.

InlineJumpTableDispatchAnalyzer recognises the dispatcher body
structurally (PLA/STA lo, PLA/STA lo+1, Y = 2*A+1 at the first
LDA (lo),Y, the pair stored to a ZP pointer, JMP through it), marks it
no-return, stops the JSR's fallthrough and repairs the garbage with
ClearFlowAndRepairCmd, then lays each table down as pointers and
disassembles and schedules functions at the targets.

The table ends at the lowest target lying AFTER the table start
(targets below it are ignored: handlers sit on both sides, and
JumpTableBound's lowest-target rule, which declines on any below-table
target, dropped 7 of smb's 12 real tables), or at the first word that
cannot be a target. A table ended only by an invalid word has its tail
trimmed while its target lands mid-instruction, on data, or does not
decode, since nothing positive marked its end. All 18 smb JumpEngine
tables were checked against the ROM (c282 = 55, the enemy-ID table).

smb: 1067 -> ~6400 instructions. Real-ROM movement is confined to
titles using the idiom: zelda (instrs.inOverlay 264 -> 5966), smb3,
smb2, lwings, zelda2, db3, tmnt3, smb. NOT re-blessed yet; the held
rows (contra, dodge, ff1, tmnt, wizwarr, dragonpower flap) are
unchanged from their recorded states. Follow-ups: grm-rnf0 (targets in
another switchable window resolve to the base block's bank),
grm-1od4 (CopyLoopAnalyzer materializes smb's tiny ZP data copies as
code, newly reachable).

events.message:
feat(app): add a word-split source to the Guiding Light, tier 5 (SQ-1645)

`pickup toolcase` reached none of the six existing vocabulary-offer
sources: not a near miss or stem of `get`, and the synonym table's key
is the two-word `pick up`, a different string from the one-word
`pickup` typed. StoryVocabulary::by_word_split closes this gap by
trying every way of cutting the typed word into a leading and a
trailing piece and asking, of each cut, whether the leading piece
names a verb this story holds and the trailing piece is a literal
word that very verb's own grammar spells — a coincidence of
segmentation rather than of sentence shape (tiers 3/4) or of meaning
(tier 1).

Tier 5, last resort after tiers 0-4 have found nothing. Marked
vetting-mandatory like tier 4, since MIN_SPLIT_LEN admits two-
character pieces and this medium is thick with short verb
abbreviations that could coincide with an unrelated typo — the
conservative default until proven against a corpus the way tier 4's
own gate was.

Confirmed no separate Scott Adams exemption is needed: that dialect's
verbs always have empty prepositions(), so the check this source makes
(does THIS verb's own literal list contain the trailing piece) can
never succeed there by construction.

Real-fixture testing against anchor.z8 (Anchorhead, fetched via
scripts/fetch-fixtures.sh) found the grounding fact holds on real
data (`pick` genuinely pairs with the literal `up`), but also that
tier 4's broader bare-noun-shape net wins first on a fully developed
game like this one — both tiers are vetting-mandatory, so the player
sees a vetted answer either way. Both behaviors are pinned as tests.

events.title: sysarg: -vol 0..10 as documented (0 = silence), no more off-by-one
events.message:
sysarg: -vol 0..10 as documented (0 = silence), no more off-by-one

The -vol help says '<vol> must be an integer between 0 (silence) and
SYSSND_MAXVOL (max). The default is to play sounds at maximal volume'. The
code stored atoi()-1 and syssnd.c used 0 as 'not given', so:
- -vol 0 (silence) was rejected as invalid;
- -vol 1 meant the default, maximal volume (stored 0 = not given);
- -vol N for N = 2..10 gave volume N-1, never the maximum.

Now:
- sysarg.c: sysarg_args_vol = atoi() as given, valid 0..SYSSND_MAXVOL
  inclusive; 'not given' is -1 (initial value);
- rd1/syssnd.c: applies it when >= 0 (sndUVol is 0..SYSSND_MAXVOL, samples
  scaled by sndUVol / SYSSND_MAXVOL); without -vol it stays SYSSND_MAXVOL.

Checks: WSL make PC/ST clean builds, warnings 229/228 (one fewer each: the
explicit U8 cast); -vol 0, 1, 10 start, -vol 11 and -vol -1 fail with 'invalid
volume'; a throwaway copy printing sndUVol after init gave no -vol -> 10,
-vol 0 -> 0, 1 -> 1, 7 -> 7, 10 -> 10; ./build.sh desktop + web build.

events.title: Blits: short rows copy longs at any even address
events.message:
Blits: short rows copy longs at any even address

The whole-group tile path sent a source that was word aligned but not
long aligned to a word loop, and the branch's other changes made gcc
compile that loop to indexed moves with a stack compare per word. One
port carves its tiles from a single bank at word offsets, so every
16x16 tile blit ran about 25% slower on a plain ST than in v1.13.2,
and its frames were no faster despite everything else.

A 68000 moves a long at any even address, so the alignment test is
gone: short rows always go through stdl_copy_rows_groups when there
is no destination mask, and copy_row_short always moves stdl_wlong.
The lng argument is gone from the aligned row paths as well.

Port, level 1, 300 logic ticks, against v1.13.2:
- 16x16 tile blit: ST -41%, STE -37%, Mega STE -31%
- time per drawn frame: ST -18%, STE -15%, Mega STE -11%
- the game area is identical on all three machines

SPRCOST on st, all 85 cases: geometric mean 1.0008 against the
branch's previous commit, inside the 0.2-0.3% same-binary floor. The
one case that moved is a blit clipped out entirely, at +6us (+3%).
PIXCHK and I8CHK pass on st, and BLITCHK passes on ste at every
budget. Pixel-path text is 52 bytes smaller (34244).

stdl_blit_unaligned stays in stats builds so code that prints it
still links, but it always reads 0 now. The header's advice to align
borrowed buffers to four bytes is withdrawn.

events.title: feat(app): add a bare-noun grammar-shape source to the Guiding Light, vetting-mandatory (SQ-1644)
events.message:
feat(app): add a bare-noun grammar-shape source to the Guiding Light, vetting-mandatory (SQ-1644)

SQ-1642 shipped `by_grammar_shape` (tier 3): a last-resort candidate source
that offers a verb this story implements when it happens to accept the
exact sentence shape the player typed. It deliberately required at least
one literal preposition in the typed command, because a bare `VERB noun`
line is the single commonest shape in the medium and an unvetted claim
built on it alone is worthless noise (confirmed against two real Scott
Adams fixtures during that quest).

That gate left a real gap: "pickup toolcase" (one word, not "pick up")
reaches none of the five existing sources — it's no near miss or stem of
`get`, the synonym table's key is the two-word `pick up`, a different
string, and tier 3 declines outright for lacking a preposition — even
though "get toolcase" works.

Adds `by_bare_grammar_shape` (tier 4): the same question as tier 3, asked
for the bare shape tier 3 excludes, but gated so it can NEVER be shown
through the unvetted "this story knows" fallback — only through a probe-
confirmed "try instead", or not at all:

- `Candidate.tier == 4` marks every candidate from this source.
- `Pick::requires_vetting` (new field, `c.tier == 4`) carries that through
  `offer_picks`.
- `offer_vocabulary` computes `must_vet` from the raw `Pick`s (before
  `config.spoken_offer` collapses them to `Vec<String>` and the provenance
  is lost) and, when every surviving pick requires vetting and no probe
  answered, drops the offer entirely instead of falling back to the
  unvetted claim.

Scott Adams is excluded for free, with no per-engine branch: gated on
`!self.prepositions.is_empty()` (the STORY's whole grammar has a literal
word somewhere), and a Scott Adams database's grammar is always `VERB` or
`VERB noun` and never spells one, so `prepositions` is always empty there
(already established by SQ-1642's own fix).

Tests: nine new vocab.rs unit cases (tier-4 candidate generation, the empty
gate, position gating, the prepositions-empty exemption in isolation, and
`requires_vetting` on both tiers 3 and 4), plus two real-game cases against
Zork I in vocabulary_vetting.rs proving the mechanism end to end (vetted and
shown; unvetted and silent). Falsified each new behavior by temporarily
reverting it and confirming the originally-described symptom reproduced
(the Scott Adams gate, the must_vet arm, and the source itself) before
restoring the fix. Also updated `silence_is_the_common_answer`, whose
`xyzzy lamp` scenario stopped being silent now that tier 4 exists (every
verb in that fixture accepts a bare noun) — moved to a shape no verb there
answers, with a comment explaining why.

Existing tier-3 real-game and Scott Adams regression suites (including the
two `hasten north` fixtures the original preposition gate was written for)
still pass unmodified.

Completes: SQ-1644

events.message:
Web player: configurable host page, wasm URL via locateFile, iPhone sound unlock

1. Host-page configuration (the user's CMS page at rick-dangerous.org/player
   needed hand edits to player.js and to the generated xrick.js, kept by the
   user as a backup in web.1/):
   - a `defaults` block -- startInDemo, start, label, status, buttons, pad,
     saveTrace, wasmUrl -- overridable by the page with window.xrickPlayer set
     before player.js loads; defaults match index.html as built. The CMS page
     uses start '#xrick', label '#xrick span', status '#player_console',
     buttons '#controls1 div[data-code]', no pad (the 2019 layout);
   - every element except #canvas (SDL3's default selector) is optional: a
     missing one is skipped instead of throwing (the CMS page had to comment
     out bindPad because it has no pad);
   - start: the overlay is hidden with style.display='none' and the canvas
     shown with display:block, which works whatever the page's CSS (the CMS
     page hides the canvas until then);
   - Module.locateFile returns cfg.wasmUrl for xrick.wasm (the CMS serves it
     at /media/1vqhdi1t/xrick.wasm), else the default next to xrick.js. The
     generated xrick.js already asks Module.locateFile first, so it no longer
     has to be edited by hand after each build.

2. iPhone/iPad sound (reported: Safari and Firefox on iPhone show the speaker
   icon but play nothing): iOS plays Web Audio as "ambient" sound, muted by
   the Ring/Silent switch. In the start tap, before callMain:
   - navigator.audioSession.type = 'playback' where the browser has the
     Audio Session API;
   - on iOS/iPadOS, a silent looping <audio> element (0.25 s of 8-bit silence
     built as a WAV blob) started in the tap, which switches the page to
     playback audio and un-mutes Web Audio -- what the 2019 player's
     startAudio() did, lost in the W1.5 rewrite;
   - after callMain, SDL's AudioContext is resumed if not running, still in
     the tap.

Checks (headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol):
- index.html as built: ?demo&speed=2&trace identical to the native trace over
  12910 lines; ?rd=2 refusal and Esc ("game ended") shown in #status;
- a CMS-like page reconstructed from the user's edits (#xrick + span,
  #player_console, #controls1 div buttons, canvas hidden by CSS, the wasm only

events.title: Window runs can stop after N instructions, as if Ctrl-X
events.message:
Window runs can stop after N instructions, as if Ctrl-X

With a window, reaching `until` in Emulator.run() pauses the run instead of ending it, and `until` is dropped so the next Ctrl-X continues. Headless runs end at `until` as before. scripts/boot_lode_runner.py passes --instructions to windowed runs too; headless still defaults to 4000000.

events.title: ci(consistency): check out the full history — Tor 72's self-test needs a claimed MF number to exist, a shallow clone has none (MF-1609)
events.message:
ci(consistency): check out the full history — Tor 72's self-test needs a claimed MF number to exist, a shallow clone has none (MF-1609)

After MF-1608 the self-test ran 44/45 in CI (run 36595998750). The one
red case, "main() vermerkt auch den Abbruch", runs main() on the REAL
repository with the number MF-1522 and expects a refusal because the
number is already claimed. actions/checkout defaults to depth 1: one
commit, so nothing is claimed and main() accepts.

Reproduced: a `git clone --depth 1` of the repository gives 44/45 with
exactly that case red; the full-history worktree gives 45/45. The test
cannot use HEAD's own number instead — Tor 72 deliberately allows the
number HEAD claims (amend).

Fix: the consistency job checks out with fetch-depth: 0, as the
teilstring workflow already does. It is also the job where a binding
number check at the integration point (P3-680) would need the history.

Kennzahl: none of the four.

events.title: Video: opaque palette (alpha 255) -- the web canvas was transparent on Chrome/macOS
events.message:
Video: opaque palette (alpha 255) -- the web canvas was transparent on Chrome/macOS

Reported by the user: at www.rick-dangerous.org/player, Chrome on an Apple
silicon (M1) Mac played the sound but showed an entirely black canvas;
Chrome/Firefox on Windows and Safari on iPhone showed the game.

Cause: sysvid_setDisplayPalette only ever set pald[].r/g/b, so .a stayed 0,
and sysvid_update copies .a into the ARGB8888 streaming texture. Natively
that is invisible (the texture is drawn with SDL_BLENDMODE_NONE into an
opaque window). On the web SDL3 creates the WebGL context with an alpha
channel (SDL_video.c: gl_config.alpha_size = 8 by default ->
attribs.alpha) and WebGL composites premultiplied: every frame was colour
with alpha 0, an invalid premultiplied value that compositors handle
differently -- Chrome/macOS shows it as fully transparent (the page's black
CSS background showed through), the others happened to show the colour.
Confirmed by the user in the Mac's console: WebGL context present, canvas
640x400, and setting the canvas CSS background to red turned the black area
red.

Fix: sysvid_setDisplayPalette sets .a = 255 for all 256 entries, so every
pixel the game writes is opaque on every platform. Blending stays off, so
native rendering is unchanged.

Checks:
- headless Chrome, build/web ?demo: a pixel read back from the WebGL
  framebuffer right after each drawArrays is 80,54,26,255 (was 80,54,26,0
  with the old sysvid.c, same probe);
- ./build.sh: desktop Release x64 (3 known MSVC warnings), web 75 files, 168
  warnings (a clean build); WSL make: ST 229 / PC 230 warnings, unchanged.

events.title: fix(gate): Tor 72's self-test commits with its own identity — on a runner without user.name it failed 35/45 and turned the merge red (MF-1608)
events.message:
fix(gate): Tor 72's self-test commits with its own identity — on a runner without user.name it failed 35/45 and turned the merge red (MF-1608)

The merge 79ebd8eb brought the main-branch session's Tor 72 work to
origin for the first time; its CI run 36587407129 failed in the
consistency job: "MF-Nummer: Vorpruefung intakt" — the self-test of
scripts/audit_mf_nummer.py was red.

Cause, reproduced: the self-test builds a throw-away git repository and
commits into it with git_umgebung(), which only strips the repository
variables. The GitHub runner has no user.name/user.email, so every
`git commit` there failed. Locally (identity configured): 45/45. With
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointing at an empty file and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1:
35/45 — the same 10 red cases as in CI.

Fix: the self-test wraps git_umgebung() and sets a fixed test identity
with setdefault (an identity of the caller stays). After: 45/45 with
and 45/45 without a global git configuration.

The same class as ci_test_gating (local green is not CI green): the
difference here was not a library or a compiler but the git config of
the machine.

Kennzahl: none of the four.

events.message:
Memory: one hook list per kind of access

Each read method calls its after_read_* hooks with (address, value), each write method its after_write_* hooks with (address, value, old_value). The old value comes straight from the memory list, so taking it does not flip a soft switch at $C0xx. Each list is tested before its loop. events.message:
log: don't pass a va_list to variadic printf functions

Log_Printf() gave its va_list to fprintf() instead of vfprintf(), and
Log_AlertDlg() passed its va_list on to the variadic Log_Printf().
Both are undefined behaviour; on arm64 macOS every such log line comes
out as garbage, e.g.:

  ERROR: Unable to get size of <garbage> HD image file

The message formatting now lives in a static Log_VPrintf() that takes
a va_list (copied with va_copy() for each vsnprintf() pass); Log_Printf()
and Log_AlertDlg() both call it. Regression from 7e0ed796.

Startup restored saved SmartPort images while the saved slot layout was
still being applied, and applying it refitted every slot. setSlotCard
built a new, empty card even for the card already there, so the restored
image went with the old one; a IIgs, whose SmartPort is never refitted,
kept its image.

Refitting a slot with the card it holds now changes nothing, as restoring
a state already assumed, and main.js restores images only after the
layout is applied, which also covers a layout that moves the SmartPort.
test_emulator_disk.cpp pins the refit and fails without the fix.

events.title: Break on an address range and on the stack pointer
events.message:
Break on an address range and on the stack pointer

The Breakpoints tab takes a range ($2000-$20FF, symbols at either end)
for every type. Read, write and R/W ranges watch every address in them,
as watchpoints already could; an exec range stops when the PC enters it,
not on every instruction inside, so Run inside a range is not Step.

A new SP source stops when the stack pointer enters a value or a range
($00-$3F catches a runaway stack), just after the instruction that moved
it; 8 bits on a 6502, 16 on a 65816. It reports through its own hit, and
the host keys it apart from addresses so SP $F0 and $00F0 coexist.

Both live in MachineDebug, so the //e and the IIgs share them, and are
primed by the first check after they are added, so one put around the
paused PC does not fire on resume. Conditions, hit counts and enabling
work as before, and the Rule Builder names what the breakpoint watches.

test_machine_debug.cpp pins the rules, test_emulator_debug.cpp and
test_iigs_debug.cpp pin them on running code, and
breakpoint-manager.test.js pins parsing and what reaches the core.

events.title: BLiTTER: same-phase copies stay on the CPU while a border is open
events.message:
BLiTTER: same-phase copies stay on the CPU while a border is open

Found by building a game conversion against this branch. With both
borders open its play ran 0.7% slower than on v1.13.2, and 4% faster
with the BLiTTER refused altogether: every operation the chip does
under a border is first placed against the beam, and this branch
made the CPU's same-phase paths - row copies in registers, the edge
and keyed merges - fast enough to beat that at the sizes a game
restores. stdl_blitter_wants (out of line, so STDL_BlitSurfaceEx is
unchanged) now keeps same-phase copies below 256 cells on the CPU
while a placement policy is installed. Shifted blits and fills keep
their rules; the chip still wins those by 2-5x under a border.

That port's 512-frame play benchmark, both borders open, v1.13.2 ->
this commit (Hatari, TOS 2.06): STE 35.45 -> 32.50 ms/frame, Mega STE
23.90 -> 20.35, plain ST 31.94 -> 30.54. Borders closed: unchanged
(STE 32.19). Its cutscenes, every frame drawn, borders open: STE and
ST within 0.3%; Mega STE 1-2% either way of the rule, which a plain
ST does not reproduce (cache layout).

SPRCOST on ste: the border-open 32x32 restores move to the CPU but
still pay the decision's decline cost, so gain little there; with no
border a 16x1 blit is 1% (about 5us) slower for the extra test.
