events.title: Review fixes: alt-RAM by presence, an atomic scroll latch, and four more
events.message:
Review fixes: alt-RAM by presence, an atomic scroll latch, and four more

From a code review of the whole branch.

- Alt-RAM was detected as Mxalloc(-1, 1) > 0 - free alt-RAM, not
  alt-RAM - behind a GEMDOS-version gate. A program loaded into alt-RAM
  (ALTLOAD) can hold all of it, and its surfaces are then exactly the
  ones the BLiTTER must not touch. It is now yes if any of: free
  alt-RAM, the program above PHYSTOP, the heap above PHYSTOP, TOS's
  ramvalid/ramtop record, or an _FRB cookie. Mxalloc on a GEMDOS
  without it returns -32, so the gate is gone. EmuTOS on st, ste and
  megaste still reads no alt-RAM (ramvalid set, ramtop zero).
- The scroll VBL's "fetch not begun" test and the counter write it
  licenses are one masked step (about 120 cycles): a level-6 MFP
  interrupt between them could let the fetch start first.
- A sprite frame offset past sixteen bits truncated the frame index
  in its 32x16 fallback; it is a plain multiply there now (a sheet of
  4370+ frames, so banks only).
- BLiTTER sprites draw the planes the CPU loops do - budget 1 as 2, 3
  as 4 - since bank art is not normalised to the budget; at budget 3
  a colour-9 sprite came out 9 or 1 depending on its size and x. A
  host test builds sprites from all sixteen colours and draws them at
  budgets 3 and 1 both ways, and fails on the old plane count.
- The host BLiTTER model carries its source buffer across lines and
  operations, as the chip does, seeded with junk: a skewed first word
  now shows stale bits unless endmask 1 trims them, where it used to
  show zeros and could not tell.
- blit_whole kept its single memcpy only while no BLiTTER was allowed;
  surfaces the chip cannot reach now keep it too, instead of a copy a
  row at a time.

events.title: fix(ipc): reliable input key taps; disk put file type; gun gate seeded from config; manifest policy+effective tier; load updates MRU; ship the IPC doc; AGENTS.md drift guard (#63)
events.message:
fix(ipc): reliable input key taps; disk put file type; gun gate seeded from config; manifest policy+effective tier; load updates MRU; ship the IPC doc; AGENTS.md drift guard (#63)

* fix(ipc): reliable input key taps; disk put file type; gun gate seeded from config; manifest policy+effective tier; load updates MRU; ship the IPC doc; AGENTS.md drift guard

- input key/chord (beads-cjej): the hold counts only frames that began
  with the pressed matrix. Every keyboard publish bumps
  g_kbd_publish_serial; the tap arms its frame step with the serial read
  after the press, and KoncepcjaIpcServer::frame_step_tick() skips frames
  that started earlier. The frame already running used to count, so a
  hold=2 tap was live for one scannable frame, or none when the release
  raced the publish. Frame-step arming goes through arm_frame_step().
- disk put (beads-otjf): optional [auto|basic|binary|ascii]. basic and
  binary write AMSDOS header type 0/2; ascii writes no header (as
  SAVE"x",A does), CR LF line ends and a ^Z, so RUN" tokenises it. auto:
  .txt/.asc ascii, a plain-text .bas ascii, a tokenised .bas basic,
  anything else binary.
- input gun/mouse gates (beads-i834): loadConfiguration() publishes them,
  so a client that reaches the running Z80 before the main loop's first
  drain no longer gets ERR 409 no-light-gun.
- startup manifest (beads-tt7v): run_tier is the policy, effective_tier
  the resolved tier, the same pair IPC tier reports.
- load (beads-00jf): a successful disk/tape/snapshot/cartridge load goes
  on the Recent list via a main-thread drain; headless runs never save
  the config.
- packaging (beads-x9fk): every archive ships docs/ipc-protocol.md at the
  path README.md links.
- AGENTS.md (beads-5bcr): gtests assert its option list equals the
  argparse table and its [sound] keys are ones the loader reads; -F/--fps
  documented.
- devtools (beads-oz0): bare devtools documented as the idempotent open it
  is; F12 toggles.

* fix(test): AGENTS.md drift guard reads CR LF checkouts

On the MSVC runners git checks AGENTS.md out with CR LF, so the search for
"\n[sound]\n" never matched and DocumentedSoundKeysAreKeysTheConfigLoaderReads
failed on all four jobs. The doc (and the source it is checked against) is
now read in binary with every CR dropped, and the [sound] header is found as
a whole line. Verified locally against a CR LF copy of AGENTS.md.

* fix(review): disk put auto-detect, MRU under Settings, manifest v2, frames dump vs breakpoints

Review of PR #63:
- disk put auto: a .bas is tokenised iff it holds a 0x00 byte. Listings with
  CPC graphics characters, a UTF-8 BOM or the 0xE5 record padding `disk get`
  returns after the ^Z are no longer given a BASIC header. ASCII text ends at
  the first ^Z (one ^Z written). A host file that already has a valid AMSDOS
  header is written unchanged. When the host extension is not .bas/.txt/.asc
  the CPC name's extension decides, so a temp file pushed as GAME.BAS is no
  longer BINARY at load 0.
- disk put rejects a directory or unreadable file instead of writing an
  empty file and answering OK.
- IPC Recent-list staging moves to ipc_mru.{h,cpp}, keyed by t_CPC member
  pointer (no enum/switch, no UI header in the IPC server). Entries wait
  while the Settings dialog is open: a save then persisted its uncommitted
  edits and Cancel dropped the entry. IPC `snapshot load` stages its entry
  too.
- Startup manifest_version is 2: run_tier changed meaning and consumers
  must be able to tell.
- frames dump steps through wait_frame_step_done() and ends at a breakpoint
  with the frames recorded so far, instead of spinning forever and wedging
  the connection.

* fix(ipc): wait pc stops on the address exactly instead of sampling it

wait pc polled z80.PC, a view the machine publishes once per frame, so it
only ever saw the PC a frame happened to end on. The -i launch test waits
for &6000 while its program sits inside KM READ CHAR almost all the time:
a frame rarely ends on &6000, and a slow CI Mac that fits fewer frames into
the deadline timed out with PC in the firmware (PR #61 and #63 macOS e2e).
The "paused" in that status was the timeout's own pause.

wait pc now runs to the address with a one-shot probe breakpoint, as step
to does. A breakpoint or watchpoint hit on the way answers ERR 409
stopped-elsewhere with its WATCH= detail; a pause and resume by someone
else (the -i injection's register rewrite) keeps the wait going; a pause
that stays runs out the deadline as before. With no machine attached the
register-view poll remains.

Harness: test_wait_pc_is_exact waits 10 times in a row for one NOP in 1024
(a frame ends on it about once in a thousand); the previous binary misses
the first wait. The inject test, which the exact wait now stops on the
program's first instruction, settles 50 frames before its tap: keys down
in the 5-10 frames after MC START PROGRAM are not delivered (measured).
make e2e_test_slow runs the CI e2e suite pinned to the efficiency cores.

* fix(review): abortable run-to-address walks, honest AUTO header sniff, canonical Recent paths

Second review pass on the IPC contract batch.

1. A `wait pc` / `step to` in flight no longer holds process exit for its
   whole deadline. z80_run_until_ephemeral() takes an abort predicate, polled
   next to its deadline (and before the no-machine bail), and returns a new
   Z80RunUntilResult::Aborted; the IPC handlers pass the server's own
   stopping flag and map it to ERR 503 shutting-down, as the polling loop it
   replaced already did. `step over`'s CALL skip gets the same predicate.
   Covered by a unit test on the walk and a harness case that quits the
   emulator with a 60s wait outstanding.

2. `disk put` AUTO no longer takes a zero-prefixed binary for an already
   headered file. The AMSDOS checksum alone (bytes 0..66 against the word at
   67..68) is satisfied by 69 zero bytes, so a pen-0 screen, a zero-padded
   bank dump or a cleared-RAM save was written with NO header and LOAD read
   nothing. The shortcut now also wants a real file type and a length that
   fits the bytes after the header.

3. A user breakpoint AT the waited address is a landing, not a stop
   somewhere else: both `wait pc` and `step to` answer OK with the hit body
   when the consumed hit's PC is the target and it is not a watchpoint.

4. AGENTS.md's IPC table: the `load` row records the Recent-list side effect
   and its GUI/headless difference, `input chord` gets `input key`'s hold
   semantics, `wait pc` its new outcomes.

5. `step to` and `wait pc` now agree on polarity: a breakpoint or watchpoint
   that fires before the target is ERR 409 stopped-elsewhere for both, so a
   client testing "the reply starts with OK" cannot read an intervening stop
   as having reached the address. docs/ipc-protocol.md and the help text
   follow.

6. `disk put` ascii drops a leading UTF-8 BOM. The detector already called a
   BOM-prefixed listing ASCII; the writer copied the three bytes ahead of the
   line number, so BASIC ran the first line as a direct command and lost it.

7. Recent-list paths from IPC are canonicalised in ipc_mru_stage()
   (absolute + lexically normal, raw path on error), so a cwd-relative
   `load game.dsk` cannot persist an entry that opens nothing from another
   directory. All five call sites get it; closes beads-qm5z.

Also from the advisories: `disk put` refuses host files over 1 MiB before
reading them; a foreign pause that leaves the CPU standing on the waited
address ends `wait pc` with OK instead of running out the deadline; the
Stalled fallback is documented as the test-only path it is.

And the IPC device gates are re-seeded from the running machine's flags
before the emulation loop starts, not only by loadConfiguration() and the
first main-thread drain, so `input mouse` cannot answer ERR 409
no-mouse-device on a session launched with the device enabled (beads-0n59,
same class as beads-i834); a gtest covers the Symbiface half of that gate,
which had none.

* fix(test): stop UI-state tests leaking an open dialog into later suites

The coverage job's suite order broke IpcMru.EachEntryLandsOnItsOwnList and
IpcMru.StagedPathsAreAbsolute: the staged Recent entries never landed, and
both lists came back empty.

Root cause: imgui_state is a process-wide global that production code reads.
ipc_mru_apply_staged() applies nothing while imgui_state.show_options is set
— that is the guard which stops an IPC load from persisting the Settings
dialog's uncommitted edits. UIStateTest resets imgui_state in SetUp but never
in TearDown, so whichever of its tests ran last (MenuAndOptionsCanBothBeOpen,
ClosingMenuWithOptionsOpenStaysPaused, ClickingOptionsMenuItemOpensOptions —
each ends with show_options true) left a dialog flagged open for every suite
after it. In the default order those suites run after IpcMru; the coverage
build's order puts them before, so every apply became a silent no-op.

Reproduced locally at 6/10 shuffle seeds with
--gtest_filter='UIStateTest.MenuAndOptionsCanBothBeOpen:IpcMru.StagedPathsAreAbsolute'
--gtest_shuffle; 10/10 green after the fix, as is the whole suite under three
full-suite shuffle seeds.

- UIStateTest gets a TearDown that restores imgui_state, so the suite cannot
  leak the flag at all.
- The Recent-list tests move onto an IpcMruTest fixture that pins
  show_options, drains the stage queue and restores the lists, and
  IpcServerTest::SetUp clears the flag too: these tests now own the
  precondition they depend on instead of inheriting whatever ran before.

Also: test_conditional_debug_matrix ran every check against the 5.0s default
socket timeout while asking the server to wait 5000-6000ms, at the slowest
run tier. The client abandoned the connection before any of those budgets
could elapse, so a slow-but-correct hit and a breakpoint that never fires
were indistinguishable — which is how its last step reported "plain bp did
not fire" on a loaded runner. Raised to 20s so the budgets are observable and
a real miss is reported as one; the carry step's comment, which encoded the
old constraint, updated to match. 10/10 green headless.

* fix(test): make the run-to-address polarity check independent of where the machine drifted

test_run_to_address_breakpoint_polarity asserted that `step to 0x6300` would
be interrupted by a breakpoint armed at 0x6200. The injected program is 1024
NOPs at &6000 followed by JP &6000, so execution is a ring: a walk from PC
reaches the target by going forward and wrapping, and it crosses &6200 only
when the machine happens to sit behind it. Locally it always did; on a loaded
runner the machine drifts between IPC commands, the breakpoint fell behind the
walk, &6300 was reached without crossing it, and the check reported a
breakpoint that "never fired" when nothing had gone wrong.

Both halves of the premise are now stated instead of assumed:

- The target is the breakpoint's own successor (&6201). In a ring, &6200 is
  executed immediately before &6201 from ANY starting PC, so the intervening
  stop is reachable wherever the machine drifted to.
- The walk must not already stand on that target: run_until resumes into a
  fetch of the PC it is parked on, so a machine sitting at &6201 lands at once
  without going round. The test steps clear of it and verifies it did.

Reproduced with `taskpolicy -b`: 8/20 failures before, 2/20 with the target
fixed but the standing-on-target case still open, 0/20 with both. The other
two load-sensitive harness tests (test_conditional_debug_matrix,
test_wait_pc_is_exact) are 20/20 under the same load.

events.message:
feat(convert): IPF -> ADF is offered — an IPF could be read but not turned into a sector image; the gate refused the pair at any price (MF-1606, P3-707)

Owner request 2026-09-29: "activate IPF/CT-Raw support". Measured before:
the IPF plugin reads BOTH encoders down to sectors since MF-1373
(test_ipf_sektorebene), ipf is on T1 — but the round-trip matrix had no
IPF entry (MF-567 had removed the verdict because the dispatcher had no
converter), so the preflight gate refused IPF -> ADF as UNTESTED even
with accept_data_loss.

Red proof first: tests/test_ipf_nach_adf.c, rc=-40 before. Inputs from a
THIRD PARTY out of a deterministic UFT source: disk-analyse
(keirf/disk-utilities, Unlicense), CAPS encoder, every sector naming
itself.

- uftc_convert_ipf_to_adf(): places the sectors the IPF plugin delivers
  at ((C*2+H)*11+N)*512 — no second decoder (MF-1177); only sectors
  marked CHECKED without an error, missing or unavailable bit; the ADF is
  written only when all 1760 are there and none lies outside 0..10,
  as for HFE -> D81 (MF-1437). A protected disk is refused by count, not
  filled with zeros.
- dispatcher branch, internal declaration, round-trip matrix entry
  UFT_RT_LOSSY_DOCUMENTED (lost: cell timing, gap and weak-bit data, IPF
  metadata).

After: closed without consent; the free 4-cylinder file yields 88 of 88
sectors and is refused as incomplete, no file written; an 80-cylinder
version of the same source (local only — produced with the Windows
disk-analyse.exe from the clone, build provenance not recorded, hence
not in the free corpus) becomes an ADF byte-identical to the source,
0 of 901120 bytes differing.

Mutation matrix 3 of 5 red; two are equivalent on these inputs: placing
by list order instead of sector number (disk-analyse writes 0..10 in
order) and accepting bad sectors (no input has one).

K7 (offered conversion paths) 20 -> 21, matrix 22 -> 23, consent pairs
12 -> 13 — derived and checked by update_inventory.py; CLAUDE.md,
MASTER_PLAN and SUBSYSTEM_MATURITY follow.

Also BERICHTIGT: the IPF plugin's header still said CAPS-encoded IPFs
yield geometry only; that has not been true since MF-1373.

Named as open in P3-707: IPF -> IMG and IPF -> SCP still without a
converter; CT-Raw (same CAPS container family — CTEI/CTEX per capsimage and fluxfox; the plugin claims the
extensions) is NOT measured — it needs a CT-Raw file; the capsimg route
(helper process P3-190, reachable only through UFT_IPF_HELPER) waits on
an owner decision about capsimg's licence (upstream: non-commercial SPS
v1.02; P3-353 says Apache-2.0 for v5.21 — both cannot hold).

Numbering: MF-1606/P3-707 from this worktree's range.

Kennzahl: K7 (offered conversion paths), 20 -> 21.

As merged in #103, volamos's cycle counter was only reachable
indirectly: the guest itself had to call ReadEClock and report its own
elapsed time. That works for an instrumented benchmark like BenchWork,
but leaves an uninstrumented binary unmeasurable -- while `vamos -v` has
printed an equivalent "total cycles:" line for its own runs all along
(amitools/vamos/main.py, summing Musashi's per-call cycle returns).

Adds Runtime::emulated_cycles(), reporting the top-level run's count and
the rate it was counted at, and prints one line from it at exit when
--clock-mhz is active. Nothing is printed otherwise, because on the
default run_batch path no cycle count exists to print.

The line goes to stderr, so a harness parsing the guest's own stdout
never sees it, and is printed even when the run ends in an error -- a
benchmark that died part-way still burned the cycles it burned.

Cross-checked against vamos on the same binary: 340,020 cycles vs
vamos's 339,044 at 68000 (+0.3%), and 157,436 vs 155,855 at 68020
(+1.0%) -- two independent cycle models (the m68k crate's timing tables
vs Musashi's) agreeing closely.

refactor(cbm): nine sectors-per-track tables onto the one calculation — and the name meant three different things with two bases (MF-1532, P3-666)

Eight files, nine tables, 21 accesses now call
`uft_cbm_sectors_per_track()`, which has been the SSOT in
`src/formats/cbm/uft_cbm_geometry.c:153` all along and was already called by
16 files.

MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER:

  tables carrying the CBM zone pattern   17 -> 9
  K3 surplus copies                      97 -> 91
  audit_cbm_zonen.py sites               23 -> 14
  counting conventions there              9 -> 6
  build / ctest                          0 errors, 602/602

THE DECISIVE PRE-CHECK came before the first edit: every table agreed with
the SSOT, **0 divergences**, verified per track and per offset. Had one
diverged, that would have been a finding, not cleanup (MF-1177 sentence 1).
The witness already existed: `tests/test_cbm_geometry.c` holds the three
legacy shapes 43/41/40 against the SSOT and names the hazard itself — "same
numbers, shifted".

A FINDING THAT IS NOT CLEANUP: `d64_sectors_per_track` denoted **three
different things with two bases** — the function in `uft_d64_writer.c`, a
0-based table in `d64/uft_d64_parser_v3.c`, and a 1-based one in
`cbm/uft_cbm_formats.c` (`[t - 1]`). One quantity, three calculations: the
confusion whose divergence looks like a defect in the DATA. The reason now
stands in a comment at all three places.

THE LINKER NAMED ONE TARGET, MEASURED THERE WERE TWO. `test_gcr_tafeln` failed
with `undefined reference` because `uft_gcr_ops.c` no longer carries its own
table. Instead of patching the named target, the blast radius was measured
over `build.ninja`: `test_zellregel` would have failed next. Both entered,
then 0 unsupplied in BOTH measurements (ninja and the CMake text). Same class
as MF-1522, where the linker named one and nine were missing.

AND MY OWN SEARCH MISSED A TABLE THROUGH ITS OWN WINDOW.
`d71_sectors_per_track` in `cbm/uft_cbm_formats.c` has **70** entries — the
zone row twice — and my length window was 30 to 60. A pattern whose bounds
come from the known cases does not see the next one. Found by reading the
neighbouring lines, not by the measurement; rewired with it, and the reason
sits in the comment so the lesson stays attached to the find.

Two earlier versions of that search were wrong in the same family: the first
counted digits from COMMENTS (lengths 53 and 64 for a 35-track table), the
second took only top-level brace groups — and headers wrap everything in
`extern "C" { … }`, so three tables were silently missing. Fixed by reading
through `scripts/c_lex.py`, which exists for exactly this since MF-1171 and
which P3-679 had named as unused two hours earlier.

DELIBERATELY LEFT STANDING, 9 tables, each with its reason:

* three PUBLIC headers (`uft_bam_editor.h`, `uft_c64_protection.h`,
  `uft_cbm_gcr.h`) — rewiring would move an include dependency into the
  public interface. Own step, own draft.
* `src/flux/uft_flux_decoder.c::c64_sectors_per_track` — **zero accesses**,
  so it is dead. That would be a deletion, not a rewiring, and deleting code
  needs an owner decision (MF-1077). Untouched.
* `src/formats/xdf/uft_xdf_api_impl.c` — `import_d64()` is
  `__attribute__((unused))`, its body says "Would copy sector data here".
* four test expectations, among them the three `legacy_40/41/43` — those are
  the witness and must stay independent (MF-644).

Both baselines shortened so the progress stands in the diff, not in a figure.

AND THE COMMIT WAS REFUSED ON ITS FIRST ATTEMPT, over a line number.
`docs/selbsttest_baseline.txt` is keyed by LINE, and the comments added here
shifted the two guards from 1905/2037 to 1907/2038. `check_consistency`
reported four findings — two "block never compiled", two "baseline line is
gone" — all one cause. Numbers pulled forward, gate then `0 neu`.

I had warned the peer session about exactly this fragility earlier today.
Then it hit me. A warning one passes on and does not follow is a note, not an
insight. Registered in the balance as Fundus: the baseline should key on
`pfad:MAKRO`, not a line — the same shape MF-1506 chose for the constant
manifest, and for the same reason.

events.title: AHI, because MorphOS has no Paula
events.message:
AHI, because MorphOS has no Paula

amiga_audio.c was being linked into the MorphOS build to satisfy the
AmigaAudio_* symbols gta_audio.c calls, with a note admitting it was unlikely
to work. That was the wrong shape. It does not drive an audio API - it drives
the chipset: ADCMD_ALLOCATE over four hardware channels, one CMD_WRITE per
effect played by DMA, sample data that must be in Chip RAM "because Paula DMA
reads nothing else", and a period register counted in the PAL colour clock.
MorphOS carries an audio.device for compatibility, so linking it produced
something that might have made a noise and might have sat silent, on a system
whose actual sound API is AHI.

native/morphos_audio.c implements the whole amiga_audio.h contract over AHI's
low-level API, so gta_audio.c - the portable mixer the game talks to - is
unchanged. Same arrangement morphos_gfx.c has with amiga_gfx.c.

Most of the model carries across directly, because AHI's low-level API is a
close relative of Paula's: allocate audio, load sounds into slots, play a
sound on a channel, change its frequency and volume while it runs.

  period      -> freq = 3546895 / period, the PAL colour clock it divides.
                 The engine note's SetPeriod becomes AHI_SetFreq and revs.
  volume 0..64 -> AHI's Fixed, which is volume << 10; 64 lands on 0x10000
                 exactly, so full Paula volume is full AHI volume.
  Chip RAM    -> plain memory. AHI mixes in software; AllocSample is AllocVec.
  channels    -> 0,3 panned left and 1,2 right, mirroring how Paula is wired,
                 because gta_audio.c's channel allocator expects that layout.
  PlayLoop    -> AHIP_LoopSound, which is ioa_Cycles = 0 by another name.

One thing does not map: knowing a one-shot has FINISHED. audio.device replies
its IORequest and amiga_audio.c polls CheckIO; AHI's equivalent is an
end-of-sound Hook, and a Hook called from AHI on MorphOS must be a PPC/68k ABI
trampoline - exactly the kind of thing that cannot be got right without a
machine to try it on. So ChannelIdle works the duration out instead: bytes and
frequency give the length, amiga_uclock_us() gives the clock. Exact for a sound
that plays to its end, which is every sound the game starts, and it errs
towards "still busy" rather than cutting one off. Music's double buffer is
swapped on the same clock, which costs a seam of up to one frame between
chunks where Paula was gapless.

gta_audio.c had AHI wired as a reason to STAY SILENT - "AHI is a promise this
port has not kept yet", and not to fall back to Paula because "a machine where
AHI was chosen is usually one where Paula is not reachable at all (MorphOS)".
That paragraph names this machine. Under __MORPHOS__ the mapping inverts: AHI
is the only backend, so every setting but OFF opens it, PAULA included - a
drawer shared with an Amiga install will say Paula, and a player asking for
sound should get sound.

The 68k build is unaffected: with __MORPHOS__ undefined, gta_audio.c,
gta_main.c and gta_prefs.c preprocess byte-for-byte identically to v0.6.1.

NOT VERIFIED. This has never made a sound - there is no MorphOS machine on the
build host. It compiles, the calls are against the SDK's own prototypes and the
arithmetic is checkable by reading, but the first run is the test.

events.title: fix(ui): Disassembly step toolbar; Disc Tools refresh on swap; toasts on the focused viewport; Options button order and Cancel revert; native menu shortcuts (#62)
events.message:
fix(ui): Disassembly step toolbar; Disc Tools refresh on swap; toasts on the focused viewport; Options button order and Cancel revert; native menu shortcuts (#62)

* fix(ui): Disassembly step toolbar; Disc Tools refresh on swap; toasts on the focused viewport; Options button order and Cancel revert; native menu shortcuts

- Disassembly window menu bar gains In / Over / Out / Run-Pause (beads-4i4).
  dbg_step_in/over/out and the new dbg_run_pause_toggle are public and shared
  with the DevTools toolbar; debug_step_controls() decides for both when a
  step is allowed, and dbg_step_walk_poll_outcome() toasts a walk's result
  from whichever surface is on screen.
- Disc Tools re-lists Files when the drive gets a different medium
  (beads-p5t). dsk_media_generation() moves on dsk_eject, file_load and when
  the board applies a queued swap/eject; the pull path leaves it alone.
- Toasts draw on the focused viewport's foreground list, clamped into its
  work rect, falling back to the main viewport (beads-ar4).
- Options buttons in Mac order Cancel | Apply | Save, Save default-focused,
  with tooltips saying which one writes the config file (beads-3v8). Cancel
  now resizes the window back when the Scale was previewed (beads-ydkw).
- The native macOS menu is built after the InputMapper exists and refreshes
  each item's shortcut text as it opens, so F-key hints show on a normal
  launch (beads-bqx). Still text only, no key equivalents.

* fix(review): apply queued disk swaps before pulling; Cancel back to Fit; keep the Quit title

- subcycle_bridge_pull_drive_view applies a queued insert/eject first. A
  disk loaded while paused is only queued, so Disc Tools pulled the outgoing
  disc over the host view, and its next edit pushed that back and cancelled
  the queued swap. New board-level tests start the board on a synthetic ROM.
- Options Cancel back to Fit restores the window size recorded when the
  dialog opened; apply_scr_scale(0) has no size to compute, so the window
  kept the previewed size.
- validateMenuItem retitles only the items add_action_item built: AppKit's
  own Quit item is retargeted to KONCPC_EXIT and was renamed "Quit  (F10)".
- Toasts pick the focused viewport with a predicate instead of building a
  std::vector every frame; toast_pos returns only the position.
- Drop DebugStepControls::run_pause_resumes, which nothing read.

* fix(review): one source for the step tooltips; close the disc-swap listing race

Second review pass on this branch.

- Step-control tooltips (devtools_ui.cpp / imgui_ui.cpp): the three step
  tooltips were hand-written at both call sites and had already drifted on
  day one ("Step In: one instruction..." vs "Execute one instruction...").
  They now come from DebugStepControls, next to the labels that exist for
  exactly this reason, and a test asserts both surfaces get the same text.

- file_load (slotshandler.cpp): the medium-generation bump moved to after
  the queue write, next to subcycle_bridge_insert_media the way dsk_eject
  bumps next to subcycle_bridge_eject_media. Announced before the queue, a
  render-thread Disc Tools pull landing in the gap listed the outgoing disc
  and then recorded the new generation as the one it had listed, so a paused
  machine kept the stale listing until a manual Refresh.

- IPC `load` (koncepcja_ipc_server.cpp): the disk arm now holds a
  CpcPauseLease and restores the run state, like the .sna arm, so a
  server-thread load cannot interleave with the render thread's pull at all.

- Disc Tools (devtools_ui.cpp): the Files listing is keyed on the generation
  read AFTER the pull. The pull applies the swap queued while paused, which
  bumps the generation again, so keying on the pre-pull value made every
  swap re-list twice — two directory walks and two pause/resume cycles of a
  running machine for one disc.

- apply_pending_media rejected-swap branch: a test for the hot-swap the FDC
  refuses, where the drive is ejected and the generation must still move.

- Options Cancel: capture no window size while fullscreen, so Cancel with
  the old scale at Fit can no longer park the display size as the floating
  window size.

Tests: DebugStepControls.BothSurfacesGetTheSameTooltips,
LiveBoardMediaTest.ARejectedHotSwapStillMovesTheGeneration,
DevToolsRenderTest.DiscToolsRelistsOncePerSwapWithTheBoardRunning (the last
two verified red without their fix). 1823 tests green.

Blits: the shifted row's opaque middle in one post-increment loop

From the efficiency review. The middle groups of an unmasked shifted
blit went through blit_store4 once a group, reading and writing at
offsets and leaving the pointer bumps and the loop test to the C
around it. blit_store_run stores the whole run in one loop with both
pointers post-incrementing (the second word of each window is 6(a1)
once the first has gone with (a1)+) and hands the pointers back at
the right edge; blit_store4 had no other caller and is gone, its C
form now the new routine's twin.

is identical at every budget on ste and megaste.

events.title: A native MorphOS/PowerPC build of v0.6.1
events.message:
A native MorphOS/PowerPC build of v0.6.1

Forward-ported from the v0.0.3 branch, which is six releases behind. The
platform contract survived intact - amiga_gfx.h has not changed a line since
v0.0.3 - so native/morphos_gfx.c still implements it as written and the work
was in the build and in what moved around it.

The engine is unchanged. Every line of the rendering, physics, traffic, script,
font, text and data code compiles from the same sources the Amiga build uses.
That was already true and stayed true through five releases of new subsystems:
it is fixed point throughout with no floating point anywhere, and GTA's
little-endian files are read a byte at a time rather than by casting a struct
over them, because the same code has to build for the big-endian 68k and for
the host test harness.

What the six releases changed here:

  * TEN NEW ENGINE FILES - score, pickup, script, script_run, front, font,
    text, iff, audio, and v0.0.3's three - all portable, all compiled as they
    are. Writing the file list out rather than globbing is what turned each of
    them into a link error naming itself instead of a mystery.

  * THE SCREEN IS A SETTING, not a binary. v0.0.4 collapsed gta-aga,
    gta-rtg240 and gta-rtg480 into one AmiGTA and moved the size into
    gta.prefs. So the MorphOS port no longer forces 640x480 at compile time;
    it changes what AUTO means, in gta_prefs_screen_size() where that decision
    lives. AUTO here is 640x480 really rasterised - the doubled variant exists
    because a 68020 cannot draw four times the pixels at a playable rate, and
    that is a statement about that CPU. All four sizes stay selectable with
    `gtaprefs SCREEN=...`.

  * THE BINARY IS AmiGTA-morphos. It was gta-morphos when there were three
    gta-* binaries to sit beside; there is one AmiGTA now, so the name follows
    it. No .exe - nothing on MorphOS carries an executable extension.

  * PAULA AUDIO IS LINKED BUT NOT EXPECTED TO WORK. gta_audio.c is portable and
    is the mixer the game talks to, but it calls AmigaAudio_*, and
    amiga_audio.c drives audio.device's four hardware channels with sample data
    in Chip RAM. There is no Paula on PowerPC. It is compiled so the link
    completes and because it fails fast rather than blocking, so the worst case
    is silence; the right answer eventually is an AHI backend behind the same
    entry points, and gtaprefs already carries the setting. Untested either way.

  * gtaiff joins the drawer, since package.sh ships it.

Unchanged from the v0.0.3 port, and still the reasons this exists: the screen
is whatever depth the machine has (8-bit first, because the chunky buffer IS
the display format there and a blit becomes a memcpy; truecolour after, via
WriteLUTPixelArray), the granted size is read back and the picture centred in
it, the graphics setting is overruled to RTG because AGA and the Workbench
window backend live in amiga_gfx.c which this build does not compile, and the
frame cap sleeps on timer.device instead of spinning - a G4 would otherwise
pin a core at 100% for fifteen of every sixteen milliseconds and look hung
while running perfectly.

Building follows the repository's own convention: tools/bin/build_morphos.sh
beside build.sh, same shape - same root discovery, same compile helper, same
written-out file list, same refusal to strip. makefile.morphos adds only the
beta/release staging and archiving.

THE 68k BUILD IS UNAFFECTED, and it is checked rather than asserted: with
__MORPHOS__ undefined, gta_main.c, gta_prefs.c, gta_peds.c, gta_traffic.c,
gta_render.c and gta_script_run.c all preprocess byte-for-byte identically to
v0.6.1. In amiga_uclock.c, where the Amiga headers stop the host preprocessor,
stripping the __MORPHOS__ arms leaves a comment and a newline as the only
difference. That check exists because the bebbo toolchain is not installed on
this machine, so the Amiga build could not be compiled to prove it.

Not verified: this has not been run on MorphOS. It compiles clean - the only
warnings are pre-existing ones in upstream code - and the reasoning above is
from the code, not from a screen.

events.title: feat(trace): CPCT v0 bus-event tap and rig for the CPCień shadow twin (#61)
events.message:
feat(trace): CPCT v0 bus-event tap and rig for the CPCień shadow twin (#61)

* hw: cpct_tap -- a bus tap Device that records every qualified Z80 access as a CPCT v0 record, and cpct_tap_rig, a headless rig that boots a given lower ROM with the tap attached

The tap is bench equipment like the probe: it watches the committed bus each
master cycle and drives nothing. The rule (in cpct_tap.h, so another
implementation can apply the same one): an access begins on the master
cycle a qualified strobe first appears (fetch = m1&mreq&rd -> M1|MEM_RD,
mreq&rd -> MEM_RD, mreq&wr -> MEM_WR, iorq&rd&!m1 -> IO_RD, iorq&wr&!m1 ->
IO_WR; refresh and interrupt acknowledge are not accesses), its record
carries that cycle / 4 (T-states) and the address and data as last seen
while the strobe was active -- the byte consumed on a read, driven on a
write -- and is emitted when the strobe ends. cpct_tap_write() writes the
CPCT v0 file (~/src/cpc/cpcien/docs/trace-format.md).

sim/cpct_tap_rig.cpp (make cpct_tap_rig, no SDL) assembles GA + CRTC + PPI +
PSG + memory + Z80 + tap, loads --rom as the lower ROM, optionally presses
--key ROW,COLUMNS, runs --cycles master cycles and writes --out. First use:
the same 96-byte stub ROM as the CoPyCat standalone RTL bench -- 65,645
paired bus records, identical sequence, 0 data mismatches (the comparison
tooling and the report live in the copycat tree, sim/tap/).

* hw: cpct_tap -- record the T1-hold artefact in the cycle stamps (strobe starts up to 3 T later than hardware; measured against the CoPyCat RTL on the same program)

* sim: psg_oracle_rig -- the PSG Device driven by a scripted register program through the AY bus, generators dumped per PSG clock; cpct_tap_rig: --upper, --screen, --garegs, --capacity, repeatable --key

The rig assembles Gate Array + CRTC + PSG + a driver Device that latches
and writes registers with the PPI's four port-C phases (one microsecond
each) at scripted times, and writes one line per 1 MHz PSG clock: tone
mask, noise bit, envelope level, the three channel levels. It is the
konCePCja half of the CoPyCat PSG comparison (copycat sim/psg/compare.py),
which judges tone, noise, mixer/amplitude and envelope by class.

MEASURED with it (2026-09-05): tone A/B/C periods, the noise LFSR stream,
the mixer and the fixed amplitudes agree exactly with an AY implemented
from the GI datasheet. The envelope does not: this PSG steps its 32-level
envelope once per 256 x EP PSG clocks (psg.cpp envelope_step: a /256
prescaler and then the 16-bit period), so one 32-step cycle takes
8192 x EP clocks; the datasheet ("counting down the input clock by 256,
then by the 16-bit Envelope Period ... further counts down the envelope
frequency by 16, producing a 16-state cycle"; Fig. 3 "EP is the envelope
period, duration of one cycle") and jotego's jt49 (32 levels, one step per
8 x EP) both make one cycle 256 x EP clocks -- 32 x faster than here. The
levels visited are in the right order. Filed as an issue; not changed on
this branch.

* sim: cpct_tap_rig --expansion KB attaches a dk'tronics-style RAM expansion (the CoPyCat 576 KB comparison: 960 records identical)

* feat(trace): CPCT v0 line events, HALT flag and GAP record in the bus tap

The tap now emits everything the v0 spec defines, not just accesses:
/INT and /RESET falling edges as line-event records (held behind an open
access so the stream stays cycle-ordered), HALT on accesses made while
/HALT is low, a RESET record at cycle 0 on power-on, and a trailing GAP
record carrying the lost count when the buffer overflowed. The header and
record encoders are split out so the byte layout is testable, and
cpct_tap_write takes the CRTC type and checks every write and the close.

Tests cover the layout byte for byte, the recording rule on hand-driven
bus cycles, overflow, and a real board running a small ROM (fetch flags,
I/O and memory writes, steady 13312 T /INT spacing, HALT).

* feat(sim): cpct_tap_rig --dump-frames writes the per-frame framebuffer oracle

With --dump-frames DIR the rig attaches the video Device and writes its
framebuffer as DIR/frame_NNNNN.ppm at every completed frame, the
reference CPCień's shadow video is checked against. The video Device only
listens, so the trace is byte-identical with or without it. The rig
checks its output writes; both rigs are ignored by git and removed by
make clean. Neither is part of the default build.

* docs: CPCT bus tap, what it records and how to run the rig

* fix(review): CPCT tap edge ordering, pending markers on write, rig exit status and argument checks

From the code review of #61:
- tap: an /INT or /RESET edge on the master cycle an access opens now
  follows that access's record, as the rule says (it came first before).
- tap: cpct_tap_write writes line events still queued behind an open
  access instead of dropping them; past the capacity they count as lost.
- tap: cpct_tap_destroy() runs the state's destructor (it owns the record
  buffer); the tests and the rig call it.
- tap/docs: record that this Z80 runs no bus cycles while halted, so HALT
  is only ever on line events, unlike a hardware capture.
- rig: numeric options are parsed strictly and range-checked (exit 2);
  exit 3 when records were dropped or no access was recorded; capacity is
  set before the board reset so it bounds the RESET record too; header
  comment points at the docs' option table.
- psg_oracle_rig: dump write and close failures exit 1.

Tests: /RESET edges, first-cycle edge ordering, the pending-slot merge,
reset after activity, GAP saturation, exact file size without loss, write
failure, pending markers in the written file; the board test now pins
HALT to line events.

* fix(review): GAP record cycle, no partial traces, one tap owner, stricter rigs

Second review pass on the CPCT bus tap and its two sim rigs.

#1 One RAII owner: CpctTapOwner now lives in src/hw/cpct_tap.h (behind
   __cplusplus), replacing the three hand-rolled guards in the rig and the
   tests. A future live-capture hook declares one instead of pasting a fourth.

#4/#5 sim/rig_args.h holds parse_u64 and bad_arg for both rigs.
   psg_oracle_rig's --us went from std::atol (which turns "20k" into 0, runs
   nothing and exits 0) to the strict parser, and its counters are
   unsigned long long so us * 16 cannot overflow a 32-bit long on Windows.
   A script line that is neither blank, a # comment, nor "t_us reg val" with
   a register 0-15 is now fatal instead of silently dropped, and an empty
   dump exits 3 the way cpct_tap_rig's "no access recorded" does.
   test/rig_args_test.cpp covers the parser.

#6 The GAP record carries the cycle of the first dropped record — the spec's
   "first cycle after the gap" — not the tap's cycle at write time, which in
   a long capture is millions of T-states later. The old test could not tell
   the two apart (16 master cycles between drop and write); it now asserts
   the drop-start cycle, and a new test advances 10000 T-states in between.

#7 A failed write removes the file it was writing. CPCT v0 has no record
   count or trailer, so a truncated trace parses as a shorter valid capture.
   Tested with RLIMIT_FSIZE (skipped on Windows).

#2 cpct_tap_rig refuses a --dump-frames directory that already holds
   frame_*.ppm: frame numbers restart each run, so a shorter second run would
   leave the tail of the first behind and a consumer would glob two captures.

#3 --out is probed before the board is built, so an unwritable path fails in
   a second instead of after minutes of simulation.

#8 The --garegs dump tracks both fprintf return values into the fclose check,
   as write_ppm and the --screen dump already do.

Also, from the advisory list: a 32 KB --rom is split between the two ROM
sockets instead of booting without BASIC; --expansion must be whole 64 KB
banks; a failed frame dump still writes the trace before returning 1; a
bad_alloc during the run is reported as "lower --capacity" instead of
terminating; and docs/cpct-tap.md records the leading RESET record, both
capacity defaults, the GAP cycle rule, and that Device.reset discards the
capture.

events.title: Simplify: one long type for plane memory, and the branch's duplicates
events.message:
Simplify: one long type for plane memory, and the branch's duplicates

From a four-way review of this branch (reuse, simplification,
efficiency, altitude). Where the target code was meant to stay the
same, it is checked against a disassembly taken before: blit.o,
blitter.o, sprite.o, blit8.o, tileset.o and hwscroll.o are
instruction for instruction what they were.

- stdl_wlong (stdl_internal.h): a long in plane memory, at an even
  address that need not be a multiple of four. It is uint32_t on the
  target, whose ABI aligns that to two already, and on the host it
  tells the alignment sanitizer the 68000's rule. It replaces four
  different treatments: plain uint32_t casts, stdl_ld32/stdl_st32,
  a word-at-a-time host twin in blit8.c (whose pattern table is now
  built in memory order so one form is right on both), and wrong
  comments claiming a long move at a word address faults. The
  long-alignment tests inside STDL_BlitSurfaceEx stay, now said to
  be for its register allocation rather than safety.
- draw.c: one pair of colour-to-plane-pair macros instead of seven
  copies; xor_row loses a flag that was always 1; the XOR mask rows
  go through span_mask_row and the three mask-column loops through
  one helper; XorPixel XORs two plane pairs like PutPixel merges
  them; PointsC drops a long-alignment test it never needed (1.3%
  faster), while STDL_Points keeps its own because without it the
  function compiled 0.8% slower.
- DrawText's row address is a mulu.w: its last __mulsi3.
- blitter.c uses the shared names (no local aliases, stdl_mul16 for
  its private muls.w copy); stdl_blit_pass loses a hop argument
  every caller set to the same value; hwscroll.c uses the shared
  video-counter defines; dirty.c loses duplicated state resets.
- tests/host/Makefile: one pattern rule for every suite, and every
  header - including tests/host's own and src's other headers -
  now a prerequisite.

Pixel-path text 34412 -> 34288 bytes. Plain ST (Hatari --machine
st, floor 0.3%): PRIMCOST unchanged within 0.4% except XorRect 0.94,
XorHLine 0.98 and PointsC 0.99.

A new host test draws every primitive on a word-aligned borrowed
surface and on a library one and compares them byte for byte; with
the type's alignment set back to four the sanitizer stops it, so it
reaches those accesses. PIXCHK, which runs it on the machine,
passes on st; I8CHK passes on st.

events.title: fix(serial): TCP connect resolution and I/O error checks; loadConfiguration stops writing globals; bounded quiescence waits; flux size-mismatch test (#64)
events.message:
fix(serial): TCP connect resolution and I/O error checks; loadConfiguration stops writing globals; bounded quiescence waits; flux size-mismatch test (#64)

* fix(serial): resolve the TCP connect before reporting connected; report failed sends

TcpSocketBackend::open() set connected_ the moment a non-blocking connect()
returned EINPROGRESS, so a refused or slow connect read as "Connected" and
every byte sent afterwards vanished. The backend now tracks a Connecting
state and resolves it with poll()/select() plus SO_ERROR: a short bounded
wait in open(), then lazily from has_data()/send()/connected(). A send()
that fails for anything but a full buffer, and a recv() of 0 or a reset,
drop the connection instead of leaving a dead line marked live. Host lookup
moves from gethostbyname() to getaddrinfo(); send() no longer raises SIGPIPE.

SerialBackend::send() now returns whether the byte was delivered, and
FileBackend::send() checks fputc/fflush and logs a failing output file once
(beads-5os).

Tests run against a real localhost listener on an ephemeral port and a
closed one; the file-backend failure uses a scoped RLIMIT_FSIZE so the
disk-full case runs on macOS too.

Refs: beads-1af

* fix(plotter): SVG export reports write errors instead of claiming success

plotter_export_svg_segments() returned true whenever fopen() succeeded, so a
full disk left a truncated SVG behind an "exported SVG" log line. It now
checks the stream's error flag and the fclose() result and returns false,
which IPC 'plotter export' already turns into ERR 500 export-failed and the
UI into an error toast.

Refs: beads-5os

* fix(config): loadConfiguration fills CPC.devices instead of switching device globals

loadConfiguration() wrote eight process-global device settings as a side
effect (g_silicon_disc, g_amdrum, g_drive_sounds disk/tape, g_smartwatch,
g_amx_mouse, g_symbiface, and the serial backend, which it also opened).
Every one is read with a default, so any test that loaded a config turned
all eight on or off for the tests after it; under --gtest_shuffle that
already broke RamExpansionTest once.

The settings now land in a t_DeviceConfig on t_CPC. apply_device_config()
makes them live (startup calls it right after loading) and
capture_device_config() reads the live devices back; the save paths call it
first, so a device toggled at runtime is still persisted.
saveConfiguration() writes CPC.devices, keeping the load/save round-trip
test meaningful. The one-off g_silicon_disc save/restore in the
configuration test fixture is gone; a new test loads a config enabling all
eight and checks every global is unchanged.

Refs: beads-ab4j

* test(flux): a size-mismatched host push must not drop the SCP backing

Locks in the push guard from 13db3b7c. With a writable flux disc in drive A
(synthetic SCP, DSK overlay synthesized on attach), a host disc of a
different size must be refused by subcycle_bridge_push_drive_view(), leaving
the same SCP and overlay attached; before the guard the push fell through
to insert_disk(), which replaced the medium and dropped the flux. A
same-size edit still lands in the overlay with the SCP kept.

The fixture starts the real bridge from rom/ and stops it in TearDown, with
drive A's file cleared so the stop has nothing to write back.

Refs: beads-csl7.4

* fix(core): bound the pause-lease wait for the Z80 thread and fail closed

CpcPauseLease and cpc_pause_and_wait() waited for g_z80_idle with no bound,
so a Z80 thread stuck in a frame hung whichever thread held the lease -- the
IPC server (one connection at a time) or the UI -- forever.

cpc_wait_until_idle() now always has a bound, defaulting to
kCpcIdleTimeoutMs (5 s). A lease whose wait times out stays held but
reports idle() == false, logs why, and every holder checks it and backs off
without touching machine state, restoring the run state it found:

- IPC: reset, snapshot save/load, .sna load, disk format/status/save/eject
  and the disk mutation helper, profile load and session playback answer
  ERR 504 z80-not-idle (documented in docs/ipc-protocol.md).
- emulator_reset(), fullscreen toggle, the video-plugin reinit and the
  Step Over, Eject and Disc Tools paths skip the work and say so.
- koncpc_rebuild_machine() returns the new ERR_Z80_NOT_IDLE.
- Shutdown logs the stuck thread and still joins it: freeing the machine
  under a running frame would crash.

Tests: a lease with a 50 ms bound against a stuck thread returns promptly,
not idle, and restore_run_state() hands the machine back running; an IPC
reset against a stuck thread answers ERR 504 within the default bound and
does not reset.

Refs: beads-csl7.5

* fix(review): one z80-not-idle answer, fast stuck-thread tests, rebuild refusal and save-path fixes

Applies the ce-code-review findings on this branch.

Pause lease / quiescence
- Every IPC lease holder now answers ERR 409 z80-not-idle, the code `step`
  already used, with the same debug-context trailer; `step` goes through the
  same helper and restores the caller's run state too. The 504 variant is
  gone. `config apply` / `profile load` map a refused rebuild to the same
  answer instead of "ERR 500 rebuild-failed code=46".
- The bound is injectable (cpc_set_idle_timeout_ms, default 5 s), so the
  fail-closed tests prove the cap in tens of ms instead of burning 5 s.
- After one timeout, later waits give up after 250 ms until the thread is
  seen idle again: a stuck thread no longer freezes the UI 5 s per click.
- Options Apply/Save no longer reopens the serial backend after a refused
  rebuild (the old backend is still wired into the live machine); the
  Options and SD-folder toasts say "Z80 thread is not responding" instead of
  blaming the ROM paths.
- bin_load() returns a BinLoadResult and copies RAM under the lease; IPC
  `load x.bin` reports z80-not-idle and ERR 500 load-bin instead of OK. A
  missing RAM-size bound that underflowed into a huge allocation is guarded.
- UI holders share imgui_lease_ready(); cpc_pause_and_wait() (no callers)
  is deleted; the ERR_Z80_NOT_IDLE comment and wait() log no longer claim
  the machine is left paused.

Config
- koncpc_save_live_configuration() is the one runtime save (capture, then
  serialize); saveConfiguration() stays the pure serializer for tests.
- capture_device_config() keeps the configured IDE image paths while the
  Symbiface is off, instead of erasing them on the next save.
- SerialConfig moves to serial_config.h, so koncepcja.h no longer pulls in
  the whole serial interface.

Serial
- CPC-transmitted bytes go through SerialInterface::host_tx(), which counts
  undelivered ones; `serial status` reports tx_dropped= and
  backend_connected=. The machine's host_tx context is now the long-lived
  interface, not a backend a config apply may delete.
- TcpSocketBackend::status() resolves a pending connect; FileBackend resets
  its log-once flag on reopen.

Tests
- Table-driven: every lease-taking IPC command against a stuck thread
  (reset, snapshot save/load, .sna/.bin load, disk format/status/save/eject/
  ls, profile load, step) answers 409, writes nothing, leaves the machine
  running. Plus the fast-fail latch, rebuild refusal, load-bin errors,
  apply/capture round trip over every device, IDE path capture, tx_dropped.
- FluxPushGuardTest also isolates drive B, M4, Silicon Disc and Symbiface.

* fix(review): bound the DNS lookup, and stop two saves from losing user settings

Second review pass on this branch.

- Serial TCP open() bounded its connect() but not getaddrinfo(), the one
  blocking call left with no deadline. A stale or unreachable resolver froze
  the whole GUI at startup and on `config apply`, and the entire IPC surface
  on `serial config set`. The lookup now runs on a worker thread behind
  run_with_deadline() (src/bounded_deadline.h): open() gives up after
  kResolveWaitMs and stays Disconnected, and a lookup that answers too late
  frees its own result. Unit-tested with an injected resolver, since a
  slow-resolving hostname is not something a test can arrange.

- "Save without restart" for a serial edit was undone by the next write-back:
  every runtime save captures the live serial config, so the MRU push on the
  next file open (or clean exit) wrote the old values back over the deliberate
  save. The serial settings now join printer/scr_window in the intent
  snapshot, written through the save override.

- capture_device_config() erased a configured IDE image path whenever the
  Symbiface was on but the image was not mounted — a failed attach detaches
  first and leaves the live path empty, and the runtime toggle never attaches
  at all. The copy is now gated on each device's `present` flag, which is set
  only after the image really opened, so a run with the volume unavailable
  keeps ide_master=/ide_slave= in the file.

- The StuckZ80Thread test helper left CPC.paused true after every use: its
  clear-lease called release(), which never resumes. Moved to
  test/stuck_z80_thread.h with restore_run_state(), so the machine goes back
  exactly as the helper found it and no shuffled test inherits a paused one.

- imgui_lease_ready(), the fail-closed guard in front of every destructive UI
  action (video shutdown, eject, format, disc-tools pull/push), had no test at
  all. Covered headlessly on both paths: idle lets the work through silently,
  a stuck Z80 thread skips it, restores the run state and toasts.

Also: FileBackend::close() reports a failing fclose (a full disk loses the
buffered bytes there and nowhere else says so); resolve_connect() settles the
state with a compare-exchange, as two threads can resolve the same socket;
ScopedFileSizeLimit clears the stream badbit a LOG_ line inside its scope can
leave behind; test/configuration.cpp reuses DeviceGlobals instead of its own
local snapshot struct.

events.message:
refactor(gate): Tor 72 is a LOCAL PRE-CHECK, not a binding gate — owner decision, plus honest retro-records for what it missed (P3-680, MF-1531)

The owner named a contradiction I had built myself: **P3-680 and "binding
gate" cannot both hold.** A gate that COUNTS as binding and binds only one
side is not a P3, it is at least a P1. Decision of 2026-09-29: Tor 72 is a
local pre-check against the known state.

WHAT CHANGED IN STATUS, at four places — script header, hook comment, CI
category (now "MF-Nummer: Vorpruefung intakt"), and CLAUDE.md with the
division-of-labour table. The header said "a MF number belongs to exactly one
commit"; measured, the hook binds only the side that passes through it. The
right reading of a green run is now written where the claim used to be:

    "my numbers do not collide with the KNOWN ones"
    — not "numbers do not collide".

WHY, MEASURED: the operational probe counts **3 of 6** commits since the
logbook began with no entry — `97b2888a` (MF-1601), `cc204479` (MF-1602),
`16880094` (MF-1603), all from the worktree `wt-dtc`. The obvious causes are
excluded: `core.hooksPath` points at the same file in both worktrees, the file
exists and calls the script, the reflog says `commit:`, and since MF-1530 even
the hook's bash writes its own line when it finds no Python. None of those
lines is missing. `--no-verify` or plumbing remain; **which, is NOT measured**.

RETRO-RECORDS, in the owner's field set and in a SEPARATE file beside the
logbook (`uft-tor72-nachpruefung.log`, `--nachpruefen`):

    status: nachgeprueft
    commit: 97b2888a
    claim: MF-1601
    urspruenglicher-hook-nachweis: fehlt
    ursache: nicht-gemessen
    nachpruefung: bestanden
    nachpruefung-zeitpunkt: 2026-09-29T11:53:18Z

Three records, all passing — and the check is real, not a stamp: it asks the
same question as the hook, and a mutation that turns it into a stamp drops the
self-test to 43/45.

THE COUNTER-DIRECTION IS THE POINT: `--betrieb` still lists those commits as
"ohne Vermerk" and names the retro-check separately. A mutation that counts a
retro-record as a hook run fails. A backfilled entry in the LOGBOOK would fake
a historical certainty that does not exist, so it does not happen.

Self-test 35 -> **45**, mutation matrix **6 of 6** for the new clamps (14 of 14
together with MF-1528/1530). And `ohne_vermerk()` is now the ONE calculation
that both the probe and the retro-check use — computed twice it drifts
(MF-1177).

A SELF-TEST CASE WAS FLAKY TO THE SECOND. "mit Vermerk: 1 Commit betrachtet, 0
ohne" was red once and green once, because the test wrote the entry AFTER the
commit while the real hook runs BEFORE it — so the commit time is never below
the entry time. At equal seconds green, otherwise red. Order reversed, 45/45
three times running, and the comment now says why the order is what it is.

NOT BUILT, and it cannot be from here: the server-side check and the merge
serialisation need repository administration and a push, neither of which this
session has. They stand in P3-680 with all ten acceptance criteria, the three
serialisation options, and the exception path with its eight mandatory fields.
A CI check alone does NOT suffice — two branches can claim the same number and
both go green against the same old target state.

The owner's condition for MF-1530 is met: that Tor 72 is provisionally only a
local pre-check is now stated in the tree. Nothing is pushed.

events.title: Peek slot ROM without reading the card
events.message:
Peek slot ROM without reading the card

While a watchpoint is armed, MMU::read peeks every address first so the
callback has a value, and MMU::peek called the card's readROM. A
SmartPort's entry points are traps that run a whole block call, so every
call ran twice and a //e booting a SmartPort image with any watchpoint
set, even one that never fired, landed at a BRK in the monitor. Reported
booting Total Replay (4cade.hdv) with write watchpoints on $C000 and
$F001. peek now asks for peekROM, as the IIgs's already did.

test_mmu_slots.cpp pins that a peek never reads a card, and
test_emulator_disk.cpp boots ProDOS from a SmartPort with a watchpoint
armed and resumed after each stop. Both fail without the fix.

events.title: fix(host): programmatic quits never raise the unsaved-disk dialog (#65)
events.message:
fix(host): programmatic quits never raise the unsaved-disk dialog (#65)

* fix(host): programmatic quits never raise the unsaved-disk dialog

IPC `quit` and every off-main-thread exit pass askIfUnsaved=false, but
the flag was dropped on the hop through SDL_EVENT_QUIT: the main-thread
handler re-called cleanExit() with the default and asked again. SDL's
own SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers fed the same event, so a harness that
terminated the emulator after dirtying a disk popped the native
"unsaved changes" dialog onto the maintainer's desktop.

Carry the flag across the hop, own the termination signals (polled
once per frame in both GUI and headless loops; no SDL handler), and
add KONCPC_NO_DIALOGS=1, which suppresses the dialog on every path.
The IPC harness sets it. The decision is koncpc_quit_should_prompt()
in quit_policy.h, unit-tested.

* fix(review): headless IPC quit exits; scripted KONCPC_EXIT never asks; signals exit 128+signo

Review follow-ups on the programmatic-quit change:

- IPC `quit` in headless mode answered OK and never exited: the off-main
  cleanExit() pushed an SDL_EVENT_QUIT that headless never polls. The
  request now goes through a QuitMailbox (code + ask flag) that the GUI
  takes from SDL_EVENT_QUIT and headless takes at the loop top. Taking
  empties it, so a QUIT SDL raises on its own no longer replays a stale
  code.
- `-a KONCPC_EXIT` replays on the Z80 thread and still raised the
  unsaved-disk dialog. KONCPC_EXIT now asks only on the main thread (F10,
  the menus, the native Quit item).
- SIGTERM/SIGINT exited 0; they now exit 128+signo and skip the settings
  save a clean exit performs. A second signal restores the default action
  and re-raises, so a wedged shutdown can still be killed. The flag is a
  lock-free std::atomic<int>, and render_one_frame's frame wait bails on it.
- Tests: QuitMailbox hop, KONCPC_EXIT thread policy, signal exit codes;
  ipc_harness test_programmatic_quit_exit_codes (headless `quit 3` -> 3,
  SIGTERM -> 143).

* fix(review): atomic quit mailbox, double-signal and SIGINT coverage

Second review pass on the programmatic-quit work.

QuitMailbox can tear when two threads post concurrently (#2): post()
wrote code, ask and pending as three separate atomics, so two quits
landing at the same instant (IPC `quit 5` while an --exit-after deadline
fires on the Z80 thread) could have the main thread read one poster's
code beside the other's ask flag. The request now lives in one
std::atomic<uint32_t> — pending in bit 31, ask_if_unsaved in bit 30, the
exit code in the low 8 bits — so a post() is observed as a unit. Eight
bits is the whole exit status a process can report, so `quit -1` reports
255 and `quit 256` reports 0, the same values the shell would have seen;
docs/ipc-protocol.md says so. QuitMailbox.PostIsObservedAsAWholeRequest
races two posters against 200k takes and sees a torn pairing on the old
code within a few hundred takes; ExitCodesRoundTripThroughTheLowByte
pins the packing for negative and out-of-range codes.

Double-signal force-kill branch was untested (#1):
test_double_signal_terminates sends SIGTERM twice back to back and
asserts the process is gone inside 5s — either force-killed by the
second signal through the restored default disposition (-15, what it
does here) or, if the main loop drained the first one in between, the
ordinary 143. Either way the operator's second Ctrl+C is not a no-op
waiting on the harness's own SIGKILL fallback.

test_programmatic_quit_exit_codes also grows the SIGINT (130) leg and
checks the runner's pinned temp config is byte-identical after a
signalled exit: a kill is not a clean exit and must not write settings.

Declined window close asked twice: after cleanExit(0) returns because
the user answered "don't quit", SDL follows the close request with a
QUIT of its own, which the SDL_EVENT_QUIT branch reads as a fresh
gesture and re-raises the dialog. SDL_FlushEvent drops it. Not testable
headlessly — it needs a real window and a modal.

KONCPC_NO_DIALOGS=false/no/off (any case) now means off rather than
suppressed, next to the existing 0; QuitPolicy.EnvVariableParsing covers
the spellings and that "offline" is not one of them.

test_runner 1803 passed / 5 skipped; ipc_harness 40 passed, 0 failed.

events.title: fix(gate): the hook's bash writes its own logbook line, so "no entry" means one thing — and the probe's first real finding is that Tor 72 binds only one side (P3-680, MF-1530)
events.message:
fix(gate): the hook's bash writes its own logbook line, so "no entry" means one thing — and the probe's first real finding is that Tor 72 binds only one side (P3-680, MF-1530)

The operational probe from MF-1528 was two hours old when it delivered:

  Laufbuch seit 09:09:57Z, 107 Vermerke
  Commits mit Anspruch seither: 4, davon ohne Vermerk: 2
     ohne Vermerk: 97b2888a  MF-1601
     ohne Vermerk: cc204479  MF-1602

Both are HEAD of the worktree `C:/Users/Axel/wt-dtc`; my own two
(`0d50177e`, `04b8a400`) each carry an entry. **Tor 72 binds only one side.**
Registered as P3-680.

The probe's arithmetic is verifiably right: the day's two other foreign
commits (10:17 and 11:00 local) lie BEFORE the logbook and are correctly
excluded — exactly the case `utc()` was built for after the date-only compare
would have missed it.

THE OBVIOUS CAUSES ARE EXCLUDED, not assumed. `core.hooksPath` returns the
same path in BOTH worktrees, the file there exists and calls
`audit_mf_nummer.py` (3 mentions), and the reflog says `commit:` — no rebase
or cherry-pick, where `commit-msg` would not run anyway. What remains is
`--no-verify` or git plumbing; **which of them is NOT measured**, and that gap
is not filled with a plausible story (the same restraint MF-1171 shows for
`repo_scope`).

WHAT THIS COMMIT FIXES is the probe's own ambiguity. "No entry" had three
causes and the probe could not tell them apart:

  1 the hook did not run (--no-verify, plumbing)
  2 the hook ran, found no Python -> notice, exit 0, NO entry
  3 the script ran, the append failed -> False, NO entry

The hook's BASH now writes its own line in the two cases it owns, each

cannot locate the logbook. My first probe of the no-Python branch used

events.title: Queue frames so every one the machine makes is shown
events.message:
Queue frames so every one the machine makes is shown

Frames are published to audio's timing, not the display's, and one that
landed just after another between two refreshes was drawn over: 60 went
out a second and about 53 were shown. The shared framebuffer is now a
queue of four slots run by two counters, frames written and frames shown,
each with one writer. A refresh takes the oldest unshown frame, and the
newest past a backlog of two, so frames that arrive together are shown on
successive refreshes. At most two wait, which keeps the Worker out of the
slot the renderer holds. The postMessage fallback queues by the same rule.

Measured: 60 published and 60 shown on the //e, the IIgs and the
fallback. frame-queue.test.js pins the rules, including a randomised run
that the Worker never writes into the held slot.

events.title: XOR: a plane pair a long
events.message:
XOR: a plane pair a long

The XOR primitives tested the colour's four bits for every group and
XORed a word at a time. They XOR a plane pair a long now, g ^= colour
& mask, the colour as two longs with 0xFFFF in each half whose plane
bit is set - a clear plane XORs with zero, the identity, so the plane
budget is still respected. Rows (XorRect, XorHLine, XorHSpans) always
do both pairs; the column loop (XorVSpans) keeps a second
instantiation for colour 3 with the colour a constant, the special
case it had before, because given the colour as a variable gcc
spilled the bit and the stride around the loop (+4-6%). XorVLine is
now one span through XorVSpans, which carries its column loops once.

docs(open-items): the last deciding gate with no test — three measured parser gaps, all latent today, so registered and NOT built (P3-679, MF-1529)

MF-1528 measured that `audit_plugin_compliance.py` is the only one of 77 gate
scripts that makes a decision and is tested nowhere (69 are tested, 10 only
report). The announced next step was "give it the bench signature".

THAT PLAN DID NOT HOLD, and the measurement said so before a line was
written. The bench `audit_selbsttest.py` plants a tree with a KNOWN answer per
tool and calls `check(pflanzung)`. This script has no `check()`, and its
decision is BASELINE-relative (`--min-pass`), not per-case — a planted tree
with one plugin answers that only with explicit thresholds. Measurement before
plan, and the plan lost.

THREE PARSER GAPS, each reproduced on planted sources.
`extract_plugin_body()` counts braces over RAW C text:

* a brace in a string literal (`.name = "B { mit Klammer"`) never lets the
  depth return to 0 — the plugin is **not found at all**, silently skipped. A
  skipped plugin can be arbitrarily incomplete without ever being counted.
* a brace in a comment (`/* Vorsicht: } */`) ends the body early —
  `spec_status` becomes `UFT_SPEC_UNKNOWN` and a compliant plugin is reported
  as non-compliant. A false FAIL.
* `.features = &x` does not match `(\w+)` — another false FAIL.

AND ALL THREE ARE LATENT TODAY. Over `git ls-files` under `src/formats/`:
**89** definitions in the text, **89** read by the parser; `.features` with a
value that is not a bare word: **0**. The parser is right by luck, not by
construction.

SO NOTHING IS BUILT. Per MF-640 the finding moves none of K0–K9, which makes
it Fundus and not a task: registered as P3-679 with what would open it — the
first plugin name or description text carrying a brace, or the first
`.features` value that is not a bare word. Both are ordinary changes nobody
would recognise as risky. And `scripts/c_lex.py` can already skip strings and
comments; it is simply not used here.

The class is this tree's most frequent one: a pattern over raw text assuming a
structure the tree only MOSTLY has. MF-1522 counts five cases in one day,
MF-1528 two more, and this is the seventh and eighth of the same day.

events.title: feat(gate): Tor 72 keeps a logbook, so "did not fire" is distinguishable from "did not run" — and its own self-test was green only OUTSIDE a hook (MF-1528)
events.message:
feat(gate): Tor 72 keeps a logbook, so "did not fire" is distinguishable from "did not run" — and its own self-test was green only OUTSIDE a hook (MF-1528)

MEASURED FIRST, and the measurement said no. Why `e36346ce` passed Tor 72 is
**not decidable in retrospect**: across **754** session protocol files in the
window 05:50–06:50Z there is **not one** `git commit` call from a foreign
session, although the commit exists. Whatever path created it leaves no trace
in `~/.claude/projects`.

That also lands on Tor 71: its operational probe (`--protokolle`) reads those
same protocols, so it is **blind to anything not coming from a protocolled
session** — "0 violations" there means "0 among the calls it saw". Its
description now says so.

So this probe measures FORWARD. Every run appends one line to
`$GIT_COMMON_DIR/uft-tor72-laeufe.log` (time, claimed number, verdict, HEAD),
and `--betrieb` counts which commit since the first entry has **no** entry.
"The hook did not run" is thereby distinguishable from "the hook found
nothing" — confusing those two was the whole finding. First run: logbook since
09:09:57Z, 0 commits without an entry.

Common, not per-worktree (`--git-common-dir`): the question is whether the
hook ran for THIS COMMIT, and commits of all worktrees sit in one object
store — exactly the situation that produced the collision.

Named limits: the logbook lives in `.git`, so per-clone and unversioned, like
the hook. It says nothing about commits before it existed, nor about another
clone. CI cannot check it; `check()` checks the classifier and the call in the
hook template. A failing append never costs a commit.

Self-test 18 -> **35**, mutation matrix **8 of 8**, every mutation now
reporting a red CASE instead of crashing the run.

THIS COMMIT WAS REFUSED ON ITS FIRST ATTEMPT, by `check_consistency.py`, and
the cause was a rule this tree documents itself. The case "a worktree could be
created" was red inside the hook (34/35) and green when called directly
(35/35). Per MF-1282 and `scripts/git_env.py`: **git exports `GIT_DIR` into
every hook, and `cwd=` does not override it.** `git init` got
`env=git_umgebung()`, the five following calls did not — so they ran against
the SURROUNDING repository. A test that is green only outside a hook does not
test the tool, it tests the environment.

AND BEHIND IT SAT A MORE DANGEROUS ONE, shown only by running rather than
reading. `laufbuch()` asks git itself, so under a set `GIT_DIR`,
`laufbuch(<throwaway repo>)` returned the path of the **REAL** logbook — and
the case "logbook is a DIRECTORY" would then have placed a directory over the
real file and destroyed it for good. `laufbuch()`, `lauf_vermerken()` and
`betrieb()` now take an optional `umgebung`: in production it stays None
(there `GIT_DIR` SHOULD be inherited, that is how `--git-common-dir` finds the
common location for a worktree commit), in the self-test it is
`git_umgebung()`. Proven in THREE environments — without `GIT_DIR`, with
`GIT_DIR=.git`, and with `GIT_DIR` pointing at a worktree — 35/35 each.

FIVE MORE ERRORS WHILE BUILDING, three caught by the mutation probe:

* `(?<!\w)-n` for "--no-verify" matches `tail -n`, `grep -n`, `sort -n`; and a
  file touched TODAY does not only contain today's lines — the first "hits"
  were from Sept 20. Now filtered by timestamp.
* The probe's time filter compared DATES only, so on the logbook's first day
  every earlier commit of that day would have been flagged. `utc()` converts
  `%cI` with its timezone and compares exactly.
* My guard helper returned `None` on a throw — and the case "`utc()` does not
  throw" checks for exactly `None`, so it could not tell the two apart. It now
  returns a SENTINEL.
* The catch clause in `lauf_vermerken()` was reachable by no case: without
  git, `laufbuch()` returns None first. It was the one mutation of eight that
  did not fall. A case that reaches it now exists.
* Three `betrieb()` calls in the self-test were unguarded, so a disarmed catch
  killed the whole self-test instead of reddening one case.

AND K0 HAD NO COUNTING RULE. A mutation-probe catch was not counted, a
compiler catch was not counted, gate catches were. Rule, binding from here: a
TOR catch is any MECHANICAL check that fires without someone deciding to look
(CI and commit hooks, audit scripts, compiler and linker via the build, a
test, a mutation matrix); a MENSCH catch comes from reading or reasoning.

Recounted: **15 of 24**. Part of the rise is NOT earned — it comes from the
definition, not from better work; under the old, unstated counting it would be
11 of 24. Both values are in the balance, because a metric rising through a
redefinition is precisely the move that "metrics are consequences, not goals"
forbids. It was admissible only because the old counting was internally
inconsistent, which is a finding and gets rewritten rather than removed.

AND ONE OF MY OWN FUNDUS FIGURES WAS WRONG, in the pessimistic direction. It
said "of 76 gate scripts, 54 have a self-test, 22 do not". Measured properly:
77 scripts, **69 tested**, and exactly **1** that makes a decision and is
nowhere tested (`audit_plugin_compliance.py`, a release gate). Two pattern
errors: the regex missed `def selbsttest(` without an underscore, and — far
worse — **a gate does not need its self-test inside itself**:
`scripts/audit_selbsttest.py` (MF-735) is a test bench that plants a small
tree with a known answer per tool and calls its `check()` in both directions,
and 18 of the 20 "untested" are registered there. A wrong backlog figure that
INVENTS a backlog costs work where nothing is missing — and it was already in
a commit. Corrected in place, not removed.

events.title: Tiles: masked rows in 68000
events.message:
Tiles: masked rows in 68000

A masked tile's rows go through a hand-written loop: each group's
mask word read first, a transparent group skipped, an opaque one
copied as two longs, the rest merged a plane pair at a time as
(d & mask) | s with the mask in both halves of a register. gcc had
kept the mask and loop counts on the stack and merged a word at a
time. C twin for the host tests; budget 2 touches planes 0 and 1.

Out of line: inlined into STDL_BlitTile it made masked tiles 0.755
of their time but cost every unmasked tile 0.7% through register
allocation; out of line, unmasked tiles are unchanged.

Plain ST (Hatari --machine st, same-binary floor 0.2%): PRIMCOST
tile 16x16 masked 737us -> 601 (0.81); nothing else moved past
0.4%. PIXCHK passes on st; a mutation in the C twin fails the host
tile test.

events.title: Add --clock-mhz: report emulated time from ReadEClock (issue #102) (#103)
events.message:
Add --clock-mhz: report emulated time from ReadEClock (issue #102) (#103)

* Add --clock-mhz: emulated-cycle-derived ReadEClock timing (issue #102)

Makes timer.device's ReadEClock report time derived from the CPU's own
emulated m68k cycle count at a configurable rate, instead of host
wall-clock time, so compiler A/B benchmarks under volamos are
reproducible and independent of host load.

- Cpu trait gains emulated_cycles()/clock_hz() with non-breaking
  defaults (0 / None).
- M68kCpu::set_clock_mhz(Some(mhz)) switches Cpu::run from run_batch to
  m68k::CpuCore::run_for_cycles, accumulating real cycle counts; the
  run_batch path is untouched when the flag is absent.
- read_eclock_handler derives ev_hi/ev_lo from cycles/clock_hz when
  active, but always reports ECLOCK_PAL_HZ in D0 -- real hardware
  derives the E-Clock from chipset timing, not the CPU clock.
  GetSysTime/TR_GETSYSTIME/DateStamp/CurrentTime are untouched.
- --clock-mhz errors cleanly when combined with an explicit --jit (the
  trace JIT never tracks a cycle count); a default-off --jit does not
  spuriously trip this, since jit only becomes true via an explicit
  override.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EHvk3UiKvgnG2xb71UJ67R

* Address review: refuse --clock-mhz+--sanitize, fix perf claims/docs (#102)

Code review fixes on the --clock-mhz branch:

1. Hard-error --clock-mhz + --sanitize (check_clock_mhz_sanitize): the
   cycle-counted run_via_cycles path never calls the sanitizer's
   per-instruction hooks, so combining the two would leave the shadow
   call stack/below-SP tracking silently stale while --sanitize still
   reports a normal-looking summary. Refused the same way as --jit,
   checked second so --jit's conflict still reports first when both
   apply.

2. Re-measured the perf claim: today's real numbers (CoreMark 1.0,
   --cpu 68020, host wall-clock throughput, three-run average) are
   ~217 iter/sec for --no-jit, ~680 for --jit, ~97 for --clock-mhz 25
   -- --clock-mhz is ~2.2x slower than --no-jit and ~7x slower than
   --jit, not the stale/wrong "~5x slower than --no-jit" previously
   quoted in three places (that figure was actually --jit-vs-interpreter,
   and pre-dated a FlatMemory read speedup that also sped up the
   precise-bus path).

3. Fixed cpu.rs's emulated_cycles doc: only Cpu::run accumulates
   cycles, never Cpu::step -- guest code reached via RawDoFmt's
   PutChProc callback or Supervisor's single-stepped routine
   (execfmt.rs) costs zero emulated cycles, same class of invisibility
   as native library handlers. Added the same caveat to
   CLI-Reference.md.

4. Documented the nested System()/Execute() cycle-counter-resets-to-zero
   caveat in CLI-Reference.md (was previously only a source comment).

5. Added MIN_CLOCK_MHZ (1 Hz) to parse_clock_mhz: --clock-mhz 1e-30
   drove ReadEClock's tick count to f64::INFINITY, saturating to
   u64::MAX on the cast -- harmless, but silently wrong.

6. check_clock_mhz_jit's error message now names --no-jit/the config
   file instead of "drop --jit" when jit came from a config file's
   JIT=true rather than an explicit CLI flag (JitSource, threaded
   through resolve()).

The "incidental pre-existing bug" reported in the previous commit is
retracted per review (reproduced by an accidental jsr-displacement typo
in the test fixture, not a real runtime bug) and not filed.
