events.title: feat(mapper): give /animate-tidy sub-step granularity and consistent coordinates for contiguify (SQ-1637)
events.message:
feat(mapper): give /animate-tidy sub-step granularity and consistent coordinates for contiguify (SQ-1637)

Part 2: `contiguify` emitted exactly ONE frame for its whole stage, under a
static, sometimes-wrong description ("Contiguity: eject foreign rooms
interleaved within a chain's span") regardless of which of its four internal
sub-steps (open_gated_holes_for_hubs, eject_interlopers, tighten_runs,
snap_leaves) actually moved anything. Give `contiguify` an optional
per-sub-step observer (CONTIGUIFY_SUB_STEPS, ContiguifySubStepObserver) and
have `relayout_auto_observed` emit one frame PER SUB-STEP THAT ACTUALLY
MOVED A ROOM, correctly labelled and naming which room(s) moved and why
(describe_contiguify_moves, mirroring cleanup_overlaps/repair_directional_
hints' "moved room N (name) from A to B" convention). A sub-step that moved
nothing emits no frame — noise avoidance, not four empty frames regardless.

On the real A129 house fixture this now correctly emits TWO frames —
"Contiguify (eject_interlopers): moved room 180 ..." and "Contiguify
(tighten_runs): moved room 76/78/193 ..." — where before there was one frame
whose static description could name the wrong mover.

Part 3: stress/align/contiguify frames were never packed or globally
anchored — only the final "pack" stage applies the per-component left-to-
right shift and the lowest-id-room-at-origin anchor — so a room's
coordinates could jump between the last pre-pack frame and the final frame
for no reason a viewer of the animation could see: the room didn't move,
the reference frame did. Apply the SAME per-component shift and the SAME
global anchor to every earlier stage's snapshot too, computed once the
per-component loop finishes (frames aren't emitted until then) so every
frame after "seed" shares one consistent coordinate system.

Known remaining limitation (documented in code and in the test above the
KNOWN LIMITATION comment): `seat_portal_leaves`, which runs strictly after
every stage frame is captured, can nudge a BYSTANDER room (not just the
portal-only leaf it's seating) to open a line on a shared row/column
(SQ-1356's `plane` rewrite). That is a genuine, separate, later-only
computation, not a coordinate-frame bug, so it is left undone here rather
than forcing a fragile early re-run of that pass for every stage.

Also updates two mapper-crate pinned tests (observed_emits_five_stage_
labels_in_order, observed_result_equals_plain_relayout) whose fixed "exactly
5 stages" / "call_count == 5" assumptions no longer hold now that contiguify
can emit 0..4 frames instead of exactly 1.

Falsified: reverting the fix and rerunning contiguify_emits_one_correctly_
labelled_frame_per_substep_that_moved_a_room /
contiguify_emits_no_frames_when_no_substep_moves_anything /
room_x_coordinate_stays_consistent_across_consecutive_stage_frames against
the pre-fix code reproduces each original symptom exactly (one generic
frame instead of two correctly-labelled ones; a spurious frame when nothing
moved; align.x=3 vs pack.x=4 instead of matching).

events.title: fix(d64-v3): the second CBM directory door lost scratched files and ran a looping chain 20 times — and a comment had claimed since MF-909 that it did not (P3-668, MF-1515)
events.message:
fix(d64-v3): the second CBM directory door lost scratched files and ran a looping chain 20 times — and a comment had claimed since MF-909 that it did not (P3-668, MF-1515)

src/formats/d64/uft_d64_parser_v3.c, d64_parse_directory():
  - `if (ftype == 0) continue;` ("Empty entry") dropped every scratched
    file. docs/format_specs/commodore/D64.TXT, byte $02: "$00 - Scratched
    (deleted file entry)", "80 - DEL".
  - the entry had no `deleted` field at all;
  - the chain had only a step brake (max_sectors = 20): a sector pointing
    at itself gave its entry 20 times, with no report.
Now the same rule as src/fs/uft_cbmdos.c since MF-1501: $00 with a name or
pointer is scratched, listed and marked `deleted`; a row with all 30 bytes
from the type byte zero was never written; $80 stays a visible DEL file;
each chain sector is remembered and a second visit stops the walk and sets
the new `dir_chain_loop`. Both new fields sit in structs private to the
.c file — no ABI change.

The MF-909 comment in src/fs/uft_cbmdos.c said of this file "dort steht
jetzt dieselbe Antwort". `git log -S MF-909` on it finds no commit — the
sentence was never true. BERICHTIGT there.

Reach, measured: `directory` and `file_count` of this parser have NO
reader — not in the file, not outside (d64_disk_v3_t is private; the v3
bridge passes geometry and sectors). The error was latent (class P3-204);

events.title: fix(app): make /animate-tidy's replay preserve gated-edge weighting and re-derive distortion last (SQ-1637)
events.message:
fix(app): make /animate-tidy's replay preserve gated-edge weighting and re-derive distortion last (SQ-1637)

run_tidy_pipeline's replay reconstruction (replay_build_and_placement) rebuilt
every edge via add_edge, which always mints PassageWeight::Hard and drops
whatever gated/Door weighting the real edge carries. Since the constraint
solver gives up on the weakest (most gated) edge first when a cycle closes,
discarding that weight let the replay's solver drop a DIFFERENT edge than
the real background tidy (tidy_layer_silent, which operates on the graph's
real weights via layer_subgraph) — a debugging tool that can show a layout
evolution the real pipeline never produces.

Also: the replay path never called remark_distorted after its four post-
relayout stages (cleanup_overlaps, repair_directional_hints, cleanup_overlaps
again, compact_empty_lines), unlike the production path (run_layer_ops_silent),
so the distortion flags written back could be stale from partway through the
pipeline (the SQ-1377 shape, reproduced in the replay path specifically).

Fix: reconstruct edges via add_edge_weighted(..., c.weight) instead of
add_edge, and call remark_distorted at the same point run_layer_ops_silent
does, right before writing positions/flags back to the live graph.

Falsified: reverting both changes and re-running the new test
(animated_replay_matches_silent_tidy_with_a_gated_passage) fails with a real
position divergence (room 3 lands at (0,1) in the buggy replay vs (0,-2) in
the real background tidy) on a 3-room same-direction cycle where the gated
edge is inserted first, deliberately decoupling weight-based drop order from
insertion-order tie-breaking.

events.title: refactor(g64): first rewiring onto the codec register — 113 surplus copies, now 111 (MF-1513, P3-666)
events.message:
refactor(g64): first rewiring onto the codec register — 113 surplus copies, now 111 (MF-1513, P3-666)

Step 3 of P3-666, first file. `uft_g64_parser_v3.c` carried its own
4-to-5 encode table and its own 32-entry decode table; both now come from
`include/uft/core/uft_gcr.h`.

    before:  113 surplus copies
    after:   111

The gate names both departures rather than just counting them:

    Familie dd00ee1840ff: 1 Fundstelle verschwunden
      (src/formats/g64/uft_g64_parser_v3.c::gcr_encode_table)
    Familie 7a9b0d4ab5aa: 1 Fundstelle verschwunden
      (…::gcr_decode_table)

The manifest is shortened in this same commit, so the progress is a diff,
not a number somebody adjusted.

## Why not the cheapest file

Three candidates sit in **zero** test targets: `uft_g64_parser_v2.c` and
both `uft_gcr_viterbi*.c`. Rewiring them would have dropped K3 by four at
almost no cost — and improved nothing, because all three are in
`docs/orphan_baseline.txt`: they have no callers, the code never runs.

That is the mirror image of P3-338, where the stated reason for a deletion
was that T3 would fall "without faking any evidence". A metric as motive.
So the first rewiring went to a file with real callers
(`uft_roundtrip.c`, `uft_advanced_mode.c`) even though it costs two CMake
entries.

`uft_g64.c` holds three tables and would be the bigger prize, but it hangs
in **11** test targets — its own commit, not the first one.

## Proof that nothing was lost

Both affected test targets green: `test_g64_v3_halbspur_index` 4 of 4,
`test_advanced_guete_ohne_messung` 25 of 25. Among them the assertion "v3
sector decoder still wrong — pinned as P3-196": that pre-existing defect is
UNCHANGED, which is exactly right. This commit replaced tables, not logic.

Behind it stands `test_gcr_register_gegen_bestehende.c` (15 assertions),
which holds the register against the shipped encoders over all 32 quintets
and all 65 536 value pairs of the bit packing.

events.title: debug: serialize HRDB run-state with the machine observed state
events.message:
debug: serialize HRDB run-state with the machine observed state

With the unified fork the HRDB transport is the default, and three of
its conventions broke the contract the native transport gets for free
from its starved stdin:

- clearBreakpoints() bypassed the stop gate (arming after a rebuild
  must not wait), so an edit `b all` executed mid-boot and deleted the
  entry breakpoint before it ever fired.
- armBreakpoint() went out as an immediate control command, so a held
  clear landed after the arms and wiped them at the next stop.
- resume() flipped m_stopped before the machine had actually resumed,
  so callers (and the stop gate) evaluated commands against a stale
  stopped state — a queued edit `b all` deleted a just-armed
  breakpoint in the window before !status(running).

m_stopped is now written by the !status handler alone. The dispatch
gate serializes with the observed state: stop-gated commands (clears
and arms both) only against a stopped machine, `run` only from the head
of the queue (so a resume kept batch is answered first, in order —
the native "b, b, then c" on one stdin), `break` only against an
observed-running machine, and both !status edges release work. pause()
queues its break behind a pending or in-flight `run` instead of
dropping it.

src/parsers/a2r/uft_a2r_parser.c computed rpm = 60 s / (length of the
WHOLE capture) on both paths. The references say a capture is longer than
a revolution — A2R 2.x: timing "about 450 degrees of rotation", xtiming
"about 810 degrees"; A2R 3.x: timing "1.25 disk revolutions", xtiming
"2.25 or more". They also say what ONE revolution is: A2R 2.x "Estimated
Loop Point contains the number of ticks from the start of the capture till
the sync sensor is triggered"; A2R 3.x the index array, "an absolute timing
(in ticks) from the start of the capture to when the index signal was
detected".

Now ONE rule, a2r_umdrehung_zu_rpm(), next to a2r_fluss_wechsel():
  - A2R 2: rpm from the loop point (timing and xtiming);
  - A2R 3: rpm from the first two index signals;
  - one index signal only (every A2R3 timing capture in the corpus), or a
    bits capture: rpm 0 = "not measurable from this capture" — written on
    the field, never "standing still"; min_rpm does not count it.

Owner decision 2026-09-28: the Copy II Plus fixture from the uft-a2r-code
package is used — LOCAL-ONLY (commercial title) as
tests/corpus/copyiiplus_3loc.a2r, with a manifest entry (sha256, source,

Applesauce files, all local only (exit 77 without them):

    394 / 590; INFO as Applesauce wrote it.
  vignau_a2r2_35/waitless_d1.a2r (3.5", two-sided): both sides near 394.

events.title: fix(mapper): stop scoring a one-way edge as reciprocal from its destination's side (SQ-1636)
events.message:
fix(mapper): stop scoring a one-way edge as reciprocal from its destination's side (SQ-1636)

room_side_score/room_alignment_score/edges_respected_at's reciprocity check keyed
its return-edge lookup off the derived (other, id) pair, which collapses direction:
when `id` was the connection's destination, `other == c.origin && id == c.dest` is
trivially true of the connection itself, so a purely one-way edge scored
RECIPROCAL_WEIGHT (2) when evaluated from its destination but correctly 1 from its
origin. A real Zork I Amiga r88 save hit this on Forest (#76): its one-way incoming
edge from Canyon View was miscounted as reciprocal, so repair_directional_hints's
trial for moving it toward South of House scored as a net loss and rejected a
genuinely improving move.

Fix: key the lookup off the connection's own origin/dest (swapped), which stays
direction-aware regardless of which end is being scored.

Adds two mapper unit tests (asymmetric one-way pair now scores identically from
either end; a genuine bidirectional pair still scores double from both ends) and
an app-level end-to-end test driving the real repair_directional_hints through the
exact accept/reject boundary. Falsified by reverting the fix: both new tests fail
with the reported symptom (3 vs 2; the room stuck at its original position instead
of moving). crates/mapper/tests/sq1364_clearing_gap.rs (the earlier stage-1 pinned
test) is confirmed unaffected.

events.title: feat(gui): which GCR is on this track — one combo box, and the refusal sits on top (MF-1511)
events.message:
feat(gui): which GCR is on this track — one combo box, and the refusal sits on top (MF-1511)

The smallest form that answers the question. `ProtectionAnalysisWidget`
gains a `QComboBox` above the existing detail field; no new group, no new
table, no heatmap column.

Per track, best first:

    Commodore 5/4 — valid 99.8 % (958 of 960 words)
    Apple 6&2     — valid 12.1 % (116 of 960 words)
    Apple 5&3     — valid  3.4 % ( 33 of 960 words)

The share comes from `uft_gcr_anteil_gueltig()` (MF-1509): the raw bits go
through each codec's predicate and the valid code words are counted. One
number per codec instead of a guess about what the container is called.

## The refusal is the point, not the suggestion

If no codec clears the threshold, the FIRST entry reads
`— kein Codec passt (best 61.2 %) —` and is preselected. A bitstream where
everything is invalid is not a codec problem: it is noise, or a protection
using deliberately invalid GCR (Fast Hack'em `-f`, nibtools `-f`). Whoever
switches codec there has traded a finding for a setting. The register
already carries that case and
`nullstrom_ist_unter_JEDEM_codec_schlecht_und_das_ist_kein_codecfehler`
nails it down.

## Measured at load time, on purpose

`uft_gcr_erkennen()` runs inside the G64 loading loop, because the raw bits
are gone after `g64_free()`. Three numbers per track instead of keeping
whole tracks in memory. `m_gcrKandidaten` shares index and lifetime with
`m_trackMetrics` and is cleared with it.

## Not in the heatmap, and that is deliberate

Its seven columns are MEASUREMENTS (weak bits, long track, …). A selection
is a SETTING. Two meanings in one table is how a reader stops trusting
either.

## Two things this does NOT do, stated rather than implied

**The selection changes the display only** — it does not re-read the track.
Re-reading is an intervention in the read path, not a surface matter, and
was not part of what was asked for here.

**The 0.80 threshold is NOT measured.** It decides only whether a
suggestion or a finding sits on top, and changes no data; the comment says
so. A measured threshold would need corpus runs across clean and protected
tracks.

**And the manual smoke test is outstanding.** CLAUDE.md requires "what was
clicked, what happened" for GUI changes; this session cannot run the GUI,
and there is no Qt test for this widget in the tree. The LOGIC behind the
box is tested (11 of 11 in MF-1509), the WIRING is not. Recorded as open
rather than counted as done.

events.title: feat(core): a GCR codec register of PREDICATES — three codecs, one table left, and the gate caught the register laying a thirteenth (MF-1509)
events.message:
feat(core): a GCR codec register of PREDICATES — three codecs, one table left, and the gate caught the register laying a thirteenth (MF-1509)

Step 1 and 2 of P3-666. The CBM GCR table stands in 12 places, the decode
table in 10, the Apple 6&2 table in 7 (measured MF-1506). Merging them does
not mean "one table for all" — it means the word set comes from a PREDICATE
that lives in one place.

`include/uft/core/uft_gcr.h` + `src/core/uft_gcr.c`, placed where CLAUDE.md
already puts it: "MFM/FM/GCR Codec" belongs to the core engine, not the
format layer.

## Three codecs, all three measured against the tables in the tree

  Commodore 5/4   no two leading zeros · no two trailing · never 000 ·
                  NOT 11111                                    16 words
  Apple 6&2       bit 7 · at most ONE zero pair ·
                  a pair of ones in bits 6..0                  64 words
  Apple 5&3       bit 7 · NO zero pair ·
                  a pair of ones in bits 6..0                  32 words

The Commodore sync exclusion is the condition that gets forgotten: a data
word of all ones could combine with the next into a SYNC mark. Without it
the rule yields 17.

5&3 differs from 6&2 in exactly one condition and is therefore a true
subset — measured, and nailed down as an assertion.

**Assignment:** for Apple it is the rule (index k = k-th valid byte
ascending), measured byte for byte against both tables. For Commodore it is
NOT — the set follows the rule, the order 0..F is Commodore's choice. That
is the only table in the register, and the counter-assertion
`cbm_zuordnung_ist_KEINE_regel_und_das_ist_gemessen` records that this was
measured rather than forgotten.

## Checked against the encoders it replaces, not against itself

`tests/test_gcr_register_gegen_bestehende.c`, 11 assertions. The decisive
one runs over `cbm_gcr_encode_chunk()` with all **65 536** value pairs —
so it covers the BIT PACKING (40 bits MSB-first into 5 bytes), which is
where faults live, not in the 16 values. A table comparison would never
have touched it. Two hands per MF-644: the old function encodes, the new
predicate recomputes.

For Apple there is no encoder in this tree — only `denibblize_6_2/5_3`, on
sector level with an XOR checksum, where a failure has two possible causes.
The test says so in its own header; the byte-exact comparison follows when
the table moves to `tests/oracles/` (step 3).

## The gate caught the register itself

The first draft carried its own 16-byte table — the **13th** copy of the
CBM encode table. A register meant to merge copies, adding one on the way.
`audit_konstantenfamilien.py` refused it by name, three hours after being
built (MF-1506).

The fix is better than the draft: the table is now READ from
`include/uft/uft_cbm_gcr.h` instead of repeated. It moves into the register
with the last caller rewiring, and then the others disappear — that is the
direction the manifest should shrink in, not one more copy on the way there.

## Recognition, which the surface will show

`uft_gcr_anteil_gueltig()` sends a bitstream through a codec's predicate and
returns the share of valid code words. One number per codec instead of a
guess. One predicate, three uses, no further copy.

And the refusal is part of it: where every codec scores badly, no codec
change helps — that is noise or deliberately invalid GCR (copy protection).
`uft_gcr_erkennung_t` carries the case and
`nullstrom_ist_unter_JEDEM_codec_schlecht_und_das_ist_kein_codecfehler`
nails it down. Whoever switches codec there has traded a finding for a
setting.

## One test error, honestly

The first recognition stream was 64 bytes — which does not divide by 5 bits,
so the trailing bytes stayed 0x00 and counted as invalid quintets. The test
was measuring its own SETUP, not the codec, and it went red. The code was
right and the measurement wrong; checked per MF-1177 sentence 1 before
anything in the register was touched. Now 60 bytes = exactly 96 quintets,
with an assertion that it divides evenly.

events.title: test(gcr): the rule in the code hit the table, the rule in the prose did not — both predicates nailed down bijectively (MF-1508)
events.message:
test(gcr): the rule in the code hit the table, the rule in the prose did not — both predicates nailed down bijectively (MF-1508)

Step 1 of the P3-666 rebuild, and the step that decides whether it works
at all: can the GCR word sets be produced from a PREDICATE, so the 12 CBM
and 7 Apple copies collapse onto one place?

Measured against the tables in the tree, before any rebuild. Both rules
hold — and both needed a correction that the prose describing them did not
have.

## Commodore 5/4: the fourth condition is the sync mark

    no two leading zeros · no two trailing · never three in a row · NOT 11111

Without the last one the rule yields 17 words instead of 16. It is not an
arbitrary exclusion: a data word of all ones could combine with the next to
form a SYNC mark (ten ones in a row), which the 1541 head reads as the
start of a track.

## Apple 6&2: two refinements, and they are what separates 64 from 74

    bit 7 set · at MOST ONE pair of adjacent zeros · a pair of ones in BITS 6..0

The circulating description ("no three zeros, at least one pair of ones")
yields **74** words. "At most one zero pair" is stricter than "no three
zeros" — three zeros contain two pairs, but not conversely — and the pair
of ones must be counted WITHOUT bit 7, which is always set and would
satisfy the condition by itself.

Worth recording who was right about what: the owner's own implementation
already carried the stricter form; only the description said 74. That is
the finding itself, and it is exactly what K6 counts — a rule that exists
only as a sentence drifts, the rule in code hit the table.

## The third assertion, which is usually missing

A predicate is nailed down with THREE claims, not two: the count is right,
every table word passes, and **no non-table word passes**. Both over-wide
rule versions above satisfy claims 1 and 2 for every table entry; only the
third one falls. It is the assertion that matters.

`tests/test_gcr_praedikat_trifft_die_tafel.c`, 7 assertions, mutation
matrix **3 of 3**: removing the sync exclusion turns three CBM assertions
red, loosening the zero-pair condition turns two Apple assertions red, and
counting the pair of ones with bit 7 turns one red. So neither refinement
is decoration.

The CBM table comes from `include/uft/uft_cbm_gcr.h` — the same definition
production code uses, not a copy. For Apple only the COUNT is proven, and
the test says so in its own header: `A2_WRITE_TAB` is `static`, so the
bijective comparison needs it visible, which is step 3 of the rebuild
(table moves to `tests/oracles/`, where it turns from a pin into an
ORACLE — producer and checker then being different hands, MF-644).

## Ratchet: the warning is now countable

`commit_verified.py` writes a skipped ratchet into the body as
`Ratsche-uebersprungen: <file> (<n>) — Konstantenkopie(n) bleiben (P3-666)`.
It still does not block (measured: it would hit every fifth commit), but a
warning that leaves no trace is a warning nobody acts on. The retrospective
counts these lines; three skips of the same file put P3-666 on the table.
Verified on the real case: `uft_g64.c` produces the line, `CLAUDE.md`
produces nothing. A note that cannot be made never blocks a commit — it is
a note, not a gate.

Where the codec register goes, since it was asked: `src/core/`, beside the
existing `uft_mfm_encoder.c`. Not an opinion — `CLAUDE.md` already places
"MFM/FM/GCR Codec" in the core engine, not in the format layer.

events.title: Amiga: records and storage copied and cleared a long at a time
events.message:
Amiga: records and storage copied and cleared a long at a time

q_copy_longs and q_clear_longs in macros.m68 copy or clear a fixed,
even length a long at a time. They replace the byte and word loops for
object records, model data, variables, ship graphics, the hold, text
buffers, the palette, the sky, the planet screen, the galaxy chart and
small table copies. From 64 bytes q_clear_longs writes a zero register
instead of clr, which is slower up to the 68030.

The ship graphics clear sits after its section, where vasm knows its
size.

events.message:
Model Paula samples as live byte views of chip memory

A Sample is now a Sequence of bytes that views memory without copying.
So writes made while a channel plays are heard, as on the hardware. Only
Channel.read_word builds the 16-bit words that DMA fetches. Six specs
copied their buffers and lost those writes, for example Oktalyzer and
Abyss, which played silence.

events.title: tool(gates): a number written in two places drifts — so the second place is abolished, not checked (MF-1507, P3-666)
events.message:
tool(gates): a number written in two places drifts — so the second place is abolished, not checked (MF-1507, P3-666)

Two owner instructions after MF-1506, both carried out by measuring first.

## 1. K0 now has one place, not two

MF-1505's subject said "1 of 7" while its own body said "2 of 10". Two
copies of the same number, written by hand at different times. That they
drifted is not carelessness — it is what two copies always do (MF-1177).

The durable fix is not care, it is removing the second place.
`commit_verified.py` now reads K0 from `.claude/SITZUNGSBILANZ.md` and
appends it as a trailer; a conflicting number written into the message is
REFUSED with both values named. Self-test 5 -> 10 cases, including exactly
the MF-1505 shape ("widersprechende K0 im Text faellt") and the boundary
cases: the most recent balance line wins when a file holds several
sessions, and without a balance nothing is appended and nothing fails.

## 2. The 113 copies: sorted before touched

Freezing was the right first step; merging is work on `src/`. Before any of
it, the sort — measured, not guessed:

  67 copies in 25 families   A-produktiv: more than once in our own
                             production code. The actual candidates.
  39 copies in 31 families   test expectations
   7 copies in  2 families   embedded FOREIGN code (src/a8rawconv/,
                             src/dtc_components/, src/samdisk/) — untouchable.
                             They belong to the other project and ARE our
                             yardstick.

And a fourth sort that forbids merging for a reason that is not licensing:
a table with which a TEST builds its INPUT
(`tests/flux_gen/xum1541/flux_gen.c::GCR_ENC`) must stay independent of the
one production code uses to READ — otherwise the test checks itself (class
MF-644, "the same hand"). There the copy is the promise, not the fault.

The largest family shows all four at once: the CBM GCR encode table stands
in 12 places — 9 mergeable (among them `src/formats/g64/uft_g64.c` TWICE,
as `gcr_enc` and `gcr_encode_table`), 1 foreign, 1 test generator, 1 test
expectation.

## The ratchet, and why it warns instead of blocking

`--ratsche <basis>` reports when a touched file still carries a manifest
site, so the manifest falls with ordinary work rather than through one big
rebuild — each line with its own red proof, no full build standing still
for a cleanup.

It does not block, and that was decided by measuring: 119 of 2116 source
files carry a manifest site (5.6 %), and **7 of the last 40 commits (18 %)**
would have touched one — including `uft_g64.c` with three sites. Armed, the
ratchet would have coupled the peer's G64 sync fix (MF-1500) to merging
three GCR tables. A coupling that hangs every fifth bugfix on a rebuild gets
worked around rather than followed. `--ratsche-scharf` stands ready if the
owner wants it otherwise — that decision is not this script's to make.

Registered as **P3-666**, Fundus, with the order of work by risk: first the
values COMPUTED in one place and typed out in another (the track capacities
6250/6666/7142/7692 are such a case), then the rest of production code,
tests last.

events.title: feat(fs): Apple DOS 3.3 catalog reader, checked against a2tools — and against a real disk DOS itself formatted (P3-384, MF-1497)
events.message:
feat(fs): Apple DOS 3.3 catalog reader, checked against a2tools — and against a real disk DOS itself formatted (P3-384, MF-1497)

UFT reads six Apple containers and until now could not tell anyone which
FILES are on a DOS 3.3 disk: the FS tier table had zero hits for dos33.
P3-384 named two blockers, both now measured away:

1. A real DOS 3.3 image exists, local only: tests/corpus/
   wozaday_copy2plus_52.woz (Copy II Plus 5.2). Through the tree's GCR
   path (woz plugin + uft_apple_gcr, throwaway converter): 560 of 560
   sectors; a2tools lists 6 entries, 80 sectors free.
2. A CI fixture after all. a2tools cannot format (dir/out/in/del only,
   MF-1207), but it writes into a skeleton it did not make:
   scripts/mk_dos33_leer.py builds the empty skeleton (own hand), a2tools
   writes five files and deletes one -> tests/corpus_free/
   a2tools_dos33_filled.do (sha256 0b2631c9..., two runs identical). The
   manifest names BOTH hands (MF-1021): the skeleton decides the volume
   and the chain's course; a2tools the catalog, T/S lists, data and the
   free map.

New: include/uft/fs/uft_dos33.h + src/fs/uft_dos33.c — VTOC plausibility
(the six bytes a2tools checks), free count, catalog chain with a loop
brake, deleted entries KEPT and marked, the original T/S track of a
deleted entry reported only when byte 30 holds a valid track (a2tools'
`del` does not move it there — no invented track). Own implementation:
the offsets are READ against a2tools' code at the named lines, no line
taken; the package neue-ideen/Apple DOS.zip (derived from a2tools) is not
used.

events.title: fix(asm): reject silently truncated operands, report real locations (#50)
events.message:
fix(asm): reject silently truncated operands, report real locations (#50)

* fix(asm): reject silently truncated operands, report real locations

Six defects, all of which assembled with exit status 0 and produced a
working binary for a program that says something else.

Undefined symbols were assembled as address 0. `parse_operand_text`
answers a bare identifier with a placeholder so pass 1 can size a
forward reference before the symbol is known; nothing checked that the
placeholder was gone by pass 2, so `JSR tippfehler` became `jsr $0.w`.
Pass 2 now rejects a placeholder whose symbol is still undefined.
Forward references are unaffected -- by pass 2 they resolve.

Oversized index displacements were masked into the 8-bit brief-format
field, so `316(A0,D2.L)` addressed 316 bytes away from what the source
said. The PC-relative variant has always reported this; the
register-based one now does too, naming the value and the limit rather
than falling through to "cannot parse operand".

ANDI/ORI/EORI/CMPI/ADDI/SUBI each masked their immediate into place
with no range check, so `ANDI.B #300,D0` assembled to `#$2C` while
`MOVE.B #300` rejected the same value. All six now share one helper.
Both spellings of a byte stay valid: `#$FF` and `#-1` mean one thing.

A macro named like a directive was stored and then silently ignored at
every call site, because the expansion check skips anything that parses
as a directive. Such a name can never be invoked, so it is rejected
where the name is chosen.

MOVEQ #128..255 and BTST/BSET/BCLR/BCHG with a bit number wider than
the operand now warn. Both are valid bit patterns the CPU will execute,
so they stay warnings -- but MOVEQ sign-extends (`#200` loads -56) and
the bit number is taken modulo the operand width, and nothing in the
output showed that the value had changed.

Diagnostics pointed at the wrong line. INCLUDE splices whole files in
and macros expand to several lines each, so the number the parser
carries refers to the expanded text, not to any file a reader can open:
an error in an include was reported against the top-level file, and
every error after a macro call was off by the body's length. A source
map now records where each expanded line was written, and diagnostics
are translated through it; a line from a macro body names the macro.
Errors raised during include expansion name their own file, since the
map does not exist yet at that point.

Verified against an external test harness covering all six with
counter-checks (boundary immediates, expressions, ORI to SR, free macro
names, forward references): 36 of 37 cases pass. The remaining case
expects a line number one above where the offending instruction
actually is.

* fix(asm): report a missing include at its own file and line

The previous commit named the file an include error came from, but only
in the message text -- the line number still rode the outer file's
counter and was then translated through the source map as if it were an
expanded-line number. So a missing include in line 3 of a nested file
was reported as line 1 of that file, and one reached from the top level
named the top-level file with the included file's line number.

An error raised while expansion is still running is different in kind
from one found afterwards: it has no source map yet, but it does know
its file, and its line already counts within that file. `AsmError`
carries an optional `file` for exactly that case, and a location that
arrives already resolved is printed as-is instead of being translated a
second time.

Also: a search path list that began with an empty `source_root` printed
"searched in " with nothing after it; the current directory now shows
as ".".

The external harness covering all six original findings plus the two
location cases now passes 39 of 39.

---------

Co-authored-by: Attackwave <attackwave@users.noreply.github.com>

events.title: tool(gates): K3 said "no audit" for every constant family but one — measured, there are 58 of them and 113 surplus copies (MF-1506)
events.message:
tool(gates): K3 said "no audit" for every constant family but one — measured, there are 58 of them and 113 surplus copies (MF-1506)

K3 named capacities, gap sizes and CRC polynomials as the families without
an audit. Following this tree's own rule (standing orders, section C: where
a rule lacks a gate, the MEASUREMENT is the next step, not the gate), the
measurement came first — and it found more than the guess.

## What was measured

All numeric initialisers across `git ls-files` (2117 files), grouped by
their contents. No pattern was guessed in advance. Filters, each with a
reason: at least 4 entries (shorter is a tuple), at most 300 (beyond that
it is data), not a running index, and — decisive — **present in more than
one FILE**. Two tables in the same file are a local duplication; two in
different modules are two truths that can drift apart. That distinction
alone is the difference between 84 and 58.

  58 families in >1 file, 113 surplus copies

  12 files   CBM GCR ENCODE table  (gcr_encode_table, DEFAULT_GCR, GCR_ENC,
             dtc_gcr_cbm_4to5, c64_gcr_encode, …) — and `uft_g64.c` carries
             it TWICE, as `gcr_enc` and `gcr_encode_table`
  10 files   CBM GCR DECODE table
   7 files   Apple GCR 6&2 table    (A2_WRITE_TAB, GCR62, kGCR6Encoder, …)
   5 files   CBM zone lengths       (the specialised gate also covers these)
   4 files   track capacities 6250/6666/7142/7692
   3 files   CRC-16 table           (crc16_table, crc_tab, test_crc_tab)

This project's memory notes said "GCR table sixfold" and "Apple GCR table
sevenfold". Measured today: 12 and 7. A hand-kept number next to a measured
one drifts — which is why the gate counts rather than reads a list.

## The gate

`scripts/audit_konstantenfamilien.py`, built in the shape of MF-1504: the
baseline is a MANIFEST of named sites (`datei::symbol`), not a count,
because against a count a tree passes even when one copy goes and a new one
arrives. A new site -> FAIL by name. A site gone -> OK plus a hint to
shorten. No manifest -> FAIL saying the gate checked NOTHING.

Self-test 10/10. Red proof on the REAL tree, not only on throwaway ones: a
13th copy of the CBM GCR encode table placed into `src/formats/c64/`
takes the gate from 0 findings to 1, **naming the file and symbol**; after
removal, 0 again and the tree unchanged (verified). Runtime 2.9 s over 2117
files.

## It does not replace the zone gate

`audit_cbm_zonen.py` computes the zone tables against the SSOT and therefore
also sees a copy that is already WRONG. This one only sees THAT a sequence
appears more than once. Breadth here, depth there — both are wired into
`check_consistency.py`, and a gate that fails to run is recorded as a
finding, not as silence.

## Correction to MF-1505

That commit's subject line says "1 of 7" while its own body says 2 of 10 —
the balance had grown by three errors between drafting the message and the
commit. The body is right. Not amended, because an amend costs a second full
build for a subject line; corrected here, which is this tree's usual way.

K0 for the session stands at 2 of 10 and is maintained in
`.claude/SITZUNGSBILANZ.md`.

events.title: docs(metrics): every metric gets a measuring command, every session a balance — and the first balance says 1 of 7 (MF-1505)
events.message:
docs(metrics): every metric gets a measuring command, every session a balance — and the first balance says 1 of 7 (MF-1505)

Owner templates from 2026-09-28, built in. The premise is the measurement
from that same day: five rules stood in the tree as prose, and the session
that wrote them broke one in the same breath — the 24th copy of the CBM zone
lengths, inside a test whose header quoted "one size, one calculation". The
gate caught it. The agent did not.

## K0, the metric above the metrics

New: the share of errors caught by a GATE rather than by a human. It does not
measure the tree, it measures whether the rules bite. If it stays low, every
further rule is prose wasted.

Honestly counted for this session: **2 of 10**. Both gate catches caught
something that already stood in the tree AS A SENTENCE — "one size, one
calculation" (the 24th copy of the zone lengths) and "gen_stand.py last"
(`[STAND.md stale]`, which rejected the merge commit). That is the entire
argument for this metric.

The eight a human caught are in `.claude/SITZUNGSBILANZ.md` with what
followed from each. Two are worth naming here. One is a near miss: I
measured T2=14/T3=2 and was about to correct CLAUDE.md as "drifted", until I
saw the file lists every format TWICE — the maintained number was right and
my measurement was wrong. MF-1177 sentence 1 stopped it, not a gate. The
other is this commit's own first draft: K4 went in as "Messbefehl fehlt"
although `gen_erzeuger_zensus.py` has measured exactly that question since
MF-1087 and runs on every commit. The metric was not unmeasurable, it was
never CONNECTED to its command. Caught only on an outside question.

**And a finding about the balance itself, which is in the file:** between
its first writing and the end of the session three more errors appeared, one
of which would have gone unnoticed. The first version named 7, the complete
one names 10. A balance reconstructed at the end measures memory, not the
session — so it is now written as errors occur.

## Every metric now names how to measure it

The four metrics are unchanged; they now say how they are read, and the
table carries a dated standing. One of them deliberately carries an
incomplete command:

  K3  only ONE constant family has an audit (zones). Capacities, gap sizes,
      CRC polynomials: no audit. Next step is the MEASUREMENT — which
      families are carried more than once? — not the gate.

The owner's template carried numbers from a different tree (Defence-Force
84/85, `tools/fixture_census.py`, D88/FDI/PianoDisc). Those are the t4
contribution, not UFT: the script does not exist here, and the equivalent of
"real fixture" in this tree is the tier table — T1 means an image from a
foreign hand. So K2 reads **11 of 89**, measured, and K1/K4 say "Messbefehl
fehlt" where that is the truth. A number nobody here can recompute is the
class this tree has paid for four times.

Corrected against the template where the tree disagreed: K5 is **199**
orphans (`docs/orphan_baseline.txt`, data lines), not 190. K6 is **2**, not
1 — "oracle numbers through the binary" plus "whoever parses a set counts it
back", the latter from my own parser silently discarding 42 of 71 track
lines.

## The balance is compulsory, and it has a price

`.claude/SITZUNGSBILANZ.md`: every session lists each of its errors with WHO
caught it — gate, human, or nobody. An error caught by a human gets a gate, a
red proof, or a Fundus line saying why neither is possible. Without a balance
the session is open, and the retrospective cannot see it.

The rule list is capped at **30 sentences**, each carrying the incident that
produced it. Sentence 31 displaces the oldest sentence WITHOUT a gate — or
becomes a gate itself. A rule list that only grows does not get read.

## Two standing orders

`.claude/STEHENDE_AUFTRAEGE.md`. The retrospective becomes the EIGHTH role of
`uft-innendienst` (its description said seven; corrected, or the number
drifts). It answers four questions and builds nothing. Its sharpest one:
where a gate has fired twice on the same error, the answer is not a second
gate but abolishing the wrong path — `commit_verified.py` as the only commit
route is the worked example.

The build order picks from the Fundus whatever moves the WEAKEST metric, not
the most interesting item, and the builder does not grade his own work.
Metrics invite gaming — "unverified formats" can be lowered by deleting, and
this tree has that on record (`rcpmfs`, P3-338: the stated reason was that T3
would fall "without faking any evidence"). Hence a measuring command in the
tree, and a different role doing the grading.

At "Check startup device!" the firmware runs its own slot 5 code over and
over, and inserting an image put the SmartPort's ROM there at once, under

it runs is readable at once and boots at the next Ctrl+Reset, and the host
says so. Ejecting the last image leaves the ROM until reset.

src/fs/uft_cbmdos.c (FS-T2) skipped type byte $00 as "never used" and
listed $80/$C0 as deleted. The reference in the tree says the opposite —
docs/format_specs/commodore/D64.TXT, byte $02:

    $00 - Scratched (deleted file entry)
     80 - DEL

A scratched file keeps its name, pointers and block count; $80 is a
VISIBLE file of type DEL. libcbmimage (GPL-2, executed in the review,
dir.c:179) judges the same. Now:
  - $00 with a name or pointer: listed, `deleted`;
  - all 30 bytes from the type byte zero: never written, not listed;
  - $80/$C0: listed as DEL, not `deleted`.

And the directory chain only had a step brake (683) — it bounded a loop
instead of noticing it. Each directory sector read is now remembered; a
second visit stops the walk and sets the new field `chain_loop` (appended
at the end of uft_cbmdos_dir_t). Entries read until then stay. The
explorer tab tells the user the listing is incomplete.

Measured in the uft-cbm-code package review (neue-ideen, t4), 18 real
D64 against libcbmimage: the scratched SINGLER on Fast Hack'em, four
entries of OpenCBM's test.d64 and one of simpletest-generator.d64 were
missing; 28 visible DEL< entries of filleddk.d64 were reported deleted;
simpletest-loop.d64 gave 5192 entries where libcbmimage gives 76 and
"Loop detected".

Red proof first: tests/test_cbmdos_scratch_und_schleife.c changes single
bytes of tests/corpus_free/vice_c1541_35trk.d64:
  before: 4 of 6 red ($80 read as deleted; $00 missing; 683 entries for
          the loop, no report)
  after:  6 of 6 green
Mutation matrix 4 of 4 red, each caught where it should be: loop brake
removed; $00 skipped again; deleted = type DEL again; GUI line removed
(test_explorer_tab_no_fiction, new case loopedD64SaysTheListIsIncomplete,
offscreen: 9 of 9 green).

tests/test_cbm_geloeschte_eintraege.c pinned the inverted reading
(MF-909). It is REWRITTEN, not removed: BERICHTIGT in its head, the
scratched case now uses $00, the never-written case zeroes the whole row,
and a fourth case pins the visible DEL file. The MF-909 intent — a
scratched entry is shown — is unchanged. uft_cbmdos.h: `deleted` and
`deleted_count` BERICHTIGT.

Still open and named in P3-664: the second door

Merging origin/main (through 7031708c, MF-1500) into the oracle-calibration
line (MF-1494…MF-1504). Three conflicts, all resolved by measuring rather
than by picking a side.

## docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md — the neighbouring-line conflict the peer predicted

Both sides appended behind P3-659: this session P3-660/661/662/665, the peer
session P3-663. Not a contradiction — both belong in the tree. Resolved by
union, sorted by number, giving P3-659…P3-663, P3-665.

The merge script ABORTED first rather than guessing, because P3-659 differed
on both sides. Measured before deciding: the origin version carries MF-1492
("Dritte Scheibe": dmk and sap compute the data CRC themselves and now set
CRC_CHECKED), mine does not — 4588 against 3386 characters, `MF-1492` once
against zero times. The peer had CONTINUED the entry; my version is the older
state of the same text, not a rival. His version wins, with that reasoning
recorded in the resolution script.

## docs/STAND.md, docs/VERIFICATION_TIERS.md — generated, so regenerated

Not hand-merged. A hand-merged generated file is a number nobody can
recompute, which is the class this tree keeps paying for. Ran
`gen_verification_tiers.py --write`, `gen_fs_tiers.py`,
`gen_erzeuger_zensus.py` instead; 0 conflict markers afterwards.

MF-1500 makes `uft_g64.c` call `gcr_find_sync()` from `uft_gcr_ops.c`. The
peer entered the dependency into eight test targets; `test_c64_g64_gegen_nibscan`
(MF-1503) was not on origin yet, so it was invisible to him. Added here, with
the reason in the comment.

MF-1500 changes G64 sector decoding — the question was whether my
differential run against nibscan still holds. It does: **7 of 7 assertions
green** under his tree, unchanged. My path goes through `g64_get_track()`
(`uft_d64_g64.c:819`) and `ufm_c64_metrics_from_gcr()` on the RAW track, with
its own sync detection; his change is a different path, and now that is
measured rather than assumed.

nibscan's zero sector errors. While `uft_g64.c` still said 33, two
independent hands already said 768. His correction is confirmed by a second
number, not just by its own.

events.title: Charge a IIgs's shadowed writes as Mega II cycles
events.message:
Charge a IIgs's shadowed writes as Mega II cycles

Shadowing copies a write in bank $00 or $01 to the Mega II side, and the
processor waits for that copy: a write to a shadowed screen runs at 1MHz
whatever the speed register says. The copy was made but charged as a
fast cycle, so anything drawing to text, hi-res or Super Hi-Res ran up
to a tenth faster than a real machine beside it.

shadowWrite now says whether it copied, and write charges a slow access
when it did, as GSSquared does (megaiiWrite, a SYNC cycle).
test_iigs_memory.cpp pins shadowed writes as slow, unwatched ones as
fast, and a region going fast again when its shadowing is switched off.

events.title: tool(gates): what a gate does not check happens again — twice measured today, so four rules got one (MF-1504)
events.message:
tool(gates): what a gate does not check happens again — twice measured today, so four rules got one (MF-1504)

Owner instruction after MF-1503, in four parts. Each one turns a sentence
that already stood in prose into something mechanical, because prose does
not hold: five times in one session I wrote down "one size, one place" and
then created the 24th copy of the CBM zone lengths myself.

## 1. The commit run states its own result

`scripts/commit_verified.py`. Twice today a `git commit … | tail` reported 0
while the pre-commit hook had REJECTED the commit — behind a pipe the exit
code belongs to the last link, and `tail` always succeeds. Once it cost a
cycle (`FAIL: STAND.md stale`), once a gate rejection was read as success
and this session announced a commit that did not exist.

`set -o pipefail` heals the exit code; the trap stays, because the next call
pipes again. So this does not heal the code, it heals the QUESTION: HEAD is
read before and after, and the verdict is the LAST LINE of the output —
`NEUER COMMIT <sha> <subject>` or `KEIN NEUER COMMIT — <reason>`, exit 1.
Hook output goes to a FILE, never through a pipe. `tail -1` on that file is
now the right check instead of one you have to remember.

Self-test 5/5, including the expensive case: a hook that prints success on
stdout AND exits non-zero.

## 2. The baseline is a manifest of named sites, not a count

`scripts/audit_cbm_zonen.py` + `scripts/cbm_zonen_grundlinie.json`.

A count cannot hold the rule, and that is measured, not argued. Against
`len(stellen) > 23` a tree passes even when an old copy disappears and a NEW
one arrives — net zero, rule broken, nobody notices. Shown on a throwaway
tree:

  A  23 sites                              -> OK
  B  23 sites, 1 NEW, 1 gone               -> OK   (!)
     by name: +frisch_angelegte_tafel, -kopie_22

With the manifest: a site not in it -> FAIL, by name. A site gone from it ->
OK plus a hint to shorten. No manifest at all -> FAIL saying the gate checked
NOTHING, rather than waving things through. The baseline can now only fall,
and visibly, as a diff in the commit — the direction MF-1077 wants, without
anyone touching a number.

**This is not a maintained list in the sense of MF-636**, and the difference
is the whole point: the CHECKED SET still comes from `git ls-files`. The
manifest does not select what is checked; it records what was found last
time, and it is generated, not typed. The file's own header says so.

Self-test 7/7 -> 13/13; the six new cases include "count unchanged (3)" AND
"new site still caught".

## 3. An oracle's constant is not typed out (docs/ORACLES.md)

Sister rule to "no oracle on assurance". Numbers from an oracle come through
its BINARY, not through a table in our tree. The rule distinguishes two
things, and that distinction is its whole content: a CONSTANT FAMILY both
sides carry (zone lengths, capacities, gap sizes) must not be copied — a
second table is a second truth, it drifts, and the divergence looks like a
fault in the DATA (MF-1177). A MEASUREMENT on a named object (this image,
this track) belongs in the tree as a table with date and build line: it is
evidence, not a second calculation.

Where the constant is needed anyway, it can usually be read off the oracle's
OUTPUT instead of its source — and that is stronger, because it would also
catch a fault in the oracle that a source comparison cannot see.

Named as an open case rather than passed over: the t4 contribution's
`data/nibtools_params.json` carries capacities and gap sizes that its
`uft_gcr5.c` computes alongside. On adoption it either goes, or it is
GENERATED from the code — never the other way round.

## 4. Gate 71 extended to inline scripts

`python -c`, `perl -e` and relatives. A heredoc is not the only way to send a
script through bash: measured today, a `python -c` whose argument contained
backticks had them EXECUTED as command substitution before python ever saw
it. Rejected now: a multi-line inline script, and one containing ` or $( in
DOUBLE quotes. In single quotes bash does not substitute, and a one-line `-c`
stays the normal way — the rule is precise rather than sweeping, because a
gate with false positives stops being believed.

Self-test 29 -> 39 cases. The "29" in `check_consistency.py` had drifted and
is corrected there; a hand-maintained number next to a measured one drifts
(MF-541), which is exactly what this commit is about.

## Metric

Per MF-640 none of the four release metrics moves. This is gate work on
owner instruction, and it says so rather than claiming a number.

events.title: emu: carry the media channel on every backend
events.message:
emu: carry the media channel on every backend

The unified hatari-pist fork speaks both HRDB and --pist-media, so the
media channel can no longer be a native-backend-only feature: with the
fork probed to HRDB, engageMediaDisplay's qobject_cast<EmulatorHost*>
failed and every session silently fell back to embedding. MediaServer,
the AUTH watchdog, mediaListen() and the KEY/MOUSE forwarders move to
IDebugBackend; both backends get the listen-before-spawn and
client-reset handling; engageMediaDisplay drops the cast.

Also: media sessions now export SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy for the fork.
PiST plays the guest's audio itself (the channel tees the mix to
EmuAudio), so the fork's own output device is pure cost — a real device
that stalls stops draining the sound ring, the 'system too slow' reset
then fires every few VBLs and those spans are dropped from the stream.
The dummy driver still runs the callback, keeps the ring flowing, is
never audible, and removes the double output of fork and IDE playing
the same mix.

events.title: fix(g64): a real disk read 33 of 768 sectors — the sync rule wanted 40 one bits where a 1541 needs 10, and one invalid off byte made a sector vanish without an entry (P3-663, MF-1500)
events.message:
fix(g64): a real disk read 33 of 768 sectors — the sync rule wanted 40 one bits where a 1541 needs 10, and one invalid off byte made a sector vanish without an entry (P3-663, MF-1500)

src/formats/g64/uft_g64.c had three faults that worked together:

1. find_sync() wanted 5 whole 0xFF bytes. A 1541 raises its sync flag
   after 10 one bits, and real disks carry 3-4 byte syncs. The reader now
   CALLS the rule the tree already has — gcr_find_sync()/_end() in
   src/formats/c64/uft_gcr_ops.c, definition A (0xFF followed by a byte with
   its MSB set) — instead of keeping a definition of its own (MF-1177).
2. One invalid 5-bit code anywhere in the 65 GCR groups of a data block —
   the two off bytes after the checksum included, which a 1541 does not
   check — dropped the sector with `continue`, no entry. Now every group is
   decoded nibble by nibble, invalid codes are counted in the first 64
   groups (320 GCR bytes) only, and a sector with invalid codes stays,
   marked as a data error.
3. Both checksums were recomputed, but no sector said so: without
   UFT_SECTOR_CRC_CHECKED a good sector reached the disk2 bridge as
   "unchecked" (the counterpart of P3-659). The crc flag fields now follow
   the verdict as well.

Reference for the behaviour: nibtools (rittwage/nibtools @ 0abdc11) gcr.c
find_sync() and convert_GCR_sector(), own implementation; nibconv from
the same package executed on the real disk: 768 of 768 good.

Red proof first: tests/test_g64_sync_und_offbytes.c. Three CI cases
derived in memory from tests/corpus_free/vice_c1541_35trk.g64 (no byte
moves), one local-only case on the real disk c64pp_aliensyndrome.g64
(Sega 1987, tests/corpus, gitignored):
  before: 5 of 6 red — 0 of 21 with CRC_CHECKED; 4-byte syncs: 0 of 21
          sectors; invalid off bytes: 0 of 21; a sector with one invalid
          GCR byte missing; Alien Syndrome 33 of 768
  after:  6 of 6 green; Alien Syndrome 768 of 768
  mutation matrix 5 of 5 red: 5-byte rule back; off bytes counted again;
          no CRC_CHECKED; invalid GCR not part of the verdict; sector
          dropped again

Rule choice measured, not assumed: throwaway builds with definition A and
with nibtools' own rule ("byte with LSB set, then 0xFF") both give 768 of
768 on the real disk. They differ only for a sync of one single 0xFF byte,
which no file in the corpus carries — named in the code, not decided.

uft_g64.c now needs uft_gcr_ops.c: added to the eight test targets that
compiled one without the other (each failed to link, measured); the CLI and
qmake already carry both. The 13 G64-related tests stay green.

Still open and named in P3-663: the disk ID is not checked against track
18 (nibtools does); a sector that runs over the end of the track is not
joined (no reference decides it — a 1541 has no index).

Found by the uft-c64-code package review (neue-ideen, t4).
Kennzahl: none of the four — but g64 stands on T1, and that tier was
contradicted by a real disk.

events.title: test(c64): nibscan is calibrated — and the five numbers that nearly made the comparison lie (MF-1503, P3-665)
events.message:
test(c64): nibscan is calibrated — and the five numbers that nearly made the comparison lie (MF-1503, P3-665)

MF-1502 entered `nibscan` as an oracle and said itself what was missing:
"NICHT gemessen und darum noch kein Urteil: der Differenzlauf UFT <->
nibscan auf denselben Abbildern". This is that run, per half-track.

UFT takes the GUI's own path — g64_load() / g64_get_track() /
ufm_c64_metrics_from_gcr() — not a reimplementation of it.

## Result: no divergence

  c64pp_aliensyndrome.g64   slots 40/40 · byte length 40 of 40 ·
                            half-tracks 0/0 · sectors 768 of 768
  c64pp_bountybob.g64       slots 71/71 · byte length 71 of 71 ·
                            half-tracks 35/35 · sectors 68 of 68 testable

`tests/test_c64_g64_gegen_nibscan.c`, 7 assertions, mutation matrix **5 of
5** — each mutation moves one entry of the oracle table and the expected
assertion falls. A test that cannot go red is a sham test; this tree has 32
measured instances of that (MF-596).

## A gate caught me, and it was right

The first attempt at this commit FAILED, and the reason is worth recording.
The test carried nibtools' `sector_map` (gcr.c:28-35) as an array, to check
it against `uft_cbm_sectors_per_track()`. `audit_cbm_zonen.py` tracks copies
of the CBM zone lengths with a FALLING baseline — 23 in the tree, direction
consolidation onto `uft_cbm_track_capacity()` — and mine would have been the
24th. Measured by stashing the file: 23 without it, 24 with it. So the gate
named exactly this table, and the honest answer was to drop it, not to raise
the baseline (that would be the move MF-1077 forbids).

The assertion survives, and in a better form: nibtools' zone values can be
read off its OUTPUT instead of its source. On a track whose expected sectors
nibscan misses entirely, the count of `[E2Sn]` marks IS its
`sector_map[track/2]`. `t_wo_nibscan_keinen_sollsektor_findet_...` counts
exactly the 68 tracks where that count equals `uft_cbm_sectors_per_track()`;
were one zone different, the track would drop out and 68 would be smaller.
A source-to-source check compares two tables — this compares a measurement
against a calculation.

The full table comparison did run (42 of 42 equal, tracks 36-42 included) as
a THROWAWAY measurement, and it is recorded in `docs/ORACLES.md` as such.

## Five sizes that do not carry their name

Every one of them would have produced a false finding against UFT. All five
were measured BEFORE the comparison, not explained after it. They are in the
test's header, because the next person to use this oracle needs them first:

1. nibscan's "bad GCR bytes" counts every invalid byte position of the whole
   track; UFT's `bad_gcr_count` counts at most ONCE per sync block and then
   breaks (`ufm_c64_metrics.c:117-118`). 244 022 against 208. -> P3-665.
2. The footer "N tracks with non-standard density" is not a total:
   `nibscan.c:537` counts only `track < 36*2`, while the message prints for
   every track. 42 printed, 40 counted; the difference is track 37.0 and 38.5.
3. `[E2Sn]` asks "is sector n of the zone present" (`sector_map[track/2]`);
   `sector_count` counts HEADER BLOCKS regardless of their number — the source
   comment says so at `ufm_c64_metrics.c:196-198`. On a protected disk those
   are different questions: an equality check reported **44 divergences that
   were none**.
4. Beyond track 35, "no error mark" means the OPPOSITE of "read cleanly".
   `nibscan.c:589-592`, verbatim: "everything is a CBM error above track 35".
5. A parser that does not know `(density:0!=3?)` silently discards **42 of 71**
   track lines and yields a plausible-looking table. Mine did, on the first
   attempt — caught only because `grep -c` had counted 71 beforehand.

## P3-665, registered as Fundus

`ufm_c64_scheme_detect.c:167` raises `UFM_PROT_BAD_GCR` at confidence 70 with
the text "Invalid GCR byte sequences" once `bad_gcr_count > 10` — a threshold
chosen for the byte reading, on a counter that yields blocks. Measured:
bountybob has 244 022 invalid bytes per nibscan, UFT sums 208 over 71 tracks
with a per-track maximum of 15, so exactly **1 of 71** tracks crosses the
threshold. aliensyndrome: nibscan 223, UFT 0.

Per MF-640 this moves none of the four release metrics, so it is noted, not
scheduled. It is also NOT decided to be a fault: which reading was meant is an
owner question, and swapping one unmeasured number for another is exactly what
MF-1077 forbids. What holds now is
`t_bad_gcr_zaehler_ist_keine_bytezahl` — it goes red if someone converts the
counter to bytes without moving the threshold. A lock against the silent half
change, not a fix.

Bounded against MF-1500 (peer session, `uft_g64.c`): different path, this
site untouched.

The old wording in `docs/ORACLES.md` stays quoted rather than deleted
(MF-1077) — it was right for as long as the run was missing, and the entry
should show when it stopped being missing.

events.title: feat(cli-host,app,zvm-cli): unify a loose story file's save key with a known disk release (SQ-1635)
events.message:
feat(cli-host,app,zvm-cli): unify a loose story file's save key with a known disk release (SQ-1635)

A loose story file whose own header (release+serial) matches a KNOWN,
CATALOGUED commercial release (cli_host::titles::title_for_build) now
keys its save directory exactly the way a disk-mounted copy of that
same build would (disk_story_key) -- so `zork1.z3` and an Amiga floppy
of the identical release share one save folder, since the underlying
save is genuinely compatible between them.

An unrecognized release (homebrew, competitions, unreleased/beta
builds -- anything not in known_titles.tsv) is completely unaffected:
still keyed on its filename, exactly as before. Version 6 is excluded
outright even when known -- a bare v6 file has no real disk medium,
and every blorb::medium::DiskImage value names one specific historical
machine; its InterpreterProfile resolves via ProfileSource::Fallback,
a measurably different answer from a real floppy's ProfileSource::Medium,
so claiming any one machine's bucket would be an unmeasured assertion.

cli_host::storage::known_loose_build/build_for_key are the new shared
policy functions, reused (not reimplemented) at every call site that
used to compute a StoryOrigin's build for a loose file: app's real boot
chain (host/boot.rs), the picker's row/scan-time keying (picker.rs,
kept in step so the list and a real boot can't name one game two
directories), and zvm-cli's own save path, so both front-ends keep
reaching one directory for the same game.

Going forward only, by design: an existing player's save under the old
filename key is not moved or merged -- it stays exactly where it is,
and a fresh launch of the same known release resolves to the unified
directory instead.

events.title: fix(pro): a bad phantom sector stays a phantom — it carried the error INSTEAD of UFT_SECTOR_DUPLICATE and became indistinguishable from the nominal sector (MF-1495)
events.message:
fix(pro): a bad phantom sector stays a phantom — it carried the error INSTEAD of UFT_SECTOR_DUPLICATE and became indistinguishable from the nominal sector (MF-1495)

src/formats/atari/uft_pro_plugin.c set a phantom's status with `=`:

    sec->status = bad ? UFT_SECTOR_CRC_ERROR : UFT_SECTOR_DUPLICATE;

so a phantom whose controller status is not 0xFF lost the only mark that
told it from the nominal sector with the same number. A reader counting
nominals took it for one. Now the phantom always carries DUPLICATE, and a
bad one carries the error as well.

The error bit itself keeps its meaning (UFT_SECTOR_CRC_ERROR for "status
byte is not 0xFF"): which controller bit means what in a PRO record is not
decidable from the two named hands — atari800 sio.c knows only 0xFF = good.
Named, not changed.

Red proof first: tests/test_pro_phantom_behaelt_duplikat.c builds a PRO
file after the layout test_pro_gegen_atari800 already uses (sio2arduino
prosys.html, atari800 sio.c): 720 nominal records, sector 33 with one
phantom (record 721), the phantom's status 0x10.
  before: 2 of 2 red (19 sectors, 0 duplicates, 1 error sector without
          DUPLICATE)
  after:  2 of 2 green; test_pro_gegen_atari800 stays 10 of 10
  mutation (error bit dropped, DUPLICATE kept): 1 of 2 red

Deliberately NOT changed and named in the test: whether the NOMINAL sector
of a phantom set should carry DUPLICATE as well (ATX marks every copy).
test_pro_gegen_atari800 pins the opposite; that is a separate question.

Found by the uft-atari-code package review (neue-ideen, t3); the existing
test had only GOOD phantoms and could not see it.
Kennzahl: none of the four.

events.title: fix(rtg): require agreement before adopting the aperture capability bit
events.message:
fix(rtg): require agreement before adopting the aperture capability bit

Codex review: the capability confirmation was one-sided -- a clear bit
was upgraded to set from a single (possibly corrupted) sample, and a
set bit was never confirmed at all. On old-firmware stacks a corrupted
set could enable descriptor verification where no descriptor exists,
and stable valid-looking register garbage could then be acknowledged as
a layout the firmware does not support. The capability gate now uses
the same evidence standard as the descriptor: two agreeing samples in
both directions, bounded resampling on disagreement (interleaving a
benign register access), and fail-closed when the value never
stabilizes. Healthy machines pay one extra capability register read at
init.

events.title: fix(app): stamp the resumed boot drain's observations with the restored turn, not 0 (SQ-1634)
events.message:
fix(app): stamp the resumed boot drain's observations with the restored turn, not 0 (SQ-1634)

`host/boot.rs`'s SQ-1629 Fix 2 boot drain calls apply_room_description/
apply_item_observations with state.turns before state.turns is restored
from the save (startup_turns, applied further down) — on a fresh-process
resume that's always 0, so the starting room's description and every item
its drain re-observes (mailbox, front door, …) lost their real "last seen
at move N" and came back stamped with move 0 instead.

Pass startup_turns.unwrap_or(state.turns) into those two calls directly
rather than reordering the restore earlier — narrower, and state.turns
isn't otherwise read between the two call sites.

Falsified: reverting the fix reproduces the exact reported symptom
(mailbox/front door last_seen_turn 0 instead of 6) on a real Zork I r88
resume.

events.title: fix(rtg): confirm the capability read before it disables verification
events.message:
fix(rtg): confirm the capability read before it disables verification

Codex review: a single glitched FW_CAPABILITIES read that drops the
layout bit sent the helper down the pre-aperture early exit with
verified=1 -- FindCard would then select legacy ownership and skip the
aperture acknowledgement while a later clean capability read (e.g. the
AHI driver's) could still accept generation 2 and carve the direct-ring
reservation against a layout that was never acknowledged. The helper
now re-reads the capability register and requires agreement before
taking that exit; on disagreement it sets the bit conservatively and
verifies the descriptor. The capability value is confirmed in place
(uint16_t pointer) so every caller negotiates and gates features on the
same view -- FindCard re-stores the confirmed caps, and ZZDiag prints
it as confirmed.

events.title: docs(oracles): nibscan is built and has run — and the table it goes into showed no reader a single licence, proof or purpose (MF-1502)
events.message:
docs(oracles): nibscan is built and has run — and the table it goes into showed no reader a single licence, proof or purpose (MF-1502)

Owner decision 2026-09-28: nibtools is Apache-2.0 and its capabilities are
to be adopted. First step, because the register demands it before anything
else — "Kein Oracle auf Zusicherung: ein Werkzeug, das nicht gebaut und
ausgeführt wurde, ist kein Eintrag".

## The tool

Built with MinGW 13.1.0 from `tools/uft-scout/work/nibtools` (remote
`rittwage/nibtools`), **148 106 bytes**. The build line needs
`-I<nib>/include/WINDOWS`, otherwise `mnibarch.h` is missing — recorded in
the entry, because that is the part the next person loses an hour to.
Self-report: "nibscan - Commodore disk image scanner / comparator, (C) Peter
Rittwage, Built Sep 28 2026".

Run against two real corpus images:

  tests/corpus/c64pp_bountybob.g64      half tracks 1.5 / 2.5 / 3.5 / 4.5 …,
                                        density conflict `density:0!=3?`,
                                        21 sector errors [E2S0]…[E2S20] each
  tests/corpus/c64pp_aliensyndrome.g64  7691 bytes per track throughout at
                                        density:3

Those are exactly the classes `CLAUDE.md` §5 lists as a catalogue **without
a caller** (P0-2: long tracks, half tracks, density mismatch).

The entry states what is NOT measured, in its own words: the differential
run UFT ↔ nibscan on the same images is missing, so it stands as a **tool
with proof, not a second hand**. An oracle without calibration is not a
verdict. The anchor for that is fixed — `g64` is T1 and
`tests/test_c64_protection_real_corpus.c` already uses these two files.

Licence, and it is no longer an obstacle: Apache-2.0 (owner statement
2026-09-28, second after MF-1008), and this tree's distributable
combination is GPL-3.0 (`README.md:600-618`, LIZ-4/MF-698), which
Apache-2.0 is compatible with. Duties per adoption are in the entry:
Apache-2.0 §4 (pass the NOTICE on, mark changes), MF-636 (attribution
naming the licence).

## The table had no header

Second finding, and it had to be fixed first: the tool table starts at what
was line 368 and has **no header of its own**. It abuts the `floptool`
table above it without a blank line, and that header names two columns —
so per the GFM table algorithm every cell beyond the second was DISCARDED.

Measured at a renderer (markdown-it-py), HEAD versus working tree:

  before:  11 tool rows rendered, **0** with >= 5 cells
  after:   12 tool rows rendered, **10** with >= 5 cells

So until now no reader saw the licence, the proof or the purpose of any
oracle in this file — 33 cells discarded. Same shape as MF-1494 in
`docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md`, second instance of the 22 measured there. My own
entry would have been just as invisible, which is how I found it.

events.title: fix(a2r): a flux byte 0xFF is 255 ticks added to the next — four of five places in the parser read it as the next byte alone and lost 255 ticks each (P3-657, MF-1496)
events.message:
fix(a2r): a flux byte 0xFF is 255 ticks added to the next — four of five places in the parser read it as the next byte alone and lost 255 ticks each (P3-657, MF-1496)

The A2R 2.x/3.x references define a flux value of 255 as an overflow that
is ADDED to what follows; a run of 255s keeps adding. Only the RWCP branch
of src/parsers/a2r/uft_a2r_parser.c did that. The STRM duration (and the
rpm derived from it), a2r_decode_flux(), a2r_flux_to_nibbles() and
a2r_get_raw_timings() each carried their own copy of the rule, and each
copy read "FF xx" as xx.

Now there is ONE rule, a2r_fluss_wechsel(), next to a2r_location_deuten(),
and all five places call it (MF-1177).

Red proof first: tests/test_a2r_ueberlauf_0xff.c builds an A2R2 file whose
STRM capture is FF FF 20 40 = 542 + 64 = 606 ticks.
  before: 4 of 4 red (43.875 us instead of 75.75; decode 3 samples 255, 32;
          raw timings 31875, 4000 ns; 1 nibble instead of 2)
  after:  4 of 4 green
  mutation (0xFF counts 0 instead of 255 in the helper): 4 of 4 red

test_a2r_layout does NOT notice the same mutation: none of its captures
carries 0xFF — which is also why the error never showed on real data. The
three helpers have no caller outside the parser (git grep, class P3-204);
the test calls them directly.

P3-657 BERICHTIGT: the row said the error was "only in the metadata"; it
was in four places. Still open and named in the row: the same rule stands
a second time in src/formats/a2r/uft_a2r_plugin.c:218-223 — correct, but
not shared.

Reported by the uft-a2r-code package review (neue-ideen, t3).
Kennzahl: none of the four.

events.title: fix(rtg): announce the alloc-clear protocol at init
events.message:
fix(rtg): announce the alloc-clear protocol at init

Driver half of the conditional-clear handshake (firmware PR #127):
write the REG_ZZ_ALLOC_CLEAR_PROTOCOL token once in the Z3 FindCard
branch so the firmware may honor u8_user[3] as a per-allocation
no-clear flag. Without the handshake the firmware always zero-fills,
which keeps legacy-driver ABMA_Clear semantics intact -- legacy
DrawLine leaves stale padding in that byte, so the flag alone was not
a safe cross-version signal.

events.title: fix(register): my own measurement hit the wrong class — LICENSE does state its version, the distributable combination is already GPL-3.0, and adopting nibtools has no licence obstacle (P3-662, MF-1499)
events.message:
fix(register): my own measurement hit the wrong class — LICENSE does state its version, the distributable combination is already GPL-3.0, and adopting nibtools has no licence obstacle (P3-662, MF-1499)

Correcting the entry I committed one commit ago (MF-1498). It claimed a
four-place contradiction about this project's licence and derived from it
that adopting nibtools was blocked. Both are wrong.

## What I measured wrongly

I ran `grep -i "later version" LICENSE`, measured 0 hits, and concluded
the file does not evidence its own version. Line **35** of that same file
reads `SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later` — the same statement in
normative form, in the place meant for it, alongside a pointer to the full
text and the copyright notice. The 37 lines are a deliberate short form
(header, preamble, pointer, SPDX, copyright), not a torso.

It is exactly the failure mode this same session found three times in
other people's code: a measurement that hit the wrong class. Recorded that
way in the entry, because a correction without its cause comes back.

## And the question was never open

`README.md:600-618` has laid it out since LIZ-4 / MF-698: own code
`GPL-2.0-or-later`; three AIR ports (`uft_ipf_air.c`,
`uft_kfstream_air.c`, `uft_stx_air.c`) `GPL-3.0-only`; **the distributable
combination is GPL-3.0**, verbatim "precisely because UFT's own licence
carries the `-or-later` clause".

Apache-2.0 is compatible with GPL-3 (one-way), and the combination
already is GPL-3.0. So **adopting nibtools has no licence obstacle**, and
`docs/QUARANTINE.md:55` now carries that: its reasoning ("Apache-2.0 ist
mit GPL-2 ebenso unvereinbar wie GPL-3-only") tests against
GPL-2-**only**, which this project explicitly is not. The sentence stays
quoted, because it would be right for a GPL-2-only project — deleting it
is not a fix (MF-1077).

The *reason* is dissolved, not the diligence. Per adopted capability:
Apache-2.0 §4 (pass the NOTICE on, mark every change), MF-636
(attribution naming the licence — "Based on X" alone does not do it),
MF-695 (pick the channel: port / clean-room / helper process / oracle,
not wholesale).

## What remains, and it is small and real

No copy of any licence text ships with this tree — only a link, while GPL
§1 wants a copy with the program, and for a GPL-3.0 combination it would
be the GPL-3 text. Measured: exactly **1** full licence text exists in the
tree, `src/a8rawconv/COPYING`, which is foreign. The README badge also
says "License: GPL-2.0", too low for the combination. That is an owner
decision about a file, not about a version — the version stands.

Measured: `grep -n SPDX LICENSE` → line 35. SPDX headers across
`git ls-files '*.c' '*.h'`: 212 `GPL-2.0-or-later`, 52 `MIT`, 3
`GPL-3.0-only`. Full licence texts in tree: 1, foreign.

events.title: impossamole: 97th pass -- disassemble the x=192 wall, it's not tile collision
events.message:
impossamole: 97th pass -- disassemble the x=192 wall, it's not tile collision

$00c450 checks every frame whether the hero's x exceeds 192; if so it computes
min(x-192, 2) as a shared correction delta ($1883c) and arms a gate ($227f1
bit 3). $00bb3a-bb68 then subtracts that delta from every object-array slot
flagged 30(A0)=$00ff (hero and every hazard checked all carry that flag),
independent of any tile check.

Live-confirmed against the disassembly, not just read: a genuine jump that
passes its own tile-forward gate (hits: entered 15 times, its add reached 7)
and writes x=194 gets pulled straight back to 192 by $00bb5c a few thousand
steps later, every time, across four consecutive real hits.

This is the actual root cause behind all three of the 96th pass's failed
escapes -- no jump timing or shape can ever cross x=192 on this screen. Real
leads now: a route that never needs x>192 here (the left tree's ladder, never
tried from a higher entry point), or confirming whether this screen is meant
to scroll at this trigger and the emulator is missing the matching
background/tile shift ($1883c has only one found reader).
