events.title: docs(register): nibtools is Apache-2.0 — settled, recorded, not to be raised again; what blocks adopting it is a 37-line file of our own (P3-661, P3-662, MF-1498)
events.message:
docs(register): nibtools is Apache-2.0 — settled, recorded, not to be raised again; what blocks adopting it is a 37-line file of our own (P3-661, P3-662, MF-1498)

Owner decision 2026-09-28, second statement after MF-1008: rittwage/nibtools
is Apache-2.0, and its capabilities are to be adopted. That question is
closed and is not to be put up again. `docs/QUARANTINE.md:55` now carries
the confirmation in those words.

The contradicting observation is kept, not deleted (MF-1077): the clone
`tools/uft-scout/work/nibtools` (remote `rittwage/nibtools`) holds a
complete GPL-3, 674 lines, and "Apache" appears 0 times in it, while
`nibtools-extra/LICENSE` is 229 bytes, dated 2026-09-10 (every other file
in that archive: 2024-11-30) and reads "licensed under the Apache License,
Version 2.0. See the LICENSE file for details." — a self-reference,
because it IS that file. It stays on record so the same find does not
come back as an open question. It does not change the decision.

## P3-662 — what actually blocks adoption is ours

`LICENSE` carries the header "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE, Version 2, June
1991" and has **37 lines**; the licence text is missing (GPL-2 runs to
about 340) and the phrase "or any later version" does not appear in it.
The source files say `GPL-2.0-or-later` **212 times**; the README says
"GPL-2", "GPLv2+" and "GPLv2".

That decides the case, and in the helpful direction: Apache-2.0 is
incompatible with GPL-2-**only** but compatible with GPL-3 (one-way), and
a GPL-2-**or-later** work may be combined under GPL-3. This tree's own
file headers say or-later 212 times — so adoption is open on the merits;
it rests on a licence file that does not evidence its own version.

One step, and it is cheap: bring `LICENSE` to the full text of whichever
version is meant to apply. This is not legal advice — it is a statement
about the files in this tree; choosing the version is the owner's call.
After that, in order: register `nibscan` in `docs/ORACLES.md` (it is built
and has run, just not entered — `QUARANTINE.md:60`), then pick the channel
per capability under MF-695 rather than adopting wholesale, then set
attributions with named licence under MF-636. Nothing has to be unwound in
`uft_gcr_ops.c` / `uft_d64_g64.c`: `QUARANTINE.md:245`/`:246` already
found them independent despite their "Based on nibtools" headers.

## P3-661 — a detector that never says no

`freezer_detect()` (`src/formats/c64/uft_freezer.c:17`) tells five C64
freezer cartridges apart. Three of its five signatures are the INITIALS of
the product name: `0xFC 0x03` for Final Cartridge III, `'S','S'` for Super
Snapshot, `'N','P'` for Nordic Power. The only structural check is
`data[4] & 0x20` — with its own comment "Bit 5 always set", i.e. the bit
that is always set in the 6502 status register: a coin toss.

Calibrated against the function itself, built with MinGW 13.1.0:

  2000 random buffers of 67 000 bytes -> 50.3 % "Action Replay",
                                         49.7 % "Generic Snapshot",
                                         0 % "Unknown"
  2000 random buffers of 64-68 KB     -> 10.0 % AR, 90.0 % Generic,
                                         again 0 % "Unknown"
  all-zero buffer                     -> "Generic Snapshot"

Comment and code also disagree: the comment says "AR snapshots are
typically 66816-67328 bytes", the code checks `66816 … 67584`; 67 329 and
67 457 bytes are measured as "Action Replay".

`C64FRZ` is known to nobody but UFT: `gh search code` returns 3 hits, all
three in this repo. And `tests/test_freezer.c:161` does
`memcpy(data, "C64FRZ", 6)` — the test builds the bytes the reader
expects, proving only that the reader understands its own writer.

Related to P3-660 but a different defect: there a signature is wrong, here
the detector says yes to everything. So the freeze option reads
differently — return `FREEZER_TYPE_UNKNOWN` **with a finding**, which
makes the "no" branch reachable at all.

## P3-660 — the cause is proven, and it is not invention

libhxcfe has `static const char plug_id[]="HXCSTREAM";`
(`hxcstream_loader.c:505`, in `HxCStream_libGetPluginInfo`), beside
`plug_desc` "HxC Stream Loader" and `plug_ext` "hxcstream". `HXCSTREAM` is
the loader's **plugin id**, not the file's magic — conflate the two and
you build exactly this reader. That changes the fix: the format
description is present and readable, the error is one line.

Measured on 16 real Pauline captures from an external contribution: **16
of 16 carry `CHKH`, 0 contain `HXCSTREAM` anywhere**.

## Reported back to the contribution's author, not registered

`memmem` (a GNU extension MinGW lacks) breaks that contribution's Windows
build; this tree already has a shim in
`include/uft/compat/uft_platform_base.h` with 8 callers. And
`system("./build/nibconv …")` reaches `cmd.exe` on Windows, which answers
"Der Befehl \".\" ist entweder falsch geschrieben"; this tree has **0**
such call sites. Measured before judging, because a deviation is first
only a deviation (MF-1177 rule 1): the same nibconv invoked directly
returns rc 0 and 174 848 bytes, and with a Windows path all five of that
contribution's test runs go green. Neither moves one of the four release
metrics, so neither is registered here (MF-640).

events.title: Run the 6502 on a cycle-exact bus and emulate the C64's chips cycle by cycle (#357)
events.message:
Run the 6502 on a cycle-exact bus and emulate the C64's chips cycle by cycle (#357)

Replaces the C64's per-instruction timing with a cycle-exact model:
every CPU cycle is a real bus access, and the VIC-II, CIAs and SID see
each read and write at the cycle it happens. Merged here from 51
reviewed PRs (#305–#358).

**CPU**
- Every CPU cycle is a real bus access, including dummy reads and
writes, verified against the SingleStepTests corpus.
- Interrupts are sampled at the cycle the 6502 polls them. An IRQ
released in the poll cycle is still taken, and an NMI can hijack an IRQ
or BRK entry.
- Added the undocumented opcodes LXA, ANE, SHA, SHX, SHY and TAS
(including page-crossing and RDY behaviour). ARR now runs in the stable
profile.
- Undriven 6510 port bits keep the charge they were last driven to.

**VIC-II**
- The VIC-II stalls the CPU on bad lines and during sprite DMA.
- Counters, the border flip-flops, DEN, display/idle state and the
sprite counters are followed cycle by cycle.
- A new default pixel generator follows the graphics sequencer pixel by
pixel, so mid-line mode, scroll, colour and pointer changes land at the
correct pixel.
- Sprite X compare, priority, collisions, Y-expansion and crunching
behave as the chip does.
- The previous generator is kept as the faster "legacy" option.

**CIA and SID**
- The 6526 timer pipeline, interrupt control register timing and
interrupt output are modelled.
- The VIC bank comes from CIA 2's port pins and changes on the cycle
after the write.
- SID register writes and OSC3/ENV3 reads happen on their exact cycle,
and reads return the data-bus latch.

**Tools and docs**
- A VICE test-program harness (`tools/vice-testprogs`) runs VICE's
VICII, CIA, CPU and interrupt test programs against their reference
pictures and results.
- The debug adapter and monitor show the VIC-II raster position and gain
`run until <condition>` and `run raster <line> [cycle]`.
- New samples were added, along with new Download & Run entries (Demus
Interruptus, Krestage 3, Chars Sucks, Robot - Not Human).
- A new page, `docs/systems/c64/accuracy.md`, describes what is emulated
and its known limitations.

**Results**
- VICE test programs: CPU, interrupts and Lorenz 413/437; VICII 226/274;
CIA 31/104. Most of the CIA failures come from features that aren't
modelled, such as TOD, SDR, CNT and cascade; `accuracy.md` lists them.
- Performance, measured on Giana Sisters (render and audio, Apple M1): a
frame takes 1.32–1.34 ms against 1.03 ms on master (+28–29%). About 0.07
ms is the cycle-exact CPU, bus and chips, spread over many small costs;
the rest is the per-pixel sequencer. The legacy pixel generator keeps
the increase at 6–7%. Details in
`benchmarks/Highbyte.DotNet6502.Benchmarks/RESULTS.md`.
- The published AOT Avalonia Browser build renders in about 7–8 ms per
frame on an M1.

events.title: fix(atari-dos2): a DOS 2.5 file with flag bit 0 is a file, not the end of the directory — 6 of 24 files were missing; and the VTOC2 bitmap is read and written at byte 84, not 0 (P3-65, P3-68, MF-1493)
events.message:
fix(atari-dos2): a DOS 2.5 file with flag bit 0 is a file, not the end of the directory — 6 of 24 files were missing; and the VTOC2 bitmap is read and written at byte 84, not 0 (P3-65, P3-68, MF-1493)

Two faults in the Atari DOS 2 reader, found by the uft-atari-code review
at a real DOS 2.5 disk (475.atr). That disk is not used in the tree: it
holds third-party programs and there is no redistribution right. The
reference is the same author the tree already cites for MF-835: Joe
Allen, atari-tools, readme.md and atr.c (commit 835d5a6f; lsatr was
executed by the review).

1. Directory. MF-835 took "flag bits 6 and 7 both 0" from the readme's
   DOS 2.0s section. The same source computes differently in its code:
     #define FLAG_IN_USE_ED 0x41
     file:             d->flag & FLAG_IN_USE_ED
     end of directory: !(d->flag & (FLAG_IN_USE_ED | FLAG_DELETED))
   DOS 2.5 marks files in the extended area with bit 0 (seen as 0x03).
   With the 2.0s rule such a file counted as the END of the directory,
   and is_valid (bit 6 only) called it no file. At 475.atr 6 of 24
   files, 41 168 bytes, were missing; lsatr lists all 24. Now
   DIR_FLAG_IN_USE_ED (0x41) is the one mask for both the end mark and
   is_valid. A 0x02 entry stays an end mark; test_atari_dir_past_end is
   unchanged and green.

2. VTOC2. The readme, DOS 2.5 section, says:
   - "0..83: Repeat VTOC bitmap for sectors 48..719 (write these, do not
     read them)";
   - "84..121: Bitmap for sectors 720..1023";
   - "122..123: free count".
   dos2_read_vtoc() copied the bitmap from byte 0, i.e. from the repeat
   (at 475.atr 23 of 304 bits differed). dos2_write_vtoc() wrote it to
   byte 0 as well, over the repeat. Now it reads at 84 and writes at 84,
   plus the repeat 0..83 taken from VTOC bytes 16..99. The constants
   VTOC2_BITMAP_OFFSET / _BYTES live in atari_dos.h.

Red first: tests/test_atari_dos25_verzeichnis_und_vtoc2.c builds an
enhanced-density disk in memory. It was 4 of 4 red before (visible 1,
entry 0x03 no file; 720/721/1023 all "used"; repeat overwritten); after
the fix 4/4. Mutation matrix 5/5. The 24 atari/atr/xfd/fs tests stay
green.

P3-65 (1) and P3-68 are marked BERICHTIGT, not rewritten away:
- (1) was listed as "rule base, no code" but was a code fault;
- the b6/b7 end-mark rule was the DOS 2.0s rule only.

Kennzahl: none of the four. The DOS 2 reader has no product caller
(inventory, not capability); its FS tier could be raised with lsatr as
a differential oracle.

events.title: docs(register): a reader can look complete, lack a door, and read a format its alleged producer never wrote — and the register that records it showed no reader its status (P3-660, MF-1494)
events.message:
docs(register): a reader can look complete, lack a door, and read a format its alleged producer never wrote — and the register that records it showed no reader its status (P3-660, MF-1494)

Two things, found one after the other, the second while writing down the
first.

## P3-660 — readers for a format nobody writes

Measured on two cases, each held against the source of the WRITER, not
against its output alone:

(1) `src/formats/flux/uft_hxcstream.c` demands the text magic
    `"HXCSTREAM"`. HxC's own loader checks a 32-bit signature instead:
    `#define HXCSTREAM_HEADERSIGN 0x484B4843` with the comment
    `// CHKH - 0x43, 0x48, 0x4B, 0x48` (`hxcstream_format.h:3,10`,
    checked at `hxcstream_loader.c:106`). Measured on 342 real files
    (176 from a Pauline dump of a damaged Oric disk, 166 from an Amiga
    set): all carry `CHKH`, 0 contain `HXCSTREAM` anywhere; UFT reads
    0 of 4 (probe no, `_read` rc=-25). This is NOT a dialect case —
    writer source and output agree, only UFT deviates.

(2) `src/formats/flux/gwraw.c:59` demands `memcmp(magic,"GWFLUX",6)`.
    Greaseweazle 1.23 has 33 output formats in `src/greaseweazle/image/`,
    none of them a GWF container, and `GWFLUX` appears 0 times in both
    cloned gw trees (source + firmware).

Origin measured, not guessed: `uft_hxcstream.c` comes from commit
`639654a8` (2026-04-10, "feat: implement all 7 remaining missing format
parsers"), which created 8 parser files. 7 of 8 have no source in the
header, no plugin door and no corpus image; the eighth is `uft_86f.c`,
whose wiring MF-961 REJECTED as a bet. `gwraw.c` comes from the v4.1.0
squash `4d622192` and likewise names no source. Both are in
`docs/orphan_baseline.txt` — the baseline says "nobody calls this", not
"there would be nothing worth calling".

It is the class of the five fabricated parsers (FMT-2/3/10/11/12),
undetected only because unreachable: what has no door fails no test. The
difference from "reader without a door" (MF-930/P3-204) matters — there,
capability waits behind a missing door; here, wiring it would be damage.

The entry carries the CHOICE per file, not a verdict (MF-1077):
prove / freeze / withdraw, each with its cost. Freezing means a REFUSAL
that carries a finding, not a silent `return 0`, and the red proof stays
as a test — inverted, so it checks that the reader REJECTS the invented
magic and names the measurement. Otherwise the evidence disappears with
the rewrite.

Not measured: the magics of the other five (`dart`, `edd`, `ndif`,
`aaru`, `savedskf`) were not held against any writer source, only their
three columns.

## The register showed no reader its status

While placing the entry I got the cell count wrong, looked at the
neighbours, and found the table header names two columns while 120 of its
146 rows write four (`ID | finding | evidence | status`). Per the GFM
table algorithm cells beyond the header width are DISCARDED — so the
column that distinguishes "offen" from "behoben" reached nobody.

Measured against a renderer, not quoted from a specification
(markdown-it-py, table rule enabled), with the counter-probe that a wide
enough header shows all cells:

  before the header fix:  653 register rows rendered, 0 with >= 4 cells
  after  the header fix:  653 register rows rendered, 628 with >= 4 cells

One line. The remaining 25 are older entries that have no evidence/status
cell at all, which is not a defect.

Two of my own numbers on the way there were wrong and are corrected here:
"4 visible" and "560 visible" both came from asking whether the status
text appears anywhere in the rendered output — which also matches rows
rendered as running text. Counting at the `<td>` blocks gives 0 -> 628.

Repo-wide the same shape exists in 22 tables / 368 cells beyond their
header width, among them generated files (`docs/VERIFICATION_TIERS.md`),
which must be fixed in the generator, not the document. Not touched here;
it moves none of the four release metrics and is offered as a proposal,
including the gate shape (falling baseline, like Tor 57).

events.title: fix(rtg): require an agreeing re-read before accepting a valid descriptor
events.message:
fix(rtg): require an agreeing re-read before accepting a valid descriptor

Codex review: a glitch can land on the OTHER valid profile for the
same board size -- the generation byte is one bit apart between
0x5a01.... and 0x5a02....., so a corrupted generation byte negotiates
as VALID for the wrong generation. Trusting the first valid sample
could write the 0xa501 acknowledgement to generation-2 firmware (layout
never activates) or make AHI carve a direct-ring reservation over the
live host window. A valid sample is now accepted only when an
independent re-read agrees; disagreement keeps sampling within the
attempt budget. Healthy machines pay one extra register pair per boot.

events.title: Install AmigaOS 3.5 and 3.9 from the CD, with the BoingBags
events.message:
Install AmigaOS 3.5 and 3.9 from the CD, with the BoingBags

Choosing to install a release booted an emulator with the disc attached
and left the installation to be run by hand. The installation is now
made here and written into the open partition, the way the PiStorm
imager makes it.

The layout of each release is the one its Installer script uses. The
layers are resolved by name first, so each file is written once from
the newest layer that supplies it. A drive with a system on it keeps
everything the release does not carry.

The BoingBag update packs are found inside the archives supplied and
applied oldest first. BoingBags 1 and 2 for 3.9 keep their fixes in an
encrypted archive, which is applied by running the pack's own Updater
under FS-UAE and collecting what it writes. Where that cannot be run,
the fixes left out are named.

Two faults found on the way are fixed. A numeric protection value was
read as hexadecimal text, so a pure command lost its execute bit, which
also affected the floppy Workbench install. The LHA reader took an
Amiga file comment to be part of the name and refused the archive.

Running the disc's own installer under emulation is kept as a separate
choice in the same dialog.

events.title: fix(rtg): retry glitched descriptors that temporarily look legacy
events.message:
fix(rtg): retry glitched descriptors that temporarily look legacy

Codex review: a corrupted HIGH halfword breaks the descriptor magic,
so zz_z2_aperture_negotiate() returns ZZ_APERTURE_LEGACY, not INVALID
-- and the recovery loop only retried INVALID. FindCard would then
silently install the legacy layout on a matched modern stack and skip
the aperture acknowledgement (wrong memory layout instead of a clean
failure), and one non-magic read mid-retry abandoned the remaining
attempts. Retry any non-VALID result while the firmware advertises
ZZ_FW_CAP_Z2_APERTURE_LAYOUT; without the capability there is no
descriptor to recover, so the single read stands.

stateChanged it can emit synchronously before m_io is assigned, which

fix(rtg): write the surface-clear flag directly, bypassing the byte cache

Codex review: byte cache slot 3 belongs to GFXDATA_BYTE_MINTERM, and
u8_user[3] doubles as the DrawLine line-padding byte written directly
by DrawLine. Routing the ALLOC clear flag through writeGfxDataU8
aliased the minterm slot (a later equal minterm write would be
suppressed as "cached") and let stale DrawLine paddings suppress the
flag write itself - an allocation without ABMA_Clear could still be
zero-filled, or a requested clear skipped. Write the byte directly,
like the other u8_user[2]/[3] command fields.

events.message:
The drivers' waits, the 0x28 protection trap, the invulnerability loop

Export 4 (both drivers) stops the three looping sounds and then GAME.EXE waits
until the sound effects are done: ADL:0x33D over all five slots with no
counter, ROL:0x55D over slots 1-4 with a 200-pass counter that never runs out
(its retry jnz lands above the reload). ROL's export 12 holds the game while a
fade runs down, or for the full 300 retraces while music simply plays. The port
now freezes its ticks (menus and attract tape included) for those waits and
runs what followed each call afterwards: level init and entry, shop exit,
respawn, game over (the fade waits for the jingle), title loop, tally.

Id 0x28's check in every driver sets GAME's DOS exit code DS:0x11A to 5, which
GODS.EXE reports as "Protection failure.", when DS:0xEA is nonzero. Nothing
writes DS:0xEA (static, plus a live write watch), and EXIT sets the code to 1
anyway: modelled as data (protectionExitCode), it cannot fire.

The shield's aura loop 0x0280 now plays from the potion (pickup or shop, both
through DS:0xD8B8) and at respawn, and stops when the aura runs out (CS:0xA9AA)
or at any export 4. Bit-7 ids loop and are refused while held on the ADL path.

Bug fixes found on the way: the shield, freeze and giant-jump potions never
took effect (their timers went into a spread copy of fx); and a level start
granted 85 ticks of invulnerability the original does not (the loader clears
DS:0x172 and parks DS:0x19C at 0xFFFF; PROVEN live at a world-2 entry).

events.title: RD1: one frame per game_period, and the ST's gameplay rate (40 ms, 25 steps/s)
events.message:
RD1: one frame per game_period, and the ST's gameplay rate (40 ms, 25 steps/s)

Two findings, from the web build's timing work (wasm.md §8):

1. The native frame timer ran at about HALF the period. game_loop did
     tmx = tm; tm = sys_gettime(); tmx = tm - tmx;
     if (tmx < game_period) sys_sleep(game_period - tmx);
   tm is taken BEFORE the sleep, so the next measured interval includes that
   sleep: frame n sleeps (period - d), frame n+1 sees d' = period - d + work.
   Frames alternate between a full sleep and none, averaging one frame per
   (period + work) / 2. Measured: the demo ran ~25.7 gameplay steps/s at
   GAME_PERIOD 75 (nominal 13.3). The web build, which schedules frames
   properly, therefore played at half the native speed.

2. The ST original runs gameplay at one main-loop iteration per 2 VBLs at
   50 Hz = 25 steps/s = 40 ms, measured in Hatari (kb/hatari.md 2026-09-28):
   606 of 608 iterations standing, 425 walking, took exactly 2 VBLs
   (flip_screen_buffer waits for a tick, vsync_wait for the next, as
   algo-system.md's main loop at 0x4DCCE predicts). Room redraws and the
   respawn take longer.

Change (rd1):
- game.c game_loop, native path: the next frame is due one game_period after
  the previous one was due (tm += game_period after the sleep); a late frame
  restarts the schedule from now, with no catching up. The web path
  (__EMSCRIPTEN__) is unchanged.
- game.h: GAME_PERIOD 40 on PLATFORM_ST (the measured ST rate). PLATFORM_PC:
  38, i.e. the pace the port had (75 run at about half) -- the PC original was
  not measured.
- The other periods were tuned under the same half-speed timer, so they are
  halved to keep the pace they had (not measured on the ST): SCROLL_PERIOD
  24 -> 12 (scroller.h), IMAIN_PERIOD 50 -> 25 (scr_imain.c), game over 50 ->
  25 (scr_gameover.c). The fades use period/2 of these and follow.

Checks (WSL, SDL with dummy drivers):
- demo at default speed: 23.9 logic steps/s over 40 s of the -trace (was
  ~25.7); the trace counts CTRL_ACTION steps only, so scroll frames and room
  redraws come out of it -- the ST walking run gave 24.0 the same way;
- -demo -speed 2 -trace: byte-identical to the previous native trace over
  37013 lines (the whole game + the start of the second loop) -- timing only;
- clean builds: warnings ST 229 / PC 230 (230 / 231 before: the old timer
  line's warning is gone).

events.title: fix(rtg): verify the Z2 aperture descriptor read; pass ABMA_Clear through
events.message:
fix(rtg): verify the Z2 aperture descriptor read; pass ABMA_Clear through

Two driver halves of the pre-v2.8.1 regression fixes (firmware side in
the paired zz9000-firmware PR).

The Z2 register bank historically served reads without a data-out
setup window before DTACK, so a marginal bus can corrupt one halfword
of a back-to-back pair - observed as the aperture descriptor reading
0x5a020000 (HI valid, LO zero), intermittently, re-rolled per
power-up. FindCard then aborted and the card advertised no RTG modes.
zz9000_read_z2_aperture_verified() re-reads (up to 4 attempts, benign
register access interleaved to break the failing bus pattern) while
the descriptor negotiates INVALID, and is now used by FindCard, the
AHI driver, and ZZDiag. ZZDiag also prints the raw descriptor and a
Z2ApertureReadGlitch line when the raw and recovered values differ,
turning repeated runs into a glitch-rate measurement. This is the
safety net for v2.8.0-era bitstreams already deployed; the root-cause
RTL fix rides the firmware PR.

ZZ_AllocBitMap now maps P96's ABMA_Clear tag onto the firmware's new
conditional surface clear: u8_user[3]=1 when the caller did not ask
for a cleared bitmap, 0 when it did. graphics.library AllocBitMap
promises no clearing, and the previous unconditional zero-fill turned
re-allocated smart-refresh save buffers into black window restores
(Z3 reports: background Workbench windows lose their content after
quitting apps; resizing repaints). Older firmware ignores the byte and
keeps clearing, so no version combination changes BMF_CLEAR behavior.

events.title: impossamole: 95th pass -- retract the 94th's timing dodge, it never fired
events.message:
impossamole: 95th pass -- retract the 94th's timing dodge, it never fired

The "safe, zero-damage timing dodge past slot 12" was a measurement
artifact: for five of its nine trial delays (250,000-450,000), the
kbd ff/kbd 09 trigger's 15,000-step hold was shorter than the game's
own ~24,000-step joystick poll cycle, so the packet never registered.
A watch on the jump routine's own frame counter ($1a5c4) shows zero
activity for those five delays and 17 writes for every delay confirmed
to fire -- "hero still at the takeoff spot, undamaged" was simply
nothing having happened, not a completed round-trip arc.

Holding 30,000 steps (> one full poll cycle) makes the jump fire
reliably even at delay 300,000, but slot 8 still catches the landing
eventually (confirmed to two further hits past the first 700,000-step
window) -- no delay/hold combination found so far survives the
crossbar rest spot indefinitely. Item 3 (dodge the guard) is reopened,
not closed, and pass94_dodge_item_landed.snap is not a valid resume
point: it is state-for-state identical to pass90_wall_192.snap.

Also answers "what decides landing height": there isn't a variable
height -- a real jump always lands at y=112; y=144 only ever meant no
jump ran. Folds the input-hold-vs-poll-cycle trap into CLAUDE.md
alongside the existing bp/watch-window trap it sits next to.

events.title: fix(app,mapper,zvm): item tracking — container identity, Vanished's location, pick-up turn, carried-and-destroyed, and scope-wide scenery false positives (SQ-1632)
events.message:
fix(app,mapper,zvm): item tracking — container identity, Vanished's location, pick-up turn, carried-and-destroyed, and scope-wide scenery false positives (SQ-1632)

Fix 1: ItemLocation::Room and ObservedItemLocation::RoomNested both grow a
`container: Option<ItemKey>` so a host can say "in the brown sack", not
just "somewhere in this room, nested". Threaded from GameSession's
zvm_item_observations, which now derives it via zvm::world::WorldModel::
real_container_in_room (Fix 5). Glulx/Scott have no containment model to
ask and always report None.

Fix 2: ItemLocation::Vanished grows `{ room: RoomId, turn: u32 }` — the
last place and moment an item was confirmed present before it went
missing, not just the bare fact of vanishing.

Fix 3: ItemRecord grows `carried_since_turn: Option<u32>`, stamped once
on the not-carried -> carried transition, left alone on every turn the
item stays held, and cleared back to None the moment it's seen not
carried again (dropped, or vanished while held).

Fix 4: note_items_absent's sweep now also checks items last known Carried
against this turn's observations, not only direct room sightings —
something eaten/burned/destroyed while held is marked Vanished (at the
room the player is CURRENTLY standing in) instead of staying Carried
forever.

Fix 5: the quest's own real repro (Zork I r88 — open mailbox, take
leaflet, take mailbox, north, east, open window, enter window, open sack,
take bottle, west, take lamp, take sword, east, turn on lamp, up, take
rope, down, drop bottle, look) recorded local-global/shared scenery
("white house", "board", "stairs", "chimney", "kitchen window", "boarded
window") as RoomNested in every room it happened to be visible from,
reading as a portable item silently relocating itself. Found a reliable
structural signal, not a name-based guess: zvm::world::WorldModel's own
doc already states a local-global object is never a child of the room it
appears in (local_globals filters by `get_parent(o) == holder`, the
shared bucket, never the room) — confirmed independently for Zork I via
`real_container_in_room`, which walks an object's REAL parent chain
upward and answers None when it never reaches the room. Objects with no
real containment relationship are excluded from item tracking entirely
rather than surfaced as nested-with-no-container.

Every fix falsified: reverting each behavior change (Fix 1's container
capture, the graph-level Vanished/carried_since_turn/carried-sweep
branches, Fix 5's real_container_in_room filter) reproduces the exact
reported symptom against a real test before being restored.

Real fixtures: zork1-r88-s840726.z3 (mailbox/leaflet for Fix 1, the
quest's own scenery repro for Fix 5) and minizork's world-model fixture
for zvm's own real_container_in_room unit tests.

Judgment calls: ItemLocation::Room/RoomNested gained a field rather than
a new variant, keeping the direct/nested distinction unchanged;
Vanished's room/turn are the LAST-seen place, not origin_room/origin_turn
(a host wanting "where it started" already has those); Fix 4's sweep
stamps the room the player is standing in now (not the item's origin) as
where a carried item vanished FROM, since that's where it was last WITH
them.

events.title: fix(dmk,sap,jv3,stx,fdi,d77): the last six producers record their CRC finding where the model reads it — all eleven from the P3-659 measurement are now done (P3-659, MF-1492)
events.message:
fix(dmk,sap,jv3,stx,fdi,d77): the last six producers record their CRC finding where the model reads it — all eleven from the P3-659 measurement are now done (P3-659, MF-1492)

Third slice of P3-659. Each reader gets the meaning its own source
gives:

- DMK and SAP recompute the data CRC themselves, so "checked" is
  something they can prove. Both now set UFT_SECTOR_CRC_CHECKED, for the
  good sector as well as the bad one. Before, only crc_ok changed, which
  the disk2 bridge does not read, and both came out as "unchecked".
- JV3: Tim Mann, the format's author: "JV3_ERROR, if set, indicates that
  the sector should show a data CRC error when read." A statement from
  the writer's side, the strongest form of Spec.
- STX: the Pasti FDC flag is a condition, not one value: "CRC error
  (data if RNF=0, ID if RNF=1)" (STX_SF_CRC_ERR, uft_stx_air.c).
- FDI (ZX): three facts that were one. Per SAMdisk fdi.cpp (read):
  - flag 0x40 is "no data": now not readable;
  - a clear CRC-ok bit for the size is a data CRC error;
  - data past the end of the file is neither: now truncated.
- D77 was among the eleven measured producers but in no slice. As the
  D88 container of the FM-7, its status byte now means what it means in
  D88: 0xB0 data CRC, 0xA0 ID CRC, 0x10 deleted, 0xE0 not readable
  (MAME; hxcfe executed in MF-1480). Before, any non-zero byte became
  set_crc(false).

Red first: tests/test_crc_befund_erreicht_modell.c, through the bridge.
DMK, SAP, JV3 and STX use committed corpus files with ONE finding
injected into sector R1, and R2 as the control; FDI and D77 are
synthetic.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DMK | `UU` | `BG` |
| SAP | `UU` | `BG` |
| JV3 | `UU` | `BU` |
| STX | `UU` | `BU` |
| FDI | `UUU` | `UBM` |
| D77 | `UUUU` | `UBIM` |

Now 11/11 cases. Mutation matrix 8/8, plus D77 run old against new.
Full run 587/587.

All eleven producers from the P3-659 measurement are converted. Still
open, named in P3-659:
- the STX "CRC with RNF = ID" branch is untested, because the reader
  skips RNF sectors without data;
- a status bit for "ID mismatch" (D64 code 0B) and the D64 write codes;
- D88/D77 status 0xF0;
- PRO, reported by the uft-atari-code review and not measured: every
  status other than 0xFF becomes CRC_ERROR.

events.title: Sound quality as a hidden option, experimental=true, and no audition
events.message:
Sound quality as a hidden option, experimental=true, and no audition

sound_quality=normal|high sets the rate the STE's voice device mixes
the modules and the sampled effects at: 6258Hz, as before and still
the default, or 12517Hz for twice the treble. It costs twice the
mixing time, measured with the modules playing (Hatari, cycle-exact):
the intro's longest scene took 43% longer to draw on an 8MHz STE, and
a Mega STE at 16MHz showed 267 of its 370 frames instead of 326. So it
stays hidden and off, with no line in RS.CFG, until it has earned one.

experimental=true, also hidden, shows work in progress - for now a
Sound Quality line on the title's Options, where the STE's sampled
sound is on. Switching it closes the voice device and opens it again
at the new rate; that takes the music and the sequencer's tick with
it, so the menu track starts again, and the idle pause starts afresh
on the new device. RS.LOG says which rate the device opened at.

sfx_audition goes: it played each effect's sample and its YM version
in turn to set the recipes' levels, and those are done.

Checked in Hatari: an STE and a Mega STE open at 6258Hz by default,
sound_quality=high opens at 12517Hz, experimental=true shows the line
and switching reopens the device and restarts the music, and a plain
ST shows no line and plays on into level 1.

events.title: The Roland path: per-world music, the MT-32 bank, ROL's SFX allocator, the 0x35E layer
events.message:
The Roland path: per-world music, the MT-32 bank, ROL's SFX allocator, the 0x35E layer

ROL.EXE modelled from its bytes (audio/rol-driver.js): the 74-entry sound id
remap (CS:0x6F4), the per-blob voices/variant/volume records (CS:0x634), the
5-slot priority allocator, its own random variants (CS:0x5FF; no game-table
draw), and the music exports 6-12 with the 50 Hz fade (two steps a tick).
PPLAYER's MPU output path (roland-sequencer.js): channel + BL, velocity scaled
by the AH=6 volume, pressure never sent, looping on bit 7.

PTITLE.RL ends in a full MT-32 bank (64 custom timbres "xplo1", "Heartbeat",
..., 128 patches, rhythm setup) that INTROV uploads; mt32-bank.js parses it and
mt32-synth.js plays a Web Audio stand-in from the real timbre parameters (PCM
partials and ROM timbres are approximations).

Music call sites wired in main.js: level load (+31 ticks), the guardian fight
(PGODSRLF), its end, the password shop (PGODSRLG), respawn dip/fade, tally
mute, game over, the title loop. Sound picker (AdLib default, ?sound=roland).
Intro under Roland plays PTITLE.RL with INTROV's DS:0x195 == 2 waits.

The DS:0x35E brackets (System A, the world-1 statue, the PAT driver) now play
0x0E49 after a kill and instead of 0x0F22 on contact; ADL drops 0x49 (its
signed id gate, now explicit). ADL's own variants (0x22 -> blob +0..2 etc.)
now pick the blob from the random word it already drew.

Also plays the missing level-start (0x7F12) and game-over (0x6413) sounds.
Suite: 2179 assertions + 43 notes, all pass; attract demos exact (AdLib).

events.title: impossamole: 94th pass correction -- the "delayed hit" was slot 8, not slot 12
events.message:
impossamole: 94th pass correction -- the "delayed hit" was slot 8, not slot 12

Reading A0 at the three previously-fatal delays (200,000; 500,000-550,000;
600,000) instead of assuming it was slot 12 catching up late shows a
different object, $1a64a -- the type=2 hazard the 83rd/84th passes spotted
and explicitly left unconfirmed ("may still be a hazard..., but nothing in
this pass's data shows it ever being the one in contact"). This pass closes
that flag: live contact, dx/dy inside the same generic thresholds, closing
84th pass's open question. All eight non-baseline delays actually clear
slot 12; the three that still died were caught by this second hazard
because the arc happened to rest at the crossbar height (y=112, in slot
8's danger band) instead of falling through to the ground (y=144) the way
the five genuinely-safe delays do. Adds the margin math (dx/dy vs
thresholds) that was missing from the original write-up, and opens a new
item: what decides which landing height a given delay produces.

events.title: tool(corpus): "do I already have this?" answered by content, and half a flux file reads plausibly (MF-1491)
events.message:
tool(corpus): "do I already have this?" answered by content, and half a flux file reads plausibly (MF-1491)

The owner points at folders of disk images and new ones keep arriving. A
prose answer is wrong the next day: measured while working, one folder
grew from 23 to 27.9 GB and its `.a2r` count from 356 to 1213.

`scripts/audit_korpus_gegen_ordner.py <folder>` answers it repeatedly.

── Three things it measures, each needed once today ──────────────────

**1. Content, not names.** The same bytes sit in the corpus as
`waitless_d1.a2r` and in the folder as `WaitLess - Disk 1.a2r`; two
different captures of one title share a name. First real run:

    size matches (therefore hashed)   15
    CONTENT-IDENTICAL with the corpus  5

Comparing by name would have found none of the five.

**2. Torsos, before they become evidence.** A half flux file reads
PLAUSIBLY — the reader walks whatever is there. `Alge-Blaster Plus`
declared 19 919 745 bytes in its STRM header and had 4 194 304; it stood
on a candidate list with "26 locations" and a geometry that looked fine
(MF-1487). Measured on the folder:

    image files (derived extension)   798, 18.61 GB
    HOLLOW (zero header), excluded    458   <- a running download
    A2R whole 651 / TRUNCATED         128

128 truncated files that all look usable.

**3. The gap.** Which extensions the folder carries that the corpus does
not.

── Derived, not maintained ──────────────────────────────────────────

The extension set comes from the registered plugins
(`gen_format_list.py --md`) plus the extensions present in the manifest —
109 of them. My own hand list, written an hour earlier, would have
swallowed `txt`, `image` and `ctr`, which the manifest carries, and a new
format would have been invisible (MF-636: file sets come from the tree,
not from lists that go stale).

── What it does not do ──────────────────────────────────────────────

It does not hash 28 GB: whoever shares no size with a corpus entry cannot
be a duplicate, so only size matches are hashed. And it decides nothing
about licence or acquisition — whether a file MAY enter the corpus is an
owner question (LIZ-1, docs/QUARANTINE_PROCESS.md). The script says only
whether it is already there and whether it is whole.

The A2R verdict is deliberately three-valued: whole / truncated /
UNCLEAR. "Lengths add up but nothing follows the flux chunk" is not
broken — it is unproven, and unproven does not become evidence.

── Two of my own mistakes, both left as comments in the file ────────

**The selftest passed and the script died.** `groessen_treffer` returns
2-tuples; I unpacked three. The selftest covered that function in
isolation — 16 of 16 green — and the run crashed at the CALL SITE.
Checking a pure function is not the same as checking its call.

**`git grep` does not see an untracked file.** I had written MF-1490 into
the new script before asking for the number, `git grep MF-149` found
nothing, and I read that as "free". It was my own line, in a file git had
never heard of. Renumbered to MF-1491 per line; a parallel session holds
1490.

    selftest   16/16
    real run   5 of 15 size matches are the same bytes

events.title: ui: three reasons audio never played
events.message:
ui: three reasons audio never played

1. EmuAudio is a plain QObject but was created in createDocks() —
   wireBackend() runs first, so the 'if (m_audio)' guard skipped the
   mediaAudioReceived connect permanently and no audio was ever
   routed in production (the direct-host tests could not see it).
   It is now created before the backend wiring, beside m_host.

2. QAudioDevice()'s default ctor is a *null* device in Qt6, not the
   system default: applyAudioOutputDevice() handed one to the sink
   at every startup, so it opened no stream (nothing in PipeWire's
   playback list, nothing audible). The sink now starts on
   QMediaDevices::defaultAudioOutput(), and only a stored id that
   resolves to a real device changes it; a vanished device falls
   back to the real default rather than null.

3. The demo beep's delay was ~16 s, not the commented ~0.5 s, and
   would have eaten every later keypress; d0 is 6 now, and the
   test's copy matches. The test also scans only the chunks each
   keypress produces — under fast-forward the beep window is brief
   inside hundreds of chunks.

Verified on this machine: a media session registers a PipeWire
playback stream (media.name = PiST, Stream/Output/Audio) — the
entry KDE's playback-streams list shows.

events.title: ui: push-mode audio, an output-device picker, and a beeping demo
events.message:
ui: push-mode audio, an output-device picker, and a beeping demo

The pull-mode sink could starve into IdleState on its first
underrun and never resume — silent output only ears would catch.
EmuAudio now pushes bounded by bytesFree() with a pump timer and an
IdleState recovery, queues ~200 ms, and drops oldest on overflow.
Audio output is selectable in Settings > Appearance (application-
wide preference, persisted as audio/outputDeviceId, resolved at
startup and on every applyAppearance; missing devices fall back to
the system default). demo/keyred.s now also plays a ~440 Hz PSG
beep under Supexec after each keypress — the keyclick's 6301 bell
turns out to have no emulation path in Hatari's ikbd.c, so a
deterministic beep is the honest audio proof; the audio test
asserts non-zero samples arrive after it. ci.yml and release.yml
request qtmultimedia from install-qt-action (Qt6::Multimedia joined
the build in phase 3).

events.title: Install AmigaOS 3.5 and 3.9 onto an empty drive, and keep what is installed
events.message:
Install AmigaOS 3.5 and 3.9 onto an empty drive, and keep what is installed

Choosing a release CD for a newly partitioned drive showed the disc as
recognised and the drive as not ready, which read as the disc having
failed. Behind that, booting with the CD could not have worked for
anyone, for four separate reasons.

What the dialog says:

- The disc and the drive are reported separately. A disc that is
  recognised is said to be fine.
- A drive that cannot be started offers to install Workbench 3.1 from
  the dialog.

Installing onto an empty drive:

- The application said 3.9 refuses a drive with no earlier release. The
  installer's own words are "OS3.9 full installation over OS3.0 or empty
  HD", for which it says to boot the emergency system.
- An empty drive is now started from the Emergency-Boot system the disc
  carries, copied onto a small drive of its own and attached beside the
  one being installed onto, with a higher boot priority.
- The lines of that system's startup which expect the emergency floppy
  in DF0: are commented out, because each stops the boot with a
  requester asking for the disk.

Why booting with the CD never worked:

- The emulator was given a temporary FAT32 card image with the drive
  wrapped inside it, not the drive. An emulator cannot boot that, it was
  limited to 4 GB, and it was deleted afterwards, so nothing installed
  would have been kept. The emulator is now given the image itself.
- FS-UAE installed as a snap cannot read the hidden folder the workbench
  keeps its images in, and opened a machine with no drive. The drive and
  the disc are now hard linked into the folder a snap can read, so a
  drive of a hundred gigabytes is handed over at once. Where a link
  cannot be made they are copied, and the drive is copied back.
- The route's undo point was named after a reason too long for the
  checkpoint store, so every request to it was refused.
- The undo point was discarded as soon as the request returned, because
  the image had not changed yet.

While the emulator runs, the drive cannot be changed or rolled back from
the workbench, and a change is refused before any undo point is taken.
A drive run to look at it is attached read-only.

A CD0 mountlist naming the emulator's own CD device is no longer written
to the drive. The emulator mounts the disc itself, and the mountlist
would have been wrong on the real machine the drive is for.

Checked in FS-UAE with Kickstart 3.1 and the AmigaOS 3.9 disc: an empty
PFS3 drive started from the emergency system to Workbench 45.1, with the
disc as CD0: and the empty partitions mounted and writable, and what the
machine wrote was in the image afterwards. A drive with Workbench 3.1
saw the disc with no driver switched on.

routine in the printer buffer that unscrambles the game and moves it to
$5E00), maps the code by playing the game in SkoolKit's simulator -- every
control method, all 625 cells a knight can stand in, the bonuses, finds,

out the town, buildings, boxes, tiles, graphic table, sprites and tunes

reassemble byte for byte and the snapshot rebuilt is the one loaded; 476
entries, every one titled, described and labelled; 4705 of 4806
instructions seen to run, the rest found by descent; no warnings.

Filmation II's drawing -- walls behind claiming screen columns, outlines in
front -- movement, the creatures and the quest), the whole town drawn by the
game's own wall routine with layers, its buildings and cell types, tiles,
graphic table, sprites, panel and font, animations and sounds recorded from
its own routines, and twelve bugs and seven tested pokes. Among the bugs:
the villains hum bytes of the ROM, a hundred per cent prints in the wrong
font, and a stack leak crashes the 157th game (watched live); the lives
poke passes the game's own check on its DEC (HL).

events.title: Teach the room editor Alien 8: its two pages of object templates, the nudge its rooms set, its inks and valves, and the art it has no remake for
events.message:
Teach the room editor Alien 8: its two pages of object templates, the nudge its rooms set, its inks and valves, and the art it has no remake for

Alien 8's profile is its disassembly's BUILD_ROOM ($CCA7). Its tables are at
$6460-$76E2 and three routines walk the rooms, so a build moves them by
patching seven operands: the rooms' in BUILD_ROOM, RESET_ROOM_COLOURS and
SUMMARISE_CHAMBERS ($CCBB, $CAD3, $AC74), the object table's where those
walks stop and in TEMPLATES_AT ($CCB8, $CAD6, $AC81, $CCA8), and the
background table's ($CD19).

Three things are its own. A group header's template 0 sets the placement
nudge for the groups after it, and 31 moves to a second page of object
templates, so the table is slots -- 32 words a full page, 0 and 31 of each
zero -- the castle keeps each group's nudge on the group, and a build writes
the groups in page order with a header wherever the page or the nudge
changes. Its inks are in bits 3-5 of the attribute byte (0-2 zero on the tape,
filled every game) and its sizes in 6-7, four at most. And its valves lie in
PLACES, 36 of Knight Lore's nine-byte rows, with no wizard's list.

Alien 8 has no remake to take a sprite layout and graphic table from, so
room_editor_art.py writes them into scripts/room_editor_art/alien8/ from the
disassembly's snapshot: each sprite's own rectangle, the sprite each graphic
draws, the commonest box its templates give it, and its pixel nudge,
harvested by running its update routine in SkoolKit's simulator, facing each
way, to SET_PIXEL_ADJ ($BF77). They agree with notes/alien8/graphic-numbers.md.
Numbers and rectangles only; publish_pages.py puts the one page beside all
three games.

Checked: the castle decodes to what the notes count and packs back byte for
byte; every sprite is painted; an edited castle, with a second-page template
raised and a first-page one after it, a fourth shape and a valve moved, packs
with its tables moved and decodes back as edited; a fifth shape and a 53rd

events.title: fix(d64,nfd): a recorded error reaches the model with the meaning its source gives — the 1541 codes and the uPD765 status bits all became "data CRC bad", which the model then read as "unchecked" (P3-659, MF-1490)
events.message:
fix(d64,nfd): a recorded error reaches the model with the meaning its source gives — the 1541 codes and the uPD765 status bits all became "data CRC bad", which the model then read as "unchecked" (P3-659, MF-1490)

Second slice of P3-659. Both readers called uft_sector_set_crc(false)
for everything. That is the loose use that made the central fix of
MF-1488 wrong, and the disk2 bridge does not even read it.

D64: the error byte now maps to what it means. Source: Peter Schepers,
D64.TXT, error byte table, read 2026-09-28:

| Byte | 1541 error | Meaning | Now marked |
|---|---|---|---|
| 05 | 23 | checksum error in data block | data CRC error |
| 09 | 27 | checksum error in header block | ID CRC error |
| 02 / 03 / 04 / 0F | 20 / 21 / 22 / 74 | header or data descriptor not found, no SYNC, drive not ready | not readable (the bytes are no reading) |
| 0B | 29 | disk sector ID mismatch | unchanged: crc_ok=false |
| 06 / 07 / 08 / 0A | write codes | — | unchanged: crc_ok=false |

The last two rows keep their old marking because the tree has no status
bit for them; this is named in P3-659.

NFD (uPD765 status):
- ST2 bit 5 (DD) is a data CRC error.
- ST1 bit 5 (DE) without DD is an ID CRC error. This is the same
  separation the EDSK reader makes.
- A sector whose data lies past the end of the file was a 0xE5 fill
  with crc_ok=false and reached the model as data. It is now marked
  truncated: the source ended, nothing is said about the medium or a
  CRC.

Red first: tests/test_crc_befund_erreicht_modell.c gains two cases
through the bridge.
- D64 track 1 with codes 01,05,09,02,04,0B: before `UUUUUU`, after
  `UBIMMU`.
- NFD r0 with ST2, ST1, clean and truncated: before `UUUU`, after
  `BIUM`.
Now 5/5 cases; mutation matrix 6/6.

test_nfd_r0 asserted "ST1 bit 5 alone -> data CRC bad". It is rewritten
as BERICHTIGT, not deleted: per the uPD765, DE without DD is the ID
field, so the entry now carries an ID CRC error and its data CRC stays
good. 4/4.

Open in P3-659: dmk and sap (recomputed, so CRC_CHECKED belongs with
them), fdi, jv3, stx.

table follows the rooms, whether a scenery entry carries a destination,
five- or six-byte object templates, the flags' passable bit, the object

Pentagram's profile is its disassembly's BUILD_ROOM ($C92C): the tables at

slots point at the scenery table and stay empty templates that point there
again; laying out a table now shares a body's tail with an earlier one's, as
the template at $6ABD does with the next. The sprites are four runs, turned
back left to right and upside down before the sheet is painted.

events.title: Web build W1.5a: keep logging, really exit the runtime, let the page flush -trace
events.message:
Web build W1.5a: keep logging, really exit the runtime, let the page flush -trace

Found while testing the page in headless Chrome (wasm.md W1.7 method):

1. config.h turned ENABLE_LOG off on the web (2019), so sys_printf printed
   nothing: `?rd=2` stopped with no message at all, since W1.4's refusal goes
   through sysarg_fail -> sys_printf. Logging is now on everywhere; on the web
   it goes to the browser console (Module.print).

2. With emscripten's default EXIT_RUNTIME=0 the runtime is kept alive, so
   exit(1) from sysarg_fail never reached the page's Module.onExit (checked in
   emscripten 6.0.10 src/lib/libwasi.js: proc_exit calls onExit only when
   !keepRuntimeAlive()). Now:
   - build.sh links with -sEXIT_RUNTIME=1;
   - rd1/game.c, EXIT state on the web (Esc): emscripten_force_exit(0) after
     game_exit/sys_shutdown, instead of only emscripten_cancel_main_loop -- a
     real exit that flushes stdio (-trace) and calls Module.onExit.

3. -trace writes through stdio with no fflush, so the file in MEMFS stayed
   empty while the game ran. build.sh exports _fflush
   (-sEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS=_main,_fflush); the page flushes before reading. No
   change to the game's C code for this.

Checks: web clean build, 168 warnings (-1: sys_printf's msg is used again);
in headless Chrome `?rd=2` ends with "the game could not start: Rick Dangerous
2 is not available in the web build yet" on the page. Native builds are not
affected by build.sh; config.h already had ENABLE_LOG on natively.

events.title: docs(tiers): the T3 metric cannot fall by work — every format left on T2/T3 has no foreign producer, and the table now says so itself (MF-1489)
events.message:
docs(tiers): the T3 metric cannot fall by work — every format left on T2/T3 has no foreign producer, and the table now says so itself (MF-1489)

`CLAUDE.md` lists the release metric "ungeprüfte Formate (T3)" with the
direction **down**, unconditionally. That reads like a backlog. Measured,
it is not one.

── The measurement ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

Every format currently on T2 or T3 carries channel **"keiner"** in the
producer census (`docs/ERZEUGER_ZENSUS.md`, itself generated) with class
"C — gemessen: dieser Weg traegt nicht". Without exception.

T1b requires an image from a FOREIGN HAND. Where no foreign hand exists,
no amount of work lowers the number. The two routes that remain are not
work at this spot: a real capture (hardware, community-delegated per
MF-310) or an owner decision about a source that carries no licence
statement.

── The single T3, twice measured ────────────────────────────────────

`syn`. In-tree, MF-1097 already closed the producer question: `floptool`
answers `Error: Format 'syn' unknown`, and hxcfe's 207 modules do not
know it either. Verified independently here: there is **no public
description of a `.syn` container** anywhere — Synclavier disks are
captured as raw flux, and the KryoFlux forum thread on them is titled
"Help Required Determining Raw Disk Format".

The geometry itself is not the problem. MF-1141 grounded it in
Synclavier's OWN NED sources (MIT) and found two of three measures wrong
— 8 sectors of 512 instead of 16 of 256, at an identical file size, which
is why nobody had noticed. What stays open is precisely stated and NOT
decidable by reading: the side count (NED reads it at runtime from the
drive ID, so it is in no file) and the layout inside a `.syn` file (the
source describes the physical disk, not that container).

── Built derived, not maintained ────────────────────────────────────

`stufen_ohne_erzeuger()` joins the tier table to the census, and
`render_md` emits a section naming the reason. The count lives only in
the generated document; a hand-kept number next to a measured one drifts
(MF-541), which is why the CLAUDE.md paragraph deliberately carries no
number at all.

    selftest           21 -> 27
    mutation matrix    4/4

── Four things that went wrong on the way ───────────────────────────

**The join key, for the third time today.** The tier rows carry DISPLAY
names (`SYN`, `AkaiS900`), the census carries symbols (`syn`,
`akai_s900`). My first draft joined on `name` and found 0 of 8 — the same
misstep as MF-1474, whose lesson I had written into a docstring in THIS
file. A connector gets looked up, not remembered; that now stands as a
comment at the line.

**My mutation expectation was wrong again, not the test.** M2 fells four
assertions, because the channel check carries four guarantees at once.
Third repetition of that lesson today (MF-931, MF-1483).

**The inventory gate rejected my wording.** "8 von 8 Formaten auf T2/T3"
was read as a claim about T3 — and a human could read it the same way.
The prose now carries no number.

**And my test-pattern was too coarse:** grepping `CHECK\|ASSERT` in
`test_syn_gegen_ned_quellen` found zero assertions and I nearly reported
a sham test. It counts through a helper with `rot++` and checks ten
things, among them 1232 of 1232 NED sectors appearing as whole 512-byte
units at their marker.

── What this does NOT do ────────────────────────────────────────────

It changes no metric value. `syn` is neither deleted nor downgraded to
make a number move — that would be the number as motive (MF-1077, the
`rcpmfs` case). The tier stays T3; what changes is that the table states
why it cannot be otherwise.

events.title: Web build W1.3: run one game step per game_period of real time in the browser
events.message:
Web build W1.3: run one game step per game_period of real time in the browser

The 2019 web loop (c2aef3d) called game_loop at a fixed
fps = (24 * GAME_PERIOD) / game_period, computed once in game_run:
- 24 fps at the default, while the native loop runs one frame per
  GAME_PERIOD = 75 ms (13.3 fps), so the web game played ~1.8x too fast;
- the screens that change game_period at run time (scr_imain.c,
  scr_gameover.c) kept the start rate.

Now (rd1/game.c, __EMSCRIPTEN__ only): emscripten_set_main_loop(web_frame, 0, 1)
-- fps 0, i.e. requestAnimationFrame, which emscripten and SDL3 recommend.
web_frame accumulates real time (sys_gettime, in tm/tmx, the native timer's
own variables) and runs game_loop once per elapsed game_period, reading
game_period afresh at every step; game_loop still does not sleep on the web.
After a stall (hidden tab) at most WEB_CATCHUP (4) steps run and the rest of
the backlog is dropped. The game logic itself is tick-based and does not see
any of this (kb/demo.md).

Checks: web clean build, 169 warnings (171 before: tm/tmx are used again);
native WSL builds unchanged (ST 230 / PC 231). The step rate in a browser is
measured in W1.7.

events.title: ui: media channel mouse input and the input grab (phase 2c/2d)
events.message:
ui: media channel mouse input and the input grab (phase 2c/2d)

The VirtualBox model, Qt-owned (PLAN §12.4): clicking the panel
during a media session captures input — grabMouse/grabKeyboard (no
OS-level grab anywhere, so the release key and every IDE shortcut
keep working), a blank cursor, mouse tracking on, and an accent
border with the release hint. F12 releases (never forwarded; it has
no ST scancode anyway), and the grab also ends on focus loss and on
session end, because a trapped user is the failure mode. The
grabbing click and its release are consumed, never delivered. A
Release Input action in the Run menu is the always-visible path.

Mouse deltas are scaled by the fitted rect's scale through
ui/MouseScaling's sub-pixel accumulator (§12.3: host pixels are not
guest pixels), and while any media session runs the host cursor
hides over the panel — the guest cursor is baked into every frame,
so two pointers would otherwise argue. Keys go through
ui/StKeyboard's table; autorepeat is left to the 6301's typematic.
The wire side is MediaServer::sendMouse and a backend mediaMouse()
the native host forwards.

Tests: mouseScalerAccumulatesSubPixelDeltas (fractional carry),
inputGrabRoutesKeysAndMouse (click captures and is consumed, keys
translate, F12 releases and is not forwarded, moves emit scaled
deltas with button state), and mouseInjectionMovesTheGuestCursor —
after the boot stream quietens, injected deltas produce a frame that
differs (the cursor sprite redrew).

events.title: Music on by default
events.message:
Music on by default

The score is part of what Flashback is, and the Options menu now
switches it off for anyone who would rather not, so music=true is the
default: an STE or Mega STE plays the original modules and any other
ST the YM versions. The RS.CFG that ships has its music line commented
out, so an existing copy gets music without an edit; music=false in
RS.CFG turns it off.

The tracks come from the player's own disks, so a copy with no MUSIC
folder is now the ordinary case rather than a mistake. The YM player
checks first that any track is installed - the same cached check the
Options menu uses - and stays quiet, instead of trying each cue's file
and warning about it.

Mixing the modules takes about a quarter of an STE, so its cutscenes
run slower with them; music=ym keeps the cheaper YM versions.

Checked in Hatari (cycle-exact, sound recorded at the title): a plain
ST with MUSIC plays the YM music, an STE the module; with no MUSIC
folder, and with music=false, the title is silent and nothing warns.

events.title: harddrive: attach fixed and dynamic VHD images
events.message:
harddrive: attach fixed and dynamic VHD images

The hard-disk file dialogs listed hdf/hdz/img/bin/chd but never vhd, so a
WinUAE VHD could not be picked, and a dropped .vhd went to the floppy
drive. Typing the path in only appeared to work: with no VHD support the
file opened as a raw image, which exposed a fixed VHD's footer to the
guest as one extra writable sector (and pushed a bare partition hardfile
off a whole number of cylinders), and read a dynamic VHD as garbage.

Add a VHD backend behind HardDriveImage, sniffed by its conectix footer
like the gzip and CHD forms. A fixed disk serves everything in front of
the footer. A dynamic disk maps blocks through its BAT, reads unallocated
blocks as zeros, and appends a block on the first non-zero write to it:
bitmap and zeroed data where the footer was, footer after, BAT entry
last. The file stays the authority, as for an HDF: an entry last seen
unallocated and the append position are read again from the file, so a
save state reopened beside the running machine sees the same disk and
never appends over it. Differencing disks are refused with a way to
merge them; hostile headers are bounded before anything is sized.

Every hard-disk dialog now filters on harddrive::IMAGE_EXTENSIONS, kept
beside the opener so a new container cannot be left unpickable again.

Fixes #729.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Stop offering .chd for new hard disk images
events.message:
Stop offering .chd for new hard disk images

The Create Image save dialog offered .chd alongside .hdf and .img, but
the writer only ever lays down raw sectors (RDB plus formatted volume)
whatever the name. A raw file named .chd does not read as a chdman hard
disk, so the drive slots and the window's drop handling took it for a
CD image.

The dialog now offers only the extensions the writer produces, from a
shared HARD_EXTENSIONS list, and create_hard refuses a .chd path before
writing anything, since some host dialogs accept whatever name is typed
regardless of the filter. The status line says to make a CHD from the
finished image with chdman createhd.

Tests check that an image written under every offered extension is
classified as a hard disk, that a raw image under a CHD name is
classified as a CD (the reason for the refusal), and that a .chd name
in either case is refused and leaves no file behind.

events.title: emu: media protocol v2 — AUTH token and randomised port
events.message:
emu: media protocol v2 — AUTH token and randomised port

The media listener's only real security surface is closed before
input lands: MediaServer generates a 16-byte per-session token at
listen time and says nothing until the client opens with it ('PSA1'
+ token, 3 s window); a wrong or missing AUTH is dropped without a
byte, so no local process receives the screen stream or, next, the
input path. The token travels to the fork as PIST_MEDIA_TOKEN in the
session environment (the PARENT_WIN_ID mechanism), carried through
SessionConfig.mediaToken and a widened engageMediaDisplay callback
(MediaEngagement: port + token). The port is now random in
20000-32767 instead of a fixed 29200-29209 scan: below the ephemeral
floor (the self-connect hazard) but not pre-bindable. Tests:
mediaServerRejectsClientWithoutAuth (wrong token, silence, and the
good token all behave) and the token/port updates to
mediaChannelDeliversFrames.

events.title: RD1 demo: one take per submap visit, and loop the demo at the end of the game
events.message:
RD1 demo: one take per submap visit, and loop the demo at the end of the game

Why: the T43 demo plays the whole game, and map 3's castle is entered twice
through 0x15/0x16 (kb/demo-solver.md §14). The demo table was indexed by
env_submap, one script per submap, and the recorder keeps the last take of a
segment -- so an export of the full run held only the second visit of 0x15
and 0x16, and playing it died on the first visit of 0x16 (checked headless:
`-demo` stopped at 0x16 with lives 0 after 14940 steps).

Change (RD1 adapter only; demo.c and RD2 untouched):
- game.c game_enterSegment passes a VISIT index to demo_enterSegment instead
  of env_submap: it moves on when a different submap is entered and stays put
  when the same one is re-entered, which only restart() does, after a death.
  So a death still replays (or, recording, restarts) the current take, and a
  revisit gets its own take. init() rewinds it for every new game.
- demoset: DEMO_MAXSEG (0x40) takes, segment name "visit". The full game is
  50 visits.
- end of game while a demo plays: fade out to XRICK_CLR instead of game over,
  so the title screens run and their demo path (scr_imain.c) starts the next
  game; the takes restart from the first. No game over, no hall of fame.
  Without -demo, and while recording, the end of game is unchanged.
- dat_demo.c (the 4 pilot takes, 0x00-0x03 = visits 0-3, same meaning):

events.title: emu: add the hatari-pist media channel (phase 1)
events.message:
emu: add the hatari-pist media channel (phase 1)

With a --pist-media-capable emulator the session runs windowless and
PiST owns the pixels: MediaServer (emu/) listens on 127.0.0.1
29200-29209 (below the ephemeral floor — the loopback self-connect
hazard measured in the spike) before the spawn, sends HELLO on
accept, and reassembles change-gated 32bpp frames. MainWindow
converts MediaFrame to QImage and feeds the panel; screenshots in
media mode save the last frame. SessionConfig gains mediaPort, which
emits exactly --pist-media <port> --frameskips 0 (frameskip would
starve the stream under fast-forward). Engagement is gated on
native backend + probed --pist-media + the PIST_MEDIA_DISPLAY dev
gate until input lands in phase 2; every other session's argv and
wiring are unchanged. Colour fidelity measured pixel-identical to
Hatari's own debugger screenshot (RMSE 0).

Tests: mediaChannelDeliversFrames (transport, skips without the
fork), mediaDisplayFeedsThePanel (UI fidelity via 8x8 cell-mean
grids, proven falsifiable against a stubbed setFrame), and
PIST_HATARI added to the missing-emulator fixtures' env stripping.
PLAN.md §12 records the plan, the spike measurements, and the phase
results; ARCHITECTURE.md gains the media-channel section.

events.title: Ask before a slow save, and keep handlers where the install is
events.message:
Ask before a slow save, and keep handlers where the install is

Saving a large drive from the browser reads every byte of it to build
the download, which takes about a quarter of a minute for each gigabyte
the drive describes: over half an hour for 128 GB. Nothing said so.

- Save image in the browser edition now asks first for a drive of 2 GB
  or more, with the size and the time it will take, and saves nothing
  if the answer is no.
- The New Image dialog says the same while a drive of that size is
  being laid out, so it is known before the drive is made.
- The desktop application saves straight to a file and is not affected.

Supplied handlers were kept per user on the desktop and per browser
owner in the web edition. They now follow how the application was
installed:

- A copy installed for one person, in their home directory or owned by
  them, keeps handlers in ~/.config/amiga-file-forge/handlers.
- A copy installed for the whole machine, from the Debian or RPM
  package, keeps them in /var/lib/amiga-file-forge/handlers for everyone
  who uses it. Writing there asks for an administrator's password
  through pkexec, as the application update does, and gives the command
  to run by hand when the prompt is dismissed or pkexec is missing.
- The Docker service keeps them in its working volume, so they survive
  the container being replaced.
- The web host never asks for a password, because the person pressing
  the button may be on another computer.

AMIGA_FILE_FORGE_INSTALL_SCOPE settles the scope for an installation
that cannot be told apart. The handlers dialog says which kind of
installation it is and where its handlers go.

events.title: fix(formats): a CRC error the container records reaches the model as a CRC error — it arrived as "unchecked", indistinguishable from a good sector (P3-659, MF-1488)
events.message:
fix(formats): a CRC error the container records reaches the model as a CRC error — it arrived as "unchecked", indistinguishable from a good sector (P3-659, MF-1488)

The flaw: uft_sector_set_crc(s, false) sets crc_ok, crc_valid and
data_crc_ok, but never `status`. uft_sector_set_id_crc(false) sets only
id_crc_ok, not the id.crc_ok the bridge reads. The disk2 bridge reads a
CRC verdict from `status` only, deliberately: memset-built sectors carry
crc_ok=false without any finding (MF-1001).

Measured: 17 calls in 14 files, and 11 of 14 producers leave status at
OK. Their CRC-bad sector came out of the bridge as data_crc_known=0 /
UNVERIFIED:
- DecodeJob counted it "unchecked" instead of "bad";
- the report put it under crc_unknown instead of crc_bad;
- FEAT_BAD_CRC was never set.
No false "OK", but a loss that looks like caution. The trigger was a
remark from the local -37 session that set_crc(false) leaves the status
alone.

The central fix (set_crc(false) also sets CRC_ERROR) was measured and
rejected, because producers call it loosely:
- D64 for every 1541 error code (02 "header not found" and 04 "data not
  found" are no CRC errors);
- NFD for a truncated 0xE5 fill and for ST1 bit 5, an ID CRC.
A central bit would turn each of these into an invented data-CRC
finding. So each producer gets the meaning its own source gives, through
two helpers in include/uft/uft_types.h:
- uft_sector_mark_data_crc_error() sets UFT_SECTOR_CRC_ERROR, not
  CRC_CHECKED: a recorded flag is not a recomputation.
- uft_sector_mark_id_crc_error() also sets id.crc_ok and
  UFT_SECTOR_ID_CRC_ERROR.

First slice, the three producers with a named meaning:

| Producer | Recorded code | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IMD | types 5..8 | Dunfield IMD.SRC |
| D88 | 0xB0 data, 0xA0 address | MAME d88_dsk.cpp |
| EDSK (dsk_cpc) | ST2 bit 5 data, ST1 bit 5 alone ID | uPD765 |

Red first: tests/test_crc_befund_erreicht_modell.c runs all three
through the bridge. It was 3 of 3 "unchecked" before; after the fix
3/3. Mutation matrix 5/5. Full run 587/587, and no existing test moved,
which matches the measurement that none covered this path.

The EDSK case opens through the plugin directly. uft_disk_open() opens
no extended CPC file at all: dsk_cpc and edsk both claim "EXTENDED" at
95, and a tie opens nothing (P3-402). The corpus test says "the order
decides"; measured, the result is NULL. Named in P3-659.

Open in P3-659, each needing its own source and red proof: d64, nfd,
dmk, sap, fdi, jv3, stx.

events.title: Declare the real macOS floor, 14.2
events.message:
Declare the real macOS floor, 14.2

The app bundle claimed LSMinimumSystemVersion 11.0, but the executable
cannot load below macOS 14.2: cpal's Core Audio host binds
AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap and AudioHardwareDestroyProcessTap (14.2)
and the host-disk code binds kIOMainPortDefault (12). Rust extern
declarations carry no availability markers, so these are strong imports
and dyld aborts the launch on older systems instead of Finder refusing
it with a version message.

Raise LSMinimumSystemVersion to 14.2, add depends_on macos: :sonoma to
the Homebrew formula (a source build on older releases cannot link the
14.2 symbols either), and state the requirement in the getting-started
guide. Older macOS releases are out of Apple support and are not a
target.

Fixes #728

Ported and checked live. The world-4 ending's [0x34A] leads to PPAYOFF.PI1
with its own palette faded in, eight two-line pages from DS:0xEF58 in the
story font (sprite ch+0x1CB = PINTROFT ch+9, x = 164-4*len, y 12/30), each

pixel-exact against the DOSBox screen (0 of 64000 pixels off, same RGB).
Then the game restarts at world 1A keeping score and lives, with money,
keys, weapons, arc and familiar reset and difficulty +1 clamped 2..4

events.title: fix(adf): an ADF with more than 80 DD cylinders is a DD disk, not an HD partial dump — cylinder 1 carried the data of track 4 (P3-658, MF-1486)
events.message:
fix(adf): an ADF with more than 80 DD cylinders is a DD disk, not an HD partial dump — cylinder 1 carried the data of track 4 (P3-658, MF-1486)

Every whole-cylinder DD size above 80 cylinders is also a multiple of
the HD track length (11 264): 912 384, 923 648, ... for 81, 82, ...
adf_classify() therefore took the HD partial-dump rule. A 923 648-byte
ADF written by greaseweazle (`gw convert --format amiga.amigados.plus`,
82 x 2 x 11, from ADFDiskBox's diskdefs) opened as 22 sectors per track
and "82 of 160 tracks". Cylinder 1 / head 0 carried the data of DD
track 4.

References, both saying DD:
- greaseweazle, the writer of such a file: 82 x 2 x 11.
- hxcfe raw_amiga.c (read, and executed as `hxcfe -infos` by the
  review: "11 sectors/track"). It reads everything below
  100 * 11 * 2 * 512 bytes as DD and allocates its floppy for 86
  cylinders.

Now a length above 901 120 that holds whole DD cylinders, at most 86
(hxcfe's allocation, named at the constant), is a full DD disk. The
geometry follows the file: 82 x 2 x 11. The size alone stays ambiguous
against an HD partial dump of the same length. The probe claims no more
than for any full size (45), and open() warns which reading it took.

Red first: tests/test_adf_mehr_zylinder.c builds the 82-cylinder image
from the committed tests/corpus_free/xdftool_dd_ofs.adf plus two
cylinders with their own fill. It was 3 of 3 red before (geometry
80 x 2 x 22, cylinder 1 wrong, cylinder 81 unreadable); after the fix
5/5, including controls:
- 901 120 bytes stays 80 x 2 x 11;
- cylinder 82 lies beyond the file.
Mutation matrix 2/2. The 87 adf/amiga/dms/probe/convert tests stay
green.

Found by the review of UFT_AmigaWorkflowBooster_v1 (neue-ideen, t3).
The package itself is Fundus:
- it has no Amiga reader and 0 callers;
- 9 of 9 red probes fire, among them gw arguments without --diskdefs
  (the standard gw answers "Unknown format") and a batch writer that
  reports "3 of 3 complete" after 1 of 160 tracks.

Also recorded: P3-657. The A2R v2 branch loses 255 ticks per 0xFF byte
in duration/rpm. That comes from the uft-a2r-code review and is not
measured in the tree; the flux path computes 0xFF correctly. The other
two findings of that review belong to P3-656, where the local -37
session measured them independently.

events.title: RD1 ST: wake scripted traps at rick x+0x0B, as the ST does (F13)
events.message:
RD1 ST: wake scripted traps at rick x+0x0B, as the ST does (F13)

Symptom: on submap 0x27 (map 4), trap 436 (type 0x40, invisible, lethal
once awake, stationary 3x248 frames) sits on the only ladder up (cols
25-26, rows 89-107); its trigger box is x 200..224. Rick can climb there
only at x >= 188 (climb probe tile (x+4)/8+1). With the PC's +0x0C probe
the ST's inclusive box fires at x=188 (188+12 = 200), so every climb woke
the trap inside Rick's own box and killed him.

ST (atari_ram.bin), both calls to trigger_box_contains_point (0x4D986)
with the player's position:
  4BEE4  move.w (0x4A752),D0 / addi.w #0xb,D0   trigger_zone_update
  4D19A  move.w (0x4A752),D0 / addi.w #0xb,D0   scripted_trap_update
         move.w (0x4A754),D1 / addi.w #0xa,D1 / bsr 0x4D986
(0x4A752/0x4A754 = player nPosX/nPosY, kb/algo-player.md.)

Port: RICK_PROBE_DX (ents.h: ST 0x0B, PC 0x0C) was already defined, with
0x4D19A cited, but applied only to e_sbonus.c (the 0x4BEE4 site). The
trap wake test in e_them_t3_action2 still had the literal 0x0C.

Fix: use RICK_PROBE_DX there. PC unchanged (0x0C, PC 0x27B1). On the ST
every rick-triggered scripted trap now wakes one pixel later when Rick
comes from the left and one pixel earlier from the right.

Checks: clean builds, warning counts unchanged (ST 230, PC 231).

commit, then drivers tags. The SDK row is folded into the firmware
row; the three-repo table and SDK-first step are gone.

events.title: grm-78b: end function bodies at a branch-always pair
events.message:
grm-78b: end function bodies at a branch-always pair

A flag branch followed directly by its complement (BNE x / BEQ y) is
always taken, but Ghidra follows the second branch's fall-through, so
the body runs on into the next routine: blmaster's FUN_f1ca absorbed
the RESET body at f23b. BranchAlwaysPairAnalyzer sets a fall-through
override of none on the second branch when nothing else references it,
and fixes up any function body laid down before it ran.

Re-blessed blmaster (FUN_f1ca ends at f23a; the RESET-path bank
comments become fully known) and megaman3 (81ae becomes a function
entry, so the JMP at 810a is typed as a call).
