events.title: fix(a2r): the v2 INFO branch was off by one byte in every field — and every A2R2 file was reported write-protected (P3-656 resolved, MF-1484)
events.message:
fix(a2r): the v2 INFO branch was off by one byte in every field — and every A2R2 file was reported write-protected (P3-656 resolved, MF-1484)

P3-656 said the v2 path does not interpret the Location. That was the
symptom. The cause sat one level down: the whole v2 INFO branch read
every field one byte early.

── The reference, read for the first time in this tree ───────────────

"A2R 2.x Reference", applesaucefdc.com/a2r2-reference/ — the document
`parse_info_chunk()` named as unread since MF-868 ("NICHT nachgemessen:
keine 2.x-Datei im Korpus"). Verbatim:

    INFO, Disk Type at +33:  "1 = 5.25, 2 = 3.5"

    STRM, Location:
      5.25"  "this value is in halfphases or quarter tracks. For example
              track 0.00 is halfphase 0 and track 1.00 is halfphase 4."
      3.5"   "this value indicates track number as well as side. The
              formula ((track << 1) + side) can be used (0 = Track 0
              Side 0, 1 = Track 0 Side 1, 2 = Track 1 Side 0)."

── Measured on a real file ──────────────────────────────────────────

`tests/corpus/fahey_a2r2/appleworks_d1_a.a2r` (Applesauce v1.1.7, entered
the corpus in MF-1483):

    d[0]      0x01                      INFO version
    d[1..32]  "Applesauce v1.1.7    …"  creator
    d[32]     0x20  (padding space)     <- branch read this as disk_type
    d[33]     0x01                      Disk Type (1 = 5.25")
    d[34]     0x00                      write protected
    d[35]     0x01                      synchronized

Four wrong answers came out of that offset, and one of them is forensic:

  * `write_protected` read the Disk Type, so it was TRUE for every A2R2
    file. A reader that calls every file write-protected makes a forensic
    claim without grounds.
  * `synchronized` read the write-protect byte and was always false,
    although the file says 1.
  * `creator` carried a leading 0x01.
  * `disk_type` was 32, which falls into the "do not interpret" fallback —
    correct by accident for 5.25", and for 3.5" it discards the side.

So the missing rule call was downstream: with `disk_type = 32` no
interpretation would have happened either way. BOTH changes are needed,
and the offset is the cause.

── Red proof, measured in both directions ───────────────────────────

`tests/test_a2r2_dreieinhalbzoll_seite.c`. The corpus has no two-sided
A2R2 — measured across all 50 Fahey captures, 50 of 50 are drive type 1,
where raw and correct coincide. So the test builds the smallest container
that triggers the RULE, with every header number taken from the
reference: Location 2 = track 1 side 0, Location 3 = track 1 side 1.

    before the fix     Disk Type 2 -> 4x1   (side discarded)
    after              Disk Type 2 -> 2x2
    control            Disk Type 1 -> 9x1   unchanged, both times

And with the old offset restored, 6 of 6 assertions fall — the four INFO
fields plus the two geometry values. After: 12 of 12 pass.
`test_a2r_blockarten` stays at 47/0, so the six real captures are
unaffected.

── A second, independent source ─────────────────────────────────────

A parallel session's scout read the same reference for its own package
review and reports the same offsets and the same diagnosis for
`uft_a2r_parser.c:222-228` (disk_type = 32, synchronized = the
write-protect byte). Provenance as they stated it: that is a scout
report they did not re-read themselves, while the measurement above is
first-hand here. Two independent readings agreeing on the same offsets is
more than the two-source rule asks for.

── What is still open, and it is the better evidence ────────────────

The 3.5" half rests on the reference plus a synthetic container, not on a
real disk.

A parallel session holds a type-2 fixture (Copy II Plus 9.1) whose
address fields confirm the formula — Location 80 -> track 40, Location
158 -> track 79. Its status, as they stated it and corrected for me: it
is NOT an original. The package author assembled it from 3 of 160
locations, so it is a constructed container too — stronger than mine,
because the flux and the address fields inside are real, but not a
capture of a disk. A commercial title with no documented redistribution,
LOCAL-ONLY at most, and it is not in this manifest; whether it is taken
in is the owner's call, not a session's.

So the honest state of the 3.5" side: the rule is quoted from the
reference and asserted against a container built from it, and a second
party reads real address fields the same way. What is missing is one
two-sided A2R2 capture. If one lands, this test should hang off it and
the synthetic file becomes the fallback rather than the evidence.

── Why this was findable at all ─────────────────────────────────────

MF-868 left the branch unverified for a stated reason: no 2.x file in the
corpus. Two years later a supplied torrent folder removed that reason.
That is what a corpus is for, and no amount of reading the code would
have produced it.

    ctest   583/583, 2 named skips, 0 failures

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01BHdqfaZ5RFb1HPcw7NYoEY

events.title: corpus(a2r): the 3.5" half now rests on two real double-sided captures — and most of the source folder is hollow (MF-1487)
events.message:
corpus(a2r): the 3.5" half now rests on two real double-sided captures — and most of the source folder is hollow (MF-1487)

MF-1484 fixed the A2R v2 offset and said plainly what was still missing:
one two-sided A2R2 capture. The corpus had none — measured across all 50
Fahey files, 50 of 50 are Disk Type 1, where raw and decomposed Location
coincide. So the 3.5" half rested on the reference plus a container built
from it.

Two real captures now carry it.

    waitless_d1      18.37 MB  160 locations, 80 odd, 80 tracks -> 80x2
    qdrive_iigs_d1    0.38 MB   10 locations,  5 odd,  5 tracks ->  5x2

── Why the selection criterion is odd Locations, not size ───────────

For 3.5" the Location is `((track << 1) + side)`, so only an ODD number
proves side 1 and triggers the decomposition at all. A capture with only
even Locations would pass green without touching the rule. That is the
mistake I nearly made with the Fahey set, where every file is type 1.

── Two measurements that changed how the files were picked ──────────

**The source folder is a LIVE, incomplete download.** Within minutes:
310 -> 335 `.a2r` files, of which 262 -> 280 have a zero header. Any count
from it is a snapshot, and a file copied now can be half-written.

**And a half flux file reads plausibly.** `Alge-Blaster Plus` declares
19 919 745 bytes in its STRM header and has 4 194 304. It was in my first
candidate list, with "26 locations" and a geometry that looked fine — the
reader simply walks what is there.

So intake required two checks: the chunk lengths must end EXACTLY at the
file size, AND a META chunk must sit behind STRM (which proves STRM was
written in full). Of 327 files, 28 remain. Each copy was re-measured after
copying, because the source keeps growing.

── Red proof, at the real files ─────────────────────────────────────

With the MF-1484 offset restored, `disk_type` reads 32 (a padding space),
every interpretation falls into the "do not interpret" fallback, and the
Location stays raw:

    waitless_d1      160x1  instead of 80x2
    qdrive_iigs_d1    10x1  instead of  5x2

All four real-file assertions fall; 10 failures in total with the six from
the synthetic half. After: 21 of 21 pass.

── Provenance, and it is weaker than the Fahey set ──────────────────

archive.org item `Antoine_Vignau_3.5_Floppies_Flux_May_2019_Batch`. Apple
II software, no licence field, so LOCAL-ONLY as usual — hash and
provenance in the repo, files never redistributed.

But unlike MF-1483 this item carries NO per-file checksums: its XML is a
`_meta.xml`, not a `_files.xml` (measured: 0 foreign a2r hashes). The
sha256 here is therefore self-computed only, not cross-checked. That is
recorded in each entry rather than glossed over.

── Note on numbering ────────────────────────────────────────────────

Written as MF-1485 first, then moved to MF-1487 because I had promised
1485 and 1486 to a parallel session. Four occurrences, each changed on its
own line — a file-wide replace is a claim about every hit.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01BHdqfaZ5RFb1HPcw7NYoEY

events.title: feat(combat): house rules travel in the rules bundle, recordings and scenarios (U38)
events.message:
feat(combat): house rules travel in the rules bundle, recordings and scenarios (U38)

RulesBundle carries a frozen house_rules map and build_rules requires it:
in-game fights take state.config.house_rules, the fight lab takes the
scenario file's map. Recordings store the map they were made under;
load(rules=) and replay refuse a recording with no map or one that
differs, naming the first differing entry, with unchanged signatures.
Every scenario file stores its all-faithful map, and a scenario with none
is refused. The fight lab reports these, and its other load errors, as
one line with exit 1 instead of a traceback.

events.title: sanitize: clear recycled-block poison in the heap, not per handler (#97)
events.message:
sanitize: clear recycled-block poison in the heap, not per handler (#97)

* sanitize: clear the freed-block poison when a block is reallocated

A block that FreeVec poisoned keeps that marking when the heap hands the
same addresses back out, so the allocating handler's own header write or
zeroing, and then every write the guest makes, are all reported as
use-after-free.  Writing over the block does not clear it either:
check_write_byte heals Uninit bytes but records and keeps Unaddressable
ones.

Clear the shadow where the block is handed out, before the handler writes
anything into it.  AddressSpace::clear_fresh_block does it, so the
allocators that only hold a &mut dyn AddressSpace can call it too.

BenchWork's "backdrop lha-pack" under --sanitize went from 6 minutes and
691416 violations to 10 seconds and none.

Fixes #95

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* sanitize: clear recycled-block poison in the heap, not per handler

Completes the #95 fix. Two things were left over.

**The clear reached only 8 of ~48 allocation sites.** Every one of them
carves guest structures out of the same GuestHeap, so any of them can be
handed a block FreeMem/FreeVec/FreePooled poisoned -- not just the exec
allocators. A guest that frees a block larger than the 64 KiB quarantine
budget (released immediately rather than held back) and then opens a
file reproduces the original symptom against the FileHandle/MsgPort that
dos Open carves out: 46 spurious "invalid write (freed block)" reports,
one per byte, attributed to the guest's PC.

So the clear moves to GuestHeap::alloc/alloc_with_requested, the one
point where a block leaves the heap's control, and they now take the
address space as a parameter -- which makes the invariant a compile
error to forget rather than a convention to remember. The whole block is
cleared, redzones included; callers that want redzone protection
re-poison via poison_allocation_edges afterwards, as they already had to.
The allocator's own placement/coalescing tests keep a module-private
`alloc_bare` shorthand, since they have no address space in play.

**The wall-clock half of #95 was not the dedup hash.** check_read and
check_write detected "did that byte report?" by comparing
violation_count() before and after -- and violation_count *sums* hits
across the whole log, so once the log filled, every byte of every
violating access walked 1000 entries twice. The byte checkers now return
that answer directly. On a 400,000-byte use-after-free loop: 1.33s
before, 0.03s after, with byte-identical output.

Verified: the #95 repro pair, the Open-after-free case above, and the
whole fixture corpus are clean; sanitizer output is byte-identical to
main for PhxAss (--sanitize, --sanitize-uninit, with and without
--cpu 68020) and for a real SAS/C `sc hello.c`; a genuine use-after-free
is still reported (new regression test, alongside one for the recycled
block at the heap level). cargo test 1010 passed, clippy and fmt clean.

events.title: fix(apple): a sector whose data field lies past the track seam is found, and a failed checksum is "not readable" instead of 256 zero bytes with status OK (P3-638, P3-639, MF-1485)
events.message:
fix(apple): a sector whose data field lies past the track seam is found, and a failed checksum is "not readable" instead of 256 zero bytes with status OK (P3-638, P3-639, MF-1485)

Two faults in the Apple 5.25" read path. Both were found by the
differential run against the uft-a2-code package (neue-ideen, t3) at the
two real Applesauce captures; hxcfe was run as a third voice.

1. Seam (P3-638, cause was "not measured").
   uft_apple_gcr_scan_track() reads one revolution with a ring reader,
   but the loop stopped at `r.pos < bit_count`. That held even when an
   address field had been read and its data field was still to come,
   and that sector vanished without a word. At copy2plus_52 this hit
   T4 P15 and T5 P7, whose address fields start at bits 50934 / 51016:
   558 instead of 560. The package and hxcfe returned both sectors
   byte-identical with good checksums. The red proof found a second
   form: a prologue that straddles the seam (D5 before it, AA 96 after
   it) lost its sector the same way.
   Now, while a field or prologue is pending, the loop reads on past the
   seam. It stops at the first address prologue that begins after the
   seam: that is the track start a second time, and recording it would
   be the 595-instead-of-560 double of MF-715. It reads at most one more
   revolution. There is no invented window constant.

2. Checksum (P3-639 said "delivers ALL 560 sectors").
   On a checksum failure the decoder leaves `data` untouched on purpose
   (MF-721). The WOZ and NIB plugins handed that zero buffer on and only
   called uft_sector_set_crc(false), which does not touch the status.
   Measured, such a sector came out as 256 zero bytes with status OK; at
   gauntlet_e7 that was 550 sectors. It is now reported with its ID,
   marked not readable (the reason H-30 asks for), without data.

Red first: tests/test_apple_gcr_naht_und_pruefsumme.c. The CI part runs
on the committed tests/corpus_free/to_woz2_uftk_dos33.woz:
- Seam: track 0 rotated in 8-bit steps over the whole revolution.
  Before, 416 of 6328 rotations were incomplete; with the pending-field
  rule alone still 32; now 0. Each of the 16 sectors comes exactly once.
- Synthetic "address field without data before the seam" (a 256-zero
  data field is 343 x 0x96): sector 0 exactly once.
- One flipped bit that breaks exactly one checksum: the WOZ plugin now
  reports it as not readable.
- A synthetic NIB with a bad checksum nibble: the same for the NIB
  plugin.
The LOCAL-ONLY part (absent in CI, where it says so and claims nothing)
measures copy2plus_52 at 560 good and gauntlet_e7 at 10 good + 550 not
readable. 8/8 green. Mutation matrix 5/5: the first version scored 3/4.
The track-start stop was untested because the real track has no
address field without data, so the synthetic case was added. The 63
woz/nib/apple/a2r/convert tests stay green.

P3-638 is closed with its cause. P3-639 is marked BERICHTIGT: its
original wording is kept. Which bytes Gauntlet's RWTS wrote stays
undecided: the checksum residue is a constant 0x3F on all 515 measurable
fields (package review), which points to a foreign RWTS, not damage.

events.title: fix(app): fix item-tracking's reuse of existing discoverability infra (SQ-1631)
events.message:
fix(app): fix item-tracking's reuse of existing discoverability infra (SQ-1631)

An audit of SQ-1625/SQ-1627 found several divergences from infrastructure this
app already has, producing real bugs:

Fix 1: zvm_item_observations/glulx_item_observations filtered candidates on
the raw printed name (`o.printed_name.is_empty()`), the exact SQ-1042 bug
list_room_objects_excluding already fixed elsewhere — Inform 7 objects
routinely have no hardware short name at all, only parse words. Switched both
to grammar_model::ObjectWords::display_name(), which was previously making
result.items empty for virtually every Inform 7 game.

Fix 2: ItemObservation now carries the full ObjectWords it was read off of
(a new `words` field), and take_noun_matches/classify_take_attempt resolve a
typed noun through ObjectWords::refers_to (the parser's own matching rule)
instead of a hand-rolled overlap against the printed name alone, which could
both miss a real referent and wrongly match an unrelated object whose printed
name happened to share a word. Strengthened fixed_in_place's own doc to name
the refusal-reason ambiguity this narrowness still can't close, per this
feature's "record nothing rather than guess" discipline — deliberately not a
phrase-list classifier.

Fix 3: zvm_item_observations/glulx_item_observations bypassed the host's
locked player-id hint (AppState::player_obj), calling each engine's raw
per-turn heuristic directly instead. Added Engine::set_player_hint (mirroring
set_mouse/set_screen_dims/set_default_colours' pattern of pushing a host-known
fact into the session); finish_command_turn's post_turn_bookkeeping calls it
once per turn, right after its own lock attempt, so the following turn's item
observations prefer the hint — the same fallback order vocab::scope_split's
own player_hint parameter already uses.

Fix 4: replaced the hand-copied, mis-sourced TAKE_VERBS list (falsely claimed
to be verb_synonyms's "take" group) with resolution through the story's own
StoryVocabulary::verb_named, mirroring how command_band::story_verbs resolves
its own take-verb — so a synonym like Zork I's dictionary-first `carry`
(or any spelling never in the old hard-coded list) is recognised because it
resolves to the same Verb, not because it happened to be copied into a list.
Also switched the tokenizer from split_whitespace to the shared vocab::words_of,
so "take lamp." now extracts "lamp" instead of "lamp.".

Fix 6: factored reprinted_room_heading's and transcript_room_description's
identical "line, trimmed, equals the room name" predicate into one shared
line_is_room_heading helper (pure refactor, no behavior change).

Fix 7: scott_session's item_observations recorded a dark room's items as
"observed" regardless of darkness — item_indices_in_room doesn't gate on it
itself, and room_block's own layouts never call it at all while Vm::is_dark().
Added the identical gate around the room half (carried items are unaffected,
matching print_inventory).

Each fix falsified by temporarily reverting to the old behavior and confirming
a new test fails with the reported symptom, then restoring: Fix 1/3 against a
real Counterfeit Monkey playthrough (Sigil Street's own unnamed scenery, and
its permanently-unidentifiable avatar), Fix 2 against a synthetic
misattribution case (a "sword"-named object whose printed name never contains
the word, versus a "sword fern" whose printed name does but whose only parser
word is "fern"), Fix 4 against a synonym absent from the old hard-coded list,
Fix 7 against a hand-built dark-room Database (scott's own doc-example
recipe for building one by hand).

grm-akiv: bound table-after-code jump tables by the switch window

The lowest-target rule declines a table stored after the code it
dispatches to (megaman e000: switch e000, cases e003..e0ca, table
e0ed), since every real target is already below the table. Add
JumpTableBound.boundBySwitchWindow, tried when that rule declines:
the real entries point into [switch, tableStart), and the first
entry that points elsewhere is past the table's end. A cut is only
trusted if the next two entries stay outside the window too.

Chosen from a survey of every declined table over check nes: the
window cut is right at all 11 table-after-code sites, including the
owner's megaman 18/19/10, and it is the only signal that catches
over-reads running into the next table's valid code addresses

events.message:
fix(fdc): rate, speed and track length of every profile describe the same track — 360K and FM SD did not, and the FM convention MF-1168 left open is decided (P3-644, MF-1482)

P3-644 named one profile. The identity
rate x 60 / rpm / 8 (FM: / 2) == track_bytes, checked for every profile
of UFT_FDC_FORMATS plus the 1581, was red for 2 of 18:

| Profile | data_rate | rpm | Identity gives | Profile says |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PC 360K | 300K | 300 | 7500 | 6250 |
| FM Single Density | 250K FM | 360 | 2604 | 5208 |

- PC 360K: 300K -> 250K. 300 kbit/s is this disk in a 1.2M drive at
  360 rpm. The profile's own named source says otherwise: greaseweazle
  26690f89 diskdefs_ibm.cfg, `disk 360`: `rate = 250` (default 300 rpm).

- FM SD: 250K -> 500K. The profile comment (MF-1168) had left open, "not
  decided in passing", whether the field means the data rate or the cell
  rate for FM entries. It is decided here with evidence:
  - Dave Dunfield, IMD.SRC |MODE|, defines the rates as FDC transfer
    rates: "00 = 500 kbps FM ... kbps indicates transfer rate, not the
    data rate, which is 1/2 for FM".
  - UFT_FDC_BBC_DFS already follows that definition (250K FM at 300 rpm
    = 3125 bytes).
  - FM SD's own raw_bits (83333 at 360 rpm = 500 000 cells/s) require it.
  - The real 8" capture tests/corpus/kor_a (1979, LOCAL-ONLY) carries its
    26 x 128 FM track 0 as IMD mode 0 = "500 kbps FM". Its Applesauce
    imaging log says "SS500kbps FM+MFM".
  The old note stays and the decision is added below it. The enum comment
  for 300K now names the 1.2M drive at 360 rpm.

Red first: tests/test_fdc_rate_passt_zur_spur.c was 2 of 18 red before;
after the fix 18/18. Mutation matrix 2/2. The 9 fdc/gap/profile tests
stay green. data_rate is read only by uft_fdc_list_formats() (display).

events.message:
fix(workflow): the PAUSE button, which nothing ever enables, now says why — and P3-643 is corrected, it read the handler instead of its reachability (P3-643, MF-1481)

P3-643 said the PAUSE button shows "paused" while the job keeps
running. That is not what happens. The finding read onPauseClicked()
and missed whether it can be reached. Measured with git grep btnPause:
- forms/tab_workflow.ui switches the button off (enabled=false);
- the WorkflowTab constructor switches it off as well;
- nothing anywhere switches it on.

The button is therefore grey at all times, during a run too, and its
handler never runs. The operator never sees a false "paused".

What remained was smaller:
- a grey button with no reason given;
- the comment "// Only enabled during operation", which is false.
No job has a pause point either: DecodeJob, FluxWriteJob and
FluxCaptureJob only know requestCancel.

The button now stays off with a tooltip that names the reason and points
to the way that works (ABORT). The comment is corrected. The unreachable
handler is marked, not removed (MF-1077): wiring it needs a pause point
in the jobs first. P3-643 is rewritten as BERICHTIGT, with its original
wording kept.

Red first: test_honest_stubs_stay_honest::workflowPauseSaysWhyItIsOff
was red before (no tooltip). After the fix the suite is 7/7, run
offscreen (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen) as the GUI smoke test.

events.title: corpus(kfx): eight Sierra disks enter the corpus as flux — six with the protection track named in advance by two independent sources (P3-651, MF-1476)
events.message:
corpus(kfx): eight Sierra disks enter the corpus as flux — six with the protection track named in advance by two independent sources (P3-651, MF-1476)

The owner pointed at a local copy of the archive.org item
20220303_20220303_0527 — digitoxin's "Sierra On-Line PC Floppy Disk Image
Collection", 18 GB, of which 294 archives are flux sets holding 157 632
`.raw` files with the magic `\r\x04…`: KryoFlux streams.

Measured before anything was copied:

    [!]  verified from two matching dumps      228
    [cp] original copy protected                62
    [M]  sectors modified                       44
    [w]  weak sectors                            9
    [U]  unmodified, sector-level duplication    6
    [MW] modified by Windows                     5
    [INC] a flux set is missing                  4

── What was taken, and why exactly that ─────────────────────────────

Not whole sets (40 MB for eight). Per disk: the track that
`tracklayout.txt` singles out, plus track 0 as an in-set control, plus
every accompanying report. 8 disks, 22 raw files, 5.6 MB, 23 reports.

The selection rests on two sources that agree, which is the point:

    disk               tracklayout.txt says        dtc_log.txt says
    bc_quest_tires     38-38:80,50,80  deviates    38.0: MFM: <mismatch>, *N
    frogger            1-1:0,140,100   deviates    01.0: MFM: <mismatch>, *N
    ulysses_1          1-1:0,140,100   deviates    01.0: MFM: <mismatch>, *N
    kq_tandy           38-38 deviates (both sides) 38.0: MFM: <mismatch>
    kq_tandy_pcjr      38-38 deviates (both sides) 38.0: MFM: <mismatch>
    story_maker        38-38 deviates (both sides) 38.0: MFM: <mismatch>
    champ_boxing       uniform (the [w] case)      all tracks OK
    coming_attractions uniform (the control)       all tracks OK

The preserver's layout and the reference tool's own log name the same
track. That gives a falsifiable expectation with numbers: on the ordinary
tracks UFT must find the stated sector count (8 or 9), and on the
protection track it must NOT report a clean sector set — the reference
tool itself cannot decode it as plain MFM.

`dtc_log.txt` is worth its own line: it carries a per-track verdict with
sector counts, so it is a reference PER TRACK without running `dtc` (which
`docs/ORACLES.md` lists as proprietary, execution-only). Three sets also
carry a `gw_log.txt` — the same disk dumped a second time with
Greaseweazle.

── A silent wrong file, caught before it was registered ─────────────

The first extraction keyed the archive entries by BASENAME. `Ulysses and
the Golden Fleece` holds two disks in two subdirectories — Disk 1 `[cp]`
and Disk 2 `[!]` — with 43 basenames appearing twice. It silently took the
LAST, i.e. the UNPROTECTED Disk 2, and would have written its hash under a
claim about copy protection. No crash, no warning.

Rewritten to be path-aware, one set per subdirectory, `tracklayout.txt`
read from the same directory, and a disk counts as protected only when its
OWN folder name carries `[cp]`. Proven, not assumed:

    Disk 1     080c739649c3ff1f   94 595 byte
    Disk 2     8ea66c9d6339c72e   94 463 byte
    extracted  080c739649c3ff1f   94 595 byte

── Licence: the established channel, verified twice ─────────────────

The item carries NO licence field and the content is copyrighted Sierra /
Tandy software. So: LOCAL-ONLY, exactly as the WOZ pair in MF-1468 —
hash and provenance in the repo, the file itself never redistributed.

Verified both ways before committing: `git check-ignore` on every one of
the 45 files reports ignored, and `git status tests/corpus/` shows
nothing. This commit carries text only.

Each entry's `source` names the archive.org item, the containing archive
with its SHA-256 for re-acquisition, the folder inside it, the
tracklayout line that justifies the file, and the verbatim `dtc` verdict
for that track. Each `content` line states what was measured, including
the stream's own OOB block — `name=KryoFlux DiskSystem, version=2.20s,
sck=24027428.5714285` — so the firmware and sample clock come from the
file, not from a label.

── Two gates fired, both correctly, one of them mine ────────────────

    audit_korpus_inhalt   67 without a content line, baseline 45 -> OK
    audit_korpus_regal    26 unregistered, baseline 1 -> 3
    audit_korpus_herkunft 0 findings

Tor 59 is my own from MF-929, and it caught exactly the 22 entries I had
added without a content claim. The regal gate caught the 23 reports; they
are now registered with `format: "n/a"`, following the existing entry
`tests/corpus/kor_a/… Imaging Log.txt`.

The remaining 3 are pre-existing `fluxfox_*` files and are NOT mine. The
baseline stays at 1: lowering it because the number currently looks good
would be the metric as motive (MF-1077). Registered as P3-651, with the
provenance explicitly NOT filled in by a plausible guess.

── No metric moved, and that is the honest state ────────────────────

    T1 9, T1b 69, T2 8, T3 1 — unchanged
    kfx still T1b

All 45 entries carry an empty `test` field, because no test consumes them
yet. 46 of 192 corpus images now have no consuming test, 45 of them mine.
That is a debt, stated rather than hidden: `kfx` reaches T1 when a test
opens one of these through `uft_disk_open()` and asserts the plugin — and
that test is likely to be RED, because `uft_kfx_read_stream()` is a stub
(P3-640). The expectation for it is already derived above.

events.title: test(a2r): both container layouts now run against real captures — and the v2 path never applied the reference rule at all (P3-656, MF-1483)
events.message:
test(a2r): both container layouts now run against real captures — and the v2 path never applied the reference rule at all (P3-656, MF-1483)

A2R carries flux in two DIFFERENT container layouts: A2R2 uses `STRM`,
A2R3 uses `RWCP`. Not two variants of one layout — two layouts.
`src/parsers/a2r/uft_a2r_parser.c` names both. Named is not tested.

Measured before this commit: the corpus held THREE a2r images and all
three were A2R3 with `RWCP`. The `STRM` half had never seen a single byte
of real data anywhere in the tree. A reader whose one half never ran
against data is inventory, not capability (MF-627/767).

    layout        before                    after
    STRM (A2R2)   0 captures in the tree    3, drive type 1
    RWCP (A2R3)   3, none earning a tier    3, all three credited
    a2r           T2                        T1   (summary T1 10->11, T2 8->7)

── The three new captures ───────────────────────────────────────────

From archive.org item `Fahey_Set_2019-07` (collection flux_compilations,
50 Applesauce captures). LOCAL-ONLY as usual: hash and provenance in the
repo, the files never redistributed.

Its `files.xml` carries md5, crc32 and sha1 per file, and all three were
RECOMPUTED here before anything was taken over: md5, sha1 and size match
for each. A supplied hash nobody checked is a claim, not evidence.

── What the mutation matrix found, which a green test would have hidden ──

There is no red proof — no defect in what the test asserts. For new test
code the honest substitute is the matrix. The FIRST attempt scored 0/3:
M1 and M2 fell NOTHING.

That is a finding about the mutation, not the test. Measured by hand:
mutate `a2r_location_deuten()`, watch the compiler rebuild the object,
and the geometry of an A2R2 capture stays 141x1. The v2 path never calls
that rule.

`parse_strm_chunk()` (uft_a2r_parser.c:409) assigns
`track_number = location & 0xFF` RAW and sets `side = 0` — and its own
comment says why: the decomposition `(track << 1) + side` is in the
**3.x** reference; whether it holds for A2R **2** is in the separate
"A2R 2.x" reference, and that one has never been read. `side = 0` is
marked "NICHT belegt". Exemplary honesty — and **`MF-1319` appeared ZERO
times in docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md**: an honestly named unknown that no register
tracks never gets scheduled. Now P3-656.

Rewritten to mutate what actually decides the outcome — line 409 for v2,
the rule for v3 — the matrix scores **3/3**, each mutation felling
exactly its own assertion, parser file restored byte-identical.

A third expectation of mine was also wrong: M3's decomposition removal
fells only ONE case, because drive type 4 goes 40 -> 80 and 80 is below
my threshold of 100.

── The corpus entry that looked fixed and was not ───────────────────

`kor_a` has earned NOTHING since MF-1066. That commit entered the test
name into an explanatory paragraph, and the tier computation compares for
character equality (MF-1332). All three A2R3 fields now carry the name
verbatim; 606 + 95 + 95 characters of prior text moved to `content`
rather than being deleted.

And a mistake of my own, caught in the act: my first expression replaced
`kor_a`'s WHOLE field value, because the string "noch keiner" occurred
inside its explanation ("hier stand 'noch keiner'"). That deleted
`test_fm_echte_aufnahme`. Recovered from HEAD and decided per entry. An
expression that judges by a text fragment judges the text, not the thing.

── What the test does NOT assert, stated in the test ────────────────

It does not verify the reference rule for v2. All three A2R2 captures are
drive type 1, where raw and correct coincide — measured across ALL 50
Fahey files: 50 of 50 are A2R2 and 50 of 50 are drive type 1. A
TWO-SIDED A2R2 capture would expose the difference; the corpus has none.

Carrying the v3 rule over to v2 would set one unevidenced number against
another — the same case as interleave 12 in P3-434 — so it was not done.

Also corrected: the plugin's comment claimed the reader had decomposed
locations "nach der Referenzregel" for both paths. True for v3 only.

── Verification ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    test_a2r_blockarten   47 assertions, 0 failures, 6 captures
    mutation matrix       3/3 (first attempt 0/3, see above)
    ctest                 581/581, 2 named skips, 0 failures
    generator             0 warnings about a2r (was 3)

events.title: fix(kfx): a KryoFlux index block carries no running position — comparing it to the byte counter rejected every capture KryoFlux hardware itself had written (P3-655, MF-1479)
events.message:
fix(kfx): a KryoFlux index block carries no running position — comparing it to the byte counter rejected every capture KryoFlux hardware itself had written (P3-655, MF-1479)

`uft_disk_open_ranked()` reported **0 claimants** for four real KryoFlux
streams: not one plugin took them, in a format named after the device that
produced them. The two streams already in the corpus — one written by HxC,
one by Greaseweazle — opened fine.

── The defect ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`verify_stream_position()` held the position field of StreamInfo, **Index**
and StreamEnd alike against the running flux-byte counter. An Index block
carries no running position: its first u32 points at the flux value DURING
which the index pulse fell — a back-reference, not the counter's state
where the block sits. The check compared two different quantities.

Replicating UFT's own check outside the tree:

    hxcfe_kfx_t00.0.raw          0 breaks  -> opened
    fluxfox track00.0.raw        0 breaks  -> opened
    sierra bc_quest_tires t00    6 breaks  -> rejected
    sierra ulysses_1 t01         3 breaks  -> rejected

Every break sat on an Index block. None on StreamInfo or StreamEnd — those
match 7 of 7 exactly in the same files. The deviations run UPWARD (+3567,
+2556, +1545, +537, …), i.e. to a position past the block.

── Why the files are right and UFT was wrong ────────────────────────

These streams were written by KryoFlux's own hardware (`name=KryoFlux
DiskSystem, version=2.20s, sck=24027428.5714285`, read from the stream's
own OOB block), and `dtc` — same vendor, their own reader — decoded them
without error; the log ships inside every archive with a per-track verdict
and sector counts. Writer and reader of the same hand agree; only UFT
disagreed. That is the *Spec* channel with the witness on the right side
(MF-1179), and it settles the authority question without guessing.

── Three wrong hypotheses, each killed by a measurement ─────────────

Worth recording, because the third is the one that decided it:

1. "My corpus is the first witness against the 65535 truncation" — WRONG.
   The existing KF files are also over 64K (115631 / 115743 / 127987). I
   nearly wrote that claim down.
2. "It is the probe window" — WRONG. `hxcfe` opens with its first index at
   byte 38128; sierra is rejected with its first index at 8376. Earlier,
   not later. Position is not it.
3. "It is real-hardware versus HxC-generated" — WRONG. The real
   Greaseweazle capture that has been in the corpus for weeks opens. That
   third measuring point is the one that pointed at the Index block, and I
   only added it because the first two explanations had fallen.

── The test ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`tests/test_kfx_sierra_schutzspur.c` — red first, for exactly this reason
(4 failures, 16 passes), green after (52 passes, 0 failures).

It uses `uft_disk_open_ranked()` rather than `uft_disk_open()`, so a NULL
says WHO claimed the stream instead of only "did not work". That is what
produced "0 claimants" and pointed the search at the probe rather than at
the file. A measurement that maps two different causes onto the same value
sends the search to the wrong place (MF-1468).

What it pins, using two independent references that agree — the
preserver's `tracklayout.txt` and `dtc`'s own log, both naming the SAME
track as deviating:

  * the plugin must win the probe race (`uft_format_plugin_kfx`)
  * the stream must arrive COMPLETE (`raw_len == file size`, MF-919)
  * no invented claim: 0 sectors, `UFT_ENC_UNKNOWN`
  * one file is one track: `read_track(1,0)` must refuse

And it pins the limit INVERTED: dtc says track 0 has 9 sectors and track
38 is `<mismatch>`; UFT says 211818 raw bytes / 0 sectors and 218918 raw
bytes / 0 sectors. **UFT cannot yet tell the protected track from the
ordinary one through this path.** That is honest, and the assertions break
the day someone decodes — forcing the dtc numbers to be entered rather
than the limit quietly moved.

── Metric ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    kfx  T1b -> T1        (summary T1 9 -> 10, T1b 69 -> 68)

Earned by a real capture with `origin: real`, not by a foreign-generated
image. Four manifest entries now name the consuming test; the other 18
Sierra files keep an empty `test` field, because no test opens them.

── Not fixed, deliberately ──────────────────────────────────────────

P3-655: the Index position is now UNCHECKED, not worthless. Checking it
properly means holding it against the accumulated FLUX VALUES and
verifying it falls inside the revolution between two index pulses — that
needs the flux decoder, not the stream checker, so it is its own
intervention with its own measurement.

- VGA: "VGA" submenu with 31 kHz (standard), 15 kHz RGB and 15 kHz with
  CSync (the framework's retro15kHz/csync outputs) and scanlines 25/50/75%

- Zoom-in: the M2M crop.vhd is made for the C64 picture and cropped the
  wrong area. The core now blanks everything but the graphics area:
  gstshifter.v outputs PIX_ACTIVE (from the first reload with DE until the
  last pixels are shifted out, delayed like R/G/B), the lines with DE of
  the previous frame are the vertical window. Verilator with EmuTOS
  (CROP=1): exactly 640x200, first pixel column and last column correct.
- Floppies: "Swap floppy A: and B:" (floppy_swap.vhd): the FDC is told
  about both images again with their stored sizes. The read-only flag of
  an image now only write-protects its own drive (before: both). GHDL test
  CORE/sim/floppy_swap.
- Hard disks: fast seek in the firmware (M2M/rom/vd_fastseek.asm): seeks
  start at the current position or at a checkpoint (the cluster of every
  2 MB, first 1 GB) instead of the start of the file. Test in the QNICE
  emulator (CORE/sim/fastseek): FAT32 image with fragmented files, random
  reads and writes compared with f32_fseek, 7.5x faster on 6 MB (grows
  with the image size). Heap reduced by 2560 words for the tables.
- tools/make_st_disk.py: blank formatted .st images (360k to 1.44M),

- README: floppy, video and MT32-pi (MIDI via the PMOD to the Pi's GPIO

events.title: fix(d88): a single-sided table is read the way it is laid out, the geometry comes from the table, and status 0xE0/0x10 are findings — decided by an executed hxcfe (P3-652 b-d, MF-1480)
events.message:
fix(d88): a single-sided table is read the way it is laid out, the geometry comes from the table, and status 0xE0/0x10 are findings — decided by an executed hxcfe (P3-652 b-d, MF-1480)

Three open parts of P3-652, each decided by a foreign reader. None is
decided by this plugin.

(c) Track table of 1D/1DD (media 0x30/0x40). The plugin always used
cyl*2+head. How the others read it:

| Reader | How known | Reads the table as |
|---|---|---|
| MAME d88_dsk.cpp (BSD-3, both load paths) | read | track*head_count+head, head_count 1: sequential |
| hxcfe d88_loader.c | executed (hxcfe.exe, D88 -> IMD) | sequential: entries 0,1,2 of a 1DD image on cylinders 0,1,2, head 0 |
| greaseweazle d88.py (Unlicense) | read | always index // 2, whatever the media byte says |

Both layouts are now kept apart by the table itself. A single-sided
table that uses an odd entry can only be sequential. One that uses only
even entries is the cyl*2 layout; read sequentially, every odd cylinder
would be empty. floptool is no oracle here: its `flopconvert d88 pc`
gives 163 840 zero bytes even for the real hxcfe_pc160.d88 (measured).

(d) Geometry. open() reported 80 x 2 for every 2D image. It now takes
the geometry from the table: the foreign tests/corpus_free/
hxcfe_pc160.d88 (entries 0,2,..,78) opens as 40 x 1 x 8.

(b) Status. hxcfe, executed on a track with each status code, emitted:
- 0x10: a deleted sector (IMD type 4);
- 0xE0 ("no address mark"): a record without ID of type 0, i.e. the
  sector cannot be found.
The plugin reported both as clean sectors. It now marks them deleted and
unavailable ("not readable", with the reason the consistency gate asks
for since H-30); the bytes in the file stay.

0xF0 stays open. hxcfe's own IMD output carries its data as a normal
sector, against its own comment "no data mark". That is two statements
from the same hand, not a decision.

Two tests used exactly the wrong geometry as their fixture. They are
rewritten, not deleted:
- test_d2_bruecke_am_korpus expected 120 and 80 failed tracks on
  hxcfe_pc160.d88 and hxcfe_uftk_nec_2d.d77. Those were tracks the
  plugin invented by guessing 80 x 2. The two clean files now pin 0
  failed tracks. The case the test exists for (a failed read_track is
  one NOTE per run, never a WARN) now runs on a copy of hxcfe_pc160.d88
  whose table entries for C10..C14 are zeroed ("0 = unformatted" inside
  the geometry): 5 tracks, 1 run, counted by the test itself. 37/37.
- test_disk_analyzer_no_fiction does the same through the GUI: the clean
  file shows no TRACK_UNREADABLE, and the copy shows exactly
  "[note] TRACK_UNREADABLE: C10..C14 H0: ". PASS, not skipped (checked
  by running the single function).

Red first: tests/test_d88_tafel_und_status.c was 5 of 5 red before;
after the fix 7/7, including two controls (status 0x00; a 1DD image
with only even entries). Mutation matrix 5/5. test_d88_spur_nach_kopf
4/4, and the 52 d88/d77/pc98/convert/probe/api tests stay green.

events.title: grm-v60.1: resolve constant-pointer indirect jumps; keep jump-table overrides on the owning function
events.message:
grm-v60.1: resolve constant-pointer indirect jumps; keep jump-table overrides on the owning function

IndirectJumpConstantPointerAnalyzer resolves a JMP (ptr) when a straight-line
path proves both pointer bytes constant. The walk starts at each direct store
to the pointer, steps into JSR (so ffbe's STA $FFCC,Y is seen with a known Y),
follows JMP abs, and stops at any conditional branch. After a store to
non-writable memory (a possible bank switch) it only continues through
instructions whose bytes are identical in every bank. The target gets a
COMPUTED_CALL reference in the jump's own space (where a direct JMP would put
it) and a function scheduled at the normal function priority.

On dragonpower/shenlong this resolves RESET's ffed JMP ($0017) = $8008, so the
main program from 82ac is disassembled, including the six JSR $9913 sites
grm-wayn needs. No other NES row resolves a site.

The newly reachable code exposed a JumpTableBoundAnalyzer order bug: an
override written while a switch sat in a caller's body (8655 in FUN_82ac) was
stranded once the JSR target became a function (FUN_8645), and the switch was
bounded again, leaving a dead label set (symbols 207 vs 259 run to run).
relocateStaleOverride moves such an override onto the current owner, called
from the bound analyzer and from the new JumpTableOverrideRelocatorAnalyzer
on function creation.

events.message:
feat(app): track each item's origin, current location and vanished state (SQ-1627)

Sibling feature to SQ-1625 (room descriptions), item-keyed instead of
room-keyed, with the same per-turn-capture / mapper-persisted /
serde(default) back-compat shape.

mapper::graph gets ItemKey (an alias for the same u32 identity space
grammar_model::ObjectWords::id already uses per engine — object
number/address/item index), ItemLocation (Room{room,direct}/Carried/
Vanished) and ItemRecord (name, origin room+turn, last_seen+turn,
fixed_in_place), plus MapGraph::note_item_seen/note_item_carried/
note_items_absent/note_item_fixed_in_place. None of the new setters
call touch_layout() — SQ-1625's set_description regression, repeated
on purpose here since these run automatically on every captured turn
too. items: BTreeMap<ItemKey, ItemRecord> is restored via a separate
restore_items() door rather than a from_parts() parameter, mirroring
restore_seam_decisions beside it.

Vanished detection needs TWO room queries, not one, per a correction
mid-quest: an item last reached only by recursing into an OPEN
container (direct: false) must never be marked Vanished when that
container closes and the recursive query can no longer see it — only
an item last seen at the room's own DIRECT top level, absent from a
later direct look and not carried, is a real observed absence. Session
gathers both per engine (Z-machine: two object-tree walks; Glulx/Scott:
one, since neither format can recurse into a container at the read
layer at all) into TurnResult::items, and
session::apply_item_observations orchestrates the update-then-sweep.

Wired into both finish_command_turn and finish_resumed_turn in
host/turn.rs (the exact second call site SQ-1625 missed on its first
pass), never into apply_game_driven_result (no turn number to stamp).

Facet 3: classify_take_attempt structurally detects a take-style
command (verb-synonyms' own "take" group) whose unambiguous noun match
visibly failed to reach Carried, and marks that item fixed_in_place —
never a phrase match against the game's own refusal text, matching
crate::probe::Refusals' documented reasoning. Deliberately incomplete
(most non-takeable items are never tested this way).

Real-game coverage: Zork I's West of House mailbox/leaflet
(stories/zork1-r88-s840726.z3) — verified against the live interpreter
before writing assertions, and it happens to be the exact
container-nesting shape the mid-quest correction is about. Observed-
only guarantee falsified by temporarily widening the Z-machine query
to a global object-tree walk (confirmed it leaks the kitchen's own
items into the registry), then reverted. Every struct_gen guard
falsified the same way as SQ-1625's own regression test.

events.title: fix(app): make resume-slot selection prefer a real resume point over merely-newer (SQ-1626)
events.message:
fix(app): make resume-slot selection prefer a real resume point over merely-newer (SQ-1626)

Follow-up to SQ-1624's split of the auto-save and quick-save slots.
boot_story previously picked whichever slot had the newer Meta::saved_at,
so a clean game-driven quit (exit_clear_resume_save rewrites default.lanthorn
with a fresh saved_at but an EMPTY resume point) always buried an
older-but-real quick save -- defeating the whole point of giving Ctrl+S its
own slot.

- resume_source(game_dir) (crates/app/src/host/boot.rs) is now the ONE place
  the decision is made: a slot with a real resume point always beats one
  without regardless of timestamp; between two that agree, the newer
  Meta::saved_at wins, and an exact same-second tie favors the quick save.
  boot_story calls it directly instead of re-deriving the comparison, so an
  external host asking "what would Continue resume?" can never disagree.
- archive::archive_has_resume_point reads only engine.txt and the game.<ext>
  zip entry's SIZE (no decompression) to answer that cheaply for both slots
  at every boot.
- BootRequest::fresh_start (plus a --fresh-start CLI flag) lets a host skip
  resume selection entirely -- no load, no mapper/aux/command-history pulled
  from whichever slot would otherwise have won -- while leaving both reserved
  files completely untouched on disk.

Falsified all three behavioural fixes by reverting each in turn and
confirming the corresponding new test fails with the expected symptom.

feat(commander): preflight Apply and recover cleanly from failed items

Commander's Apply had no image-side preflight and stopped at the first bad
item: the pane then showed only the error text, the queue still held the edits
that had landed (so a retry failed at edit 1), and the only way out was to
close and reopen the image.

- Apply first scans the queue on a worker: name conflicts (now case-folded
  where the destination folds case), folders blocked by a file, parent folders
  that no longer exist, and allocation-rounded free space. A clean verdict
  applies at once; otherwise a review offers Skip existing / Overwrite.

  reports (without trying) anything under a folder that failed, and stops after
  25 failures in a row.

  remaining queue and the current folder, and shows a report with Retry /
  Discard remaining.

events.title: fix(st): a PC boot sector is no Atari ST evidence — the probe's x86 check stood behind the BPB return and was never reached (P3-653, MF-1478)
events.message:
fix(st): a PC boot sector is no Atari ST evidence — the probe's x86 check stood behind the BPB return and was never reached (P3-653, MF-1478)

st_probe() returned 75 as soon as the BPB described the file. Its own
check "x86 JMP: this is far more likely a PC image of the same size"
came after that return. It was therefore unreachable for every PC image
whose BPB is correct, which means every normal one.

Measured in the tree: a DOS 5.0 720K boot sector as FORMAT writes it got
75 from the ST probe. The docs/SONDEN_DOKTRIN.md cap for a claim without
a format-specific marker is 45. The sector used:
- EB 3C 90, OEM "MSDOS5.0";
- BPB 512/2/1/2/112/1440/F9/3/9/2;
- 55 AA at offset 510.

The x86 check now runs before the BPB return, so the PC sector gets 30.
The same BPB behind a 68000 BRA.S keeps its 75 (control).

Red first: tests/test_st_sonde_pc_bootsektor.c was 1 of 2 red before
(75); after the fix 2/2. The mutation that restores the old order is
red. All other tests stay green.

Not fixed, named in P3-653: 75 (BPB matches) and 65 (BRA.S) without a
marker still exceed the cap of 45. That is the known debt in
docs/sondendoktrin_baseline.txt, and audit_sondendoktrin.py is
unchanged. Converting every branch would also move the 90 for a valid
boot checksum, which two tests pin.

Found by the uft-st-code package review (neue-ideen, t3).

A cross-volume copy staged source names verbatim, so a name the destination
refuses (a '/' on FAT, a 40-char name on HFS, "Icon\r" on FAT, a folder

events.title: feat(fs): generic filename legalizer + validate_name on every editable driver
events.message:
feat(fs): generic filename legalizer + validate_name on every editable driver

Copying between filesystems failed at apply time whenever a source name was
illegal on the destination, and 20 editable drivers never exposed their rules
through validate_name, so nothing could check ahead of the write.

- name_legalize::legalize_name repairs a name for any destination by using its
  validate_name as an oracle: per-character substitution (uppercase, ASCII
  transliteration, '_'/'-'/'.'), structural fixes (trailing dots, reserved
  names, leading letter, extra dots), then length cuts that keep the extension.
  unique_name adds _N suffixes for collisions.
- validate_name overrides for ADFS, Alto, Apple DOS, Atari DOS, CBM, CP/M, DFS,
  DragonDOS, Human68k, JFS, MFS, Minix, OS-9, PFS3, QDOS, RS-DOS, SFS, SquashFS,
  UCSD, UFS and XFS, reusing each driver's existing encoder where it had one.
- ADFS create silently cut names to 9 bytes while rename allowed 10; create,
  mkdir and rename now share one check that also refuses RISC OS path syntax.
- FAT refuses control characters; FAT/exFAT/NTFS refuse DOS device names.
- Host exports go through the same legalizer, so "Icon\r" and "CON" no longer
  fail on Windows while macOS keeps the real Finder "Icon\r".

events.title: fix(commander): resolve staged parent paths whose folder names contain '/'
events.message:
fix(commander): resolve staged parent paths whose folder names contain '/'

Classic Mac volumes allow '/' inside a name (Photoshop's "Acquire/Export",
"Schwarz/Weiss", "MacDRUMS Instruments/Tracks"). Staged edits address their
parent by a '/'-joined path, and apply split it strictly, so any copy into
such a folder failed mid-batch with "directory 'Acquire' not found".

Resolution now walks components and, on a miss, rejoins neighbours with '/'
and backtracks, trying fewest components first so strict paths are unchanged
and a decoy prefix folder cannot capture the files. It also folds case the way
the create-folder step already did. The daemon's resolve_path falls back to the
same walk, and Commander's remote apply escapes literal backslashes.

events.title: fix(d77): a sector's ID is its header's C/H/R/N, a recorded R=0 stays 0, and data length 0 is a sector without data — not the end of the track (P3-652 a, MF-1477)
events.message:
fix(d77): a sector's ID is its header's C/H/R/N, a recorded R=0 stays 0, and data length 0 is a sector without data — not the end of the track (P3-652 a, MF-1477)

D77 is the FM-7 variant of the D88 container. It had the same two
faults that MF-1475 fixed in d88, plus one of its own. d77_read_track():
- gave every sector the physical cylinder/head as its ID, with N
  computed from the data length;
- turned a recorded R=0 into R=1: `if (sec_num > 0) sec_num--` left the
  0 alone, then uft_format_add_sector() added 1;
- ended the track at a header with data length 0, dropping that sector
  and every one after it.

Measured before the fix (red proof tests/test_d77_spur_nach_kopf.c, 3
of 3 red):
- a header C5 H1 R3 N2 came out as C0 H0 R3 N1;
- a recorded R0 came out as R1;
- of three sectors, where the middle one has data length 0, one
  remained.

Reference, the same as MF-1475: MAME src/lib/formats/d88_dsk.cpp
(BSD-3-Clause, read only), d88_format::load(). The ID is hs[0..3] as
recorded; size 0 is a sector without data (data = nullptr). Now the ID
is the header's C/H/R/N. A sector with data length 0 stays with its ID,
marked unavailable, as in d88 and imd, and the track continues.

After the fix 4/4, with the foreign
tests/corpus_free/hxcfe_uftk_nec_2d.d77 as control: 1280 sectors, IDs
equal to the position, R 1..16. Mutation matrix 3/3. P3-652 (a) closed;
(b) to (d) stay open.

events.message:
fix(app): also capture a room description on a resumed turn

SQ-1625 wired session::apply_room_description into finish_command_turn
only. finish_resumed_turn drains through the SAME finish_turn/drain_turn a
submitted command does (per its own doc, "mirrors the post-turn block in
the submit path") and can carry a real TurnResult::description too — e.g.
a Glulx @save/@restore continuation that goes on to print more of the
room. Wire it in there as well, using state.turns unchanged (a resume is
the second half of the SAME command turn, never a new one).

apply_game_driven_result (a char-mode keypress / timed-input interrupt) is
deliberately left alone: it already skips post_turn_bookkeeping because
it is not a completed player turn, and state.turns is never advanced for
it either, so there is no turn number a capture there could be stamped
with — now said explicitly in its own doc.

events.title: fix(d88): a track holds the sectors its own headers name, with their recorded IDs — it read on into the next track and invented a sector (P3-652, MF-1475)
events.message:
fix(d88): a track holds the sectors its own headers name, with their recorded IDs — it read on into the next track and invented a sector (P3-652, MF-1475)

d88_read_track() read `geometry.sectors` sector headers, a count
estimated from the FIRST track, whatever the track itself said. It also
gave every sector the physical cylinder/head as its ID, with N computed
from the data length, and it stopped the track at a header with data
length 0.

Measured before the fix (red proof tests/test_d88_spur_nach_kopf.c, 3
of 3 red):
- a one-sector track C0H1 behind a two-sector C0H0 returned 2 sectors;
  the second carried C1H0's data (0x33) under an invented ID;
- a header C5 H1 R3 N2 came out as C0 H0 R3 N1;
- of three sectors, where the middle one has data length 0, one
  remained.

Reference: MAME src/lib/formats/d88_dsk.cpp (BSD-3-Clause, read only),
d88_format::load():
- the count comes from get_u16le(hs+4) of the first header (0x1000 means
  0x10, "broken vfman converter");
- the ID is hs[0..3] as recorded;
- size 0 is a sector without data (data = nullptr), not the end of the
  track.

Now the count comes from the track's own first header (1..256). The ID
is the header's C/H/R/N. A sector with data length 0 stays with its ID,
marked unavailable, as the IMD plugin marks its type 0, and the track
continues. The reference stands at the code.

After the fix 4/4, with the foreign tests/corpus_free/hxcfe_pc160.d88
as control: 320 sectors, IDs C = track, R 1..8. Mutation matrix 3/3.
The d88/d77/pc98/convert/probe/api tests (40) stay green.

Found by the differential run against the uft-pc98-code package
(neue-ideen, t3). On the real files in the corpus, package and tree read
the same:
- hxcfe_pc160.d88: 320/320;
- hxcfe_uftk_nec_2d.d77: 1280/1280;
- the two FDI files: 1232/1232.
The package itself stays Fundus.

Named open in P3-652:
- d77 has the same ID and length-0 faults;
- status 0xF0/0xE0 is reported as a clean sector;
- the track-table index for 1D/1DD;
- 2D opens as 80 cylinders.

The read_track contract gate (scripts/audit_read_track_contract.py) did
not know uft_format_add_sector_with_id() as an API that allocates
sectors, although it calls uft_track_add_sector(). It therefore reported
the fixed reader as "writes through NULL". The API is added, with a
self-test case: red without it, 77/77 with it.

Also recorded:
- P3-653: the ST probe gives a PC-720K boot sector 75, because its x86
  branch is unreachable; found by the uft-st-code review. That package
  is Fundus.
- P3-641: the fixed 300 rpm in SCP -> HFE is refuted at real captures.
  In the digitoxin Sierra collection (archive.org
  20220303_20220303_0527), 35 of the 38 sets with a notes.txt say
  "Dumped on a 1.2M floppy drive (360 RPM)", none says 300 (35 of 294
  sets; the other 256 say nothing about the speed). Measured by
  the local -37 session.

events.title: Flush what is cleared before a volume is formatted
events.message:
Flush what is cleared before a volume is formatted

The PFS3 and SFS formatters write through a file handle of their own, at
their own block size. The zeros written to clear a partition's first
64 KiB, and a card's first and last mebibyte, went through the caller's
handle and could still be in its buffer when the formatter ran. They
then reached the file when that handle was closed, after the volume,
and took the root block with them.

Whether that happened depended on how much the interpreter buffers.
Python 3.12 writes a block of that size straight through, so the drives
built and booted while this was written were sound. Python 3.13, which
the application image runs, holds it back, and every new PFS3 or SFS
partition lost its root block.

What is cleared is now flushed before a formatter runs, and both
formatters flush their caller's handle themselves before opening their
own. The new tests give every handle a buffer larger than anything they
write, so they fail without this on any version of Python.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: feat: add BBC Micro Model B (#31)
events.message:
feat: add BBC Micro Model B (#31)

* feat: add BBC Micro Model B (WD1770 DFS, Mode 7)

New 6502-based machine: the BBC Micro Model B. Boots the real MOS 1.2 /
BASIC 2 ROMs to the Mode 7 banner and BASIC prompt, with the Acorn 1770 DFS.

Commodity cores:
- m6502: cycle-counted NMOS 6502 (official + stable undocumented opcodes).
- m6522: 6522 VIA (timers, IFR/IER, ports, CA1/CA2/CB1/CB2 handshakes).
- saa5050: teletext generator with character rounding, emitting the doubled
  12x20 cell the BBC's video hardware produces.

Machine (src/machines/bbc/):
- 32K RAM, OS/BASIC ROMs, 16 sideways sockets and the ROMSEL latch.
- Sheila IO decode: CRTC, Video ULA, ROMSEL, System/User VIA, 1770 DFS, Tube.
- IC32 addressable latch; keyboard matrix + option links (boot mode selection);
  column-based CA2 for the MOS's scan.
- Mode 7 (480x500) rendering plus a generic bitmap path for modes 0-6.
- Acorn 1770 DFS interface, .ssd/.dsd codec and disk service, DFS ROM loaded
  through prepare().

Also adds the m6502 debug family (disassembler + DebugService), registry /
model / menu registration, and unit tests for the CPU, VIA, SAA5050, SSD
codec, IO decode and Mode 7 rendering.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): character-based keyboard layout and SN76489 sound

- Route printable keys by the character they produce (event.key) so the BBC's
  own layout types correctly on a PC: its shifted symbols differ (e.g. '*' is
  Shift on the ':' key, not Shift+8; the number row is `! " # $ % & ' ( )`).
  Letters stay positional; the host's physical Shift is no longer mapped, so a
  shifted host key presses the BBC key that actually yields that character.
- Drive the SN76489 from System VIA port A writes (gated by IC32 latch bit 0)
  through the shared AudioMixer, with the anti-alias strategy read from the
  Sound panel, and expose the PSG activity LED.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): hardware-pane DFS toggle, on-screen keyboard, palette/charset

- Hardware pane: fit/remove the Acorn 1770 DFS interface. The DFS ROM is
  fitted at build time, so toggling rebuilds the machine; the drive service
  hides its drives while the interface is absent.
- On-screen skeuomorphic keyboard (red function strip plus the QWERTY deck)
  driving matrix cells directly, with live key highlighting; BREAK resets.
- Display pane gains a 'bbc' palette family (PAL / Measured), and the Memory
  pane a 'bbc' ASCII glyph table (pound sign at 0x60).

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): render modes 0-6 with the cell-major layout and ULA palette

Modes 1-6 rendered as garbage. The hi-res display memory is cell-major, not
linear: one 6845 MA unit is a byte-wide column of eight scanlines, so the byte
for a cell is (MA << 3) | RA and the row address advances by R1. The renderer
now follows the beebwiki address-translation formula, including the IC32 C0/C1
hardware-scroll wrap when the address overruns the top of RAM.

The ULA palette register's logical-colour field also depends on the mode's
colour count (2, 4 or 16), which follows the chars-per-line and clock bits.
Decoding it by the top nibble alone mapped the foreground to black on the
2-colour modes, so modes 0, 3, 4 and 6 came out blank.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): decode multi-bpp bitmap pixels with the ULA's bit interleave

The video ULA interleaves pixel bits across a display byte rather than
packing them contiguously: the top `bpp` bits hold the most-significant
bit of each of the `n` pixels in the byte, then the next group, and so
on. Reading contiguous bit pairs split every logical-1 pixel in modes 1,
2 and 5 into an alternating 1/2 (red/green) pair, corrupting the image.

Decode pixels with the interleave and add regression tests for the 2bpp
(0b01100101 -> 0,3,2,1) and 4bpp (0b10001001 -> 10,1) cases.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(debug): stop repeating PC/SP in the generic register panel

GenericRegisters renders the whole RegisterSnapshot.regs list and then a
separate PC/SP line, but the Z80 and 6502 family services both list SP and
PC among their registers, so every non-Z80 machine (the BBC's 6502, the
CPC's Z80 uses its bespoke panel) showed each of them twice. Filter PC/SP
out of the listed registers — the dedicated line already draws them.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): selectable disc system (8271/1770/none) and sideways ROM pane

Replace the Acorn 1770 on/off checkbox with a "Disk system" dropdown
offering None, the original Acorn DFS (Intel 8271) and the Acorn 1770 DFS,
and expose the Model B's sixteen sideways ROM sockets in the ROM pane.

- Add an Intel 8271 FDC core (command/parameter/result phases at FE80-FE84,
  data-register DRQ handshake, NMI on completion, DskImage-backed) plus the
  Acorn 8271 peripheral. Semantics cross-checked against BeebEm's
  disc8271.cpp: the interrupt is asserted only for Seek/Read/Write/Verify/
  Format/ReadID (never for READ DRIVE STATUS or READ SPECIAL REGISTER), the
  drive-status result is 0x80|drive1|drive0|track0|wp, and "sector not found"
  is 0x1E.
- Fit the DNFS ROM (Acorn DFS 1.20 + NFS 3.60) for the 8271 option; mirror an
  8K sideways ROM across both halves of its 16K socket.
- Route the floppy window (FE80-FE87) to whichever controller is fitted; the
  disk service and the frame probe go through a common BbcDiscController, and
  the Drive pane hides the drives when no interface is present.
- Decode the whole 0xFE20-0xFE2F Video ULA window (A0 selects control vs
  palette): Acorn DFS probes 0xFE28/0xFE29 with a write/read-back.
- ROM pane: new SidewaysRomSlot SPI. The BBC exposes all sixteen sockets (13
  = disc interface ROM, 15 = BASIC); the shell persists per-socket overrides
  in IndexedDB and applies them at build time, and the pane renders them.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): give the 8271 a delayed command completion (busy phase)

BeebEm's 8271 holds BUSY for a short interval (SetTrigger) after a command
finishes, only then raising the result and the interrupt — it does not
complete the instant the last parameter is written. Model that: a completed
command enters a BUSY phase with a queued result that a cycle countdown
applies.

- Add `tick(cycles)` to BbcDiscController; the machine drives it at the
  1 MHz disc clock from the per-instruction VIA tick (the WD179x has no such
  timer, so its tick is a no-op).
- The 8271 queues the result/idle transition and holds BUSY (0x80) for
  COMPLETION_CYCLES before delivering it. Seek/Read/Write/Verify/Format/ReadID
  use the delay; READ DRIVE STATUS / READ SPECIAL REGISTER still return a
  result immediately and without interrupting, and SPECIFY / WRITE SPECIAL
  REGISTER finish immediately.
- Extend the core tests with a `done()` helper that advances the disc clock.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): Mode 7 OCR overlay, BASIC listing, 5.25" drive sound

The BBC was missing the two pull-on-demand UI features every other machine
has, plus two smaller nits.

- Add a Mode 7 screen-text OCR engine (src/ocr/bbc.ts): the teletext field
  is read straight from the 40x25 SAA5050 codes rather than recognised from
  pixels, mirroring the renderer's MA-to-address mapping and its
  colour/mosaic state machine. Wired as the frame probe's transcribe driver
  (blanking matched cells to their paper colour) and as the machine's
  ocrScreenForMcp, so both the TEXT overlay and the MCP ocr tool work.
  Bitmap modes 0-6 are not transcribed yet (they would need the OS font).
- Add a BASIC II detokeniser (src/basic/bbc-basic-parser.ts) and expose it
  through the probe's basicListing, so the BASIC Listing pane fills in.
- Publish the 5.25" floppy-sound profile — BBC DFS drives are 5.25" units.
- Make the "Disk system" hardware row span both columns (as the Ace's does).

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* feat(bbc): BASIC variables pane, aligned like the register panels

Add parseBbcBasicVariables(): BBC BASIC II keeps variables in a heap indexed
by a first-character chain table at &0480, plus a separate resident-integer
block (A%-Z%) and a fixed FOR-control stack at &0500. Decode number (float
and integer), string, array and live for-next variables and wire the result
through the frame probe's basicVars.

Reformat the BASIC Variables pane into two aligned columns (name, value) so
the "=" lines up down the pane, like the Z80 register panel, instead of the
ragged `name = value` text.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): transfer 8271 data one byte per disc-clock interval

BeebEm drives the 8271 data register off a per-byte timer
(TIMEBETWEENBYTES): each byte is offered a fixed interval apart and
re-raises the interrupt. Our core delivered a whole sector the instant a
read/write command started, so the Acorn DFS's per-byte NMI handler ran an
arbitrary number of times and its byte counter (READNO) barely advanced —
the DFS then read far past the end of the disc and aborted with a
"Disk fault 1E at 50/00".

Arm a byte countdown on the 1 MHz disc clock: beginRead/Write queue the
first byte, `tick` offers each subsequent byte (re-raising DRQ) and
completes once the last is serviced. The DNFS now boots a disc — the
Plotmate Welcome Disk's !BOOT runs — instead of faulting.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): drive the Acorn 1770 from NMI and fix its control latch

Make the Model B 1770 DFS work end to end:

- The Acorn 1770 interface wires DRQ and command completion to the CPU's
  NMI line; Acorn DFS 2.26 transfers each sector byte from an NMI handler,
  so give WD179x an optional onInterrupt with a per-byte cadence on the
  1 MHz disc clock plus completion edges for Type I/II/III commands (and
  for commands that fail before transferring). BbcMachine wires it to
  cpu.nmi(); the polled hosts (+D, Beta Disk, Einstein) are unchanged.
- The drive-control latch at &FE80 is write-only and floats high. The DFS
  presence probe reads it and requires a bit set, so stop echoing the
  written value (it previously concluded no controller was fitted and the
  machine fell back to the ROM/tape filing system).
- Drive select is bit 1 = drive 1 (not a binary number) and reset is
  active low.
- List the disc-interface and language (BASIC) ROMs first in the ROM pane.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* test(bbc): cover a read across a track boundary on the 1770

Pin the Citadel 2 loading case: its CitBits file runs from LBA 137 to
142, so the DFS reads track 13 sector 9, STEPs onto track 14 and then
reads sectors 0-2. The test drives the peripheral the way the DFS does,
including waiting for the completion edge on the 1 MHz disc clock before
issuing the STEP (otherwise the still-busy controller drops it).

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>

* fix(bbc): disc boot, sound, bitmap-mode OCR, border and keyboard

Discs
- Default to no keyboard links (*FX255 = &FF): a plain BREAK no longer
  auto-boots (and faults on an empty drive); SHIFT+BREAK does.
- Loading a disc into drive 0 performs a SHIFT+BREAK auto-boot, and the
  library's disk boot holds SHIFT through the reset.
- Keep the partial last track of truncated .ssd/.dsd files and pad them
  to the 40/80 tracks the DFS catalogue declares.
- Offer blank DFS discs (SS/DS, 40/80 track) in the drive's New menu
  instead of the +3/CPC DSK formats.

Sound
- Latch the slow-bus byte into the SN76489 when IC32 latch 0 strobes /WE
  low, matching the MOS's write sequence; nothing reached the chip before.

Video
- Draw each bitmap-mode scanline twice in the 512-line buffer and take the
  row pitch from CRTC R9, blanking the gap lines of modes 3 and 6.
- Render into a black-bordered 768x576 buffer so the Border setting crops
  it like the CPC's.
- TEXT overlay and MCP OCR in modes 0-6: match cells against the MOS font
  (normal and inverse video) and anchor the overlay to the mode's grid.

UI
- Model B keyboard layout: ESCAPE/TAB, CTRL beside CAPS LOCK, cursor
  cluster, BREAK after f9, edge-to-edge caps filling the pane, olive
  cursor/COPY keys, indicator lamps; clicks now raise the keyboard
  interrupt so they type. Map @, _ and £ to their BBC keys.
- Dedicated 6502 register panel (no Z80 EI/DI/IM fields).
- No Spectrum colour stripe on pane title bars in BBC mode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(bbc): SN76489 stereo split, true 1x scale, blended Mode 7

Sound
- SN76489 stereo placement of its three tone channels (Mono/ABC/ACB/
  BAC/BCA/CAB/CBA, noise centred) with per-side AC coupling and filter.
  Own 'sn-stereo' setting, default Mono (the chip is mono); offered as
  "PSG Channels" on the BBC Micro and MTX. The BBC now also shows the
  Filter control it already read.

Video
- One buffer line per TV scanline: 768x288 (640x256 picture + border)
  shown at half width like the CPC, so 1x is really 1x. Bitmap modes are
  no longer line-doubled.
- Mode 7 at 10 lines per row: each line blends the SAA5050's two
  interlaced half-lines (ink / 50% / paper), keeping the character
  rounding. OCR overlay, text layout and border crop follow.

UI
- Keyboard indicator lamps sit below their legends.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

events.title: Create, partition and write drives of 128 GB and beyond
events.message:
Create, partition and write drives of 128 GB and beyond

A partitioned drive could be created with one FFS partition, and the FFS
formatter stopped at the 25 bitmap blocks the root block names, which is
about 50 MB. A bare hardfile stopped at 4 GB, the image was built in
memory before it was written, and nothing could add a partition or put an
image on a card. A drive can now be any size up to 2 TB.

Creating a drive:

- File -> New -> New Image -> Partitioned drive opens a partition editor.
  Each partition has a device name, a volume name, a filing system, a
  size, a boot flag and a priority, and one with no size takes what the
  others leave. The server plans the layout after every change, so the
  editor shows exactly what would be written and says what is wrong.
- A starting layout and the filing system for its large partitions are
  offered and not chosen: PFS\3, PDS\3 or SFS\0.
- FFS is kept to 4 GB for one partition in the editor, which names PFS3
  instead. The engine still formats larger FFS volumes when asked to.
- Sizes are counted in powers of 1024. An image can be sized for a card
  of a labelled size, or for an attached card to the byte.
- A drive image is a sparse file. A new 128 GB drive is made in under a
  second and takes a few megabytes, and about 40 MB with Workbench on it.
- A raw drive image can hold one PFS3 or SFS volume with no partition
  table.

Handlers:

- A drive is given the handlers its partitions need, as FSHD and LSEG
  blocks in the Rigid Disk Block, so a drive with PFS3 partitions boots
  on a machine that has never had PFS3 installed.
- pfs3aio 19.2 is shipped in app/handlers with its BSD-4-Clause licence.
  Any other handler is supplied through Tools -> Filing-system handlers,
  from a file or from a drive that carries one. In the web host each
  owner keeps supplied handlers to themselves.

Changing a drive, from Tools -> Partitions:

- Add a partition in unused room, format one in any filing system,
  rename one, change how it boots, or remove it.
- Make a drive image larger, or claim the rest of a card that is larger
  than its partition table says.
- Each change to an image is one undo point. A table carrying a bad-block
  list or drive initialisation code is read and not rewritten.

Real cards, in the Linux desktop:

- Initialise, in the attached drive list, partitions and formats a card
  in place and opens it for writing, so Workbench and software are
  installed straight onto it.
- File -> Write image to attached drive writes only what the image holds,
  clears the start of the card and its last mebibyte, and reads back
  what it wrote.
- File -> Save drive image to a file saves a drive, one partition or a
  wrapped volume without its empty space. Save image does the same for
  a drive image of 2 GB or more.

Fixed on the way:

- The Rigid Disk Block was written with the vendor text and the last
  table block in the wrong fields, and without the cylinder limits.
  Partitions mounted, but HDToolBox showed nonsense. The layout now
  follows devices/hardblocks.h. A drive written by an earlier release is
  still read, and is put right when its table is next changed.
- MaxTransfer is 0x1FE00 on new partitions, which is what the IDE ports
  of an A600, A1200 and A4000 need.
- Export as -> Partitioned drive rounded the partition up to a whole
  cylinder, which moves where FFS looks for the root block. The partition
  is now exactly the volume's size, and both conversions copy only what
  the volume holds.
- The SFS allocator read every bitmap block of a volume to place one
  file, which took four seconds a file on 100 GB.
- An unformatted partition of many gigabytes was searched block by block
  for a root block.
- A sparse drive image is compressed in its download ZIP.

Checked on an emulated A1200 with Kickstart 3.1: a 128 GB drive built
here, with Workbench 3.1 installed onto a PFS3 partition, booted to the
end of its startup with the handler loaded from the drive. PFS\3, PDS\3
and FFS partitions all mounted, and what the machine then wrote to them
read back and validated here. amitools reads the partition table and the
FFS volumes with bitmap extension blocks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
