events.title: fix(tiers): a corpus format name no plugin carries was dropped in silence — and my own WOZ entries were among the losers (P3-646..648, MF-1474)
events.message:
fix(tiers): a corpus format name no plugin carries was dropped in silence — and my own WOZ entries were among the losers (P3-646..648, MF-1474)

`gen_verification_tiers.py` joins the corpus manifest to the plugin table
on `p["symbol"]`. A `format` value that matches no symbol is therefore
never looked up — the entry simply vanishes. Both neighbours of that
lookup do warn: a missing provenance warns, a test that exists but is not
attributed to the plugin warns. Only the name did not. That asymmetry is
the defect.

Measured on the real manifest: 5 names, 10 files.

    n/a                      1   a capture log — deliberately not a format
    none                     1   negative fixture without a magic — likewise
    protection:copylock_st   6   protection evidence, namespaced on purpose
    kfraw                    1   MISCLASSIFIED — the plugin is `kfx`
    fat12_fs                 1   names nothing anywhere (P3-647)

So eight of the ten are deliberate, and the function therefore COUNTS
rather than judges. An allow-list for the deliberate three would be the
enumeration that has gone stale four times in this tree (MF-636).

── The gate corrected its own author ────────────────────────────────

My first hand count said 10 names / 17 files. It compared against the
DISPLAY names from `gen_format_list.py --md`, not against `p["symbol"]`
— so `adf_ext`, `cpm`, `dsk_cpc`, `msx_disk` and `sap_thomson` looked
broken and are valid. Whoever does not take the connector the code takes
measures something else (class MF-1177). The docstring records both
numbers, because the wrong one is the more instructive.

`gen_fs_tiers.py` is not a second consumer: it keys the manifest on the
BASENAME and never reads `format` (measured). The field has exactly one
connector.

── The metric moved, and here is why it was allowed to ──────────────

    T1   8 -> 9        `woz` T1b -> T1
    T1b 70 -> 69

Not from the rename. `tests/test_woz_echte_aufnahme.c` already opened the
two real Applesauce captures through `uft_disk_open()`, but never named
`uft_format_plugin_woz` — so the generator reported "no tier credit" for
both, wörtlich, on my own MF-1468 entries. In MF-1436 I had learned that
exact lesson and did not apply it here.

The added line is not bookkeeping: without it the test passed when a
FOREIGN plugin won the probe race. Now it asserts the winner.

    CHECK sites   5 -> 6
    run           8 passed, 0 failed, three files, plugin "WOZ" each time

`kfraw` -> `kfx` deliberately moves NOTHING: `test_external_integration`
reads that file with plain fopen/fread and calls `uft_kf_init()`, so it
verifies the parser, not the plugin. The entry now produces a VISIBLE
attribution warning instead of an invisible drop. That is a
misclassification rewritten, not a number improved (MF-1077).

── Verification ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    selftest              15/15 -> 21/21
    mutation matrix       5/5, file restored byte-identical
    ctest                 575/575, 0 failed

The suite needed a note of its own: the first run reported three tests
"Not Run" (`test_convert_d81_hfe_roundtrip`, `test_d77_schreiben_-
positioniert`, `test_hfe_kodierung_nicht_erfunden`). Those are a parallel
session's new tests whose executables had never been built in this build
dir — not failures. Built and run: 3/3 passed. "Not Run" and "failed" are
the same line in a ctest summary and mean different things.

M3 fells TWO assertions, and that is correct: a missing `format` field
produces the same empty name, so the cases overlap by nature. That they
both still carry weight is proven by M5, which fells only one. My
expectation was wrong, not the test (lesson from MF-931).

── Also found, not fixed ────────────────────────────────────────────

P3-646: `--md` dies on Windows before printing a single row —
`UnicodeEncodeError` on a `→` against the cp1252 console, rc 1, stdout
empty. Pre-existing; `--write` is unaffected because it writes with
`encoding="utf-8"`. It is why my first greps of `--md` came back empty.

The mechanism is worth naming, because it also says why the new WARN is
safe: Python gives **stderr** the error handler `backslashreplace`, so a
non-ASCII byte there degrades (the neighbouring WARNs print `�` on this
console and do not fail). **stdout** has no such handler, so `print(md)`
raises. The new warning is on stderr, like its neighbours.

P3-647: `fat12_fs` needs an owner decision, not a guess — either the

events.title: Disassemble Alien 8 from its tape to the standard of the others: every entry described, the station mapped, and pages, pokes and notes
events.message:
Disassemble Alien 8 from its tape to the standard of the others: every entry described, the station mapped, and pages, pokes and notes

A new, complete disassembly of Alien 8 (Ultimate, 1985), built from the
tape by scripts/build_alien8.py:
- The tape loaded by running its own loader; the code mapped by playing the
  game in SkoolKit's simulator -- every control method, all 128 rooms, game
  over, the clock running out, valves carried and seated, all 24 chambers
  and the ending, the remote robots, the ceiling drops -- then by recursive
  descent: 4550 of 4602 instructions seen to run.
- The level data generated from the game at build time (alien8_data.py):
  each room, template, background, the 36 places, the graphic and update
  tables, every sprite with its picture, the font.
- All 622 entries titled, described and labelled by five agents, reusing
  Knight Lore's and Pentagram's names where the engine is the same.
  Reassembles byte for byte, 0 warnings.

Pages: how the game is put together; how a moving object is drawn; how the
robot moves and turns; rooms and doorways (all 300 walked at build time --
the station splits into 13 regions joined only by climbs); valves, sockets
and the cryogenic chambers; the clock, the remote robots and the dangers;
the station -- every room drawn by the game on Knight Lore's grid, with
layers; backgrounds, templates, all 132 graphics, every sprite and the font;
29 animations; 34 sounds, each checked wave by wave; and bugs, pokes and
facts, the pokes and most bugs watched live -- among them a turn that
forgets he was walking, a life that destroys the valve it starts on (with
three extra lives one game in four has no valve to spare), and the stray
OUT that crashes a 128K. Knight Lore's werewolf sound, its colour_panel,
its moveable-block blip and its copyright line are all still in there.

notes/alien8/: 28 notes in the skill's format, with the live-driving
recipes.

Also: both new builds now count their structure pass's warnings (which
found the ratings table read as words from its first byte); Pentagram's
bugs and facts pages link Knight Lore from reference/ correctly; the
publisher, README and site index list Alien 8.

events.title: fix(imd): a track record outside Dunfield's value ranges is rejected — it was read on into invented geometry and sectors (P3-642, MF-1473)
events.message:
fix(imd): a track record outside Dunfield's value ranges is rejected — it was read on into invented geometry and sectors (P3-642, MF-1473)

The IMD plugin read size code 7 as 512 bytes and then walked into the
sector data as if it were track records. The 0xFF size table it read as
sector types. Head 2, mode 6 and sector record type 9 it accepted
silently. Measured before the fix, every case opened with rc 0: a
one-sector file with size code 7 came out as 66x3x67, the 0xFF table as
2x1x65, head 2 as 1x3x1.

Reference: Dave Dunfield, ImageDisk 1.20 source
(neue-ideen/floppy1/IMDSRC.ZIP; COPY.TXT: "for any reasonable purpose",
attribution requested). IMD.SRC defines:
- |MODE| 00..05
- |SSIZE| 00..06
- |HNOTE| "HEAD can only be 0 or 1"
- sector records 00..08
- |SNOTE|: 0xFF is only a suggested extension that "ImageDisk does not
  currently handle"
IMDU.C stops on the first three itself ("... out of range"). open() now
answers UFT_ERROR_FORMAT_INVALID for all four ranges; the reference
stands in the file head.

Red first: tests/test_imd_ausser_spec_abgewiesen.c. Before the fix all
5 cases were red; after it, 7/7 green, including two controls:
- a valid record opens as 1x1x1;
- hxcfe_pc160.imd opens as 42x1x8, with its 42 records counted by an
  independent walker.
The filler bytes are 0x00, so they read on as valid empty records and
only the checked limit can catch each case. Mutation matrix 4/4 (with
the old 0x40.. filler the size-code case was masked by the mode check;
it is fixed now).

Found by the differential run against the uft-imd-code package. On the
three real IMDs, package and tree read 0 differing sectors; the
differences lie only outside the spec. The package itself stays Fundus.

Also recorded:
- P3-643: the workflow PAUSE button shows "paused" while nothing
  pauses; the calls are commented out.
- P3-644: the PC 360K profile says 300 kbit/s at 300 rpm with 6250
  bytes per track (it would be 7500).
- P3-645: four packages of the t2 round are Fundus (apd, Jazwiec
  RecoveryKit, SmartWorkflowCore v2, limits v2), each with what would
  open it.

events.title: A new page's colours go in with it, not a frame later
events.message:
A new page's colours go in with it, not a frame later

After a level's opening cutscene, the first room could show for all
or part of one frame in the colours put back from before the
cutscene. copyRectPlanar copied the page to the screen and
updateScreen wrote its colours afterwards, and where the two met the
VBL decided how much of a frame came out wrong - so it showed on some
runs and not others.

A full-page copy that brings new colours now waits for the VBL and
sets them in the blanking before it copies: with a border open STDL
holds the write for that VBL, so it is made before the wait; in Fit
and Fill it goes straight to the registers, so after it. Only pages
with new colours wait without a border - scene changes, not frames.

Recorded frame by frame in Hatari (cycle-exact): before, Fit on a
plain ST showed the level 1 room for one frame in the old colours;
after, Fit on ST and STE and the top border on ST all bring the room
in with its own.

events.title: fix(test): a missing LOCAL-ONLY corpus is a skip, not a failure — and the ASan gate reported it as a memory error (MF-1472)
events.message:
fix(test): a missing LOCAL-ONLY corpus is a skip, not a failure — and the ASan gate reported it as a memory error (MF-1472)

CI went red on my MF-1468 and the cause was mine, but it was not what the
gate said it was.

tests/test_woz_echte_aufnahme.c guarded the LOCAL-ONLY half on
`UFT_CORPUS_RESTRICTED_DIR[0] == '\0'` — whether the MACRO is empty. CMake
always sets it, also to a path that does not exist in CI, because
tests/corpus/ is gitignored (.gitignore:153). So in CI the guard passed,
the two captures could not open, and a CHECK fell.

The measured tell was the runtime: ***Failed 0.02 sec — far too fast to
open three WOZ images. It never read anything.

── Why the report pointed the wrong way ─────────────────────────────

The ASan job runs the full suite, so my failing test surfaced there, and
the falling-baseline gate reported:

    test_woz_echte_aufnahme: NEU unter ASan fehlgeschlagen.
    Nicht in docs/asan_baseline.txt.

That reads like a leak or an overflow. There is none. The gate is right to
report a NEW failing test; it cannot know the test failed for a missing
file. Worth remembering when the next "new under ASan" appears: check the
runtime first — 0.02 s is not a sanitizer finding.

── The fix ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A missing LOCAL-ONLY corpus is a SKIP. The test now returns 77 (MF-598)
when neither capture opens, and it says where they belong. The control
image — to_woz2_uftk_dos33.woz, which IS in git — is measured BEFORE that
point and its assertions still count, so the test never reports "passed"
for work it did not do.

Measured both ways, exit code taken without a pipe in between (a `$?`
after `| grep` is grep's code, not the test's — my own note on that, and I
walked into it once here before measuring again):

    with tests/corpus/      rc 0,  9 of 9 assertions
    without (like CI)       rc 77, control 2 of 2, real captures skipped

── Not changed ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Nothing about the findings P3-637..639, the fixtures or the manifest. The
defect was in the test's skip condition, not in what it measures.

events.title: fix(hfe): SCP -> HFE and G64 -> HFE write the encoding they know — not a fixed ISO/IBM MFM; the KryoFlux converters run into a stub (P3-640, P3-641, MF-1440)
events.message:
fix(hfe): SCP -> HFE and G64 -> HFE write the encoding they know — not a fixed ISO/IBM MFM; the KryoFlux converters run into a stub (P3-640, P3-641, MF-1440)

Reported by the local -37 session: uft_hfe.c maps UFT_ENC_UNKNOWN to
HFE_ENC_ISOIBM_MFM on the write side (uft_to_hfe_encoding()), so a round
trip would turn "unknown" into "MFM". Checked: that mapping has NO
caller, and hfe_create() — which does hard-code MFM — is reachable only
through uft_disk_create_image(), which only tests call. The report was
right about the class, wrong about the place. The production paths that
write the field are the converters, and three of them wrote 0x00 as a
fixed value:

- SCP -> HFE (offered, LOSSY_DOCUMENTED): PLL-decodes flux into cells
  and never determines the encoding. tests/corpus_free/
  gw_fm_acorn_3trk.scp is an FM capture (greaseweazle's own decoder:
  "IBM FM (10/10 sectors)", corpus manifest, MF-1142) — its HFE said
  MFM. Now HFE_ENC_UNKNOWN (0xFF), the value greaseweazle itself writes
  (measured on its D81 -> HFE) and that UFT's reader maps to
  UFT_ENC_UNKNOWN.
- G64 -> HFE: content is Commodore GCR by definition, header said MFM
  ("Raw bitstream"). Now 0x12: the HFE format's author, HxC libhxcfe.h
  (GPL, read only — channel Spec, the number taken), defines
  C64_GCR_ENCODING 0x12, and HxC's own HFE writer puts the track's
  encoding into this field (hfe_writer.c). New HFE_ENC_C64_GCR in
  include/uft/uft_hfe_format.h.
- KryoFlux -> HFE: same change as SCP, but it cannot run —
  uft_kfx_read_stream() is a stub that always returns -1 (measured on
  all three KryoFlux streams in the corpora, which the KFX plugin reads).
  All four KryoFlux converters are dead behind it; none is in the
  roundtrip matrix, so no user reaches them. P3-640.

Red first: tests/test_hfe_kodierung_nicht_erfunden.c — SCP (FM) -> HFE
and G64 (written by VICE, tests/corpus_free/vice_c1541_35trk.g64) -> HFE,
both inputs committed, so CI runs it. Against the old converters 2 of 2
red (both 0x00), now 2/2. The 93 hfe/scp/g64/convert/roundtrip/d64 tests
stay green.

Named, not fixed (P3-641): SCP -> HFE also writes interface IBMPC_DD and
300 rpm for any capture. The interface can steer a Gotek/HxC, so it needs
a device measurement or a named HxC source per value; the rpm is
measurable from the SCP index times.

Full build and ctest with corpus: 575/575, two named skips.

events.title: fix(d77): write_track repositions between reading a sector header and writing its data — under MinGW it reported success and wrote nothing (P3-636, MF-1439)
events.message:
fix(d77): write_track repositions between reading a sector header and writing its data — under MinGW it reported success and wrote nothing (P3-636, MF-1439)

Owner request: check the other plugins that open files "r+b" for the
missing fseek the cloud branch found in d88_write_track (MF-1470).

ISO C 7.21.5.3: on an update stream, input must not be followed by
output (and output not by input) without a positioning call in between
(fflush suffices only for output -> input). glibc tolerates it, the
MinGW runtime does not — the class is invisible on Linux/macOS CI.

The scan: a token-based checker (scripts/c_lex.py; not committed) over
ALL 102 files that open an update stream (`git grep` for fopen with a
"+" mode). It orders read (fread/fgetc/...), write (fwrite/fputc/...)
and positioning calls per function, plus the wrap of each loop body.
Self-test on d88 before/after MF-1470: 1 candidate -> 0. Result: 13
candidates in 5 files:
- src/formats/d77/uft_d77.c d77_write_track — REAL (registered plugin),
  the same code as d88: fread the 16-byte header, fwrite the data,
  loop, fread the next header, never repositioning;
- src/formats/d88/uft_d88.c d88_write_track — the case itself; fixed on

events.title: fix(app): record each turn's own room and always keep a map baseline
events.message:
fix(app): record each turn's own room and always keep a map baseline

SQ-1621: TurnRecord::map_snapshot is only taken on a structurally-changing
turn, and that snapshot's baked-in `current` (mapper::persist::PersistState)
is frozen at whichever turn produced it. A later non-structural turn that
walks between already-known rooms reused an OLDER snapshot via map_at_turn,
so replaying it flagged the wrong room current. record_turn now derives
TurnRecord::location/location_name from the mapper at record time,
independent of map_changed, and TurnSummary exposes location_name too;
main.rs's replay_graph reconstructs the snapshot and then overrides
`current` with the SELECTED turn's own recorded location via
MapGraph::set_current (confirmed harmless to struct_gen).

SQ-1622: map_at_turn answered None for every turn until the next structural
change in two cases — recording switched on mid-game (the mapper already
has rooms, so the first recorded turn has no structural change to trigger
on), and cap_history evicting the sole record holding the only surviving
snapshot. record_turn now also snapshots unconditionally on the first
record written into an empty history, and cap_history carries the latest
snapshot in a doomed prefix forward onto the new oldest surviving record.

archive.rs's HistoryIndexEntry gains location/location_name (#[serde(default)]
for old archives) so save/reload doesn't silently drop the new fields; every
TurnRecord{...} test literal updated to compile. draw_history's turn list
now shows the room name per turn as a bonus (cosmetic, e.g. "T6 * east ·
Kitchen").

Verified both fixes with reverts: without main.rs's set_current override
the SQ-1621 host_session test fails (wrong room flagged current); without
record_turn/cap_history's baseline logic all three SQ-1622 tests fail
(no snapshot at index 0). Confirmed host::persist::resume_from_turn is
unaffected by the SQ-1621 bug (it re-derives location from the live engine
via reobserve_location) and that the SQ-1622 fix closes its related
plan.map_json-is-None edge case for any newly-recorded history going
forward, since index 0 always carries a snapshot now.

events.title: test(woz): two real Applesauce captures enter the corpus — and the WOZ reader throws the bitstream away (P3-634..636, MF-1468)
events.message:
test(woz): two real Applesauce captures enter the corpus — and the WOZ reader throws the bitstream away (P3-634..636, MF-1468)

The corpus carried seven protection fixtures: two C64 G64 (one protected,
one negative control) and five Atari ST CopyLock files. Apple II: none.
And the only WOZ image was to_woz2_uftk_dos33.woz — produced by UFT
ITSELF, which cannot answer what the reader does with a disk it did not
write.

Two real captures from 4am's woz-a-day collection now sit in
tests/corpus/ (gitignored, .gitignore:153), LOCAL-ONLY, provenance and
SHA-256 in the manifest, channel Daten/Fixture (MF-695) — same treatment
as tests/corpus/c64pp_*.g64:

    wozaday_gauntlet_e7.woz     235440 B  Gauntlet (Mindscape 1986)
    wozaday_copy2plus_52.woz    234779 B  Copy II Plus v5.2 (1985)

Neither states a licence, so nothing of them is redistributed.

── Why these two, and not the "disk crack" search ───────────────────

The search that started this (archive.org "disk crack", page 4) yields
GitHub mirrors, keygens and PDFs. Its 3156 "4am crack" items carry .dsk
files — CRACKED images, protection REMOVED, and .dsk/do is already
covered at T2. A fixture whose protection is gone measures nothing.

woz-a-day is the opposite: images of originals, captured with
Applesauce. Measured on the TRKS chunk, the difference is stark:

    to_woz2_uftk_dos33.woz   35 tracks, ONE bit length (50624), spread 0
    wozaday_gauntlet_e7.woz  35 tracks, 28 lengths, 51505..51624
    wozaday_copy2plus_52.woz 35 tracks, 33 lengths, 51050..51211

A real capture differs on every track because drive speed and the
original write vary. A synthesised image has exactly one length. Anyone
testing only against the latter has never seen the normal case.

── What the measurement then found — three open findings ────────────

P3-634: the WOZ reader discards the bitstream. Measured through
uft_disk_open() + read_track(): 0 of 35 tracks carry raw_data, and
raw_bits is NEVER set (0 mentions in uft_woz_plugin.c). Only sectors come
out. This is SHARPER than P3-599: there the container holds only a byte
count and `bytes * 8` would be invented bits — a WOZ2 records the bit
count per track explicitly. UFT throws away a number the format hands it,
and the model's bitstream layer stays empty for Apple II.

P3-635: Copy II Plus v5.2 yields 558 sectors, not 560, at 35 tracks —
while both the synthetic control and Gauntlet yield 560. WHY is not
measured: a damaged spot, a protection feature, or a reader fault are all
possible for a 1985 copy utility.

P3-636, and this is the one that matters: a disk DOCUMENTED as
E7-protected yields ALL 560 sectors — exactly as many as the unprotected
control. Three explanations stand side by side: (a) E7 does not obstruct
ordinary sector reads and shows only in the bitstream, which UFT does not
deliver (P3-634); (b) `00playable.woz` is the EDITED version, not the
original; (c) UFT reads past the protection without noticing. Until (b)
is ruled out this image is NOT a proven protection fixture but a real
capture of unknown state — and it says so in the manifest. Apple II
therefore still has ZERO proven protection fixtures, and that must not be
counted as two.

── The test, and a measurement error of my own ───────────────────────

tests/test_woz_echte_aufnahme.c runs all three images through the REAL
uft_disk_open() and pins the current state. The loss in P3-634 is pinned
INVERTED: the assertion fails as soon as someone sets raw_bits, which
makes the fix visible instead of protecting the loss.

The first version of that test asked for raw_bits and reported "0 tracks"
for all three — including the control that the H-30 corpus sweep reads
fine. That looked like the images were broken. They were not: the reader
never sets the field. A measurement that reports "cannot open" and
"opens, delivers something else" as the same 0 sends the search to the
wrong place, so the function now prints the plugin and geometry it got.

── Acceptance ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    ctest                     572 of 572, two named skips
    check_consistency.py      OK, all categories 0

No source behaviour changed. Opens P3-634, P3-635, P3-636.

events.title: grm-ld68: carry a stack/mirror read-back through the index register
events.message:
grm-ld68: carry a stack/mirror read-back through the index register

contra c0d3 (PLA / TAY / JSR $C13F, helper LDA $FFD0,Y / STA $FFD0,Y) and
lifeforce e7fa (same shape, FUN_e61e) re-commit a bank read back from the
$8000 ROM_IDENTIFYING byte, but through Y -- grm-oj20 correctly stopped
attributing that to A. Three pieces:

1. StoredValueScanner: a Y (X) walk meeting TAY (TAX) now keeps tracking the
   value as A (transferSource, previously unused), so PHA/PLA pairing and the
   mirror read-back classification apply. A->X/Y only; TXA/TYA unchanged.
2. RegisterEnv carries per-register ReadBacks; callSiteRegisters fills them.
   The classification comes from a second scan at the mechanism's field mask,
   because at 0xFF a ROM_IDENTIFYING byte's proven-zero upper bits make
   stopped() demote RESTORED_BANK to RESOLVED.
3. Identity-table rule: LDA base,idx with idx's env read-back re-commits that
   bank iff idx reaches the helper entry unmodified (a mask-0 classification
   scan must stop HELPER_ARGUMENT -- value equality was rejected, a helper
   reloading idx from the same mirror matches it by coincidence), the cell is
   a plain-identity ROM_IDENTIFYING mirror whose realized banks are all
   verified, and table[v] == v over those banks (realized, not the
   descriptor's family-wide mask: contra's UxROM mask is 16 banks, the cart
   has 8). HelperDeposit carries the read-back out; recoverCallArgument uses
   it when the argument did not resolve.

New IdentityTableIndexHelperProgramTest (11 cases incl. traps: non-identity
table, writable table, idx redefined, idx reloaded from the same mirror,
WRITE_THROUGH cell).

events.title: fix(app): fall back to raster when a v6 story-slot grid outruns its viewport
events.message:
fix(app): fall back to raster when a v6 story-slot grid outruns its viewport

Zork Zero's and Shogun's Amiga InvisiClues menus put their topic list in a
promoted story-slot Grid. At a Hybrid pane narrow enough (relative to the
host's own font size) that native_viewport_box's inward-rounding computes a
viewport narrower than the grid's own native column count, both
hybrid_story_slot_grid and the terminal's real draw (draw_grid_transparent)
clip identically and silently drop the grid's right-hand column ("AS A LAST
RESORT", "FOR YOUR AMUSEMENT" on Zork Zero) with no ring geometry able to
show it.

story_slot_grid_wider_than_viewport (screen.rs) detects this and ORs a new
"grid_wider_than_viewport" reason into picture_takeover_reason's answer at
the three places that ask it (the terminal's own hybrid-ring dispatch,
hybrid_chrome_layout, hybrid_story_slot_grid), so a host and the terminal
agree. hybrid_raster_fallback_reason special-cases this reason so it routes
straight to the raster composite (which draws the whole native canvas with
no per-column clipping) rather than the chrome-runs-only painted-screen
shortcut, which would drop the grid's text entirely.

Narrowly scoped to panes that UPSCALE the native screen (frame.scale.s >=
1.0): v6_hint_menu_mouse.rs's own pinned 50-column pane clips this same grid
too, but it is DOWNSCALING (the pane genuinely has fewer device pixels than
the game's own screen), so nothing — raster included — could show more
without shrinking past legibility, and today's ring still answers mouse
clicks there. Confirmed via cargo nextest that both of that suite's existing
panes (190 and 50 columns) stay on their current path unchanged.

Falsified: reverting the picture_takeover_reason/hybrid_raster_fallback_reason
changes reproduces the original symptom (the ring publishes a placement and
clips the grid) and the new test fails accordingly.

events.title: fix(fc5025): detection asks fcdrives whether a device is attached — a found fcimage is no detected drive (issue #34, P3-589 b, MF-1438)
events.message:
fix(fc5025): detection asks fcdrives whether a device is attached — a found fcimage is no detected drive (issue #34, P3-589 b, MF-1438)

Issue #34 (second point, confirmed 2026-09-27): the FC5025 "connects"
with no device plugged in. The detect runner ran `fcimage` without
arguments and took its usage text as a detected drive, with an invented
drive kind "5.25\" (auto-detect)". The usage text proves the TOOL, not
the drive — the same class as MF-1434 (KryoFlux, "Device not found" with
exit 0).

The driver package already answers the question. FC5025 Driver Source
Code v1309 (neue-ideen/1, read for behaviour only — channel Spec, no line
taken; the package carries no licence file): `cmd/fcdrives.c` prints one
line "<id>\t<description>" per attached drive and exits 0; with no device
`get_drive_list()` (backend drives.c) returns NULL and it exits 1 without
output. `fcimage` itself says "No devices found." only after a full
argument list.

make_fc5025_detect_qprocess_runner() now runs `fcdrives` (next to a
configured fcimage, else on PATH):
- a line -> found, drive kind = the driver's description;
- exit 1 or no line -> not found, clean absence (DriveAbsent);
- fcdrives missing / timeout / crash -> not found with a reason
  (ProviderError), naming fcdrives.

Red first, on a real process: test_laeufer_argv case 7 (the echo tool
stands in for fcimage AND fcdrives; tests/argv_echo gained
UFT_ARGV_ECHO_STDOUT / _RC). 7a replays #34 word for word (usage text,
exit 1). Against the old runner 3 of 3 red (14/17), now 17/17.

Comments corrected (qprocess_subprocess_runner.h, hardwaretab.cpp);
P3-589 (b) marked done, (a) stays open; A-039 progress noted.

Move Sonix Music Driver to template 2 with a spec

specs/sonix_music_driver.py models the SNX copy of the driver: four
tracks of event words, the voice lifecycle, and instrument types as

events.title: feat(convert): D81 <-> HFE for the Commodore 1581, laid out as the 1581 ROM writes it — greaseweazle reads ours and we read theirs byte for byte; offered paths 18 -> 20; A-037 closed (MF-1437)
events.message:
feat(convert): D81 <-> HFE for the Commodore 1581, laid out as the 1581 ROM writes it — greaseweazle reads ours and we read theirs byte for byte; offered paths 18 -> 20; A-037 closed (MF-1437)

Owner decision (A-037 step 2, 2026-09-27): "Weg D81->HFE bauen". The
1581 profile row had no reader — the only readers of the FDC table are
the two HFE writers, both via geometry, and a geometry row for
80x2x10x512 would have claimed every such disk. It now has one: the new
path, chosen by SOURCE format.

Reference: the writer itself, the 1581 ROM (neue-ideen/1/1581.zip, read,
nothing taken — channel Spec):
- MROUT.SRC `fmtrk`: 32x 4E, no index address mark; per sector 12x 00,
  3x A1, FE, track, side, sector, size, CRC, 22x 4E, 12x 00, 3x A1, FB,
  data, CRC, gap3 x 4E. DSKINT.SRC `psetdef`: gap3 35, 10 x 512 from 1.
- The sides are swapped. MSUB.SRC gives logical sectors below
  numsec/2 = 20 the side 0; `fmtrk` writes it into the ID field;
  `side_ctl` selects PHYSICAL head 1 for side 0 ("lda #0 ; side one").
  So the first half of each D81 track is on head 1 with ID side 0.
Second hands, measured on a D81 with distinguishable halves:
greaseweazle 26690f8 (Unlicense; `image/d81.py` sides_swapped,
`disk 1581`) — same placement; MAME floptool (d81_dsk.cpp, BSD-3) — the
opposite, contradicting the ROM and its own comment table (P3-634).

What is built:
- include/uft/formats/uft_fdc_gaps.h: UFT_FDC_CBM_1581 (32/0/22/35/35/128,
  6250 bytes, 300 rpm, no IAM, BELEGT with the ROM symbols), deliberately
  NOT in UFT_FDC_FORMATS so geometry detection is unchanged.
- uftc_convert_sectors_to_hfe(): D81 branch (80x2x10x512, 250 kbit/s,
  Shugart interface like MAME), 1581 gaps from the profile, logical side
  for data and ID field, physical head for the buffer.
- uftc_convert_hfe_to_sectors(): D81 target. Placement by the ID-field
  side existed already; new is a completeness gate — exactly 1600
  sectors and no data field with R outside 1..10, else refused. Without
  it an 18-sector PC HFE (80x2 too) came back as a "complete" D81.
- dispatch and conversion table (44 -> 46 pairs); roundtrip matrix:
  D81->HFE LOSSLESS, HFE->D81 LOSSY_DOCUMENTED like HFE->IMG.

Measured:
- tests/test_convert_d81_hfe_roundtrip.c, 9 checks: round trip 0 of
  819 200 bytes different; head 1 carries ID side 0 and the first half,
  head 0 ID side 1 and the second; first sync at cell 704 (32 gap + 12
  zeros, no IAM); a D81 with error table and a PC HFE are refused.
  Written after the code, so the red proof is a mutation matrix: side
  swap off, PC gaps instead of ROM gaps, D81 gate off — 3 of 3 caught
  (the last one returned "1600 sectors" for the PC disk).
- Foreign hands (not in CI, tools local): greaseweazle reads the UFT HFE
  as commodore.1581 -> 1600/1600 sectors, D81 byte-identical; UFT reads
  the HFE greaseweazle writes from the same D81 (gap3 30) -> 0 of
  819 200 bytes different; MAME reads the UFT HFE -> exactly the halves
  swapped per track (P3-634).

Metric: offered conversion paths 18 -> 20 (lossless 7 -> 8, consent
11 -> 12); untested stays 26 — docs pulled (CLAUDE.md, MASTER_PLAN,
SUBSYSTEM_MATURITY, SHOWCASE, BACKLOG). BACKLOG A2 said "30 von 44";
counted, it was already 26 of 44 before this commit.

Full build and ctest with corpus: 571 of 572 on the first run —
test_roundtrip_matrix pins the LOSSLESS pairs by name and went red
(7 != 8), as it is meant to; D81->HFE added there with its proof, then
all 63 conversion/roundtrip/HFE/FDC tests green; two named skips.

Not measured: a real 1581 or a Gotek with this HFE (MF-310). The HFE is
a reconstruction, not a capture.

Numbers: the cloud branch moved its MF-1436..1442 to MF-1460..1466
(6c69cd30); MF-1437 and P3-634 are free at every branch tip.

events.title: feat(g71): G71 calls G64's verified GCR decoder instead of copying it — 1604 sectors arrive (P3-599, K4/E-19, MF-1436)
events.message:
feat(g71): G71 calls G64's verified GCR decoder instead of copying it — 1604 sectors arrive (P3-599, K4/E-19, MF-1436)

P3-599 measured that vice_c1541_1571.g71 delivered 0 sectors while the
image carries 1604 readable ones. The owner decided K4 — now rule E-19 in
docs/ENTSCHEIDUNGSREGELN.md: a format that extends another CALLS its
reader instead of copying it.

── What it calls, and why that one ──────────────────────────────────

g71_plugin_read_track() now calls gcr_extract_sector() and
gcr_sectors_per_track() from src/formats/c64/uft_gcr_ops.c.

NOT g64_read_slot(): that one is `static`, rejects `head != 0`
unconditionally (`// G64 ist single-sided`) and reads through a `FILE*`
from g64_data_t, while g71_plugin_data_t holds a memory blob. Three
couplings. gcr_extract_sector() takes BYTES, knows no side restriction
and is already public — all three fall away, and the working G64 reader
is not touched at all.

It was also a wiring job with no new decoder: the public API of
uft_gcr_ops.c had been called ONLY from tests — P3-204 class, capability
without a door. This is its first caller from a production path.

What the decoder rests on: it checks the header block against
`track ^ sector ^ id1 ^ id2` and the data block against the XOR over its
256 bytes. Both sums were written onto the DISK by the machine that wrote
it, not by our code (MF-1013, same route as MF-869 on the FM path). Until
MF-1013 gcr_extract_sector() was a facade that returned 256 zero bytes
AND success.

── Measured ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    sectors side 0          802      (was 0)
    sectors side 1          802      (was 0)
    total                  1604
    data checksum errors      0

The 802 is not a remembered number: it falls out of
gcr_sectors_per_track() a second time, i.e. from the format. It also
matches the count an INDEPENDENT GCR decoder outside the tree produced
before any code was written (P3-599).

── Red proof and counter-proof ──────────────────────────────────────

tests/test_g71_liefert_sektoren.c — before the wiring three assertions
fell (side 0 and side 1 at 0 instead of 802, track bytes missing).

Mutation matrix 3 of 3, each at its own assertion: sector loop removed,
`spur_nr = cyl` instead of `cyl + 1`, head dropped from the index.

A FOURTH mutation would have stayed green, and the test says so:
ignoring `pruef.data_ok` cannot be caught, because this image has ZERO
checksum errors. The error path is therefore NOT measured at this plugin;
closing that gap needs an image with a provably broken sector.

── Two of my own errors on the way, because they are instructive ────

1. The guard against a wrong index first compared the PAYLOAD of track 1
   sector 0 on both sides, and it fell. The assertion was wrong, not the
   code: on a freshly formatted disk the 256 payload bytes are identical
   across sides, so payload cannot prove the mapping. The RAW track bytes
   can — they differ in 84 of 7692 bytes — and the track numbers on the
   disk confirm it: slot 0 says track 1, slot 84 says track 36.

2. `sek` got `data_size` but not `data_len`. The "Sektor-Laenge" gate
   caught it at the new line: without `data_len`, uft_sector_copy()
   returns rc=0 AND data == NULL, and uft_mfm_encode_from_track() writes
   0x00 instead of the bytes (MF-1080). Both fields are set now.

── The price of calling, paid rather than avoided ───────────────────

Two test targets that link uft_g71.c now also need uft_gcr_ops.c
(test_g71_read, test_corpus_cbm_vice). The product build had both
already. Copying the decoder would have avoided this and violated E-19.

── Opened ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

P3-632: a 1571 carries two numbering systems and UFT names only one.
Slot 0 (cyl 0, head 0) says track 1, slot 84 (cyl 0, head 1) says track
36 — side 1 is CBM tracks 36..70. sek.id.cylinder carries the container
coordinate while gcr_extract_sector() reports the disk's own number in
pruef.track_in_header, and nobody compares them. What a caller EXPECTS is
not measured, so any change would be a bet.

P3-633: the tier table counts the weaker test and cannot see the
stronger one. gen_verification_tiers.py maps tests to formats via
`uft_format_plugin_<sym>` references, so a test going through the REAL
uft_disk_open() is invisible while one poking the plugin struct counts.
This test was missing from the g71 row until an assertion on

refactor(installer): flatten the install flow

Core components (P96 card, network, audio, CLI tools and ZZTop) no
longer ask a gate question before their version-carrying step: one
question per component, with the version visible. Per-copy confirm
pages are gone except where they protect something (overwrites of
existing files, destructive cleanups, and the zz9k-* file list).
The Roadshow template follows the network driver.

Manuals follow the tools they document, into one drawer of the
user's choosing (default the ZZ9000 drawer): ahi.guide with the
audio drivers, usb-poseidon.guide with the USB driver, sdk.guide
with the SDK runtime, amissl.guide with the accelerated library,
tools.guide with the CLI tools, ZZCapture.guide with the diagnostic,
and the package overview on its own. The standalone manuals question
is gone, along with the native-video lecture message (its content
lives in ZZTop.guide).

Also ignores the packaging-generated installer drawer slots (guides,
staged binaries, diagnostic payloads) that local release assembly
writes into the tree.

events.message:
CLAUDE.md: add rule on proximity/partial-sample fallacies in reversing

A visible sprite near an object's expected screen position isn't proof it
belongs to that object, and a memory region's first N bytes (or a struct
field's first byte alone) aren't proof of its whole content. Both cost
impossamole's 81st pass a wrongly-reported finding this session.

fix(kryoflux): "Device not found" with exit code 0 is no detected drive — measured by running dtc 3.50; the C builder passes -r too; A-035 closed (MF-1434)

Last open pieces of A-035 (DTC upgrade): the C builder named in DTC-3,
and DTC-6 (docs, with "dtc calibration in docs/ORACLES.md").

1. dtc executed, not just listed. The owner's package
   neue-ideen/fertige/kryoflux_3.50_linux_r4.tar.gz carries a Linux
   x86-64 build; run under WSL/Ubuntu with libusb-1.0-0 unpacked locally
   (apt download + dpkg -x, nothing installed). Banner "KryoFlux
   DiskTool Console, v3.50_Linux_x86-64_LU, uiv.1, Oct 26 2025"; binary
   SHA-256 b56f7ffd...be9be55. `dtc -h`: rc 0, 139 lines, and all 14
   switches UFT sets (-p -d -c -t -r -f -s -e -g -k -i -w -a -b) are there
   with the meaning the tests assume.

2. Found by that run: without a board `dtc -i0` — the exact call of
   do_detect_drive() — exits with **0**, stdout empty, stderr
   "Device not found" (17 bytes). The provider checked only the exit code
   and returned a DriveDetected ("Unknown (no RPM signal)", firmware
   "version unknown") for a KryoFlux that is not there. The read path
   failed honestly but named the wrong cause ("DTC wrote no stream file").
   Both now return a ProviderError "KryoFlux not connected" quoting DTC.
   Red first: test_kryoflux_provider_v2, new case with the measured
   stdout/stderr/exit code — detect red (assertion), then green; the read
   half proven by a mutation (its check off -> red). The Windows build's
   exit code is NOT measured; added to the DTC-7 bench list.

3. C builder: uft_kf_build_capture_command() carried cfg->revolutions
   (default 5, from presets and uft_kf_set_revolutions()) and never passed
   it. It now emits -r<n> in its global part before -f, the same word as
   the C++ builder (MF-1386). test_kryoflux_dtc_befehl: 5 checks red ->
   green, including parity between the two builders.

4. The head of kryoflux_provider_v2.cpp still described the V1 command
   from before MF-1046 (-s{head} -b{cylinder}) and claimed there is no C
   shell; corrected, the old lines quoted.

Not answered: what -c2 on every read does (P3-341) — without a device
all variants only print "Device not found". Added to DTC-7.

events.message:
Move Jochen Hippel ST to template 2 with a spec

specs/jochen_hippel_st.py models the ST replay and Wanted Team's sound
chip emulator: positions stepped per voice, patterns with note lengths,
pitch and volume lists, both vibrato and slide variants ('MMME' scales
them by the period), the register copy in RAM, tone, noise and silence
on Paula channels 0, 3 and 2, samples and the SID pulse on channel 1,
and NotePlay's busy-waits.

The emulator reverses the noise pitch: a higher chip noise register
gives a higher Paula noise pitch. A silent channel restarts an empty
sample every tick.

- aticatac_reference.py: ten pokes, each tested live against the same trial

events.title: feat(disk2): bit positions are ring positions when the revolution length is known — FIELD_ORDER and index crossing side by side, DAM_FAR from the WD17xx window; rules E-16..E-19 (P3-631, MF-1433)
events.message:
feat(disk2): bit positions are ring positions when the revolution length is known — FIELD_ORDER and index crossing side by side, DAM_FAR from the WD17xx window; rules E-16..E-19 (P3-631, MF-1433)

Owner decision on P3-631 (2026-09-27): the question "linear or wrapping"
was the wrong question — order and position are two questions, and on a
ring both hold. Two measurements corrected the proposal before it was
built:

1. The ring length is NOT nbits. uft_disk2.h says of the bitstream
   "length MEASURED, not clamped" and of the searcher "over the index,
   overlapping". New field uft_d2_bitstream_t.rev_bits (0 = unknown ->
   linear as before), setter uft_d2_set_rev_bits(); a new bitstream
   resets it. In .uftd it is its own sub-block REVB after BITS: an older
   reader skips unknown blocks and records them (property 1 in
   uft_disk2_io.h), so UFTD_VERSION does not change.
2. The proposal's example of a broken sector, 10 000 -> 90 000 -> 4 000
   on a 100 000-bit ring, PASSES the order check (80 000 + 14 000 <
   100 000) and would even be reported as crossing the index. What tells
   it apart is the distance IDAM -> DAM against the controller's search
   window: WD1772 documentation "the DAM must come within 30 bytes (FM)
   or 43 bytes (DD)", quoted in src/a8rawconv/sectorparser.cpp
   (SectorParser::Parse) and used by decode_mfm_sector()/decode_fm_sector().
   New WARN DAM_FAR, not an error: the same source names Blue Max, which
   interleaves IDAM and DAM on purpose.

uft_d2_sector_crosses_index(): on the ring when rev_bits is known — the
sector 99 900 -> 400 with the index at 0 now crosses it (data over
index); unchanged linear fallback. uft_d2_validate(): FIELD_ORDER (ERROR,
only with rev_bits) and DAM_FAR (WARN; MFM (7+43)x16 = 800 cells, FM
(7+30)x16 = 592, from mark to mark).

Tests: test_disk2 case 12 (normal / doi / far / reversed, window edge
800 vs 801, linear fallback), test_disk2_io case 6 (REVB round trip, no
REVB without rev_bits, new bitstream resets). Written after the code, so
the red proof is a mutation matrix: ring off in crosses_index (= the old
function), FIELD_ORDER off, DAM_FAR off, window +1 — 4 of 4 caught.
Full build and ctest with corpus: 570/570, two named skips.

Open, in P3-631: no producer sets rev_bits today — the bridge does not
know the revolution length of its sources; which formats can supply it
is to be measured per format, not assumed.

Also:
- docs/ENTSCHEIDUNGSREGELN.md: the owner's answer becomes rules, as the
  file's ratchet requires, in this commit: E-16 (ring positions, with the
  two corrections above), E-17 (duplicate numbers: the later session
  renumbers, whoever PUSHED first keeps — measured by the fetch reflog,
  not %ci; for MF-1403/1405 the push order is undecidable from the logs:
  the cloud commits first appear in the 12:33:31 fetch, absent at 11:15,
  and my MF-1403 push was 11:41), E-18 (no bundled pushes), E-19 (an
  extending format calls the base reader instead of copying it: G71 ->
  G64, K4). Proposed as "E-20"; given the next free numbers like
  E-13..E-15.
- E-10 (no line numbers in comments): my own comments from MF-1427,
  MF-1432 and this commit named file:line; rewritten to symbols and
  SAMdisk's own error messages. The 851 older occurrences in src,
  include and tests are not touched here.
- uft_disk2.h: INDEX_BEYOND (MF-1432) was missing from the documented
  list of validate() codes — NACHGETRAGEN with the two new ones.

events.message:
impossamole: 80th pass -- real-Hatari cross-check retracts two "broken crack" readings as this emulator's own bugs

Drove the actual disk image live in real Hatari v2.6.1 (not this repo's F#
core) through the same crack-menu -> title-fire -> world-select -> confirm
sequence this workstream already uses. Two things this emulator concluded
were broken crack content turn out to work fine on (emulated) real hardware:

- Confirming Klondike Mine reaches genuine gameplay (mine cavern, HUD, a
  visible hero, a real GAME OVER death screen) in Hatari, not the blank-logo
  bounce this emulator produces with zero disk reads.
- The Amazon gameplay screen shows a clearly visible mole-hero sprite in
  Hatari, in the same scene this emulator has only ever rendered without one.

The hero's object struct in Hatari ($1a572, type=2, position/frame-index
fields) matches this workstream's reverse-engineered layout exactly, so the
addressing and struct work stands -- the divergence is specifically that this
emulator's confirm->load path never executes whatever real hardware executes

events.message:
grm-mej.3 X1: cross-block PHA/PLA pairing (fallback, oracle path only)

findMatchingPush pairs a PLA with its PHA only straight-line and gives up at the first flow break.
crossBlockMatchingPush is a bounded backward ALL-PATHS search over the listing, run only where that
walk already fails (ANALYZER_LIMIT) and only under a state oracle (Hooks.hasStateOracle, true only
in OracleHooks), so direct-site strategies and effectDependsOnPriorState's MirrorProbe are
byte-identical. Every backward path must reach the same PHA at depth 0 with each address at a single
owed depth, under the closed-world predecessor rules now shared with BankDataflowEngine.joinArms;
calls are crossed by the existing fall-through witness; zero-net loops are stepped over regardless
of trip count. Anything else abandons to today's answer -- never withdraw-and-continue (the
ironsword rule). Span.crossedBlock resumes through Hooks.stateAt exactly like crossedCall. Own cap
64 nodes / 8 joins, charged ONCE per node (owner ruling Q1), one step against MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN.
restoreDetail gains "carried on the stack across control flow <push>..<pull>".

events.message:
impossamole: 79th pass -- proves the hero's sprite-bank unpacker never runs in this crack

A watch 42e00 9600 held across the entire confirm->load->gameplay transition
(after_confirm_amazon.snap through 5,000,000 steps, well past confirmed entry
into real gameplay) recorded zero writes to the hero's sprite bank; the same
watch mechanism caught 100/100 sanity-check writes to $53000 over the same
run, ruling out a tooling gap. A hits census on the $b288 block believed to
unpack into $42e00 (and its call site, plus the gameplay loop entry as a
sanity check) landed zero hits on all four addresses across the same window.

The unpacker routine ($1c6de) itself did fire twice, but both returns trace
(bt 1) to the *other* per-world decompression block at $b328-$b3a8 (keyed by
the selected-world index), which targets $40600/$4c400 -- not $42e00 -- and
even there only 2 of its 3 straight-line calls fired (the first, targeting
$53000, must be reached some other way, now a small open item on its own).

Conclusion: the hero is invisible throughout everything driven so far because
nothing in this crack's boot-to-gameplay path ever populates its graphic bank
-- not a per-frame state question. Whether that's this crack being broken
(it already has one dead world) or the real trigger sitting further into the
game than explored yet is the new open question.

events.title: grm-eyn: bound 6502 jump tables by their lowest target, extension-side
events.message:
grm-eyn: bound 6502 jump tables by their lowest target, extension-side

Ghidra's decompiler switch recovery takes all 128 values of a doubled, unbounded 1-byte index
and reads the code after the table as bogus targets; each one seeds disassembly at an arbitrary
offset (phantom code, fake helpers, bistable goldens). The owner ruled the fix ships in the
extension rather than as a patched decompile.exe, so every user gets it.

JumpTableBound is a pure port of the fork's boundByLowestTarget, working from the COLLAPSED
LoadTables Java receives (per-entry extent = table extent / case count; decline if it does not
divide). JumpTableBoundAnalyzer runs at CODE_ANALYSIS.before(), ahead of stock
DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer: it decompiles functions with computed jumps (synthesizing an
UndefinedFunction exactly as stock does, since functions do not exist yet at that priority) and,
when the bound shrinks a table, pins it -- a JumpTable override for a real function, or computed
refs + disassembly for an undefined one (stock skips any jump that already has a computed ref).
Case/load spaces are compared overlay-of-physical, not by equality: on banked ROMs the decompiler
reports loads in RAM: and cases in the overlay.

Real-ROM (check nes, 4 runs): megaman a734 93 -> 8 (truth 8), rcproam 8068 -> 4 distinct (truth
6 slots / 4 distinct), ff1 b174 -> 24 distinct (truth 30 slots), dragonpower/shenlong warnings
6 -> 2 (all four removed sites are owner-verified phantoms), megaman instrs 7428 -> 7666 with the
12 owner-verified 8d1f phantom comments gone. 32/34 rows byte-identical run to run. Blessed:
megaman, rcproam, dragonpower, shenlong, ff1. Left failing for an owner listing read: rcransom,
db3, ultimaav, dodge (see docs/human-research-todo.md).

Also: GRM_THREAD_PIN=0 measurement opt-out (grm-nems re-measured: the pin stays, now for
core-count independence), and the thread pin is part of the real-ROM cache key so a measurement
run can never serve a bless.

events.title: docs(g71): P3-599 measured — the plugin hands over raw bytes, and 1604 readable sectors never arrive (MF-1431)
events.message:
docs(g71): P3-599 measured — the plugin hands over raw bytes, and 1604 readable sectors never arrive (MF-1431)

P3-599 recorded that vice_c1541_1571.g71 goes red through the bridge and
yields 0 sectors, and it said explicitly: the next step is a MEASUREMENT,
not a change. Two measurements follow, and neither guessed anything.

── 1. WHY the bridge refuses ────────────────────────────────────────

The model names the reason itself; it was simply never printed:

    [RAW_BITS_UNKNOWN] 84 tracks carry raw data without a bit length
                       — bitstream not taken, not invented from bytes.

g71_plugin_read_track() sets raw_data and raw_size but NO raw_bits, and it
adds no sectors either: 0 hits for add_sector in src/formats/g71/uft_g71.c
against 1 in src/formats/g64/uft_g64.c. The bridge therefore has neither a
bitstream it may take nor sectors. It refuses and carries 0 tracks.

The bridge is RIGHT, and that is the interesting part. A GCR track's bit
length is not in the container — what is stored is a BYTE count.
`bytes * 8` would be up to seven invented bits, which is exactly what
RAW_BITS_UNKNOWN prevents. The defect sits in the plugin.

── 2. WHAT is on the image ──────────────────────────────────────────

Measured with an INDEPENDENT GCR decoder outside the tree — deliberately,
so the verdict does not rest on the code being judged:

    slots populated          84 of 168   (42 per side, whole tracks only)
    tracks with GCR headers  84 of 84
    header blocks            802 per side, 1604 total
    track lengths            7692 / 7142 / 6666 / 6250  (the four zones)

802 is exactly the 42-track 1541 sector count — the same number the
MF-928 round trip produced. Numbering decodes correctly: slot 0 -> track 1
sectors 0-3, slot 2 -> track 2, slot 4 -> track 3.

So the content is there and readable, and UFT delivers none of it. A valid
double-sided 1571 disk is ABSENT for the operator — same class as P3-204
(capability without a door), one layer up.

Named limit of this measurement: the disk IDs came out non-printable — my
assumption about the nibble order inside the header block does not hold
there. That is a limit of the MEASUREMENT, not a statement about the file;
track and sector numbers are right and carry the count.

── 3. A correction to this register entry ───────────────────────────

The entry previously called option (a) "wiring existing code". That was too
optimistic, and the measurement corrects it. G64's decoder is
g64_read_slot() (src/formats/g64/uft_g64.c:485-683) and it is coupled three
ways: it is `static`, it rejects `head != 0` unconditionally
(`// G64 ist single-sided`), and it reads through a `FILE*` from
g64_data_t while g71_plugin_data_t holds a memory blob.

Three couplings, not one line. Still permitted under the FREEZE RULE as
work on existing code, but it is a job with a red proof, not a patch.

── What was NOT done ────────────────────────────────────────────────

No source behaviour changed. The plugin and the bridge are untouched. This
commit carries two measurements, their findings, and the diagnostic output
that produced the first one: the corpus sweep in
tests/test_h30_ohne_daten_nennt_grund.c now prints the model's findings
when the bridge refuses, instead of reporting only "rot". That turned a
silent red into a named reason in ONE run.

The owner's three options stay open, now with numbers: (a) recovers 1604
sectors; (b) makes the plugin say "detected, content not readable"; (c)
keeps it as Fundus.

── Acceptance ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    ctest                     570 of 570, two named skips
    check_consistency.py      OK, all categories 0

events.message:
Flow Control Macros: Support IF ... JUMP for forced long branches

GOTO uses the standard branching which is just a simple branch op
unless the target is known during the ca65 single pass assembly, in
which case a JMP is used if necessary. This means the assemble might
fail if the target is out of range, but this project prioritizes
small code so that's desired.

If the target is out of range, use JUMP instead of GOTO.

This is more pessimistic than the longbranch.mac macros (jcc, etc)
which only use a JMP if the target is out of range or it can't
be determined. That'll come next.

No binary changes.

events.title: RD1 ST: move Rick's x and y in one collision probe, as the ST does (F12)
events.message:
RD1 ST: move Rick's x and y in one collision probe, as the ST does (F12)

Symptom: on submap 0x12, Rick cannot get under the one-way platform
(row 30, cols 8-23). The only way down is to walk off its left end and
steer right while falling, clearing the spike tiles at row 35, cols 4-7,
to land on the floor at cols 8-11. In the port he always died at x=58
(he needs 60): on the frame his body reaches row 35, y moved first at
the old x, hit the spikes and zombied before x moved.

ST (atari_ram.bin, player_controller, read in the disassembly):
  4C0F6-4C124  D2 = x -2 (LEFT) or +2 (RIGHT), D3 = new y
  4C12A        move D2,D6 / move D3,D7 / bsr 0x4CD70 (probe_player_tile_collision)
  4C132        bcs 4C168                       ; blocked -> retry
  4C134-4C142  store x AND y, then gravity (4C148), then LADDER_CHECK
  4C168-4C176  retry at the OLD x with the new y (x rejected)
So one probe covers the diagonal step, and lethal / ladder flags come
from the probe that succeeded.

Port (and PC, per the addresses already cited in e_rick.c: vertical
probe 0x1596/0x15AB, horizontal 0x166D/0x1673): vertical envtest at
(old x, new y) with its own lethal -> zombie, then a separate
horizontal envtest at (new x, new y).

Fix, PLATFORM_ST only, in the "VERTICAL MOVE" branch of e_rick_action2
(vertical move already known to be free at the old x):
- if LEFT/RIGHT is held and x +/- 2 stays inside the submap, probe
  (x +/- 2, new y) with the vertical test's own mask;
- free: take x now, set game_dir, and use that probe's env1 for the
  lethal and climb tests that follow; `stdiag` then makes `horiz`
  return, so x is not moved twice;
- blocked: nothing changes -- vertical move at the old x, then `horiz`,
  whose probe is that same blocked (x +/- 2, new y): the ST retry path.
Landing / ceiling paths (vert_not) are untouched: there the ST also
retries x at the snapped y (POST_MOVE), which `horiz` already does.

Checks: clean builds, warning counts unchanged (ST 230, PC 231).
Behaviour (xrick-core, solver branch, 0x12 from the platform: walk
off the left end, RIGHT held): before, zombie at x=58 on the frame
that reached row 35; after, x=60 on that frame (y 200), landing at
y 203 on the floor at cols 8-11.

events.title: fix(disk2): validate reports an index position beyond the bitstream (INDEX_BEYOND); the wrap-around question behind FIELD_ORDER goes to the owner (P3-631, MF-1432)
events.message:
fix(disk2): validate reports an index position beyond the bitstream (INDEX_BEYOND); the wrap-around question behind FIELD_ORDER goes to the owner (P3-631, MF-1432)

Follow-up of the A-032 review of the owner's package UFT_AnalysisBooster.
It named two gaps in uft_d2_validate(); one is unambiguous, one is not.

1. INDEX_BEYOND. validate() has long checked that SECTOR bit positions
   lie inside the bitstream (POS_BEYOND), but not the index. A .uftd file
   carries index_bit as its own field (uft_disk2_io.c:433) and
   uft_d2_set_bitstream() stores it unchecked; with the index beyond the
   stream, uft_d2_sector_crosses_index() silently answers "no" for every
   sector. Now a WARN on the bitstream layer, next to ENC_MISMATCH.
   Red first: test 11 in tests/test_disk2.c (index 70 in 64 bits) was
   red, now green; index 63 (last bit) and unknown (SIZE_MAX) stay quiet.

2. FIELD_ORDER (dam_bit < idam_bit) is NOT built. crosses_index()
   (uft_disk2.c:447-460) silently assumes linear positions and returns
   false for bis <= von. If a bitstream does not start at the index, a
   sector whose data field runs past the end of the stream is exactly
   the data-over-index protection pattern — then dam < idam is the
   signal, not an error. Neither uft_disk2.h nor crosses_index() states
   the convention, and the only producer of real positions is the .uftd
   reader (uft_disk2_io.c:458-462; the bridge sets SIZE_MAX). Building the
   package rule would write one answer down unmeasured. Recorded as
   P3-631 with the two options for the owner.

No package code taken.

events.title: fix(msa): a broken MSA file is refused instead of opened with zero padding, and cylinders before the start track are "not recorded"; A-032 closed (MF-1427)
events.message:
fix(msa): a broken MSA file is refused instead of opened with zero padding, and cylinders before the start track are "not recorded"; A-032 closed (MF-1427)

Found while reviewing the owner's package UFT_SurfaceIntegrity_v1.0.0
(A-032): its MSA checker disagreed with the registered plugin on the
same inputs, and the references side with the checker.

src/formats/msa/uft_msa_plugin.c decompressed into a calloc'd image and,
on every inconsistency, left the loop with `break` and returned UFT_OK.
Measured on the real HxCFE file tests/corpus_free/hxcfe_msa_rle.msa cut
100 bytes short: UFT_OK, 9198 invented zero bytes. Also accepted with
UFT_OK: stored track length above the track size, length 0, RLE that
expands to 100 of 4608 bytes, an E5 block cut short (copied as data), a
run past the end of the track (silently clipped). And a file holding
only track 1 served cylinder 0 as nine zero sectors marked OK.

Reference: SAMdisk src/samdisk/msa.cpp ReadMSA() (MIT, in the tree, the
named reference of msa's T1b row) throws in every one of these cases
(:66-67, :70-71, :75-76, :83-84, :96-97, :106-107, :119-120) and writes
only the tracks start..end (:59-126). Hatari floppies/msa.c:220-224
(GPL-2+, read only) refuses the short file as well. Cylinders before the
start track now return UFT_ERROR_TRACK_NOT_FOUND, the convention SCP
already uses (uft_scp_plugin.c:254-260): not recorded is a statement
about the capture, not the disk.

Not changed, named: a run of length 0 — SAMdisk refuses it, Hatari
tolerates it; the references disagree, so it stays accepted. The
package's own limits (9-11 spt, last track <= 85) are narrower than
Hatari's (<= 56, <= 86) and were not taken.

Red first: tests/test_msa_kaputt_ist_kein_ok.c, 7 of 11 red before, 11/11
after; the two real HxCFE files still open. No package code taken.

Also in this commit (A-032 closed, moved to Erledigt with its evidence):
- docs/neue_ideen_urteile.json: victor9k-flux-tools-main.zip licence
  BERICHTIGT from "ungemessen" to MIT — pyproject.toml INSIDE the package
  declares it, same author as the MIT text next to it; its own tests run
  (25 passed, 3 skipped for want of a real capture), so it is a named
  oracle candidate for a Victor-GCR flux decoder UFT does not have, not a
  calibrated oracle.
- "nächste runde": UFT_AnalysisBooster and UFT_SurfaceIntegrity reviewed.
  Booster: Fundus as a module (6 of 9 stages duplicate uft_d2_validate /
  uft_copy_plan_check, thresholds unsourced, README timing not
  reproduced); two gaps it exposes in uft_d2_validate are a follow-up.

events.message:
fix(gvm,app): persist Glk line terminators/echo-line; fire the gate on Glulx too

Two-part bug: Model::serialize never wrote a window's terminators/echo_line
fields, and Model::deserialize unconditionally rebuilt every window with
terminators: Vec::new(), echo_line: true — discarding whatever the game had
registered via glk_set_terminators_line_event/glk_set_echo_line_event.
GlulxSession::silent_look round-trips through exactly this serialize/
deserialize on every look-driven room-name probe, so a registered terminator
silently stopped working far more often than a player-triggered Save State.
Bump GLK_SNAPSHOT_VERSION 6 -> 7 and gate the new fields on version >= 7,
per the Frozen (0.x) save-format ritual.

Separately, main.rs's line-terminator key gate checked pending_input() only
through zvm_session_opt, which is None by design for a Glulx session — so the
gate's body (deliver_line_key_terminator, already engine-aware since SQ-1613)
never ran for Glulx at all. Call session.pending_input() directly through the
Engine trait instead.

events.title: Review Tim Follin: chained sample cost, direction byte, trill
events.message:
Review Tim Follin: chained sample cost, direction byte, trill

The chained sample needs flag bit 7: without it, a loop longer than a
tick lets the second sample replace the first before it plays. Only
instruments 0-3 are pulse waves. The direction byte is flipped with
EOR 1 and tested for non-zero, so a byte other than 0 or 1 never
turns; the spec now keeps it as a byte. The trill's first lower part
also lasts upper_ticks.

Trill joins the glossary; glide becomes portamento, also in the slug.

events.title: RD1 ST: re-arm the gun every frame unless UP+FIRE are held (F11)
events.message:
RD1 ST: re-arm the gun every frame unless UP+FIRE are held (F11)

Symptom: after one shot, releasing FIRE and pressing FIRE+UP again did
not fire. Rick took the shoot pose, no bullet left, the count did not
drop. Found on submap 0x0E: an enemy falls on Rick about 15 frames after
he lands, and the bullet-triggered bridge (trap 166) needs a second shot.

ST (atari_ram.bin, player_controller):
  4C094  move.b (0x4922B),D0      ; joystick
  4C09C  andi.b #0x81,D1 / cmp.b #0x81,D1 / beq.s 4C0AC
  4C0A6  clr.b  (0x4BF15)         ; shoot_debounce
Every frame, after the death check and before the climb dispatch,
shoot_debounce is cleared unless UP (0x01) and FIRE (0x80) are both
held. Every reference to 0x4BF15 (byte search): 4BF4E reset_player_state,
4C0A6 the per-frame clear, 4C4DC/4C4E8 test and set in FIRE+UP,
4C8FA the shoot pose.

PC (ibmpc_cs.bin): the trigger is byte 0x7D86, referenced only at
0x175C (read), 0x1766 (set) and 0x17C3 (clear, FIRE held without UP
while standing). The port copied the PC: `trigger = FALSE` only in the
standing FIRE branch. So the PC build is unchanged.

Fix: under PLATFORM_ST, clear `trigger` at the top of e_rick_action2,
right after the zombie return, when (control & (UP|FIRE)) != UP|FIRE.
Not done: the extra clear in reset_player_state (4BF4E). It matters
only when UP+FIRE is held through a respawn, and I have not checked
which port routine matches reset_player_state.

Checks: clean builds, warning counts unchanged (ST 230, PC 231).

events.message:
impossamole: 78th pass -- corrects the blank-hero explanation: the sprite bank is unloaded, not idle-gated

Live-drove the hero into an actual walk (kbd ff/08 + ~70,000 steps) and caught
it mid-stride with real non-zero sprite-frame indices (6(A0)=7, then 9 on a
second drive), superseding the prior commit's untested "idle selects a blank
frame" guess. Checked the exact live source address the type-2 draw body was
about to read (bpc 1b4f8, A2 matched the hand-derived $42e00+index*384 formula
exactly both times) against that same address's memory: every entry checked
(0, 7, 9) is all-zero, and a 4000-byte scan from $42e00 found no non-zero byte
at all. The hero's own sprite bank is a separate table from the type-1 body's
$3b600 (384 bytes/entry at $42e00+$7800, not 128 at $3b600 as first assumed).

The $b1b6 per-frame template's own setup code has an unpacker call targeting
exactly $42e00/$9600 bytes -- matches closely enough to be the same resource,
but whether it actually runs on this crack's path into Amazon gameplay is the
new top open item, since it's the direct cause of every "hero invisible"
observation so far.

events.title: Attract demos: joyl2's shop replays exactly as in DOSBox
events.message:
Attract demos: joyl2's shop replays exactly as in DOSBox

joyl2 types the attract shortcut "L2". In the original that opens the
world-2 shop, which the demo then drives for ~1200 tape entries before
gameplay starts at cursor 1330. The port went straight to gameplay.
Fixed, each piece pinned by a live capture of DS:0x385/0x258/0x194 and
the SS:0x408C grid during the demo:

- The bypass and a real match both land at CS:0x2EA0 -> 0x2D9E; the
  level start then opens the shop because [0x38C] is still set (only the
  BEGIN QUEST path clears it). enterViaPassword is now a full restart +
  the shop (money set to 80000, CS:0x0643) for worlds 2-4.
- ShopScreen#iterate: one pass of CS:0x6C19's loop per tape entry, with
  the [0x339]/[0x33A] held-input auto-repeat, the flat 0..0x11 cursor
  (LEFT/RIGHT wrap rows), and the fire-release wait (CS:0x6E62) that
  consumes entries until fire is let go. During a demo the shop is fed
  from the tape at 20 Hz (CS:0x6D72's 2-PIT-tick wait) plus the unthrottled
  fire-wait polls.
- Grid order: survivors are pushed onto the stack and bubble-sorted there
  (CS:0x7347), so equal prices end up in reverse list order (197 before
  38 in world 2).
- Prices are per world (CS:0x7392 reads the loaded world's POBJECTS +6):
  items 2/3 cost 20000/32500 in worlds 2-4, not world 1's 6000/12000.
- DS:0x258 is not cleared by a purchase, and a rebuild with no survivors
  forces the cursor to EXIT (CS:0x730D) - which is how the demo leaves.

Captures: all six demos, re-captured every emulator frame with the random
table snapshot (tools/attract-capture/*.raw.json).

events.title: fix(graph): writers starved on Windows — take the lock only to write, and ask again
events.message:
fix(graph): writers starved on Windows — take the lock only to write, and ask again

e2e:store-concurrency on the Windows runner, the first time it ran there:
in 1 of 6 trials of eight processes creating and filling one graph, a writer
died with `database is locked`. Never on macOS, 0 of 100 trials at 8 and 16
writers — so it was investigated on Windows itself, on a throwaway branch
that stressed the same race and printed node:sqlite's own error.

What that showed, in order:
- errcode 5 (plain SQLITE_BUSY), in the GraphStore constructor, on
  exec(GRAPH_DDL). First read as the SHARED->RESERVED deadlock a
  read-then-write statement gets (no busy wait). Wrapping every write in
  BEGIN IMMEDIATE on that theory made it WORSE: 10 of 60 trials at 16
  writers, now dying at BEGIN IMMEDIATE itself.
- A BEGIN IMMEDIATE cannot deadlock, so the failure was timed: ~5.5 s after
  the step began — the 5 s busy timeout running out. STARVATION: SQLite's busy
  handler sleeps between attempts, and under enough writers on Windows' slower
  locking a waiting connection keeps missing the free window.

The fix, all in one place (knowledge-graph/write-tx.ts):
- Do not queue for the lock when there is nothing to write. Every open ran the
  schema DDL and every door rewrote two meta rows — writes that changed
  nothing, on every call. The schema is now checked against sqlite_master
  first (names read from the DDL itself, so a statement added later is
  covered) and the transaction is taken only when something is missing.
- When the lock is needed, take it at BEGIN IMMEDIATE and, if BEGIN comes back
  busy, ask again after a random pause, up to 30 s. Safe because nothing has
  happened yet; the jitter breaks the lock-step in which the same connection
  keeps losing.
- Every graph transaction goes through writeTx/beginWrite — the store, the
  human door (withStore, which also ran its schema check outside its
  transaction), the migration and import paths, the resolver — re-entrant per
  connection, so a door inside a door joins the outer transaction instead of
  failing with "cannot start a transaction within a transaction".
- recordProducer was a read-modify-write outside a transaction when called on
  its own; it is inside one now.

Proved on the Windows runner, 60 trials each: 0 dead writers at 8 and at 16
(before: 1/20 at 16; the first attempt: 2/60 and 10/60).

New 5d in e2e:store-concurrency, deterministic on any OS: a second process
holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 3 s while GraphStore.open and the 822 schema check
are timed. With this fix 0 ms and 0 ms; on the old code the schema check every
door runs waited 3073 ms — the full hold — which is the queue writers starved
in. The open check guards against the first attempt's regression.

Full gate 85/85; the graph gates (823, 842, 849, 866, 877 x4) green.

events.message:
fix(trd): the probe looks for the TR-DOS ID at 0x8E7, not in the catalogue at 0x227; neue-ideen register closed, 224 of 224 judged (A-032, MF-1405)

Two things from the last A-032 sweep, one of them a live defect.

1. trd_probe() (src/formats/trd/uft_trd.c, the REGISTERED reader, T1b)
   gave its "real signature" (confidence 92) for data[0x227] == 0x10,
   under a comment naming the info sector at 0x800. 0x227 is byte 0x27
   of the third sector — the catalogue. The ID lives at 0x800 + 0xE7.
   References: SAMdisk scl.cpp `pb[231] = 0x10` and HxC scl_loader,
   both already tabulated in the head of uft_scl_plugin.c (MF-1014).
   Measured on two real TR-DOS images from neue-ideen/1/ (WDC11sorc.trd
   from wdc1.zip, betadisk_dsdd.trd from ZX-Spectrum-FD-Images-main.zip,
   655 360 bytes each): [0x8E7] = 0x10, [0x8E3] = 0x16, [0x227] = 0x00
   in BOTH — the old check gave neither its ID, only the size-only 45.
   Red first: tests/test_trd_kennung_bei_0x8e7.c, 2 of 3 red before
   (45 for a real info sector, 92 for 0x10 in the catalogue) -> 3/3.
   The images are not committed (redistribution not measured).
   The orphan uft_trd_parser_v2.c has the same swap in its own probe
   (0xE2/0xE7 against its own field map); left alone per P3-290 (orphan
   second readers are not repaired one by one) — it is named in the
   register verdict of "UFT-NN – TR-DOS.zip".

2. docs/neue_ideen_urteile.json: the last 51 top-level entries of
   neue-ideen/ get a verdict (licence read at the file, channel, metric,
   next grip), from four read-only reviewers; three verdicts checked by
   hand against the tree (Tor 67 / MF-1230, SCP integrity / MF-1162, the
   TRD probe above). None moves one of the four metrics.
   scripts/gen_neue_ideen_register.py reads second-level keys of the form

   "orphan" verdict (WHDLoad_dev) was an existing second-level entry the

events.title: fix(store): one spelling per path in the artifact store (#28)
events.message:
fix(store): one spelling per path in the artifact store (#28)

knowledge/artifacts.json has two writers. The MCP server stored relativePath
with `/`; the pipeline registrar stored whatever path.relative answered — `\`
on Windows. The registrar skips a file already registered by comparing
relativePath with `===`, so on Windows a file the server had registered was
registered a second time in the other spelling. Reported by @mrr19121970 with
every site cited; each one checked against the code and correct.

- The registrar normalises at the source, as the server already did.
- Both readers heal on load: a store written on Windows before this is read in
  the one spelling, so the registrar's skip sees those rows, and the next write
  stores them healed.
- The mirror site the issue did not name: prg-workflow compared the store's
  relativePath with a raw relative() — `\` on Windows — so it never matched a
  server-written row, and after disasm the listing never reached the payload
  entity. Derived from the code, not observed.
- Rows that were already registered twice are REPORTED by the audit, under
  their own finding, not merged: entities and the graph cite their ids, and
  which one survives is a decision. Measured on 9 real project stores (7660
  rows, macOS): zero hits, so the finding is silent where nothing is wrong.

e2e:relpath-spelling plants what a pre-fix Windows store holds, so it bites on
every platform — 9/0 here, and 4/5 with the fix removed, reproducing the
duplicate row the issue predicted. It runs in the Linux job and on the Windows
runner, together with e2e:store-concurrency, the test the mismatch was first
seen in (37/1 on Windows) — the only place path.relative answers with `\`.

Full gate 85/85.

events.title: docs(dtc): DTC-5 differential run attempted — stays Fundus; with two revolutions the solver's output is revolution 0 bit for bit (A-035, MF-1403)
events.message:
docs(dtc): DTC-5 differential run attempted — stays Fundus; with two revolutions the solver's output is revolution 0 bit for bit (A-035, MF-1403)

The owner decided DTC-0 (package is theirs, GPL-2) and asked for the
differential run of uft_rev_path_solver against uft_multi_rev_fusion on
real multi-revolution captures.

Measured in the corpus: every capture carries exactly two revolutions —
gw_amigados.scp (Greaseweazle, header byte 5 = 2), gw_fm_acorn_3trk.scp
(2), hxcfe_kfx_t00/t40 (3 index marks = 2 revolutions, copies from a
sector image, MF-1024). On the one real capture the production path
already decodes everything: test_convert_scp_adf, SCP -> ADF byte for
byte, 3/3 green today.

And with two revolutions the solver cannot rescue anything, by its own
code: uft_rev_path_solver.c:233 picks
`one > zero ? 1 : zero > one ? 0 : reference`. Two votes give 2:0 (the
value of revolution 0) or 1:1 (reference = revolution 0), so the fused
stream equals revolution 0 regardless of alignment quality. The
disagreement bitmap it adds is already produced by
uft_fuse_revolutions_ausgerichtet().

Corrected in docs/plans/DTC_UPGRADE.md: the opening condition said
">= 2 index marks", which is one revolution. It now reads: a real capture
with >= 3 revolutions and a sector that reads bad in every single one
(otherwise the per-sector choice across revolutions, MF-473, already
recovers it). No code taken; no number moves.

Numbers: MF-1400..1402 are on the cloud branch; MF-1389+ belongs to the
local -37 session.

Separate a project's committed artifacts from its machine-local output

A project's .c64-re-tools/ now has two folders. Its root holds the
project's artifacts (annotations.db) and is meant to be committed.

project commits .c64-re-tools/ wholesale with no rule of its own. A
tools.json left at the old place is refused by name with the move as the

events.title: fix(fdc): the track budget takes gap2 from the profile, and ED carries gap2 41 — gw and MAME agree; uft-limits package checked (P3-603, P3-604, A-041, MF-1388)
events.message:
fix(fdc): the track budget takes gap2 from the profile, and ED carries gap2 41 — gw and MAME agree; uft-limits package checked (P3-603, P3-604, A-041, MF-1388)

Found while checking the owner's package uft-limits-code.zip against the
tree. fdc_satzlaenge() in src/formats/uft_fdc_gaps.c counted gap2 as a
fixed 22 (MFM) / 11 (FM), while every profile carries its own
gaps.gap2 — the same quantity in two places (MF-1177). All 15 MFM
profiles say 22 and both FM profiles 11 (measured), so the switch to the
profile field changes nothing for them.

The ED profile is where it mattered. gap2 at ED rate is 41, from two
independent hands:
- greaseweazle src/greaseweazle/codec/ibm/ibm.py:738-742 (Unlicense,
  read at 26690f8): "At ED rate the default GAP2 is 41 bytes";
- MAME src/lib/formats/pc_dsk.cpp:90-92 (BSD-3-Clause, from
  neue-ideen/formats1.zip): 2880K entry, gap_2 41.
With the fixed 22 the budget left 36 x 19 = 684 bytes too much track
space. PC 2.88M moves from UNBELEGT to TEILBELEGT: gap2 belegt, gap3 and
gap4b still the copied values (MAME says "gaps unverified"); it still
does not close (82 bytes short, before 766), as TEILBELEGT requires.

Red first: tests/test_fdc_gap2_aus_profil.c, 3 red (gap_space did not
move when gap2 moved, for MFM and FM; ED gap2 22) -> 4/4 green. The
evidence distribution pinned in test_fdc_profil_verdrahtet.c moves by
measurement from 11/1/5 to 11/2/4 (quoted). test_gap_gegenrechnung
(MF-1377) stays green — both calculations now take gap2 from the
profile. Full build and ctest WITH corpus: 567, all passed except the
two named skips.

Not changed and named: uft_fdc_calc_gap3()/uft_fdc_calc_gaps() compute
without a profile (capacity, sectors, size, mfm) and know neither the
rate nor a gap2 — they cannot be right for ED.

Package verdict (P3-604): nothing of its code is taken — a second track
calculation with a FIXED track head 146/130 (the MF-1177 error; 5 of 17
profiles differ), an "oracle" from the same hand with the same numbers,
a third profile table, and uft_limits.h colliding with
uft_format_common.h. Its yield: this fix, and P3-603 — UFT_MAX_SECTOR_SIZE
is defined twice, 8192 (uft_config.h:258) and 16384
(uft_format_common.h:356); owner decision.

Numbers: MF-1387 / P3-602 belong to the cloud branch (144bd2b5).
