events.title: feat(app): add HHGG walkthrough-regression harness (SQ-1600)
events.message:
feat(app): add HHGG walkthrough-regression harness (SQ-1600)

Second lane of SQ-1600: a headless walkthrough-regression suite for The
Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (hitchhiker-r59-s851108.z3, v3 Z-code),
mirroring Phase 1's Photopia harness (walkthroughs.rs). Boots the real
story via GameSession, drives a committed ~600-command script to the
game's own real winning ending (stepping onto Magrathea) at the maximum
score (400 of 400), exercises an in-game @save/@restore round trip, a
host Save State/Restore State round trip and a restart-reboot probe,
checks the mapper (populated, unlike Photopia's empty graph) and hints
machinery (Available via the SLAG-named hhgginv.z5 sidecar, unlike
Photopia's None) don't error, and pins a normalized golden transcript.

The script is long because HHGG's middle act throws the player into one
of several randomly-selected flashback vignettes each time the spare
Improbability Drive's switch is pushed, including repeat visits to
already-completed ones -- the game's own manual documents this as
unpredictable. zvm's Z-machine `random` opcode seeds from a fixed
constant with no OS entropy at initial boot, which is what makes the
script reproducible turn-for-turn despite that randomness (confirmed:
two fresh boots produce byte-identical transcripts). One wrong branch
(a second visit to the Vl'hurg/G'Gugvunt War Room's time-paradox maze)
is scripted to kill the player outright ~5 turns later no matter what --
confirmed by letting it happen once -- so the script routes around it.

Command list reconstructed empirically by booting the real game and
confirming every reply, using two IF Archive solutions as a guide only
(hitchhiker.txt by Scorpia, hitchhiker.step by Doug Howell/Peter van
Turennout) -- the committed script is this project's own derived list,
not a copy of that prose (cited in the script file's own header).

Quest: SQ-1600

feat(kryoflux): the requested revolutions reach dtc as -r<n> — belegt in the KryoFlux manual; DTC-0 decided by the owner (A-035 DTC-3, MF-1386)

DTC-3 had been halted at the evidence since 2026-09-26: -r was nowhere
belegt in the tree (MF-1046 checked the switches against the manual,
-r was not among them). The owner pointed to the source: the official
package neue-ideen/fertige/kryoflux_3.50_linux_r4.tar.gz carries
docs/KryoFlux Manual.pdf (Release 3.50). Read, nothing copied (Spec):
- p. 13: "-r<rev> : set number of revolutions to sample (default by
  image type)";
- p. 14, order rule: "Revolutions (-r)" is listed among the GLOBAL
  settings that "can be anywhere in the command line" — not image
  local, so its position is free.

Change: KryoFluxProviderV2::build_read_argv() takes the requested
revolutions and adds -r<n> when > 0; 0 leaves DTC's default by image
type (nothing claimed that nobody asked for). read_raw_flux() passes the
REQUESTED count, not the clamped internal one. The MF-1046 command line
stays word for word, -r is the only addition.

events.title: fix(td0,imd): IMD carries ONE sector size per track — the feature table said otherwise, and TD0->IMD refuses a mixed track instead of padding it with zeros (P3-524, A-032, MF-1384)
events.message:
fix(td0,imd): IMD carries ONE sector size per track — the feature table said otherwise, and TD0->IMD refuses a mixed track instead of padding it with zeros (P3-524, A-032, MF-1384)

A-032 continued on the owner's machine, where neue-ideen/ exists. Step 4
of the TD0 rebuild was already done by MF-1307 (matrix entry LOSSY with
VAR_SECTOR_SZ). Its open core, P3-524 way (a) — "use IMD's has_varsizes /
ssize[] instead of flattening" — rested on a false table row.

Measured against the author of the format: Dave Dunfield's own ImageDisk
1.20 source (neue-ideen/1/imd120sc.zip), TD02IMD.C:907-908:
    if(!issame(Smap, Size = Smap[0], Stop))  // 765 cannot do mixed sector sizes
        error("Cannot do mixed sector size within track");
Second hand: MAME imd_dsk.cpp:554-556 rejects the size code 0xFF as
"Unsupported variable sector size". The ImageDisk source is read, not
copied — its terms forbid redistribution and allow "the ideas and
algorithms ... with no restriction" (Spec channel).

UFT_D2_FEAT_VAR_SECTOR_SZ means unequal sizes WITHIN a track
(uft_disk2.c, reference reset per track). IMD has one size code per track
header. uft_format_traegt.c listed the feature for IMD, so TD0->IMD
computed "no feature lost", and the converter flattened a mixed track to
its first sector's size, padding smaller sectors with ZEROS — invented
bytes in a sector. has_varsizes/ssize[] have no writer in the tree.

Change:
- uft_format_traegt.c: VAR_SECTOR_SZ removed from F_IMD, with the two
  sources. TD0->IMD now computes exactly VAR_SECTOR_SZ, which is what its
  matrix mask already says; IMD->IMG loses four features, not five.
- uft_td0_to_imd(): a mixed track is refused (UFT_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED)
  via the new uft_td0_erste_gemischte_spur(), one rule for converter and
  message; a size without an IMD code is refused too instead of being
  set to 512 silently. Both callers (TD0->IMD, TD0->IMG) name the track
  and the reason.
- Matrix note, conversion table warning and the uft_imd.h field comment
  corrected (BERICHTIGT notes, nothing deleted).

Red first: test_matrix_form 3 red (TD0->IMD loss 0 instead of
VAR_SECTOR_SZ, IMD->IMG five instead of four, "identical" TD0->IMD no
contradiction) -> green. test_verify_after_ist_verdrahtet group 4 now
demands the named refusal (C0 H0) in both runs and NOT_RUN for the
requested check; the dispatcher wiring stays proven by the passed run
(READBACK_COMPARE, 160 tracks). Side effect named as P3-600: no case
shows the FAILED outcome at dispatcher level any more — it hung on the
defect. The "short mask" counter-proof lost in P3-534 is buildable again.
Full build and ctest: 566/566 green; after renumbering (comments only)
the 39 affected tests again green.

Also: A-038 moved to Erledigt (42123a24 / MF-1382), A-032 stand.
Numbers: MF-1383 / P3-599 are taken by the local branch
h30/schritt3-ohne-daten-nennt-grund.

events.title: feat(disk2): no data must name a reason — the other half of the H-30 rule (H-30 step 3, MF-1383)
events.message:
feat(disk2): no data must name a reason — the other half of the H-30 rule (H-30 step 3, MF-1383)

Step 1 (MF-1370) enforced "absence carries no data" at the single door
into the model. Step 2 (MF-1371) made 37 markings in 34 files name their
reason, and gate 62 holds that.

Nobody held the converse: NO DATA MUST NAME A REASON.

A sector with has_data = false, data_len = 0, conf = 0 and origin
CONTAINER passed silently. The model listed it as "from an image file"
with nothing in it — it looked like a sector that was READ and happened
to be empty, which is exactly the claim nobody can support, and telling
it apart from "missing" is the whole point of H-30.

The path was open in the bridge:

    out->has_data = !missing && out->data_len > 0u;
    if (!missing) out->origin = UFT_D2_ORIGIN_CONTAINER;

Any plugin that does NOT mark a sector missing but leaves its data
pointer NULL or its length 0 landed exactly there.

── The rule ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

uft_d2_add_sector() now rejects it with the finding
ABSENCE_WITHOUT_REASON. PADDING and RECONSTRUCTED fall with it: filler
without filling and a reconstruction without a result are not reasons,
they are empty claims.

No gate needed. The rule sits at the only door into the model and
enforces itself at runtime — a new caller fails immediately, not in a
later audit.

── Measurement BEFORE the rule ──────────────────────────────────────

House rule "measurement before plan": the corpus half of the red proof
ran as a REPORT first, not as an assertion. 94 images through
uft_disk_open() + uft_d2_from_disk(), 0 sectors of that shape. Had real
plugins produced them, rejecting would have been wrong and the right
answer a dedicated reason for that case.

The file set comes from the DIRECTORY, not a list in the source
(MF-636), and a section that opened nothing FAILS instead of silently
passing (MF-1340).

── The loader had to follow ─────────────────────────────────────────

herkunft_lesen() clamped an unknown origin byte to UNKNOWN
unconditionally. With the new rule that would have DISCARDED a
data-less sector while LOADING. A lost sector is worse than a cautious
statement, so it now clamps to UNAVAILABLE when there is no content.
The ORIGIN_RANGE finding is unchanged — the file is suspicious, not the
entry.

── Red proof and counter-proof ──────────────────────────────────────

tests/test_h30_ohne_daten_nennt_grund.c — three assertions fell before
the rule:

    FEHLGESCHLAGEN 154: a sector with NO data and NO reason was accepted
    FEHLGESCHLAGEN 156: expected 1 ABSENCE_WITHOUT_REASON, measured 0
    FEHLGESCHLAGEN 172: PADDING without data was accepted

Mutation matrix 5 of 5, each falling at its own assertion: rule
removed, PADDING exempted, condition inverted, finding code renamed,
loader clamp reverted.

── Four callers had to follow, and that was the real find ───────────

  * test_d2_querpruefung and test_st_reihenfolge_bericht built fixtures
    with ONLY an ID and origin CONTAINER. They now carry data, because
    they represent READ sectors, not absent ones.
  * test_decode_job_no_fiction built a sector meant as MISSING without
    a reason — now UNAVAILABLE with confidence 0.
  * test_disk2_io expected the UNKNOWN clamp; it now expects
    UNAVAILABLE and asserts the sector is KEPT.

An intermediate version was measured and rejected: setting the two
fixtures to UNAVAILABLE made the model write one finding per absence
(MF-1370), and the ST report then counted 512 instead of 3. A fixture
that CLAIMS absence without representing one falsifies what is being
measured.

── Acceptance ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    ctest                     566 of 567, two named skips
    check_consistency.py      all categories 0

The one failure, test_ipf_zellstrom, was measured against the previous
state and was already red — not a consequence of this change.

Side finding, recorded as P3-599: of the 94 corpus images, 93 pass the
bridge and vice_c1541_1571.g71 returns false with no sector layer. WHY
is explicitly NOT measured.

Completes H-30. Opens P3-599.

events.title: Bring Ant Attack to Knight Lore's standard: how-it-works pages, animations, sounds, a layered city map, bugs, pokes, trivia and notes
events.message:
Bring Ant Attack to Knight Lore's standard: how-it-works pages, animations, sounds, a layered city map, bugs, pokes, trivia and notes

The listing: the 216 entries sna2ctl had split out of the sprite tables, the
render buffer and the city map -- titled "Message at" and "Data block at" --
are folded back by declared spans, and every sprite frame ($8000 + 64 x
frame, with its picture) and every row of the city ($C000 + 128 x row) is an
entry of its own, generated at build time. Every entry has a label: BASIC
lines LINE10 onwards, the system variables, channels and BASIC variables, and
the filler between routines named after the routine before it (..._PAD).
446 entries, none unlabelled, no placeholder titles, no warnings.

The pages, each family a module the build calls (PAGE_MODULES), each running
the game's own code in SkoolKit's simulator:
- antattack_howitworks.py: how a scene is drawn (one real frame followed
  stage by stage, the four views, PLANES), how people move (17 set pieces),
  how the ants hunt (the XOR into the map, DIRECTION_TO's pinwheel, speeds),
  how a grenade flies, and finding and rescuing (level 1 played by a
  scripted player to the score card; the ending staged through level 10).
- antattack_animations.py: 26 GIFs from real game frames.
- antattack_sounds.py: every script's sound, the footsteps and BASIC's four
  BEEPs as WAVs, each checked against the timing the code implies.
- antattack_reference.py: six bugs (four new), six pokes each tested live
  against the same trial without it, thirteen facts.
The city page gains layers -- where the player starts, the one gap in the
wall, the ants' homes, every waiting place by level -- read from the map and
BASIC's DATA, and each row of the map links to its entry.

notes/antattack/: 21 notes in the skill's format -- README, overview,
journal, driving (with the breakpoints and staging watched live), memory map
and a topic per question.

Corrections, each checked against the tape, the bytes or the code: the
header does auto-run (the loader); the unused OWCH script has no stream byte
and stops after OWC; the grenade's own frames are drawn near its home; $F0-
$F3 are drawn by nothing ("an ant on its back" was a guess); RANDOM gives
NOISE bit 4 of A, not the carry, and NOISE leaves the speaker on; a rescue
stops play at the end of the same frame and game over four frames later;
PLAY's SEED write is undone by the RANDOMIZE that calls it; the NOP at $852A
is unreachable; a blown-up ant shows its blast only on frames it skips; an
ant faces the player within three cells, not four; a blast's stun is 24 of
the ant's turns; HANDLE_EVENTS loses the other person's event on a bad fall;
the build's ending session runs out of memory at line 3610.

Also: a poke's POKE statement is a paragraph of its own, on Knight Lore's
pokes page too.

project.title: NESRecomp
project.display_title: NESRecomp — 6502-to-C static recompilation framework
project.notes: Translates NES ROM 6502 machine code into C and provides a PPU/APU/mapper runner; generated C alone is not a playable game. The opt-in cycle-accurate compiler/runtime uses bounded interpreter fallback and trace-parity verification. Its 27 September generated catalog reports 57 of 458 known mapper IDs supported, covering 6,682 of 10,632 known dumps; every supported mapper has contract/fixture checks, while title validation is explicitly bounded rather than exhaustive. README describes Windows x64 as mature, macOS as experimental and Linux as less tested; no minimum host CPU/RAM is stated.

events.title: feat(blorb): publish which real-world machine a disk image belongs to
events.message:
feat(blorb): publish which real-world machine a disk image belongs to

DiskImage::interpreter_number() and implies_ibm_pc() are Z-machine
concepts (header byte $1E and its version-dependent PC rule) and
can't name Atari 8-bit media (AtariDos2/AtariXex) at all — both
answer None/false there, indistinguishable from a medium naming no
machine at all, so a host badging a library row (Amiga/Atari
ST/Mac/Apple II/C64/PC) has no way to place an Atari 8-bit disk.

Add a new DiskImage::machine() -> Option<Machine> accessor (and a
MountedDisk::machine() forwarder), independent of
interpreter_number(): AtariDos2 and AtariXex now answer
Some(Machine::Atari8Bit) even though ZMSD §11.1.3 numbers no such
machine and interpreter_number() stays None for both. Iso9660 still
answers None at both, since a hybrid disc is two machines and no
single one is the right answer.

Machine's spellings deliberately match two existing enums exactly:
app::interpreter::InterpreterProfile and scott::SagaPlatform.

events.title: Give Knight Lore animations, sounds, layers on the castle map, and pages on the depth sort, collision, day and night and the charms
events.message:
Give Knight Lore animations, sounds, layers on the castle map, and pages on the depth sort, collision, day and night and the charms

Three new page modules beside knightlore_pages.py, each called from its
build() and each running the game's own code in SkoolKit's simulator:

- knightlore_animations.py: 17 GIFs -- walking in both views as man and
  werewolf, the transformation, materialising, dying, an extra life, the
  guard, the wizard, the ghost, fire, flame, ball, bubbles, the crumbling
  block and a day in the sun window. Every frame is one pass of the frame
  loop, timed by its T-states.
- knightlore_sounds.py: 21 WAVs, the four tunes and seventeen effects, from
  single calls on fresh machines or from real room runs where the effect's
  object is the only thing making a noise. Tune pitches were checked within
  5% of freq_tbl, edge counts against what each routine implies.
- knightlore_howitworks.py: the depth sort's 27 cases drawn from the table
  and a scene run through it; the collision code run on seven set pieces;
  day, night and the werewolf; the charms, the deal and the cauldron.

The castle map gains layers a checkbox shows or hides, with no script: the
start rooms, the wizard's room, the 32 charm places, and the rooms with
something deadly or a portcullis -- deadly meaning a handler that sets the
deadly flags, which showed the wizard is as deadly as a guard.

sound_materialise was described as 3 to 27 steps for types 120-126; the
handler moves the type on before calling, so it is 7 to 31 steps for types
121-127, which the recording's edge count confirms. Notes, the journal, the
README and the site's index are updated. Not animated: the finale's sparks,
which need the ending staged.

events.title: fix(app): probe the raw pane, not the header-floored one, in min_story_pane_for_floor
events.message:
fix(app): probe the raw pane, not the header-floored one, in min_story_pane_for_floor

min_story_pane_for_floor's Z-machine probe called declared_story_screen_dims,
which floors its result at boot_screen_cols. Once a host seeds
TerminalFacts::min_story_screen at boot, the pre-boot search already widens
boot_screen_cols past the floor, so every later probe trivially passed and
the live-resize search returned the too-narrow real pane unchanged. Probe
story_screen_dims directly instead -- the raw measurement, not the
write-time header clamp -- since the search is answering a different
question than sync_zvm_screen_dims.

events.message:
fix(workflow): "Success" only when sectors were decoded — the job hands out its tally, one rule decides (P3-555, A-038, MF-1382)

src/workflowtab.cpp put every finished DecodeJob under
QMessageBox::information(this, tr("Success"), result) and sent
operationFinished(true) — since MF-1350 also for "Lauf beendet — keine
Sektoraussage" (flux the plugin does not split into sectors). The class
of P0-17 one level up: a success message the content does not carry.

- DecodeJob::decodedAnything(const DecodeResult&): true iff the model
  holds at least one sector — the same line resultMessage() draws
  between "N Sektoren gelesen" and "keine Sektoraussage". One rule.
- DecodeJob emits resultReady(DecodeResult) right BEFORE finished(), by
  value: the tab must not read the job object after finished(), which is
  also wired to deleteLater. Same receiver, queued in emit order.
- WorkflowTab: "Success" and operationFinished(true) only when that rule
  holds; otherwise "Finished — nothing decoded" and false.

Test: test_decode_job_no_fiction — the two flux rows (HFE bit stream,
SCP flux) are NOT decoded, the MSA container with 1512 sectors in the
model IS; resultReady fires exactly once with the same total. Red first:
the test did not compile against the old job (no resultReady, no rule).
Mutation matrix 3 of 3 caught (always decoded, never decoded, signal not
sent). Full build and ctest: 566/566 green.

Not clicked: the dialog itself (WorkflowTab runs the job in a worker
thread and shows a modal box).

the word at the falling edge before and then raised wait again for the
handshake with the core. The CPU therefore never saw wait low and
repeated the same write forever: black screen on the MEGA65, because
the firmware auto-loads tos.img before it shows anything.

Wait is now only raised while an earlier word is in flight, not for
the word of the current write access (qnice_taken).

Add a GHDL test (CORE/sim/tos_loader) with a QNICE-like master: the
old loader repeats word 0 forever, the new one transfers every word
exactly once (also with a very fast and a very slow core).

Taken over from origin/claude/umsetzungsplan-8yi6w3 (e2ceea1a and fa2bc856) as the net diff 1f995725..a79499f9 of that branch. Their

=== e2ceea1a (MF-1380) ===

refactor(ipf): one IPF record reader — four callerless parallel parsers retired, the IPF part of uft_amiga_caps.c removed (P3-598, MF-1380)

Owner decision 2026-09-27: "die Parser zusammenfuehren". IPF record
headers were read in five places; only uft_ipf_air.c is reachable from
the registered plugin, and only it reads a real IPF. The other four:

- src/formats/ipf/uft_ipf_ctraw_v2.c (780 lines): record types read as
  little-endian integers 1..7 instead of ASCII, so no real record ever
  matched its switch. On a match it would have dereferenced
  track->blocks, which is never allocated. Its header promised "CAPS
  Library Integration" and contained none.
- src/formats/flux/ipf.c (96 lines, stub) + include/uft/formats/ipf.h
  (empty hook header): demanded the magic "IPF" instead of "CAPS", so it
  rejected every real file.
- src/formats/ipf/uft_ipf_caps.c/.h (182+333 lines): dlopen/LoadLibrary
  adapter for the SPS library, "Based on ipflib 4.2 and spsdeclib 5.1
  headers". That derives from headers under the SPS licence, which
  docs/QUARANTINE.md measures as incompatible, and it contradicts the
  path chosen there (helper process, no linking).
- src/protection/uft_amiga_caps.c, its own IPF reader (7 functions, 233
  lines):
  - INFO/IMGE were read 4 bytes off (data + 16 instead of record start
    + 12);
  - no CRC check;
  - fixed CTRaw values (25 MHz, 200 ms, 0.9) returned as "analysis".
  The protection heuristics, uft_ctraw_extract_flux() and the name
  tables stay; P0-2 decides about them.

Measured: the 17 exported functions of the three format-layer files have
0 mentions outside their own .c/.h (git grep per symbol). The 7 removed
functions of uft_amiga_caps.c had none either. This duplication is the
shape that caused MF-1002 (ASCII fourcc compared against an enum 1..10),
see MF-1177 "one quantity, one calculation".

What is lost, named in P3-598: the 30-name protection table of ctraw_v2
(names only, no detection, source not given) and the dlopen route. Both
remain in git history. The format count does not change: ipf is one
format with one plugin, FORMAT_ROLL stays "aktiv".

Ruecknahme: vier IPF-Nebenparser ohne Aufrufer, drei davon lasen kein echtes IPF, einer aus SPS-Headern abgeleitet (P3-598, MF-1380)

Also updated:
- .pro SOURCES (3 lines);
- orphan_baseline (3), selbsttest_baseline (IPF_CTRAW_TEST);
- stub_inventory (flux/ipf.c);
- enum_macro_baseline: IPF_DENS_AUTO no longer collides, the tool
  demanded its removal;
- FORMAT-VARIANTS row IPF;
- BACKLOG C1 now (40, 358, 9, 42) instead of 365. The count falls
  because unverified code is gone, not because anything was verified;
- comments in uft_ipf_plugin.c and uft_ipf_air.h that pointed at
  uft_ipf_caps.h.

Checks:
- cmake build green.
- ctest: 561/563. test_hardware_tab_gui and test_provider_switch fail
  locally only (no Qt6::SerialPort).
- check_consistency.py rc 0.
- verify_build_sources.py: no new divergence.
- amiga_caps compiles with -Wall -Wextra without warnings.

=== fa2bc856 (MF-1381) ===

fix(86f): a sector with a bad checksum is not a good sector — the decoder's CRC result reaches the track (P3-595, MF-1381)

f86_read_track() decodes the track with uft_mfm_decode_track(), which
recomputes both CRCs. It then added every sector via
uft_format_add_sector_with_id(), which unconditionally sets
UFT_SECTOR_OK and both CRC flags to good. id_crc_ok, data_crc_ok and
deleted were never read, so a sector with a bad checksum came out as
valid (class MF-980/P3-300: not invented, but misjudged).

Red first: tests/test_86f_crc_flaggen.c flips two cells in
fluxfox_sector_test_360k.86f (real 360K disk, free corpus): one data
cell of sector 5 and the top cylinder bit in the header of sector 7. The
track position is computed by the test from the 86Box specification.
The decoder only locates the cells. Before: "9 of 9 sectors good", 5 of
11 promises red. After: exactly one data-CRC and one header-CRC error,
7 good, all marked checked, 11 of 11.

The rule now lives in ONE place (MF-1177): uft_format_mark_last_crc()
in include/uft/uft_format_common.h. It sets UFT_SECTOR_CRC_CHECKED,
inverts crc_ok/id_crc_ok plus the status flag for each bad checksum, and
carries the deleted mark. Both bitstream readers call it: the 86F reader
(new) and uft_ipf_sektoren.c, instead of its own copy. Mutation matrix
6 of 6 over the helper and both callers.

tests/test_disk2_bridge.c guarded the defect. It expected "the 86F
plugin passes no checksum" (0 sectors with a known CRC, no confidence
255, report "ohne CRC-Angabe: 1440"). On this real disk all 1440 CRCs
now check out, so by the bridge's own rule (255 only with a measured,
matching checksum) all 1440 get 255. The three promises are rewritten
to the measured state, with a correction note; the report line now
reads "mit CRC-Angabe: 1440 (davon falsch: 0)". Same shape as MF-1016:
a green test guarding the defect.

events.title: fix(app): stop hybrid_text_rows from also dropping the row's recorded runs
events.message:
fix(app): stop hybrid_text_rows from also dropping the row's recorded runs

SQ-1609/1611's hybrid_text_rows correctly suppresses the composite's own
PAINT of a row a Hybrid host already draws in cells, but build_chrome_canvas_into
filtered g.px_texts by the skip set ONCE, upstream of everything — so the
per-character glyph loop, which is the ONE place a chrome run's characters
ever reach GlyphSink::blit (the only place a V6TextRun is ever pushed), never
saw a skipped row's characters at all. A host reading V6Frame::text to draw
Arthur's status bar or Journey's menu itself got no runs for it.

GlyphSink::blit gains a `suppress_paint` parameter that skips just its own
blit_glyph_styled call while recording proceeds unconditionally, independent
of the mode-wide RecordOnly gate. build_chrome_canvas_into's px_texts glyph
loop now walks pen_chains over the UNFILTERED g.px_texts (recomputing
text.skips per run for suppress_paint) instead of the skip-filtered `kept`,
which stays feeding only the two flood fills (fill_reverse_row_gaps,
fill_explicit_bg_rows) exactly as before; the row_bar_tops lookup moves to
the same unfiltered set so a skipped row's recorded `bar` classification
matches what it would be unskipped. The kept.is_empty() early return no
longer skips the whole window's recording, only the two floods. The GridCell
cell-grid fallback gets the identical treatment: the row-level `continue` is
replaced with a per-row suppress_paint flag threaded into fill_cell (blank
cells) and blit (glyph cells).

Added hybrid_text_rows_still_records_the_status_bar_row_it_stops_painting,
which reproduces the brief's Arthur churchyard specimen and asserts the
row-192 runs recorded under an empty hybrid_text_rows and under one naming
row 192 are byte-identical, while the canvas pixel still differs (baked vs.
transparent) — falsified by temporarily reverting the glyph loop to the
skip-filtered list, which reproduced the reported symptom (row's runs vanish
entirely) before the fix was reapplied.

The GridCell fallback shares the identical blit-signature fix but has no
specimen in this suite exercising that path with hybrid_text_rows populated;
building one is left uncovered here as disproportionate new fixture work,
relying on the px_texts case's coverage of the shared GlyphSink::blit change.

It is not a foreign hand (same owner, not an executed third-party tool),
so it is not an Oracle; the test head says so. Its independence is its
structure (gap4a + gap1 [+ IAM] + n x (enc + gap2 + gap3) + gap4b, gap2
from the profile instead of a fixed 22/11) and its constants, which do
NOT come from the tree but from gw's own track-length calculation,
greaseweazle src/greaseweazle/codec/ibm/ibm.py:715-725 with :269-272 and
:692-698 (Unlicense): MFM presync 12 / synclen 4, FM 6 / 1, i.e. 40 / 22
bytes per sector around the data and an IAM of 16 / 7.

Promises per profile: (a) the cross-calculation's sum equals track_bytes
exactly where uft_fdc_gaps_schliessen() says the profile closes; (b) the
gap4b it derives equals uft_fdc_gap_space() - gap3_fmt * sectors;
(c) BAD_ORDER exactly where scripts/audit_fdc_gaps.py's rule
gap3_fmt >= gap3_rw fails; (d) its IAM branch — untested in its own
package (mutation M18 slipped there) — adds exactly the IAM. Two
counter-proofs: gap4b + 1 breaks (a) in BOTH calculations, swapped gap3
values are BAD_ORDER.

Measured: 17 profiles, 11 close, 16 in the gap4b comparison, 13 with an
IAM; 67/67 green. Mutation matrix 7 of 7 caught: three in the tree's
calculation (MFM record 60 -> 58, MFM IAM 16 -> 12, FM record 31 -> 30)
and four in the cross-calculation (gap2 dropped, IAM never counted,
order check removed, gap4b not added). Nothing in src/ changed.

today only the CMake comment and the directory say it.

hand-verified command script (tests/fixtures/walkthroughs/photopia.txt,

of Graham Pearce's published solution, used only as a guide) to the
game's own real ending: "You turn out the light." followed by has_quit()
going true on its own, with no explicit quit+confirm needed. Photopia has

text plus no fault/hang, not a score assertion.

the harness exercises an in-game @save/@restore round trip through the
host archive path, a host Save State/Restore State round trip, and a
separate restart-reboot probe, without disturbing the main run. It also
confirms the mapper and hints machinery don't error while being driven
(Photopia gives the mapper no location signal at all on any turn, so an
empty graph is the verified-correct shape, not a bug) and, since the user
asked to verify determinism empirically rather than trust genre
reputation, runs the entire script twice from fresh boots and asserts the
two transcripts are byte-identical (normalized), pinning the result as a

events.message:
fix(gw): Shugart drives 0-3 and IBM-PC A/B are two buses — the drive combo names both, the provider sets the bus (issue #43 follow-up, MF-1376)

Reported by petrkr on #43 after MF-1365: "Drive 0/1/2 is NOT same as
Drive A/B. Drives 0,1,2 are Shugart interface, drives A,B are IBM/PC —
you can not interchange them and assume Drive 0 == A". Correct:
MF-1365 labelled the combo "A: (Drive 0)" / "B: (Drive 1)" and never set
a bus, so uft_gw_select_drive() fell back to IBM-PC and a Shugart drive
was unreachable (drives 2 and 3 not even offered).

Reference: gw's own drive argument, greaseweazle
src/greaseweazle/tools/util.py:127-141 (Unlicense, read at 26690f8):
'A'/'B' -> (BusType.IBMPC, 0/1), '0'..'3' -> (BusType.Shugart, 0..3).

- gw_drive_unit_select.h: GwBus/GwDrive; gw_drive_from_combo() returns
  bus AND unit. Combo data: A/B keep 0/1, Shugart unit u is 16 + u.
- GreaseweazleProviderV2::set_drive(bus, unit); set_drive_unit(u) stays
  as the IBM-PC shorthand. ensure_drive_selected() sends
  uft_gw_set_bus_type() before every (re)select — as gw does — and
  checks the unit against the bus (IBM-PC 0..1, Shugart 0..3).
- HardwareTab: "A: (IBM-PC bus)", "B: (IBM-PC bus)", "Drive 0..3
  (Shugart bus)"; connect and change pass bus and unit.
- src/hal/uft_greaseweazle_full.c (protected) is NOT touched; its public
  uft_gw_set_bus_type() suffices.

(test_gw_rpm_indexzeiten, B1-B3): with set_drive() but without the bus
command, B1 "Shugart drive 2 -> firmware on the Shugart bus, unit 2" was

The "24 entries" was JumpTableProbe's targets= field, which counts distinct

events.title: fix(fat): Atari ST DD rows carry 5 sectors per FAT — SED 5.68 and Hatari agree; SED registered as a Spec source, one attribution corrected (MF-1374)
events.message:
fix(fat): Atari ST DD rows carry 5 sectors per FAT — SED 5.68 and Hatari agree; SED registered as a Spec source, one attribution corrected (MF-1374)

Owner package sed_568.zip (SED 5.68, Atari-ST disk monitor by Anton
Stepper and Claus Brod). It contains no C code and no tests, only a
68000 program, a tokenised GFA-BASIC source and documentation, and it is
NOT freely licensed ("kommerzielle Software, keine PD-Software!",
SED_568.HLP; "alle Verwertungsrechte bleiben bei den Autoren",
README.1ST). Channel: Spec only — numbers cited, no file of the package
in the tree or the corpus. Most of what it holds was taken over in
MF-831/832 (P3-59/61/62); three points were new:

- uft_fat_std_geometries[]: the Atari ST SS and DS rows listed 3 sectors
  per FAT, the PC-720K value. SED's media-byte table (12 of 12 rows
  arithmetically consistent, recomputed) and Hatari
  createBlankImage.c:13-27/:143-148 (GPL-2, read only: nTracks >= 80 ->
  SPF 5) both say 5. The file size cannot decide it: with SPF 3 there
  are 713 clusters and the 12-bit FAT needs 1073 bytes, which fits in 3
  sectors. Owner decision: correct DD only. Left as they were and named:
  the HD row (SED SPF 6, Hatari SPF 9 — the sources disagree) and the SS
  media byte (SED 0xF9, Hatari 0xF8).
- scripts/audit_fat_boundary.py attributed the cluster limit 4086 to
  "SED 5.68 HLP". Measured: neither 4086 nor 4085 occurs in the HLP, the
  DOC, the diff or the strings of the GFA source. Corrected to
  "unbelegt"; the gate's behaviour is unchanged (11/11, 0 findings).
- docs/ORACLES.md: SED 5.68 row, Spec source with a redistribution
  restriction, treated like Sedory (MF-1181).
- P3-597: the Atari rows are unreachable — uft_fat_geometry_from_size()
  returns the first row of a size and the PC/MSX rows come first — and
  HD plus the SS media byte stay unbelegt.

Red first: tests/test_fat_atari_geometrie.c, 2 red (SS 3, DS 3) -> 6/6;
it also holds every other field of both rows and the PC-720K row's 3.

events.message:
feat(app): let a live resize honor min_story_screen in pane space (SQ-1606)

sync_zvm_screen_dims/resize_glulx's own live-resize entry point,
host::screen::set_story_pane, takes a PANE — the rect a host's own layout
already carved past the help bar — not the terminal size
min_terminal_size_for_story_floor needs, so a host at a live resize had no
way to reach that search without re-deriving a terminal size or making a
second call just to learn what pane its answer yields (exactly what
sq1596_min_story_screen_floor.rs's own
a_host_can_call_the_search_directly_at_a_live_resize test had to route
around).

Adds host::screen::min_story_pane_for_floor: an engine-aware, pane-space
sibling of min_terminal_size_for_story_floor. A v4+, non-v6 Z-machine
session searches the same declared_story_screen_dims chrome subtraction a
live resize already applies, via the exact bump_dim_for_floor sweep
boot.rs uses (widened to pub(super) rather than forked); v1-3/v6 sessions
are exempt, matching declared_story_screen_dims's own exemption; a Glulx
session has no chrome subtraction at all, so bumping real against floor
directly is the identity mapping.

set_story_pane now consults state.min_story_screen and routes the incoming
pane through this search before either engine call, so a host only has to
set TerminalFacts::min_story_screen once at launch and every later resize
honors it automatically. None (the default) leaves behavior byte-identical
to before.

events.title: feat(ipf): IPF delivers sectors — CAPS-encoded elements, blocks sized by the file, and the gap filled as the format says (P3-360 part 1, P3-361, MF-1373)
events.message:
feat(ipf): IPF delivers sectors — CAPS-encoded elements, blocks sized by the file, and the gap filled as the format says (P3-360 part 1, P3-361, MF-1373)

Until now every IPF yielded cells and zero sectors (P3-360). The two
files used here did not even yield cells: 0 of 160 tracks with a cell
stream in both full 80-cylinder versions. The Amiga file failed with
"cell count does not meet the announced 100150 bits"; the PC file
failed with "19 blocks, the reader holds 16". The reference files come
from disk-analyse (Keir Fraser, disk-utilities, public domain, source
5e690f3a), whose IPF writer is independent of AIR, the base of
uft_ipf_air.c. The input is UFT's own self-naming image; recipe:
tests/corpus_manifest/gen_ipf_corpus.py.

What was missing in the reader:
- Data elements were only split for the SPS encoder. MF-1079 stated
  that the CAPS encoder has none; it has them, counted in bytes.
- For the CAPS encoder the block flags field does not apply. Keir
  Fraser's ipfinfo/ipf.txt says "ignored and assumed 0", and MAME
  ipf_dsk.cpp does the same.
- At most 16 blocks per track (P3-361). Blocks are now allocated per
  DATA record: as many as announced AND carried by the payload (32
  bytes per descriptor).
- The element parser misbehaved silently:
  - from the 17th element on it stopped advancing;
  - a value past the end left an uninitialised block of full length;
  - data_size*8 overflowed uint32;
  - offsets were checked against the end of the file instead of the
    end of the payload.
- The gap was always MFM(0x00) forward. For the CAPS encoder it is now
  the file's fill byte, forward and backward, with the splice at the
  index for the last block (ipf.txt "1. No gap streams", MAME
  generate_block_gap_0).
- The SPS path stays bit-identical: it is calibrated on the two SPS
  images (MF-1079) and there is no measurement for another fill value
  (P3-596).

New: src/formats/ipf/uft_ipf_sektoren.c. It decodes nothing itself.
- It passes the cell stream to the two existing decoders,
  uft_mfm_decode_track() and flux_decode_amiga_bits().
- It picks one by valid header checksums, not by the platform field;
  disk-analyse writes "Amiga" for every file.
- If both find valid headers, it creates no sectors.
- Sectors carry what the decoder measured: header/data CRC, deleted
  mark, and UFT_SECTOR_CRC_CHECKED.

Red first: tests/test_ipf_sektorebene.c against the IPF sources of
e98e0e9a gave 11 of 20 red, 0 of 88 and 0 of 72 sectors; the full disks
gave 0 of 1760 and 0 of 1440.

After the fix, 30 of 30:
- 88/88 Amiga and 72/72 PC sectors at their own location mark, all
  checksums valid;
- full disks: 1760/1760 and 1440/1440;
- MFM cell rule: 0 adjacent ones, longest zero run 3;
- gap check: 1531/1531 and 640/640 data cells, splice at cell 3062
  of 4342 (the index).

Mutation matrix 12 of 12. T3 (CAPS flags not zeroed) escaped at first,
because disk-analyse already writes 0. Probe F now sets flags = 7.

Also:
- test_ipf_satzlauf_schranken 4a/4b (element past the payload end): red
  against e98e0e9a only via the SPS encoder, because the CAPS path did
  not split elements there. The probe was changed accordingly.
- test_ipf_air_accessors 7b now pins the new meaning of
  blocks_truncated with three tracks (20/20, 20/8, 8/no DATA).
- The IPF test branches link the one format-layer library instead of
  a fifth explicit list. The two probe tests with long explicit lists
  get the decoders added, so their plugin set stays the same.

The data regions of all 160 tracks of both disks are cell-identical to
disk-analyse's HFE of the same source. Gaps differ by design: for
containers without a gap description, disk-analyse's tbuf_gap() writes
MFM(0x00).

Not measured:
- SPS originals: the restricted corpus was not available.
- Gap streams (types 1-3).
- Copy-protection tracks.

Found on the way:
- P3-595: the 86F plugin takes sectors with a bad CRC as good.
- P3-596: SPS gap fill vs. MAME/ipf.txt.

Checks:
- ctest: 561/563. test_hardware_tab_gui and test_provider_switch fail
  locally only (no Qt6::SerialPort).
- check_consistency.py rc 0.
- verify_build_sources.py: no new divergence.

events.title: fix(ipf): bound the record walk, hand the CRC to the track, and count dropped track headers (MF-1372)
events.message:
fix(ipf): bound the record walk, hand the CRC to the track, and count dropped track headers (MF-1372)

ipf_air_parse() computed positions and record lengths in uint32_t and
never checked that a record covers its own 12-byte header. Any file that
starts with "CAPS" could therefore:
- hang the reader: an unknown record with length 0 left the position
  where it was;
- make it read past the buffer: a DATA payload length of 0xFFFFFFF0
  wrapped `pos + dr.length <= size` (ASan: stack-buffer-overflow in
  air_crc32_buffer).

Two further cases passed silently with IPF_AIR_OK: a record running past
the end of the file, and a DATA payload behind the end of the file. Both
were skipped without a CRC check.

The CRC was computed and read only by a printf, while the plugin
advertises UFT_FORMAT_CAP_VERIFY. IMGE records outside 84 x 2 and every
record after the 512th (fixed images[512]) were dropped without a count.

Fix:
- A record shorter than its header is IPF_AIR_BAD_RECORD.
- A record or DATA payload past the end of the file is IPF_AIR_TRUNCATED
  (sums in 64 bit).
- The CRC now belongs to the track:
  - a broken IMGE record sets UFT_TRACK_HDR_CRC and the track is ended,
    the same rule as TD0;
  - a broken DATA record sets the new UFT_TRACK_DATA_CRC (uft_types.h,
    1 << 7) and the track is still delivered, named;
  - open() warns with the total.
- Out-of-range track headers are counted (ipf_air_get_dropped_images())
  and the DATA link list grows.

Red first: tests/test_ipf_satzlauf_schranken.c against the unchanged
reader.
- 1a hangs (timeout 10 s, rc 124).
- 1b hangs (killed at 20 s).
- 1c is the ASan overflow.
- 8 further promises fail: 1d, 1e, 2g, 2h, 2i, 2k, 3b, 3d.

After the fix: 22/22 green under ASan/UBSan. The mutation matrix catches
12 of 12. M12 escaped at first because the test track had
track_bits = 0; the fixture was sharpened.

The test computes its CRC-32 with its own bitwise routine after
Louis-Guerin, "IPF Documentation" V0.0 (2012), ch. 2.1/2.5 (PDF sha256
eb1bfcdb95c0ca6f59a526b8f08752c12b2ce76b6c5276bae3c006d3c28241b5), not
with the reader's table.

Checks:
- ctest: 560/562. test_hardware_tab_gui and test_provider_switch fail
  locally only (no Qt6::SerialPort), unchanged by this commit.
- check_consistency.py rc 0.
- verify_build_sources.py: no new divergence.

Docs:
- OPEN_ITEMS P3-594 documents the fix. Still open there: gap/data
  offsets are still summed in uint32, and a second CTEI record leaks the
  first allocation.
- QUARANTINE.md line count 1098 -> 1189. The +91 lines are own code.
- The selftest baseline line number follows the shift.

events.title: cputestgen: fix crashes and invalid header writes
events.message:
cputestgen: fix crashes and invalid header writes

Allow feature_instruction_size to be omitted without dereferencing a null
string. Stop mnemonic searches at the empty-string table sentinel, and
retain a lookup result only when a mnemonic actually matches. This also
lets FPU mnemonics reach their fallback lookup without walking past the
integer instruction table.

Write both reserved header words from a zeroed four-byte buffer instead
of reading beyond that buffer. Rename the private trim helper to avoid
conflicting with the externally declared my_trim function.

Validated Linux and MinGW x64 builds with Windows runs under Wine:
68000/68020 integer samples, 68882 FADD.X, gzip output, an omitted size
setting and an unknown mnemonic. Generated data matches across platforms
after timestamp normalization; all 38 generated headers have zeroed
reserved words.

events.title: feat(app): fold story-overlay rows into hybrid_text_rows's derivation (SQ-1611)
events.message:
feat(app): fold story-overlay rows into hybrid_text_rows's derivation (SQ-1611)

V6HybridChromeLayout::text_rows() (screen.rs) is the correct native-pixel
row-top set for V6FrameInputs::hybrid_text_rows: SQ-1609's own test derived
this by walking only `runs` (the chrome ring's own text), which happened to
match every chrome run on its one specimen (Arthur, which never populates
story_overlay). A host that copied that runs-only walk verbatim would
silently miss any row story_overlay owns on a frame that DOES populate it
(Shogun's boot menu). text_rows() now folds both Vecs together, reading
each entry's shared native-pixel `run.y` (never either type's own `row`
field, which are two different incompatible terminal-cell spaces).

v6_headless_compose.rs's `hybrid_rows` helper now calls text_rows() instead
of hand-rolling the runs-only walk. A new test on Shogun's boot menu proves
text_rows() adds coverage a runs-only walk misses, and — since that
specimen paints no ground at all, so hybrid_text_rows's three existing
compose_v6_frame_into consumers can never show a visible difference on a
story-overlay-only row without one — composes with a synthetic painted
ground standing in for a release that does, to get a real pixel-level
disagreement between the old and new row sets through the actual
blit_paint_ground/fill_story_page_under_chrome_text mechanism. Verified by
reverting text_rows() to skip story_overlay and confirming the new test
fails.

events.message:
feat(formats): every missing sector names its reason — 37 sites, gate 62 without a baseline, and a cut IMD stops dropping sectors (H-30 step 2, P3-558, MF-1371)

H-30 step 2 of 2. Since MF-1370 the bridge maps "missing without a
reason" to UNAVAILABLE plus MISSING_NO_REASON — right as a fallback,
wrong as the rule: a file that is simply too short would read as "not
readable". Every marking in src/formats now carries its reason.

- New helper uft_format_mark_last_short_read(track, f): after a short
  fread, ferror(f) set -> UNAVAILABLE, otherwise the file ended ->
  TRUNCATED. Measured instead of assumed.
- 21 short-read sites use it; d67, dsk_msx and jvc keep their separate
  fseek branch, whose failure is reported as UNAVAILABLE.
- 10 "offset past the data end" sites -> TRUNCATED (cfi, cpm_diskdef,
  cpm_diskdefs x2, hardsector, logical, posix, rcpmfs, sap, myz80).
- Single cases decided: apridisk record missing -> UNAVAILABLE, record
  cut -> TRUNCATED; QRST without a track record -> UNAVAILABLE; DMS
  unpacker ends before -> TRUNCATED, bad track record -> UNAVAILABLE
  (both may stand, the bridge then says TRUNCATED); TD0 partially
  decoded -> TRUNCATED.
- Gate 62 (audit_erfundene_sektoren.py) gains measurement (d):
  mark_missing / "|= UFT_SECTOR_MISSING" without a reason in src/formats,
  baseline 0. Self-test 21/21; against the previous tree 37 findings.
  short_read counts as marking in measurements (a) and (c).

P3-558, IMD half: a file cut inside a track record. Measured before the
fix: a record naming 4 sectors, file ending in sector 3 -> read_track
returned 2 sectors, the other two vanished silently, and sector 3's
"deleted" mark landed on sector 2 (flags went to sectors[count-1] even
when nothing was created in that iteration). The real hxcfe_pc160.imd,
cut in half: cylinder 19 with 7 instead of 8 sectors. Now every sector
the record head names is reported with its ID; the bytes the file holds
stay, the rest is fill marked TRUNCATED; flags go only to the sector of
the current iteration. Not fixed and named in P3-558: the geometry of a
cut file stays smaller (IMD carries no total), a cut inside the record
head still yields no sectors for that track, and the six geometries.

Red first: test_imd_sektor_ids 3 red -> 22/22; new assertions in
test_kurze_datei_erfindet_keine_sektoren (TRD), test_dms_gegen_adf2dms,
test_kurzes_cfi_erfindet_keinen_sektor, and a new partial-decode case in
test_td0_erfindet_keine_sektoren. Full build (4765 steps) and ctest: 561/561 green.
Mutation matrix 8 of 8 caught (helper, TRD, DMS, CFI, TD0, three IMD).

Also filed: P3-593 — the owner's UFT_AdaptiveCopyCore package, checked,
nothing taken over: the transfer core breaks two of its core claims
(retry budget 5 instead of 4 with fallback; an empty backend status
counts as "good" with uninitialised bytes in the buffer), CONTROLLER_CRC
vs READBACK_COMPARE is a label only, and it would add four parallel
worlds (second track-budget calculation against MF-1177, a fourth
capability family, a second recipe table, its own absence model). No
product caller exists (no sector-capable backend). Mutation matrix of
the package: 9 of 20 caught.

caller's default, reproducing today's behaviour exactly.

events.title: feat(disk2): absence is a reason, not padding — SKIPPED/UNAVAILABLE/TRUNCATED as origin, and absence never carries data (H-30 step 1, MF-1370)
events.message:
feat(disk2): absence is a reason, not padding — SKIPPED/UNAVAILABLE/TRUNCATED as origin, and absence never carries data (H-30 step 1, MF-1370)

Owner decision 2026-09-26: H-30 is not a feature but a field in the
center; three values, without EMPTY (a uniformly read sector stays a
sector with data).

- uft_d2_origin_t: SKIPPED = 7, UNAVAILABLE = 8, TRUNCATED = 9, appended
  AFTER UNKNOWN with explicit numbers, because uft_disk2_io.c writes the
  origin as a raw byte into every .uftd file — inserting before UNKNOWN
  would have changed the meaning of every stored UNKNOWN (6).
- uft_d2_add_sector() rejects an absence origin carrying data, a length
  or confidence (ABSENCE_WITH_DATA); each class gets its own ingest note.
- The loader checks the origin byte (ORIGIN_RANGE) instead of accepting
  any byte.
- Plugins name the reason: UFT_SECTOR_UNAVAILABLE (bit 8) and
  UFT_SECTOR_TRUNCATED (bit 9), always together with MISSING, via
  uft_sector_mark_unavailable/_truncated and uft_format_mark_last_*.
  Producers in this step: IMD type 0, TD0 "no data" and unknown method
  (decoded_len == 0), ATX FDC "data not found".
- The bridge stopped mapping every missing sector to PADDING with the
  note "auf dem Traeger stand hier nichts" — measured on an IMD "data
  unavailable" sector: origin 4 (PADDING) instead of 8. Missing without a
  reason becomes UNAVAILABLE plus the finding MISSING_NO_REASON; missing
  sectors no longer pass their fill bytes into the center.
- Tor 62 (audit_erfundene_sektoren.py) accepts the reason helpers as
  marking; self-test 10/13 red with the new cases, 13/13 green.

Red first (old code): test_disk2 14 failures, test_disk2_io 2, test_disk2_
bridge 5, test_imd_sektor_ids 2, test_td0_erfindet_keine_sektoren and
test_atx_layout 1 each — all at the new assertions, every existing
assertion stayed green. Green on current main: full build, ctest
561/561. Mutation matrix 9 of 9 caught.

Not done here (step 2): the 27 "source ends early" sites (TRUNCATED),
apridisk/DMS/QRST single cases, a gate against mark_missing without a
reason, P3-558. Corrected claim: H-14/H-15 do NOT follow automatically —
no verify or copy path uses the center. Named: P3-591 (the real prefix
of a partial sector does not reach the center), P3-592 (a second
absence model in uft_track_layout).

events.title: 0.9.14: AdLib music, a settings program, and the game says why it is silent
events.message:
0.9.14: AdLib music, a settings program, and the game says why it is silent

Why there is no music. A player reported silence and no conversion, and there
was nothing to go on: with no tunes to convert the game simply said nothing.
The reason is now decided right after the file map is built and printed on
the loading screen for ten seconds, with a line to quote in a report (mute,
no GM.CAT/ADLIB.CAT, music off, no music.bnk, volume 0). Drawn with the
system font into our own splash buffer, so AGA, RTG and a Workbench window
all show it. (This was 0.9.13; it never shipped on its own.)

AdLib as a second music source. Every tune in ADLIB.CAT carries its own
instruments and the YM3812 emulator (fmopl.cpp, LGPL) was already in the
tree, so nothing new is shipped. Three bugs on the way, all measured:
 - silence: init_music_data read 16-bit lengths from PC data with a raw
   pointer cast - upstream's own big-endian bug; the player never started a
   note (poly=0 peak=0 per tick). Now read byte by byte.
 - 0.74x real time: a float multiply per sample for volume 1.0; skipped,
   1.34x.
 - 320 MB: AdLib scores loop for ever; the render now stops at the first
   repeat using the player's own position, 36 MB for all 22 tracks.
Level >>10, no clipping (at >>9 6.9% of samples clipped).

Retro loading pictures are the default, forced once on an older options.cfg
(config version 3), along with the system pointer; what the player sets
after that is kept.

AmiXcomPrefs, copied from the Master of Magic port's settings program and
fitted to this game: a GadTools window plus a Shell interface that edits the
game's own user/options.cfg line by line. One "Music" row sets both source
and mode (Off, Samples/AdLib live, Samples/AdLib converted); "Convert music"
is disabled in the live modes and runs the game with -amigaConvertOnly 1; a
source.txt next to the tunes records what they were made from, shown in
green (there) or red (missing). Every text in the window is drawn by us with
a black shadow under light letters, so it stays readable whatever palette
the player picks. "Delete music" looked for ReMoM's muzyka/#?.wav and found
nothing - it now counts user/music/#?.raw (32, measured, nothing deleted in
the test). Saving from the window verified: file rewritten byte for byte.

MIDI through camd.library is not in this release.

Keep each project's annotations in its own committed database

A project's annotations are an artifact of that project, so they live in
<project>/.c64-re-tools/annotations.db, one project per file, opened
in-process by the client and committed with the rest of the project. The
first write creates the file; a read without one is refused and creates

gone: the database identifies its own project.

worker thread and its host, and the annotation engine in the broker's
resources. The boundary test now proves no broker module reaches the
store. export-asm again refuses an --out at or above the store.

events.title: fix(gw): open short port names on Linux/macOS, honour the drive combo and measure RPM from the capture (issues #42, #43, MF-1365)
events.message:
fix(gw): open short port names on Linux/macOS, honour the drive combo and measure RPM from the capture (issues #42, #43, MF-1365)

Reported by petrkr (#42, #43). The protected HAL file
src/hal/uft_greaseweazle_full.c is NOT touched; all changes sit in the
provider and the GUI.

#42 — "can not open greaseweazle ttyACM0":
GreaseweazleProviderV2::open() received the SHORT port name from the
GUI ("ttyACM0") and handed it to the HAL unchanged. Outside Windows a
name that does not start with '/', './' or '../' now gets "/dev/" in
front — Qt's own portNameToSystemLocation() rule. Windows is unchanged
(#ifdef _WIN32). Using systemLocation() in the GUI instead was rejected:
on Windows it would give a doubled prefix.

#43 — "drive select seem to not work":
- D1: the drive combo selected nothing. Its entries now carry the unit
  (0/1) with IBM-PC labels "A: (Drive 0)" / "B: (Drive 1)", the unit is
  passed to open() and set_drive_unit() (motor off first), and the combo
  is locked while a flux job runs (WorkflowTab::fluxJobRunningChanged ->
  HardwareTab). Firmware check (greaseweazle-firmware floppy.c): B: is
  IBM-PC unit 1, select pin 12, motor pin 16 — the reporter's
  `gw rpm --drive=1`.
- D2: do_measure_rpm() sent CMD_GET_INDEX_TIMES (0x0A), which the
  firmware does not know, and always failed with "no index intervals".
  It now reads the index times of the capture it just made, skips entry
  0 (partial revolution), averages full revolutions only, refuses 0 Hz
  (UFT_GW_ERR_NO_CLOCK) instead of assuming 72 MHz, and names the pulse
  count in the error.

Red first (against base 3557ecfb): test_gw_rpm_indexzeiten 10 of 15
promises red ("RPM measurement produced no index intervals",
unknown_cmds=1); test_hardware_tab_gui 2 failed ("Drive 0" instead of
"A: (Drive 0)", combo not locked). Green: rpm 15/15 (300, 150, partial
+ 2 full = 150, 84 MHz = 300, jitter 0.995 %), drive_unit_select 7/7,
hardware_tab_gui 15/15, port_kurzname 6/6 on Linux (pty rig), named skip
on Windows.

Review round 1 found 8 defects (among them a false "12 of 12
mutations" claim in the draft issue comment and 7 stale "drive_unit 0
is the only value" comments); all 8 were fixed and re-checked against
the patch. Full build and ctest on current main: see below.

Not tested (measured, not assumed): no test target compiles the GW
connect branch (UFT_HAS_HAL occurs 0 times in the test build.ninja), so
connect-with-unit, combo change while connected and the job lock wiring
are exercised by NO test -> P3-564. The drive combo is read only by the
Greaseweazle path; KryoFlux (-d0), FluxEngine (drive:0), XUM1541
(device 8) and SCP (no SELA/SELB sender) ignore it -> P3-565. No real
hardware (MF-310).

events.title: Add export-project and import-project, and close the store milestone
events.message:
Add export-project and import-project, and close the store milestone

A project lives only in the broker's database and project.json is
gitignored, so anno export-project --out FILE writes the whole project as
the fixtures' export document, and anno import-project FILE fills an
empty project from one. Import runs in one transaction through a new
applyAtomically() in the store, so a document the store refuses part-way
leaves the project untouched; a non-empty project is refused, never
merged. The smoke test moves a project between two workspaces through the
real bin and gets identical bytes back.

The store-ownership standard, tech stack, mission and roadmap now
describe the broker-owned store as built.

events.title: Route every anno verb and call through the broker's project
events.message:
Route every anno verb and call through the broker's project

The anno CLI and anno call no longer take a store: each call confines its
paths, stages the input bytes, and asks the broker for this workspace's
project, named by .c64-re-tools/project.json. A first write registers the
project; a read before any write is refused and creates nothing.
render-memmap and export-asm now require --out, decomp-completeness
takes --fixture, and the render banner no longer names a store.

A new structural test walks every shipped client module's imports and
proves none reaches anno-store or node:sqlite; its first run caught an
inline type import that still loaded the store. Refusal tests cover a
missing broker, an old broker and a malformed project.json, and smoke
tests drive the real bin against a harness broker. The skill docs and
the routine-queue-walker gate follow the new verb shapes.

events.title: grm-om3i: compute the effective target once per WalkInputs
events.message:
grm-om3i: compute the effective target once per WalkInputs

PcodeConstantSemantics asked for the effective target, forced its own address
thunk (another walk for the index register), and then called memoryOperand(),
which recomputed the target. TABLE resolves it once. Every repeat spent the
shared Budget, so a deep PCODE query could run out where TABLE resolved.

WalkInputs becomes a small class that memoizes the target. PCODE forces its
own address only when a target exists to disagree with. TABLE asks for the
target once per instance, so its behaviour is unchanged.

Also corrects the SBC-borrow commentary from grm-4wqd. It is grm-ef46 defect
(2), already fixed in 6502core.sinc and in upstream PR #9656 (grm-2g7g, closed
as a duplicate), not a newly found bug.

Gates: build-and-test.sh check SUITE PASS. realrom-test.sh check nes (TABLE):
pass=29 fail=5, all known-varying (megaman shows its 1705<->1698 jitter).
PCODE forced: pass=31 fail=3 (dodge, ff1, lwings), rcransom passes.

events.message:
fix(kryoflux): der Lesepfad dekodierte DTCs Protokoll als Fluss — jetzt liest er die Stromdatei (P3-562 Teil 2, MF-1363)

DTC schreibt den Rohstrom nach `<praefix>NN.S.raw` (KryoFlux-Handbuch:
„test_23.1.raw will be stream test_") und druckt auf stdout ein
Protokoll. do_read_raw_flux() nahm `result.stdout_text` als Strom — der
Kopfkommentar nannte das selbst einen „test-mode shortcut"; in
Produktion war es DTCs Konsolentext. Die Tests konnten es nicht sehen,
weil sie den Strom selbst ueber stdout lieferten.

Rotbeweis zuerst: die neue Test-Attrappe
tests/mock_hardware/dtc_strom_datei.h trennt stdout (Text) und
Stromdatei. Gegen den Vorzustand kommt FluxMarginal statt Fluss heraus
— der Provider dekodierte den Text.

Behoben im PROVIDER, nicht im Laeufer (Abweichung vom Plan, begruendet
in docs/plans/DTC_UPGRADE.md): er liest die Datei selbst, DtcRunResult
und DtcRunner bleiben unveraendert. Der Name kommt aus EINER Funktion,
KryoFluxProviderV2::stream_file_path() (dazu stream_prefix()). Vor dem
Lauf wird eine alte Datei gleichen Namens entfernt, damit nie der Strom
eines frueheren Laufs als dieser gelesen wird; fehlt die Datei nach
Erfolg, ist das ein ProviderError mit Pfad, kein FluxMarginal.

Abnahme ueber einen echten Prozess: test_laeufer_argv Fall 6 — das
Test-Werkzeug schreibt im DTC-Modus den Korpus-Strom
hxcfe_kfx_t00.0.raw nach der Handbuchregel, rechnet den Namen dabei
UNABHAENGIG, und der Provider liefert 115 342 Uebergaenge und 3
Indexmarken, wie der Korpusbefund MF-1024 sie nennt. 13 von 13.

Mutationsmatrix 4 von 4: stdout wieder als Fluss (decodes_stream, 6a),
alte Datei nicht entfernen (alte_datei), Name ohne Nullauffuellung
(NUR 6a — die Attrappe benutzt dieselbe Funktion wie der Provider,
deshalb braucht es die unabhaengige Rechnung), fehlende Datei als
FluxMarginal (stdout_ist_kein_fluss).

Neu offen (in P3-562 eingetragen): die Stromdatei bleibt im

events.message:
fix(laeufer): dtc und fluxengine bekamen ihren eigenen Namen als erstes Argument — gemessen an einem echten Prozess (P3-562 Teil 1, MF-1362)

Die Provider bauen argv nach der execve-Konvention (Programmname an
Stelle 0), QProcess nimmt das Programm aber schon ueber setProgram().
Der unveraendert weitergereichte argv kam deshalb als `dtc dtc -i0`
und `fluxengine fluxengine version` an — bei JEDEM Aufruf, auch der
Geraeteerkennung. Die Mock-Tests konnten das nicht sehen: der
SubprocessMock startet nichts.

Rotbeweis zuerst: tests/test_laeufer_argv.cpp laesst die ECHTEN Laeufer
einen echten Prozess starten (tests/argv_echo/uft_argv_echo.c, schreibt
seine Argumente auf) — einmal direkt, einmal ueber
KryoFluxProviderV2::detect_drive() und
FluxEngineProviderV2::query_version(). Gegen den Vorzustand 7 von 10
Zusagen rot, danach 10 von 10.

Behoben an EINER Stelle, aber nicht in run_subprocess(): der
FC5025-Laeufer baut seine Argumente ohne Programmnamen, ein pauschales
Abschneiden haette dort `-f` verschluckt (Zusage 5). Der Helfer
werkzeug_argumente() gilt fuer die beiden execve-Laeufer und sagt mit
rc -4 ab, bevor ein Prozess laeuft, wenn argv leer ist oder an Stelle 0
eine Option steht — sonst wuerde still das erste Argument verworfen.

Mutationsmatrix 4 von 4, jede an ihrer eigenen Zusage: Abschneiden weg
(1b 2b 3a 3b 4a-c), nur KryoFlux behoben wie im Zulieferpaket (2b 3b 4c),
pauschal in run_subprocess() (4a-c, 5), blind schneiden ohne Absage
(4a 4b).

Regression: test_kryoflux_provider_v2, test_kryoflux_dtc_befehl,
test_provider_temppfad, test_fluxengine_provider_v2,
test_fluxengine_befehl, test_fc5025_provider_v2, test_wiring_runtime,
test_honest_stubs_stay_honest gruen. test_hardware_tab_gui und
test_provider_switch fallen in dieser Umgebung (Qt 6.4.2 ohne
Qt6::SerialPort) VOR und NACH der Aenderung identisch.

Offen: P3-562 Teil 2 (stdout als KryoFlux-Fluss) und Teil 3 (-r) —
DTC-2 und DTC-3 in docs/plans/DTC_UPGRADE.md. A-035 in Arbeit, A-032
an der Umgebung angehalten (neue-ideen/ liegt nicht im Container).

events.title: grm-4wqd: PcodeConstantSemantics, selectable per program by analyzer option
events.message:
grm-4wqd: PcodeConstantSemantics, selectable per program by analyzer option

The constant evaluator seam grm-as0m left now has a second implementation:
PcodeConstantSemantics interprets one instruction's own p-code, lazily, so
only the inputs the queried location depends on are ever asked of the walk.
Arithmetic goes through Ghidra's OpBehaviorFactory. The walk and all of its
guards stay in StoredValueScanner, unchanged.

The operand byte is always Inputs.memoryOperand(), the same authority TABLE
uses. PCODE declines only when its own computed address and the scanner's
effective target are both known and disagree. That keeps the stack-relative
reload (rcransom FUN_fed1) resolving under PCODE.

Loc gains D. Under PCODE an unestablished D is assumed 0, through a single
per-program seam (owner ruling 2026-09-26). Follow-ups are grm-jjwx (per-game
override) and grm-lly5 (tracking D alongside bank state). The walk and TABLE
still decline on an unknown D.

BoardBankAnalyzer registers a "Constant Evaluator" option, TABLE (default) or
PCODE. It is read once per query tree via Budget. SetAnalyzerOption.java lets
the real-ROM tier force PCODE through REALROM_EXTRA_PRESCRIPT.

Known differences from TABLE, pinned in PcodeConstantSemanticsDifferentialTest:
stock 6502 ADC drops a carry that arises from the carry-in alone (grm-o9k);
stock SBC's borrow flag is wrong on A=$01,SEC,SBC #$02; and SED in the window
makes PCODE evaluate decimal mode while TABLE stays binary.

Gates: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK (TABLE, no golden moved).
realrom-test.sh check nes with PCODE forced: pass=31 fail=3 (dodge,
dragonpower, lwings, all bistable), rcransom PASS. megaman is
nondeterministic on unmodified HEAD too (ab-test.sh, 2 repeats per side),
so it is not attributable to this change.

events.title: Let the Knight Lore room editor change the castle's floor shapes and add more, up to the 32 the game can name
events.message:
Let the Knight Lore room editor change the castle's floor shapes and add more, up to the 32 the game can name

A room names its shape in bits 3 to 7 of its attribute byte, and
room_size_tbl -- each shape's X and Y half-sizes and floor height, which
found_screen copies into $5BAB, $5BAC and $5BAE -- runs up to the rooms. Only
retrieve_screen's LD HL,location_tbl at $D3CC names where they start, so both
packers now write however many shapes the castle has, move the rooms down
three bytes a shape, and patch that operand ($D3CD). A half-size is 1 to 127,
keeping the walls inside a byte either side of $80. The decoder reads the
shapes a patched game has, and the castle's rules say shapeLimit 32; a castle
saved in the page before now is given it, as it is given the starting rooms.

The editing itself is the room designer's new Shapes tab, in the emulator
repository.

Checked: a fourth shape, 48 by 48, with room $B3 on it, packs to the same
bytes in Python and JavaScript, with the rooms at $6254; and the game, made
to start in $B3, built it with half-sizes of 48 and its floor at 128. Its
walls are still drawn where the square room's are -- they are scenery -- which
is what the designer now warns about.

events.title: fix(input): smooth magic-mouse pointer on native screens (#2363)
events.message:
fix(input): smooth magic-mouse pointer on native screens (#2363)

* fix(input): smooth magic-mouse pointer on native screens

Absolute IECLASS_POINTERPOS events from the virtual mouse driver are
serviced by the guest at a low rate, so the native-screen pointer moved
in visible multi-pixel steps while the host delivered smooth positions.
Feed the delta between consecutively delivered absolute positions into
the relative mouse pipeline (serviced every vsync like normal mouse
input); the absolute events still anchor the exact position, so there
is no double movement.

Fixes #2279

* fix(input): route mousehack deltas via the originating mouse device

Multi-mouse setups map each host mouse to its own device index; the
native-screen delta injection always dispatched through mice[0]. Record
the device that delivered the position and select its mapping for the
relative events, so the injected movement follows the same port
bindings as the originating device.

Wrap all added code in ifdef AMIBERRY guards and keep shared lines
byte-identical to upstream WinUAE so future core merges do not
clobber the additions.

* fix(input): skip mousehack delta injection for disabled mouse devices

The disabled-device branch of setmousestate() still delivers absolute
positions through mousehack_helper(), but the synthesized relative
events must not bypass the user's disabled-device setting. Gate the
native-screen delta injection on the originating device being enabled.

* fix(input): keep mousehack anchoring deltas un-inverted

Per-axis ID_FLAG_INVERT would reverse only the synthesized relative
delta while the absolute IECLASS_POINTERPOS anchor stays un-inverted,
moving the pointer opposite to the host between guest driver updates.
The delta is already exact in the absolute coordinate space, so drop
the inversion from the native-screen injection.

events.title: fix(app): give a Glk proportional split's second child its own true cell count (SQ-1605)
events.message:
fix(app): give a Glk proportional split's second child its own true cell count (SQ-1605)

gvm floors each proportional Glk split's two children independently, so a
50/50-ish split can leave a one-cell remainder that belongs to neither
child (crates/gvm/src/glk.rs's `layout_window`/`split_rect`). The app's
own `engine::Split` only ever carried the FIRST child's fact (`fixed`),
so `render::screen::split_area_bordered` sized the second child by giving
it "whatever's left of the area" — which silently included gvm's withheld
slack cell, drawing the second child (a graphics canvas or grid) one cell
too large. Kerkerkruip's centre-column rule windows and its right-edge
window are real examples of this shape.

Fix: `Split` gains a `rest: Option<u16>` field carrying the second
child's own real, independently-floored cell count, as gvm's layout
actually computed it (`None` for a `WinNode::Pair` not built from a real
gvm split — the Z-machine/Scott simple two-window layouts and hand-built
test fixtures, which have no rounding slack to account for and correctly
keep the old "second gets whatever's left" behaviour).

- `glk_backend::AppGlk::convert_tree` reads it straight off gvm's own
  `WinTree`'s `second.rect()` on the split axis, instead of discarding it.
- `render::screen::split_area_bordered` sizes `second` from `rest` when
  known, so a genuine proportional-rounding remainder shows up as
  unclaimed gutter beside the separator (matching gvm's own `split_rect`
  anchoring) instead of being absorbed into `second`'s canvas. It still
  reclaims one cell back into `second` whenever no separator is actually
  drawn there (a `winmethod_NoBorder` split, or a theme that suppresses
  the rule per SQ-0821) — preserving the pre-existing borderless-abut
  guarantee (SQ-0341) rather than exposing a new visible gap on ordinary
  splits that never had slack in the first place.
- Both call sites (`render_node`, `collect_graphics_rects`) now pass
  `split.rest` through.

`WinNode::Pair.border` is sourced from the same `split_border(method)`
call gvm's own layout uses to reserve the border cell (crates/gvm/src/glk.rs
~line 2724), so it cannot disagree with what gvm actually reserved; the
pre-existing, intentional divergence is between that fact and the
THEME's separate decision whether to draw a rule at all (SQ-0821), which
this fix's "reclaim" step accounts for rather than regresses.

Added `split_area_bordered_second_child_uses_its_own_rest_not_the_remainder`
and `split_area_bordered_reclaims_the_border_cell_but_not_the_slack_when_no_rule_is_drawn`
(render::screen tests, t-render), and
`glk_backend::tests::screen_model_split_carries_second_childs_true_cell_count`
(t-session) exercising `convert_tree`'s new field population directly via
`AppGlk` without booting a real game. Falsified: reverting the second
child's sizing to the old "extent minus fixed minus border" formula makes
the new render::screen test fail with a rect exactly one cell too large
(40 instead of 39); reapplying the fix passes.

events.title: fix(app): release the SQ-0681 restore-width floor once a story re-reads $21 (SQ-1604)
events.message:
fix(app): release the SQ-0681 restore-width floor once a story re-reads $21 (SQ-1604)

The SQ-0681 floor on GameSession::boot_screen_cols protects a story that
computes its status-line field columns ONCE at boot (Zork 1 r52) by pinning
the restored save's screen width for the rest of the session. For a story
that instead recomputes its layout from header byte $21 every turn (Lost
Pig), that pin protects nothing after the first post-restore repaint but
still clips the status bar permanently.

zvm: add Machine::header_width_read, a sticky per-turn flag set only inside
the loadb/loadw opcode arms (never Memory::read_byte/read_word generally,
which the interpreter itself calls constantly) when the accessed address
covers header byte $21 - mirroring ScreenState::erase_lower_requested's
shape. Machine::take_header_width_read drains it.

app: GameSession::note_restored_screen_cols now remembers what
boot_screen_cols was immediately before a restore raises it
(pre_restore_screen_cols), but only when the restore actually raises the
floor. GameSession::drain_turn - run once per finished turn, covering both
line- and char-mode paths without any host/turn.rs plumbing - drains
take_header_width_read() and, once it reports the game's own read, reverts
boot_screen_cols to the pre-restore value.

New zvm unit tests exercise loadb $21 / loadw $20 (aligned and misaligned)
directly via exec_2op, confirming the flag fires only for header-width-
covering reads and drains as one-shot. New app suite
lostpig_restore_status_width.rs (LostPig.z8, which re-lays its status line
from $21 every turn) reproduces the permanently-clipped-width symptom
against the pre-fix code and confirms the release; the existing
zork1_restore_status_width.rs regression guard (Zork 1 r52, which never
rereads $21) passes unchanged, keeping its permanent pin.

events.title: feat(809 §5): source in, bytes out — a block assembler
events.message:
feat(809 §5): source in, bytes out — a block assembler

The monitor assembled one line at a time. A patch is a handful of instructions
with at least one label, and typing them through `a` is not a loop anyone runs
twice.

assemble_block: two passes over the existing assemble_line, so `d` and `a`
keep agreeing. Labels (`loop:`), `name = value`, `*`, `<`/`>`, `+`/`-`,
`.byte`, `.word`, one `*=`/`.org` before the first byte. Not a build system —
an include is refused as such. A label used before it is defined is sized
wide in BOTH passes, or the line would shrink between them and every later
address would move; a label known before its use may fold to zero page.

Doors:
- monitor `asm <addr> [<<TAG]` collects lines until `end` (or TAG) and then
  assembles the whole block; sent as one command with newlines (monitor/exec)
  it assembles at once. Writes like `a`, and only if the WHOLE block assembled.
- `asm-file <path> [addr]` — read by the daemon, where every file verb resolves
  its path; the address comes from the file's `*=` when none is given.
- RPC `asm/block {origin, source}` writes NOTHING and answers bytes, labels,
  per-line errors and a `patch` shaped exactly as sandbox/run takes one.

The monitor classified a line by its verb, so lines inside `a` mode and an
`asm` block counted as observing. The entering verb already cuts the future,
so nothing was wrong in practice; classify_in now classifies each line for
what it does.

G6: every documented opcode, as bytes, disassembled by the monitor's own `d`,
assembled back as one block — the same bytes. Plus labels both ways, the wide
rule, `<`/`>`/`*`/`+`, data, and errors carrying their line.

Also: a_client_arriving_while_paused_gets_a_frame read the request flag after
subscribe, while the stream thread subscribe starts CONSUMES that flag the
moment it presents — so under a full workspace run it went red on a machine
that had already sent the frame. It now asserts the frame reaching the client.
20/20 alone; red again with the fix it guards removed.

events.title: A whole-surface blit is one memcpy on a machine without a BLiTTER
events.message:
A whole-surface blit is one memcpy on a machine without a BLiTTER

STDL_BlitSurface of a whole surface onto one the same size - the
background restore - went through STDL_BlitSurfaceEx a memcpy call a
row, and each call's set-up is as long as the copy of a 320-wide row:
42ms for a full screen on a plain 8MHz ST. When the source rectangle
is NULL and the rows have no padding, the surface is one block and
one memcpy of it takes 19.5ms. Keyed, masked, clipped, offset or
padded surfaces, a plane budget below 4 and an active BLiTTER all go
the general path as before.

The check is out of line and only reached without a source rectangle,
so a blit that names one pays a single test: the blitcost sweep on an
STE is within one 5ms tick in 1500 blits at every size. A long-row
path inside STDL_BlitSurfaceEx was tried first and made every small
blit 1-2% slower, through gcc's register allocation in that function.

Measured cycle-exact, full screen: ST 42.2 -> 19.5ms; STE and Mega STE
with the CPU path forced 42.2 -> 19.5 and 33.5 -> 18.2; with a BLiTTER
unchanged (17.2, ~9). Mega STE CPU-forced wide rows move 2-4% in the
sweep; the same library before this change, with only libc shifted by
the same 312 bytes, moves identically, so that is cache placement.

test_pixel checks the copy, the dstrect writeback, that a keyed
source keeps its key, and that a blit between views into wider rows
leaves the bytes beside them alone. BLITCHK passes on ST and STE.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: Explain how Knight Lore draws a moving object, with a frame traced through each stage by the game's own code
events.message:
Explain how Knight Lore draws a moving object, with a frame traced through each stage by the game's own code

A new page, "How a moving object is drawn", and the note moving-objects.md
behind it, follow one object through a frame: save_2d_info keeps its old
picture, the handler moves it and collision shortens the move,
set_wipe_and_draw_flags flags it and marks everything overlapping the
rectangle of its old and new pictures, the rectangle is cleared in the
off-screen buffer, every marked object is drawn into it whole in depth
order, and only the rectangle is copied to the display -- nothing erased on
screen, nothing else changed.

The page's example is generated at every build: knightlore_pages.py runs the
game in the simulator to room $01 and stops frame 3 after the object walk,
after the wipe, at each render_obj and after the copy, and shows the four
stages with the rectangles outlined, the depth order the sort chose and the
rectangles copied -- 3 changed objects, 3 rectangles, 14 objects redrawn.

Reading the copy code settled an open question in depth-order.md: marking
only the objects that overlap a mover's rectangle cannot leave a glitch,
because only the rectangle is copied and nothing else can put a pixel in it.

1. uft_gw_open_stream() fuhr KEINEN Handschlag. dev->info blieb leer,
   jede Erfassung ueber die Naht meldete sample_freq = 0, und
