events.title: Describe all of Knight Lore: every entry titled and described, every placeholder name replaced, the rooms laid out from the game
events.message:
Describe all of Knight Lore: every entry titled and described, every placeholder name replaced, the rooms laid out from the game

The map from tcdev (as converted by Michael R. Cook) gave every byte a block
and most routines a name, but 817 of the 844 entries had only a placeholder
title, 289 labels were placeholders (loc_B000) and 20 instructions carried a
comment. All 844 are now titled and described, no placeholder names are left,
and 1894 of 4352 instructions are commented. The descriptions were written in
one pass by eight agents, a subsystem each, from a shared brief; each
fragment passed ctl_tools.py's checks and a build before it was merged.

Corrections to what was written before, each checked against the code:
- the sprite header's width is bits 0-3; bits 6 and 7 say whether the stored
  sprite is currently mirrored or upside down, since the game flips sprites
  in place -- so spr_014's bit 7 is not a flag;
- the sprite table at $7112 is a word per graphic number, not type x 8 + frame;
- read_port's OUT does not select the half-row: IN A,($FE) does, by itself;
- the special-object table is filled by init_special_objects, not the
  play_audio the old text linked; game_loop runs once per room, not per frame.

The rooms, background pieces and charm places, described record by record,
are the level design in other words, so they are not committed:
knightlore_data.py generates them from the snapshot at every build, and
trim_overlaps makes room for them. Checked against the agents' decoding: all
128 rooms, 89 pieces and 32 places agree.

The build now lists every routine's callers (ListRefs=2), links LD operands,
and names each routine after its address in the routines list. Warnings went
from 65 to none: addresses in comments became links, the shift tables at
$F200 got an entry of their own, and twelve constants that look like
addresses got nowarn.

Checked in a running game: driving it, the input byte, the pause, the room
variable, and pushing -- a table moves a step per frame of contact, and the
block the game calls moveable cannot be moved at all.

Reassembles byte-for-byte and writes back the snapshot it read.

events.title: Add ctl_tools.py: count instruction-comment lengths from the listing, and check a fragment before merging
events.message:
Add ctl_tools.py: count instruction-comment lengths from the listing, and check a fragment before merging

An instruction comment in a control file is `$ADDR,N`, and a wrong N makes
sna2skool silently re-decode from the middle of an instruction. `ranges`
takes a draft written with instruction ranges ($A-$B) and fills in N from the
game's own listing, reporting any #R$ADDR that is not an entry start.
`check` is what a fragment must pass before it is merged: comments start and
end on instructions, every entry in the range has a title, no label ends in
_<digit> or clashes with another, and nothing strays outside the range.

Three of the eight agents that described Knight Lore wrote the range
converter for themselves; this is it once, for every game.

events.title: feat(809 §4): a sandbox that writes its media writes a copy
events.message:
feat(809 §4): a sandbox that writes its media writes a copy

A run that writes its disk or programs its cart's flash now gets its own copy
in <project>/sandbox/<stamp>-<run-id>/, reported under `media` in the run's
result; a run that only reads makes no folder. The original image is never
written. The stamp is the daemon's start time, so a restarted daemon — which
numbers its runs from 1 again — never writes into an earlier run's folder.

Written is decided on the bytes, not on a dirty flag: the disk as written
after the run against the disk as written at the anchor, the cart's image
after against before. A flag inherited from the live machine would copy media
for a run that never wrote.

G7b, asserted with real writes rather than mount flags: a GCR sector encoded
onto the clone's track (the disk auto-persist test's write) lands in the copy
at T18/S0 while the original .d64 and the live disk stay byte-identical; an
EasyFlash programming sequence lands in the copy's .crt while the original
file stays identical and the live cart never goes dirty. A run that reads
only reports no media.

events.title: fix(809 §9): a sandbox run is not the live machine
events.message:
fix(809 §9): a sandbox run is not the live machine

sandbox/run and sandbox/runMany dispatched runtime/overlay_run against the
shared state, and overlay_run restores into st.session and pauses it. Every
"sandbox" run rewound, patched, ran and stopped the machine the human was
watching, one after another, while the door's comment said the live machine
was never used. G7 was never a test, so nothing contradicted the comment.

Now the shared state is touched twice: to take the anchor's snapshot and a
clone of the machine, and to file the results. Each run restores into its own
clone and runs on its own thread, as many at once as the host has cores; the
lock is not held while anything runs.

What a run reports changed with it:
- ids are numbered daemon-wide (r-0001 is never handed out twice);
- `endAnchorId` held the START anchor. It is `anchorId` now, and `endStateId`
  (sb-r-NNNN) names the run's real end state, captured from its clone and kept
  (the last 32) so runtime/component_diff can compare two of them;
- registers, reads, and a RAM digest ride every run.

G5 was also narrower than claimed: overlay_run and goto resolved a mark name,
component_diff and pin did not. The ring resolves it now, at the one lookup
every door passes through (id first, so a name never shadows an anchor).
unpin stays id-only: unpinning a mark by name would release the pin G1 needs.

The patch/read/register/run code overlay_run had inline is shared with the
sandbox, so the two cannot drift in what a patch means; checkpoint capture
works on any machine.

Tests: G7 (live clock, PC, RAM digest and run state identical after a
three-run fan-out) — proved RED on the old handler, green on this one; runs
isolated from each other with diffable ends; ids unique across calls; G5 at
component_diff and pin. cargo test -p trx64-daemon -p trx64-core: 1184 ok.

events.title: glibc-2.34 was the first version with user-accessible 64-bit time_t.
events.message:
glibc-2.34 was the first version with user-accessible 64-bit time_t.

glibc-2.31 started using 64-bit time_t syscalls, but glibc-2.34 was the
first one to expose it to userspace.

Expanded Ubuntu listing:
- Ubuntu 19.04 (Disco):   kernel  5.0 ❌, glibc-2.29 ❌
- Ubuntu 19.10 (Eoan):    kernel  5.3 ✅, glibc-2.30 ❌
- Ubuntu 20.04 (Focal):   kernel  5.4 ✅, glibc-2.31 ❌
- Ubuntu 20.10 (Groovy):  kernel  5.8 ✅, glibc-2.32 ❌
- Ubuntu 21.04 (Hirsute): kernel 5.11 ✅, glibc-2.33 ❌
- Ubuntu 21.10 (Impish):  kernel 5.13 ✅, glibc-2.34 ✅

There's a larger range of releases that support 64-bit time_t syscalls
in the kernel but don't support 64-bit time_t in glibc than what I had
listed previously, but it's still a 2-year window. Adding dirct support
for 64-bit time_t syscalls for these particular releases doesn't make
sense, especially when Ubuntu stopped supporting i386 as a host system
after 18.04 (Bonic). (armhf could potentially still make use of it, but
armhf is still supported with current releases, so just upgrade.)

events.title: fix(audit): C6 hielt das Malzeichen in `n * sizeof(int)` fuer einen Zeiger — Code-Scanning-Alarm #16 (P3-560, MF-1353)
events.message:
fix(audit): C6 hielt das Malzeichen in `n * sizeof(int)` fuer einen Zeiger — Code-Scanning-Alarm #16 (P3-560, MF-1353)

Die Regel C6 („sizeof als Laengenargument") sucht die Zeigergroesse
einer Zeichenkette als Vergleichslaenge. Sie schlug an, sobald im
Laengenargument IRGENDEIN `*` stand — auch das Malzeichen in
`memcmp(l->rc_vor, l->rc_jetzt, l->koepfe * sizeof(int))`
(src/core/uft_disk2_bridge.c:114, aus MF-1347). Beide Puffer sind
`calloc(koepfe, sizeof(int))`; die Laenge ist genau richtig.

Seit MF-1353 zaehlt nur ein Stern IM Operanden von sizeof
(`sizeof(char *)`, `sizeof(*p)`), und ein Typname ohne Stern
(Grundtypen, `struct X`, `_t`-Konvention) ist ausgenommen. Was die
Regel ohne Typwissen nicht entscheiden kann — ein Ausdruck wie
`sizeof(a->b)` —, bleibt ein Fund `pruefen`.

Gemessen ueber src und include (alte Fassung aus HEAD gegen neue):
278 -> 277 Funde, weg genau uft_disk2_bridge.c:114, dazu 0; die
Grundlinie ist nicht betroffen (Tor: 464 in der Grundlinie, 0 NEU).

Rotbeweis: 8 neue Selbsttest-Faelle (Defekt K), 3 davon rot gegen die
alte Regel; Selbsttest jetzt 26/26 (im Worktree 25/25 — dort fehlt
tools/uft-scout/work/, der Fall sagt es). Mutationen 6 von 7; die
siebte ist gleichwertig: die Namenspruefung weist jedes Satzzeichen
ohnehin ab.

Alarm #15 (src/core/uft_disk2.c:741, `sizeof(a->b)`) ist korrekt —
`a->b` ist `uint8_t b[32]` (Z. 728) — und bleibt fuer die Regel
unentscheidbar. Er wird auf GitHub als „false positive" mit Beleg
verworfen, NICHT in die Grundlinie geschrieben (sie ist nach ihrer
eigenen Notiz eine Schuldenliste). Die 51 Grundlinien-Eintraege, die
eine Namensheuristik als Feld erkennt, stehen als P3-560 — mit dem
Hinweis, dass dieselbe Heuristik #15 falsch einstufte.

Eigentuemer-Entscheidung 2026-09-26: „Regel reparieren + #15 verwerfen".

events.title: The display's rate read at start-up, not assumed to be 50
events.message:
The display's rate read at start-up, not assumed to be 50

stdl_vbl_hz started at 50 and only STDL_SetRefresh changed it, so a
machine that boots at 60Hz - an NTSC ST, or one switched before the
program ran - replayed every VBL-counted sequencer (STDL_Music, the
voice tick, STDL_Sfx steps) 20% fast, and STDL_SetRefresh(-1)
reported 50. STDL_SetVideoMode and the shutdown path now take the
rate from bit 1 of $FFFF820A, which is what TOS set for the
machine's region, as stdl_video.h always said. TT and Falcon video
does not run from that register; they keep 50.

tests/host/test_refresh.c checks both register settings and the TT
case. On target, a probe that switched the display to 60Hz before
opening STDL now reads 60, and measured 30 VBLs in half a second.

project.display_title: STM32 USB Floppy Tracer — Amiga/Atari physical disk imaging
project.notes: STM32F407 firmware plus Rust host CLI/GUI reads ADF and ST and writes ADF, IPF, ST and experimental patched STX. events.title: feat(app): accept a fractional Glk host cell size, rounded per window (SQ-1603)
events.message:
feat(app): accept a fractional Glk host cell size, rounded per window (SQ-1603)

TerminalFacts::glk_cell_px / AppState::glk_cell_px / AppGlk::char_px are
now (f64, f64) instead of (u32, u32), so a host with a genuinely
fractional text cell (e.g. 10.2x22.95 device pixels) no longer has to
round before calling into lanthorn at all. canvas_size rounds each open
graphics window's own `cells x char_px` independently, at the
multiplication, rather than sharing one pre-rounded ratio across every
window — closing the cumulative drift a single rounded ratio produces
across windows of different cell counts.

GlkBackend::char_pixels() (the gvm trait boundary a game's own bytecode
observes via glk_window_get_size) stays integer and rounds once, since
gvm's own layout math is unaffected and out of scope here — only AppGlk's
own storage and canvas_size's multiply gained precision.

Threading char_px as f64 through GlulxSession's constructors touched
every call site across crates/app/src and crates/app/tests that passed a
literal cell-size tuple; each was converted mechanically (parsed by call
site, not by blind regex) and re-verified against cargo check.

New discriminating test (sq1598_glk_cell_px.rs) proves per-window
rounding against real Kerkerkruip graphics windows of different cell
counts at char_px = (10.2, 22.95), where global-ratio rounding and
per-window rounding disagree by a different amount on each window
(11px/9px/3px) — falsified by temporarily routing canvas_size through a
single pre-rounded ratio and confirming the new test fails.

events.title: c64os-llvm: UNO for C64 OS in C, built by llvm-mos
events.message:
c64os-llvm: UNO for C64 OS in C, built by llvm-mos

The same kind of windowed C64 OS application as c64os/, but the game
rules are the shared cards.c/game.c/ai.c -- byte-identical to every other
C port, and now enforced for this one by `make check` -- instead of a
hand port to assembly. C64 OS has no C toolchain, but an application is
only a $0900 PRG with five vectors and a KERNAL link table, and llvm-mos
links one. src/app.s supplies that contract and the OS<->C trampolines.

What C64 OS asks of compiled C, each found as a failure first:

- Zero page. C64 OS's own map (//os/docs/memory.t) gives $02-$21 to its
  timers, exception handler and screen layers, and its IRQ decrements $02
  and $09 while C runs -- which moved the soft stack pointer and scattered
  stray bytes through the program (jams at $2020, $2461; a half-cleared
  screen). The imaginary registers now sit at $4E-$6D, BASIC's float
  accumulators, and a crawl of every instruction reachable from C64 OS's
  IRQ and NMI vectors, in a RAM snapshot of the running system, touches
  none of it. The registers are still swapped at every OS/C crossing.
- Everything inside the loaded file: C64 OS allocates only the pages the
  file covers, so .bss and the soft stack are in it (512 bytes reserved,
  34 measured after several rounds).
- The draw callback runs with I/O out ($01=$34), so $D800 is C64 OS's
  colour buffer; key and menu handlers run with it in ($36).
- The buffers are not the screen: the VIC shows $DC00, and C64 OS copies
  its buffers there at the end of each event. A chain of CPU turns runs
  inside one key event, so os_present does that copy itself and each move
  is seen as it is made. (redraw_ would re-enter C from inside C, which
  llvm-mos's static stack frames do not allow for.)
- volatile. src/sid.c is the bare C64 port's SID effects, which cc65
  builds without volatile registers; compiled unmodified by llvm-mos,
  sfx_draw's raster wait became `jmp .`.

The installer (make install) copies the bundle onto a copy of the user's
C64 OS disk and compares every byte against the build: an interrupted
install leaves a zero-block unclosed main.o, and C64 OS's response is to
reload the File Manager silently, indistinguishable from a crash.

Played in VICE (x64sc, CMD HD, JiffyDOS, REU): several full rounds, sound,
CPU turns one at a time, Game > New Game and Game > Quit. main.o is
13,091 bytes, reproducible byte for byte, and identical to the binary
that was played. Not yet exercised: a hand past 20 cards, and the empty
draw pile.

The Wild Draw Four prompt here challenges on [yes]; c64os/'s passes
challenge_sel (0 for [yes]) straight to resolve_wd4, where 0 declines.
c64os/ is left untouched.

events.title: fix(gfx): scale full-window nominal crop insets to the actual frame size (#2362)
events.message:
fix(gfx): scale full-window nominal crop insets to the actual frame size (#2362)

WinUAE applies the AUTOSCALE_STATIC_NOMINAL full-window insets to a fixed
nominal drawbuffer. Amiberry applies them to the dynamic visible frame
(vb->outwidth/outheight), whose size also grows with doubled modes such as
the AmigaOS DBLPAL/DBLNTSC doublescan screenmodes and changes with overscan
borders. Fixed pixel insets on a doubled frame produced a crop that swallowed
nearly the whole frame while the aspect was forced to 4:3, resulting in a
too-wide, edge-truncated image (issue #2273, regression from 050e21f).

Scale the insets by the ratio between the actual frame and the nominal
PAL/NTSC frame for the current resolution and line mode. Standard PAL hires
double still crops to ~640x528 like WinUAE; doubled frames get doubled
insets so the crop stays on the nominal visible area and preserves 4:3.

events.title: feat(app): let a host state its own Glk cell pixel size (SQ-1598)
events.message:
feat(app): let a host state its own Glk cell pixel size (SQ-1598)

Glk graphics windows were always measured against a hardcoded 8x16 cell
(picker-derived font size, or 8x16 with no picker), so a host whose text
cells are a different size - a proportional-font frontend, or any host
stating its own pixel size directly rather than through the cover-art
image picker - got graphics canvases that didn't match its actual
windows and had to stretch them unevenly to compensate.

- TerminalFacts::glk_cell_px (boot.rs): an explicit (width, height)
  override that wins over the picker/8x16 cascade, carried onto
  AppState::glk_cell_px so an @restart (reset.rs) agrees with the
  launch instead of reverting to the fallback.
- AppGlk::set_char_px / GlulxSession::set_char_px (glk_backend.rs,
  glulx_session.rs): makes the backend's char_px mutable after
  construction and relayouts through the same Machine::rearrange()
  path resize/set_borderless already use, so open graphics canvases
  resize live and the game gets its usual Arrange event.
- host::screen::set_glk_cell_px: the resize-time entry point, sibling
  to resize_glulx/set_story_pane.

New suite crates/app/tests/suites/sq1598_glk_cell_px.rs verifies, against
a real Kerkerkruip boot, that graphics canvases scale with the host's
declared cell size (not 8x16), that a live cell-size change resizes an
already-booted game's canvases, and that @restart preserves the host's
choice. All three mechanisms were falsified (temporarily disabled,
confirmed the targeted assertion fails, then restored) before landing.

events.title: fix(combat,waf): hit, damage and weapon-buy score match the BASIC (U7a)
events.message:
fix(combat,waf): hit, damage and weapon-buy score match the BASIC (U7a)

The port tests (U7) found three divergences; all now match the source
exactly at every draw, not just in distribution:
- :30247 the craft miss factor is int(rnd*(kr/10+1))=0, i.e.
  rnd*(kr+10) < 10: draw range(kraft+10) and miss below 10. The old
  range(kr//10+1) missed too often (kr=15: 1/2 instead of 1/2.5).
- :30255 y=int(rnd*tg+bt/10)+1 equals (range(10*tg)+bt)//10+1 for
  integer bt, so the carry from bt's last digit survives and the
  source's maximum damage is reachable again.
- :13065/:13072/:13073 change gf without a clamp. ScoreChange gains

events.title: Cutscene shapes as sprites, baked from their polygons
events.message:
Cutscene shapes as sprites, baked from their polygons

A cutscene shape - a character, a head, a machine - is 15-20
overlapping polygons, and drawn that way each of its rows pays the
fill's row set-up once per polygon crossing it, 420-510 cycles before
a pixel is written, plus the overdraw between them. A foreground shape
drawn again at the same x phase is now a sprite: its polygons are
drawn once into a scratch layer in the fill's priority mode, which
marks what they cover, and the result is kept as runs - a covered
group is two moves, a part-covered one a masked write, an empty one
nothing (shpBlit). Level 1's opening draws 211 of its shapes that way
and its polygon draws fall from 3,908 to 1,756.

Bakes are unclipped and keep the exact bounds of what they covered,
so a shape is a sprite in any frame where the clip does not cut it and
polygons in one where it does; bounds with a pixel's margin had turned
away the shapes that reach the clip's edge, which were most of the
work. Sprites are baked through the scene part's locked colours and
kept across a part whose colours come out the same. A shape with a
shadow polygon draws as polygons.

A bake costs more than the draw it replaces, so it waits for a
shape's second sighting, and a bake that would make an on-time frame
late waits for the time the frame would have slept: on a Mega STE,
whose intro runs at 60% of its budget, baking at once had turned on-
time frames late and dropped more of them than without sprites.

Checked by drawing every sprite's shape both ways from the same page
and comparing the band, over the logo, the intro, the level openings
and the credits, on an STE and a Mega STE: no differences in about
3,500 shapes.

Measured, cycle-exact, Top screen, one binary with sprites and
without, every frame drawn:

  STE       intro 27.1s -> 23.2s   level 1 7.6s -> 6.5s (late frames 50 -> 19)
  Mega STE  intro unchanged        level 1 5.0s -> 4.1s

With frame skipping, the default, the STE's intro drops 138 frames
rather than 155 and level 1's opening 15 rather than 21. A Mega STE's
level 1 opening drops 8 rather than 5: its first frame, loading the
scene, runs late, and the frame after it bakes at once.

events.title: Stop every process the broker started when the broker stops
events.message:
Stop every process the broker started when the broker stops

Only emulators were killed on shutdown, pid by pid. Host tools were not
tracked, descendants (Ghidra's JVM) survived even a timeout kill, a crash
respawn or a new acquire could start mid-shutdown, and a SIGKILL of the
broker left everything running.

Every emulator and host tool now starts in its own process group and is
tracked in one registry. Shutdown stops intake and respawns first, then
stops every group, descendants included. A watchdog forked at startup
learns each group over IPC and stops them all when the broker is gone,
which covers SIGKILL. Verified with stub trees and against real x64sc:
200 ms after kill -9 of the broker, the emulator and the watchdog are gone.

events.title: perf(gfx): duty-cycled auto-crop scan with coarse signature trigger; crop UI and IPC improvements (#2361)
events.message:
perf(gfx): duty-cycled auto-crop scan with coarse signature trigger; crop UI and IPC improvements (#2361)

* perf(gfx): duty-cycle the auto-crop content scan behind a coarse signature trigger

The DIW/DDF register window already forms the deterministic crop base, and
the per-frame content scan only ever expands beyond it for pixels outside
the display window (raster/copper border effects). Run that scan on a duty
cycle instead: immediately when the register base or source buffer changes,
when the outside regions change, and every 25th frame otherwise, reusing the
last scan's rect in between.

Between scans the outside regions are sampled on a coarse two-pass grid
(every row at every 32nd column, every column at every 32nd row) and
compared in place against a color-agnostic signature from the last
observation; any sampled change triggers an immediate scan. The comparison
carries no color semantics, so stable sub-threshold specks the last scan
rejected stay silent while new content of any color triggers within one
frame. A trigger-initiated scan that leaves the rect unchanged parks the
trigger for 8 frames so animated outside content cannot force a full scan
every frame, and the periodic scan bounds every other delay.

The grid stride is a measured trade-off: at stride 4 the per-frame
signature check on a small centered crop (large outside regions) cost more
than the full scan it was guarding. Measured on x86-64 over Toki, Fuzzball
and Pinball Illusions WHDLoad runs: per-frame cost drops from ~50 us
(pure-border frames) / ~120-430 us (frames with outside content, full
flood machinery) to 12-27 us plus one amortized scan; crop rects are
identical to the per-frame-scan build, including Toki's bottom HUD drawn
below DIWSTRT (638x432 gameplay crop) and Fuzzball's content extending
110 px beyond its display window (640x516 crop).

* feat(gui): add numeric entry to crop fields, gate offsets on manual crop

The manual-crop H/V offset sliders only affect the manual render path, so
hide them unless Manual Crop is selected. Every crop slider gains a numeric
input box next to it so measured geometry (e.g. 750x494 from #2308) can be
typed exactly, and slider bounds derive from the active surface
(AMIGA_WIDTH_MAX << gfx_resolution x AMIGA_HEIGHT_MAX << gfx_vresolution)
so rendering the Filter panel no longer truncates a valid full-width crop
or a WHDLoad-centered offset above the old fixed limits.

* feat(ipc): expose crop options via SET_CONFIG/GET_CONFIG

Cover gfx_auto_crop, gfx_manual_crop, gfx_manual_crop_width/height,
gfx_horizontal/vertical_offset and gfx_overscanmode so crop behavior can
be scripted and A/B tested over the IPC socket without the GUI. Values are
validated on the parsed long before narrowing: overscan rejects outside
0-8, crop dimensions clamp to the resolution-derived native bounds and
offsets to the native surface, so a headless client cannot push the
Display panel's overscan_items index or the render rects out of range.

* fix(gfx): hold the auto-crop rect through alternating effect frames

Pinball Illusions' intro strobes full-surface raster shots between smaller
intro pictures while the DIW/DDF register window stays constant, so
consecutive scans produce alternating rects and the presentation flickered
between aspects every few frames (master, with its per-frame scan, flapped
every frame).

Two fixes:

- Trigger back-off frames now still present the last scan's rect; they
  previously fell back to the raw register window, which showed through as
  one-frame flickers whenever a trigger scan left the rect unchanged.
- Shrink hysteresis: when a scan result is smaller than the presented rect
  while the register base and surface are unchanged, keep presenting the
  larger rect until the smaller one has persisted for 12 consecutive
  frames. Growth, moved rects and any register-base/surface change still
  apply immediately, and the presented rect is always a superset of the
  freshest scan result, so coverage never narrows below the per-frame-scan
  behavior.

On the 60-63 s intro section this replaces ~15 rapid rect flaps
(754x574/754x340/640x240) with a handful of clean transitions: the strobe
expands to 754x574 instantly, holds it through the alternation, and shrinks
once the intro picture stays stable.

* fix(gfx): re-baseline the outside signature during the scan

The first trigger check after a scan compared against a signature that was
either empty (first activation) or sampled against the pre-scan rect
geometry, so it adopted that frame as the baseline instead of reporting a
difference — new outside content appearing between a scan and the first
check went unnoticed until the periodic scan (up to 24 frames). Capture the
signature against the scan's own frame and the post-scan rect when the scan
completes, so every subsequent check compares against a true baseline.
This also removes the spurious trigger scans the stale geometry caused.

* fix(gfx): detect stale auto-crop rects fast, shorten the shrink hold

After a full-surface effect shot (Pinball Illusions' intro strobes), the
picture that follows is smaller and lives inside the previous scan's rect,
so neither the outside-region signature nor the periodic scan noticed the
rect was oversized for up to 25 frames, and the 12-frame shrink hold then
delayed the correct crop further — short-lived intro pictures never settled
at all and showed mispositioned inside the stale rect.

Two changes:

- Per-frame stale-rect detector: if any one side's 4-pixel perimeter band
  just inside the scan rect is entirely border-colored, the content moved
  inward and a scan runs immediately (~150 stride-16 samples, well under a
  microsecond). Confirm-then-stay-quiet semantics keep benign cases — a
  register window that legitimately includes border, like Toki's black
  bottom HUD panel — at one confirming scan per transition instead of a
  per-frame scan loop.
- Shrink hold 12 -> 6 frames (the libretro path's long-standing value): a
  delayed settle is visible for the whole hold, while a wrong shrink during
  effect strobing is masked by the strobing itself.

On the Pinball Illusions intro this settles each post-strobe picture to its
correct crop within roughly a dozen frames of the picture appearing
(previously 40-70 frames, with short pictures never settling), while the
strobe sections keep the stable held rect.

* fix(gfx): clear the auto-crop trigger back-off on a context change

A surface, resolution or register-base change forces a scan for the new
context but left a back-off armed by the previous context's animated
content, suppressing outside-change checks for up to eight frames after
the mode switch. Clear the back-off whenever the scan context changes: it
only ever described animation in the previous context.

* fix(gfx): bound the band detector reads and track sides independently

Two hardening fixes for the stale-rect detector:

- The 4-pixel perimeter band was not bounded by the rect dimensions, so a
  DIW/DDF window narrower or shorter than four pixels at a surface edge
  made the detector read past the pixel buffer. The band extent is now
  clamped per axis.
- The empty-band confirmation was a single latch over all four sides, so a
  side that legitimately always shows border (a letterboxed edge, a status
  panel) kept it set and masked a later transition on another side; the
  oversized crop was then retained until the periodic scan. The helper now
  reports each side separately and the caller keeps a per-side
  confirmation mask that only re-arms when that side gains content again.

events.message:
fix(decodejob): der Oberflaechen-Scan zaehlt, was das Modell gelesen hat — nicht, was die Geometrie verspricht (P0-17, Tuer Stufe 2, MF-1350)

P0-17: `DecodeJob` meldete bei Flussdateien Sektoren als gut, die niemand
gelesen hatte, und zaehlte bei Sektorabbildern ueber einen flachen
Versatz. Seit MF-1350 oeffnet er ueber `uft_disk_open()` (derselbe Weg
wie der Analysator), speist per `uft_d2_from_disk()` ins Modell und
leitet den Status JE SEKTOR aus `uft_d2_sector_t` ab:

  OK         nur bei BEKANNTER, stimmender Pruefsumme
  CRC_BAD / ID_CRC_BAD, WEAK, DELETED, MISSING
  UNCHECKED  Daten ohne Pruefsummenangabe (IMG, D64, ADF ...) — weder
             gut noch schlecht
  REJECTED   vom Modell abgewiesen — genannt, nicht verschluckt,
             steht NEBEN totalSectors

Spuren ohne Sektor gehen als NO_SECTORS und zaehlen nie gut und nie
schlecht; Fluss ohne Sektorzerlegung endet mit „Lauf beendet — keine
Sektoraussage", ohne Haken im Status-Reiter. `sectorUpdate` traegt den
Kopf; vorher kamen Seite 0 und 1 eines Zylinders als dasselbe Paar an.

Ein UNVOLLSTAENDIGES Modell endet in error() mit „Lesen abgebrochen —
Teilergebnis". Gemessen daran, dass die Bruecke weniger Spuren fragte,
als die Geometrie hat — NICHT am Rueckgabewert von `uft_d2_from_disk()`:
der ist `sectors > 0 || bitstreams > 0` und fuer jede vollstaendig
gelesene Flussdatei false. Die erste Fassung benutzte ihn und liess die
KFX-/SCP-Faelle rot werden; das war der Rotbeweis fuer das Kriterium.

Rotbeweis `tests/test_decode_job_no_fiction.cpp`, 17 Faelle, gegen
Korpus-Abbilder und ein synthetisches Modell (ein abgewiesener Sektor
ist ueber keine Korpusdatei erreichbar). Die eigene Matrix der ersten

die entkamen (u. a. CRC-Fehler als gut
gezaehlt, WEAK/DELETED als gut, Daten-OK ohne `known`, verschwiegene
Teillesung); alle geschlossen. Eigene Probe danach 9 von 9 gefangen

Nebenbefunde aus der Tuer-Stufe 2 (DecodeJob, P0-17), vor dem Eintrag
nachgeprueft; behoben ist keiner.

P2-2 (gelesen): MainWindow::openFile() fragt zuerst
DiskImageValidator::validate() und bricht mit "Unknown format: .xxx" ab,
wenn es ablehnt. Das Pruefor kennt eine feste Endungsliste (adf, scp,
ipf, hfe, raw, img, ima, d64, g64, nib, dsk, do, po, st, msa, ssd, dsd)
und als Rueckfall fuenf Kennungen (SCP, CAPS, HFE, GCR-1541, "DOS").

Explorer, Forensik-Reiter und DecodeJob. Die Absage selbst hat der
Umsetzer an Korpusdateien gemessen; den Weg durch openFile() habe ich
gelesen, nicht an der Oberflaeche geklickt. Klasse MF-636 (gepflegte
Aufzaehlung neben der Registry).

gekennzeichnet): die GCR-Pruefsumme von G64/NIB erreicht das Modell nicht

events.title: fix(imd): jede Sektor-ID war um eins zu hoch — und "data unavailable" kam als guter Sektor heraus (P0-18, MF-1348)
events.message:
fix(imd): jede Sektor-ID war um eins zu hoch — und "data unavailable" kam als guter Sektor heraus (P0-18, MF-1348)

Eigentuemer-Freigabe 2026-09-26: "ja, P0-18 IMD beheben".

Das IMD-Plugin reichte die ECHTEN Sektor-IDs der Nummernkarte an
uft_format_add_sector(), das laut include/uft/uft_format_common.h einen
0-basierten INDEX nimmt und 1 addiert. Jede ID jeder IMD-Datei kam damit
um eins zu hoch heraus. Gemessen an der FREMD erzeugten
tests/corpus_free/hxcfe_pc160.imd: die Datei traegt die Karte 1..8,
gemeldet wurden 2..9 — 0 von 320 IDs richtig. Dazu, im selben Leseweg und
derselben Klasse "ID-Feld falsch gemeldet": die Zylinder- und Kopfkarte
(Bits 0x80/0x40) wurden uebersprungen, die ID nannte die physische Lage
statt des Sektorkopfs. Und ein Sektor mit dtype 0 ("data unavailable")
kam als GUTER Sektor voller 0xE5 heraus (status 0, crc_ok 1).

Warum kein Test es sah, obwohl imd auf T1 steht: die IMD-Tests finden
Sektoren ueber ein Kennbyte im INHALT, und MF-1068 hat an zwei echten
Aufnahmen die ZAHL der Sektoren abgeglichen (26 + 76 x 8 = 634), nie
ihre IDs.

Referenz (im Dateikopf): MAME src/lib/formats/imd_dsk.cpp,
imd_format::load() — sects[i].sector = snum[i]; track/head aus tnum/hnum,
wenn die Karte da ist; stype 0 ohne Daten. Dieselbe Quelle, die
docs/spec_verification.json fuer imd nennt.

Jetzt: uft_format_add_sector_with_id() mit der ID aus der Karte;
Zylinder und Kopf aus ihren Karten, sonst die Lage; "data unavailable"
behaelt die Fuellung, ist aber mit uft_format_mark_last_missing()
gekennzeichnet (MF-980); die Karten werden nur gelesen, wenn der
Satzkopf in die Datei passt (vorher las der Code die Nummernkarte ohne
diese Pruefung).

Rotbeweis zuerst: tests/test_imd_sektor_ids.c — eigener Zerleger fuer
die fremde Datei (befragt nicht dieselbe Quelle wie der Pruefling),
dazu synthetische Faelle mit IDs 0/0xC1/7/3, dtype 0 und den Karten.
Vorher 6 rot, danach 14 von 14. Mutationsmatrix 6 von 6 — im ersten
Lauf 5 von 6: "Kopfkarte statt Zylinderkarte" entkam, weil mein Fall
immer BEIDE Karten trug; die Einzelfaelle (nur Zylinder-, nur
Kopfkarte) sind ergaenzt. ASan+UBSan+bounds-strict (WSL, gcc 15.2):
test_imd_sektor_ids 14/0, test_imd_error_marks 2/0. Volle Suite im
Hauptbau: 553 von 553 gruen (1 benannter Skip, test_freezer) — keine
andere Stelle im Baum verliess sich auf die falschen IDs.

P0-18 in docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md auf behoben, dabei berichtigt: dort stand
"imd steht auf T1b", richtig ist T1.

NICHT behoben, benannt (im Dateikopf und in P0-18): eine abgeschnittene
Datei verliert ihre letzten Sektoren ohne Kennzeichnung, und ein
Groessencode ueber 6 wird als 512 gelesen (MAME: 8192).

Kennzahl: keine der vier.

events.title: fix(883): nothing ships that nothing can reach
events.message:
fix(883): nothing ships that nothing can reach

Socket's scan of 0.1.2 reported SQL in dist/analysis/regression.js, which
nothing could run. It was the visible end of a shape: two tools absent from
DEFAULT_TOOLS whose handlers returned a sentence pointing at an unshipped
script, in front of an entry that always throws — and package.json allowlisted
dist/ wholesale, so it shipped.

An audit found the shape throughout:
- The TypeScript trace stack (query-events, taint, follow-path, loader-profile,
  trace-events, trace/store/*) shipped long after the daemon took its job. Its
  smokes were green, testing implementations no tool used.
- runtime_bookmark_add/_list failed on every store the live system writes
  ("Table with name trace_bookmarks does not exist"); their one green test
  used the dead store as its fixture. Deleting them orphaned the TS indexer
  chain, which trace-store.ts already said had moved to the daemon (802).
- ws-handlers and ingress-request served the deleted ws-server; a barrel
  nobody imported; four dead pipeline modules; buildD64FromGCR, writeback for
  the deleted TS 1541.
- Visible tools named tools that do not exist (runtime_session_undump,
  snapshot_dump) or that a session cannot see — ten redirects, including the
  steering project_init seeds and the snippet c64re setup writes.
- Hints that assume a checkout, in text a package user reads.

The rule: a module ships only if an entry a user can start reaches it.
check:dist-reachable walks the BUILT dist/ — where `import type` is erased,
which is how the trace stack looked alive — from the bin, the workbench and the
pipeline child; it fails on a shipped orphan and on a stale !dist/ exclusion,
both proved red before it went in. npm run build clears dist/ first: tsc never
deletes an output, so a deleted source's .js kept shipping from any machine
that was not a fresh clone.

Reduced to their types: flow-focus, trace-definition, asset-join-knowledge.
Excluded from the tarball by name: build-time platform-kb and fingerprint
extractor, the disk fixture builders, three modules the UI bundle compiles.

Fixing one hint exposed one that could not be followed: c64ref_lookup's
auto_build acted only on a missing file while its own note told a ROM-only
snapshot to rebuild. It rebuilds that too now — proved on a trimmed copy of
the real snapshot, the original restored byte-identical.

Also: smoke:input asserted the pre-BUG-026 mapping (Escape → RUN_STOP); it
now checks Escape → ← and Tab → RUN_STOP, 11/11. Spec 882 opened for the
backwards Exomizer depack the server can pack but not unpack; Spec 884 for
ring marks in C64RE, which found that TRX64's sandbox/run restores and pauses
the LIVE machine.

Removes four tools from the advanced tier, so this is a minor release.

Gates: full gate 84/84, check:dist-reachable 303/321 reached, 10 excluded.

events.title: Cutscene polygons replayed from a cache, and STDL v1.13.0
events.message:
Cutscene polygons replayed from a cache, and STDL v1.13.0

A cutscene redraws the same polygons frame after frame at new
positions: 87% of what the intro and level 1's opening draw had been
drawn earlier in the same scene, 93% through the intro's camera
moves. For a whole-pixel move the edge walk is the same one, shifted,
so the first draw now records the walk - relative to the shape's
origin and unclipped, as the segments the fill cores take (edge
positions and steps, row counts) - and every later draw hands those
straight to the fill. The vertex parse, the setup and the edge chains
are skipped. A hit's lookup, clipping and colour setup are in
assembly (segHit): the same work in C cost nearly as much as the walk
it replaced, and a first version written that way saved only 10%.

The recording is made by the existing walker in a record mode
(rs4_run), so the pixels are the same ones. Checked by drawing every
cached polygon both ways from the same page and comparing, over the
logo, the intro, the level openings and the credits: no differences
in about 60,000 draws. The cache is a 32K arena per played scene,
emptied when full, keyed by the primitive's vertex data; a shape's
changed box is applied once, not per polygon. The scene's log line
now says how many polygons came from the cache.

Measured in Hatari, cycle-exact, Top screen, one binary with the
cache off and on; work with every frame drawn:

  intro      ST 34.5s -> 26.1s  STE 34.7s -> 26.4s  Mega STE 20.8s -> 15.8s
             (budget 27.2s)
  level 1    ST  9.4s ->  7.5s  STE  9.6s ->  7.5s  Mega STE  5.8s ->  4.5s
             (budget 4.8s)

With frame skipping, the default, the intro drops 141 frames rather
than 205 on an STE and 29 rather than 79 on a Mega STE, and level
1's opening on a Mega STE now runs inside its budget. A 2.5MB STE
with the modules plays that scene from the cache and on into the
level.

STDL v1.13.0 moves its SDL_mixer layer onto the voice mixer and makes
the ring device cheaper, neither of which the port uses; splitting
the sound DMA code into separate objects makes FLASHBAK.TOS 3.1KB
smaller.

events.title: fix(diag): der Oberflaechen-Scan sagt ab statt hinter sector_status[36] zu schreiben, fragt nach den Nummern der Diskette — und bekommt einen Leseweg ueber den Greaseweazle (Tuerstufe 4, MF-1346)
events.message:
fix(diag): der Oberflaechen-Scan sagt ab statt hinter sector_status[36] zu schreiben, fragt nach den Nummern der Diskette — und bekommt einen Leseweg ueber den Greaseweazle (Tuerstufe 4, MF-1346)

Stufe 4 der vom Eigentuemer am 2026-09-26 freigegebenen Tuer fuer den
Oberflaechen-Scan (Folge von H-18). Umgesetzt in einem isolierten
Worktree, von einem Gegenpruefer zweimal geprueft (Runde 1 "nachbessern",
Runde 2 "annehmen"), vor diesem Commit SELBST nachgebaut und gemessen.

Teil A — Grenzen. uft_diag_init und uft_diag_surface_scan prueften
nichts. Gemessen gegen den Vorzustand:
  sectors = 37          UBSan (bounds-strict) "index 36 out of bounds for
                        type 'uint8_t [36]'" — reines ASan/UBSan schweigt
                        (Index 36 liegt in der Polsterung des letzten
                        Mitglieds; P3-550)
  sectors 64 nach init  ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE, nativ 0xC0000374
  sectors = 0           UBSan "division by zero", nativ 0xC0000094
  retries = 0           18 BAD bei 0 Lesungen
  tracks 85 / sides 3   angenommen (MAX_TRACKS 84 stand da, unbenutzt)
Seither: tracks 1..84, sides 1..2, sectors 1..36, sector_size >= 1,
retries >= 1, sonst -1 vor dem ersten Lesen; der Scan prueft tracks x
sides zusaetzlich gegen die in init angelegte Zahl, und die Grenze ist
EXAKT abgenommen (angelegt + 1 sagt ab, genau angelegt wird gelesen).

Teil A — Nummern. Der Scan fragte fest 1..n; eine CPC-Datendiskette
(0xC1..0xC9) war damit 72 von 72 BAD. An uft_diag_config_t angehaengt:
sector_ids[36] + sector_id_count (0 = altes Verhalten).

Teil B — Leseweg. src/diag/uft_diag_gw.c: ein uft_diag_read_fn ueber
uft_gw_read_track -> flux_decode_track -> Suche nach Nummer, C/H, beiden
CRCs und exakter Groesse. Jede Wiederholung ist eine NEUE Erfassung, nie
der Zwischenspeicher. Kein Schreibparameter, kein uft_gw_write*/erase*.
Den Takt fragt der Adapter per GET_INFO, weil uft_gw_open_stream()
dev->info nie fuellt (P3-551, geschuetzte Datei unveraendert).
Drahtbruecke des Emulators (MF-848): READ_FLUX stroemt, Write/Erase
werden gezaehlt, /TRK0 folgt dem Zylinder auf Wunsch (Vorgabe aus).

ABI, bewusst und im Kopf benannt: uft_diag_config_t 24 -> 64 Byte, alte
Versaetze unveraendert; uft_diag_ctx_t 88 -> 136 (die 40 der Konfiguration
plus das neue 8-Byte-Feld track_results_count), weil ctx config als Wert
einbettet. Uebersetzte Nutzer ausserhalb src/diag, include/uft/diag und
tests: 0. Im Adapterkopf: bei revolutions > 1 gewinnt die erste gute
Kopie (GOOD statt WEAK); kein Doppelschritt (fuer t > 0 BAD, Spur 0 GOOD).

Selbst nachgemessen im Hauptbau: ctest diag/entscheidet/gw_ 14 von 14
(einschliesslich der sechs Greaseweazle-Emulator-Tests, deren Bruecke
der Patch erweitert). Eigene Stichprobe der beiden Mutanten, die Runde 1
entkamen: ID-CRC-Pruefung gestrichen -> test_diag_gw_emulator 25 gruen /
4 rot; Anlage um eins zu gross -> test_diag_grenzen Absturz 0xC0000374;
Grundfassung danach wieder 29/0 und 24/0. Umsetzer und Gegenpruefer:
ASan+UBSan+bounds-strict (WSL, gcc 15.2) 7/7 ohne Befund; Mutationsmatrix
Teil A 14/14, Teil B 13/15 (entkommen und benannt ungetestet: FM-Weg,
Aufsummieren der Indexzeiten).

NICHT gemacht, benannt: eine Tuer im Produkt (Scan und Adapter haben 0
produktive Aufrufer; die Oberflaeche wartet auf Phase 6 des
GUI-Plans), FM-Weg, Zonenformate (eine Nummernliste fuer alle Spuren),
das doppelte free in greaseweazle_backend.c (P3-547).

fix(716): drop the one module only scripts/ can call, and say what a checkout has to build

Two things a published tarball showed.

dist/analysis/regression.js shipped in 0.2.0 and cannot run from an install: its
only callers are scripts/regress-cli.mjs and scripts/smoke-regression.mjs, and
scripts/ is not in the package. Nothing under src/ imports it, static or dynamic;
the two MCP tools named after it are stubs whose text points at that same
unshipped script. Socket duly read it as live code and reported SQL findings in
it. Excluded from files, and e2e:716-package now asserts its absence, because

build". Only the first does. ui/dist/ is gitignored, so a fresh clone has no
bundle until npm run ui:build, and npm run workspace runs build:mcp — a full tsc
— on every start. INSTALL.md already said this correctly; the README did not.

launcher: warn that HD floppies do not work in the emulated drives

Storage -> Create Image offers HD (1.76M) floppies, which the emulated
double-density drives cannot read in either container. The images are
still worth making -- the workshop writes disks for other emulators and
real Amigas too -- so the option stays, and the Create Floppy page now
shows a warning under its rows while HD is picked, in the style of the
Networking page's determinism warning. The Density value box has no room
for a caveat in the label itself.

A launcher test writes each density in each container through the page
and checks the warning appears exactly when the drives refuse the image,
so it fails if a high-density drive model is ever added. The UI preview
test renders the HD variant of the page.

events.title: libretro: accept only the double-density ADF size
events.message:
libretro: accept only the double-density ADF size

The core's ADF check accepted 1,802,240-byte HD images and its error
claimed 1760 KiB support, but the machine's DD drives then refused
them. The check now accepts only the core's own ADF_SIZE and says so,
and the libretro guide no longer lists 1760 KiB ADFs as supported.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: floppy: refuse high-density tracks in UAE extended ADFs
events.message:
floppy: refuse high-density tracks in UAE extended ADFs

Every emulated drive is a double-density unit: it answers the drive-ID
poll as DD and turns at the DD rate, so at most 11 AmigaDOS sectors pass
under the head per revolution. A plain 1,802,240-byte HD ADF, an HD DMS
archive and an IPF recorded at the HD cell rate were already refused,
but the UAE-1ADF and legacy UAE--ADF decoders took a type-0 (sync 0)
AmigaDOS track of 22 sectors without a density check. The track was
then encoded into one DD revolution, a track no DD drive can read: a
bootable OFS HD disk in the extended container ended Kickstart 1.3's
boot in Guru Meditation #30010000, while the same disk at DD density
reached the CLI.

Both decoders now refuse an AmigaDOS track carrying more sectors than a
DD track holds, naming high density as the DMS and IPF paths do. Raw MFM
tracks carry their own timing and are left alone, as are the all-zero
raw-length blank tracks exporters pad extra cylinders with. The
configuration guide lists the high-density images that are refused.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: fix: no hand-written SQL literals in the two stores that still had them
events.message:
fix: no hand-written SQL literals in the two stores that still had them

Socket's scanner flagged @trex64/c64re 0.1.2 with five "AI-detected code
anomaly" instances. Three do not hold against the code — id-path's baseRelative
is a constant at both call sites, effective-segments needs a segment end of 9e15
in the project's own analysis JSON, and service.ts's shell:true is a build step
the project owner typed. Two do.

trace-run-store.writeTraceRunHeader interpolated overheadMs raw while every
neighbouring value in the same INSERT went through num(). num() itself used
Math.trunc, which turns NaN into the bare word NaN and the statement into a
syntax error — verified against DuckDB: "Binder Error: Referenced column NaN was
not found". Both helpers now return NULL for a non-finite number, and overheadMs
takes a real() that keeps its fraction instead of a num() that would truncate it.

analysis/regression wrote payloadHash unquoted between a family that was escaped
and a cycle that was not. That is the shape this defect always has: not the value
nobody considered, but the one neighbour in a row of identical-looking ones. The
file now has the same two helpers and no hand-written literal anywhere — the
read paths were already correct and were converted too, because one literal left
by hand is how the next one gets missed.

Reachability, stated rather than implied: insertBaselineRun sits behind
runScenarioById, which always throws (scenario execution needs the runtime's
scenario_run). So the regression half is hardening of code that cannot currently
run, and no test covers it. The trace-store half is live and is proved: NaN lands
as NULL, 12.5 stays 12.5, and a quote in a name round-trips.

Gates: e2e:834-trace-store 93/0, smoke:regression 6/0, tsc clean.

events.title: docs: describe the Flatpak as build-it-yourself, not a Flathub install
events.message:
docs: describe the Flatpak as build-it-yourself, not a Flathub install

The README and Getting started told Linux users to run
`flatpak install flathub dev.copperline.Copperline`, but Copperline is
not on Flathub: the submission (flathub/flathub#9401) closed unmerged,
the AppStream API returns 404, and releases attach no .flatpak bundle.

- getting-started.md: AppImage is listed first as the Linux download.
  The Flatpak section becomes "build it yourself" from
  packaging/flatpak, with prerequisites, the build commands and the
  clean-checkout caveat. The lavapipe note, the command-line tools
  table and the VS Code chapter now refer to a self-built Flatpak.
- README.md: the Linux section is AppImage only, with a pointer to the
  Flatpak build instructions.
- packaging/flatpak: the local build recipe ran
  `flatpak run org.flatpak.Builder` without installing it and assumed
  a flathub remote. It now adds a user flathub remote and installs
  org.flatpak.Builder, as Flathub's own docs do;
  --install-deps-from=flathub already fetches the runtime, SDK and Rust
  extension. The README notes the Flathub status.

docs(open-items): das IMD-Plugin meldet jede Sektor-ID um eins zu hoch — und fuenf weitere Nebenbefunde der Tuer-Arbeit (P0-18, P3-547..551, MF-1344)

Die Umsetzer und Gegenpruefer der Tuer-Stufen fuer den Oberflaechen-Scan
(Folge von H-18) haben unterwegs Befunde ausserhalb ihres Auftrags
gemeldet. Jeder ist hier SELBST nachgeprueft, bevor er eingetragen wird;
behoben ist keiner — dafuer fehlt die Freigabe.

P0-18 (gemessen): das IMD-Plugin (T1b) reicht die ECHTEN Sektor-IDs der
Nummernkarte an uft_format_add_sector(), das einen 0-basierten Index
erwartet und 1 addiert. An der fremd erzeugten
tests/corpus_free/hxcfe_pc160.imd traegt die Datei die Karte 1..8, das
Plugin meldet 2..9. Und ein Sektor mit dtype 0 ("data unavailable") kommt
als GUTER Sektor voller 0xE5 heraus (status 0, crc_ok 1) — erfundene
Daten. Die IMD-Tests finden Sektoren ueber ein Kennbyte im Inhalt, nie

events.message:
feat(881): the graph before the listing — a door and a measure

The server's own instructions say the graph tools ARE the static analysis,
indexed, and that they come before opening a full listing. Nothing enforced it
and nothing measured it. Across the supervised runs of 2026-09-24/25 there were
103 reads of the rendered listing against 5 disasm calls, spread 25/19/17/16/14/12
over six participants.

D1, a door: read_artifact refuses a listing at >= 1500 lines until one of
graph_find / graph_node / graph_edges / graph_path / graph_overview was called
this session. Session, not process: the ledger is a file under knowledge/,
re-armed by agent_onboard the way 877 D4 re-arms the alias notices. The refusal
names the file, its size and the calls that open it, and does not come back for
that file.

D2, a measure: the ratio rides the contract footer, reports and never refuses,
and speaks only on a delta — run 7 of the unattended series moved model_assert
0 -> 12 by carrying its blockers back as a delta where run 6, without it, moved
nothing. It counts tool reads and says so; the 103 were shell reads an MCP
server cannot see.

The counter went into withGraph first and e2e:823 refused it — that spec draws
an import boundary around graph-tools.ts. The server's footer wrapper already
sees every tool by name and is the better home.

Also: the gate note now records the state captured at the START of the run, not
at the end, so an edit while the gate runs can no longer leave a note claiming a
tree the gate never saw.

events.title: fix(716): the workbench starts from the package, and the gate proves it starts
events.message:
fix(716): the workbench starts from the package, and the gate proves it starts

0.1.1 shipped a workbench that could not be started. The launchers project_init
writes ran `npm run workspace`, which is `tsc -p tsconfig.json && node
scripts/workspace.mjs`; an installed package has no tsconfig, no scripts/ and no
TypeScript, and `scripts/` is not in the tarball. Reported by a reader of the
published package. Every gate here was green.

The orchestration moved from scripts/workspace.mjs into
src/workspace-ui/launch.ts, so it compiles into dist/ and ships. Two doors reach
one implementation: scripts/workspace.mjs for a checkout, `c64re ui` for an
install. The package root is computed from the module, not from a caller's cwd
or a baked path.

The launchers now branch on what they were written beside. In a package they
invoke `c64re` if it is on PATH and `npx -y @trex64/c64re` otherwise, with no
build step and — the third defect reported — nothing baked: under npx the
package sits in a cache directory that changes every version and can be evicted,
so a path written into a project's launcher goes stale silently. The name is
stable; the path is not. build-ui says there is nothing to rebuild.

Also corrects `--help`: `setup` writes the process-discipline block into an agent
config (Spec 044), not "an MCP host configuration". Written two hours ago without
opening the file it describes.

THE RULE, recorded in the spec as §6a: every shipped component gets an acceptance
criterion that says it STARTS, not that it is PRESENT.

An earlier draft of this spec asked whether the UI belonged in the package. The
rewrite deleted that question and answered it silently. When that was corrected,
ui/dist went in and the gate learned to check the files were there — and §7 was
not extended, so nothing asked what starts it. Presence is not function, which is
this spec's own founding argument, missed one layer up.

The gate now starts the workbench from the installed package and fetches its
page: 705 bytes of the built bundle. It also asserts the launchers carry no
`npm run workspace` and no absolute path into the package.

40 pass, 0 fail. Version 0.1.2.

feat(tor71): Sperre 1 aus MF-1096 bekommt ein Werkzeug — und der Mechanismus war nie das Heredoc (MF-1343)

CLAUDE.md, "drei Sperren", Regel 1: mehrzeilige Dateiaenderungen ueber
Edit/Write, nie ueber Heredoc. Fuer die Sperren 2 und 3 baute MF-1096
Werkzeuge, fuer Sperre 1 nur Text. Gemessen ueber ALLE 624
Protokolldateien des Projekts (Hauptsitzungen, subagents/, workflows/):
43 670 Bash-Aufrufe, 4 157 verstossen gegen die Regel, 919 davon seit
MF-1096 — und am 2026-09-26 war der Schaden wieder derselbe.

Der Mechanismus, selbst gemessen: das Bash-Werkzeug halbiert jedes
doppelte Backslash-Paar, BEVOR bash es sieht — auch in einfachen
Anfuehrungszeichen, auch ohne Heredoc. `printf '%s' 'x<2 BS>y' | wc -c`
ergibt 3, dieselbe Zeichenkette in PowerShell hat Laenge 4; ein
einzelnes Backslash-n bleibt erhalten. Das Heredoc ist das Fahrzeug.

scripts/audit_heredoc.py — EIN Klassifizierer, drei Betriebsarten:
* --haken: PreToolUse-Haken, weist mit exit 2 ab. Registriert auf
  User-Ebene (~/.claude/settings.json, absoluter Python-Pfad; nicht im
  Repo, weil .claude/settings.json ungetrackt ist und fremde Eintraege
  traegt) — Eigentuemerentscheidung 2026-09-26, strenge Fassung:
  abgewiesen wird jedes doppelte Backslash-Paar im Bash-Befehl, jedes
  Heredoc, das eine Datei fuellt, und jedes mehrzeilige Skript per
  Heredoc; Commit-/PR-Nachrichten bleiben erlaubt. Ein Absturz mit `<<`
  oder Doppel-Backslash in der Eingabe weist ab statt durchzulassen.
  Einspeiseprobe live in dieser Sitzung: ein `cat > probe <<EOF` wurde
  abgewiesen (die Datei existiert nicht), und ein Doppel-Backslash
  ebenso — der Haken sieht den Befehl also VOR der Halbierung.
  Einbau 2026-09-26T09:05:19Z.
* --protokolle: Messgeraet, nur Bericht, ueber alle Protokollebenen;
  meldet immer auch "gesehen", damit "0 Abweisungen" bei "0 gesehen"
  nichts behauptet (Klasse Tor 64 / MF-1000).
* check(repo): Tor 71 in check_consistency.py — der Klassifizierer an
  seinen 29 Faellen (24 Befehle, 5 Hakenfaelle inkl. kaputtem JSON,
  Umlaut, fremdem Werkzeug). Das ist der Teil, den das CI sehen kann.

Mutationsmatrix gegen die Faelle: zuerst 6 von 11 gefangen — fuenf
Durchrutscher waren Luecken in MEINEN Faellen (jeder betroffene Fall war
auch ohne die gepruefte Regel schon rot). Geschaerft, und der neue Fall
"cat <<EOF | python > out" fand dabei einen echten Fehler: die Umleitung
zaehlte vor der Pipe, der Inhalt ging aber an Python, nicht in die
Datei. Danach 11 von 11 auf gruener Grundfassung.

Benannte Grenzen: ob der Haken auch in Workflow-Unteragenten feuert, ist
beim Einbau nicht gemessen (--protokolle zeigt es); PowerShell sieht er
nicht; ein fehlender Interpreter oeffnet (die Hook-Doku kennt nur exit 2
als blockierend). Meta-Tor: 70 Tore, 47 ohne eigenen Pruefstandsfall —
Tor 71 prueft sich ueber seinen eigenen Selbsttest.

CLAUDE.md Regel 1 um den Nachtrag erweitert (nicht umgeschrieben).

events.title: docs(solutions): relational learning is 'minus-one'; drop the :30240 proof
events.message:
docs(solutions): relational learning is 'minus-one'; drop the :30240 proof

The doc's filename said 'is-plus-one', the opposite of its rule; it is
now basic-relational-boolean-is-minus-one-when-porting.md and live
references follow (historical plans keep the old path). Its fourth
'proof', :30240 fori=1to1-2*(w=4), does not decide anything: a C64 FOR
loop runs its body once even with bound -1, and w=4 is the throwing
stars, not a machine gun. It is now supporting evidence only; the three

events.title: SDL_mixer chunks on the voice mixer, and a ring device that costs 2%
events.message:
SDL_mixer chunks on the voice mixer, and a ring device that costs 2%

The ring device's refill stepped its source with
`while (acc >= frames) { acc -= frames; f += frame_bytes; }`, and
gcc 4.6 folded that into a closed form with a __mulsi3 call on every
output frame: 37% of an 8MHz STE with a callback that did nothing,
73% at 12517Hz. The converter (stdl_audio_convert, now in src/wav.c
with the WAV loader) steps a byte pointer and a 16-bit fraction, set
up with divu.w and mulu.w, one loop per layout. A callback in the
hardware's format - signed 8-bit at a DMA rate - now writes straight
into the ring. An empty callback costs 2% at either rate; converted,
13% for unsigned 8-bit mono at 12517 and 48% for 16-bit stereo at
22050, which plays at 25033 in stereo.

The SDL_mixer compatibility layer's chunks play on STDL_Voice, mixed
from the VBL, instead of in C over the ring device. On an 8MHz STE
one to four chunks at 6258Hz take 9/15/20/26%, where they took
58/83/99% and four overloaded it; at 12517, 18/29/40/51%, all of
which overloaded it before. A Mega STE takes about half. For ports:
- Mix_OpenAudio mixes at 6258 or 12517, whichever is nearer the rate
  asked for; a PC game's 22050 gets 12517.
- A chunk at full volume plays at half scale, the voice mixer's room
  for two loud sounds: 6dB quieter than before, so balances held
  against the music want re-checking.
- Chunks are converted to the device rate as they load, at most
  65535 frames (about five seconds at 12517); a longer WAV is cut.
- Mix_PlayChannel's loop count is exact, counted by the voice mixer
  through an internal stdl_voice_start; Mix_Playing reads the voice.

audio.c is split three ways: the DMA primitives and STDL_PlaySample
stay, the ring device moves to src/ring.c and the WAV code to
src/wav.c, so a program that plays only voices or one-shots links
neither. An example using voices alone is 12.5KB smaller.

Tests: tests/host/test_wav.c (each format, stereo kept and mixed,
rates up and down, a long source), test_mixer.c (the layer through
its own API), test_ring.c (the direct and converted refills, pumped
by hand) and a loop-count case in test_voice.c; the sound tests share
their fake-DMA helpers in ymtest.h. tests/hatari/mixbench.c measures
the ring device and the chunks. On target, voicechk.c still matches
the C twin at the same speed, loopwave's same-rate and resampled
stereo recordings match v1.12.0's, and examples/playmus.c plays every
other beep three times with a loop count. AGENTS.md records the
multiply no loop asked for; the headers, limits, porting guide, skill
and README carry the new figures.

events.title: fix(store): retry the store rename when Windows refuses it
events.message:
fix(store): retry the store rename when Windows refuses it

writeJsonStoreAtomic renamed its staging file over the store exactly once.
On Windows that rename fails with EPERM / EACCES / EBUSY while any other
process holds the destination open - a virus scanner or the search indexer
reading the store it just saw change, or a sync client's file filter
(OneDrive keeps its filter loaded even while sync is paused). Those holders
are not writers and take no lock, so the cross-process lock cannot help.

Seen on a project under OneDrive: 1-4 registrations lost per 40-file
extract_disk, a different file each run, serial and parallel alike:

  EPERM: operation not permitted,
  rename '.../knowledge/artifacts.json.<pid>.<n>.<salt>.tmp' -> '.../knowledge/artifacts.json'

The holder lets go within milliseconds, so the rename is now tried again up
to 10 times with a growing wait (10, 20, 40 ... ms, capped at 200 ms - about
1.3 s overall), the same remedy graceful-fs applies. Any other error, or one
that outlasts the retries, is still thrown. Both copies of the file are
changed identically, so the byte-identity gate still holds.

events.title: Read the reconnect epoch from the broker over the socket, not from a file
events.message:
Read the reconnect epoch from the broker over the socket, not from a file

The grant named a broker-side epoch.json that the MCP server read from its
own disk. Inside a container the file is absent, so every reconnect was
refused as a restart and the stopwatch and video-standard epoch guards
compared null with null. The server now asks the broker's status reply for
the epoch of the instance its grant owns, at handshake and on reconnect,
and the grant no longer carries epoch_file or supervisor_dir.

A respawned emulator is a new pid the grant does not own, so a reconnect
after a crash reports no current epoch and is refused, and the refusal says
why. Verified against stock VICE 3.9: a dropped relay reconnects, a
SIGKILL-respawn is refused.

events.message:
fix(716.2): read the tarball, not npm's stdout

The release run failed at the first gate with the same parse error this gate had
once before: Unexpected token 'P', "Pipeline ...".

`npm pack --json` does not silence the lifecycle scripts it runs, and prepack is
a full build that prints, so the report is never the only thing on stdout. The
first fix sliced for the last JSON array; the release job installs npm@latest,
whose array is formatted differently, and the slice found nothing and parsed the
build output.

Parsing a tool's chatter was the mistake both times. The tarball is the artifact
under test, so the gate now packs without --json, finds the .tgz it produced, and
reads the contents with tar -tzf — one answer, the same on every platform and
every npm.

Nothing was published: the tag check passed, this failed, and every step after it
including Publish was skipped. That is the ordering working as intended.

in one good way. The v0.1.0 tag would have been a no-op — gates run, publish
skipped, version already there. v0.1.1 is a real first automated release that
also fixes a published defect, and nothing is burned if the pipeline is
misconfigured: 0.1.1 simply stays unpublished until it is not.

events.title: fix(879): the gate leaves a note, and the push does not prove it twice
events.message:
fix(879): the gate leaves a note, and the push does not prove it twice

Two problems, one push.

First, every master push ran the full 82 steps even when they had just been run
by hand a minute earlier — twenty minutes spent on ten minutes of answer. The
gate now leaves a note naming the tier it proved and the state it proved it on:
the commit, plus a digest of the working tree's dirty state. When that matches
what is being pushed, the hook says so and skips. An all note satisfies a docs
push; a docs note never satisfies an all one. No expiry, on purpose — the note is
keyed to the code, not the clock, and touching a file moves the digest, which is
exactly when the gate should run again.

Second, and the reason master is still not pushed: git connects to the remote
and fetches the ref list BEFORE it runs pre-push, so the SSH connection sits
open and idle for however long the hook takes. After ten minutes the server
closes it, and git dies of SIGPIPE writing the pack — exit 141, after the hook
has printed "push allowed". It happened at 370s and again at 599s, and never on
a five-second docs push. A repo-local core.sshCommand with ServerAliveInterval
keeps the connection warm; the global ssh config is untouched.

The first fix makes the second rare, but both are real: a gate that has to run
still takes ten minutes, and the connection still has to survive it.

events.title: Start on the title menu, and fixes from a review of the unpushed work
events.message:
Start on the title menu, and fixes from a review of the unpushed work

The title's main page is now START / LOAD GAME / OPTIONS / QUIT. Start
opens the level list, on the level last played - the Jungle when the
game has just started, so Start and fire begin a new game - with Back
(or Escape) to return, as Options does. Frees seven lines of the main
page. START, QUIT and LOAD GAME come from the game's menu dictionary in
the data's language; OPTIONS is in capitals to match, as no DOS menu
had one to translate. The longest, Italian's CARICA IL GIOCO with a
save point, ends at x=299.

A /simplify and /code-review pass over everything not yet pushed found
these, all fixed and re-tested in Hatari:

- Action music on an STE never started when the idle pause had
  stopped the voice device: its first note comes from its own tick,
  which a paused device does not run. Installing a tick now resumes
  it (ST_setVoiceTick), for every sequencer. In r19.
- The title's module took the voice tick from action music still
  playing (after Abort from the in-game menu, say), leaving it marked
  playing and every later action cue ignored. Cutscene and title
  music now stop it first.
- Load on the title drew level 2's rooms from the wrong half of the
  level when the save was made in the second half: the half only
  switches on passing a transition room. A room with no data in the
  loaded half (it ends where the room before it ends) now loads the
  other; checked against both files for every room.
- Module notes started past a loop's end by a 9xx sample offset
  (OPTIONS1, TELEPORA) were silenced; they wrap into the loop as the
  software mixer's position does, and a start inside a loop plays the
  whole loop rather than a shorter one at another pitch.
- A module now loads only with 128K to spare beyond it, else the YM
  stream plays: it is 10-30 times the stream's size and loads before
  the cutscene's own data.
- A module note due while an effect held voice 3 replayed off the
  beat when the effect ended; it is dropped instead. A module that
  cannot be found no longer leaves the previous one playing.
- Distant YM effects were copied per play into a ring that could be
  rewritten while STDL read it. Each recipe is now built at every
  distance up front, at level load and only on machines that play
  YM effects (the build is about a frame of an 8MHz ST).
- The Music line said YM with no YM tracks installed; the newest save
  could fall off a Load list of more than 64.

Simplifications: the track-name step and the Paula loop rules shared
between the two music players (mixer.cpp); the music kind worked out
in one place; the Load line one of the menu's settings, and one main
page enum for both builds; one voice sync per VBL, divu.w for the
sequencer's pitch changes and no multiply or divide in its volume
table; logging dropped while a sequencer tick runs (a flag set by
ST_setVoiceTick) instead of #ifndef around each warning; the pacing
step a table; the report tool's analysis shared.

Measured after the fixes: the title module's pitch content matches
the previous recording (correlation 1.000) at the same level, and a
plain ST's YM pistol shots and distant beep sound as before.

events.title: merge: Spec 716 — C64RE as an npm package, with the runtime beside it
events.message:
merge: Spec 716 — C64RE as an npm package, with the runtime beside it

The package is @trex64/c64re: packed, installed into an empty directory and
answering MCP on Linux, Windows and WSL2, started three ways — node, npm's own
shim, and npx. 1373 files and 23.2 MB of source tree became 642 files and 1.8 MB
that start; runtime dependencies went 13 to 4.

The runtime is fetched on first use rather than at install time, checksum-verified
against the release, into a per-version cache that the resolution chain now knows
about along with PATH. The pin is cross-checked against the sibling checkout and
the daemon's own protocol string, because two hand-maintained numbers that can
silently disagree only surface on someone else's machine.

Eight defects came out of it, and every one was found by leaving this machine:
c64ref_lookup needed a 27 MB derived file that is in no package and whose builder
fetches from the network; the Node floor turned out to be node:sqlite rather than
a version anyone could name; TRX64 built no Intel Mac while the installer claimed
to serve one; and five POSIX assumptions in the gate itself that only a Windows
runner could see.

Publishing is 716.6 and stays a human act.

events.title: cli: refuse flag combinations a run would silently drop
events.message:
cli: refuse flag combinations a run would silently drop

--benchmark-until, --gdb and --control each take over the run loop
before the App that fires scheduled work is built, so some flags were
accepted and then ignored:

- --control with --expect-screenshot never compared anything.
- --insert-cd-after was dropped by all three modes (only floppy
  inserts were refused).
- --exit-on-return under --gdb or --control never saw the program's
  return code, since neither watches the --run completion marker.

Each combination is now refused with an error naming the flag. Netplay
also refuses --pen-after, as it already did the other scripted pointer
input that only the local machine would see.

A lone --run PROG --exit-on-return now runs windowless and unthrottled,
like a lone --coverage: run_headless already accepted it as a capture
trigger and docs/guide/run.md already described it that way, but the
windowless check never included it, so it opened a window instead. With
--control-gui or --gdb-gui the session stays windowed as before.

events.title: ci(716.6): a version already on the registry is not an error
events.message:
ci(716.6): a version already on the registry is not an error

Two ordinary things land on the publish step with nothing to do: re-running a
release job whose publish already succeeded, and tagging a version that was
published by hand. The second is not an edge case — it is the FIRST release by
necessity, because a trusted publisher is configured on a package and cannot be
configured on one that does not exist yet.

Neither should paint the run red, and neither can be answered by publishing over
something, which npm forbids regardless. The job now asks the registry first and
skips the publish when the version is already there, while still running both
gates — which turns the v0.1.0 tag into a free end-to-end test of the pipeline
rather than a guaranteed failure.

events.title: debugger: decode ADKCON, BPLCON2 and DDF bits at their hardware positions
events.message:
debugger: decode ADKCON, BPLCON2 and DDF bits at their hardware positions

The IO Map and console CUSTOM decode tables had drifted from the chips:

- ADKCON/ADKCONR named WORDSYNC, MSBSYNC and FAST one bit high. Bit 11
  is UARTBRK, 10 WORDSYNC, 9 MSBSYNC, 8 FAST, as Paula and the disk
  controller already use them.
- BPLCON2 put KILLEHB on bit 10, which is ZDCTEN; KILLEHB is bit 9. The
  table now also names ZDBPEN, ZDCTEN, RDRAM and SOGEN, and shows
  ZDBPSEL as a field beside PF1P/PF2P.
- DDFSTRT/DDFSTOP were always masked to $FC, hiding the bit-1 comparator
  precision ECS and AGA Agnus honour. The decode now takes the fitted
  Agnus revision and uses the same ddf_register_mask the fetch sequencer
  does; BPLCON0 bit 4 likewise counts as BPU3 only on AGA.

New tests pin every ADKCON bit one at a time, the BPLCON2 names and
fields, and the per-revision DDF and BPU views.

feat(716): the package is @trex64/c64re, and a tag will publish it

Name decided. Scoped, though not for the usual reason — there are no npm
siblings and probably will not be, because TRX64 and the U64 work are Rust and
801 settled that they ship as release binaries and a tap, never crates.io and
never npm. The scope is taken because it cannot be retrofitted: a name written
into somebody's MCP config is permanent, packages can be added to a scope
forever, and c64re-mcp could not have been moved under @trex64 later without
breaking every config naming it. The npm scope need not match the GitHub org and
does not — trex64-dev is the org, @trex64 the scope.

c64re rather than mcp inside the scope, because MCP is how the thing is reached
and not what it is; a TRX64-side server would otherwise find its name spent. The
executable follows and is now plain `c64re`, which is what the CLI has always
called itself in every subcommand — `c64re graph`, `c64re doc`, `c64re setup` —
with the bin name the one place it said otherwise.

Manifest completed for a registry: author, repository, homepage (the org's Pages
site, which is live), bugs, keywords, private:false, and publishConfig pinning
access public and registry npmjs. That last one matters: a scoped package is
restricted by default, and without it a publish is either refused or silently
private.

release-npm.yml publishes on a v* tag and nothing else, with no stored token —
npm trusted publishing over GitHub OIDC, which also generates provenance
attestations automatically, so the package carries a verifiable link back to the
commit and run that produced it. That is worth more here than for most packages,
because the thing being shipped runs inside somebody's agent. The workflow
refuses a tag that disagrees with the manifest version, and runs both 716 gates
against the artifact about to leave.

What it cannot do is the first publish: a trusted publisher is configured ON a
package, so the package has to exist first. Step one stays a human act, and it is
irreversible after 72 hours. Recorded as such in 716.6.

Gate green under the new name: 29 pass, 0 fail.

events.message:
impossamole: debunk the VBL-stuck theory, reach the world-select screen via joystick-1 fire

VBL was never stuck: $1a2e9 is a genuine per-frame VBL counter (proven live via
hits/watch), immediately consumed and cleared by its own wait-for-next-vbl utility
- the two earlier snapshots just happened to sample that idle poll, which is where
an attract-mode loop spends >97% of its time. The real gate on the title screen is
a joystick-1 fire packet ($1c4c1 bit 7, fed by the game's own raw-IKBD ACIA
handler), proven by injecting one through the REPL's kbd command and reaching and
screenshotting the world-select screen (world_select.png).

events.message:
fix(st): eine Luecke in der Sektorfolge ist keine kleinere Geometrie — und der Seitenfehler war nie mit zwei Seiten geprueft (H-18, MF-1339)

H-18 verlangt, die beiden Fehler von CERTIFY 1.0 (Moore/Small, Antic
1988, certify.lzh!CERTIFY.C Z. 173-194; gesichtet in
docs/research/ATARI_COPY_TOOLS_2026-09-23.md) als Regression aufzunehmen:
der Fehlerzweig von Seite 1 liest erneut Seite 0, und EIN Leseversuch
auf Sektor 10 entscheidet 9 oder 10 Sektoren je Spur.

Gemessen, welche Stellen im Baum in dieser Klasse stehen:

1. uft_st_order_messen() setzte `spt = sector_count`. Fehlte auf der Spur
   ein Sektor MITTEN in der Folge (1..8,10), meldete sie `gemessen` und
   spt 9 — aus einer 10-Sektor-Spur wurde eine 9-Sektor-Spur, und
   Interleave und Spiralfaktor liefen ueber Feldpositionen, die keine
   physischen Plaetze mehr sind. Eine doppelte Nummer (Phantomsektor)
   ergab ebenso eine Messung. Jetzt: traegt die Spur nicht jede Nummer
   1..n genau einmal, bleibt `gemessen` false. Rotbeweis 3 von 5 rot,
   danach 5 von 5; test_st_spiralfaktor weiter 10 von 10.
   GRENZE, festgenagelt statt verschwiegen: fehlt der LETZTE Sektor ganz,
   zeigt die Spur es nicht — spt ist, was diese Spur traegt, nicht die
   Geometrie der Diskette. Das steht jetzt im Header.

2. uft_diag_surface_scan() nimmt die Geometrie aus der Konfiguration und
   wiederholt auf derselben Seite — richtig. Aber jeder vorhandene Test
   lief mit `sides = 1`, die Seitenlokalisierung war also ungeprueft.
   Neuer Test mit zwei Seiten (Seite 0 gut, Seite 1 Spur 5 kaputt) und
   einem Sektor 10, der erst beim zweiten Versuch liest: 10 von 10 gruen.
   Dass er rot werden KANN, ist gemessen: Mutation "immer Seite 0 lesen"
   (die CERTIFY-Gestalt) -> 5 rot; Mutation "nicht wiederholen" -> 3 rot.

Zwei Testdateien statt einer, weil uft_disc_diagnostics.h ein eigenes
uft_sector_status_t definiert, das mit uft_types.h kollidiert — beide
Header gehen nicht in eine Uebersetzungseinheit (Nebenbefund, nicht
behoben).

Produktive Aufrufer beider Funktionen: 0 (nur Tests). Keine der vier
Kennzahlen bewegt sich; die Einheiten sind richtig, bevor jemand sie
verdrahtet. Struct und Signaturen unveraendert.

Nicht gelaufen: ASan (keine Allokation im geaenderten Pfad).
Vorbestehend rot und unberuehrt: test_dms_loch_ist_kein_guter_sektor
(Windows-Wegwerfdatei, siehe CLAUDE.md).

events.title: P5: two-car edge cases -- the exit hold's 855A, and a double fall (M3.93)
events.message:
P5: two-car edge cases -- the exit hold's 855A, and a double fall (M3.93)

The race exit's 100-tick hold calls 855A with a drifting BX (92BC clears
BL): the gate passes on iteration 1 when the camera car is the scorer,
and on all 100 when that is P1. A deciding pass writes [2630], which the
exit fix-up reads -- a cheat exit during P2's deciding blink is a loss.
Ported as exitHold855a. The double fall ([2682] with no in-flight guard),
forced through runStep on ROUND31: mid-blink the first point is lost and
the second counts; during the re-appear, a clean second exchange. Neither
window is reachable in play.
