events.message:
fix(geos): 00/00 beendet die VLIR-Tafel, 00/FF ist ein leerer Platz — und einen Loeschvermerk gibt es nicht (H-12, MF-1338)

geos_parse_vlir_index() las den Record-Block eines GEOS-VLIR-Files gegen
drei Belege falsch:

- 00/00 galt als "Empty record", und der Lauf ging WEITER. Er ist das
  Ende der Tafel (GEOS.TXT:170-182; GEOS-2.0-Kernal _OpenRecordFile zaehlt
  bis zum ersten 00/00). Nichtnull-Bytes dahinter wurden als Records
  gezaehlt.
- 00/xx galt als "letzter Sektor, Byte ist Groesse" -> 00/FF bekam
  size 255. 00/FF ist der LEERE Record (Kernal _WriteRecord mit Laenge 0).
- Spur 0xFF galt als "geloescht". GEOS kennt keinen Loeschvermerk,
  _DeleteRecord schiebt die Tafel zusammen (MoveBackVLIRTab). Erfunden.
- num_records zaehlte nur "gueltige" Records statt der Plaetze; damit
  verschob jede Luecke alle folgenden Recordnummern, und der Rundlauf
  parse -> write schrieb nur 85 von 127 Plaetzen zurueck.

Belege: docs/format_specs/commodore/GEOS.TXT und CVT.TXT (eine Hand,
dieselbe Sammlung) und als FREMDE Hand der rekonstruierte GEOS-2.0-Kernal
von Michael Steil, github mist64/geos, kernal/files/files10.s — nur
gelesen, keine Zeile uebernommen (Kanal Spec).

rot gegen den Vorzustand, danach 14 von 14 gruen. ctest -R geos: 5 von 5.

mit), records[] hinter dem Ende genullt, Rueckgabe 1 wenn hinter dem Ende
Nichtnull-Bytes stehen (forensischer Hinweis statt stillem Verwerfen).
geos_vlir_record_empty(): Spur 0. geos_vlir_record_deleted() bleibt als

events.title: feat(app): publish per-run over_art/bar on V6TextRun for a raster host (SQ-1592)
events.message:
feat(app): publish per-run over_art/bar on V6TextRun for a raster host (SQ-1592)

A host drawing V6 Hybrid chrome itself had no way to tell, per V6TextRun,
whether a run sits over opaque frame artwork or whether its row is a
reverse-video BAR versus furniture built from reversed spaces — both
answers exist today, but only inside the hybrid ring's private
ChromeRowOracle::over_art and row_is_reverse_bar.

Add V6TextRun::over_art and V6TextRun::bar, computed on the raster path
(GlyphSink::blit's callers) by calling the SAME primitives the hybrid
ring calls — region_has_opaque over the frame's art-only canvas, and
row_is_reverse_bar over the row's own runs — rather than re-deriving
their logic. Only Chrome-sourced runs get a real answer; every other
source (GridCell, Panel, StoryProse, StoryCanvas, Pager) carries
false/false, since none of them is asked this question today. The
SQ-1593 menu-flank continuation runs ask both questions fresh at each
continuation row's own position, since a divider's continuation can
cross from real artwork into the extension's own manufactured gap.

GlyphSink::blit's join fast path now also requires over_art/bar to
match before joining two glyphs into one run, or a joined run could
report one answer for pixels that actually disagree.

Cross-path agreement tests (Zork Zero's banner for over_art, Arthur's
Amiga F3 inventory status bar for bar) prove the raster path's
independently-computed answer matches the hybrid ring's own
classification for the same frame; falsifying either computation
fails the corresponding test.

events.title: feat(app): ease the story pane's own follow when new output arrives (SQ-1595)
events.message:
feat(app): ease the story pane's own follow when new output arrives (SQ-1595)

A turn's output used to jump the transcript straight to the new bottom with
zero animation, even though [animation] already eases the story pane's own
explicit scroll actions and the hint panel's. Give autoscroll-follow the same
treatment, on a dedicated `follow_ms` timing key:

- `AnimationConfig::follow_ms` (default 200ms) — its own config key, honoring
  the master `enabled` switch and the shared `easing` curve. `ScrollAnim::over`
  is the sibling of `ScrollAnim::to` that takes an explicit duration instead
  of always reading `cfg.scroll_ms`.
- `pager::apply_frame` arms the ease exactly where it already decides where a
  turn's new output lands: only when the reader was at the bottom before the
  turn (a reader scrolled into history is never dragged back down, same as
  today), and only up to wherever the `[more]` pager would park — paging
  further afterward is a reader action and stays on `scroll_ms`.
- Any key press or mouse event finalizes an in-flight follow-ease immediately
  (`AppState::finalize_transcript_scroll_anim_now`), mirroring
  `settle_picture_pacing`'s "the player outranks paced output" hook in the run
  loop; the run loop's own natural on-`done()` finalize now shares that same
  path instead of a second copy of it.

Falsified both behaviors by temporarily disabling the arm and the early
finalize in turn; the new tests failed as expected, then passed again once
reverted.

events.title: YM sound effects for an ST without DMA sound, and STDL v1.12.0
events.message:
YM sound effects for an ST without DMA sound, and STDL v1.12.0

A plain ST, a Mega ST, or an STE with ste_sound=false cannot play the
Amiga's sampled effects, and until now played none at all. They now
play simplified versions on the YM, automatically, wherever samples
cannot play; an STE with its sound on is unchanged.

- src/ym_sfx_st.cpp: about 30 recipes, each a dozen hand-written
  numbers (length, volume curve, noise and tone slides, a warble or
  rattle flag), expanded into STDL_Sfx steps the first time an effect
  plays. Gunfire, the pistol's boom, hits, deaths, the shield, beeps,
  doors, the lift, teleporters and more; footsteps very quiet, on
  trial. Ambient loops (birds, jungle, frog, fans) stay silent: they
  fire constantly - 138 calls in 20 seconds of level 1's first room.
  Sounds no Amiga bank carries have no recipe either.
- All effects share voice C, the voice a YM stream's melody misses
  least. A playing effect is not cut short by a less important one,
  and a distant sound counts as less important: the first room
  retriggers a distant beep about twenty times a second, which would
  otherwise have held off footsteps and doors.
- Levels set from the samples: sfx_audition=true (a hidden test
  option) plays each effect's sample and then its YM version at a
  level's start, with its name in RS.LOG. Recorded on an STE, the
  first drafts at full scale were 8dB over their samples on average,
  14dB for the explosion; each recipe now sits within 2dB, so a plain
  ST keeps the balance an STE has between effects and YM music.
- Measured in play: Conrad's pistol is sound 5, "explo", not "tir2",
  so it gets the explosion's recipe - a boom sinking into a rumble.
- The save-point jingle (play_gamesaved_sound) gets a two-tone beep.
- tools/ym-sfx-report.py measures the samples in dist/DATA - length,
  a volume curve on the YM's scale, noisiness, brightness, pitch - to
  write recipes from. The recipes are written by hand, not copied.

STDL v1.12.0 gives an effect a noise period per step, sounding with
the step's tone on the same voice (a crack over a thump, a noise that
sinks), and keeps effect timing right at 60Hz.

README, docs/configuration.md and RS.CFG: effects are no longer
STE-only, and ste_sound=false now means the YM versions.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: YM effects: per-step noise, and steps that keep their length at 60Hz
events.message:
YM effects: per-step noise, and steps that keep their length at 60Hz

STDL_Sfx gains an optional `noises` array, one noise period per step.
With it, tone and noise are separate each step on the same voice:
periods[i] sounds the tone, noises[i] the noise generator at that
period, both together when both are set. A gunshot is a crack of
noise over a thump of tone on one voice, not two; an explosion a
noise whose period climbs as it fades, where before the noise period
was fixed for a whole effect. Without `noises` an effect reads
exactly as it did - tone throughout, or noise throughout with period
0 a rest - and initialisers written for the old struct compile
unchanged, though -Wextra now asks for the missing field.

Wanted by a port that approximates its sampled effects on the YM for
machines without DMA sound, where gunfire and explosions are most of
what matters.

Step timing: the tick counted 20ms a VBL, so after STDL_SetRefresh(60)
every effect ran 20% fast. It now counts in thousandths of a tick
against stdl_vbl_hz, as STDL_Music and the voice tick already do, so
a step lasts its step_ms at either rate. The headers, porting guide
and skill said effects could not compensate; they now list them with
the ones that do.

tests/host/test_sfx.c: the old tone and noise forms unchanged, per-step
noise sounding alone, with tone and handing the generator back, and an
80ms effect taking four ticks at 50Hz and five at 60Hz (four without
the change - the test fails on the old timing). examples/sfxdemo.c
adds three gunshots and a sinking explosion; recorded on an emulated
plain ST, the explosion's spectral centroid falls from 7.8kHz to
4.0kHz as it fades.

P3-545. src/formats/c64/uft_d64_g64.c las die G64-Geschwindigkeitstafel mit data[0x15C + i] — Schrittweite 1 statt 4 und fester Versatz statt 12 + 4 * n — und schrieb spiegelbildlich buf[0x15C + i]. Referenz: docs/format_specs/commodore/G64.TXT (je Halbspur ein 4-Byte-Eintrag LO/HI ab $015C). Gemessen an tests/corpus_free/vice_c1541_35trk.g64: 28 von 84 Eintraegen falsch, 26 von 35 Vollspuren in der falschen Zone. Produktiv: g64_load_buffer speist die Wandlung (uft_format_convert_bitstream.c, uft_format_convert_sector.c). Weil Leser und Schreiber denselben Fehler trugen, war jeder Rundlauf gruen; das Plugin src/formats/g64/uft_g64.c las die Tafel die ganze Zeit richtig.

Berichtigt: 4-Byte-Eintraege ab 12 + 4 * n; ein Eintrag ueber 3 ist laut G64.TXT der Versatz einer Zonentafel je Byte und passt nicht in das 8-Bit-Feld speed — abgesagt mit -4 statt gekuerzt; ein Kopf mit weniger als 84 Eintraegen wird nicht mehr an der festen Groesse 0x2AC abgewiesen, verlangt wird 12 + 8 * n; und die zwei Laengenbytes einer Spur muessen im Puffer liegen (offset + 2 <= size statt offset < size, vorher ein Lesezugriff hinter das Ende bei offset == size - 1).

events.title: fix(app): record the Menu flank's chrome-run continuation as text, not pixels (SQ-1593)
events.message:
fix(app): record the Menu flank's chrome-run continuation as text, not pixels (SQ-1593)

fill_menu_flank_extension carried a chrome run's own ink stroke or reverse
block down through the Menu-anchor gap with a bare, unconditional
canvas.put_pixel loop that had no V6TextMode/GlyphSink parameter at all,
unlike every other glyph in this pipeline. Under RecordOnly a host drawing
its own chrome text got the border rows above the gap as recorded
V6TextRuns but this continuation as pixels always painted at lanthorn's own
stroke width underneath them - a visible seam on Journey PC r83 and Amiga
panes tall enough for the Menu plan.

Only the nearest_run-driven sub-cases (a divider's ink stroke, or a
reverse-video block) are chrome text and now go through glyphs.blit one
chrome row at a time - the same call every real border row above the gap
already makes, so it paints under Rasterise/RasteriseAndRecord exactly as
before and records nothing under RecordOnly but a V6TextRun a host can
paint itself. The canvas-scan fallback (a window's own uniform page fill,
SQ-1578) and the art-recentre/panel-flood branches (SQ-1576/1577) are
untouched - they are art/page colours reaching down, not text, and stay
unconditional canvas paints in every mode per RecordOnly's own contract.

events.title: grm-as0m: constantRegisterValue becomes a location + operation evaluator
events.message:
grm-as0m: constantRegisterValue becomes a location + operation evaluator

The all-or-nothing constant evaluator now walks backward over a location
(A, X, Y or C), stops at the last instruction that writes it, and asks a
ConstantSemantics implementation what that instruction leaves there; each
input it reads is another walk under the same guards. carryValueBefore --
a second walk that duplicated every guard of the first -- is gone: carry is
just another location.

Mos6502ConstantSemantics is the table implementation (design (a)). New over
the old mnemonic list: SBC, ROL/ROR A, carry out of ASL/LSR/ADC/SBC and
CMP/CPX/CPY, and the memory-operand forms of AND/ORA/EOR/ADC/SBC/CMP over a
load the scanner resolves. writes() is the union of the mnemonic modifier
tables and the instruction's p-code result objects, so an undocumented
writer (LAX) now stops the walk instead of being stepped over.

StoredValueScanner.semanticsFor(program) is the seam for design (b), a
p-code evaluator selectable per program (grm-4wqd).

events.message:
Merge pull request #23 from vibecodekun/feat/cycle-accurate-mode

Add the opt-in cycle-accurate compiler and separate NES runtime, including review fixes for MMC1 bank folding, ordinary-ROM startup, verifier failure handling, and Linux libm linkage.

Independent validation: AccuracyCoin 144/144 at alignment 0 and 143/141/143 at alignments 1-3, with native/interpreter/oracle trace parity; 12,000-frame stress and 3,000-frame SMB3 World 1-1 route parity at all four alignments; nine audio checks; Windows and Linux builds, CPU helper checks and synthetic MMC1/startup regressions; eleven verifier tests. Default output from the combined tree is byte-identical to current master for SMB3, Mega Man and AccuracyCoin (180 files).

The nonzero-alignment AccuracyCoin failures and remaining hardware/host limitations are documented. Trace parity is distinct from hardware correctness. Review corrections: d2c125de914cec5e53ff3b2270cc6df998503641.
events.author: mstan

events.title: The voice mixer's loops run four samples to a pass
events.message:
The voice mixer's loops run four samples to a pass

Each voice-sample paid a dbra, 12 of its 68 cycles, just to go round
the loop. The body is now written out four times with .rept, so the
dbra comes once in four samples. A run that is not a multiple of four
enters its first pass part-way in: every instruction in the body is a
fixed size, 16 bytes in all, and a jmp (d8,PC,Xn) skips (-run & 3)
bodies. The source still holds one body, in a macro shared by the
store variant for a block's first voice and the add variant for the
rest. The clamp pass is unrolled the same way; a block is 128 frames,
a whole number of passes, so it needs no part-way entry.

tests/hatari/voicechk.c: all 120 random mixes identical to the C
twin, and 400 four-voice blocks in 2065ms against 2305ms before - 10%
off the mixing. Four busy voices at 6258Hz now take 25% of an 8MHz
STE, down from 28%; the header, limits, skill and voice.c quote the
new figure. The C twin is unchanged. ovvoice.c still reads no border
misses.

events.title: The original modules on an STE, and STDL v1.11.0
events.message:
The original modules on an STE, and STDL v1.11.0

An STE or Mega STE now plays the Amiga score as it is: the ProTracker
modules, from MUSIC\<NAME>.MOD, on STDL's four voices. Every other ST
keeps the YM streams, and so does an STE whose modules are missing or
whose sample device is off (ste_sound=false).

- mod_player.cpp's sequencer runs from the voice tick - notes,
  effects, speed and tempo as upstream - and after each tick tells
  the voices what changed: a trigger, a pitch, a volume. The software
  mixer stays out of the ST build. Voice 3 is shared: an effect takes
  it and the module's fourth channel sits out until the effect ends.
  Module volume is scaled by music_volume through a table (per tick it
  was a __mulsi3 and a divide a channel, 1.6% of an STE); at 50 the
  title plays 2.5dB above the YM stream.
- music=true (or mod) plays the modules where they can play and YM
  elsewhere; music=ym is YM everywhere. The Options Music line cycles
  Off, YM and MOD among what is installed and playable.
- tools/make-music.sh copies each module beside its stream, under the
  same 8.3 name; RExtract does the same.
- The idle pause stays off while a sequencer owns the voice tick. A
  paused device runs no tick, so a module - or the action music - that
  fell quiet for two seconds would never have played its next note.
- A module that does not fit in memory is given up and freed, and the
  YM track plays; upstream would read the rest of the file into the
  wrong samples.

STDL v1.11.0 is what makes it affordable. Its voice mixer took 45% of
an 8MHz STE with four voices; the rewrite takes 28%. It also fixes
SetVoice holding interrupts off through a division, which lost the top
border on an STE whenever the module retriggered notes: 55 misses by
the end of level 1's opening scene, none now.

Measured in Hatari (STE, cycle-exact, screen=top, every frame drawn),
work YM against MOD: intro scene 0D 34.5s / 48.7s against a 27.2s
budget, level 1's opening 9.4s / 13.8s against 4.8s. Mega STE intro
20.4s / 25.8s, inside its budget. With frame skipping on, an STE
shows fewer cutscene frames with the modules; the README says so.

README, docs/configuration.md and RS.CFG cover the music settings,
and the disk space is 3.5MB with the modules.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: Put the modules in MUSIC as well, for the STE to play
events.message:
Put the modules in MUSIC as well, for the STE to play

The port now plays the original ProTracker modules on an STE or Mega
STE, on its DMA sound, and keeps the YM streams for every other ST. So
each module goes into MUSIC unchanged as <NAME>.MOD, beside the
<NAME>.STM converted from it - the same 8.3 name, which is how the game
asks for both and plays whichever the machine can.

A track whose YM conversion fails still ships its module, and the
note about it now says a plain ST will be quiet there while an STE
plays the original. The summary counts tracks rather than files, so
it still reads 21 rather than 42. About 720KB more in the download.

The fixture test compares every module against the port's own copy
from tools/make-music.sh, byte for byte, as it already did for the
streams: 21 of 21. The page, the README and the zip's header comment
say what MUSIC holds now; the README's source map also said "deflated"
for the zip, which has been stored since 614086b.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: SetVoice masks the stores, not the arithmetic
events.message:
SetVoice masks the stores, not the arithmetic

STDL_SetVoice worked out the voice's step inside stdl_int_off(), and
that division is a __udivsi3 call, about a scanline on an 8MHz
machine. A module player calls SetVoice from the voice tick, around
2ms into the frame - where an open top border's Timer A lands, with a
line and a quarter of grace - and on an STE the border was lost every
few seconds while the music played. Never on a Mega STE, whose tick is
done before line 32.

Found by breaking on the miss path in Hatari's debugger and reading
the interrupted PC off the ISR's stack: every miss had interrupted the
move to SR that ended SetVoice's masked section. The step, table row
and 16.16 bounds are now computed first and only the stores are
masked.

tests/hatari/ovvoice.c opens the top border and counts misses for
20 seconds each with the device idle, with four voices looping, and
with all four retriggered from the tick after a delay that sweeps the
calls across Timer A's window: 18 misses on the last before the change,
none after; the port that found it went from 55 to none over the same
scene. AGENTS.md records the rule: a call a tick or ISR may make does
its arithmetic first and masks only the stores.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: The voice mixer accumulates in 16 bits, in 68000 assembly
events.message:
The voice mixer accumulates in 16 bits, in 68000 assembly

Four voices at 6258Hz took 45% of an 8MHz STE, measured under a port
playing four-channel modules: gcc 4.6 compiled the per-voice loop,
which clamped every sample with two compares, to about 170 cycles a
voice-sample. Each voice now adds into a block of 16-bit sums and the
block goes to the ring through one clamp table. The inner loop is a
byte fetch, a table fetch and an add, hand-written, with the 16.16
step split so add.w/addx.w carry the fraction into the index. Each
voice works out once per stretch how many frames it can run, with a
divu.w rather than __udivsi3, so the loop has no end test. Four
voices now mix a block in 5.8ms: 28% of the machine.

The C loop stays beside the assembly (voice_run_c) as the twin
tests/host exercises. tests/hatari/voicechk.c runs 120 random mixes
of one to four voices - short samples and one-frame loops included -
through both on target and compares them byte for byte, then times
them: all 120 identical, 400 four-voice blocks in 2305ms against
3505ms for the C.

Two behaviour changes come with it, both fixes:

- Clamping once is the sum. Clamped per voice, three loud voices
  saturated at +127 before a fourth negative one came back down.
  A host test sums 3 x 63 - 64 and wants 125; the old mixer gave 63.
- A loop carries its overshoot. The wrap restarted on the loop's
  first frame and dropped the fraction, so a loop a few frames long
  came back late every time round and played flat - measurably, for
  the 8- and 16-byte loops modules use. The fraction now carries in,
  as Paula's period counter does. A host test of an eight-frame loop
  at a step of 1.5 fails on the old wrap and passes.

stdl_voice.h, docs/limits.md and the skill carry the measured cost;
AGENTS.md points at voicechk.c for anyone touching either loop.

events.title: fix(zvm): erase a mixed run's covered ink when reprinting the same slot (SQ-1589)
events.message:
fix(zvm): erase a mixed run's covered ink when reprinting the same slot (SQ-1589)

V6Windows::paint_run's padding-space segments only erased BLANK cells
underneath, never ink, to protect a genuine neighbour field (Shogun's
status padding, SQ-1054). Amiga Journey's combat-menu party column
reprints one field slot with a shorter name over a longer one ("Tag"
over "Esher") as one mixed run, so the old word's tail survived as a
stray "Tager".

Discriminator: per glyph, snapshot BEFORE this call's own trims
whether the pixel span already carries a run that started at or
before this run's own x (a same-slot overwrite) versus one that
starts strictly after it (a genuine neighbour, spared regardless of
whether the gap is interior or trailing). The snapshot has to be
taken pre-call because an ink segment erased earlier in the SAME call
trims the old run into a remnant whose OWN x has moved past this
run's x — asking the live state at that point reproduces the bug.

Verified against the real repro (Amiga release floppy, r30): a
scripted encounter partway through the intro drops "Esher" from the
party and reprints "Tag" at its old slot. Falsified by reverting the
new erase condition — both the synthetic unit test and the real-story
test then fail with the exact "er     " remnant the report described.

Shogun's status padding (SQ-1054), Zork Zero's "Great Hall" (SQ-0498)
and advent.z6's help bar (SQ-0504) are unaffected: none of their
covered runs start at or before the printing run's own x.

Completes: SQ-1589

exactly the rows that rule rejects. A host composing Hybrid with
V6FrameInputs::bottom_anchor_menu therefore had every menu click silently
dropped on any pane with spare height.

V6Frame now carries menu_band_shift (story_bottom, extension), captured at
the exact call site that moves the band so it cannot drift from whether
the band actually moved, and V6Frame::menu_band_game_px inverts the three
canvas regions this creates: unshifted above the band, None in the gap the
extension opened (grown prose/scrollback), and shifted back up in the
band itself. Every other plan (Frame/Extend/Letterbox) leaves the field
None and falls straight through to the plain game_px, unchanged.

events.message:
fix(tests): 27 Tests gaben ihre Spuren nie frei — und fuenf davon mit einem Aufraeumer, der nur die Haelfte kannte (MF-1335)

Der Sanitizer-Lauf zu e60d3e7d war rot, und zwar nur im Schritt
"ASan-Rueckstand gegen fallende Grundlinie": seit diesem Commit ist das
Tor scharf, ohne dass `docs/asan_baseline.txt` existiert, also zaehlt
jeder Leck-Fehler. Gemessen waren es 27 Tests (CI-Lauf 35813314830),
alle "Subprocess aborted" durch LeakSanitizer — und KEINER davon durch
eine Aenderung am Produktivcode: `uft_format_plugin.c`, `atari_check.c`
und `uft_kryoflux_stream.c` sind in e60d3e7d unveraendert. Der Rueckstand
war alt; neu war nur, dass er zaehlt.

Behoben statt eingefroren. Die Grundlinie zu saeen haette die 27 fuer
immer erlaubt; die Kennzahl heisst "leckende Tests null halten".

Die Ursachen, gemessen an den Stapeln (84 von 108 Meldungen aus
`uft_track_add_sector`):

  * 5 Tests: wortgleicher Nachbau von uft_track_cleanup(), der nur
    `t->sectors` freigab, nicht `t->sectors[i].data`. Jetzt ruft der
    Helfer den kanonischen Aufraeumer (MF-1177, eine Rechnung).
  * 8 Tests: `free(X.sectors); free(X.raw_data);` von Hand — dieselbe
    Luecke, 37 Stellen. Ersetzt durch uft_track_cleanup(&X), nur wo X
    nachweislich ein uft_track_t ist.
  * 10 Tests: Spur gelesen und nie freigegeben, der Lesefehlerzweig
    sprang mit `continue` heraus. Aufraeumen hinter der letzten
    Verwendung und vor jedem solchen `continue`.
  * atari: `check_result_t` auf dem Stapel, `r.issues` nie frei
    (check_free() gibt auch die Struktur frei, passt also nicht).
  * kryoflux: `uft_kf_init()` ohne `uft_kf_free()`.
  * d64: `zurueck` und `orig` nur im Fehlerzweig freigegeben.
  * td0: die IMD aus uft_td0_to_imd() nie freigegeben; uft_imd_free()
    ist die passende Freigabe (der Wandler ruft sie selbst, und sie
    gibt die Struktur nicht frei, die hier auf dem Stapel liegt).

Der Produktivcode macht es richtig: 22 Aufrufe von uft_track_cleanup()
in src/, zwoelf Tests ebenfalls. Die Lecks lagen alle in Tests.

Abnahme, lokal gemessen statt auf CI gewartet:
  * Unter MinGW gibt es kein ASan. Die genaue Quelliste je Test kommt
    aus build-tests-ci/build.ninja und wurde unter WSL (Ubuntu, gcc 15.2)
    mit -fsanitize=address und den ASAN_OPTIONS des CI-Auftrags gebaut.
  * Rotbeweis: 27 von 27 rot mit Lecks — derselbe Befund wie CI
    (z. B. dms 6 Lecks, CI 6).
  * Nach der Korrektur: 27 von 27 gruen, 0 Lecks.
  * Windows-Bau der 27 Ziele: 0 Fehler; ctest 24 gruen, 3 rot — genau
    die vorbestehenden tmpnam()-Faelle (d13, dms, do), die VOR jedem
    Spurlesen scheitern ("Wegwerf-Datei fehlgeschlagen").

Am Werkzeug gemessen und berichtigt, bevor es schrieb: die erste Fassung
des Block-Zerteilers setzte in test_pro_gegen_atari800.c:320 ein
Aufraeumen vor das `continue` einer INNEREN Sektorschleife — das haette
die Spur mitten in ihrer Auswertung freigegeben und das `continue`
unbedingt gemacht. Die Vorschau zeigte es, geschrieben wurde es nicht;
die neun zuvor behandelten Dateien sind nachweislich nicht betroffen.

events.title: populous: retract "dead code" on the CHEAT hooks -- pop_ad58.asm is truncated,
events.message:
populous: retract "dead code" on the CHEAT hooks -- pop_ad58.asm is truncated,
both $37eae and $3c4e4 have real writers

Dave asked "are we sure the cheat strings are dead or just un-emulated parts" --
good challenge, and the answer is no, an earlier pass this session got this wrong.

It grepped pop_ad58.asm for a writer to $37eae and $3c4e4, found none, and called
both dead debug scaffolding. pop_ad58.asm is not actually a whole-image listing
despite the name (CLAUDE.md correction, this session): it stops at $1d462, under
40% of the real image ($ad58..$3d550). Re-checked with find_field_writers.py:

- $37eae has a real writer at $02004e, inside ikbd_read_byte ($01ffb4, named in
  populous.sym) -- the central IKBD-byte dispatcher every keyboard/mouse byte
  passes through. It stores the scancode of any non-shift key press there (0 on
  release), an ordinary, central piece of input handling. The $b9fa "CHEAT" print
  is reachable by holding the right key with the mouse in that screen corner and
  query mode selected; not yet triggered live (a control test with a known-good
  scroll code failed too, for the same reason -- write-target confusion, not
  proof the mechanism is inert).
- $3c4e4 (emit_cap50_side in populous.sym) has a real writer at $01fbc4, inside
  the terrain.md-documented command-14 "misc" sub-dispatcher's case 0xf. The same
  dispatcher's case 10 doubles the local player's mana (capped 100000) when its
  sub-arg is 0 -- a second, more striking cheat effect in the same handler,
  missing from terrain.md's existing sub-command table. A text-entry flow
  (FUN_0001a01e, guarded by DAT_0003c4e0) that feeds keystrokes through
  ikbd_read_byte and then calls this dispatcher is a candidate for how it's
  issued -- a possible cheat-code entry screen -- but not traced yet.

Corrects graphics.md's Scrolling section and mechanics.md 7 (the $3c4e4 bullet).
Neither hook is proven live yet; both are proven no longer to be provably dead.

events.title: netplay: lobby fixes (identity fits 31 chars, session keys before caps, LAN members), cold-boot resume reset, digest mutation test, size guard, capability matrix
events.message:
netplay: lobby fixes (identity fits 31 chars, session keys before caps, LAN members), cold-boot resume reset, digest mutation test, size guard, capability matrix

- game_version is '<=18 of the release pin>+<12 hex of exe SHA-256>': the
  lobby carries 31 characters and a longer identity made every join fail
  version_mismatch.
- The engine's widescreen key is registered before the room publishes its
  caps (a first match was refused 'host did not settle widescreen').
- runtime_session_reset clears a pending guest-resume request and the frame
  continuation state: the offline Play after a rematch resumed $8057 on
  zeroed RAM. After the fix it equals a fresh process (RUN_DONE identical).
- NES_RB_PROBE=mutation: one byte per partition flips exactly that
  partition's digest and restores (8/8). _Static_assert on SaveStateData.
- rb_lobby.sh: waits only on the peers, refuses a server that failed to bind.
- docs/NETPLAY.md: capability matrix with measured evidence, open defects.

events.title: ci(716.5): WSL2 proved, the /mnt warning measured, and the Linux job given room
events.message:
ci(716.5): WSL2 proved, the /mnt warning measured, and the Linux job given room

WSL2 works. Debian-13 under wsl-version 2, node installed inside it, the package
packed, installed into an empty directory and answering MCP three ways: 29 pass,
0 fail. The job asserts /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop too, so a green run
cannot mean it quietly ran somewhere else.

The /mnt warning is now a number instead of a phrase. Both filesystems run the
full check: 23s on the distribution's own disk, 31s under /mnt, both 29/0. That
is a third slower — not the "great deal" INSTALL.md claimed — so INSTALL.md was
corrected to say what was measured, while noting that this check is not a
file-heavy workload and a disassembly listing is, so the gap widens with the
work. The advice survives; its justification changed from assertion to
measurement. That was the deal this step was built under.

Also raises the Linux job's timeout from 15 to 30 minutes. Spec 716 added two
steps to it and the package one is expensive by nature — a full build through
prepack, a real npm install including a native dependency, three MCP sessions —
which pushed a job that used to finish in ~11 minutes past its own limit. The
first symptom was a bare "The operation was canceled" with no failing step above
it, which reads like a flake and is not one.

events.title: netplay: 2-4 player co-op online over rollback (nesrecomp feat/rollback-netplay)
events.message:
netplay: 2-4 player co-op online over rollback (nesrecomp feat/rollback-netplay)

- Pin nesrecomp f6daf6b (rollback netplay: recomp-net 03ee1b1 episode driver,
  INCREMENTAL replay, N seats, shared lobby) and recomp-ui 9edc243
  (RetroPortingToolKit feat/genesis-netplay-4p: master b688ca7 with the shared
  netplay backend + the profile seat-ceiling clamp; NES profile max 4).
- CMake: SMB_ENABLE_NETPLAY (default ON for Linux) links it.
- Co-op is online-capable: the local-only refusal is gone; the co-op mode is
  a session configuration key (host offer = the offline selection of the

events.title: fix: make the CPC CAS READ trap replace the read, not the setup
events.message:
fix: make the CPC CAS READ trap replace the read, not the setup

The instant-load trap hooked the routine at os464 0x2873 / os6128 0x29E3
and resumed at entry+0x0D, treating it as the block reader. It is only
the shared read/write/verify setup (stash sync, motor on, PPI setup,
RET): the bit-level read happens back in CAS READ (0x2836 / 0x29A6)
after it returns. So after each instant-loaded block the firmware went
on to pulse-read the NEXT block into the same buffer against a stale
sync byte; on the 464 that surfaced as "Read error a" (1942 at block
21, 180, 10th Frame), and only ever worked on the 6128 by accident.

Now the CAS READ entry, its shared sync/record-read block and teardown
tail are located by signature scan (identical shape in os464/664/6128).
The request (A/HL/DE) is captured at the entry, the firmware's own setup
runs, and at the record-read block the CRC-checked block is delivered
and control resumes at the teardown with the reader's success result
(A=0, C+Z). Only fires while the lower ROM is paged at 0x0000.

With the trap on, every CAS READ now returns the same result and bytes
as pulse loading on 464, 664 and 6128 (1942, 180, 10th Frame, 1943,
2048, 3D Starstrike), and whole files (data too) instant-load.

events.title: fix: model the Z80 CTC daisy-chain in-service latch and RETI unwind
events.message:
fix: model the Z80 CTC daisy-chain in-service latch and RETI unwind

The CTC cleared a channel's pending interrupt on acknowledge with no
interrupt-under-service tracking, so an ISR that re-enabled interrupts
before RETI could be re-entered by the same or a lower-priority channel,
or by a device further down the daisy chain.

Per the Zilog CTC manual, acknowledge now sets the channel's IUS latch;
while it is set that channel and every lower one are inhibited (a higher
channel may still nest), and a new ieo getter reports the CTC's IEO for
downstream devices. reti() clears the highest-priority channel under
service. The Einstein and MTX wire Z80.onReti to it, and the Einstein's
keyboard/ADC/fire and 256 VDP interrupts wait for the CTC's IEO. RETN
does not unwind the chain. Also drops the per-instruction closure from
interruptPending.

events.title: fix(app): record assist_intro_line at the index the intro actually lands on
events.message:
fix(app): record assist_intro_line at the index the intro actually lands on

`push_assist` set `assist_intro_line` from `transcript.len() - 1` right
after pushing the once-per-session introduction. In inline-prompt mode
(`command_bar = false`, lanthorn's default), `push_transcript_internal_styled`
inserts app-internal output ABOVE the trailing game `>` prompt rather than
appending it (SQ-0270) — so the prompt, not the intro, ends up last, and
`len() - 1` named the wrong line. The offer printed right after the intro
(e.g. Zork I's vetted "try instead — light") was then misreported as the
intro, losing its own offer structure for any headless host reading
`assist_intro_line`/`assist_intro_offer` (SQ-1557). The TUI itself never
reads this field, so nothing visibly broke on screen.

Fix: capture `insert_above_prompt_at()`'s result once, before calling
`push_transcript_internal_styled`, and use that same index for
`assist_intro_line` — the index the line lands at either way (inserted at
the captured base, or appended at the captured `len()` when `None`).
`assist_offer` needed no analogous fix: `Offer` carries no line index at
all.

Added real-game coverage in both prompt modes (`vocabulary_vetting.rs`),
using Zork I's canonical `illuminate lamp` vetted offer as the session's
first `push_assist` call so the introduction actually fires: one case pins
inline-prompt mode (the mode that broke), the other command-bar mode (the
mode that was already correct). Falsified by reverting the fix and
confirming the inline-prompt case failed with the reported symptom
(`assist_intro_line` naming the offer line instead of the intro) while the
command-bar case still passed.

events.title: feat: stretch CPC Z80 bus cycles to the gate array's 1us wait-state grid
events.message:
feat: stretch CPC Z80 bus cycles to the gate array's 1us wait-state grid

The CPC gate array holds /WAIT low for 3 of every 4 CPU clocks, so each
Z80 memory, I/O and interrupt-acknowledge cycle waits until its WAIT
sample lands on the one free clock of the microsecond. Internal cycles are
never stretched. Model that in the CPC's memory/port hooks (memory cycles
start on phase 0, I/O on phase 3, INT ack on phase 2) and on the Multiface
NMI, which gives the published CPC NOP timings: PUSH 4, EX (SP),HL 6,
OUT (C),r 4, LDIR 6/5, CPI 4, IM 1 ack 5 (4 after an instruction ending in
internal cycles), IM 2 ack 7, HALT 1 per re-fetch.

Frames now also start where the previous one was scheduled to end, so the
last instruction's overshoot no longer lengthens every frame and line
boundaries stay on the microsecond grid.

The Z80 core is untouched, so other machines keep identical timing.
Table-driven tests check every main/CB/ED/DD/FD/DDCB/FDCB opcode against
Caprice32's CPC cycle tables and the CPCWiki microsecond table.

events.title: fix(716.5): a runner environment variable does not cross into WSL
events.message:
fix(716.5): a runner environment variable does not cross into WSL

The gate ran green inside WSL2 on the first try — 29/0, all three start paths
including npx. The step then failed on the line after it: GITHUB_ENV: unbound
variable. setup-wsl gives run steps a shell inside the distribution, and the
runner's own environment is not in it, so carrying the timing from one step to
the next through $GITHUB_ENV could never have worked. $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
would have failed the same way.

Both filesystems are now measured in one step, and nothing reads the runner's
environment. The numbers go to the log instead of a summary table — a table
nobody can write is worth less than two lines that always appear.

WSL2 itself is not the problem and never was: the distribution came up, the
interop check confirmed it really is WSL, node installed, and the package
packed, installed into an empty directory and answered MCP three ways.

events.title: fix: size standard DSK sector data by the Track-Info N
events.message:
fix: size standard DSK sector data by the Track-Info N

Standard (MV - CPC) tracks were laid out using each sector's own ID N, so
a sector whose ID claims another size desynced every following sector's
data. The CPCEMU format stores every sector of a standard track at the
Track-Info sector size (0x14); only EXTENDED records per-sector lengths.
Use the Track-Info N, falling back to per-sector N only when that N is
evidently unset (the sector sizes exactly fill the track and it doesn't).

MAME camplynx.cpp clocks the 48K/96K Z80 at 24MHz/6 = 4MHz but the 128K
at 24MHz/4 = 6MHz; every model ran at 4MHz. The clock is now per model
and drives the frame length (divided across the CRTC's lines), the tape
pulse scale and the audio mixer.

events.title: ci(716.5): WSL2, which turns out to be testable after all
events.message:
ci(716.5): WSL2, which turns out to be testable after all

This spec said WSL2 could not be proved on a GitHub runner, because the images
lack nested virtualisation. That was out of date and the claim is withdrawn:
nested virtualisation arrived with the Dadsv5 image in January 2024, WSLv2 works
from windows-2022 onward, and Vampire/setup-wsl defaults to version 2.

A third job asks two different questions.

A — does the package install and run inside the distribution, on its OWN
filesystem? That is the route INSTALL.md tells people to take, and it is the one
that decides whether WSL2 is supported.

B — does it still work from /mnt, and what does that cost? The boundary warning
is the only WSL-specific claim the document makes, and it is a claim about COST,
not correctness. So B gates on the package working in both places and prints the
two wall times into the run summary. If the numbers ever stop supporting the
advice, the advice is what changes rather than the test.

The job also checks it really is under WSL — /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop
exists only there — so a green run cannot mean it quietly ran somewhere else.

Known flaky rather than impossible: actions/runner-images#12321 reports
windows-2022 + WSL hanging after an otherwise successful step.

events.message:
fix: limit the Lynx 48K/96K cassette input to keyboard line 0

With the motor running the tape level replaced bit 0 of every keyboard
line, not just line 0 (MAME camplynx.cpp port80_r), so keys in column 0
of lines 1-9 read as the tape signal during loads.

fix: resume MCP-loaded .z80/.szx snapshots at their saved frame position

The MCP loader bypassed the snapshot service, so .z80 v3 and SZX loads
still fired an interrupt immediately instead of tpf - offset T-states
later. Call resumeAtFrameOffset as the service does.

events.title: feat: add ASCII8, ASCII16 and Konami MSX mega-ROM mappers
events.message:
feat: add ASCII8, ASCII16 and Konami MSX mega-ROM mappers

Cartridges over 64KB (or 64KB with an AB header) now bank-switch
through the ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami or Konami SCC mapper. The mapper is
guessed with openMSX's heuristic of counting LD (nnnn),A stores to each
mapper's register addresses. Banks reset on machine reset, and the
memory-map pane shows the chosen mapper. SCC sound is not modelled.

events.title: feat: read zip64 archives
events.message:
feat: read zip64 archives

A Zip64 archive stores an all-ones entry count and central-directory offset
in the classic EOCD, so the parser walked nothing and silently returned no
entries. Follow the Zip64 EOCD locator to the Zip64 EOCD record for the real
count and offset, and take overflowed per-entry sizes and local header
offsets from the Zip64 extended-information extra field.

events.title: fix: overlay the PCW keyboard matrix on block 3 reads
events.message:
fix: overlay the PCW keyboard matrix on block 3 reads

The gate array presents the keyboard at &3FF0-&3FFF of block 3 as a
read-side overlay (MAME pcw.cpp installs a read handler there); writes
reach the RAM underneath. The matrix was instead copied into RAM six
times a frame, clobbering anything software stored there. Reads now see
the live matrix; the per-tick scan only flips the heartbeat bit.

events.title: fix: re-encode HFE tracks re-formatted in the emulator on save
events.message:
fix: re-encode HFE tracks re-formatted in the emulator on save

serializeHFE only patched data fields into the retained cells by index,
so a track formatted in the emulator (new IDs, sizes or sector count), or
a cylinder/side the image never had, was saved with its old layout or
dropped. When a side's decoded IDs no longer match the image, MFM-encode
the track afresh (gaps, syncs, marks, CRCs, keeping deleted marks and
deliberate bad CRCs). The patch path now also rewrites a data mark that a
write changed and lays a good CRC over a rewritten bad-CRC field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix: classify .z80 hardware modes per the WoS spec
events.message:
fix: classify .z80 hardware modes per the WoS spec

v3 hwMode 11 (Didaktik), 14 (TC2048), 15 (TC2068) and 128 (TS2068) are
48K-class but were treated as 128K. Decode the byte-37 'modify hardware'
flag (48K->16K, 128K->+2, +3->+2A) into a sourceModel, and save hwMode
13 for the +2A, 12 for the +2 and the modify flag for the 16K instead of
writing 7 (+3) for every 4-ROM machine.

events.message:
fix: decode legacy zip entry names as cp437

Entry names without the UTF-8 flag are IBM code page 437 per the ZIP
APPNOTE, but they were decoded with TextDecoder('ascii'), which the WHATWG
encoding standard maps to windows-1252. Accented and box-drawing names came
out wrong. Decode them through a CP437 table instead.

events.title: fix: swap Jupiter Ace ArrowUp/ArrowDown to SHIFT+6/SHIFT+7
events.message:
fix: swap Jupiter Ace ArrowUp/ArrowDown to SHIFT+6/SHIFT+7

On the Ace SHIFT+6 is cursor up and SHIFT+7 down (the reverse of the
Spectrum), as the on-screen legends and the ROM agree: booting it,
SHIFT+6 moves the input cursor up a line. The host arrows were swapped.

events.message:
fix: type Jupiter Ace symbols with SYMBOL SHIFT, not SHIFT

Host characters ! @ # $ % & ' ( ) _ and " were sent as SHIFT + key, which
on the Ace gives the editing controls (DELETE LINE, cursor keys, DELETE)
or a capital letter. The ROM's SYMBOL SHIFT table at 0x03C6 decodes all
of them as SYMBOL SHIFT + that key.

events.message:
fix: skip encrypted zip entries instead of failing the archive

An encrypted entry (general-purpose flag bit 0) was handed to inflate as if
it were plain deflate data, which threw and lost every other entry in the
archive (or, if stored, returned ciphertext). Skip encrypted entries and keep
reading the rest.

events.message:
fix: pulse the PCW 300Hz timer interrupt for 100us

The gate array pulses /INT for about 100us (MAME pcw.cpp) instead of
holding it until the CPU responds, so a tick that lands while
interrupts are disabled is only recorded in the &F4 counter. CP/M Plus
and LocoScript still boot to identical screens headlessly.

fix: decode HFE sectors whose data field straddles the index

decodeHfeTrack stopped scanning at the end of the revolution, so an ID
field near the end whose data field lay past the index lost its sector.
The track is circular: while an ID is pending, keep scanning past the
index for its data mark (up to a gap-2-sized window), stopping if the
track's first ID comes round first.

events.title: fix(zvm): stop a v6 window's character grid from outliving its erase (SQ-1582)
events.message:
fix(zvm): stop a v6 window's character grid from outliving its erase (SQ-1582)

Scopa reuses one scratch window for every title-screen button ("New Game"/
"Help"/"Credits"/"Quit"), moved and resized per label with "Quit" drawn
last. Going to Help erases the whole screen: `erase_screen_rect` already
trims `texts`/`retired`/`streamed` for every window whose PIXELS the erase
covers ("the screen is one shared raster"), but only ever called
`grid.clear()` on the erase's own TARGET window. The scratch window's
pixel-positioned "Quit" run vanished correctly; its CHARACTER GRID cells —
the hybrid backend's parallel copy of the same glyphs, addressed by the
window's current origin rather than a captured paint position — survived
untouched under whatever screen printed next. The app's SQ-0729 rule ("a
live label wins over the transcript") then read those stale cells as
current chrome and spared them from the Help transcript's own glyphs,
blanking whatever word happened to land on them.

`erase_screen_rect` now also blanks any window's grid cells whose derived
pixel rect overlaps the erase, matching the treatment `texts` already
got. `paint_run`'s own erase-before-paint call (which fires on every
print, to erase what a fresh run's opaque glyphs are about to cover) has
to exclude its OWN window from this pass via a new `skip_grid` parameter:
the print loop already writes the new characters into `win.grid` before
`paint_run` runs, so an unqualified pass would erase the very glyphs just
printed (caught by `v6_print_text_routes_to_current_window_grid`).

Traced via a real-session probe (not guessed): a grid window's non-blank
cells kept "Quit" long after its pixel-positioned `texts` run was
correctly trimmed, confirming the gap is specifically the untouched
`grid.cells` layer, not the SQ-0729 precedence rule itself (which is
right for fmvpoker's live secondary-buffer panel and unmodified here).

New test in v6_raster_text_loss.rs (the SQ-0729 suite) drives scopa
title -> deal -> abort (ESCape twice) -> Help and asserts the box the
title screen last drew "Quit" into shows the Help transcript's own ink
rather than reading byte-identical to a blank-transcript render.
Falsified by reverting the zvm fix: the test fails with "0 px differ",
exactly the reported symptom.

Ran: lanthorn-zvm (924/924), v6_render/v6_windows/zmachine_screen/
zork_classic/v6_scopa group binaries (372/372, includes the untouched
SQ-0729 fmvpoker/Shogun/advent cases), the v6_arthur_advent/v6_journey/
v6_shogun/v6_zork0 presses (283/283, incl. Zork Zero's hint-menu banner),
and the full in-crate t-all suite (3791/3791). Clippy clean on both
crates.

events.title: fix: place MSX cartridges by their AB header
events.message:
fix: place MSX cartridges by their AB header

Plain cartridge images are now laid out where their header says, using
openMSX's RomPlain location vote: a 48KB image with its header at file
offset 0x4000 maps at 0x0000-0xBFFF, and BASIC cartridges (TEXT in page
2) sit at 0x8000. Slot lookup moves to 8KB segments, the granularity
mega-ROM mappers need, and the memory-map pane labels only the pages the
cartridge actually decodes.

events.title: fix: list microdrive print files and all no-autorun programs
events.message:
fix: list microdrive print files and all no-autorun programs

The MDR listing treated RECFLG bit 2 as "record in use", but on the IF1 that
bit is reset for PRINT/OPEN# data files, so those files vanished from the
listing. Judge occupancy by RECLEN instead, and don't parse a SAVE* header
out of a PRINT file's raw data. Also treat any autostart line with bit 15
set as no auto-run, not just exactly 0x8000.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: scale tape pulses to the 128K-class CPU clock
events.message:
fix: scale tape pulses to the 128K-class CPU clock

TZX/TAP pulse lengths are T-states of a 3.5MHz reference clock, but the
128K/+2/+2A/+3 run at 3.5469MHz and the Spectrum deck left pulseScale at
1, so tapes played ~1.3% fast. Set pulseScale = cpuClock / 3.5MHz as the
other machines do (still exactly 1 on the 48K).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: merge SCP revolutions by full sector ID and good-CRC reads
events.message:
fix: merge SCP revolutions by full sector ID and good-CRC reads

mergeRevolutions grouped readings by R alone, folding distinct sectors
that share an R into one fake weak sector, and flagged a sector weak
whenever any revolution differed - including a plain bad-CRC misread of a
sound sector. Key readings on C/H/R/N plus occurrence within the
revolution, and judge weakness only among good-CRC readings when any
exist; a sector bad on every revolution still gets its differing readings
as weak copies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: carry leftover tape t-states across block boundaries
events.message:
fix: carry leftover tape t-states across block boundaries

When a pulse, direct-recording sample or pause finished partway through an
advance() step, the overshoot was discarded: beginBlock zeroed the pulse
clock and an expired pause's negative remainder was dropped, so every block
boundary stretched the tape by up to one step. advance() now feeds the step
through consecutive elements and blocks, carrying each overshoot into the
next. A data block with no pause now starts the next block on its last edge
instead of via a zero-length pause.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: rebase the Spectrum tape advance point when the deck restarts
events.message:
fix: rebase the Spectrum tape advance point when the deck restarts

When the loader detector auto-starts the tape mid-frame, or the tape
service plays/resumes it, tapeLastAdvanceT still pointed at the frame
top, so the deck was handed every T-state since then (tens of pilot
edges) in one go. Add Spectrum.resetTapeAdvance and call it on restart,
as the Jupiter Ace and Lynx already do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: test: update the emulator Spectrum stub for snapshot frame resume
events.message:
test: update the emulator Spectrum stub for snapshot frame resume

The stub lacked contention.timing and resumeAtFrameOffset (used by the
snapshot service since frame-position resume), and its +2A-origin SZX
mock needs sourceHas1FFD now that 128K-origin snapshots are remapped.

events.title: fix: end WD179x multi-sector writes in record not found
events.message:
fix: end WD179x multi-sector writes in record not found

A multi-sector WRITE SECTOR that ran out of sectors ended with a clean
status, unlike the read path. The controller keeps searching for R+1 and,
not finding it, terminates with RECORD NOT FOUND; do the same for writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: raise the Jupiter Ace frame interrupt after the active display
events.message:
fix: raise the Jupiter Ace frame interrupt after the active display

The ULA asserted /INT at line 0 and then drew scanlines 0-191, so the
ROM's frame work raced the beam. MAME raises the IRQ at scanline 248,
directly below its display window: assert the 8-line /INT pulse once the
192 active lines are done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: treat PCW port &F6 as the roller RAM start entry
events.message:
fix: treat PCW port &F6 as the roller RAM start entry

&F6 selects which roller RAM entry scan line 0 reads, walking 256
entries and wrapping within the 512-byte table (MAME pcw_v.cpp). It was
modelled as a raster shift of the picture inside the border, so screens
scrolled through &F6 showed the wrong lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: disable WD179x side compare on the WD1770/1772
events.message:
fix: disable WD179x side compare on the WD1770/1772

Type II bits 1 and 3 were always taken as side-compare enable/select. Only
the FD1791/1793 compare sides; on the 1770/1772 those bits are write
precomp and spin-up disable, so a +D or SAM command with them set could
fail RNF on a valid sector. Side compare now defaults on for the 1793
(NOT READY) parts and off for the 1770/1772 (MOTOR ON) parts, with an
explicit sideCompare option to override.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: flush the beam before shadow-screen changes
events.message:
fix: flush the beam before shadow-screen changes

The beam was only flushed for ULA-port OUTs and writes to 0x4000-0x5AFF,
so a 7FFD bit-3 screen flip, or writes into the displayed bank through
0xC000 (bank 7 while shown, or bank 5 aliased there), rewrote pixels the
beam had already passed. Track which slots map the displayed bank
(SpectrumMemory.slotIsScreen) and flush before those writes and before
a screen flip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: keep the last edge's level for 1ms when a pause block follows
events.message:
fix: keep the last edge's level for 1ms when a pause block follows

A Pause block (and a Direct Recording's own pause) forced the level low the
moment it began, so the final edge of a preceding pulse sequence, tone, CSW
or zero-pause data block lasted zero time. TZX 1.20 requires at least 1ms of
that level before the pause goes low, and a pause always ends low. Route every
pause through one helper that holds the level for 1ms (or the whole pause,
if shorter) and then drops it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: let WD179x verify match any ID field on the track
events.message:
fix: let WD179x verify match any ID field on the track

Verify compared only the first sector's cylinder with the track
register, failing a track whose first ID happened to differ. The
controller reads ID fields until one matches TR with a good CRC; do that,
and set CRC ERROR alongside the seek error when only bad-CRC IDs match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(app): prune px_runs of exact duplicates a v6 canvas window has since repainted (SQ-1583)
events.message:
fix(app): prune px_runs of exact duplicates a v6 canvas window has since repainted (SQ-1583)

fmvpoker's HOLD/un-HOLD toggle never erases via erase_window — it just
reprints "HOLD" or a same-width blank at the card's own set_cursor
position — so ZWindow::record_streamed's append-only shadow piled up a
fresh run at the identical pixel rect on every toggle, forever (56 runs
after 4 hands and still growing). v6_screen_model now prunes px_runs of
runs a LATER one in the same list exactly duplicates (same position,
text, style and colours) before publishing it, which a host reading
px_runs as real text (accessibility, a non-raster renderer) sees as
just the current state instead of the whole toggle history.

Deliberately exact-duplicate matching, not "any later run whose rect
contains this one's" — that looked equivalent and changed the
Rasterise composite by hundreds of pixels once honor_game_colours was
off, because draw_story_canvas_runs_into forces every run's background
to None in that mode, so a blank run paints nothing and does not
actually erase what is behind it. An exact duplicate has no such mode
dependency, so dropping one is provably invisible to the composite in
either mode.

Tests: fmvpoker_stale_hold_labels_are_pruned (30 real hold-toggle turns,
list stays bounded to at most one run per distinct text at a position)
and fmvpoker_pruning_does_not_change_the_composite (diffs the pruned
composite against one rebuilt from the raw, unpruned shadow — zero
pixels differ), both honor_game_colours modes.

events.title: feat: LOAD and SAVE on the ZX81 through ROM traps
events.message:
feat: LOAD and SAVE on the ZX81 through ROM traps

Trap the ROM's LOAD ($0347, and IN-NAME $0366 while it waits for a
signal) and SAVE ($02FB) after NAME has parsed the filename, and move the
.p image (VERSN up to E_LINE) directly, resuming at SLOW/FAST as the
ROM's LOAD/SAVE end test does. Mounted programs form a tape: LOAD ""
reads the next one, LOAD "NAME" winds to a matching name, SAVE records
onto it, and a program mounted while LOAD waits is played into it
instead of resetting, so multi-part programs load. Traps are enabled
only for ROMs carrying the standard routines. ZX80 is not trapped yet.

events.title: fix: decode CPC FDC ports on A7=0 and ignore status-port writes
events.message:
fix: decode CPC FDC ports on A7=0 and ignore status-port writes

The FDC is selected by A10=0 and A7=0; A7 was unchecked, so OUT &F8FF
(expansion peripheral reset) switched the drive motor. A write to the
read-only main status port &FB7E was also fed to the data register.

events.message:
fix: report the last sprite checked in TMS9918A S0 bits 0-4

With no fifth sprite on a line, S0's sprite-number field now holds the
last sprite examined (the Y=0xD0 terminator, else 31) instead of stale
data, per the TMS9918A data manual.

events.title: fix: leave CPC FDC ports unanswered on the 464 and GX4000
events.message:
fix: leave CPC FDC ports unanswered on the 464 and GX4000

Without a disk interface the uPD765A is not on the bus, so reads of
&FB7E/&FB7F float to 0xFF and motor/data writes do nothing. The port
decode ignored config.hasFDC.

events.title: fix: make WD179x SEEK step relative to the track register
events.message:
fix: make WD179x SEEK step relative to the track register

SEEK set the head to the data register value outright. The datasheet has
the controller step, updating TR, until TR equals DR, so the head moves
DR - TR tracks from its real position. Model that (clamped at the track-0
stop, and setting the step direction), which keeps a STEP-without-u
TR/head desync intact across a seek.

events.title: fix: resume SZX/.z80 snapshots at their saved frame position
events.message:
fix: resume SZX/.z80 snapshots at their saved frame position

SZX dwCyclesStart (and the .z80 v3 T-state counter) record how far into
the frame the snapshot was taken, but runFrame rebased the frame to the
load point and fired an INT immediately. Add Spectrum.resumeAtFrameOffset
so the first frame starts in the past and the next INT lands
tpf - offset later (INT taken at once only inside the INT window). Load
and save the .z80 v3 T-state counter, and save the frame offset relative
to the current frame's INT.

events.title: fix: hold the last tape edge for 1ms before a pause drops low
events.message:
fix: hold the last tape edge for 1ms before a pause drops low

After a data block the deck dropped the level low 945 T-states (a 3.5MHz
figure scaled by pulseScale) into the pause. TZX 1.20 requires at least 1ms
of the opposite level before the signal goes low. Hold for 1ms of real time,
derived from the CPU clock.

events.message:
fix: hold a seek-end interrupt per drive on the uPD765A

A single ST0/PCN latch meant a seek on one drive overwrote another's
pending result, so seeking two drives returned only the last one. Keep
the seek-end status per unit and have each Sense Interrupt Status hand
back one drive's result until none remain; INT stays up while any is
pending.

events.title: fix: resume the tape after a tzx stop-the-tape block
events.message:
fix: resume the tape after a tzx stop-the-tape block

A zero-length Pause (or Stop-if-48K on a 48K machine) parked the deck idle
with playing still true. Every resume path only clears paused, and advance()
returned immediately while idle, so the tape stalled forever. The deck now
remembers it was stopped and, once unpaused, starts the block after the stop.
A stop found by the ROM-trap peek parks the deck the same way, so resuming
no longer replays the stop a second time.

events.title: feat: model Einstein keyboard, ADC and fire interrupts
events.message:
feat: model Einstein keyboard, ADC and fire interrupts

Ports 0x20/0x21/0x25 now mask the keyboard, ADC and fire interrupt
sources (bit0 set = disabled, all masked at reset). A 50Hz scan raises
the keyboard request for a key down on a selected line and the fire
request for a held button; an ADC0844 conversion raises INTR ~40us after
a write to 0x38. They follow the CTC on the daisy chain in MAME's order
(keyboard, ADC, fire) with IM 2 vectors 0xF7/0xFB/0xFD. Reading 0x20
clears the keyboard request and reading 0x38 the ADC's.

events.title: fix: report the datasheet CHRN when an MT transfer runs off EOT on head 1
events.message:
fix: report the datasheet CHRN when an MT transfer runs off EOT on head 1

With MT=1 the result after the second head reached EOT was the last
sector's own CHRN. The uPD765A result table gives C+1, H complemented and
R=01 for MT=1 HD=1 at EOT; apply it. A TC landing on that last sector
still rewrites the result to the sector transferred, now restoring H too.
The TC CHRN convention itself and MT=1 on a single-sided image are left
as documented.

events.title: fix(zvm): stop a v6 host restore from widening a game-sized window back to full screen (SQ-1580)
events.message:
fix(zvm): stop a v6 host restore from widening a game-sized window back to full screen (SQ-1580)

SQ-1572's post_restore_fixups re-applies the host's pixel screen after every
restore via set_v6_screen_px, which also resets windows 0 and 1 to full-screen
width — correct for @restart's frotz restart_screen semantics (nothing has
been sized yet), wrong for a restore, whose window table Quetzal never
touches at all. A game that sized its own window before the save — FMV
Poker's title-banner window 1, 289px inside a 640px screen — came back
stretched to full width, so its blue erase-fill painted over pixels that
should still show the poker table's own frame art.

Added Machine::redeclare_v6_screen_px, which re-stamps header $22/$24 (and
the derived grid/cell bytes) via write_screen_dims_px without touching the
window table, and pointed post_restore_fixups's v6 branch at it instead.
@restart's own call site is untouched.

Falsified both the new zvm unit test and the new FMV Poker in-game
@save/@restore app test by reverting to set_v6_screen_px: both reproduce the
exact reported symptom (window 1 back to 640px; pixel (600,20) reading the
banner's blue 0,107,181 instead of the table frame's 68,102,136).

events.message:
fix: honour DTL as the transfer length when the uPD765A command N is 0

cmdBuf[8] (DTL) was never read. The datasheet makes DTL the data length
when N is 0: read and write only DTL bytes of the 128-byte sector, with
the controller zero-filling the rest of a written data field. DTL of 0 or
above 128 transfers the whole sector.

fix: model the +2A/+3 gate array floating bus

The +2A/+3 is not fully pulled up: ports of the form 0000 xxxx xxxx xx01

events.title: fix(app): report Hybrid's raster fall-through in the host-facing plan (SQ-1584)
events.message:
fix(app): report Hybrid's raster fall-through in the host-facing plan (SQ-1584)

`V6HybridPlan` (SQ-1574) had no way to tell a host that a frame falls all
the way through to the RASTER composite instead of drawing a chrome ring
or the coherent all-text painted-screen path — the no-story-window +
painted-ground case (SQ-0711, Scopa's card table) and a picture takeover
(SQ-0729/SQ-0725, FMV Poker's full-screen canvas story window). A host
drawing its own Hybrid chrome had no signal for either, so it would
restyle a screen's labels in its own font where the TUI silently falls
back to raster.

Add `V6HybridPlan::raster_fallback: Option<&'static str>` and a new
`hybrid_bottom_plan_for` parameter (`painted_ground: bool`, the host's
equivalent of `state.v6_paint`). Both are answered by a new private
`hybrid_raster_fallback_reason`, extracted from — and now the single
source for — the exact decision `render_story_pane_frame`'s own Hybrid
arm already made at its two fall-through sites; the TUI's inline checks
now call it too (and its `runs` extraction now reuses the existing
`paint_runs` helper instead of restating it), so the two cannot drift the
way SQ-1577/SQ-1578 did earlier this session.

`kind`/`stretch_flanks`/`band_top_native`/`band_rows` are unchanged for
every existing title (Zork Zero, Journey, Arthur, Shogun) — this only
adds a signal. New oracle test
`hybrid_bottom_plan_for_raster_fallback_matches_the_tuis_own_decision`
covers Scopa's table (raster) vs. after clicking its title's "Help" label
(not raster — a real story window opens), and FMV Poker's opening screen
(not raster) vs. its table one keypress in (raster), each checked against
the TUI's own real render path.

events.message:
feat: decode z-rle compressed csw blocks in tzx files

A TZX 0x18 CSW Recording may store its pulse stream Z-RLE (zlib-compressed
RLE), and the parser threw on it. The TZX parser is synchronous and called
synchronously by every machine, so add a small synchronous zlib/DEFLATE
decoder under media/tape and inflate the stream inline, capped at five bytes
per declared pulse.

events.title: fix: update the data mark and CRC state when the uPD765A writes a sector
events.message:
fix: update the data mark and CRC state when the uPD765A writes a sector

A write replaced the sector bytes but kept the stored ST1/ST2, so WRITE
DATA over a deleted sector still read back as deleted, WRITE DELETED DATA
left a normal mark, and a rewritten bad-CRC sector stayed bad (and weak).
The write lays down a new mark and a good data CRC: set or clear the
deleted mark per command and drop DD/DE and MD/MA. Write results also no
longer report CM for a mark the write overwrote rather than read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: start CPC VSYNC on the R7 line and clock the GA at HSYNC end
events.message:
fix: start CPC VSYNC on the R7 line and clock the GA at HSYNC end

The CRTC tested VSYNC onset after drawing the (R7, RA=0) scanline, so
PPI port B bit 0 read 0 throughout it and the Gate Array's post-VSYNC
re-sync fired on the 3rd HSYNC instead of the 2nd. Onset is now tested
on entry to each scanline. The frame loop also clocks the Gate Array at
the CRTC HSYNC trailing edge (R2 + width characters in) rather than at
the end of the line, drawing the display portion just before it.

not at 2px/1T resolution. Floor the high-accuracy renderer's beam

fix: drive ZX81/ZX80 INT from refresh address bit 6

/INT is wired to A6, so it goes low when the M1 refresh address (R) has
bit 6 clear. The ROM loads R so each display scanline lasts 207T however
short the row; raising INT as soon as a row HALTed made collapsed 1K
display files run ~66% fast (FRAMES advanced 166 per 100 frames, now 101).

events.title: fix: match sector C and H as well as R in uPD765A ID searches
events.message:
fix: match sector C and H as well as R in uPD765A ID searches

The sector search looked up R alone through sectorMap, so a sector with the
right R but a different cylinder or head was read, and on duplicate-R
tracks the first R always won. The controller compares its ID register
against each ID field: search for C, H and R together (H complemented on
the MT side-1 pass), report No Data with ST2 WC/BC when the track's IDs
carry another cylinder, and write back into the exact sector found. N stays
uncompared so the undersized protection-sector handling keeps working.

events.message:
fix: defer Z80 CTC time-constant reloads and honour timer trigger

A time constant written to a running channel now waits for the current
count to reach zero, as the Zilog manual specifies; only the first load
after a reset starts the channel. Timer-mode channels with control bit 3
set now wait for a CLK/TRG edge before timing.

events.title: fix: skip unknown and deprecated tzx blocks instead of rejecting the tape
events.message:
fix: skip unknown and deprecated tzx blocks instead of rejecting the tape

Since TZX 1.10 every block ID the spec does not define is followed by a
DWORD length so readers can step over it. The parser threw on any unknown
ID, refusing otherwise-playable tapes. Skip unknown blocks by that length,
and skip the deprecated 0x16/0x17 (DWORD length), 0x34 (8 bytes) and 0x40
(24-bit length) blocks by their documented sizes.

events.title: fix: page the 48K ROM for 128K snapshots loaded on a +2A/+3
events.message:
fix: page the 48K ROM for 128K snapshots loaded on a +2A/+3

128K/+2 snapshots (.sna, .sp, .z80 non-+3 hwModes, .szx 128K/+2 IDs) carry
no 0x1FFD. Their 7FFD bit 4 selects the 48K BASIC ROM, which on the 4-ROM
+2A/+3 is page 3 and needs 1FFD bit 2 too; loading paged the +3 syntax ROM
1 instead. Mirror 7FFD bit 4 into 1FFD bit 2 via a new
SpectrumMemory.selectSnapshot128KRom (analogue of selectSnapshot48KRom).

events.message:
fix: use the full data-bus byte as the IM 2 vector

interruptWithVector() forced bit 0 of the vector low, but the Z80 builds
the IM 2 table address from I and the whole byte on the bus; even vectors
are only a convention of Zilog peripherals. All current callers (CTC,
PIO/AMX, CPC ASIC, Einstein VDP) already supply even vectors, so they are
unaffected.

Writing a tone period no longer reloads the divider: the running count
finishes and the new period is picked up at the next zero, as on the
real chip. The discrete TI part now treats period 0 as 0x400 like the
MTX model; only Sega's integrated PSG holds periods 0/1 constant.

events.title: fix: apply M1 wait states to interrupt acknowledge cycles
events.message:
fix: apply M1 wait states to interrupt acknowledge cycles

The INT acknowledge (M1 + IORQ) and the NMI response are M1 cycles, so
board WAIT logic keyed on /M1 stretches them just like an opcode fetch.
m1WaitStates (MSX: +1T) was only added to opcode, prefix and HALT
fetches; now IM 0/1/2 acknowledges and NMI include it too, and
interrupt() reports the stretched length.

group of four CLUT entries the 2bpp pixels reach. Latched per line.

events.title: fix: load the flat memory dump in v3 CPC snapshots
events.message:
fix: load the flat memory dump in v3 CPC snapshots

A v3 .SNA still carries the flat dump sized by header bytes 0x6B-0x6C;

events.title: fix: mix ULA EAR and MIC as weighted speaker levels
events.message:
fix: mix ULA EAR and MIC as weighted speaker levels

The ULA drives the speaker from bit 4 (EAR) and bit 3 (MIC) through
different resistor paths, so the pin voltage is a weighted sum (Issue 3:
0.39/0.73/3.66/3.79V), not an OR. The 48K ROM BEEPER holds MIC=1 and
toggles EAR, so the OR was a constant 1 and BEEP/key click were silent.
Feed the mixer a normalised level via a new AudioMixer.accumulateLevel.

events.title: ncr5380: drop the TT-MFP interrupt line on reset-parity/interrupt, check phase when DMA mode is armed
events.message:
ncr5380: drop the TT-MFP interrupt line on reset-parity/interrupt, check phase when DMA mode is armed

Two things a 5380 driver can rely on that the emulation did not do on the TT:

- Reading the reset parity/interrupt register (7) cleared scsi->irq but
  left the TT-MFP GPIP7 line high (only the Falcon FDC IRQ was cleared),
  so the next ncr5380_set_irq() produced no edge and the interrupt was
  lost. Drive the line low there, as the Falcon path already clears its
  IRQ source.

- Setting the DMA mode bit in the mode register while the target is
  already in a phase other than the one in the TCR raises the
  phase-mismatch interrupt on the real chip. The emulation only noticed
  the mismatch on the next CPU access to the chip. Run the phase check
  when DMA mode goes from 0 to 1.

Atari System V (UniSoft SVR4) arms DMA after the command phase and sleeps
for exactly that interrupt; with both changes its disk driver completes
its first DMA read instead of waiting forever.

events.title: control: add leftdown/leftup/mousemove fifo events for mouse injection
events.message:
control: add leftdown/leftup/mousemove fifo events for mouse injection

The command fifo could inject key events, doubleclick and the right
mouse button, but not the left button or any pointer motion - leaving
GEM desktops and mouse-only programs undrivable from the fifo.

Add three events to hatari-event:
- leftdown / leftup : left mouse button, mirroring rightdown/rightup
- mousemove <dx> <dy> : relative motion in emulated screen pixels,
  injected the same way host SDL motion is (KeyboardProcessor.Mouse).
  Absolute positioning is achieved by pinning the pointer into a
  screen corner with a large negative move (the OS clamps at the
  edges) and then moving by the wanted coordinates.

Verified by driving the TOS 2.06 desktop headlessly: opening a GEMDOS
drive window, navigating folders and launching a program with clicks
only. Note that VDI drivers may scale mouse deltas (the Nova VDI
applies its ms_speed setting, x4 by default), so absolute targeting
must account for the active driver's scaling.

events.title: fix(716.5): resolve npx the way npm is resolved, not through a quoted shim
events.message:
fix(716.5): resolve npx the way npm is resolved, not through a quoted shim

The Windows run got all the way to the last check: the shim npm wrote runs, does
an MCP initialize and answers a tool call as c64re-mcp.cmd. Only npx failed, and
it died inside its own CJS loader.

Cause: the command was passed to a shell as "npx.cmd" — quoted. Quotes tell
cmd.exe the string is a path, so it stops searching PATH; it found something else
and tried to load it.

Resolved the same way npm already is. npm_execpath points at npm-cli.js and
npx-cli.js sits beside it, so this Node spawns that directly: no shell, no shim,
one code path everywhere. The fallback keeps an unquoted npx.cmd for a run where
nothing set the variable.

--no-install as well, so a missing bin fails instead of quietly reaching for the
registry.

A failing session now prints eight lines of stderr instead of three. Three was
exactly one line short of naming the module that could not be loaded, which cost
a CI round trip.

29 pass, 0 fail locally.

events.title: test(716.5): run the executable the way a harness runs it, not the way a test does
events.message:
test(716.5): run the executable the way a harness runs it, not the way a test does

Every session this gate opened was `node <entry>`. No harness does that — a
harness names the command, and the name is a shim npm wrote. The gate checked
that the shim EXISTED and never ran it, which says nothing about whether it runs:
on Windows it is a .cmd that Node refuses to spawn without a shell, and a config
saying "command": "npx" goes through a second one.

The stdio plumbing is now one session() helper, and the gate completes an MCP
handshake three ways: node <entry> as the baseline, npm's own shim, and
`npx <name>`. On Windows the shim is quoted and run through a shell, because
that is what a harness ends up doing and a temp path is not guaranteed
space-free.

npx gets the install directory as its cwd rather than a temp directory — that is
how it finds a locally installed bin at all, and running it from elsewhere sent
it to the registry for a package that does not exist yet, where it hung. The
other sessions keep running from elsewhere on purpose, to prove the server does
not lean on the cwd.

This is one step short of the documented command: `npx -y @c64re/mcp` adds only
the registry fetch, and that cannot be proved before the package is published.
Verdaccio would close that half, and was weighed and left out — the official
action is a Docker container action and therefore Linux-only, and for a single
package with no internal dependencies it proves dist-tags and resolution we do
not have. The honest way to prove the documented command is a prerelease under
its own dist-tag, which is 716.6 and is the owner's call.

29 pass, 0 fail locally. Also records Windows as proved in the spec: run
36183644245, both jobs green.
