events.title: feat(877 D3): a document may not deny what a tool does, and a gate says so
events.message:
feat(877 D3): a document may not deny what a tool does, and a gate says so

`docs/runtime-sandbox.md` told agents in bold that "The MCP `runtime_*` tools
cannot give you that" and "Do NOT use the MCP `runtime_*` tools for this". True
when it was written; false since `runtime_sandbox_run` shipped — that tool IS a
private daemon on its own port, started as a child of the call. A run read the
document, believed it, and grew a parallel surface out of it: its own daemon, its
own WebSocket driver, a regex parsing the monitor's text dump back into bytes, and
an `until` loop polling the PC every 50 frames where a breakpoint stops on the
instruction.

The document now leads with `runtime_sandbox_run` — one call, its own machine,
its own budget — and keeps the raw-WebSocket recipe for the one thing that tool
genuinely cannot be: a machine that is still there after the call. An interactive
loop (step, breakpoint, monitor, trace) on a machine that is not the shared one
is the remaining case, and the recipe now says so where it used to say "do not
use the MCP tools". `docs/agent-doctrine.md` §1.2 points at the tool first and
keeps the raw recipe as the exception.

The gate: `check:doc-capability-claims` greps the agent-facing docs
(`agent-doctrine.md`, `runtime-sandbox.md`, `docs/tools/**` — the ones an agent
is pointed at and reads as instruction; the generated surfaces are excluded
because their sentences are the tools' own) for a capability denial standing in
the same sentence as a tool name, and fails when that tool exists in the
regenerated surface inventory. A denial that is TRUE is marked and must say why:

  <!-- deliberate-limitation: runtime_sandbox_run — it returns no session id ... -->

A mark with no reason (under 30 chars) fails, and so does a mark whose sentence
has gone. Two self-tests run the detector over the exact paragraph this gate was
written for, so widening a regex to silence a false positive cannot quietly
disarm it.

Red before: 4 claims (agent-doctrine 202/235, runtime-sandbox 5/15).
Green after: 12 docs, 296 tools, 3 marks, 3 covered denials, 2 self-tests.

Live DOSBox pass: 0B51's own new findings all PROVEN (M3.68)

Checks the [STATIC]-only findings M3.67 left open against a fresh TWO
PLAYER walkthrough on the managed DOSBox instance (reconnected cleanly
at Z:\>), plus a fourth found mid-pass.

P1 confirmed "HANDICAP ANNE ?" (a character other than WALTER/MIKE
observed live for the first time). P2's own fire pressed during P1's
question had no effect; RIGHT toggled the scratch answer live; BRAKE
dismissed it exactly like FIRE. P2 then confirmed "HANDICAP MIKE ?" --
P1's own fire during P2's question had no effect (the same finding
confirmed in the other direction); holding LEFT then RIGHT, and later
RIGHT then LEFT, both read the scratch answer as NO while genuinely
both held -- LEFT beats RIGHT independent of press order.

A real live-automation pitfall was hit twice testing that same toggle
(new PLAN.md pitfall): releasing two held keys a few ms apart leaves a
brief single-key window a level-based poll re-evaluates, which can
silently flip a "both held" test's own downstream commit. The second
hit genuinely committed MIKE's own answer wrong; caught and corrected
by fixing the release order.

The session unexpectedly bounced from CHOOSE GAME back to SELECT GAME
mid-pass. Full disassembly of RunTwoPlayerHeadToHeadSetup (1E20) and
its own caller chain explains why: 1E20 calls the CHOOSE GAME menu
exactly once with no loop, so any exit from it returns control to
SELECT GAME's own redraw -- not an artifact, the same path a normal
finished match takes. Re-entering TWO PLAYER from there gave the
strongest result: two different characters' own handicap answers, set
through two different paths, both defaulted correctly on a later visit
this session, closing M3.67's "likely session-scoped" hedge.

Investigating a second unexpected finding -- the race-info screen
advancing without further input -- led to a real, previously-mis-read
bug in already-committed documentation: a wait function's own second
timeout compare was read as a permanently-dead constant because an
earlier sweep only searched the literal CS-relative byte encoding,
missing that the same physical byte is also addressed via a completely
different DS-relative encoding this file already tracks over a dozen
writers for. Confirmed via segment arithmetic against list_segments
and this session's own live register read. That function has a real
~700-tick (~10s) timeout, currently missing from this port on three
screens. A new, unticked P3 regression item tracks the actual fix as
its own next commit, kept out of this one's scope.

tools/check-charselect.mjs gained one more assertion (44 total,
reintroduction-proven). No other test changes. Full 30-script
regression suite plus build re-run clean. docs/engine.md has the full

events.title: 0B51 ported (state): the handicap question's own interactive Y/N toggle (M3.67)
events.message:
0B51 ported (state): the handicap question's own interactive Y/N toggle (M3.67)

GOAL-DOS-PARITY.md P4's own "Remaining" list carried the handicap question
screen as interactive UI/state as its next-smallest, best-bounded item: the
gate (handicapQuestionApplies) and the roster-word link were already ported
and live-proven; only 0B51's own body (0B89-0C14, the actual Y/N screen) was
still unported.

Full disassembly of 0B51-0C14 (prior sessions had only ever cited individual
addresses, never the complete instruction stream) confirms the already-known
mechanics and finds three details not previously documented:

- The exit test fires on either BRAKE (0x10) or FIRE (0x08), not fire alone.
- LEFT beats RIGHT when both are held (the RIGHT test is unreachable code on
  a tick where LEFT is also held).
- [0x108B] here is the picking player's own reader alone, not P1|P2's OR'd
  byte -- 09E0 (read in full this session) never writes [0x1080] itself, so
  it stays at whatever single reader block its caller set up per-player,
  the same convention charSelectStep already uses. The eventual wiring
  commit must feed handicapStep only the picking player's own bits.

Also settled: the per-character answer cells (DS:0x1D6-0x1D8) have no reset
site anywhere in the binary -- 0B51 is their only reference, confirmed via
search_byte_patterns -- so an answer is session-scoped, the same shape as
the lifetime win/loss counters.

Ported as handicapInitialState/handicapStep in charSelect.js, alongside the
already-ported handicapQuestionApplies. Confirms, byte-exact, the
already-live-proven no-release-wait quirk: unlike charSelectStep's own
AWAIT_RELEASE, this screen has no entry debounce at all, so a fire (or now
also brake) already held from the carousel's own commit press resolves the
question instantly. Not ported: the roster-word-bit-7 merge (no two-human
H2H roster-word storage exists yet) and the screen's own pixel draw, both
flow.js/screens.js concerns for the wiring commit.

tools/check-charselect.mjs gained 7 new blocks (43 assertions, up from 31),
reintroduction-proven with four mutations (1/43, 1/43, 1/43, 7/43 failures).
Full 30-script regression suite and build re-run clean.

events.title: 256E ported (state), DS:0002 resolved, roster-taken/pose-select questions closed (M3.66)
events.message:
256E ported (state), DS:0002 resolved, roster-taken/pose-select questions closed (M3.66)

Full disassembly of 256E-26BF, 0DB0-0E01, 17FF, 11D5, 216C-2192,
InitLoadAssets/049C/053A/04B8/240A, and 1FAF's own tail, plus DS:0002's own
13 immediate-store sites (get_xrefs_to/search_byte_patterns), closes several
open questions from GOAL-DOS-PARITY.md P4.

256E (the WINNER!/LOSER! results state) normalizes the winner/loser polarity
from [0x3FC] (the direct H2H decision site, not [26B8]), slides both round
icons a fixed 22 ticks at every smoothness, blinks each portrait through
0DB0's own bank/frame resolver (FCHAPPY/FCSAD, a shared 5-bit rotation), and
waits for dismissal through 17FF's own bounded two-phase wait -- ONE 20-tick
budget shared across both phases, not reset at the phase transition, with
the tick counter incrementing before either exit check. Ported as
RACE_RESULT_SLIDE_TICKS and raceResultWaitStep/raceResultWaitInitialState.

The winner/loser portrait pose-select tag looked at first like it could
persist stale across races, but reading 240A (DrawH2HWinRecordDigits) in
full -- not just its own late [0x8A5] gate -- shows it unconditionally
clears that tag before every real screen that reads it (get_xrefs_to:
3/3 matching call pairs), so the concern doesn't reach a real read. Bit 6
of the same field is closed too: its only writer is the Challenge-only
elimination screen, and 0EBA/09E0 guarantee no leftover survives into H2H.

DS:0002 is not a from-boot free-running counter (GOAL-DOS-PARITY.md P4's own
assumption) -- 11 of its 13 immediate-store sites reset it to 0 on entry to
a wait-for-input screen; the other 2 (ShowChampionScreenTune3,
ShowRaceOutcomeMessageTune8or6) seed a nonzero value that forces those
screens' own separate inline blink loops to toggle immediately, then behave
like every other site. It's a shared "ticks since this wait began"
primitive, not a boot clock -- v's real source is raceResultWaitStep's own
tick count at the instant of dismissal, preserving the goal file's intended
human-timing non-determinism. 17FF itself turns out to have 8 real call
sites across 5 functions, not just 256E and the one other site read this
session; the remaining callers are flagged as a lead, not read yet.

Also closes the roster-taken question (09E0 marks/releases a "taken" bit on
the roster byte, so P2 cannot pick P1's character) and forward-corrects
citations in already-committed text (M3.62-M3.65) that read a function only
down to its own late gate instead of from its entry, which had produced a
wrong "gated off" characterization of 240A.

discriminating test for the shared-vs-per-phase tick budget and a
tick-ordering test for the increment-before-check order; four
reintroduction-proven mutations (18/133, 6/133, 1/133, 1/133 failures).

mirror as RESTORED_BANK, but only through OracleHooks on the call-site path; each
strategy's direct-site hooks kept isLiveBankMirror's default false, so the same

- BankAnnotationAdapter.setBookmarkClearingOther: setBookmark only replaces a
  SAME-type bookmark, so a site that warned in an early round (mirrors not yet

project.status: active
project.notes: Independent reproducible disassemblies of six ZX Spectrum games: Atic Atac, Manic Miner, Fairlight, Knight Lore, The Hobbit and Ant Attack. Build scripts take user-supplied original media, generate commented/source-level-debuggable disassemblies and snapshots, and verify reassembly against the original bytes. Ant Attack is documented as 100% covered (41,984/41,984 bytes), with every routine named and every instruction but three observed to execute; its build reassembles byte-for-byte. The Hobbit also has an optional verified-source fast-draw patch whose 22 pictures are compared against the original run with whole-memory equality checks.

events.title: Rename Links to Resources and render its entries as cards
events.message:
Rename Links to Resources and render its entries as cards

/resources is canonical again; /links, /links.html and #links now
redirect to it, reversing the earlier direction.

Each list item becomes a half-width card (one column under 600px)
whose whole area follows the main link; secondary links are folded into
the caption and stay clickable above the overlay.  build-site.mjs moves
an item's image or blockquote to the top of the card.  The intro prose
is gone; section headings stay.

Quotes are verbatim from each linked page (Wayback captures where the
live page refused).  Pictures reuse the box front and two of our own
screenshots.

events.title: feat(app): let a v6 host override the live input line (SQ-1567)
events.message:
feat(app): let a v6 host override the live input line (SQ-1567)

Addendum found while integrating SQ-1567 against 5844eb4d: a host that owns
its own input line had no way to keep its draft out of a v6 composite
without blanking state.input.value around every call.

V6FrameInputs gains `input: Option<&'a str>`, the single override
compose_v6_frame applies to BOTH the story prose box's live line and a
secondary panel's echo (panel_input is now derived from it), so the two
cannot disagree about the host's draft. `Some(text)` draws exactly `text`
with the caret one glyph past it; `None` draws neither text nor caret,
pairing with RecordOnly's existing caret-painting suppression. from_state
defaults this to Some(&state.input.value), so the TUI's own behaviour is
unchanged; for_model takes it explicitly, since a host composing without a
render has no AppState::input of its own.

Two new v6_headless_compose cases cover both ends: None suppresses the live
line and caret regardless of what the prose callback asked for, and
Some(text) draws exactly that text with the caret positioned after it.

Completes: SQ-1567

events.title: Live DOSBox pass: raceInfoSlideTicks proven exact, handicap link resolved (M3.65)
events.message:
Live DOSBox pass: raceInfoSlideTicks proven exact, handicap link resolved (M3.65)

Pure live-verification pass against the still-live DOSBox instance,
checking two of §9bj's own predictions. No new port.

Two automation pitfalls hit and fixed, both new PLAN.md pitfalls:
mcp__dosbox__input_key with pressed:true is a tap, not a hold, so an
initial responsiveness check falsely read as broken input; separately,
0B51's own poll loop shares the character carousel's own fire bit with
no release-wait, so holding fire through a carousel commit silently
swallows the handicap screen with no visible trace.

Once fixed, a live walkthrough (WALTER answered YES, MIKE answered NO)
resolves UNKNOWN_handicap_rosterword_link end to end: 09E0 calls 0B51
unconditionally per car-0/car-1 commit, and OR's its return value
directly into the roster word, setting bit 7 of the low byte on YES --
the exact bit altTuningFieldsFor's own 3F3B path already tests.

raceInfoSlideTicks confirmed exact via execute breakpoints: DS:0002
advanced by precisely 23 ticks (963->986) at smoothness 1, matching
the formula exactly; the resting X positions (92/132) matched the
hand-derived table exactly too.

Session left mid-race again for a future pass to finish and capture
256E. Neither GOAL-DOS-PARITY.md checkbox changes -- P4's remaining
scope is screens/flow wiring, unchanged from M3.64.

events.title: feat(app): TextFace::glyph_image and repertoire expose the raster path's exact glyphs (SQ-1569)
events.message:
feat(app): TextFace::glyph_image and repertoire expose the raster path's exact glyphs (SQ-1569)

A host drawing v6 text with its own font machinery needs the pixels
`render::bitfont::blit_glyph_styled` paints, which come out of a chain of
decisions (release/system face at its text scale, the fixed-pitch alternate,
misc7x14 at a 7-wide cell, vga16, the 8x8 masters and their tiling columns,
synthesised bold/italic or the machine's emphasis rule). It could blit into a
scratch canvas but had to guess the cell, and could not enumerate what the
chain draws: the tables are private statics.

`blit_glyph_styled`'s body moves unchanged into a private `blit_glyph_chain`
that also answers what it drew — `Some(footprint width)` when a table carried
the glyph, `None` for a blank cell — computed from the same Options that pick
the pixels; `blit_glyph_styled` is a one-line wrapper, so production pixels do
not move. `TextFace::glyph_image(ch, style)` calls that chain in the declared
cell (as every v6 composite does) and reads the ink back as a `GlyphImage`
(advance = `advance_styled`, width = painted footprint, MSB-left bits, rows
byte-padded). `TextFace::repertoire()` takes the face's codes (body and
alternate), misc7x14, vga16 and the 8x8 chain (font8x8 BASIC/LATIN/BOX/BLOCK
plus EXTRA_GLYPHS) and keeps what the chain actually finds in some style.

New suite `v6_glyph_image` (engines group): for Arthur's Amiga char.data, FONT
524 alone and under a synthetic System face, the real Zork Zero FONT 524,
Kickstart topaz 8 at (1, 2), and cell_only 8x16/7x15 — all sixteen style
bytes, transparent and on a painted page — stamping glyph_image at the pen
reproduces blit_glyph_styled's canvas pixel for pixel, every advance equals
advance_styled, and repertoire equals exactly the set glyph_image draws.
Falsified by blitting glyph_image in style 0 (all six faces fail at bold) and
by dropping EXTRA_GLYPHS from the candidates (repertoire check fails).

Completes: SQ-1569

events.title: fix(app): derive a v6 frame's machine page pair from the screen model (SQ-1566)
events.message:
fix(app): derive a v6 frame's machine page pair from the screen model (SQ-1566)

`V6FrameInputs::from_state` took the machine's own screen pair (ZMSD §8.3's
Amiga white on grey, SQ-0740) from `AppState::v6_page_pair`, a cell only
`render_story_pane` writes. A host composing through `compose_v6_frame`
without ever rendering to the terminal therefore composed Journey's Amiga
frame on its own default pair.

The rule that fills the cell is now `screen::v6_machine_pair(model, honor)`
(Layered root, colours honoured, concrete model bg), and
`render_story_pane_frame` publishes the cell by calling it. The new host
entry point `V6FrameInputs::for_model(state, model, paint, prose)` derives the
pair from the model itself; `from_state` is unchanged for the TUI.

`v6_headless_compose` gains `Journey - The Quest Begins.adf` (r30 / 890322,
booted as Amiga off Adf, 320x200, art 2x2, cell 8x16): 6 taps, a host
save/restore into a fresh boot, one more move, then a `for_model` composite
that never touches the cell matches `build_v6_raster_canvas` pixel for pixel
in both honour modes. A separate case pins that `render_story_pane` publishes
exactly `v6_machine_pair` on that frame. Zork Zero r393 and Journey r83 have no
machine pair and compose identically. Falsified by making `for_model` read the
cell: 199612 pixels differ with colours honoured.

Completes: SQ-1566

events.title: feat(app): deliver a v6 mouse click from any host (SQ-1568)
events.message:
feat(app): deliver a v6 mouse click from any host (SQ-1568)

The rule for what a v6 click does lived only in the terminal binary's run
loop. It is now `app::host::input::deliver_v6_click`: which read takes a
click (`input::v6_click_read`), `set_mouse(y, x)`, ZSCII 254 for a char
read or the click as a line terminator, the echoed compass direction
adopted as the turn's command, then `apply_game_driven_result` or
`finish_command_turn`. `None` when the pending read takes no click. The
per-session turn facts travel as `host::turn::TurnCtx`.

`RasterFrame::game_px` maps a 0-based canvas pixel to the game's 1-based
pixel, refusing an extended frame's added rows and anything past the native
width; `V6ClickMap::map_click`'s proportional inverse now goes through the
same per-axis rule. The TUI's press/drag/release gesture is unchanged and
calls `deliver_v6_click` on an unmoved release.

Completes: SQ-1568

events.title: feat(app): a v6 composite reports its story box, page, caret and run sources (SQ-1567)
events.message:
feat(app): a v6 composite reports its story box, page, caret and run sources (SQ-1567)

A host drawing a v6 frame's text itself (`V6TextMode::RecordOnly`) needs the
facts the composite already computed and threw away:

- `V6Frame::story` — the prose box the transcript callback was asked to fill,
  native px with extension rows included, and the (cols, rows) grid it was
  called with; `None` wherever no prose was asked for.
- `V6Frame::page` — the colour the canvas was flattened onto.
- `V6Frame::caret` — where the input caret went. Both caret sites (story prose
  and a secondary panel reading input) now go through `GlyphSink::caret`,
  which reports it in every mode and paints it in every mode but RecordOnly,
  on the same gate `GlyphSink::blit` images a glyph by. Under RecordOnly the
  host's art no longer changes on every keystroke; Rasterise is unchanged.
  When both carets are live the panel's wins, since it exists only when the
  game reads through that panel.
- `V6TextRun::source` (`V6RunSource`): Chrome (a grid's pixel-positioned
  runs), GridCell (column-addressed grid cells), Panel, StoryProse,
  StoryCanvas, Pager. Runs of different sources never join.

v6_headless_compose pins each fact on Zork Zero r393 and Journey r83 in both
honor_game_colours modes; `record_only_images_no_glyph_...` now also allows
the reported caret cell, which is the intended change. An in-crate sink case
covers the caret rule on CI.

Completes: SQ-1567

events.message:
grm-ic5.1: a curated prg_mode hint is a known layout mode -- suppress the other modes' overlays

DescriptorSupport.gameHintedLayoutMode returns a game descriptor's hint for the
board's layout mode field (null whenever applyGameInitialStateHint would refuse
it); NesRomLoader lets it win over scanImageMode for liveMode, so planWindows
drops the other modes' overlay blocks, as its javadoc already claimed.

Re-blessed drmario, tetris (38 -> 12 blocks, removals only) and rcproam
(14 -> 6 blocks). rcproam is a 32 KiB cart, so its M3 overlays were byte copies
of base: 4826 duplicate overlay instructions go away; follow-ups grm-yjiq
(helper now named caseD_1d) and grm-6ild (prg_bank=0? precision).

web: SMS / Game Gear tile sheet, like the Genesis one

The convert result now carries the SMS/GG tiles and tilemap in the same
fields the Genesis tile diagnostic uses (genesisTileBytes /

tile with the palette of the first cell that uses it, 16 per row at 2x,
under the preview.  The tile stats line shows the 448-tile VRAM budget

events.title: native-par: fixed-buffer modes fit a small source to the buffer
events.message:
native-par: fixed-buffer modes fit a small source to the buffer

With --native-par and no explicit size, the target width was
min(buffer width, source width) unless the mode was flagged hires, so
any source narrower than the buffer stayed at its own size inside black
bars on all four sides.  cpc-mode2 (640x200, not flagged hires) hit it
for every source under 640 px: a 540x360 photo came out 540x180 in the
middle of the buffer.  TED, Thomson, GBA, SMS/GG and the other CPC modes
did the same for sources smaller than their buffers; the Atari/CGA/EGA
640-wide modes escaped only because they are flagged hires.

A fixed-buffer mode now always takes the full buffer width and then
letterboxes or pillarboxes as before, in both the CLI (main.cpp) and the
API/web path (api.cpp).  Amiga lores keeps its don't-upscale rule.

ctest native-par-small-source-{cpc-mode2,cpc-mode1,stf-med}: photo.jpg
must come out 600x200, 300x200 and 640x178.  Full suite passes.

events.title: Add Sega Master System / Game Gear and Amstrad CPC output modes (#14)
events.message:
Add Sega Master System / Game Gear and Amstrad CPC output modes (#14)

New fixed-buffer modes:
  sms-mode4        256x192, VDP mode 4, 2 x 16 of 64 (RGB222), <= 448 tiles
  gg-mode4         160x144, VDP mode 4, 2 x 16 of 4096 (RGB444)
  cpc-mode0/1/2    160/320/640 x 200, 16/4/2 inks of the 27-color palette
  cpc-plus-mode0/1/2  same, 4096-color RGB444 ASIC palette

SMS/GG (src/sms.*): genesis::cluster_tiles (K=2) -> per-cluster palette
(ega_histogram; RGB222 is the EGA gamut, OCS brute-force for RGB444) ->
dither::diffuse_cells_mirrored -> genesis::dedup_tiles (H/V flips) ->
tile_merge::merge_to_budget + Lloyd refit (single-palette slots) -> planar
tiles, u16 tilemap (bit 9/10 flips, bit 11 palette), CRAM. Preview decoded
from the packed data. Output: PNG, devkitSMS .h, .bin (tiles ++ tilemap ++
CRAM).

CPC (src/cpc.*): 16 KB &C000 screen, pen bit order and hardware color
numbers from MAME amstrad_m.cpp. Inks via gamut_histogram (16) or an
exhaustive C(27,K) search scored on a dithered proxy (K <= 4); Plus via OCS
brute-force. Output: PNG, .h (screen + firmware/hardware inks or Plus
0x0GRB words + ASIC bytes), .bin, AMSDOS .scr, companion .pal.

Shared pieces extracted (byte-identical output for Genesis, SNES Mode 7,
EGA verified against main):
  dither::diffuse_cells_mirrored  per-cell mirrored ED (was inline in the
                                   Genesis branch)
  tile_merge::merge_to_budget      greedy merger (was inline in the SNES
                                   Mode 7 packer)
  quantize::gamut_histogram        EGA histogram picker over any gamut
  genesis::cluster_tiles           tile k-means with a palette count

Gates: --depth/--chipset no-ops, lock/pin/palette/reserve, copper/strips/
dpf, --best, .iff and viewer outputs rejected. Web: sms/cpc/cpcplus
chipsets, preview scales, PAR, export buttons (convertScr binding).
Tests: smoke outputs + sizes/AMSDOS checks, rejections, and a bit-exact
decode round-trip per mode (tools/check_sms_cpc_roundtrip.py).

events.title: fix(gvm,app): carry a graphics split's pixel-exact footprint to the canvas (SQ-1565)
events.message:
fix(gvm,app): carry a graphics split's pixel-exact footprint to the canvas (SQ-1565)

A fixed/proportional graphics split's pixel-exact footprint
(gvm's `window_pixel_size`) previously stopped at cell-rounding in
`Windows::relayout` — the game got the exact pixels back via
`glk_window_get_size`, but nothing carried that fact onward. The app's
graphics-window canvas was allocated `cells × char_px`, so Kerkerkruip's
2-3px coloured title rules got a canvas rounded up to a whole 16px cell
row/column instead of their true pixel size.

gvm's `WinTree::Pair` now carries `split_px: Option<u32>` alongside the
existing cell-based `split`, computed via the already-public
`Model::window_pixel_size` when the first child is a graphics window.
`engine::Split` gains the matching `fixed_px` field, copied in
`AppGlk::convert_tree`. `AppGlk::canvas_size` uses it (via a new
`graphics_split_px` lookup into `layout_tree`) in place of the
cell-rounded figure on the split axis; the resize this drives moved from
`window_layout` to `window_tree` so it always sees the freshly-set tree.
The TUI's own cell-based layout math is unchanged — this is additive.

Verified against the real Kerkerkruip.gblorb fixture: every one of its
seven thin title-rule/divider graphics windows now reports and allocates
its exact pixel footprint (1-7px) instead of the rounded-up 13/29px cell.
Falsified by temporarily reverting the canvas_size override and confirming
the new tests fail with the original symptom (a 240x16 canvas instead of
240x2).

Completes: SQ-1565

events.message:
docs: the genuine MACRO-80 and LINK-80 build these too; stale notes

- README: the 4k8k/ tree listed mbasic_521's files; show them under
  mbasic_521/, and show 4k8k/ and mystery_8k/ as they are. Name the
  other variants' build scripts. A new section says that MACRO-80 and
  LINK-80 3.44 (under a CP/M emulator) build mbasic_521, both 4K BASIC
  sources and 8K BASIC byte for byte, that the .REL files of M80 and
  um80 mix, and what to know: CR LF line endings for M80 (given LF
  only, it assembles nothing and warns only "%No END statement"),
  six-character names, L80 does not clear DS space (the last seven
  bytes of mbasic_521, 5FF9-5FFF, and the 7 bytes after 4K BASIC),
  /P:0 for the Altair ROMs, whole 128-byte records, and why mbasicz
  builds only with um80.
- mbasic_521, 4k and 8k READMEs: the same, for each.
- 4k/README.md said that only 4kbas40_new.mac builds byte-exact; both
  do. Say that build_4k.sh builds 4kbas40_new.mac, and how to build the
  annotated 4kbas40.mac.
- 4k/build_4k.sh said that 4kbas40.mac does not build to an exact
  match, and its header described build_4k_hack.sh (--regenerate,
  disassembly, fix_overlaps.py). Describe what it does. The header of
  build_4k_hack.sh named build_4k.sh; name it, and say that it
  overwrites 4kbas40.mac.
- 4k/.claude/CLAUDE.md said that build_4k.sh builds 4kbas40.mac. It
  builds 4kbas40_new.mac. Warn that build_4k_hack.sh overwrites
  4kbas40.mac.
- 4k/WORK_IN_PROGRESS.txt said that 4kbas40.mac does not match. It
  does (it has since ad3c4be, before the file was added); mark the
  notes as history, and compare only 3833 bytes in its commands.
- 4k/fix_overlaps.py said that um80 does not support DC. um80 has set
  the high bit as M80 does since 0.3.7 (4kbas40_new.mac uses DC), and
  the script converts only the DC 'IN' keyword.

events.title: feat(app): layer_layout carries a connector's folded Up/Down/In/Out directions (SQ-1562)
events.message:
feat(app): layer_layout carries a connector's folded Up/Down/In/Out directions (SQ-1562)

A room pair joined by both a compass passage and an Up/Down one draws only the
compass line; `select_shared_paths` folds the other onto it as
`RoutedConnector::secondary_exit`/`secondary_entry`, and the SVG export badges it
(SQ-1368) — but `LayoutConnector` (SQ-1540) never carried the fact, so a host
reading `layer_layout`'s data lost the passage entirely. Zork I's Canyon
View<->Rocky Ledge is one of eight such pairs in a fully explored map.

`LayoutConnector` gains `secondary_exit`/`secondary_entry: Vec<Direction>`,
filled from the same router fields and left empty for a merge stub (mirroring
`render_svg_body`'s own `!conn.merge` guard on the same data). Purely additive:
the SVG's own rendered output and portal-marker suppression are unchanged.

events.title: fix(app): command bar strips every game prompt shape before a line read (SQ-1564)
events.message:
fix(app): command bar strips every game prompt shape before a line read (SQ-1564)

In command-bar mode the host echoes `> cmd` on its own line, but
strip_read_prompt only removed a single `>` alone on its line, so most
games left their own prompt sitting above the echo. The strip now also
removes:

- a RUN of `>` alone on its line (Bureaucracy r116's `\n>>`), and
- before a LINE read only, a trailing `>` run closing a sentence: the
  character before it (allowing one space) is one of ? . ! : ] )
  (Beyond Zork r57 `[Please type YES or NO.] >`, Bronze `…before? >`,
  Counterfeit Monkey r11 `Can you hear me? >>`, Fairest / What Heart
  Heard `…the game?>`).

A `>` straight after a word (`Go east, then go >`) is still ambiguous
and kept, as the existing strip_prompt_does_not_remove_gt_mid_line pins.
Before a read_char the after-text rule does not apply: the command bar
draws no prompt there and the host echoes nothing, so the game's `>` is
the player's only cue (Border Zone r9's `…(R)estore? >`, Nameless's BBS
`Q>>`). The drain sites pass the pending read kind via the new
strip_read_prompt_for.

ends_with_read_prompt keeps its exact old meaning (a single `>` alone on
its line) and no longer derives from the strip: Glulx's silent LOOK
(SQ-1293) relies on it to tell a parser prompt from a question, and the
widened strip would have typed LOOK into Fairest's yes/no question.

Inline-prompt mode is untouched: strip_prompt is only on when

events.title: fix(app): a launch-time honor_game_colours override survives boot's own reload (SQ-1563)
events.message:
fix(app): a launch-time honor_game_colours override survives boot's own reload (SQ-1563)

boot_story applied LaunchOverrides.honor_game_colours (the launch-options
dialog's per-launch "Game colours" choice, SQ-1532) to cfg, then called
reload::reload_style before returning — which recomputes the honour key from
only the per-game sidecar, garglk.ini and the global base, none of which know
about a choice that never touched disk, so it silently overwrote the
override before the player's first frame. Every later reload (a live
/reload-style, the style watcher, …) repeated the same overwrite.

reload_style already has a hold for exactly this shape of fact —
state.game_colours_cli, which the --game-colours CLI flag rides and which
already outranks the sidecar/garglk sources the same way the dialog's choice
is documented to. Folding overrides.honor_game_colours into that hold at
boot fixes it for every subsequent reload, and host::settings::apply's
existing "editing the row ends the hold" bookkeeping (SQ-1559) already
handles it identically to the CLI-flag case with no further changes needed.

Completes: SQ-1563

events.title: mbasic_521: rename fbufp27 to fbup27, like fbup33 and fbup34
events.message:
mbasic_521: rename fbufp27 to fbup27, like fbup33 and fbup34

bintrp.mac declares `public fbufp27', and f4.mac uses it. MACRO-80
keeps six characters of a name, and writes FBUFP2 to the .REL file;
um80 writes the whole name. The link is right when bintrp and f4
come from the same assembler, but a .REL of one from M80 and of the
other from um80 does not link: LINK-80 reports "1 Undefined
Global(s)" and leaves the references at 2CF2H and 2E89H zero, and
ul80 stops. fbufp33, fbufp34 and filnm12 were renamed for the same
reason in 6cbfb25.

fbup27 is unique within six characters in all 14 modules. Every
PUBLIC and EXTRN name in mbasic_521 now has six characters or fewer,
so the .REL files from M80 and um80 mix without um80 -t. The binary
is unchanged.

events.title: 4k: build scripts compare only the length of 4kbas40.bin
events.message:
4k: build scripts compare only the length of 4kbas40.bin

ul80 pads its output with zeros to a whole 128-byte CP/M record, as
LINK-80 writes whole records; it has done so since um80 0.3.18. 4K
BASIC is 3833 bytes, so the file ul80 writes is 3840 bytes, and
build_4k.sh and build_4k_hack.sh reported "Output differs" for an
image that is byte for byte the original. Compare the first 3833
bytes. This is `head -c | cmp', not `cmp -n': the macOS cmp reports
"EOF on 4kbas40.bin" when the files differ in length, even within the
-n limit. build_8k.sh needs no change: 8192 bytes is a whole number
of records.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LvvZEtwVuhHsVFcrJjB72Q
events.author: Aaron Wohl

events.title: 4k, 8k: write the '>' and '<' keywords with db, not rdc
events.message:
4k, 8k: write the '>' and '<' keywords with db, not rdc

The rdc macro passes its argument to `irpc ch,<str>'. For the '>'
keyword, `rdc <!>>' gives `irpc ch,<>>'. MACRO-80 ends the list at
the '>' that matches the '<', so the list is empty and the keyword
byte is not assembled; in 8K BASIC every address after the keyword
table then moves by one byte. `rdc <!<>' gives `irpc ch,<<>', which
M80 reads as '<' and '>' and flags Q. These sources built the
historic binaries only because um80 up to 0.3.49 read the list
differently from M80; the um80 that reads the list as M80 does gives
3 wrong bytes for 4kbas40.mac and 6645 for 8kbas_src.mac.

Write the two keywords as `db '>'+80h' and `db '<'+80h', as
8kbas_src.mac already writes '<'. The other rdc arguments (and there
are no other irpc or irp in the tree) have no '<' or '>' in them.

The binaries are unchanged, and now build byte for byte with um80,
and with the genuine MACRO-80 and LINK-80 too.

events.title: iff: web IFF export sets HIRES and LACE in CAMG (#13)
events.message:
iff: web IFF export sets HIRES and LACE in CAMG (#13)

api::convert_iff, the path the web app's IFF export takes, never set
IffOptions::hires (nor has_transparency), so a hires or ham6-hires
conversion saved from png2amiga.app opened on a lores screen in AMOS and
other loaders.  The CLI set it; the API did not.  The transparency mask
export had the same gap for hires.

make_camg also ORs in the mode's own is_hires / is_interlaced, so a
caller that passes only the mode still gets the right viewport bits.

iff_camg_check (ctest iff-camg-web-export) converts through
api::convert_iff for lores, lores-lace, hires, hires-lace, ham6,
ham6-hires, ham6-hires-lace and ehb-lace and checks HIRES, LACE and HAM
in CAMG.  Without the api.cpp fix, ham6-hires and ham6-hires-lace fail.

events.title: mbasicz: message strings are db, not dc, as in mbasic_521
events.message:
mbasicz: message strings are db, not dc, as in mbasic_521

DC sets the high bit of a string's last character, as MACRO-80 does.
um80 up to 0.3.6 assembled DC as DB, so these twelve messages built
right; since um80 0.3.7 each one ends with a high-bit byte, and
mbasicz no longer matched MBASIC 5.21 (for example "Ok" at 0C46H).
The historic binary has no high bits in them, and mbasic_521 has used
db for the same strings since 1ba49ad.

The binary is unchanged: out/mbasicz.com is again byte for byte
com/mbasic.com.

ResetTournamentState (0EBA-0F16), RunHeadToHeadChooseGameMenu

character-select and CHOOSE-GAME-menu state machines need no new

pointer-swap (charSelectStep's own `input` parameter already supports

JLE reading from reaches-or-exceeds by a direct reintroduction test.

events.title: feat(app): host::settings — apply a changed config to a running session (SQ-1559)
events.message:
feat(app): host::settings — apply a changed config to a running session (SQ-1559)

The settings screen's Save applied a config to the live game in two
places no other host could reach: `Action::ConfigSave`'s arm in input.rs
(the config, the `_base` values, the SQ-0860 one-run holds, the sound
sink, the status-bar / room-number mirrors) and a tail in main.rs's run
loop (write config.toml, re-strip the prompt, reload_style after the
write). A non-terminal host letting a player edit config.toml mid-game
had to copy both, field by field, and drift the next time a base or a
hold was added.

Both halves now live in `host::settings`: `apply(state, working,
per_game) -> Applied` is the AppState half verbatim, plus an optional
PerGameConfig layered back over the top with host::boot's order and pins
(base lowered from the global first, then the sidecar value pinned);
`commit(state, session, &applied) -> Committed` is the tail — Glulx sound
gestalt, write, prompt strip, borderless relayout, then reload_style —
and reports the write result, the reload outcome and whether borders
changed. The TUI's ConfigSave arm and main.rs both call them; only mouse
capture and the style watcher stay in the binary.

Tests hold the new pair to a frozen transcription of the pre-refactor
path (a64394b5): field-for-field equality of every touched field and of
the written config.toml after flipping honour, guidance, room numbers,
period look and the command bar; the per-game layer reproducing boot's
pinned guidance; and a hold on an untouched key (the pixel lock's pin,
the artwork's honour force-off) surviving the apply.

Completes: SQ-1559

events.title: fix(app): per-game config sidecar preserves keys/tables it doesn't recognise (SQ-1560)
events.message:
fix(app): per-game config sidecar preserves keys/tables it doesn't recognise (SQ-1560)

PerGameConfig::write rebuilt config.toml from scratch out of only its own
known fields, so any other key or table already in the file — including a
host's own settings — was silently dropped on every write, and the file was
deleted outright once no known field was set. Switch to the same read-modify-
write toml_edit approach write_config_at already uses: known keys are set or
removed as before, but unrecognised top-level keys/tables are left exactly as
they were, and the file is now deleted only when nothing at all remains in it.

Also adds an optional read_host_table/write_host_table pair, sharing the same
read-modify-write path, so a host can round-trip one whole table by name
without touching anything else — and documents the "lanthorn ignores unknown
keys, namespace under [host.<name>]" convention on per_game_config_path.

Completes: SQ-1560

events.title: feat(app): resolve_at + BackgroundTidy::key for non-CLI hosts (SQ-1558)
events.message:
feat(app): resolve_at + BackgroundTidy::key for non-CLI hosts (SQ-1558)

A host embedding crates/app without a clap Cli (e.g. a web frontend)
had no way to resolve a Config for a given directory short of faking
argv through Cli::try_parse_from. Split resolve()'s defaults-under-file
merge (plus the --user-dir override/pin) into a shared resolve_config_file
helper, and expose it as resolve_at(user_dir) — equivalent to resolve()
given a Cli whose only flag is --user-dir. resolve() itself becomes a
thin wrapper that layers the remaining CLI-flag overrides on top.

Also give BackgroundTidy a public key()/from_key() pair, matching the
v6_render_key/kitty_shared_memory_key convention already in this file,
so a host can read/write the config-file spelling without a TOML round
trip. write_config_at now calls cfg.background_tidy.key() instead of
duplicating the match inline.

events.title: P4 engine refactor, step 3 of 4: twoHuman.js, two-human H2H's tournament state (M3.62)
events.message:
P4 engine refactor, step 3 of 4: twoHuman.js, two-human H2H's tournament state (M3.62)

New pure-state module (src/frontend/twoHuman.js), matching tournament.js/
elimination.js's own architecture: track pick with no repeats (nextTrack,
H2H_TRACK_TABLE/DS:09BA), win tally + first-to-4 champion detection
(reportRace, [0x98A]/[0x98C]), per-character lifetime win/loss stats, and the
skill-label formula (skillLabel). RunHeadToHeadTournament 1000:1FAF's real
body disassembled (1FAF-2098; 2099 on is the separate, confirmed-dead
ShowHeadToHeadResultUnreferenced) -- it runs the race itself via 216C, then
256E for the post-race WINNER!/LOSER!/tally screen.

Two real findings along the way: the lifetime WON/LOST counters are genuinely
live (a second increment site inside 256E itself, not just the dead
function's own), and have no reset site anywhere this session's own
exhaustive sweep found -- unlike the win tally, which resets every
RunHeadToHeadChooseGameMenu entry. Since the two have different lifetimes,
state is split into twoHumanSessionState() (lifetime counters, created once)
and twoHumanMatchState(session) (everything else, created fresh per match).

H2H_TRACK_TABLE/H2H_SKILL_INDEX_TABLE/H2H_SKILL_LABELS moved into
data/frontend-tables.js per the project's established data-table convention,
checked byte-exact against MICROU.EXE by check-tables.mjs, and confirmed live
via DOSBox mem_read on the same running session as M3.61's own capture.

docs/engine.md §9bh. Tests: tools/check-twohuman.mjs (46 assertions,
reintroduction-proven for all four mechanisms). Step 3 of 4 for P4's first
checklist item; screens/flow wiring remains, its own commit.

events.title: feat(app): save rename, text-only launch override, Blorb frontispiece flag (SQ-1556)
events.message:
feat(app): save rename, text-only launch override, Blorb frontispiece flag (SQ-1556)

Three small library-level APIs for a non-terminal host:

- persist_files::rename_save / archive::rename_archive: rename a Save
  State's display name and, when its slug changes, its file — an atomic
  raw-copy rewrite of meta.json that touches no other archive entry.
  Refuses the reserved default slot and an unrelated-save collision.
- LaunchOverrides.images: an explicit "None, text only" choice, offered
  as a real row in the launch-options dialog's art list (always last,
  one past every candidate). Forces cfg.images off for one launch —
  the same gate every engine's picture resolution already reads —
  without touching the per-game sidecar.
- StoryMeta.frontispiece: the Blorb Fspc chunk's declared Pict number,
  read off the same self-blorb parse that already fills self_blorb, so
  a host can tell whether a cover exists before asking for one.

feat(app,verb-synonyms): show truncated dictionary keys as whole words (SQ-1553)

A Version 3 dictionary keeps six Z-characters (ZMSD 1.1 §13.3), v4+ nine
(§13.4), so completion, the command band's VERB column and object rows,
and the vocabulary offer showed `examin`, `lanter`, `brandi`. Matching was
already right; only the display was cut short.

- story_text: read every word a Z-machine story can print, once, from a
  private copy of the image -- a linear decode of high memory (string area
  and inline print/print_ret strings) plus object short names. A call-graph
  walk reaches too little, because Infocom dispatches text through tables.
- Engine::story_text_words (Z-machine only; Glulx/Scott answer None).
- StoryVocabulary::spell: key -> whole word, built in VocabState::get from
  the story text pooled with verb_synonyms::words() as a lexicon.
  Inflections fold to their base; only a unique answer is used; ambiguous
  or unknown keys stay as stored. Keys under 6 chars (Scott Adams) are
  never spelled out.
- Applied at boot's dict_words (completion + ghost), refresh_verbs,
  typeable_name/typeable_words, and spell_out (offers).

Two pinned Zork I offer lines now show the story's own `destroy`/`consume`
asides, which used to be dropped as unspellable fragments.

events.title: feat(app): rank the command band's verbs into core / story / more tiers (SQ-1554)
events.message:
feat(app): rank the command band's verbs into core / story / more tiers (SQ-1554)

The VERB column listed every grammar spelling alphabetically -- 200-odd
rows in Zork I, `take` buried between `swim` and `tell`. The story's
column is now one row per grammar verb, tiered for a player:

- Core: CORE_VERBS (look, examine, take, drop, inventory, open, close,
  put, go, enter, wait, read, push, pull, turn, give, talk, ask, tell)
  intersected with the story's grammar via its own dictionary, shown as
  the curated spelling, in curated order. 18 rows on Zork I / Mini-Zork.
- Story: verbs whose spelling the story's own text uses (SQ-1553's
  text_words) or the player has typed (command_history first words,
  resolved through the dictionary). Alphabetical.
- More: the rest, alphabetical.

VerbEntry gains `tier` and `synonyms`; other spellings fold behind the
row (representative: core word, else the spelling in most verb-synonyms
groups). verb_by_word answers to synonyms; parse_phrase keeps a typed
synonym so the prompt tail still matches. Sigil and adult filters reach
folded synonyms and promote a survivor. extra_verbs keep tier/synonyms.
refresh_verbs re-ranks once per turn_epoch. The tier rides BandData
(SQ-1549) for non-TUI hosts; built-in/configured tables are all Core and
otherwise unchanged. verbs_from_grammar is replaced by story_verbs.

events.title: feat(app,mapper): treat every non-compass exit as a portal, dot the SVG line, drop its arrowhead (SQ-1555)
events.message:
feat(app,mapper): treat every non-compass exit as a portal, dot the SVG line, drop its arrowhead (SQ-1555)

A separate lanthorn-web host session filed this against export_svg.rs: the
map layout/export's own "portal" flag (`is_portal = matches!(exit_dir, Up |
Down)`) was narrower than the mapper's own notion — `mapper::layer::
planar_region` already stops a layer walk at Up/Down/In/Out/Unknown, via
`grid_offset(dir).is_none()`. The two could disagree the moment a direction
other than Up/Down ever needed portal treatment.

1. `mapper::direction::portal_kind(Direction) -> Option<PortalKind>` is the
   new shared predicate — `Some` for exactly the directions `grid_offset`
   has no offset for, `None` for the eight compass directions — with a
   `PortalKind` (Up/Down/In/Out/Other) a host badges by. A new in-crate test
   pins it against `grid_offset` for all thirteen directions. Every
   `matches!(dir, Up | Down [| In | Out])` spot-check in export_svg.rs's
   `is_portal` computation, channel-widening pass, and secondary/stacked
   badge loops now reads `portal_kind(dir).is_some()` instead, so the
   layout, the layer logic, and the renderer share one predicate. In
   practice only Up/Down ever reach a routed `RoutedConnector` (In/Out/
   Unknown never carry a `layout_offset` and so never enter the router's
   working set — they surface as `LayoutPortalMarker`s instead), so this is
   presently a no-op for what actually draws, but it can no longer silently
   drift if that ever changes.

2. `LayoutConnector` gains `exit_kind`/`entry_kind: Option<PortalKind>` —
   the per-END portal family, mirroring `exit_dir`/`entry_dir` — so a host
   can apply the same arrowhead rule this file's own SVG draw pass does
   without re-deriving it from the bare directions.

3. Addendum from the quest owner: a connector END whose direction is a
   portal no longer draws the normal compass arrowhead — only a real
   compass end keeps one. `draw_travel_arrival` (the one function that
   places every arrival marker) drops its `arrowhead_inward` call for a
   portal word, keeping only the lettered badge, and its badge letter is
   now `direction::short_label(word)` generally instead of a hardcoded
   Up/Down `if`. A pure Up/Down passage now carries no arrowhead at either
   end (the badge already says which way); a room pair reached by both a
   compass word one way and a portal word the other routes as two separate
   lines (Up/Down and compass never share a trunk — `route::mod`'s own
   `ch_key`/`back_edge_idx`), and only the compass line's own end keeps its
   head. The existing `.edge.portal{stroke-dasharray:1 3}` stylesheet rule
   (already dotted, already inheriting `.edge`'s `stroke-linecap:round` for
   round dots, distinct from `.edge.conditional`'s `1.5 3.5` and
   `.edge.distorted`'s `5 3`) needed no change — it already applies via the
   same `is_portal` flag this quest widened.

Three existing tests asserted the old SQ-1362 "portal draws a head AND a
badge" behavior and are rewritten for "badge only, no head":
`a_one_way_portal_gets_a_badge_and_no_arrowhead`,
`a_two_way_stairway_draws_two_badges_and_no_arrowheads`, and the ghost-
crossing half of `a_reciprocal_crossing_ghosts_both_panels_naming_the_partner`.
Falsified by temporarily reverting the `arrowhead_inward` removal and
confirming those three fail again.

New tests: `a_mixed_pair_keeps_the_arrowhead_only_at_its_compass_end` (two
connectors between one box pair, compass East one way / portal Up the
other — only the compass end keeps a head); `portal_connectors_render_
dotted_and_compass_connectors_render_solid` (class + stylesheet dash-
distinctness check); `an_in_and_an_out_passage_yield_correctly_kinded_
portal_markers` (`LayoutPortalMarker` + `portal_kind`, since In/Out never
route to a `LayoutConnector`); `layer_layout_exposes_per_end_portal_kind`
(compass-only / pure-portal-reciprocal / one-way-portal `exit_kind`/
`entry_kind` combinations). The pre-existing byte-level
`layer_layout_boxes_and_connectors_match_render_svg_of_exactly` correspondence
test still holds unmodified.

TUI unaffected: `render/map.rs`'s own cell renderer keys off its own local
`is_updown`/`Direction::Up | Direction::Down` checks (portal icons, not
arrowheads, per its own doc comments) and reads none of the changed code.

Tests: cargo nextest run -p lanthorn-mapper (455 passed); cargo nextest run
-p lanthorn --lib --features t-all export_svg (46 passed, including 4 new
cases); cargo nextest run -p lanthorn -E 'binary(mapper_ui)' (319 run, 10
failed — confirmed pre-existing by stashing this change and rerunning the
same 10: identical failures, all "tracked fixture must be present" for
stories/ files this worktree's stories/ symlink doesn't carry, e.g.
minizork-r34-s871124.z3); cargo check --all-targets and cargo clippy -p
lanthorn --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo clippy -p
lanthorn-mapper --all-targets -- -D warnings (all clean).

Completes: SQ-1555

events.title: Review fixes for the palette and sprite work, and no jacket pin
events.message:
Review fixes for the palette and sprite work, and no jacket pin

The inventory icon is put into the background before the sprites are
drawn, not after: copying it onto the visible layer after them wiped
any sprite in that corner for a frame on a change of item. It goes in
without priority marks, so a sprite crossing it keeps the fast path,
and is drawn back on top only when something was drawn over it that
frame - the engine always draws it over everything.

New palette weights no longer force a full requantise on their own;
only turning them on or off does. A room that loads a slot with
another palette number, or the same colours under another, paused
~620ms on its way in instead of taking the patch path. In play the
patch path gives a copied colour - an enemy's half of the object
palette - the slot of the identical colour, and otherwise compares in
CIELAB like the rebuild. The Amiga demo data gets no weights; they
were measured on the full game.

The halves of the object palette a level's enemies use are worked out
from Game::_monsterListLevels rather than a hand-copied list in the
table generator. prioUnder checked one group too many for an aligned
sprite (foreground next to it sent it down the slow blit) and now
scans unrolled, eight rows at a time. The row copies share one
width dispatch (copyRowN, 1-5 groups or a whole row) between the
screen copy and the restore, and the quantiser skips work it did not
need, with identical output.

The jacket pin is gone. Since the weighted palette it only acted on
the title, where entry 0x17 is a title colour: holding it exact cost
the flare its highlights, and measured against the Amiga original the
title's mean colour error is 7.66 without it against 7.91 with.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: feat(app): structured assist offers and per-game quick words (SQ-1552)
events.message:
feat(app): structured assist offers and per-game quick words (SQ-1552)

Give a headless host what it needs instead of parsing the assist text
back apart: `AppState::push_assist` now attaches a structured
`assist::Offer` (kind, unknown word, and per-pick fill command) to
every assist line, readable off `AppState::assist_offer` without
matching `LEAD_DICTIONARY`/`LEAD_VETTED` or re-deriving the unknown
word by reimplementing `vocab::words_of` (now `pub`). Also add a
per-game `quick` override to the style sidecar, read the same way
every other per-game key is (`resolve_quick_for`, per-game wins when
present), so an embedding host can let a player edit quick words per
story and have the choice actually persist through
`PerGameConfig::write`. The TUI's own behavior and its `quick` list
editing are unchanged.

events.title: P4 engine refactor, continued: 3F3B's alternate tuning path, ported and live-proven (M3.61)
events.message:
P4 engine refactor, continued: 3F3B's alternate tuning path, ported and live-proven (M3.61)

Closes M3.60's own prerequisite. race.js gains altTuningFieldsFor and
spawnCars's explicit altTuning/rosterWords options (not inferred from
controllerTypes -- DOS decides by per-race mode), implementing the seven-field
3F3B-3FBD formula derived in M3.60. Default off/empty, full suite unchanged.

A live DOSBox capture (a two-human H2H race found already in progress) proved
the fork itself live (CS:[0x9C62]==DS:[0x8A2]==1, same linear address, read at
a breakpoint on the real 3F30) and all seven formulas for the bit7=0 case --
car 0 and car 1 tuning identical, matching CAR_TYPE_INFO[6]'s own raw row
exactly, with the real roster-word input [5,6,11,11] proving the low 7 bits
are genuinely ignored while bit 7 is clear. It also resolved
UNKNOWN_8a2_meaning: the screen reached after both character picks is
RunHeadToHeadChooseGameMenu (Tournament vs Single Race), not a handicap
question, correcting an earlier draft's own claim within this same session.

docs/engine.md §9bg, PLAN-ENGINE.md M3.61. New open items:
UNKNOWN_handicap_rosterword_link, UNKNOWN_4be7_twocar_rubberband.

events.title: Disassemble Ant Attack from its tape, every routine named and nearly every instruction seen to run
events.message:
Disassemble Ant Attack from its tape, every routine named and nearly every instruction seen to run

scripts/build_antattack.py loads the original Quicksilva tape in SkoolKit's
simulator, plays it to find the code, and disassembles everything the one
tape block loads -- $5C00 to $FFFF, the system variables and the game's own
BASIC included, each BASIC line a block described by its listing and each of
the seventeen scripts a labelled block. The build fails unless all 41984
bytes reassemble byte for byte.

The playthrough is random play plus staged scenes: a rescue, running out of
time, the ending (BASIC's fin set to 1), bites, grenade hits and near misses,
landings on an ant, a wall and each other. Each scene only places things on
the simulated machine; what follows is the game's own code. Between them they
run every instruction but three -- FALL's branch for flag bit 3, which
nothing sets.

scripts/antattack_annotations.ctl names, describes and comments every
routine, and labels every variable and record field the code touches, so the
assembly has no numeric addresses left and skool2asm no warnings.
scripts/antattack.ref and --html add pages on how the game works, the city
(drawn whole with the block picture DRAW_BLOCK itself paints), the levels, the
sprites and the scripts, each script screenshotted as it runs. The pages that
quote the game are generated, not committed.

publish_pages.py takes --game antattack, and the landing page and README list
it. Not done: sound for the scripts.

events.title: docs: BUG-065 — the Binky run, from inside and from outside
events.message:
docs: BUG-065 — the Binky run, from inside and from outside

A run watched live from outside while it happened, then compared against
its own field report. Both halves are in the record because they disagree.

The run reports eleven frictions, all real: a sandbox that says LOAD → RUN
and lands at READY, a CPU-reached wait that never fires on a polling loop,
a length parsed as hex without saying so, no mid-run capture and no
breakpoint step, the shared session occupied by another project, and — the
one that explains the most — a listing that prints bare addresses for
everything outside the image while the names sit in the graph.

It does not report the other half: 103 shell reads of that listing against
5 disasm calls, a foreign disassembler used eight times with a wrapper
built around it, 21 runtime runs with zero steps and a hand-built 6502
tracer, five self-invented annotation writers, and a merge script holding
the judgements as Python literals in a scratchpad that dies with the
session.

Friction is remembered. A detour is not — from the inside it feels like
working.

events.title: P4 engine refactor: car.isDrone reflects controller type, not car index (M3.60)
events.message:
P4 engine refactor: car.isDrone reflects controller type, not car index (M3.60)

spawnCars now derives car.isDrone from an explicit controllerTypes param
(controllerTypes[i]===6, the real [BX+0x12EB] flag), not car index, proven
against every reachable runtime reader (keyboard fire-preempt, round-7 TANKS
steer-mod, collide.js's wall-stuck counter) -- behaviour-neutral for every
existing one-player caller via the unchanged [1,6,6,6] default.

Tracing an adjacent, already-ported mechanism turned up a real inversion:
tuningFieldsFor's own car-index tuning (4070) only runs when a per-race mode
fork (CS:[0x9C62]/DS:[0x8A2]) is 0, and two-human H2H's own entry always
takes the fork's OTHER branch (3F3B) -- an entirely unported, symmetric
per-car tuning computation, now derived formula-by-formula and recorded as a
prerequisite for that mode's first playable race (UNKNOWN_alt_tuning_path).

docs/engine.md §9bf, PLAN-ENGINE.md M3.60. Two new PLAN.md pitfalls from this
session's own research: car-record fields are relative to CAR_RECORD_BASE,
not raw [BX+n]; CS:9C62 and DS:08A2 are the same cell reached by two
different addressing encodings, so a byte-pattern search needs both.

events.title: A busy room at full pace on a plain ST
events.message:
A busy room at full pace on a plain ST

Level 1's room 45 with enemies on screen ran at 20.5fps on an STE and
20.9 on a plain ST. Both now reach 28.3, the same as the Mega STE
(28.5) and the ceiling of the 30Hz pacing, so the room plays no
slower than an empty one.

The inventory icon is drawn into the room's background layer once,
when it changes, instead of being blitted and restored every frame.
A sprite whose rectangle has no foreground in the priority plane
skips the masked path that checks it pixel by pixel. Dirty runs of
2-5 groups are copied to the screen and restored from the background
a row at a time with movem, where the word loop cost ~50 cycles a
group, and the squashed screen modes read each row's screen offset
from a table instead of multiplying.

RS.LOG was costing ~130ms a line: a text-mode write makes MiNTLib
emulate fstat, which converts the file's DOS date through mktime. It
is now opened in binary mode with an explicit CRLF, so the file reads
the same. With logging=true that was a visible hitch whenever
anything logged, and every log_fps average carried one, so fps
figures measured before this read about 5% low.

events.title: Flow Control Macros: Allow pre-increment/decrement in typed compares
events.message:
Flow Control Macros: Allow pre-increment/decrement in typed compares

You can now replace:

    WHILE inc var : u8 var < #kMax

With:

    WHILE u8 ++var < #kMax

This only works as a prefix for the LHS of the expression, and works
for u8, u16/s16, and u24 expressions (although dec24 is NYI)

Note that to ca65, ++var and --var are just the unary positive and
unary negative operators repeated, so effectively no-ops. Therefore
the Flow conditional expression parser will flag those when in
unexpected locations.

Also, added test coverage for u24 expressions.

events.title: feat(import): --expand-gunzip strips one gzip layer; sniff pre-POSIX tars
events.message:
feat(import): --expand-gunzip strips one gzip layer; sniff pre-POSIX tars

`--expand-archives` unpacks a tarball fully. `--expand-gunzip` is the lighter
option: it strips only the gzip layer and keeps what is inside, so
`x.tar.gz` / `x.tgz` land as `x.tar` and `disk.iso.gz` as `disk.iso`. With
both, tarballs are unpacked and only non-tar gzip files are decompressed.
A file named `.gz` that is not gzip is copied through untouched.

The decompressed size is counted by streaming (MultiGzDecoder), not taken
from the trailer's ISIZE, which wraps at 4 GiB; `measure_dir_for` and the
preflight use the same count so `--size auto` sizes to the unpacked tree.

Tar detection also accepts pre-POSIX (v7) headers, which carry no `ustar`
magic and were silently copied in unexpanded: two of NeXT's own 3.3 patch
tarballs are this shape. The fallback requires a name, octal numeric fields
and a matching header checksum.

- `rb-cli import --expand-gunzip`; the CD/HD builders pass `false` for now.
- `ImportStats::gunzipped` counts it; `import` reports it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: feat(partition): build NeXT UFS CD-ROM images, pinned to NeXTSTEP 3.3's own CDs
events.message:
feat(partition): build NeXT UFS CD-ROM images, pinned to NeXTSTEP 3.3's own CDs

A NeXT "ISO" is not ISO 9660: every NeXTSTEP 3.x CISC disc is a dlV3 disk
label in 2048-byte sectors wrapping one 4.3BSD UFS partition. The new
`partition::next_cd_builder` streams that shape from scratch, reusing the
existing label writer and 4.3BSD formatter.

For a disc the size of NeXTTIME.iso, every derived superblock word, the label
header and slot 0 match the reference disc byte for byte; cylinder-group
headers and fs_postbl / fs_rotbl differ only where the reference holds files.

- ufs_format: `Bsd43Geometry` fixes ntrak / nsect / rps / maxcontig / maxbpg
  (preset `NEXT_CDROM`: 32 x 64, 5 rps, 20000, 512); HD behaviour unchanged.
- ufs: `DIRBLKSIZ` on NeXT is the kernel's compile-time 1024, not the media's
  device block. All 3168 directories on the 3.3 CISC CD chunk at 1024, while
  `fsize >> fsbtodb` said 2048, so editing a NeXT CD was writing chunks a NeXT
  kernel would call corrupt. `dir_block_size` caps it for reader + formatter.
- next: `NextPartitionSpec::cpg` (16 on disks, 2 on CDs); boot-block numbers
  are scaled to d_secsize (32/96 at 1024 is 16/48 at 2048).
- Scope: data discs only (no boot blocks); RISC hybrids not produced.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: uaenet: keep the pcap device list intact on a lookup by name (#2351)
events.message:
uaenet: keep the pcap device list intact on a lookup by name (#2351)

uaenet_enumerate(name) cleared nd[] and refilled it with only the named
device. The global ndd[] list from target_ethernet_enumerate() points
into nd[], so its pcap entries lost their names. The next
ethernet_getselectionname() then returned NULL, and a2065_config()'s
ethernet_enumerate(&td, romtype) took the list-all path, writing the
whole device list through &td and over the globals that follow it.

With the A2065 on a pcap interface this corrupted CSR4 (ASTRP_RCV set,
so received frames lost 4 bytes and were dropped by the driver) and
made AddNetInterface fail with an I/O error in about half the runs.

Look up an already enumerated device first, as uaenet_tap_enumerate()
does.

events.title: fix(sana2): give transmit its own scratch buffer (#2350)
events.message:
fix(sana2): give transmit its own scratch buffer (#2350)

createwritepacket() has the guest's CopyFromBuff() copy the outgoing
payload into pdev->tempbuf and then snapshots it into the host packet.
CopyFromBuff() is guest code; while it runs, the receive path can
deliver a packet, and handleread() writes that packet into the same
tempbuf. The outgoing frame then carries received bytes.

Allocate tempbuf at twice its size and use the second half for
transmit only. A write that starts while another one on the same
opener is still copying is refused instead of sharing that half.

events.title: fix(sana2): deliver multicast and stop unread frames stalling receive (#2349)
events.message:
fix(sana2): deliver multicast and stop unread frames stalling receive (#2349)

* fix(sana2): don't let an unread packet hold up the receive queue

uaenet_int_handler2() only looked at the head of the read queue. When
no reader wanted that packet, for example a broadcast of an EtherType
nobody reads, it started the drop timer on every queued packet and
stopped, so packets behind it that did have a reader waited until the
head was dropped DELAYED_DROPPED_PACKET_FRAMES frames later.

Step over a packet that has no reader, keeping it queued with its own
drop timer, so later packets are still delivered.

* fix(sana2): accept multicast frames the guest registered

uaenet_gotdata() dropped every multicast frame unless the unit was
promiscuous, so the multicast filter in handleread(), which checks
frames against the S2_ADDMULTICASTADDRESS ranges, never saw one and
multicast protocols such as mDNS/DNS-SD received nothing.

Admit multicast frames in uaenet_gotdata() and drop those for
addresses nobody registered when the read queue is processed, where
the multicast list is already read. They then neither wait in the
queue nor reach S2_READORPHAN readers.

---------

events.title: fix(uaenet): enable BPF immediate mode on macOS (#2348)
events.message:
fix(uaenet): enable BPF immediate mode on macOS (#2348)

On macOS every BPF write wakes readers sleeping on the same descriptor,
and a buffered read that wakes without timing out sleeps again for a
full new read timeout. The pcap backend transmits and receives on one
handle, so a guest transmitting more often than the 10 ms timeout keeps
received packets buffered until transmission pauses or the buffer fills.

Enable BIOCIMMEDIATE on the capture descriptor before starting the
worker so packets are returned as they arrive. Fail the open if the
ioctl fails, as for pcap_open_live().

Co-authored-by: Dimitris Panokostas <midwan@gmail.com>

events.title: fix(uaenet): give uaenet.device an MTU and a MAC address (#2347)
events.message:
fix(uaenet): give uaenet.device an MTU and a MAC address (#2347)

* fix(uaenet): give uaenet.device an MTU and a MAC address

pcap devices were enumerated with MTU 0 and an all-zero MAC, and TAP
devices with an all-zero MAC. uaenet.device takes both from the
enumerated device. Over pcap, Roadshow could not configure the
interface; over TAP, it configured but nothing reached the network.

Take the pcap MTU from the host interface, capped at 1500 (1500 if it
can't be read), and give pcap and TAP devices a guest MAC derived as in
WinUAE: the locally administered prefix aa:82:8a followed by the low
three bytes of the host interface address. When uaenet_open() is given
no MAC, use the enumerated one, as WinUAE does, so sana2.cpp stays
unchanged.

* uaenet: offset the guest MAC by the IPC instance number

Instances sharing a host interface derive the same guest MAC. The IPC
socket already numbers running instances (0 for amiberry.sock, 1 for
amiberry_1.sock, ...), so expose that number and add it to the low
bytes of the guest MAC. The MAC is set again when uaenet.device opens
the device, in case it was enumerated before the IPC socket existed.

---------

Co-authored-by: RLH <rlh_amiga@protonmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Dimitris Panokostas <midwan@gmail.com>

events.title: An automatic palette measured against the Amiga original
events.message:
An automatic palette measured against the Amiga original

Every room of every level was rendered by the desktop build and the
ST's automatic palette scored against it, colour difference weighted
by pixels. It was far off - background dE 10-24 on most levels - for
two reasons: colours were weighed by how many palette entries shared
them rather than how much of the screen they cover, and compared in
RGB. The jungle's teal, a quarter of every screen, was merged with a
grey and Conrad's trousers into purple, which is also why the
trousers vanished against it; levels 6 and 7 lost their deep blue to
black.

In play the quantiser now compares colours in CIELAB (a table of all
4096 STE colours), weighs each by its average share of the level's
room pixels (a table measured from every room, tools/
gen-palette-tables.py) plus a fixed importance for the object palette,
Conrad's colours and the half of it the level's enemies are drawn
with, and keeps each merged cluster at its heaviest member rather than
an average. Background dE is now 0.7-3.4 and Conrad 0-3.2; the rooms
look like the original. Per-level palettes fitted offline by hand were
no better, so nothing is shipped but the weights. The title and the
cutscenes keep the old rule.

A colour no room shows is floored at weight 1, or it would merge at
no cost with the first colour in the list rather than the nearest.
Conrad's weight replaces the jacket pin in play; the pin was on the
wrong slot for most levels anyway (0x17, where Conrad draws from
0x47). And a merge no longer recomputes the nearest partner of every
colour pointing at a survivor that did not move: pixel weights point
most colours at the same few heavy ones, and that had made the
rebuild twice as slow. A full rebuild at a level start or a change of
room palettes takes about 620ms on a plain ST, against 540ms before.

On the Amiga data an enemy has no palette of its own: its slot is
loaded with half of the object palette. The README lists what each
of the 32 Amiga colours is used for, for custom palettes.

feat(libretro): add on-screen keyboard overlay with software rendering (#2352)

* feat(libretro): add on-screen keyboard overlay with software rendering

The libretro core previously shipped the OSK as a no-op stub, so
gamepad-only users could not type into the Amiga under a frontend.
This renders the OSK into the frame presented to video_cb (no ImGui
in the core) and routes its input through gameplay/OSK ownership
tracking, so controls held while the keyboard opens keep their
gameplay releases and OSK-held controls are discarded on close
instead of leaking into gameplay mappings.

- Software-rasterized OSK with an embedded 8x8 public-domain font,
  drawn into a presentation buffer copy; emulation surfaces and RTG
  guest VRAM are never drawn into.
- Crop modes are bypassed while the OSK is visible or animating and
  resume after it closes.
- Per-button and per-axis input ownership with capture-only dispatch:
  unrelated key/mouse action mappings and autofire are suppressed
  while the OSK owns input; mouse polling stays on the gameplay
  passthrough path.
- Disabling the core option while open shuts the OSK down and
  releases sticky modifiers; reinitialization mirrors transparency,
  language, and numpad settings across graphics recreation.

* fix(libretro): wire OSK toggle into libretro input, keep close capture

Address PR #2352 review findings:

- options.h: default vkbd_toggle to "leftstick" in the libretro
  build, like Android, since the frontend joypad action space has no
  guide button.
- libretro.cpp: install the configured toggle in
  apply_libretro_osk_options() and consume both edges in poll_input()
  instead of routing it as gameplay. When the configured button is not
  pressable in the frontend joypad space (e.g. the standalone default
  "guide" in a loaded .uae config), fall back to L3 and log a
  warning. Hoist joypad_map[] to file scope with
  libretro_joypad_supports_button() for the action-space check.
- libretro.cpp: keep input OSK-owned during the 300 ms closing
  animation (imgui_osk_should_render() instead of
  imgui_osk_is_active()) so fresh presses and axis movement are
  discarded rather than dispatched to the guest while the keyboard
  still covers the screen.
- sdl_stub.cpp: implement SDL_GetGamepadButtonFromString() as a
  case-insensitive reverse lookup of SDL_GetGamepadStringForButton().

* fix(libretro): fall back to L3 when vkbd_toggle is a keyboard hotkey

A loaded .uae config can set vkbd_toggle to a keyboard hotkey such as
F12. SDL_GetGamepadButtonFromString() doesn't resolve key names, so the
previous guard (valid-but-unsupported gamepad button only) left
libretro_vkbd_button invalid and the OSK unreachable from the gamepad.

Extend the fallback: any nonempty toggle value that doesn't resolve to
a pressable joypad button now falls back to the left-stick default,
with a warning. The keyboard hotkey itself still works through the
shared my_kbd_handler hotkey path, so this only adds the gamepad
binding.

* fix(libretro): drive the on-screen keyboard directly and keep the statusline beneath it

Address the two open libretro OSK review findings:

- Route the RetroPad's OSK controls (D-pad / A / left stick) directly into
  osk_control() from the polled physical gamepad state, independent of which
  guest device (joystick or mouse) each core port maps to. This mirrors the
  standalone controller path, so the keyboard can be navigated and a key
  selected even when no port is assigned to an emulated joystick. East (B)
  hides the keyboard, mirroring the native path.

- Composite the bottom-anchored statusline before the on-screen keyboard in
  gfx_platform_present_frame(), so the statusline no longer paints over the
  keyboard's Alt/Amiga/space/cursor row and the keyboard stays readable.

* fix(libretro): keep pre-OSK gameplay input out of the keyboard

Address two libretro OSK review findings about the direct keyboard driver:

- Exclude gameplay-owned holds from the published OSK state. A D-pad
  direction, select (A) or left stick that was already held for gameplay
  before the keyboard opened is gameplay-owned; the publisher now only
  emits controls the keyboard acquired after it opened (owner == osk).
  Otherwise the pre-existing hold is misread as a fresh OSK press and moves
  focus or types a key while the same control is still active in the guest.

- Forward releases for gameplay-owned close buttons. The East/B handler now
  only consumes B when the keyboard acquired its press (owner == osk). A B
  that was held for gameplay before the keyboard opened stays gameplay-owned,
  so its release is routed to the guest instead of being swallowed, which
  left the guest seeing B asserted until the close animation finished.

events.title: feat(app,mapper): public move-region choice, an accept split from the maze flag, and a tried-direction generation counter (SQ-1551)
events.message:
feat(app,mapper): public move-region choice, an accept split from the maze flag, and a tried-direction generation counter (SQ-1551)

A headless host building map-editing UI against `AppState`/`Mapper` had to
mirror `input.rs`'s own move-region logic, work around a bundled side effect,
and had no signal for the matrix view's tried-direction markers. All three
close here, with the TUI itself unchanged.

1. `input::choose_region` and `input::move_targets` are now `pub`, along with
   the `SeamRefusal` error type (now `#[derive(Debug)]`). They pick which
   rooms a "move region" takes (portal boundary, a single inbound bridge, or
   several bridges to ask about) and which layers a region could land on — the
   TUI's own `move-region` command and a host's "Move to another layer…"
   action now share one copy instead of the host reimplementing the tiers
   against `mapper`'s public API.

2. `apply_region_prompt`'s accept for a layer suggestion split into
   `accept_layer_suggestion(state, mapper, region, target, set_maze_flag)` —
   the move itself, plus the maze flag as an explicit `bool` rather than a
   bundled side effect keyed off the trigger. `suggestion_sets_maze_flag`
   is the one place "does accepting this trigger set the flag" is decided;
   both the accept path and `open_layer_suggestion`'s "Separating it also
   flags the layer as a maze" line now read it, so the sentence can't promise
   something the accept doesn't do. The TUI still always passes
   `suggestion_sets_maze_flag(trigger)`, so its own behaviour is unchanged.

3. `MapGraph::mark_tried`/`unmark_tried` now bump a NEW counter,
   `tried_gen` (plus a `Mapper::tried_gen()` convenience), when the tried
   set for a room actually changes — the matrix view's `×`/`·` markers.
   Deliberately NOT folded into `struct_gen`: `observe` calls `mark_tried`
   on every typed direction including a foiled move (one that bounced off a
   wall), and `state::tests::a_foiled_move_shows_up_immediately_without_a_geometry_change`
   pins that a foiled move must not invalidate the routed DRAWN-layout memo
   `struct_gen` gates — confirmed by actually trying the struct_gen bump
   first and watching that exact test fail under
   `cargo nextest run -p lanthorn --lib --bins --features t-all`. A separate
   counter gives a host the signal it needs for the matrix view without
   forcing an unrelated, expensive DRAWN re-route on every failed compass
   attempt.

New suite `crates/app/tests/suites/sq1551_host_map_editing.rs` (in the
`mapper_ui` group binary) exercises 1 and 2 from outside the crate's own
binary: `choose_region`/`move_targets` against rebuilt versions of `input.rs`'s
own three seam-tier fixtures, and accepting a name-triggered suggestion with
the flag off (maze stays unset) alongside the TUI's own path (maze still set).
New `crates/mapper/src/graph.rs` in-crate tests cover 3, including the
falsified case (`tried_gen` bumps on a genuinely new direction, not on a
repeat) and the counters' independence (`mark_tried`/`unmark_tried` never
touch `struct_gen`).

Deviation from the brief, with reasoning: item 3 asked to bump `struct_gen`
itself, offering a separate counter as a fallback "if you conclude it
genuinely shouldn't bump". It shouldn't — see point 3 above — so this uses
that fallback.

Tests: cargo nextest run -p lanthorn-mapper (454 passed); cargo nextest run
-p lanthorn -E 'binary(mapper_ui)' (319 passed, including the 7 new SQ-1551
cases); cargo nextest run -p lanthorn --lib --features t-input input (357
passed); cargo nextest run -p lanthorn --lib --bins --features t-all with no
filter (3737 passed, 15 skipped); cargo check --all-targets and
cargo clippy -p lanthorn --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings (also
-p lanthorn-mapper --all-targets), all clean.

Completes: SQ-1551
