events.title: P3 elimination: the bounce icon squashes into the panel floor, not just moves
events.message:
P3 elimination: the bounce icon squashes into the panel floor, not just moves

Follow-up to the previous commit. A further advisor pass challenged the
"icon frozen at its last bounced position" assumption behind that commit's
own step-freeze fix; re-disassembling 1000:1776 (RestoreSpriteBackground)
and 1000:1790 (the real game's own next full-screen present) showed the
icon actually vanishes entirely once the bounce ends, not a beat later --
fixed with an explicit `done` flag that suppresses the icon draw.

A second, independent finding from the same investigation: the bounce
loop's own 1000:1767 (SUB byte [BX+0x19],AL) shrinks the sprite's drawn row
count by the current wobble offset every step, while its draw position
still moves down -- so the icon's visible bottom edge stays pinned at the
panel row's own floor and the icon appears to sink into it, squashing down
to a single (transparent, on this sprite) row at the deepest point of each
dip, rather than translating as one whole sprite. An earlier theory (a
narrow VGA-refresh row band from a different function, 089C) was a red
herring; independently confirmed against three separate functions and
ported via a new `cropRows` option on blitChr/blitTransparent.

Every fix confirmed by reintroducing its own bug and re-running the suite,
including a bounding-box invariant across all 16 bounce steps that
distinguishes the real squash-toward-the-floor behaviour from two
plausible-looking wrong variants (frozen position, fixed-Y-with-crop), and
by rendering multiple steps to PNG and looking.

docs/engine.md §9ba has the full derivation.

events.title: keyboard: a key held down typed once and never again
events.message:
keyboard: a key held down typed once and never again

A Wayland compositor does not repeat keys. It says a key went down and
that it came up, hands over the rate and delay it would like, and leaves
the repeating to the client - and kb_repeat took those two numbers and
dropped them, so holding a cursor key moved the cursor one place.

On an ST the repeating is TOS's as well: the keyboard only ever sends
make and break codes, and the 50Hz tick types the last key again by the
two numbers Kbrate sets. So that is where it is now, in keyboard.c,
where the test can hand it a clock. Kbrate was already keeping its
numbers and nothing read them; they start at EmuTOS's 15 and 2 instead
of 25 and 5, then follow the desktop's settings until a program sets its
own. Only the last key down repeats, only that key coming up stops it, a
modifier never repeats and does not stop one, and the keyboard leaving
the window lets go. A program that was busy gets one repeat when it
comes back rather than a buffer full of a key nobody is holding.

The repeat has nothing of its own to wake a wait with, so evnt_multi and
the console's key wait sleep no longer than until it is due - evnt_multi
only when a key was asked for, since otherwise nothing takes the repeat
and the sleep would be none at all.

And conterm, at 0x484, which is how a program turns the repeat off, was
ordinary memory that nobody read. It is the console's own variable now,
which vt52.c already reads for the bell, so clearing bit 2 silences the
bell as well, and the setting outlives a Pexec as it does on an ST.

events.title: feat(app): host APIs for completion, reveal-from-text, guidance switch, command band (SQ-1549)
events.message:
feat(app): host APIs for completion, reveal-from-text, guidance switch, command band (SQ-1549)

Four input-help features used to live in bin-only or crate-private code, so a
GUI or network host driving `AppState` had to re-implement them to offer the
same assistance the TUI does. All four now have a host-facing entry point,
and the TUI is refactored to call the same underlying code rather than a
parallel copy:

1. Completion: `input::recompute_suggestions`/`apply_completion`'s ranking
   and apply logic is pulled out into pure functions on `complete.rs`
   (`completion_candidates`, `apply_completion_to_line`, `partial_word`) —
   the module that already documents itself as "pure, no I/O". The ghost-text
   "rest of the word" hint (`render::transcript::ghost_completion`) is split
   the same way into `complete::completion_ghost_tail`. The TUI's own
   functions are now thin wrappers over these.

2. Reveal: `reveal::arm`'s two word-filter tiers (object tree / dictionary
   fallback) are pulled into `words_known_to_objects`/`words_known_to_dictionary`,
   and a new `reveal::arm_from_text(guidance, visible, engine, vocab)` answers
   the same question for supplied plain text instead of the TUI's own
   wrap-cache read — same guidance switch, same "nothing lit" answers, no
   `Reveal`/hold-duration/state write (expiry stays the host's business).

3. Guidance switch: `/set-guidance`'s persistence (write the per-game
   sidecar, update `state.config.guidance`, pin/release the one-run override)
   moves to `host::assist::set_guidance`, returning the effective value.
   `slash_dispatch.rs` now calls it and keeps only its own label/transcript
   text.

4. Command band data: `host::assist::refresh_band_data` calls the same
   `refresh_verbs`/`refresh_objects` the TUI's loop tick calls, opening a
   `CommandBandState` first if none is open (mirroring `open_command_band`'s
   own initial verb table and quick row) and closing it again afterward if it
   did — so a host gets the plain `BandData` (verbs+shapes+source, quick,
   here/carried/seen, the WITH slot's candidates) with no cell layout or
   TUI overlay state left behind, and a TUI with the band already open keeps
   its normal once-per-open/once-per-turn caching.

Added the acceptance suites: `scope_completion.rs` (candidates match Tab's
ranking; applying a candidate matches what Tab does to the line),
`word_reveal.rs` (reveal-from-text lights the same words `arm` does, and
honors the same switch/empty answers), `host_session.rs` (guidance persists
across a reboot), `command_band.rs` (band data for Zork I: grammar verbs with
shapes, room/carried objects, the WITH slot).

Deviation from the brief, with reasoning: the brief describes the completion
API as taking a "line + caret position". The TUI's own `current_partial`/
`apply_completion` have never actually been caret-aware — they always read
the trailing word of the WHOLE input value, cursor position notwithstanding,
and no test exercises a mid-line cursor. Rather than make the TUI's own path
caret-aware (an unrequested behavior change with no test coverage either
way), `complete::partial_word(line, caret)` generalizes the rule properly
(the trailing word of `line[..caret]`), and the TUI calls it with
`caret = state.input.char_len()` (the line's own length) — which is exactly
today's whole-value behavior. The two can only diverge for a caret NOT at
the end of the line, a case the TUI itself has never defined.

Tests: cargo nextest run -p lanthorn --lib --features t-input input (357
passed); cargo nextest run -p lanthorn adult_words vocabulary_offer
vocabulary_vetting assist_voice word_reveal command_band scope_completion
story_word_scrape (147 passed); the six new acceptance tests individually
(6 passed, none vacuously skipped — real fixtures present); cargo nextest
run -p lanthorn --lib --bins --features t-all with no filter (3737 passed,
15 skipped); cargo check --all-targets and cargo clippy -p lanthorn
--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, both clean.

events.title: cpu: 68030 MMU — a frame $A RTE leaves the next opcode in IRC before replaying the write
events.message:
cpu: 68030 MMU — a frame $A RTE leaves the next opcode in IRC before replaying the write

When the pending write of a frame $A RTE faults again, the bus error
frame built for it stores regs.irc as the opcode of the instruction to
resume, but at that point IRC still holds this RTE's own opcode: the
frame $A path restores the stage B opcode into mmu030_opcode_stageb
only. So after the handler's RTE the CPU resumed the faulted
instruction by executing an RTE at its PC, on a stack that holds no
frame, and took a format error — the second panic Atari System V hit
at every copyin that straddles an unmapped kernel page, once the
first (stale stage B opcode) was fixed.

Load IRC with the stage B opcode from the frame before the replay so
a nested fault records the right instruction, and clear mmu030_opcode
so the RTE's own opcode is not written back over it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: cpu: 68030 MMU — a deferred prefetch fault is taken when the word is consumed
events.message:
cpu: 68030 MMU — a deferred prefetch fault is taken when the word is consumed

get_word_030_prefetch() defers the bus error for an invalid pipeline
stage while a branch is in the pipe (pipeline_stop), on the grounds
that the words past a taken branch are never used. That is right for
the words after the branch, but the branch's own extension words are
also past the point where pipeline_stop is set: a BSR.L or Bcc.L whose
32-bit displacement straddles a page boundary, with the second page
not yet resident, had its low displacement word returned as $FFFF
instead of faulting. Under Atari System V that made every such call
into a PLT stub — the displacement's low word being the page's first
word — branch to an odd address (BSR.L with displacement $FFFFxxxx
read back as $FFFFFFFF, target PC+1) and the process died with an
address error; XFaceMaker2 was the first program with a PLT call at
exactly that spot.

Keep the deferral for the words ahead, but fault when the word being
returned is the one that never arrived: the instruction is using it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: slaapliedje

events.title: cpu: 68030 MMU — undo address register fixups when a prefetch fault restarts the instruction
events.message:
cpu: 68030 MMU — undo address register fixups when a prefetch fault restarts the instruction

A prefetch fault raised from inside an instruction — the next opcode's
fetch landing in an unmapped page — is reported with mmu030_opcode =
-1, the same as a fault while filling the pipe before the instruction
starts, and the run loop's handler discarded the mmufixup entries for
that case. But the generated MOVE handlers pre-decrement the address
register and record its fixup before the fetch of the next opcode, and
the write comes after: MOVE.L (d16,An),-(SP) at the last words of a
page faulted with SP already decremented, the fixup was thrown away,
the instruction restarted after the RTE and decremented SP again. The
result was one unwritten stack slot in the middle of an argument list;
in XFaceMaker2 that was XtCreateApplicationShell's num_args, which came
out as whatever the stack held, and Xt walked the ArgList off its end.

Restore the fixups in that case too. A completed instruction has
already cleared them, so a fault while filling the pipe for the next
one — or for a branch target — is unaffected; the condition codes are
deliberately not restored, since a completed RTE/RTR must keep the CCR
it loaded.

events.message:
Tagesroutine wie im Original: Karriereende, Angebote und sechs Abweichungen (GitLab #81, #83)

Umbau nach dem Zweigbuch docs/abgleich/0DF0D.md.

#81 - Karriereankündigung und Verlängerungsangebot waren vertauscht:
* 0x0E76F (Bit 7, Vorlage 4) ist die Ankündigung "kündigt an, dass er seinen
  Vertrag nicht mehr verlängern wird" - ohne Verhandlung
  (`retirementAnnouncements`). Die Spieler mit Bit 7 sind in allen
  Originalspielständen 33 bis 35.
* 0x0E83E (Byte 24 = 100 + Jahre, Vorlage 0) ist das Angebot "bietet an, von 1
  auf 2-4 Jahre zu verlängern" - mit Verhandlung (`contractOffers`).
* Karriereende am Saisonende (0x0D475): Kaderspieler nur bei ausgelaufenem
  Vertrag und Ankündigung, ohne Ablöse; Spieler ohne Verein nach
  Alter > random(32,34), je Manager ein Durchgang. Vorher werden alle Spieler
  ein Jahr älter (0x0D420) - deshalb ist im Original kein Spieler ohne Verein
  älter als 34. Bei uns gingen Kaderspieler nach Alter und vereinslose nie.

#83 - sechs Abweichungen aus demselben Zweigbuch:
* F1: nach Krawall sinkt Komfortnote 390 (1/3, mit über 2 Mio. 2/3)
* F2: Komfortabnutzung nur in der Bundesliga
* F3: Angebotsschwelle mit dem Einsatzsummanden N = N₀ - N₀·T/10
* F4: Leihspieler bieten keine Verlängerung an
* F5: Trainingsverletzung nur bei ganz leerem Kaderbyte 9
* F6: ab Saisontag 322 entfällt die ganze Tagesroutine, nicht nur das Training

Was der Vertragsdialog 0x251FF beim Annehmen mit Byte 24 macht, klärt dessen
Zweigbuch; bis dahin bleibt es stehen und verfällt über contractCooldown.

events.title: Leihgehalt mit dem Abschlag des Originals (GitLab #79)
events.message:
Leihgehalt mit dem Abschlag des Originals (GitLab #79)

Ein geliehener Spieler kostete das volle Gehalt: im Test 4.100 statt 1.366 DM,
also das Dreifache.

`addToSquad` (0x224A8) rechnet das Gehalt selbst aus und nimmt den Modus aus
einem Argument: bei 99 wird mit Modus 3 gerechnet statt mit 1 (0x226EE bis
0x226FA). Modus 3 ist die Gehaltsbasis plus Leihabschlag, also ein Drittel. Von
den sieben Aufrufern übergibt genau einer die 99, und zwar als `99 mal Schalter`
bei 0x23E79 - der Schalter LEIHEN/KAUFEN des Transfermarkts.

Beim Kauf fiel es nicht auf, weil `completePurchase` das Gehalt gleich mit dem
ausgehandelten überschreibt. `completeLoan` liest es zurück und behält es.

Gefunden mit der Prüfung "Aufrufstellen mit festen Argumenten" aus #78: von 92
mehrfach gerufenen Routinen bleiben sechs, deren Aufrufer sich in einer
aufgelösten Konstante unterscheiden - diese war darunter.

events.title: Eine Absage hält nicht ewig: der Spieler verhandelt wieder (GitLab #80)
events.message:
Eine Absage hält nicht ewig: der Spieler verhandelt wieder (GitLab #80)

Sagt ein Spieler, dass er nicht verlängert (Kaderbyte 24 = 100 + Stufe), oder
lehnt man sein Angebot ab (100), war das im Remake endgültig - die Tagesroutine
macht nur unter 100 Angebote, und der Wert änderte sich nie wieder.

Das Original hebt das in der Tagesroutine wieder auf (0x0E5DC bis 0x0E64C): mit
random(0,5) = 0, also einem Sechstel je Tag, kommt der Wert auf random(9,17)
zurück; unter 100 zählt er täglich um eins herunter. Im Schnitt nach sechs Tagen
verhandelt der Spieler also wieder.

Der Zweig hängt dort an Kaderfeld 48/50. Die Werte darin sahen wie Unix-Zeiten
aus - tatsächlich ist es ein Fernzeiger auf den Meldungstext zu diesem Spieler,
den 0x30954 aus der Meldungsliste räumt. Unsere Meldungen hängen nicht am
Kaderplatz, deshalb gilt die Rückkehr hier ohne diese Bedingung und der alte
Hinweis bleibt stehen; im Quelltext steht, warum.

Gefunden mit der Prüfung "Würfel und Klemmschritte" aus #78.

events.message:
Liga des Managers wandert beim Auf- und Abstieg mit (GitLab #76)

`swapClubs` setzte dem Manager den neuen Verein, ließ aber seine Liga stehen
(Managerbyte 312). In allen 41 vorhandenen Spielständen des Originals - 117
Manager - stimmt dieses Byte mit dem Ligaband des Vereinsindex überein; beim
Saisonwechsel zieht das Original es nach (0x1E3A4).

Ohne das wäre ein Aufsteiger dauerhaft Zweitligist geblieben: an Byte 312 hängen
der Einnahmedeckel der Zuschauerrechnung (700.000 statt 300.000 DM), die
Saisonprämie (1,6 statt 0,8 Millionen), Gehaltsforderungen, Werbung, Spielerpool
und die Meldungen.

Die Liga hängt jetzt am Setzer für den Verein, damit sie auch bei künftigen
Umzügen mitwandert. Der Test prüft Ab- und Aufstieg einzeln und danach die
Invariante über drei Saisonwechsel; gegen den alten Stand schlägt er fehl.

Gefunden bei einer Stichprobe für den Abgleich: welche Bytes schreibt das
Original, die das Remake nur liest. Die laufenden Runden sind nicht betroffen -
dort ist noch keine Saison zu Ende.

  Schützen (mode 0), nicht der Vorlage; der Betragsterm liest die
  x-Position (Kaderbyte 25), nicht Byte 19.

  Chancen derselben Minute kommen in der Reihenfolge ihrer Plätze, nicht
  Heim vor Gast. Nach 100 vergeblichen Zügen bleibt ein Platz leer.

- Zu Halbzeitbeginn werden die Chancen aller Paarungen gewürfelt, bevor
  die erste Minute läuft (Server-Tick zweiteilig).
- Pokalrunde: der Verlierer behält die erreichte Runde (0x19410); der
  Test erwartete fälschlich 30.

Werkzeug: kontrollpunkte.py mit --spur, --still, --halt, --ohne, --ring
und Punkten für Torwürfel, Chancenhandler, Karten-/Verletzungswürfe und
Halbzeitende.

events.title: Read The Hobbit's keyboard under interrupt, so commands can be typed ahead
events.message:
Read The Hobbit's keyboard under interrupt, so commands can be typed ahead

patches/hobbit_keyboard.s, included by the fast-draw patch: an IM 2 interrupt,
set up once the title screen's key is pressed, runs the second half of the
game's own SCAN_KEYBOARD fifty times a second and keeps each new key in a
16-byte ring. SCAN_KEYBOARD keeps its debounce delay, since GET_KEY's patience
counts scans, and takes keys from the ring. The wait after a picture returns at
once when something has been typed ahead and leaves it to be read, and
otherwise throws its key away as before; NEW_KEYPRESS (PAUSE, SAVE) throws its
key away; the DIs after the tape routines become EIs.

The game never enables interrupts and borrows IY, so the ROM's IM 1 routine is
out: I = $39 takes the vector $FFFF from the ROM's unused $FF bytes, where a JR
lands on a JP at $FFF4, both in the UDG area the game never uses and written at
set-up. The ring and the start of the set-up go in UNREACHED_WALK_HELD and
UNREACHED_WIPE_EXIT; the rest in the space the drawing patch left.

Checked live on the emulator: a command typed while the last one's picture drew
was obeyed in full, PAUSE's key did not reach the next command, and the game
still typed WAIT when left idle. check_fast_draw.py (now over all the patch's
ranges): all 22 pictures still identical. 699 bytes change in all.

events.title: cadaver: 120(A5) is a cache, not the source - $0144b8 runs backwards to refresh it on crossings
events.message:
cadaver: 120(A5) is a cache, not the source - $0144b8 runs backwards to refresh it on crossings

No GEMDOS/BIOS/FDC trap activity at all during a real TUNNEL->CAVERN crossing (confirmed
both ways), ruling out the disk-load hypothesis from the previous commit despite 120(A5)'s
content genuinely changing to CAVERN art. Chasing the crossing's actual $0144b8 call (by
register content, not step count - watch's printed steps are the persistent lifetime
counter, not any command's own local budget) shows it running with source and dest
swapped: A0=$20f00 (the display double-buffer's inactive half), A1=120(A5)'s own buffer.
Same copy mechanism as the ordinary per-frame flip, reversed - it banks the freshly-drawn
inactive half back into 120(A5) as a cache, not the other way round.

Reframes the open question again: the real room-background painter writes the display
buffer's inactive half directly (RAM-to-RAM, matching the no-disk-I/O finding), not
120(A5) - which is why every prior watch on 120(A5) found nothing.

P3 opponents: port the real interactive opponent picker (M3.54)

FUN_1000_1A4A, "pick 3 opponents after passing the Challenge qualifier",
replacing tournament.js's own old auto-pick (first-3-untaken-roster).

Resolves the item's own known trap (§9k: "the qualifier needs 3 opponents
before the picker exists"): the qualifier's own 3 opponents are a
hardcoded JETHRO trio (102b/10a0's own raw writes to [266A]/[266C]/
[266E]), not a real pick -- no roster taken flag, no tuning effect
(tournamentIndex<=0 always discards the character-based KID_MODIFIER
lookup for the qualifier, confirmed by re-tracing InitRaceCarsFromTables'
own branch structure past an intermediate false alarm that the whole
mechanism looked dead). ResetTournamentState resets all 4 face-preview
slots to an "unpicked" sentinel the qualifier's own raw writes never
clear, so the real picker, run once right after a PASS, reliably finds
exactly 3 unfilled slots every time.

tournament.js: pickPlayerCharacter no longer auto-picks; QUALIFIER_OPPONENTS,
opponentCharactersFor, needsOpponentPick; pickOpponentCharacter now
appends instead of replacing. flow.js: enterOpponentPick, wired into
nextAfterOutcome; leaveCharSelect's new challenge-opponent branch (ESC
loops back, never exits, matching 1A4A's own loop).

A second advisor review caught a real regression in the first working
draft: confirm()'s own PRESS_ANY_KEY branch called startNextRace()
directly, skipping nextAfterOutcome() -- harmless for that phase's
original pre-qualifier use, but the picker's own trailing PRESS_ANY_KEY
took the same shortcut, so the just-shipped tournament board (M3.53)
never actually showed before race 1. Fixed, and live-tested end to end
afterward: driving the real picker (including a mid-pick ESC, confirming
it re-prompts the same slot rather than exiting) through to a live BOARD
render -- closing M3.53's own "not obtained" live-check gap too. Also
fixed: a wrong citation for the roster's own taken-bit write site (the
real one is 1000:0AC2), a missing subMenuMusic call, and

events.title: sana2: give transmit its own scratch buffer
events.message:
sana2: give transmit its own scratch buffer

createwritepacket() has the guest's CopyFromBuff() copy the outgoing
payload into pdev->tempbuf and then snapshots it into the host packet.
CopyFromBuff() is guest code; while it runs, the receive path can
deliver a packet, and handleread() writes that packet into the same
tempbuf. The outgoing frame then carries received bytes.

Allocate tempbuf at twice its size and use the second half for
transmit only. A write that starts while another one on the same
opener is still copying is refused instead of sharing that half.
events.author: RLH

events.title: sana2: don't let an unread packet hold up the receive queue
events.message:
sana2: don't let an unread packet hold up the receive queue

uaenet_int_handler2() only looked at the head of the read queue. When
no reader wanted that packet, for example a broadcast of an EtherType
nobody reads, it started the drop timer on every queued packet and
stopped, so packets behind it that did have a reader waited until the
head was dropped DELAYED_DROPPED_PACKET_FRAMES frames later.

Step over a packet that has no reader, keeping it queued with its own
drop timer, so later packets are still delivered.
events.author: RLH

events.title: sana2: accept multicast frames the guest registered
events.message:
sana2: accept multicast frames the guest registered

uaenet_gotdata() dropped every multicast frame unless the unit was
promiscuous, so the multicast filter in handleread(), which checks
frames against the S2_ADDMULTICASTADDRESS ranges, never saw one and
multicast protocols such as mDNS/DNS-SD received nothing.

Admit multicast frames in uaenet_gotdata() and drop those for
addresses nobody registered when the read queue is processed, where
the multicast list is already read. They then neither wait in the
queue nor reach S2_READORPHAN readers.
events.author: RLH

events.title: Draw The Hobbit's pictures nine times faster: rows beside the sweep in IX and IY, each cell coloured once, whole bytes filled at a time
events.message:
Draw The Hobbit's pictures nine times faster: rows beside the sweep in IX and IY, each cell coloured once, whole bytes filled at a time

The fill keeps the bytes above and below its sweep in IX and IY instead of
stepping the address up and down for every pixel; colours a cell only as the
sweep enters it, since the colouring writes the same byte every time; and fills
a whole byte at once at the start of a clear byte whose neighbours above and
below are each clear and seeded, all set and unseeded, or off the canvas --
where all eight pixels would push no seed and change no flag.

The loop along a sweep lives in the 165 zeros after the last picture
(-): no code refers to them, SAVE and START's world copy stop short
of them, and twenty turns of play left them zero. The game never enables
interrupts, so borrowing IY is safe.

check_fast_draw.py: all 22 pictures identical in the whole of memory, the
stack no deeper. 126.1 s of drawing originally, 33.1 s after the first pass,
13.4 s now (9.4x); Bag End 0.55 s, the slowest 1.04 s. The Patches page,
its GIFs' captions, the plan's record and the README say so.

docs: add a machine-read prose rule, scoped to the surfaces that need it

A model reads three surfaces in this repo with no human present to resolve an
ambiguity: the tool descriptions in tools-manifest.stock.json, the reason
strings a refusal carries, and each SKILL.md description frontmatter. Those
are where ambiguity has a cost, so the rule covers them and the planning
documents that instruct agents.

- Name what the rule does NOT cover, because a blanket version would do
  damage: docs/ is the owner's own writing, a historical record says what was
  true when it was written, and a module header must stay WHY-prose naming
  its incident, which the Comments rule already requires.
- Reference asd-ste100 as an optional accelerator only. .claude/skills/ is
  gitignored, so CI and a fresh clone do not have it, and this repo already
  forbids branching on a gitignored install. The discipline stands without it.
- Record the measured gap rather than claiming compliance: nineteen tool
  descriptions carry a semicolon and the longest runs to 3639 characters.

The rule is written to its own standard. Both copies lint clean apart from
one deliberate passive, which is the bad example it quotes.

events.title: feat(64-16): move the startup staging sweep behind the confirmed control-port bind
events.message:
feat(64-16): move the startup staging sweep behind the confirmed control-port bind

G-64-6 (XFER-07, truth #5): a second broker started while a live broker held
the control port ran sweepOrphanedStaging() before it learned it had lost
the bind race, deleting every staging session directory the live broker's
own sessions owned. The sweep now runs once, in run(), after the loopback
bind is confirmed and before the first writeBrokerRecordFile() -- the only
distribution channel for the control token that gates acquire and
stage_file -- so no directory under the staging root can belong to this
process's own sessions when the sweep runs, and no losing process ever
reaches it.

Three new spawned-real-broker tests in broker-control.test.ts prove it: a
losing second broker leaves a live broker's staging session and its staged
file intact; a broker that fails loudly on a squatted port leaves seeded
staging untouched; a broker that wins the bind still removes crash residue
(a staged file plus an empty, interrupted-removal-shaped directory) before
its discovery record exists. Both losing-broker tests fail on today's tree
and pass after the fix; the winning-broker test passes throughout.

startRealBroker() and the liveness round trip's spawn now default
VICE_BROKER_HOME to their own temporary state directory, confining every
automated-suite broker spawn away from the machine-level ~/.c64-re-tools.

events.title: Βήμα 27: η αποικία μεγαλώνει — μετάλλευμα, πλοίο αποίκων, σειρά υποδοχών
events.message:
Βήμα 27: η αποικία μεγαλώνει — μετάλλευμα, πλοίο αποίκων, σειρά υποδοχών

Το §15 έλεγε «η αποικία ξοδεύει το μέταλλο της αρχής και δεν φτιάχνει άλλο»:
κάθε παρτίδα παιζόταν μέσα στο άνοιγμα. Τέσσερα πράγματα το άλλαξαν, και τα
τέσσερα μετρημένα στο tools/balance.py — κανένα δεν βρέθηκε διαβάζοντας κώδικα.

ΤΟ ΒΙΟΠΛΑΣΤΙΚΟ ΣΦΡΑΓΙΖΕΙ, ΔΕΝ ΣΤΗΡΙΖΕΙ. Πάνελ, ανεμογεννήτρια, συλλέκτης,
αντλία, ορυχείο και πίστα είναι σκελετοί στον αέρα και κοστίζουν μέταλλο μόνο·
βιοπλαστικό ζητά ό,τι κρατά ατμόσφαιρα. Ως τώρα τα πάντα ήθελαν και τα δύο,
και το βιοπλαστικό ήταν το πραγματικό ταβάνι: η μόνη πηγή του θέλει θερμοκήπιο
ΚΑΙ μεσαίο εργοστάσιο, δηλαδή δύο θόλους που κοστίζουν βιοπλαστικό.

ΤΟ ΜΕΤΑΛΛΕΥΜΑ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΟ ΕΡΜΑ ΤΟΥ ΣΚΑΦΟΥΣ: 60 μετάλλευμα, 75 μέταλλο, 45
βιοπλαστικό. Ηλιακό, αντλία και μικρό εργοστάσιο κοστίζουν 57 από τα 75, και
τα 18 που μένουν είναι το νόημα: μετρημένο στα οκτώ sols, το εργοστάσιο έφαγε
όλο το μετάλλευμα ως το sol 4 και έβγαλε 30 μέταλλο — 18 -> 48, δύο μετάλλευμα
το ένα. Τα 48 είναι ένα ορυχείο (30) και ρέστα, οπότε ο κύκλος κλείνει από την
παραγωγή και όχι από το άνοιγμα.

ΤΟ C ΚΑΛΕΙ ΤΟ ΠΛΟΙΟ ΤΩΝ ΑΠΟΙΚΩΝ — ο μηχανισμός υπήρχε από το βήμα 9 και δεν
τον καλούσε κανείς. Το ui_ship ρωτά ό,τι ρωτά και το ship_call και λέει ποιο
λείπει: αίθουσα ελέγχου, πίστα, ή πλοίο που ήδη έρχεται. Το test_game το περνά
ολόκληρο: άρνηση χωρίς Control, ταβάνι 4 -> 52 με τον θόλο, και 4 -> 8 ζωντανοί
με ένα πάτημα.

ΚΑΙ ΤΟ ΜΗΝΥΜΑ ΕΒΓΑΙΝΕ ΚΕΝΟ, ΟΧΙ ΛΑΘΟΣ. Το ui_hide πάει στο gh_undo, που χαλάει
το HL· ο δείκτης του κειμένου φορτωνόταν πριν από την κλήση, οπότε το ui_msg
τύπωνε από σκουπίδια που έδειχναν σε μηδενικό. Η κατάσταση ήταν σωστή σε κάθε
έλεγχο — το έπιασε μόνο η δοκιμή που διαβάζει τη σειρά 3 ως γλύφους.

Η ΣΕΙΡΑ ΤΩΝ ΥΠΟΔΟΧΩΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ Η ΣΕΙΡΑ ΤΟΥ ΔΩΜΑΤΙΟΥ, ΟΧΙ ΤΟΥ ΠΙΝΑΚΑ. Μια μηχανή
τρέχει μόνο αν η υποδοχή της είναι μικρότερη από το πλήθος των χειριστών, άρα
σε θόλο με έναν άνθρωπο μέσα τρέχει ΜΟΝΟ η υποδοχή 0 — και με την αριθμητική
σειρά της room_machines το εργαστήριο έβγαζε επεξεργαστές, που τους φτιάχνει
και το control, και ΠΟΤΕ vitromeat. Το θερμοκήπιο ήταν χειρότερο: plant_class
0-4 άμυλο, 5-9 λαχανικά, άρα ένα μεσαίο φύτευε τέσσερα αμυλούχα και κανένα
λαχανικό. Το mach_food θέλει και τα τρία, οπότε η αλυσίδα της τροφής ήταν
άφτιαχτη σε κάθε μέτρηση. Δύο πίνακες στο rooms.asm: rm_pref (μία μηχανή ανά
δωμάτιο για την υποδοχή 0 — αυτή που δεν τη φτιάχνει κανένα άλλο δωμάτιο) και
rm_plants (εναλλαγή κλάσεων αντί για αρίθμηση). Τώρα ένα μεσαίο θερμοκήπιο
είναι άμυλο, λαχανικά, φάρμακα, δέντρο — και το κυλικείο βγάζει γεύματα.

Ο ΤΟΙΧΟΣ ΜΕΤΑΚΟΜΙΣΕ ΑΠΟ ΤΟΥΣ ΡΥΘΜΟΥΣ ΣΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΘΡΩΠΟΥΣ: η τροφή ανεβαίνει πια
(34 -> 38 ενώ τρώνε από πάνω της), αλλά τέσσερις άποικοι δεν προλαβαίνουν εφτά
μηχανές και να φάνε — ο πρώτος θάνατος στο sol 2 με 37 τροφή στην αποθήκη.
Γραμμένο στο §15 ως μέτρηση, με τα τρία μονοπάτια που το λύνουν.

DESIGN: §6.5 η σειρά των υποδοχών, §6.11 το κουμπί, §9.1 το C, §9.3 ο κανόνας
του βιοπλαστικού, §10.1 το νέο άνοιγμα και η καμπύλη του, §15 δύο γραμμές που
έκλεισαν και τρεις που άνοιξαν — μαζί με το φάντασμα που αφήνει υπόλειμμα όταν
η λίστα βρώμικων ξαναγράφει από κάτω του.

events.title: Custom palettes can say which Amiga colour each of their 16 replaces
events.message:
Custom palettes can say which Amiga colour each of their 16 replaces

On the Amiga a room is drawn in 32 colours: 0-15 the background
palette, 16-31 the object palette that Conrad, items and the
inventory share. After any of a .hex file's 16 colours, "= 1,2,17"
now lists which of those 32 it replaces; anything not listed - and
enemies, level 2's extra palette and the text colours, which have no
number - still takes the nearest (or with palette_hue the closest
hue). The lists are optional, so plain 16-line files work as before.
It is how a palette whose only greens are bright keeps the jungle's
muted olives green: nearest colour sends them to grey.

The numbering is worked out per room from the game's own palette
setup (the background palette wherever it is loaded is 0-15, the
object palette 16-31), and the lists are honoured in the full rebuild
and in the few-entries update that palette animations take.

Ctrl+P's file now carries the room's 32 Amiga colours, numbered, in a
comment block, and each of its 16 lines already lists the ones it is
used for, so an author changes colours and moves numbers between
lines; reloaded unchanged it draws the room as the automatic palette
did. The parser reads a line at a time, so comments sit anywhere.

events.message:
P2 charselect: port the real character-select carousel (M3.52, closes P2)

RunCharacterSelectMenuTune2 1000:09e0, its own scroll-step helper
(FUN_1000_0cd3), DrawCharacterSelectGrid (1000:0d1f), FUN_1000_0db0
(face-frame math) and FUN_1000_0b51 (the handicap question's own
gate), all fully re-disassembled and live-confirmed in the browser
end to end. Replaces the flattened list-based character select.

Key finding: there is no explicit "if taken" check anywhere in this
screen. tournament.js's own roster array already stores each slot's
identity byte OR'd with 0x40 once taken, so any consumer that gates
on "<=10" (the entry-time auto-skip loop, the fire-confirm gate)
treats a taken slot as invalid for free, with no dedicated branch --
the M3.9 port's own prior comment citing a specific address for the
taken-check was actually citing the bounds check, not a taken-specific
test.

Ports:
- the real 13-step ease scroll (DS:0185, sums to exactly 64), with
  LEFT/RIGHT mapped to the scroll's own add/subtract branches --
  confirmed live to move the character index the opposite way a first
  guess might expect;
- two distinct wait mechanisms: a held-fire release-wait only once at
  entry (unlike the two-item menu's own per-press re-wait), and a
  real LEFT/RIGHT press that always settles after one slot regardless
  of validity (only the entry-time skip auto-scrolls past an invalid
  one);
- the 5-blink, 80-tick commit sequence's own exact toggle timing
  (0/16/32/48/64, exit at 80, not the off-by-one a first draft got
  backwards);
- the handicap question's own gate, ported as evidence ahead of its
  own call site (two-human H2H is P4) since neither of its two gating
  conditions is ever satisfiable by this port's own reachable flows.

This closes out P2 in full: the boot chain now ends with the real
title screen, real two-level menu, and real character-select carousel.

events.title: cadaver: 120(A5)'s buffer fully decoded - it's the pre-flip room frame, chunk-reversed
events.message:
cadaver: 120(A5)'s buffer fully decoded - it's the pre-flip room frame, chunk-reversed

Pulled the full linear disassembly of $0144b8 (not just the elided excerpt from the
prior pass) to get the exact movem structure: 571 56-byte chunks (14 regs D0-D7,A2-A7)
plus one $5a99-gated 24-byte remainder chunk, forward-read/backward-write. Predecrement
movem's fixed transfer order cancels the read-order reversal within each chunk, so only
chunk order is reversed across the whole 32000-byte transfer.

Reconstructing that exactly and decoding as plain 320x200x4bpp st-interleaved reproduces
(A5)+0's live bytes with 0/32000 diffs against room2_tunnel_entry.snap - settles item 1(a)
outright and reframes 1(b): since 120(A5) holds a complete pre-rendered raster rather than
a compositor source, it's more likely loaded straight off disk than painted at runtime.

Promoted as reversing/cadaver/py/decode_backbuffer.py.

events.title: cadaver: $0144b8 disassembled - reveals a third resident buffer at 120(A5), not a two-way swap
events.message:
cadaver: $0144b8 disassembled - reveals a third resident buffer at 120(A5), not a two-way swap

The "ScreenBufferA/B role-swap" model was wrong: (A5)+0 and (A5)+$7d00 are the two halves of
one 64000-byte double-buffer feeding the shifter directly (confirmed via the live hardware
video-register read). 120(A5) is a separate, third buffer that $0144b8's own source register
reads from - the real candidate for where room art lives before the flip. Inspected it live:
not blank, not a clean 320x200x4bpp frame either with the standard decode. Two other writers
near it (entity/sprite renderer, $00bf72's sprite bitmap cache) are ruled out as already-known
systems, not new leads.

events.title: Draw The Hobbit's pictures four times faster, as a patch on the exact source
events.message:
Draw The Hobbit's pictures four times faster, as a patch on the exact source

patches/hobbit_fast_draw.s INCLUDEs the byte-exact hobbit.asm and rewrites the
plotting code in place: FLOOD_FILL and DRAW_LINE visit the same pixels in the
same order and push the same fill seeds, but carry each pixel's screen address
and bit mask along with the point instead of rebuilding it from (D,E) every
time -- PIXEL_ADDRESS was half of all drawing time. The attribute rule, the ink
flipped where it would match the paper, is kept, with its three values written
into the comparison's immediates once per line or fill.

The new code fits either side of the ATTR_ routines, which RUN_PICTURE's PAINT
calls and which stay put, and in special word slot 0's handler, $82FD-$8390,
which nothing can run. The plan's printer buffer was wrong: the game's PRINT
command uses it through the ROM.

build_hobbit.py --fast-draw assembles it after the byte-exact check and writes
hobbit_fast.sna with its SLD, refusing a patched image that differs outside
the three declared ranges (427 bytes change, all inside them).
scripts/check_fast_draw.py draws all 22 pictures from the same machine in both
and compares the whole of RAM afterwards: all identical, the stack never
deeper, 126.1 s of drawing down to 33.1 s, 3.81x; Bag End 6.7 s to 1.7 s.
Recorded on the emulator from the title screen, Bag End finishes after 7.0 s
in the original and 1.9 s patched.

The plan doc, uncommitted until now, records what was built and where the plan
was wrong; the README says how to build it.

events.title: Label every address Atic Atac's code and comments use
events.message:
Label every address Atic Atac's code and comments use

Every operand that is an address now assembles as a label or an equate, and
every address the prose mentions is a #R reference; what is left as a number is
a number -- pitches, sound-and-length pairs, pixel coordinates, the stack's top.

- The runtime records above the loaded block and the game's variables below
  it are equates: PLAYER, PLAYER_ROOM, WEAPON_X, SOUND_SLOT, LIVE_DOORS;
  FRAMES, TILE_SOURCE, ROOM_COLOUR, LIVES, FOOD_LEVEL, SCORE, CARRIED, CLOCK,
  ROOMS_SEEN and the rest, 73 in all.
- INITIAL_STATE's records the code names are labelled: the four keys by colour
  (a key is sprite $81, its colour its drawing mode), ACG_KEY_PARTS, FOOD,
  MUSHROOMS, each monster by name. The collectables $8C-$8E are the three
  pieces of the A.C.G. key: ACG_DOOR opens only when the three inventory slots
  hold them, in order.
- Code other code writes into, or reads a table less a bias from, is labelled
  and written as label plus offset: the eight blitters' combining opcodes,
  the outline's vertex fetches, two patched JRs, PLAYER_TEMPLATE's fields,
  the roast's height bytes, TEXT_FONT-$0100, ACTOR_HANDLERS+$0144. Each has a
  line comment saying which field, since the HTML shows the address.
- SPRITE_TABLE is words, split at FURNITURE_SPRITES and FURNITURE_COLOURS;
  SPAWN_TYPES is the sixteen creatures a new monster can become, running on
  into SPAWNABLE_SPRITES; the panel layout is one row to a line.
- The 59 numbered entry points other routines use, and L954D and L9565, are
  named (DOORWAY, DRAW_DOOR, OPEN_DOOR, SHUT_DOOR, STEP_ACTOR, BEEP_BC...).

Three routines were named for a guess and are renamed for what they do.
CYCLE_ROOM_COLOUR is PLACE_KEYS: it puts the green, red and cyan keys in
random rooms and the mummy with the red one. ESCAPE_SEQUENCE is TRAPDOOR_FALL:
reached only from the trapdoor's handler, it draws room $96, the fall's
outline, with a falling note, and ends in ENTER_ROOM to the room below; the
ending is reached instead by MAIN_LOOP finding the player in room $8E, and the
CONGRATULATIONT note now says so. CARRYING_8C is ACG_DOOR. SCAN_EB18 is
SCAN_COLLECTABLES. Two notes were a byte out ($9876, $934A) and one named a
caller ($9340) that does not call.

The room pictures no longer show room $8E overwritten by the end screen: the
render's own copy of MAIN_LOOP's CP $8E is pointed at a room there is none of.

Built from the tape: 30208 bytes reassemble byte-for-byte. skool2asm's only
warnings are 11 numbers in comments.

Full re-disassembly of RunOptionsScreenWithSettingsDat 1000:2770 and its
four sub-screens (ShowCredits, the joystick-calibration gate,
RunRedefineKeysScreen, AutoDetectSmoothnessByRetraceLoops), live-confirmed
in DOSBox (game/ mounted read-only). Adds flow.js's OPTIONS phase between

F1/F2's real device-cycling gate is asymmetric, not a simplification: P1
can never reach JOY2 or MOUSE, regardless of hardware; P2 can, gated on
real presence. Live-confirmed with no joystick/mouse present (this port's
own state until P6): one F1 press and one F2 press each cycled through
every rejected candidate and landed back on their own starting value.

F4's real cycle is 5 values, not 4: HIGH/GOOD/MEDIUM/LOW/AUTO, live-
confirmed on a real DOSBox screen (four F4 presses from HIGH shows "AUTO").
This corrects docs/engine.md §9t's own prior "AUTO proven NOT part of the
set" claim, which checked only the display walk's own upper bound, not
whether F4's own input cycling (1000:29CC-29D8, CMP CH,5/JLE) could reach
it. AUTO resolves at RETURN via a real VGA-retrace CPU-speed probe
(AutoDetectSmoothnessByRetraceLoops 1000:3AD0) with no browser equivalent;
the port resolves it to HIGH unconditionally. Also ticks Part R's "AUTO
string" box, resolved as a byproduct.

F5's redefine-keys screen is NOT cleared between the KEYS1/KEYS2 groups
(live-confirmed: a real screenshot showed both stacked together); SPACE
and a same-pass duplicate scancode are both rejected (live-confirmed). The
dirty-flag save rule: ESC never writes; RETURN writes only if [0xF63] was
touched, even by an F-key press that cycles back to the same value. The
25011968 cheat's cursor resets to 0 on a mismatch WITHOUT re-testing the
mismatched key (typing "225011968" does not trigger it) -- its lives-to-10

events.title: Decode every Atic Atac room list, and the records they name
events.message:
Decode every Atic Atac room list, and the records they name

Each room's list is a word per entry now, each assembling as the label of the
record it names -- DOOR_R03_R02, CYAN_DOOR_R6C_R03, TRAPDOOR_R03_R65,
SUIT_OF_ARMOUR_R01_R03 -- and linking to it, with a comment saying what the
half in this room is: a door and the room it leads to, a trapdoor and where it
falls, where a trapdoor from above lands, or which piece of furniture. The
rooms named link to their own lists. A room's page also lists the objects and
monsters that start there, which the list does not name: MAIN_LOOP finds them
by their own room byte.

INITIAL_STATE is generated a record to a line, each said in words: the three
slots a game fills in, every object and monster with its room and place, and
every sixteen-byte door or furniture record with its two rooms. A record's type
is read as its handler would: a door when DISPATCH_FROM_LIST's lookup reaches a
door routine, furniture when it reaches DOOR_1's draw-only tail, and named for
the picture it draws. Its old note called all 274 of the sixteen-byte records
doors; they are 205 doors and 69 pairs of furniture, 36 of the pairs two
different pieces, and it says so. The collectables are named by their code,
since the annotations name them only as a group.

Built from the tape: 30208 bytes reassemble byte-for-byte; no new warnings.

events.title: Add a map of Atic Atac's castle, floor by floor
events.message:
Add a map of Atic Atac's castle, floor by floor

The game has no map and no idea of a floor, so the map is worked out from its
doors. Every room lists what is in it (ROOM_CONTENTS); a door is two records
eight bytes apart, one in each room, with its wall in its +$05; and a record's
type is a door exactly when its handler -- ACTOR_HANDLERS + 2 * ($A2 + type),
as DISPATCH_FROM_LIST looks it up -- is one of the door routines rather than
DOOR_1's draw-only tail. Rooms are placed beside the room they were reached
from, on the side of the door; trapdoors drop a floor, and each staircase's big
door frame is taken as a floor above its other end, the reading of the six
that leaves the fewest doors out of place. Each room then takes the floor most
of its doors agree on: 149 rooms on five floors, the lowest all caves, and 6 of
199 doors that no choice of floors satisfies, marked as links elsewhere. A room
whose square is taken goes to the nearest free one.

The page draws each floor as SVG: every room in its own outline and colour from
ROOM_TABLE and ROOM_SHAPES, linked to its contents list; doors grey, locked
doors in their colour, the character doors dashed; the ways to other floors
marked with the room they reach. read_shapes now keeps each outline's groups
for it. The landing page links it.

Checked in Edge, headless.

Amiga: empty the mirror during the transfer

The transfer zeroes each mirror piece it reads, so the next drawing
viewport arrives empty: clear_image skips the shadow and the row clear

events.title: Amiga: sprites cost less Chip RAM time
events.message:
Amiga: sprites cost less Chip RAM time

The cursor, the compass, chart planets and panel icons are sprites
drawn straight on screen. Each plane word was read for the saved
background and then masked and drawn in place: three reads and two
writes. It is now read once, saved, masked and drawn in a register,
and written once.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: plots cost less Chip RAM time
events.message:
Amiga: plots cost less Chip RAM time

Dots, line pixels and the edge words of each polygon row masked and
coloured the screen word in place: two reads and two writes per
plane. They now read it once and write it once, which matters where
drawing goes straight to Chip RAM: a 68020 without Fast RAM, the
panel, charts and menus.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: the shadow carries only what changed to Chip RAM
events.message:
Amiga: the shadow carries only what changed to Chip RAM

Each Chip buffer has a Fast RAM copy of its view; frames draw into a
third. Only 16-byte pieces differing from the target's copy cross; rows
it shows empty skip the compare. Sums missed changes.

After crossing, the drawn view is the target's copy: the three rotate,
and the replaced one is cleared where it held data. One allocation holds
all of it.

Writes past the shadow into a flight view (primitives outside the live
window, shadowless frames, AMIGA_FLIP_ADDRESS users, the scroller) make
that copy unknown; its next transfer sends everything.

Frame time builds count crossed pieces.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: load files through workspace buffers, not the second screen
events.message:
Amiga: load files through workspace buffers, not the second screen

On a 68040 (ACA1240) in pal-hireslace, BITMAPS.IMG read into the
second screen sometimes arrived wrong, and the loader then searched
its offset table forever: the machine froze on the loading picture.
The bitmaps now load through a 4 KB workspace buffer and the title
through the bitmap bank, both in Fast RAM when there is some. A read
that fails or ends early quits instead of hanging.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: shadowcopy=changes|counter|all says what the shadow carries
events.message:
Amiga: shadowcopy=changes|counter|all says what the shadow carries

changes (default) carries changes, counts nothing. counter also shows
total/crossed in frame time builds. all carries every piece and shows
total/ALL, to measure the saving; only that decision differs.

events.title: Amiga: the radar costs less Chip RAM time
events.message:
Amiga: the radar costs less Chip RAM time

Each frame the radar draws and erases a stick per ship directly on
screen, in Chip RAM, where every access waits for the slow bus. It
now reads and writes each screen word once instead of three reads
and two writes, and skips the right word when the stick's head does
not reach it.

events.title: Watch MMIO accesses and trace CD32 drive commands in emulated time
events.message:
Watch MMIO accesses and trace CD32 drive commands in emulated time

Value-comparing watches cannot see a device register: they peek a word
before and after each instruction, and a register like Akiko's cannot be
peeked (reading its PIO port pops a byte), so every Akiko, CIA or Gayle
access looked like an unchanged 0000. An MMIO watch is taken at the CPU's
own bus access instead: every data access to the range (fetches
excluded) is recorded with its size, value, direction, PC, frame, beam
position and colour clock, stamped when the access completes. It stops
the machine from the Break tab ("MMIO +/-"), the console (MWATCH) and the
control protocol (break.add kind "mmio", whose stop carries the access);
COPPERLINE_DBG_MMIO logs every hit headlessly, and event.mmio streams them
without stopping.

The CD32 drive gains a host-side command trace. Each packet becomes a
record stamped when the host issued its first byte (TX DMA fetch or PIO
write, tracked through the drive's receive buffer), when the drive parsed
it, executed it and delivered its reply, when a read, play or TOC dump
delivered its first and latest unit, and when it ended, with the decoded
command, sector range, requested speed, reply status and outcome. The Bus
sets the trace clock before every register access and deferred tick, and
a countdown that expires inside a tick's batch is stamped where it
expired. The trace is an observer only: never serialized, carried across
state loads (ending what was in flight as abandoned), and it survives a
guest reset. It is the debugger's new CD tab, the console's CDTRACE,
COPPERLINE_DBG_CD, and the control protocol's cd.trace and event.cd.

Both are pure observers: a CD32 Kickstart boot with every Akiko access
logged and the trace on leaves chip RAM byte-identical at 70 s to an
uninstrumented run, and the debugger transparency test now arms MMIO
logging and streaming. An armed MMIO watch forces the precise CPU loop and
blocks run-ahead, like the other debugger hooks.

events.title: feat(app,host): per-command bookkeeping, resumed flag, save outcome, public zcolour (SQ-1545)
events.message:
feat(app,host): per-command bookkeeping, resumed flag, save outcome, public zcolour (SQ-1545)

A first headless embedder driving the session host (SQ-1537..1539) hit four
small gaps where it had to duplicate TUI logic. All four addressed:

1. Per-command bookkeeping (record_command / turns += 1 / unsaved_progress =
   true) moved from main.rs's three call sites into
   `host::turn::finish_command_turn` itself, which now runs it first thing.
   A headless caller that just does `session.submit` + `finish_command_turn`
   gets the same history/turn-count/autosave behaviour the TUI does, with no
   extra lines of its own. main.rs's slash-command branch still records into
   history before routing (a slash command never reaches
   `finish_command_turn` at all), which lands as a harmless consecutive-
   duplicate no-op when the same command is non-slash and reaches the
   function's own record (AppState::record_command already dedupes
   consecutive repeats).

2. `host::boot::BootedStory` gained a `resumed: bool` field, set when
   `cfg.auto_load` was on, an archive was present, and `Engine::restore_state`
   succeeded — a host no longer has to infer resumption from console hooks or
   re-read the archive itself.

3. `host::ingame_io::handle_save_as` now returns a `SaveAsOutcome` (Saved /
   EmptyName / Exists{path, existing_name} / Failed(reason)) alongside the
   notice it always pushes for the TUI. Existing callers that ignore the
   return value are unaffected (no #[must_use]).

4. `render::resolve_zcolour` is `pub` instead of `pub(crate)`. Left in
   `render` rather than moved to `colors.rs`: `AppState`'s own
   `transcript_styles`/`transcript_runs` already carry
   `ratatui::style::Style`/`Color`, so a host reading them already depends on
   ratatui and gains nothing from a plain-RGB variant — the only thing
   missing was visibility.

Extended tests/suites/host_turn.rs, host_boot.rs and host_session.rs per the
quest's acceptance criteria: a headless command turn's bookkeeping with no
extra caller code, resumed true/false on both a fresh and a resumed boot, a
SAVE answered to an existing name and to an unwritable directory (unix-only,
root-safe probe) both yielding the error outcome, and resolve_zcolour called
directly from an integration test.

Deviation from the brief, with reasoning: for the one main.rs call site whose
`cmd` is reassigned AFTER submit (the v6 compass-click synthesized-direction
path, SQ-0576), moving record_command inside finish_command_turn means it
now records the synthesized direction word (e.g. "north") into shell history
when the player clicked with nothing typed, where the old code recorded
nothing (record_command ran on the pre-reassignment, empty cmd). No test
covers this narrow combination either way, it is a plausible reading of that
call site's own comment ("goes through the same path as a typed command —
history"), and avoiding it would have required a second, divergent cmd
parameter just for this one caller.

Tests: cargo nextest run -p lanthorn host_boot host_turn host_session (17
passed); cargo nextest run -p lanthorn --lib --bins --features t-all with no
filter (3737 passed, 15 skipped); cargo check --all-targets and cargo clippy
-p lanthorn --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, both clean.

Completes: SQ-1545

runtime_profiles.name: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST 68000 build
runtime_profiles.notes: The shipping ST/STE binary is compiled for a bare 68000 and is explicitly described as the safe run-on-anything Atari build; a stock non-e ST is verified.

evidence.excerpt: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST — openua-atari-st-*.zip, 2 MB, colour monitor; tested on TOS 2.06, EmuTOS and TOS 1.04.
A 68000 build runs on any Atari, and a stock non-e ST is verified too.

runtime_profiles.name: Atari Falcon030 / TT030
runtime_profiles.notes: One -m68020-60 binary serves both Falcon030 and TT030; the standard target machines documented here are 68030 systems.

evidence.excerpt: Atari Falcon030 / TT030 — openua-falcon-*.zip, 4 MB, TOS 4.04 (Falcon) or 3.0x (TT). One binary serves both.
The Macintosh 68k code is retargeted to machines including the target 68020/030 family; Falcon030 and TT030 are supported backends.

runtime_profiles.name: Accelerated Atari ST / STE 020+ build
runtime_profiles.os: No extra TOS floor documented; TOS 2.06 tested
runtime_profiles.notes: On an accelerated ST/STE the Falcon/TT -m68020-60 binary detects ST hardware and selects the native ST display backend. The documentation explicitly states an 020 or better is required for this variant.

evidence.excerpt: Run the Falcon/TT zip's binary; the Falcon/TT zip is -m68020-60. Requirements are just the accelerator: an 020 or better.

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga ECS/OCS
runtime_profiles.notes: Bare-68000 ECS/OCS build; Kickstart 1.3 will not launch it. The documentation describes 7 MHz as playable, with acceleration improving comfort.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga ECS/OCS (A500+ / A600 / A2000, bare 68000) — Kickstart 2.0 or later, 2 MB; playable at 7 MHz.

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga AGA / RTG
runtime_profiles.notes: One -m68020 Amiga binary serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG, selecting the display path at runtime. The hardware guide describes memory as about 4 MB, so no exact minimum RAM value is asserted here.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga AGA (A1200 / A4000) and RTG — Kickstart 3.0+, about 4 MB; one frua serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG.
The codebase is already GCC -std=gnu99 -m68020 C.

events.title: fix(app): tighten game_echoes_command to a whole-line match, not a prefix
events.message:
fix(app): tighten game_echoes_command to a whole-line match, not a prefix

game_echoes_command decided a game self-echoed the typed command whenever its
turn output merely STARTED WITH the command word followed by a non-word
boundary. In Zork I, typing `north` from West of House prints the room
heading "North of House" — which starts with "north" — so the host wrongly
concluded the game echoed the command and suppressed its own echo, leaving no
record of what the player typed anywhere in the transcript.

A genuine self-echo (CounterfeitMonkey and the rest of the SQ-0275 family)
repeats the command as its own whole first line. Replace the prefix-plus-
boundary heuristic with an exact (trimmed, case-insensitive) comparison
against the transcript's first line, which keeps every self-echo case passing
while no longer matching a room heading, or any other output, that merely
begins with the same word.

Adds a_room_heading_starting_with_the_command_word_does_not_swallow_the_echo
to tests/suites/host_turn.rs (walks `north` from West of House in Zork I) and
a same-shape case to the existing unit tests beside the SQ-0275 family in
main.rs. Falsified: both fail against the pre-fix heuristic with the reported
symptom (the room heading merged onto the prompt line, no distinct echo) and
pass after.

Completes: SQ-1546

events.title: palette_hue: match a custom palette by hue instead of nearest colour
events.message:
palette_hue: match a custom palette by hue instead of nearest colour

The jungle's greens are muted olives, and against a palette whose only
greens are saturated - EGA's - the nearest colour is a grey. With
palette_hue=true each colour is matched on hue weighted by the
saturation both share, then saturation, then brightness, so the
olives stay green; greys and pale colours come out noisier, which is
why it is an option and nearest colour stays the default. It applies
only to custom palettes: the automatic one is built from the room's
own colours, so every entry already has a near twin.

events.title: refactor(app,mapper): wire Mapper::struct_gen into the map render memo (SQ-1544)
events.message:
refactor(app,mapper): wire Mapper::struct_gen into the map render memo (SQ-1544)

app hand-maintained its own AppState::graph_gen counter at ~15 call sites
across input.rs/loop_tick.rs/main.rs/reset.rs/host/reset.rs/host/turn.rs,
bumped by hand alongside mapper::MapGraph::struct_gen (SQ-1540), a
correctly-guarded counter that already bumps for exactly the mutations that
change what the map draws. Two counters that must be kept in sync by hand
across files is the exact smell CLAUDE.md's refactoring policy names; this
retires graph_gen and reads struct_gen off the live graph directly.

In-place mutations (rename/notes/relabel/delete/move-region/tidy-apply/
view-map/mark-maze) needed no replacement at all: cached_map_render now
reads graph.struct_gen() straight from its `graph` parameter, so removing
the hand bump just lets the graph's own counter, which was already correct,
be visible. Guarded call sites (`if rooms_before != rooms_after { bump }`)
are deleted outright for the same reason.

A wholesale mapper replacement (restore, resume, imported map, `/reset
map`) is different: struct_gen is scoped to one graph object's lifetime and
restarts at 0 on a fresh Mapper (documented on the field), so a generation
number alone can't tell a genuinely unchanged map apart from a stale cache
or in-flight job whose captured generation coincidentally matches the new
object's. AppState::invalidate_map_render() replaces every unconditional
bump at those sites (reset.rs, turn::reobserve_location, slash_dispatch's
LoadMap, main.rs's rewind) with an unconditional clear of map_render/
map_derived/render_job/tidy_job/anim_build_job instead of a number
comparison. poll_render_job now takes the live graph to compare against.

turn.rs's post_turn_bookkeeping map_changed flag (for rewind/replay
history) moves from a rooms/conns count comparison to a struct_gen
before/after diff, which the quest also flagged as a rooms/conns-count
proxy worth replacing.

Audit (also in scope): mark_random_exit/unmark_random_exit/
note_random_destination didn't bump struct_gen even though they change a
room's drawn `?` badge and its printed destination count — SQ-1540 scoped
them out. Fixed in graph.rs, guarded to bump only on a real change (not a
re-mark, not an inherited-flag-only change, since random_inherited is
never drawn). add_self_loop needed no fix: it already bumps transitively
through add_edge.

Falsified: reverted mark_random_exit to its pre-fix body and confirmed
random_exit_marks_bump_struct_gen_only_when_the_drawn_badge_changes fails;
neutered invalidate_map_render and confirmed
invalidate_map_render_defeats_a_generation_collision_after_a_wholesale_graph_swap
fails with the poisoned cache's stale room served. Both restored before
committing (graph.rs diffed byte-identical to the checkpoint).

Tests: cargo nextest run -p lanthorn-mapper (451 passed), -p lanthorn
-E 'binary(mapper_ui)' (311 passed), -p lanthorn --lib --bins --features
t-all with no filter (3737 passed, includes the new/renamed struct_gen
tests in state.rs/input.rs/host/turn.rs/reset.rs and the maze_layer_commands
integration suite). cargo check --all-targets and cargo clippy -p lanthorn
--all-targets --all-features / -p lanthorn-mapper --all-targets, both clean.

events.title: Custom room palettes from PALETTE\, and Ctrl+P to write one out
events.message:
Custom room palettes from PALETTE\, and Ctrl+P to write one out

palette_custom=true: for each room the game looks for
PALETTE\L1R45.HEX, then PALETTE\L1.HEX for the whole level, and uses
the file's 16 colours in place of the ones the quantiser would choose;
every logical colour takes the nearest of them. Level 2 is two level
files whose room numbers overlap, so its rooms carry the part too:
L2_1R17.HEX, L2_2R17.HEX. Neither file, and the room keeps the
automatic palette; the title and cutscenes always keep their own.

A file is 16 lines of RRGGBB, as Lospec and Aseprite export .hex
palettes, rounded to the STE's 4 bits a channel. Ctrl+P writes the
room's current colours to the game folder under the room's name and
says so on screen for a couple of seconds, so an author starts from
the game's own choice - or from the custom palette in use, which
round-trips exactly.

PALETTE\ is scanned once at startup, so a room change touches the disk
only when it has a file to load, and palette_st.cpp uses GEMDOS
directly: the C library's fopen converts the file date through mktime,
over 100ms a call on a 68000. The quantiser's closing steps - the
remap, its generation counters, the reconversion - are now one helper
shared by the automatic and custom paths.
events.author: neilrackett

events.title: feat(audio): decode sound with no output device; app `playback` feature (SQ-1541)
events.message:
feat(audio): decode sound with no output device; app `playback` feature (SQ-1541)

The audio crate gains a public, device-free decode API that never touches
rodio: `decode_aiff` (now public, returning `Pcm`), `tone` and `bleep` (the
Z-machine's high/low bleeps, whose 800/400 Hz / 150 ms constants the app now
reads from here instead of spelling them itself), `render_mod` (ProTracker
MOD through once, or up to a frame cap; `mod_stream` is public too), and
`Pcm::to_wav`, a RIFF 16-bit PCM encoder. Ogg stays as its bytes.

`app` depends on audio with `default-features = false` and forwards its own
features: `default = ["playback", "mod-music"]`, `playback =
["audio/playback"]`. SQ-1538's `SoundSink` already confined the device to
one place, so the gating is small: `impl SoundSink for AudioBackend` and the
device-opening `default_sound_sink` are `playback`-only, and without it the
default sink is `host::sound::Silence` (starts nothing, so no routine ever
waits); the test-only `disable_output_for_tests` calls are gated to match.
`cargo build -p lanthorn --no-default-features` no longer has rodio, cpal or
alsa-sys in its tree. The TUI keeps default features. The decoders are
re-exported from `app::host::sound` for a host's own sink.

CI gains a `no-playback` job: Linux, no libasound2-dev installed, a
`cargo tree` check that no audio device library is in the
`--no-default-features` tree, and the build itself.

Tests: tone/bleep PCM length and rate; AIFF (16-bit and 8-bit) and a tone
round-trip through the WAV encoder, checked by an independent RIFF reader;
a generated one-pattern MOD renders to exactly 64 x 6 x 882 stereo frames
(ProTracker's default speed and tempo) and a cap stops it; `Silence` starts
nothing. The audio crate's tests now also build and pass with
`--no-default-features` (one pre-existing call to the playback-only
`disable_output_for_tests` is gated), as does app's whole in-crate suite.

events.title: refactor(app): boot a story through the library with no terminal (SQ-1537)
events.message:
refactor(app): boot a story through the library with no terminal (SQ-1537)

The per-story build — mount, profile, palette, per-game overrides, engine
construction, resume archive, banner and seed turn — moves out of the
binary's startup.rs into a new library module, `app::host::boot_story`,
which returns a terminal-free `BootedStory` (engine, Mapper, seeded
AppState, paths). The TUI's `startup::boot_story` now probes the terminal
(image-protocol picker, OSC 10/11 colours, size), calls it, and does only
the terminal half: raw mode, the alternate screen, the Terminal, the
keep-it prompt for a fetched story, and printing a story that quit at boot.

- Terminal answers cross the boundary as `TerminalFacts`, which a headless
  host leaves at its default; the pre-alt-screen console lines and the
  loading spinner go through `BootHooks`; an unrecoverable failure is a
  `BootError` the TUI prints and exits 1 on, as before.
- `engine_helpers` becomes a library module (it has no terminal
  dependency and the boot restores archives through it).
- `resolve_pict_blorb`, `random_seed_line` and the trace flushes move with
  the boot; `story_screen_in` is the terminal-free half of
  `host_story_screen`, which a restart still reaches.
- Two source guards (sq1434, v6_cga_stencil_page) now read host/boot.rs.

New suite host_boot: Z-machine (Tangle.z5), Glulx (chlorophyll.gblorb)
and Scott (tiny_cave.dat) boot with no TTY to a banner and a Line read;
a missing story is an error, not an exit; and boot / two moves / resume
archive / boot again resumes the same room, transcript tail, turn count
and map, and plays the next move identically.

events.title: refactor(app): apply a turn through the library, sound through a sink (SQ-1538)
events.message:
refactor(app): apply a turn through the library, sound through a sink (SQ-1538)

The per-turn apply — `finish_command_turn`, `apply_game_driven_result`,
`finish_resumed_turn`, the post-turn bookkeeping, launch resume and the
map-maintenance scheduler — moves from the binary's turn.rs into
`app::host::turn`, with the in-game SAVE/RESTORE/filename requests a turn
opens (`host::ingame_io`). None of it called crossterm; the one terminal
fact it took was the map pane's `Rect`, used only to recenter the map, and
that is now `map_view: Option<(cols, rows)>` (`None` for a host with no
map). The TUI passes `Some(map_pane_dims(rect))`, so it recenters exactly
as before.

Each entry point returns a `TurnOutcome`: `quit`, plus a `Paging` report —
would the pager arm, is [more] suppressed, and the transcript line the
turn's output starts on — for a host that paginates by its own viewport.
The TUI's pager is unchanged and still render-driven.

Sound: `AppState::audio` is now a `host::sound::SoundSink` (tone, play a
resource, stop/pause/unpause/gain, stop_all, master volume, finished). The
rules — which resource, which channel, which finish routine or Glk notify —
stay in `play_turn_sounds` / `play_glulx_sound_ops`; the TUI's sink is
`audio::AudioBackend`, still opened lazily on the first sound played
(SQ-1423). `sound_finished` runs a finished sound's routine or notify; the
TUI's clock loop calls it for each id its device reports, and a headless
host calls it when its own player reports one.

New suite host_turn: Zork I r88 walked through the library with no map
pane — the transcript and its parallel style runs grow, the map gains the
six rooms and the trap-door passage, and the grue's direction is rolled
back off the Cellar (falsified by disabling the rollback); a
hand-assembled v5 `@sound_effect` story heard by a recording sink in the
story's order, and reporting the sample finished runs its routine.

events.title: refactor(app): clocks, pane size, saves, reset and file prompts as library APIs (SQ-1539)
events.message:
refactor(app): clocks, pane size, saves, reset and file prompts as library APIs (SQ-1539)

The rest of a session moves behind `app::host`, and the TUI's event loop
calls it instead of its private copies:

- host::clock — `refresh_input` (input-mode flags, line seeds, deadline
  re-arm; was loop_tick::refresh_engine_input), `next_deadline`, and
  `fire_due(now)` (timed-input interrupts, Glk timers, sound finishes via
  `sound_finished`, Sound2 ramps; was main::dispatch_due_game_clocks),
  plus `input_request` (what the game waits for, and its timeout). The TUI
  still adds its own picture-pacing deadline to the loop's wake time.
- host::screen — the host names the story pane in cells:
  `sync_zvm_screen_dims` (ZMSD §8.4 header, SQ-0679 floor), `resize_glulx`,
  and `set_story_pane` for both. loop_tick keeps only the drag debounce and
  the PaneRects measurement.
- host::persist — `exit_auto_save`, `exit_clear_resume_save`, `exit_save`
  (the game_ended choice), `save_state_now`, `restore_file`,
  `answer_ingame_restore` and `load_save` (the saves manager's Load). The
  TUI's lifecycle.rs wraps them with the termination-watchdog guard and
  its stderr lines; `/restore-state` and the saves manager call them.
- host::reset — `reset_game(…, terminal_size, ResetOptions { clear_map,
  delete_data })`; the TUI's reset.rs passes the live terminal size. The
  SQ-1061 source guard now checks both halves (the library measures the
  pane through `story_screen_in`, the TUI hands it the live size), and
  `startup::host_story_screen` is gone with its last caller.
- host::ingame_io — `resolve_pending` (the resolve-and-persist the TUI ran
  after six dialog paths), `pending_file_prompt` and `answer_file_prompt`
  for a host that answers the game's SAVE/RESTORE/create_by_prompt with a
  name or a cancel.

The clock dispatch tests moved into host::clock with the code.

New suite host_session: a hand-assembled v5 timed read_char fires its
routine through refresh_input/next_deadline/fire_due and keeps waiting;
Kerkerkruip's timer-driven intro moves the screen on host ticks alone
(skips when absent); the host sets a v5 story's header size; an exit save
is what the next boot resumes (then one more move matches); a reset with
clear_map restores the banner, turn 0 and a one-room map; Spider and Web's
own SAVE answered by name writes the .lanthorn a later RESTORE answered by
name reads back; and a cancelled SAVE hands the game its prompt back.

events.title: Count the coverage honestly, and sweep the port clean
events.message:
Count the coverage honestly, and sweep the port clean

The coverage table is real now: docs/COVERAGE.md lists the disc's 382 routine
files and classifies them - 112 named in the port, the rest the drawing, text,
sound and loader machinery whose behaviour the port carries under modern names.
The README's story numbers ("447 subroutines, 161 named") are the measured
figures now, and the table's method is written beside them.

The nearest-reachable-system rule lived in two places, the flight scene and the
scene factory, and each copy could have drifted; the one rule is Galaxy's now,
with both callers reading it. The dead code went: SceneFactory.Create, the
never-called viewer knobs, GameSession.IsWanted, Galaxy.DistanceLightYears,
the station's write-only SpinRoll, ShipDataBlock.FlagDocking and
FlightSim.EscapePodLaunchedThisFrame - a value written by the sim and read by
nobody, the exact pattern the README's own rule 2 warns about, one more of the
same shape swept before it could mislead anyone.

The orientation convention the renderer folds into its own x axis is now
written where the next reader will find it: RigidFrame's side is roof x nose,
the negative of the disc's sidev, and the ship viewer verified the pipeline
against the disc's models, so the sign is the drawing's convention.

The extractor no longer guesses whose home directory its source library lives
in: with no path and no ELITE_SOURCE_LIBRARY it explains what it needs.

And the flight controls - the roll and pitch angle tables, BUMP2 and REDU2's
recentre, the damping - and the missiles' steering have their own tests, the
genuine gaps in the suite; the earlier sweep's "untested" list had been
outdated by three rounds of tests that grew in the meantime.

437 tests pass.

events.title: Review fixes: SDL build, true level headroom, one VBL per push
events.message:
Review fixes: SDL build, true level headroom, one VBL per push

The memory log's hook in stepLogic was not fenced, so the SDL build
no longer compiled; and it ran before the level's first room was
decoded, which is what allocates the tile pool, so level 1's figure
left out 96K. Measured after the room, level 1 is the tightest at 2MB
with music and both borders. The README now says a 2MB machine is a
tight fit rather than putting a number on it.

With a border open, a scene's first push waited for the VBL twice -
once in stShow and again inside copyRectPlanar's full-page sync - a
lost frame per scene. stShow now leaves a full page to that sync.

double_buffer: Fill maps the rows outside its window to row 0, so a
copy running past the window recorded its damage as a backwards
range and the pages drifted apart; damage now covers the rows that
are displayed. And the palette is written after the flip, not before,
where it recoloured the old picture until the VBL.

Tidied from the review: ST_pageBand and a leftover include removed,
ST_copyPage's unreachable band copy and ST_pageShowRect's untracked
branch folded away, comments still describing the abandoned per-row
and per-block masks rewritten, the whole-rows threshold named,
pageTouch returns first when no scene is running (every in-game
sprite and fill called it), and the unused .prf track names left out
of the ST build.

gateboy: declare its 63 gate-level columns as extension fields

GateBoy's columns outside the DMG vocabulary (bus_addr, op_state,

counters/flags, the IRQ/halt flags, vram_* and apu_write_*) are now

header fields like vram_*.

defs; describe rejects an extension that shadows a vocabulary name. The
FFI exposes a profile's per-adapter [fields.extensions] names
(morepork_profile_num_extensions / morepork_profile_extension_name),
which the adapter appends to its field list.

not available); only its header-building code was compiled standalone
against the FFI and produced a writable trace.

events.title: Re-found the system vocabulary on missingno's state schemas
events.message:
Re-found the system vocabulary on missingno's state schemas

The library keeps no field tables of its own: a trace's system, ISA,
instruction-address column and entry hint are read from its header, and
a header without field definitions is an error. A new morepork-systems
registry obtains each system's schema from missingno's crates and types a
producer's columns against it, the shared trace observations, and the
system's capture-bridge observations; the CLI moves to morepork-cli and
the FFI types adapter columns through the registry, rejecting unknown
names. Every adapter writes the schema's names (the Z80/TI-VDP family
splits the VDP status byte into the schema's flags and index; the VCS
adapters take the RIOT and beam names), the ColecoVision id is
`colecovision` with `coleco` kept as a CLI alias, and the missingno
adapter gains SG-1000 and ColecoVision drivers for the corpus scripts.
