events.title: Prepare the 1.6.0 release
events.message:
Prepare the 1.6.0 release

Records 1.6.0 in every place a release identifies itself: VERSION, the
pinned version test, the AppStream release history, the apt commands in the
README, the in-app Help and the installation and Linux desktop guides, the
HFE guide, the health-response example, the release-checklist example and
the documentation index.

A feature release, covering #31. Drives attached through USB open in place,
and can be exported to an image file or copied onto another drive. SFS, PFS3
and the FFS long-filename variants are read and written, Directory Cache
volumes keep their caches, and copying between panes works again for
floppies and now works for partitions.

The notes call out the changes to how images are written: Directory Cache
caches are now maintained, the long-filename variants are writable, and the
FFS hardfile repairs no longer touch SFS or PFS3 volumes. They also say
plainly that long-filename volumes have not been checked by a real AmigaOS
3.2 FastFileSystem.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: peteclarke-del

events.title: Open drives attached through USB, and fix copying between panes
events.message:
Open drives attached through USB, and fix copying between panes

A hard drive or memory card from an Amiga, attached through a USB adapter,
can now be opened where it is from Add Pane or File -> Open attached drive.
Only disks behind a USB controller are listed. A drive opens read-only, has
no undo, and takes changes only once Allow writes is chosen; one that Linux
has mounted is refused. Linux gives whole drives to the administrator, so
the package carries a udev rule for the desktop user, documented but not
installed.

A drive can be copied out and duplicated without passing through the page:

- File -> Export drive to image file streams the drive, as its partition
  table describes it or every byte of it, or one partition with a .geo
  sidecar, to a file chosen in a native Save dialog. Empty space is not
  written, and a stopped copy leaves no file behind.
- File -> Copy drive to another drive writes a verified copy over another
  attached drive. The target is chosen from the attached-drive list, must
  be large enough, unmounted and writable, and is named again before it is
  erased. Every byte is written, then read back from the drive and compared.

SFS and PFS3 volumes with no partition table open as single volumes, and
each volume and partition now reports its own filing system and name
limit, so SFS and PFS3 partitions allow long names in every dialog. A
partition for another system is refused with its DOS type rather than an
engine error. The FFS hardfile repairs that run when an image is saved no
longer touch SFS or PFS3 volumes, whose root block is not where FFS keeps
it.

Copying between panes is fixed:

- A copy whose target was a partition went to the engine's command line,
  which addresses the whole drive, and failed on its partition table.
- The direct copy used for floppies and single volumes called a method
  that did not exist, so it has failed since 1.1.1.
- Files are read one at a time rather than all before writing, and a copy
  that would replace a file, use a name the target cannot hold or overrun
  its free space is refused before anything is written.
- A drop is one tracked operation that shows each file and can be stopped
  from Jobs.
- In the Linux desktop a multi-file drag arrived as its first file alone,
  and its drag image stayed on screen. The GTK drop target now leaves drags
  that began in the window to the page, and the page keeps its own record
  of what is being dragged.
- Whole partitions can be dragged, from the partition table or a partition
  pane, into a drawer or onto another drive's partition, including another
  partition of the same drive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: peteclarke-del

events.title: Read and write PFS3, long-filename and Directory Cache volumes
events.message:
Read and write PFS3, long-filename and Directory Cache volumes

Large Amiga partitions are usually PFS3 or SFS, and amiganut could only
name PFS3. It now reads and writes PFS3 volumes in place, bare or inside
an RDB partition, for the PFS\1, PFS\2, PFS\3 and PDS\3 DOS types. Changes
are made copy-on-write in the handler's own order, with the root block
written last, and a volume the handler left with a postponed operation is
opened read-only. Deleted files are freed at once rather than moved to
the deleted-files drawer, and new links are not created. The work was
checked against pfs3aio 19.2 on an emulated A1200: DiskValid passed every
volume built and changed here, and every change pfs3aio then made read
back and validated.

Directory Cache volumes (DOS\4, DOS\5) were listed as writable, but no
change updated the cache, so a real machine listed a drawer as it used to
be. Every change now keeps each directory's cache blocks exact, validate
compares them with the hash chains, and rebuild_dircache repairs a volume
left stale. The Kickstart 3.1 FastFileSystem listed volumes written here
without a difference, and its own changes validated cleanly afterwards.

Long-filename volumes (DOS\6, DOS\7) are read and written with names of
up to 107 characters, following the layout amitools documents. No AmigaOS
3.2 FastFileSystem has yet checked a volume written here. is_dircache no
longer reports these two types as Directory Cache.

Also:

- The Kickstart probe declines anything larger than a ROM can be before
  reading it. It read its whole input, and mounting a partition of a
  256 GB drive attached over USB read the drive into memory.
- The FFS bitmap is decoded and encoded a long at a time, and only the
  bitmap blocks that changed are written back. Rewriting every one on
  each flush made copying many files take longer the larger the volume.
- Copy collection can carry each file's size instead of its bytes, so a
  tree from a hard-drive partition is not held in memory before writing.
- A block device is accepted wherever an image file is.

events.title: Draw the disc's own dials, bulbs, crosshair and planet lines
events.message:
Draw the disc's own dials, bulbs, crosshair and planet lines

The dashboard gains the disc's altitude bar: part 15's ALTIT, which starts at
&FF - "a long way above" - and otherwise holds LL5's square root of the sum of
the squared high bytes of the planet's distance, less the 37 the SBC #36 takes
with the carry clear. Aligning the bar aligned the crash test with it: the
original's BCC on the subtraction going negative crashes at the surface
itself, and the port crashed a byte further out. The bar carries a test
working the disc's own figures by hand.

The two indicator bulbs above the energy banks are the disc's ECBLB and SPBLB:
"E" lights while the E.C.M. runs, "S" while the space station is about.

The laser crosshair is the disc's own SIGHT: a cross drawn at size 20 and again
at size 10, which on the BBC erases the middle of itself and leaves four arms
with a gap in the middle - "draw crosshairs of size 10 at the same location,
which will remove the centre part from the laser crosshairs, leaving a gap in
the middle". It draws only when the view we are looking through has a laser
fitted, as SIGHT's own "LDA LASER,Y / BEQ LO2" does.

The planet draws PL9 part 2's two meridians through its disc, from its own
orientation vectors - the disc feeds PLS5 roofv's ratios and then sidev's, and
the planet's orientation on the disc is ZINF's identity, nosev pointing at us,
so the two meridians draw as a vertical and a horizontal line through the disc,
which is the planet's look. This replaces the port's soft ring for the second
planet type's extra line, which had no counterpart in the disc's code.

The sound table's audit found it already byte-verified: all ten of the disc's
SFX entries match variable/sfx.asm in the tests, and the audit's job turned out
to be the last trigger the disc's own code makes - the docking dent now makes
EXNO3's pair of explosion entries, as MA63 does.

The gamepad maps the rest of the flight's keys: the left shoulder locks a
missile, X fires one, Y fires the E.C.M., Start engages the docking computer,
Back cancels it, and the right stick looks through the four windows.

427 tests pass.

events.title: powermonger: how land changes side, proven (field conquest $539a, heartbeat revolt); $4f68 decoded
events.message:
powermonger: how land changes side, proven (field conquest $539a, heartbeat revolt); $4f68 decoded

- Mode $2c ($152f8) picks targets through $4f68's 38(A1) table at $4fa2 (hunt a lord / a group /
  one target, follow, shoot, walk to, help allies, group done). A lord is conquered when every man
  of his settlements is dead or routed: $5240 -> $539a -> $550e, new side = the attacker's.
  The mission-1 win was this path ($53f6 1 hit, $158cc 0).
- The heartbeat revolt also runs from mode $7e (a man idle at home, no $57fd0 gate): the spy
  order's captain pulsed lord 0 (608) into side (22 mod 4)+1 = 3. Hunger adds +2, plenty -1.
- Gate py/diff_4f68.py: 1804/1804 over 192 states (170 natural); transcription merged into
  tools/pm_fsm_ref.py. call_35f4 gains the $3720 wait-stamp write; all 13 older gates unchanged.

events.title: build: give the installer licence a name CPack can use, and no dmg SLA
events.message:
build: give the installer licence a name CPack can use, and no dmg SLA

Pointing CPACK_RESOURCE_FILE_LICENSE at the repository's LICENSE broke both
non-Linux legs of the 0.8.4 release, in two different ways, and neither is
visible from Linux.

CPackWIX converts the licence resource to RTF by extension and accepts .txt or
.rtf. LICENSE has no extension at all, so the MSI failed with "unsupported WiX
License file extension ''" - it only ever worked before because CMake's own
placeholder is named CPack.GenericLicense.txt. It is now copied to license.txt
in the build tree at configure time: one licence text to maintain, and an
extension CPack understands.

CPack.cmake:880 enables a dmg Software Licence Agreement whenever the licence
resource is anything other than that placeholder and CMP0133 is not NEW. An SLA
cannot be accepted headlessly, so hdiutil attach answered "attach canceled" and
the macOS leg could neither verify nor publish its dmg. The first response to
that was a five-attempt retry, which is the wrong answer to a deterministic
error; the retry is gone and the SLA is off. The licence still travels inside
the bundle - LICENSE, NOTICE and the generated THIRD-PARTY.txt - which the dmg
step already asserts.

events.title: build: narrow the /usr/lib guard to shared objects, and retry hdiutil attach
events.message:
build: narrow the /usr/lib guard to shared objects, and retry hdiutil attach

Two failures from the 0.8.4 release attempt, both in verification rather than
in what ships.

The /usr/lib guard fired on /usr/lib/.build-id, which rpmbuild adds for its
debuginfo links on the runner - the local rpmbuild does not, which is why the
dry run of this step passed. A directory is not cached by ldconfig and cannot
be handed to another application, so the check now matches shared objects,
which is the actual hazard: it still fires on the 0.8.3 layout it exists to
prevent, and passes on the private prefix with .build-id beside it.

hdiutil attach died with "attach canceled" on a dmg CPack had just reported as
generated, eleven seconds earlier. CPack's DragNDrop generator attaches the
image itself to write its .DS_Store and detaches it again, and the device can
still be busy a moment later, so the attach is retried at an absolute
mountpoint. A genuinely broken image fails all five attempts, so the retry
cannot mask one.

events.title: release: 0.8.4
events.message:
release: 0.8.4

0.8.3's deb could not be installed at all: it carried the build host's
copyright file for every library the bundle links, into paths dpkg knows
belong to installed packages, and dpkg refuses to take a file from another
package. The packages also installed their Qt, glib and D-Bus into /usr/lib,
where ldconfig hands them to every other application on the machine, and no
package stated a name, an author or a licence that a software centre could
read. All three are fixed here: the installers stage a private prefix, the
release workflow installs the deb to prove it, and PiST ships AppStream
metadata, a DEP-5 copyright and its own licence text as the installer
licence. Assets are named PiST-<version>-<platform>.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: docs: record the installer layout, and what an AppImage cannot do
events.message:
docs: record the installer layout, and what an AppImage cannot do

The install text named an AppImage without a version, because that is what the
workflow produced. It carries one now, so the snippets use a glob rather than a
literal file name: naming an artifact a release does not actually ship has been
a defect here before, and the release body is published verbatim with nothing
in the release checklist that would remind anyone to bump it.

Both the README and the release body now say what an AppImage cannot do -
register itself with the desktop - and name what can: AppImageLauncher,
appimaged, or the deb and rpm. That is what makes the packages the recommended
route on Linux, and it is the answer to "installing the AppImage works but
nothing appears in the menu".

PLAN.md Phase 4 records the facts the packaging now rests on: the dpkg rule
that made 0.8.3 uninstallable, the ldconfig precedence that made /usr/lib
unsafe, the private prefix and why moving the subtree rigidly preserves the
rpath and qt.conf, the AppStream id choice, the empty CFBundleIdentifier, and
the measured portal behaviour behind the conditional desktop-file name. NOTICE
records where the relocated distro copyright texts live, and why the AppImage
keeps them where linuxdeploy put them.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: ui: state the desktop-file name so Wayland groups the window
events.message:
ui: state the desktop-file name so Wayland groups the window

On Wayland the app_id came from the application name, "PiST", which matches no
desktop entry, so the taskbar showed a generic icon and would not group the
window under the launcher. Under X11 nothing was wrong: xprop on the 0.8.3
binary reports WM_CLASS "pist", "PiST", because Qt derives res_name from the
executable name rather than from setApplicationName. pist.desktop now states
that with StartupWMClass=pist.

setDesktopFileName() is called before the application object exists, which is
when Qt reads it, and only when an entry is actually installed - pist.desktop,
or the appimagekit_pist.desktop that AppImageLauncher generates for an
integrated AppImage. An unconditional call was measured to make the desktop
portal fail to register the app ID on every build-tree and unintegrated-AppImage
start, which is a warning printed for a name nothing on that system can
resolve. With the guard, a run that has no entry stays silent and a run that
has one claims exactly that name.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: packaging: name the product PiST, its author Koala Software, and its licence
events.message:
packaging: name the product PiST, its author Koala Software, and its licence

A software centre had nothing to read. The deb reported the name its file
happened to carry and "Unknown Author", and no licence anywhere: the package
had no AppStream metadata at all, CPACK_RESOURCE_FILE_LICENSE was still CMake's
CPack.GenericLicense.txt placeholder, and there was no DEP-5 copyright file,
which is where Debian policy puts the statement. The RPM's vendor was the
literal string "unknown", CPACK_PACKAGE_VENDOR being the product name rather
than an author.

CPACK_PACKAGE_NAME is now the product name an installer shows - PiST, in the
MSI product name, the NSIS/STGZ install directory and the dmg volume - and
CPACK_PACKAGE_VENDOR the author, which is what WIX.template.in writes as the
MSI Manufacturer and CPackRPM as the Vendor. The distro package names are
spelled out lowercase, as Debian policy requires; CPackDeb lowercases whatever
it is given and CPackRPM does not. On macOS the bundle presented itself as
"pist" and shipped an empty CFBundleIdentifier, because neither
MACOSX_BUNDLE_BUNDLE_NAME nor MACOSX_BUNDLE_GUI_IDENTIFIER was ever set.

packaging/io.github.idontwantyourspamthanks.pist.metainfo.xml carries the name,
the developer and the licence a store displays. Its id is reverse-DNS and the
menu entry stays pist.desktop, joined by <launchable>: a flat id also merges,
but appstreamcli then fails validation, which is a trap for whoever adds a CI
gate later. The developer is stated twice, because Ubuntu 22.04's AppStream
0.16 - the oldest release these packages support - cannot read the 1.0 tag.

packaging/copyright is the DEP-5 statement, installed beside LICENSE and
NOTICE. Its Files patterns are layout-agnostic (*/vasmm68k_mot, */libQt6*)
because that one file ships in packages with three different layouts, and a
pattern naming usr/bin/ would silently stop matching the installers' private
prefix - leaving the non-free assembler and linker claimed by the GPL-2+
catch-all, which is the one thing the file exists to prevent.

The deb's description was mangled too: it was assembled from five adjacent
quoted arguments, which set() joins into a list, so the semicolons reached the
control file as a literal "; " at the head of every continuation line. It is
one multi-line string now, shared with the rpm so the two cannot drift.

The icons are installed at 128, 256 and 512 px instead of leaving the hicolor
directories the AppImage deployer creates empty.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: build: stage the deb and rpm from a private prefix
events.message:
build: stage the deb and rpm from a private prefix

The 0.8.3 deb could not be installed. It was staged straight from the AppDir
the AppImage is built from, and linuxdeploy copies the build host's copyright
file for every library it bundles into usr/share/doc/<package>/. Inside an
AppImage that is attribution; inside a .deb those are paths dpkg knows belong
to libglib2.0-0, libpulse0, libxcb-* and fifty more installed packages, and
dpkg will not take a file away from another package:

  trying to overwrite '/usr/share/doc/libglib2.0-0/copyright', which is also
  in package libglib2.0-0

Nothing in the workflow could see it: the verification extracted the package
with dpkg-deb -x and ran the binary from the extracted tree, which never asks
dpkg whether the files are free to take.

Two more defects came out of the same stage. The AppImage's own plumbing was
installed into / - AppRun, AppRun.wrapped, .DirIcon, apprun-hooks/ and the
root-level pist.desktop and pist.svg symlinks. And the bundle's 74 libraries
sat in /usr/lib, which ldconfig scans before the multiarch directory: with two
copies of a soname in the cache the /usr/lib one is listed first and is what
ld.so resolves, so the package made itself the system-wide provider of
libQt6Core.so.6, libglib-2.0.so.0 and libdbus-1.so.3 for every other
application on the machine.

The installers now stage /usr/lib/pist - Debian's private-library convention,
and a directory ldconfig does not recurse into - holding bin/, lib/, plugins/
and the ROM, with only pist and pist-mcp symlinked into /usr/bin so the bundled
hatari, vasm and vlink cannot shadow a user's own. The subtree moves rigidly,
which is what keeps it working: the $ORIGIN/../lib rpath and the qt.conf
linuxdeploy wrote beside the binary (Prefix = ../, Plugins = plugins) resolve
inside the prefix unchanged, and the ROM walk finds share/emutos two levels up.
The foreign copyright texts move to doc/pist/licenses/distro/ rather than being
dropped: they are the only licence texts for the transitive system libraries
the bundle carries, which collect-notices.py does not attest.

Verified against the 0.8.3 artifact. The packaged binary runs from the new
layout under xvfb, resolving the assembler, linker, hrdb emulator and EmuTOS
inside it; a Prefix one level deeper aborts with "Could not find the Qt
platform plugin xcb", which is why this runs under xvfb rather than offscreen,
the offscreen plugin not being bundled. Rebuilt from the same content, the
package installs into a dpkg database that owns the colliding path, where
0.8.3's does not.

The step now installs the deb on the runner and removes it again. The runner
has the very packages whose copyright files used to collide, so that is the
check that fails if a distro-owned path ever returns to the stage. It also
asserts the control fields, the rpm's name, licence and vendor, and that
nothing is owned directly under /usr/lib.

Asset names lose the tag's "v": github.ref_name interpolated verbatim is what
produced pist-v0.8.3-linux-amd64.deb, and a store truncating that at the first
dot is what reported a package called "pist-v0". Every artifact is now
PiST-<version>-<platform>, the version derived once, and VERSION is exported to
appimagetool so the AppImage carries it too instead of shipping unversioned.

The deb self-containment loop asserted nothing: it tested the same pattern

events.title: Stage the mission briefings as the disc's docked code stages them
events.message:
Stage the mission briefings as the disc's docked code stages them

The mission business on docking no longer ends in a one-line message: the disc's
own five staged screens are the reward. DOENTRY's order of business is the
port's now - BRIEF for mission 1's offer (which sets bit 0 of TP before it
prints anything, so the mission is accepted the moment the briefing is staged,
as the disc accepts it), BRIEF2's initial contact for mission 2, BRIEF3 when
the plans are picked up, and DEBRIEF and DEBRIEF2 to pay the two thank-yous.

The briefing scene runs the disc's own order of business: BRIS's "INCOMING
MESSAGE" banner, up for the two seconds its DELAY waits; then mission 1's
Constrictor, set up at 256 units and rotated for 64 iterations with roll and
pitch counters of &7F that never damp, as BRL1 has it; then BRL2's drift - two
z_lo steps and one y_lo a time, y capped at 112 - until it is near the top of
the screen; and then the token's own text, cut into pages at the points the
printer's events report, with jump token 22 showing the ship and waiting for a
key press, and 24 just waiting. Every briefing ends at the Status Mode screen,
which is BRP's own exit.

Finding it found a latent bug in the printer: the events were recorded as the
text printed, but the tidy that follows collapses runs of spaces and trims the
ends, so an event could sit past the returned text's end - the briefing's last
"show ship and wait" token does exactly that, and the pagination crashed on it.
The events are clamped into the tidied text now.

426 tests pass, with the mission flow tests asserting the staged tokens: 10
with the Constrictor for the offer, 11 for mission 2's contact, 222 for the
plans, 15 and 223 for the debriefs.

feat(64-12): GREEN - gate the relay attach on the emulator leg actually connecting (G-64-4)

- broker-relay.mts: dialEmulatorLeg() is the one place this broker waits
  for the emulator leg to become connectable -- retries ECONNREFUSED at
  a short fixed interval (DEFAULT_RELAY_DIAL_RETRY_MS, 50ms) up to a
  bounded deadline (DEFAULT_RELAY_DIAL_DEADLINE_MS, 5000ms); any other
  connect error fails at once. spliceRelay() no longer dials -- it takes
  an already-connected emulator socket
- vice-broker.mts: handleRelayAttach() is now async. Every synchronous
  refusal (unknown target, no holder, handle mismatch, already attached,
  no text-monitor port) is unchanged and still runs before any await.
  On success it marks the channel attached, pauses the client leg, awaits
  the bounded dial with an abandonment predicate (client leg destroyed,
  or the instance/holder identity this attach validated no longer
  matches live state), re-checks that predicate on connect, and returns
  a `start` continuation rather than splicing directly
- broker-control.mts: onRelayAttach/RelayAttachOutcome widened to allow a
  Promise; the `attach` dispatch arm awaits the outcome, writes
  `attached` BEFORE calling the success continuation (so that line
  precedes any emulator byte in program order), and resumes the socket's
  line reader on a refusal
- host-tool-transport.test.ts: `ok: false as const` (not just `code`) is
  now required on its onRelayAttach stub -- RelayAttachOutcome's `ok:
  true` branch gaining a required `start` field stops TypeScript's usual
  leniency for a two-branch boolean-discriminated union from accepting
  an inferred, widened `{ ok: boolean }` return type
- resources/{broker-relay,vice-broker,broker-control}.mjs regenerated

The RED test committed previously now passes: a binary attach sent before
the emulator's port is bound is answered only after the bind, and the
stock handshake's first PING is answered, with zero incident records

events.title: Run the disc's own death, hangar and pause, and let a harness drive the game
events.message:
Run the disc's own death, hangar and pause, and let a harness drive the game

The death is no longer a message. The disc's DEATH hides the dashboard, prints
GAME OVER, and keeps running its flight loop for 5.1 seconds while five bits of
debris - a cargo canister or an alloy plate on the toss of a coin, half of them
exploding, pointed away from the wreck at double the speed, at Ze's own
coordinates - drift off it; the game-over screen comes after, as DEATH2 does.

Docking now shows the ship hangar, as the disc's DOENTRY does while the docked
code loads: half the time a group from the HATB table (a Shuttle and a
Transporter, three canisters, a Transporter and a Cobra Mk III, a Viper and a
Krait), half the time a solitary ship or an empty bay, every ship spun on the
deck, with HAS1's own heights off the ground. The bay picture itself is an I/O
processor image the port does not ship, so the bay's floor is a converging grid,
and that is recorded in DIVERGENCES.md.

Finding the hangar found a real bug in the docking sequence: the state that
keeps the docking check from firing again covered only the rings, not the
hangar, so the check fired again while we sat parked at the slot - the rings
came back up and the hangar flickered between them, for ever. The hangar is
part of the docking sequence now, and the tunnel-hangar-market flow verifies
clean from the harness.

The disc's pause arrives: backspace (for COPY) stops the flight loop, DELETE
starts it again, and while it is stopped Q silences the sound, S brings it
back, A toggles the keyboard's auto-recentre and CAPS LOCK toggles flight
damping - the disc's own configuration keys, and the two toggles the
simulation modelled but nothing could reach. A PC keyboard has no COPY, and
the disc's five hardware keys (bitstik, author names, flashing bars, joystick)
have nothing to configure here, so that is recorded as a departure.

Also in this round: the charts' O and F keys - O snaps the crosshairs onto the
current system, the disc's ping, and F searches for a system by name, the disc
docked code's HME2, saying "UNKNOWN PLANET" to a low beep on a miss; CTRL-L
loads the commander from any docked screen, the load half of the disc's docked
file menu; and the development harness.

The harness is --dev-server <port>: a small HTTP server that drives the live
game from outside. /status asks where things stand, /step advances whole drawn
frames at a fixed sixtieth, /screenshot writes the next frame, and /launch,
/dock, /autopilot and /pause act through the game's own keys. A paused game
still answers /step, which is how a mid-sequence frame is caught atomically
with step?screenshot=. The README documents it with a worked example; it is
how the docking sequence, the hangar and the death animation are checked now.

426 tests pass.

events.title: zxn: missing nextreg constants, and a fix to REG_TILEMAP_OFFSET_X_LSB
events.message:
zxn: missing nextreg constants, and a fix to REG_TILEMAP_OFFSET_X_LSB

Adds the registers and value constants listed in nextreg.txt that the zxn
target had no name for, following the header-file approach introduced in #2773:
the constants live in .h files under target/zxn/config and config_zxn_from_headers.m4
turns them into the C and assembler config files.

New headers:
  config_zxn_ula.h          0x68 ULA Control, 0x69 Display Control 1
  config_zxn_layer_2_control.h  0x70 Layer 2 Control, 0x71 Layer 2 X Scroll MSB
  config_zxn_interrupt.h    0xC0 Interrupt Control, 0xC4-0xC6 INT EN,
                            0xC8-0xCA INT Status, 0xCC-0xCE DMA INT EN,
                            0x64 Vertical Line Count Offset
  config_zxn_keyboard.h     0xB0/0xB1 Extended Keys
  config_zxn_peripheral.h   0x0A Peripheral 5 Setting
  config_zxn_audio.h        0x2C/0x2E DAC B/C mirrors

config_zxn_tilemap.h gains 0x6B Tilemap Control, 0x6C Default Tilemap
Attribute, 0x6E Tilemap Base Address and 0x6F Tile Definitions Base Address.

It also corrects REG_TILEMAP_OFFSET_X_LSB, which I introduced in #2773 as 0x3.
Nextreg 0x30 is Tilemap X Scroll LSB; 0x03 is Set Machine Type, so a write
meant to scroll the tilemap landed on the machine type and display timing
register. The MSB half of the pair is 0x2F, which makes 0x30 the intended
value.

Values are taken from the ZX Spectrum Next FPGA register reference
(cores/zxnext/nextreg.txt). Verified by running the three m4 config passes
(CFG_C_DEF, CFG_ASM_DEF, CFG_ASM_PUB) and checking the generated definitions
for correct values and no duplicate symbols.

doc/target/zxn/ adds a generated markdown rendering of the register reference
annotated with the z88dk constant for each register and bit value, plus the
script that produces it. nextreg.txt itself is not vendored; the script takes
its path and the header comment says where to fetch it.

Label every address The Hobbit's code and comments use

Every operand that is an address now assembles as a label, and every address
the comments mention is a #R reference, so the asm reads it as a label and the
HTML links it. What is left as a number is a number: word references, a port,
constants and negative offsets.

- The variables at $B6DA-$B71E, 48 of them, each labelled (ACTION, TARGET,
  PLAYER_AT, DOING_IT...), and the work areas the generated control file took
  for unused -- the AND checkpoint, the two windows' cursors, the fill's seed
  flags, MOVE's and CHARACTERS_ACT's bytes -- given blocks and labels. PHRASES
  is worked out field by field; ENDINGS is 24 bytes, followed by ORDER_COUNT;
  the frames below COMMAND_FRAME are a block of their own.
- The generators label any record field the code or a comment names: object
  fields (PLAYER_WHERE, RED_GOLDEN_DRAGON_FLAGS), room descriptions and exits,
  the characters' slots, Bard's rewritten script step. Room descriptions are
  DEFWs to their messages. The timers are laid out field by field, their
  routines as DEFWs.
- Messages are named from their text (MSG_YOU_HEAR_A_NOISE), including the
  ways into the middle of one; $ADC4 is a sixth. Script jump targets are named
  after their table (GANDALF_F, GOBLINS_A). The printed-word list is decoded a
  word to a line, by PRINT_WORD's own rule for a third letter.
- Code other code writes into, or enters part-way, is labelled and written as
  label plus offset (LOCK_BIT_OP+3, SHUT_ROAD+2, OBJECT_INDEX-3); the 83
  numbered entry points other routines use are named (RUN_MESSAGE_HL,
  PRINT_WORD_DE, NEXT_CHARACTER).
- Three comment addresses were off: the title screen waits at $6C6D, not
  $6C60; PRINT_WORD's second entry is $74C1 and the class dispatch $75C1.
  ROOM_PREPOSITIONS held OUTSIDE as a wrong label, now kept a number.

events.title: Flow Control Macros: Introduce typed comparisons
events.message:
Flow Control Macros: Introduce typed comparisons

Instead of:

  IF scmp16 var1, var2 : NEG

... where you need to remember that NEG means "less than" for 16-bit
signed comparisons, and that you need to use ecmp16 if you want equality,
you can now write:

  IF s16 var1 < var2

The microsyntax is:

  IF <type> <arg1> <op> <arg2>

Where type is one of: u8 u16 s16

And op is: = <> < >=

This plugs into the existing parser so NOT, OR and AND work too.

No binary changes (except for the tests)

events.title: fix(drive): VIA2 port B is live without a disk (BUG-062)
events.message:
fix(drive): VIA2 port B is live without a disk (BUG-062)

TRX64 skipped VIA2's store_prb and undump_prb while the drive had no disk, a
guard from the TS port; VICE's drive is live either way. The DOS's power-on
"motor off" was lost whenever the disk came later, so the rotation ran while
the pin said off, and a restore (which re-derives the motor from the pin)
left the straight run. Head steps and zone changes made with no disk in were
lost the same way.

New gate: a drive that never spun restores cycle for cycle (red before: apart
after frame 47). snapshot_roundtrip_fidelity's drive-active scenario never
pressed RETURN (nine keys for a ten-key buffer) and passed only through this
bug; it now enters the command and the drive really seeks.

events.title: Animate The Hobbit's pictures as the game draws them, and decode their commands
events.message:
Animate The Hobbit's pictures as the game draws them, and decode their commands

Each location's picture is now captured frame by frame while the game's own
DRAW_LOCATION_PICTURE draws it in the simulator, one frame per 50 Hz frame
interrupt, and saved as a GIF that loops at the game's own speed -- slow
fills and all -- holding the finished picture for three seconds before it
starts again. The Locations page shows these (a click restarts one) with
how long each takes to draw, and each picture's block in the disassembly
opens with its animation.

The picture streams, which were rows of bytes, are now a line per command
in words: the border and starting attribute, MOVE to x, y, LINE of n
pixels in a direction (diagonally, or stepping the other way every n),
FILL with a colour from a point, PAINT a colour along a path of cells, and
the end. Each block's title names its location.

Frames are made with PIL's own operations -- the bitmap as a mask choosing
between ink and paper layers blown up from the attributes -- since there
are some hundreds per picture.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte; Bag End's animation sampled -- walls,
door, then the floor filling -- and drawn in 6.8 s, as measured earlier.

The window scaled the renderer's output-mode image, which had already

each C64 pixel was rounded twice and the font came out uneven.
Renderer::render_scaled maps each target pixel straight to its C64 pixel
and blends the overlay, drawn at canvas size, over it; render() is that
at canvas size and unchanged.

events.title: Βήμα 26: ο θόλος αποκτά δωμάτιο — και τρία που τον εμπόδιζαν να χτιστεί
events.message:
Βήμα 26: ο θόλος αποκτά δωμάτιο — και τρία που τον εμπόδιζαν να χτιστεί

Το §15 έλεγε «ο επόμενος κρίκος, πάνω από κάθε άλλο νούμερο»: ό,τι έχτιζε ο
παίκτης μετά την αρχική αποικία ήταν κέλυφος. Το bd_commit έγραφε «δωμάτιο:
κενό ως την επιλογή» και οκτώ NO_MACH, και επιλογή δεν υπήρχε πουθενά.

Η ΕΠΙΛΟΓΗ ΕΙΝΑΙ Ο ΔΕΥΤΕΡΟΣ ΑΞΟΝΑΣ ΤΟΥ ΙΔΙΟΥ ΜΕΝΟΥ. Δεξιά-αριστερά το
αντικείμενο, πάνω-κάτω το δωμάτιο, και ο θόλος δείχνει το δωμάτιό του εκεί που
τα άλλα δείχνουν όνομα: «< OXYGEN     S >» αντί για «< DOME S >». Δέκα δωμάτια
με τη σειρά που τα χρειάζεσαι. Μια οθόνη μετά την τοποθέτηση θα ήθελε δική της
κατάσταση διεπαφής, δικό της φάντασμα και δικό της «ποιον θόλο δείχνεις»· ο
δεύτερος άξονας ενός μενού που ήδη υπάρχει δεν κοστίζει τίποτα από αυτά.

ΤΑ ΜΗΧΑΝΗΜΑΤΑ ΕΡΧΟΝΤΑΙ ΜΕ ΤΟ ΔΩΜΑΤΙΟ. Οι δύο πίνακες των assets έλεγαν ήδη τα
πάντα: room_machines[δωμάτιο] είναι μάσκα 12 bit, machine_rules[μηχανή] μάσκα
μεγεθών. Το χτίσιμο περνά τη μάσκα, κρατά ό,τι χωράει, και μοιράζει ΚΥΚΛΙΚΑ —
ένα μεγάλο εργοστάσιο βγαίνει σίδερο, βιοπλαστικό, όπλα, ρομπότ, ανταλλακτικά
αντί για οκτώ ίδια, και ένα θερμοκήπιο γεμίζει με τα δώδεκα φυτά, δηλαδή άμυλο,
λαχανικά, φάρμακα και ένα δέντρο. Το οξυγόνο δεν προσφέρεται σε μεσαίο ή μεγάλο
θόλο: η γεννήτρια χωράει μόνο σε μικρό (machine_rules bit0) και ο παίκτης θα
πλήρωνε θόλο που δεν μπορεί να παράγει.

ΚΑΙ ΤΡΙΑ ΣΦΑΛΜΑΤΑ ΠΟΥ ΒΓΗΚΑΝ ΧΤΙΖΟΝΤΑΣ ΕΝΑΝ ΘΟΛΟ ΚΑΙ ΠΕΡΙΜΕΝΟΝΤΑΣ:

* ΤΟ ΕΡΓΟΤΑΞΙΟ ΣΥΝΔΕΟΤΑΝ ΜΕ ΤΟΝ ΕΑΥΤΟ ΤΟΥ. Το bd_link ψάχνει τον κοντινότερο
  ζωντανό θόλο για να δώσει ακμή στο νέο — και ο κοντινότερος ήταν το ίδιο το
  εργοτάξιο, απόσταση μηδέν. Ο έλεγχος «ο εαυτός του» γύριζε χωρίς καμία ακμή:
  κανένας θόλος του παίκτη δεν είχε τελειώσει ΠΟΤΕ, από το βήμα 12. Οι δομές
  δεν το έδειχναν (παίρνουν κόμβο 64+) και καμία δοκιμή δεν είχε περιμένει.

* Ο ΠΡΑΚΤΟΡΑΣ ΠΑΡΑΙΤΕΙΤΑΙ ΑΛΛΑ ΚΡΑΤΑΕΙ ΤΗ ΔΟΥΛΕΙΑ. Οταν το NEXTHOP λέει
  «απρόσιτος», αφήνει τον προορισμό αλλά όχι το task — και ο πίνακας εργασιών
  κρατά την ανάθεση όσο το task δείχνει σε αυτήν. Μια εργασία που δόθηκε μέσα
  στα ~5 δευτερόλεπτα της ανοικοδόμησης δρομολόγησης κολλούσε για πάντα πάνω σε
  κάποιον που είχε ήδη σταματήσει. Μετρημένο: ο ίδιος θόλος τελείωνε σε 400
  frames ή σε 10.800 — όσο χρειαζόταν για να πεινάσει ο μηχανικός, που είναι το
  μόνο άλλο πράγμα που καθαρίζει το task.

* ΤΟ ΕΠΙΜΕΤΡΟ ΤΟΥ ΦΟΡΤΩΤΗ ΚΡΑΤΟΥΣΕ 512 BYTES ΓΙΑ ΣΑΡΑΝΤΑ. Το #3E00 ήταν
  στρογγυλός αριθμός και το ταβάνι της τράπεζας 0· στο #3F80 μένουν 128 για
  σαράντα και η τράπεζα 0 πήρε πίσω 384. Τα δωμάτια δεν χωρούσαν χωρίς αυτά.

ΤΟ ΕΡΓΟΤΑΞΙΟ ΖΩΓΡΑΦΙΖΕΤΑΙ ΑΔΕΙΟ. Τα μηχανήματα γράφονται στην τοποθέτηση —
κανένα πέρασμα δεν κοιτάζει θόλο που δεν είναι DS_ACTIVE — αλλά αν φαίνονταν
από τότε, ο μισοχτισμένος θόλος θα έδειχνε τελειωμένος. Κενό εικονίδιο, καμία
μηχανή, ως να μπει η ακεραιότητα στο 255.

Δοκιμές: το tests/test_build.py ελέγχει τον δεύτερο άξονα (πάνω-κάτω αλλάζει
δωμάτιο, ο μεγάλος θόλος δεν δέχεται οξυγόνο, η επιλογή κολλάει) και ότι η
εγγραφή βγαίνει με δωμάτιο 4 και mach_oxygen με υγεία 200 στην υποδοχή 0. Το
tests/test_game.py χτίζει θόλο μέσα από το κανονικό μενού και περιμένει: η
εργασία Build κλείνει σε 400 frames και η παραγωγή οξυγόνου διπλασιάζεται, 20
-> 40. Το tools/colony.py βάζει έναν μισοχτισμένο θόλο στην αποικία δοκιμής,
ώστε ο κανόνας του εργοταξίου να περνά από τη σύγκριση Z80 προς αναφορά·

events.title: Sweep the flight loop's bookkeeping against the disc sources
events.message:
Sweep the flight loop's bookkeeping against the disc sources

Thirteen faults found by measuring the port against the disc version's own
routines, each pinned by a test:

* The station appeared 3,000 units ahead the moment you arrived, again: the
  hyperspace and galactic-jump arrivals still called the flight scene's
  ArriveInSystem without a distance, so its development default pre-empted
  the ported part 14. The default is zero, which is the original's rule.
* A ship that had started to explode could still be collided with and
  re-killed. The disc's part 7 ORs the exploding bit into its distance test,
  so a wreck is past colliding with and past scooping as soon as it blows up;
  the port only skipped the killed bit.
* The energy bomb's victims were not all paid: their kills flowed through one
  destroyed-this-frame flag the last victim overwrote, and the scene's
  compensation counted kills without bounties or legal status. Kills and
  drops are now collected until the game drains them, which also stops the
  earlier iterations of a frame from losing theirs.
* A mining laser became a military laser across a save and load: the reader
  clamped every saved laser into 0-3, and the mining laser is the fourth.
* Mission 2 is the disc's own DEBRIEF2 now: the special navy energy unit
  (ENGY = 2, recharging the banks by 3 a tick), 256 kill points, and DOENTRY's
  own offer gates - mission 1 done and out of progress, 5 in the tally's high
  byte, the third galaxy. The energy unit is the original's ENGY byte
  throughout, and the shop refuses to sell one while any is fitted.
* The missile lock survives its launch and arrival now that RES2 clears it -
  "Reset MSTG, the missile target, to &FF" - as the disc does at every
  launch, arrival and mis-jump.
* Dying with an escape pod fitted is game over, as the disc's DEATH is fatal
  however the ship was lost: the pod is launched by its own key while the
  ship is still there to press it. The invented refill of the replacement
  ship's energy is gone with it, and the Docking comment that claimed the
  disc recharges shields and banks now names the cassette version's RES4 as
  the routine that does.
* The death is resolved after the scene's update, so the flight scene sees
  the died flag before the shell clears it and the commander no longer dies
  in silence.
* CTRL-S is answered once, in the shell, from every docked screen, and no
  longer sells a unit at the same press.
* The compass shows the station inside the safe zone, as COMPAS does, instead
  of preferring the planet whenever it was in the bubble.
* The E.C.M.'s invented 20,000-unit range is gone: the disc's E.C.M.
  destroys every missile in the local bubble.
* ESCAPE docked launches from the station, as the disc's own docked key does,
  instead of quitting; F10 still quits from anywhere, and ESCAPE quits from
  the title screen and game over.

419 tests pass.

events.title: Photographs of the game, and a sleeve to put it in
events.message:
Photographs of the game, and a sleeve to put it in

Two tools, both of which draw what they claim rather than illustrate it.

tools/shots.py photographs the game without a CPC.  It loads a level
with the real load_level, walks in through enter_level and turns the
actual game_loop as many times as the shot needs, then reads the Mode 0
bytes straight out of the emulated buffer -- so a screenshot cannot
drift from the game the way a mock-up would.  Only the clock and the
keyboard are faked.  Three things the emulator does not do are made
good by hand: the level blob is staged at #4000 where its bank would
have appeared, the pen list load_level chose is decoded through the
Gate Array's 32 hardware colours, and frames() adds the 300 Hz stub's
six ticks per frame itself -- without that the vent clock never
advances and no nozzle in any picture would ever blow steam.

Six pictures in docs/: the title screen with the prompt caught
mid-blink, the attract loop's exhibits page, the machine deck with the
lift's floor readout lit above its doors, a gantry on 14 with the whip
out, the rails on 30, and the administrative tiers on 45.  Re-rendering
gives byte-identical files.

tools/cover_art.py draws the 3-inch disc sleeve: back | 10mm spine |
front as one 210 x 125 mm wrap, plus the 70 x 45 mm rectangular label
the CF-2 shell actually takes.  There is no vector renderer and no
photo source on this machine, so it is painted in code -- the soft
light is a gradient computed at postage-stamp size and blown up
bicubic, which is what an airbrush physically does, and the title is
drawn as polygons because no 1987 title was set in an available
typeface.  The barrel is one geometric idea: every level is the one
below it scaled by p^k toward the vanishing point, asserted so that
nothing can cross anything else.  The three zones of the game are told
by the deck lips alone -- sodium orange, grow-lamp green, cold blue,
doubled where a zone changes so they can be counted -- and only the top
four floors have their windows lit.

Fixes that came out of looking at the rendered sheet rather than the
code: the mechanic was invisible at 4% contrast against his own wall;
the ribs were spaced evenly across the picture instead of by angle, so
a mile-deep cylinder read as a flat cone with lines on it; the "press"
pass shifted the red channel only, which is 2010s chromatic aberration
rather than a plate out of register, and has been replaced by the
halftone screen that was already in the file and never called; a
#04040A ground converts to about 320% ink and no press will take it,
so the floor is now ~250%; and the hairline keyline 0.8mm inside the
trim is gone, because a guillotine drifts half a millimetre and would
have shaved it off one edge and doubled it on the other.  Bleed and
crop/fold marks ship alongside.

Known and not fixed: everything except the drawn logotype is set in
Liberation Sans, there being no typeface of the period on this machine.

channels 4 and 5, and the ring, the device fill, the WAV writer and the
UDP audio stream carry both sides. wav-tone.py reads stereo.

events.title: Decode The Hobbit's character scripts, as editable source and on the Characters page
events.message:
Decode The Hobbit's character scripts, as editable source and on the Characters page

The scripts region ($C82D up to TIMERS) is now generated by script_blocks,
like the rooms and objects: each script table and every step on a line of
its own, commented in words ("TAKE", "GIVE TO: curious map, the player",
"Switch to one of its first 4 scripts at random"), with a block per
character's table and one for the scripts several share. Every address in
them -- a table's scripts, a step's fallback, a jump, a routine a step calls
-- is a DEFW, and so a label in the generated source (GANDALF_A,
ON_ATTACK_WITH, GANDALF_WHATS_THIS...), which makes a script editable there
with the addresses following. The CHARACTERS slots are decoded field by
field the same way, their script pointers labels too. script_program checks
that every byte of the region is a table or a step, and stops the build if
not; 13 tables and 148 steps cover it exactly.

The Characters page writes every character's scripts out step by step,
linked to the source, a script that runs on into another saying so.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte; the generated asm read to confirm the
DEFWs are labels; the page read in a browser.

events.message:
docs(64-11): G-64-1's own truth measured live -- all four migrated tools succeed

A real systemd-run broker, spawning the absolute /usr/bin/x64sc, granted
an unconfigured vice-proxy.ts session that found broker.json through
plan 64-10's shared resolver with nothing configured on either side.
vice_autostart, vice_disk_attach, vice_snapshot_save and vice_snapshot_load
all returned isError:false live, with zero broker-side path leaks across
every result; the write-loss wording was read against a real
attach-write-close cycle (screen-RAM directory proof, unchanged local
sha256) and holds. Independently reproduced through a real nested Claude
Code session. Teardown verified clean on all four checks; full suite green
(4416/4332/0/84).

Surfaced, precisely traced and NOT fixed here (production edits are
prohibited in this plan): a third, independent live defect -- a
cold-launched instance's first relay attach races the real emulator's own
startup, and the broker's kill-never-recycle release policy kills the
still-booting process on that race's failure. This blocks the FIRST stock
tool call in a fresh session almost every time on this host; the driver's
own bounded retry (and a real nested Claude session's own retry) worked
around it to still reach this plan's own truth. Filed as a new pending
todo. A second, intermittent vice_disk_attach 0x8f finding and a
vice_keyboard_type petscii_upper finding are recorded in WINDOWS.md,
neither a G-64-1 root cause.

events.title: A back and a spine: the sleeve is now a wrap
events.message:
A back and a spine: the sleeve is now a wrap

BACK | SPINE | FRONT on one flat sheet, 2550 x 1600 = 215.9 x 135.5 mm at
300 dpi, folding at 101.6 and 114.3 mm. The front panel is byte-identical
to what it was.

SPINE 12.7 mm, which is the CASE and not the disc — the media is 5 mm, the
cassette-style library case is 10-13, and deriving the spine from the disc
is the classic way to come out 6 mm short and pull the front title off
centre. Drawn landscape and rotated CLOCKWISE so it reads top-to-bottom
with the wordmark at the bottom end, which is the British convention.
Same INK as both panels: a spine in its own colour puts a hard edge
exactly on a crease, and one slipped fold then shows as a printing fault.

BACK: three real screenshots off tools/cpcshot.py — fort 1 at full draw,
fort 46 with a bird in the air, fort 37 in the desert palette — halved
exactly from 688x448 with NEAREST, which undoes the emulator's doubling
and nothing else. Blurb, ten feature bullets, a specification block and
the legal line dark-on-light, because small reversed-out type fills in.

Every claim on it was written with file:line evidence and then handed to
an agent told to REFUTE it. That killed two: the score is not only what
the wreckage lands on (pig_hit is called from src/shot.asm too, so the
bird scores directly), and fort size grows as a group but not monotonically
(48 is the biggest, not 50). Fifteen more were rejected before they were
ever set — six materials (there is one), bird special powers (no ability
branch exists), fifty unique designs (fifteen shapes rotated), real
physics, 50 fps, joystick support, a score table.

Three of those rejections were errors in our own docs, now fixed:
README's 20x10 grid of 16x16 cells is a 32x16 grid of 10x10, blocks.png
is one material and not six, and the manuals' "about twenty pixels" of
aim line is five dots reaching fifty.

No barcode and no publisher address. A fake scannable code and an invented
street address are worse than the 1985 sleeves that simply had neither,
and plenty had neither.

fits() raises rather than letting a line run off the panel — it caught
three overflows while this was being laid out.

feat(872): the 1581 board — drive CIA, WD1772 + MFM surface, D81, checkpoints

A drive position holds a 1541 or a 1581 (Spec 872 D1-D5):

- ciacore.rs: VICE core/ciacore.c ported 1:1 for the drive CIA — IFR and
  SDR delay lines, FLAG, SDR/CNT/SP, port hooks, the IRQ line as
  cia_set_int_clk drives it — with the 8520 TOD as a binary event counter
  on a pin held high (WD1772 board, J1 open). The C64's CIAs are untouched.
- fdd.rs / wd177x.rs: fdd.c and wd1770.c ported 1:1; is1772 = 1; a sector is
  always built from its own bytes (D81 error bytes kept and ignored).
- drive1581.rs: the board — own 6502 at 2 MHz, 8 KiB RAM, open bus at
  $2000-$3FFF, CIA/WD mirrors, 32 KiB ROM, CIA-port glue (cia1581d.c).
- drive.rs: the position carries the board; the 870/871 part rules apply
  unchanged; set_board_type refused while powered; D81 media; lazy
  write-back; pair_* fold and deliver ATN per type (FLAG for a 1581).
- iec.rs: type-aware fold; conf3 reads unit_type by slot.
- drive_snapshot.rs / c64re_snapshot.rs: DRIVE8 (type 1581), DRIVECPU0
  (0x2000 RAM), CIA1581D0, WD17700, FDD0, IMAGE0; drivePart.boardType
  (absent = 1541, not written for a 1541).
- tests/drive1581_gate.rs: §9 tests 1-10 over the real KERNAL and DOS.

events.title: Give The Hobbit's HTML disassembly locations, objects, characters and actions pages
events.message:
Give The Hobbit's HTML disassembly locations, objects, characters and actions pages

The index now has a "The game" section. Locations lists all 79 places with
the game's own description, exits linked to where they lead, what starts
there, the first-visit score, the arrival hook and the HELP hint -- and,
for the 22 that have one, the picture, drawn by the game's own
DRAW_LOCATION_PICTURE in the simulator and saved as a PNG. Objects,
Characters and Actions are tables of every record's size, weight,
strength, defence, flags, side, script slot, order limit, reactions and own
handlers, and of all 59 sentence patterns with their handlers and options,
cross-linked to each other and to the code. A Reference section has Bugs
and Credits.

The four game pages are the game's own text and art, so
scripts/hobbit_pages.py generates them on each --html build into
game_disassembly/ (gitignored); scripts/hobbit.ref, committed, holds only
the layout and prose. Tables are read from the tape's data, not the running
game, which by its first prompt has already had Gandalf give the player the
map.

Hobbit.message's scratch stack moves from $BF00, in the room records, to
$5E80 below the game's own stack: the flood fill's queue on it had been
landing on the rooms and breaking the next picture.

Checked: pages rendered and looked at in a browser; each picture drawn from
a clean machine.

events.title: Amiga: the credit scroller is as tall as the text on an interlaced screen
events.message:
Amiga: the credit scroller is as tall as the text on an interlaced screen

It blitted its eight lines onto eight rows of the screen and started ten
rows above the panel, which is right while a text line is eight rows. On
an interlaced screen a line of text is sixteen, so the scroll came out
half height and crowded against the panel. Each of its lines now covers
zoom_y rows, and it starts ten text rows up.

events.title: Leave out the code and tables the ST can never use
events.message:
Leave out the code and tables the ST can never use

The ST plays Amiga data and has no software mixer, so the other
versions' loaders (Mac, PC98, the DOS demo archives and their
decompressors), the DOS SEQ cutscene player and the digital music
players (.mod, .ogg, CD-i, .prf and its MIDI parser) can never run -
but the engine still names them, from resource-type switches and as
members of Mixer and Game, so they were linked in and loaded into
memory with the rest. st_stubs.cpp stands in for them with the few
entry points the engine links against, all left idle, and the upstream
sources are untouched. The toolchain's TOS target cannot drop unused
functions at link time, which is why this is done by hand.

staticres.cpp: on the ST the Japanese font, strings and texts, the
DOS credits and the DOS language-menu flags become one-byte
placeholders - their call sites only run for Japanese, PC98 or DOS
data and stay as upstream wrote them - and the tables only the
removed players used are left out.

The font cache kept each 8x8 glyph in the decoded cell's 16-byte
rows; it keeps 8-byte rows now, and the half that was padding, 6K,
is gone.

The program's code is 510,412 -> 467,928 bytes and its fixed buffers
107,936 -> 101,792, 48K in all. In Hatari on a 2MB STE with music and
both borders open, the title has 432K free where it had 391K, each
level about 40K more, and the intro, every level, the credits and
dying back to the title all run.

and paint_art already works this way, so it is the file's own precedent.

events.title: feat(873): a folder on the bus — the line-level device, its DOS and its checkpoint
events.message:
feat(873): a folder on the bus — the line-level device, its DOS and its checkpoint

A third kind of thing on the IEC bus beside the two 1541 positions: no CPU, a
timed state machine (VICE serial-iec-device.c states, the Ultimate's timing by
default, VICE's as the second profile) that pulls CLK and DATA in its own slot,
and a DOS serving a host folder through the FolderSource trait. Advanced at every
sync point the drives have, event-driven on the C64 clock; the device map marks
its slot IECDEVICE (conf3). Refused beside a drive at the same unit. The
checkpoint carries the device (line state, channels as host path + position,
status, cwd, listing), never the folder's contents; rewind never touches the host.

Gate: tests/folder_device_gate.rs — directory bytes, KERNAL load/save, command
channel, SEQ + the 8→9 copy, not-in-the-way, refusals, read-only, checkpoints
mid-LOAD/mid-SAVE (500-frame lockstep), timing against the KERNAL read off the ROM.

events.title: The paperwork: docs/, and a sleeve for it
events.message:
The paperwork: docs/, and a sleeve for it

The two manuals move into docs/ and the PDFs are built there rather than
into dist/, which is in .gitignore — a manual that does not survive a
clone is not a manual.

tools/mkcover.py draws the sleeve: 1200x1600 at 300dpi, which is 101 x
135 mm, which is a 3" disc case inlay. It is a program and not a painting
for the same reason the spritesheets are generated — so it can be
changed. The subjects are painted in the game's own sixteen firmware
pens, so the bird on the sleeve is the bird on the screen.

Three things took more than one go and are commented where they are:

  * the bands. Twice they were the same brown as the fork and ran nearly
    parallel to its left limb, so the eye read them as a third branch.
    They are grey rubber now, straight, and the pouch sits BEHIND the
    bird the way a real one does, so both bands visibly pass it.
  * the clouds, which were round enough to read as flying saucers.
  * the roof, which floated a storey above the fort it belonged to.

Also docs/disc-label.png for the disc itself, and each manual PDF now
opens on the sleeve.

Describe the last of The Hobbit: the main loop, the font, and the code nothing reaches

START runs on into MAIN_LOOP, now commented: the title screen and the N key
that turns pictures off, the divider, the first turn's "> LOOK", and each
turn's read, tokenise -- quotes making an order, an unknown word echoed in
"i do not know the word ..." -- parse and obey. The story's FONT, both key
maps, CONTROL_CODES, ENDINGS, the character SCRIPTS and the two word
buffers are single blocks now, through `; span`.

0's handler, an OPEN for the wood elf alone, a routine that would wipe an
exit, and some fragments. They are left as data with what they would do said
beside them, keeping to the rule of marking as code only what there is
evidence runs.

With that no block is left untitled, and the README says 100%. The
character scripts are described as one block, not yet entry by entry.

This probably seems silly, but the intent is to align with the

cmp16/scmp16/etc, just like there is copy8 and copy16.

This is not used when the load into A has side effects. A common case
is when it is the first in a chain e.g. LDA / CMP / BEQ / CMP / BEQ.

No binary changes.

events.message:
c64: cart RAM takes its writes with its window banked out (S28)

The FPGA writes AR/RR, SS5 and Pagefox RAM by address alone; TRX64 calls
the mapper only while the PLA maps the window. While one of these logics
is in, cart::RamSnoop sits on the expansion port and snoops $8000-$BFFF,
so every write cycle, DMA and RMW included, reaches the cart RAM.

events.title: Name the rest of The Hobbit's parser: PARSE_ACTION and the replies to names that do not fit
events.message:
Name the rest of The Hobbit's parser: PARSE_ACTION and the replies to names that do not fit

PARSE_ACTION turns a parsed sentence into an action code, sets the
pattern's options, and hands a pattern with objects to MATCH_AND_TRY --
going round again for each object with ALL, past those an EXCEPT names
(EXCEPTED, believed, not traced in play). What the parser says when a name
does not lead anywhere is TARGET_TROUBLE and INSTRUMENT_TROUBLE: "which
... ?" when several fit (ASK_WHICH, which keeps the sentence so the next
line can answer), "i do not see the ... here", "... what ?", and
UNKNOWN_VERB. Also TRY_INSTRUMENTS, PRINT_NOW, KEEP_QUESTION, NO_INSTRUMENT
and PUSH_PATTERN_WORDS, which picks words by rewriting its own jumps.

ASSIGN_PHRASES no longer claims an example it had not been checked on, and
MATCH_AND_TRY no longer states which way its flag goes.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte; the spans in PARSE_ACTION checked against
the decoder.

Name how The Hobbit matches a sentence to its action pattern

into a probe and searches ACTION_PATTERNS with NAME_MATCHES; with no match
the verb does nothing, "you ... . time passes...". ASSIGN_PHRASES uses the
pattern's preposition to decide which noun phrase is the target and which
the instrument, so word order in the sentence does not matter, and keeps
the target's name for IT. Also PICK_WORD, NAME_OF_NUMBER and SEARCH_START
(the last marked as not worked out further).

events.title: Load no samples a machine cannot play, and no music it cannot either
events.message:
Load no samples a machine cannot play, and no music it cannot either

A plain ST has neither the voice device nor DMA sound, so its sound
effects are never heard - yet every level loaded its sample file,
119-152K, and each effect the game asked for then logged "Unknown
sound num" once none were loaded. The samples are now loaded only
where they can play (and not with ste_sound=false), and the effects
are dropped silently without them. On a 2MB ST the first level leaves
271K free where it left 127K; the STE is unchanged.

When a track has no .STM - every track with music=false, the default
- playMusic fell through to upstream's .ogg, CD-i, .mod and .prf
players, none of which can make a sound on the ST: a file probe at
every track change, and a .mod left in DATA\ would have been loaded,
a hundred K or more, and never heard. The ST stops at its YM player.

PATTERN_OPTIONS takes four flags from the pattern's word references. $B711

object, is set by no action in the game. $B70F (TAKE OFF, FOLLOW, JUMP ONTO)
is read only by object matching not yet worked out. SENSIBLE and
PATTERN_FLAGS now say so instead of "not yet traced".

events.title: Βήμα 25: η ισορροπία μετρημένη — τρία δομικά λάθη, όχι κακά νούμερα
events.message:
Βήμα 25: η ισορροπία μετρημένη — τρία δομικά λάθη, όχι κακά νούμερα

Το §15 έλεγε «Balance | Certain: κάθε νούμερο του §6.5 είναι πρώτη εικασία».
Το tools/balance.py τρέχει το ΚΑΝΟΝΙΚΟ binary στο x4 για οκτώ sols, χτίζει
μέσα από το κανονικό μενού και τυπώνει την καμπύλη της αποικίας. Δεν βρήκε
κακορυθμισμένους ρυθμούς. Βρήκε τρία πράγματα που δεν δούλευαν.

Η ΟΙΚΟΝΟΜΙΑ ΔΕΝ ΕΙΧΕ ΡΟΛΟΙ. Ο πίνακας του §6.5 γράφει ρυθμούς ΑΝΑ SOL· η
παραγωγή και το ισοζύγιο είναι θέσεις τροχού, δηλαδή έτρεχαν 750 φορές το sol.
Η μηχανή οξυγόνου έπινε τα εξήντα νερά σε είκοσι δευτερόλεπτα. ECON_DIV = 16
(μία παραγωγή ανά 16 περιστροφές, άρα μία μηχανή ανά 64) και FLOW_DIV = 64 για
την μπαταρία και τις αντλίες — ένας συλλέκτης των 360 άδειαζε σε 18
περιστροφές, το 6% μιας νύχτας. Η μέτρηση ζωντανών μένει σε κάθε περιστροφή:
είναι η συνθήκη ήττας. Και ό,τι τελειώνει να χτίζεται σπρώχνει το ισοζύγιο να
ξαναμετρήσει αμέσως, αλλιώς το πρώτο πάνελ έβγαζε ρεύμα και το HUD έγραφε
ακόμη NO POWER.

ΤΟ ΡΕΥΜΑ ΜΕΤΡΟΥΣΕ ΚΑΤΑΝΑΛΩΣΗ ΑΝΤΙ ΓΙΑ ΖΗΤΗΣΗ. Στο μπλακάουτ καμία μηχανή δεν
καίει, άρα η ζήτηση διαβαζόταν μηδέν, το ισοζύγιο έβρισκε 0 >= 0 και το ρεύμα
ξαναγύριζε — στο 50% του χρόνου, για πάντα. Μια αποικία χωρίς ούτε ένα πάνελ
έπαιρνε το μισό της οξυγόνο δωρεάν και ζούσε πέντε sols. Τώρα ο συσσωρευτής
μετράει όσα ΘΑ έτρεχαν: χειριστής υπάρχει, είσοδοι υπάρχουν, μόνο το ρεύμα
λείπει.

ΤΟ ΚΑΤΑΛΥΜΑ ΗΤΑΝ ΔΕΥΤΕΡΗ ΓΕΝΝΗΤΡΙΑ ΟΞΥΓΟΝΟΥ. Το ob_domeadr χαλάει το DE, και
εκεί κρατούσε το ng_colony τον κωδικό της μηχανής: κάθε θόλος της αρχικής
αποικίας έπαιρνε το χαμηλό byte του G_dome_tbl, δηλαδή 0. Τίποτα δεν φαινόταν
λάθος — ο ύπνος τον δίνει το ΔΩΜΑΤΙΟ, όχι τα κρεβάτια — αλλά η υποστήριξη ζωής
έπινε διπλάσιο νερό και ζητούσε διπλάσιο ρεύμα.

ΤΑ ΝΟΥΜΕΡΑ ΠΟΥ ΑΛΛΑΞΑΝ, όλα μετρημένα: αντλία 6/24/54 -> 1/2/5 νερό τον κύκλο
και 12 -> 6 ρεύμα (τα δύο τρίτα ενός πάνελ έκλειναν το άνοιγμα του παιχνιδιού),
ορυχείο 20 -> 2 μετάλλευμα· αμμοθύελλα 1/128 -> 1/512 ανά περιστροφή (ήταν το
ένα τέταρτο κάθε sol χωρίς ήλιο), βλάβη 1/32 -> 1/128, έκλαμψη 1/256 -> 1/1024·
απόθεμα εκκίνησης 30+10 -> 55+30 μέταλλο και βιοπλαστικό, που είναι ακριβώς τα
τρία κτίσματα μιας αποικίας που ζει — πάνελ, συλλέκτης, αντλία.

ΚΑΙ Η ΠΑΓΙΔΑ ΤΗΣ ΙΔΙΑΣ ΤΗΣ ΑΛΛΑΓΗΣ: διαλέγοντας θύμα με το ev_r2 ενώ η ζαριά
κοιτάζει το ev_r3. Μοιάζει με τον κανόνα του §6.10 («άλλο πεδίο η κάθε δοκιμή»)
και είναι το αντίθετό του — το r2 είναι η προηγούμενη ρίψη του ίδιου Galois και
το #B400 δεν αγγίζει το χαμηλό byte, οπότε το r2 % 64 έβγαινε ΠΑΝΤΑ 0: επτά
βλάβες το sol, όλες στη μοναδική γεννήτρια οξυγόνου. Ο δείκτης βγαίνει από τα
bits που περίσσεψαν, το r3 >> 7.

Η ΚΑΜΠΥΛΗ ΤΩΡΑ, με τον παίκτη να μην αγγίζει τίποτα μετά το χτίσιμο:

  τίποτα                   νεκροί στο sol 2, από ασφυξία, με 54 νερό στην
                           αποθήκη — ακριβώς τα «περίπου δύο sols» του §10.1
  ένα πάνελ                sol 7, δίψα και μετά πείνα
  πάνελ + συλλέκτης        sol 5, δίψα — αλλά το οξυγόνο δεν πέφτει ποτέ
  πάνελ + ανεμογεννήτρια   sol 5, δίψα — η ίδια απάντηση από τον άλλο δρόμο
  πάνελ + αντλία           κανένας θάνατος σε 8 sols, νερό 247
  και τα τρία              sol 8, από πείνα, με νερό 419 και γεμάτη μπαταρία

Κάθε γραμμή που λύνει το νερό τελειώνει στον ίδιο τοίχο: την ΤΡΟΦΗ, που θέλει
θερμοκήπιο και mach_food, που θέλουν θόλο με δωμάτιο — και αυτό δεν υπάρχει
ακόμη. Μπήκε στο §15 ως ο επόμενος κρίκος, πάνω από κάθε άλλο νούμερο.

tests/test_balance.py: η αποικία χωρίς παίκτη δεν ανάβει ΤΙΠΟΤΑ (κανένα δείγμα
με ρεύμα ή οξυγόνο — αυτό ακριβώς έπεφτε με την ταλάντωση), πεθαίνει από αέρα
και όχι από δίψα, και μέσα στο παράθυρο sol 1-3. Μπήκε στο build.sh.

Δύο δοκιμές που μετρούσαν τον παλιό ρυθμό, διορθωμένες: το test_game περίμενε
το νερό να πέσει κάτω από 55 σε 2.000 frames (τώρα η μηχανή οξυγόνου σταματά
μετά το πρώτο ισοζύγιο και η πτώση είναι δύο μονάδες), και το test_save
περίμενε την εικόνα να αλλάξει σε ένα sol — κανείς δεν σηκώνεται από τη θέση
του πριν από τις 12.000 frames.

events.title: Unload the level on the way back to the title
events.message:
Unload the level on the way back to the title

The title needs a 70K block for its picture, and on a 2MB machine it
could not find one with level 5 or 7 still in memory and music or a
border open: dying and returning to the title stopped the game with
"Failed to allocate screen buffer". Nothing a level loads is needed
until the next level loads it again, so leaving one now frees it all -
the level files, the sprite positions, the sound effects (up to 152K),
the rewind states and the port's sprite, slab and tile caches - after
stopping the effects, so a playing sample is not read from freed
memory.

load_SPC kept the previous level's table on every level load after
the first; it frees it now.

With logging on, RS.LOG records the largest block TOS can still hand
out at the title and when a level has loaded and unloaded. It asks
TOS rather than probing with malloc: the library keeps the big blocks
a probe takes and splits them later, and that alone stopped level 1
finding room for its tile pool at 2MB.

In Hatari at 2MB with music and both borders open, every level starts
(119K free at the tightest), dying on 2, 5 and 7 gets back to the
title, and a second trip round leaves the title with the same 192K
free as the first. The README keeps 4MB recommended and says how
little a 2MB machine has to spare.

events.title: c64: drives A and B on TRX64's drive part (S27, TRX64 Specs 870/871)
events.message:
c64: drives A and B on TRX64's drive part (S27, TRX64 Specs 870/871)

TRX64 v0.8.8 models the drive as a part: power, its own reset, a stopped
clock, the ROM as bytes, the unit, read access to RAM and ports, and a second
position on the bus. The bridge's workarounds go:
- the parked stand-in for a held drive -> set_power / set_reset_held /
  set_stopped (RESET bit 2 with the C64 frozen, c1541_drive.vhd:164-165);
- the TRUEDRIVE/DRIVETYPE re-set around power changes -> set_power;
- the ROM through a temporary file -> set_rom, now the whole 32 K;
- the $77/$78 patch -> set_unit (the FPGA has two address bits too, 8-11);
- stepping aside around warm_reset -> the C64's RESET line is cut in TRX64 and
  the bridge drives each drive's reset level itself.

Two things stay on the bridge: a drive reset in TRX64 builds a new rotation
model and re-mounts only its own disk, so the firmware's surface is held across
the calls that may reset; and the firmware changes the ROM with a reset alone,
which the bridge turns into off-and-on because TRX64 takes a new ROM at
power-on (870 §4).

Drive B's window moves into C64Port beside drive A and reaches position B.
The firmware builds drive B only with CAPAB_DRIVE_1541_2 in the capability
word; with --caps 35640226 it mounts a D64 over REST and LOAD"$",9 lists it.
The monitor lists the powered drives by unit.

Tests: workspace green; drive smoke (directory, LOAD, SAVE, write-back equal),
carts 27 PASS, ready, prg, type, freeze and UCI smokes pass.

events.title: docs: the jsbeeb keyDown silence is reported as mattgodbolt/jsbeeb#1172
events.message:
docs: the jsbeeb keyDown silence is reported as mattgodbolt/jsbeeb#1172

Separating the two halves of what bit us, since only one is anyone else's
bug.

The keyDown type change is NOT a jsbeeb fault: v2.0.0's release notes carry
it as a breaking change and the note explicitly names "anything driving
jsbeeb headlessly by key code, jsbeeb-mcp included". The kit met it
unprepared because the harnesses take the highest jsbeeb in the npx cache
and the MCP was unpinned, so the version moved under them with nobody
reading the notes. Both pinned now.

What is reported is the SILENCE. via.js's set() ends `if (!mapping)
return;`, so a typo, a null, an object or a pre-2.0 integer all press
nothing and say nothing - which is what turned a documented migration into
a hunt through a port that was working fine. Asked for a throw, offered a
PR. jsbeeb-mcp already refuses an unknown key name with the full valid list
for the model, so the strictness exists one layer up already.

Decode The Hobbit's breaking, looking through doors, digging, and the ring

DO_STRIKE: the weapon's strength, the striker's and a random 0-21 against
the thing's defence; enough, and it breaks (flag bit 3, renamed BROKEN by
BROKEN_OR_DEAD, strength halved, contents spilled) -- and then the weapon is
tried against the same defence, so a weak weapon breaks on a hard target:
the sword on the trap door. LOOK_THROUGH shows the place beyond a door (or,
from $8EF8, across a river) if it is lit. DIG opens the sand to show the
trap door. The crack only opens from the dark stuffy passage.

WEAR_RING makes the wearer invisible and a quarter as strong, and starts
timer 6 at a random 2 to 10 turns; when it runs out the ring comes off
(TAKE_OFF_RING). That corrects the timer table, which had timer 6 as never
started, and names what RING_CHECK goes on to.

decoder; messages printed through the game.

events.title: Name The Hobbit's containers, food and rivers, and how the troll dies of gluttony
events.message:
Name The Hobbit's containers, food and rivers, and how the troll dies of gluttony

The containers' own handlers: TAKE OUT OF, PUT IN and DROP IN (open, except
to PUT something ON, and with room), EMPTY, CLIMB INTO (big enough for the
actor and its load). DO_EAT gives ten points of strength and removes the
thing from everywhere; strength reaching 128 kills the eater -- which is the
"foul gluttony" that kills a troll after it eats the player. DRINK from a
container gives one. The fast river can be swum, by opening its exit for
the length of the move; the black river, or its water, sends you to sleep
for good. Flag bit 2 on a container is full.

DO_FILL is described as read: it fetches a fresh water and puts it in with
the objects swapped, but the liquid would then be refused by CAN_LIFT's last
check, so FILL looks as though it can never succeed. That is not confirmed
in play -- the simulator test harness did not work -- and is said so.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte; messages printed through the game.

events.message:
Decode The Hobbit's doors and locks, and room capacity

Flag bit 0 is locked and bit 5 is open: DO_OPEN and DO_CLOSE set and clear
the one, DO_LOCK and DO_UNLOCK the other (one routine, which rewrites the
byte of its own SET or RES). Each lockable door names its key in a handler
of its own -- the small curious key for the side door, the red key, the
large key for the rock door -- and nothing fits the round green door or the
trap door (NO_KEY_FITS). An earlier note that a door's record never changes
when it opens was wrong, and is corrected.

CAN_PASS says whether a way can be used: shut, too small for the actor and
its load ("the ... is too small for you to enter."), or the room beyond too
full. That settles room head byte 1: capacity, $FF for no limit, set on six
rooms, which the generated room blocks now say, with byte 0's bits.

events.title: Name The Hobbit's TIE, UNTIE, BURN, CAPTURE and CLIMB OUT, and its state words
events.message:
Name The Hobbit's TIE, UNTIE, BURN, CAPTURE and CLIMB OUT, and its state words

DO_CAPTURE says where captives go: the wood elf and the butler take them to
the elvenking's dark dungeon (31), anyone else to the goblins' dungeon (13),
never their own side, and a captured player is shown the new place. DO_TIE
ties things to the rope (TIE ROPE TO X is swapped round), refusing liquids,
anything already holding something, and the living; DO_UNTIE hands the thing
to whoever has the rope. Only the dragon can BURN, and it kills.
DO_CLIMB_OUT refuses a thing that is shut (IS_SHUT).

SAY_STATE prints "the ... is ..." from STATE_WORDS ($A224), sixteen words in
pairs picked by bit 7 of the state: unlocked/locked, empty/full, broken,
off/on, closed/open, dead/alive.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte; the messages printed through the game and
the words decoded from the dictionary.

events.title: Decode The Hobbit's fighting: strength, defence, sides, and who can kill the dragon
events.message:
Decode The Hobbit's fighting: strength, defence, sides, and who can kill the dragon

DO_ATTACK weighs the attacker's strength (byte 5 of its record, plus the
weapon's -- a bare FIST otherwise) against the target's defence (byte 6),
each jostled by -10 to +10. A blow no stronger is wasted, one more than 16
stronger kills, and anything between picks a message from WOUNDS and wears
the target down. KILL marks a character dead (flag bit 3), drops what it
held and ends its script. Byte 4's high bits are sides: SAME_SIDE stops
anyone attacking its own, and the player attacking a friend turns it into
an enemy.

DO_SHOOT needs the bow; Bard never misses, anyone else misses the dragon
every time -- only Bard can kill it -- and everything else a third of the
time. DO_GIVE and DO_EXAMINE are named too, and IS_ALIVE.

That closes two open items: object bytes 5 and 6, and what reads byte 4's
high bits; and it confirms flag bit 3 as dead or broken.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte; every message printed through the game.

feat(64-09): the production dials stop declaring, reading or sending a credential

Per G-64-1 route (b) and owner decision 5, plan 64-08 made the broker
authenticate attach/transfer by handle alone -- this removes the
client-side empty-token parameters those dials have carried since Phase
63 with nothing ever filling them. Deleting the slot (rather than leaving
it as documented dead weight) makes route (a) -- threading the per-boot
token back through -- unwritable by a future caller.

  lose their credential field; performAttach()/performTransfer() stop
  writing one onto the wire.
- stock-connect.ts: StockConnectDeps loses controlToken; the default

- text-connect.ts: TextConnectOptions loses controlToken; its default
  dial mirrors stock-connect.ts's.
- text-tools.ts: withTextTool() stops passing a credential to

- stock-dispatch.ts: StockDispatchDeps loses its test-only credential
  field and its copy in stockConnectDepsFor().

Every touched JSDoc that described these dials as "authenticated with"
a token is rewritten to state the handle is the only authority
presented. The six test files still passing a credential to a dial are
fixed in the next commit -- until then tsc reports an excess-property
error at each such call, and the 28 errors observed are exactly those
calls (verified against /tmp/64-09-t1-tc.txt).

events.title: Name The Hobbit's two text windows: the story's narrow font and the input line
events.message:
Name The Hobbit's two text windows: the story's narrow font and the input line

PRINT_CHAR sends a character one of two ways. STORY_CHAR writes the
narration in the game's own six-pixel font (NARROW_CHAR, 42 columns),
lower-casing everything and capitalising after a carriage return or a full
stop, indenting as LIST_HELD asks, copying each finished line to a ZX
Printer when PRINT is on (LINE_TO_PRINTER), pausing briefly, and scrolling
rows 1-17 up (SCROLL_STORY) -- which is how a picture scrolls away. INPUT_CHAR
writes the bottom five rows in capitals with the ROM's font (ROM_FONT_CHAR),
scrolling them with SCROLL_INPUT and, for a backspace past the line start,
SCROLL_INPUT_BACK.

pobtastic's disassembly of the same tape named Print Character, Scroll Line
and Print Proper Character first; the reading is re-derived from the code.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte. Not yet traced: what sets $B716, which
skips the end-of-line pause.

events.title: Name The Hobbit's special words, SCORE, HELP, PAUSE, QUIT, SAVE and LOAD
events.message:
Name The Hobbit's special words, SCORE, HELP, PAUSE, QUIT, SAVE and LOAD

The handlers behind SPECIAL_WORDS: PRINT and NOPRINT (a ZX Printer, if port
$FB shows one), ALL and EXCEPT, IT (the last noun phrase again), and the
game's own commands. The score is kept in tenths of a per cent -- 1000 is a
finished game -- and SHOW_SCORE prints it with one decimal place. HELP has a
hint for eleven places (HELP_HINTS) and "YOU'RE DOING FINE." elsewhere.
SAVE writes the four blocks START keeps a copy of through the ROM's
SA-BYTES and then verifies them; LOAD restarts the game if a block fails,
since it would be half-loaded. Three bytes of a character script that the
game rewrites ride along in the variables block.

pobtastic's disassembly of the same tape named this area first (Save Game,
Load Game, Game Over, the help message); the reading here is re-derived from
the code.

events.title: Name RUN, FOLLOW, THROW AT, TALK TO, ENTER and GO THROUGH in The Hobbit
events.message:
Name RUN, FOLLOW, THROW AT, TALK TO, ENTER and GO THROUGH in The Hobbit

RUN goes off in a random direction that has a way out; FOLLOW takes one step
through the exit towards the one followed; THROW AT becomes ATTACK WITH or
STRIKE WITH with the objects swapped (SWAPPED_OBJECTS), and the target
reacts; GO THROUGH is the handler doors carry, a move in the direction of
the exit through them. EXIT_VIA and EXIT_TO are FIND_EXIT with its match
field patched.

DO_TALK settles the last field of a character's slot: byte 6 is how many of
the player's orders it takes at once, a random number up to it each time,
with "... says " no "" at 0 -- Thorin 6, Gandalf and Elrond 5, the goblins
and the warg never. Gollum waiting for his riddle's answer takes exactly
one, which is how the answer reaches him. ASSIGN_ORDERS hands them out.

Checked: rebuilds byte-for-byte; the messages printed through the game. Not
yet understood: how ENTER's object number stands for a place.

Records the security trade plan 64-08 made: attach and transfer are now
authenticated by their broker-minted handle alone, ahead of the per-boot
token gate, reversing 63-SECURITY.md's T-63-01 ("attach requires the

per-claim handle"). The evidence file itemises the replacement
mitigation (the handle checks vice-broker.mts already owned, untouched in

longer destroys the connection -- infeasible against a 128-bit handle
space), and flags explicitly that no RM-* requirement names the token
gate's own removal, so Phase 66's planner must name it rather than
inherit it silently.

Appends a dated Superseded note below 63-SECURITY.md's threat register
pointing at the evidence file, leaving the historical T-63-01/T-63-05
rows unedited. Appends a Resolution section to the pending todo that
first traced this defect, naming route (b) over the thread-through its
