Game: TAB sets the bomb off, with the explosion sound

Roadmap corrections:
- The docking music is NOT a disc-version feature. startbd is called only in
  the C64 build, so the Blue Danube is not part of disc parity and has been
  removed from the list
- Docking mechanics are recorded as the largest remaining gap: flying into the
  station's slot to dock, and the docking computer doing it for us, both of
  which the disc version has and this implementation only stubs with a
  debug shortcut

Verified by test: the bomb needs to be fitted, cannot be set off twice, is
consumed, destroys the pirate but not the station.
events.author: tkleisas

events.title: Add the mission trail of hints
events.message:
Add the mission trail of hints

Tools:
- The token extraction now also reads RUTOK, the second extended token table
  that holds the mission hints, plus the RUPLA and RUGAL tables that select
  them, and follows the references the hints make into the main table so
  their text expands in full. Numbers are parsed as the original's source
  writes them, including &hex and %binary, which RUGAL needs

Core:
- MissionHints applies the original's criteria: the system number must match,
  and either the hint is always shown (RUGAL bit 7, which is Teorge's) or it
  belongs to the galaxy we are in and mission 1 is in progress. Hints are only
  shown for the system we are docked at, not the one the charts point at
- TokenPrinter takes an optional second table, so a hint token from RUTOK can
  refer to tokens in the main table, and it no longer assumes sentence case:
  the tokens set the case themselves, which is why the hints keep the capitals
  the tables store them in while the generated descriptions do not

Game: Data on System shows a hint in place of the description for a system on
a mission's trail

The hints read as the original has them, typos included:
  Xeer      THE CONSTRICTOR WAS LAST SEEN AT REESDICE, COMMANDER.
  Reesdice  A FUNNY LOOKING SHIP LEFT HERE A WHILE BACK. LOOKED BOUND FOR AREXE.
  Arexe     YEP, A FUNNY NEW SHIP HAD A GALACTIC HYPERDRIVE FITTED HERE. USED IT TOO.
  Orarra    THERE'S A REAL SON OF A BITCH PIRATE OUT THERE.

Verified by test: the trail systems have the tokens the original's table
gives them (Xeer 2, Reesdice 3, Arexe 4, Tivere 21, Orarra 24), hints belong
to their own galaxy, the always-on hint shows without a mission, and a hint is
only shown where we are docked.
events.author: tkleisas

events.title: Fix the galaxy generation: the seeds twist four times per system
events.message:
Fix the galaxy generation: the seeds twist four times per system

The original's TT20 twists the three 16-bit seeds four times to move from one
system to the next, and this implementation twisted them once. That is a quiet
bug: a galaxy generated with one twist per system still looks entirely
plausible — the right kind of names, sensible coordinates, Lave in the right
place — but only every fourth system is one the original actually has, and the
other three quarters were inventions. It showed up as six canonical systems
sitting at exactly four times their correct system numbers (Lave at 28 instead
of 7, Arexe at 112 instead of 28) and as systems beyond number 64, such as
Orarra at 193, being absent altogether.

The fix was found by using the original's own mission tables as a reference,
because they name systems by their number within the galaxy. With four twists
per system, all 23 entries plus Lave land exactly where the original puts them,
and both of the anchors that had been failing now hold:

- Orarra, system 193 of the second galaxy, is at (144, 33), precisely where the
  original's THERE routine looks for the Constrictor
- A galactic jump arrives at the system nearest (96,96), and in the second
  galaxy that system is ORORRA, as the original's documentation says

Adds Galaxy.NextSystem for the four-twist advance, used by both the galaxy
generation and the closest-system search, and 24 theory tests pinning the
original's system numbering. The earlier suspicion about the seed rotation was
wrong: the rotation, the twist and the name rules were all correct, and the
fault was one line of the galaxy loop.
events.author: tkleisas

events.title: Pin the galaxy anchors, and record what the rotation investigation ruled out
events.message:
Pin the galaxy anchors, and record what the rotation investigation ruled out

Tests:
- The first galaxy is pinned against the original's own systems: TIBEDIED as
  system 0, Lave at (20,173), and the mission systems Reesdice and Arexe
- Every galaxy has 256 systems, and each one's arrival system — the nearest to
  (96,96), which is where a galactic jump always lands — is within a sensible
  distance of it

Roadmap:
- Recorded the whole investigation into the second galaxy, so it does not have
  to be redone: the twist matches TT54 line for line including its carry
  handling; the name length rule really is bit 6 of s0_lo, tested by the
  original with a BIT on QQ15, so it was right all along; and four readings of
  the seed rotation — per-byte left, 48-bit rotate, 48-bit shift, per-byte
  right — were all tried, and none of them produce the Ororra that the
  original's documentation puts at the arrival point, the Orarra it puts at
  (144,33), or a system at (144,33) at all

The rotation is therefore probably not the fault, and the divergence lies
elsewhere in how a galaxy is built from its seeds. An authoritative listing of
the second galaxy would settle it; the Elite wiki has no such page and the
deep dives name only the mission systems.
events.author: tkleisas

events.title: Fix the A? name token, and correct the mission facts from the source
events.message:
Fix the A? name token, and correct the mission facts from the source

Core:
- The original's two-letter token table contains 'A?' at token 15, and the
  question mark is not part of the name: 'A?' + 'RE' + 'XE' is the system
  AREXE. Dropping it brings canonical names out of the generator, including
  Arexe and Ausar, two of the systems the Constrictor mission sends you to
- Mission 1 now follows the original's own conditions: the offer needs a
  combat rank of Competent (256 kills) in one of the first two galaxies, and
  the debrief clears bit 0, so a finished mission reads %10 rather than %11

Tests:
- The galaxy is now checked against systems the original names itself, in its
  mission hint tables: Reesdice and Arexe in the first galaxy, Ausar, Ramaza
  and Veriar in the second
- Names may no longer contain the question mark, and their lengths vary
  because that token contributes a single letter

Two findings from the original's documentation, both recorded in the roadmap:
the Constrictor mission is really a trail of hints through named systems
across the first two galaxies, ending at Orarra in galaxy 2, rather than a
single target — this implementation still simplifies that. And galaxy 2, while
laid out correctly in general, still has no system at (144,33) where the
original expects Orarra, so the seed advance within a galaxy remains suspect.

Core:
- Missions tracks the original's TP byte: bit 0 mission 1 in progress, bit 1
  complete, bit 2 on the way to the plans, bit 3 carrying them
- The Constrictor appears only in its own system while mission 1 is open and
  there is not one in the bubble already, carrying the original's AI flag of
  %11111001: E.C.M., the highest aggression, hostile and under AI control.
  Killing it completes the mission and pays the original's 5,000 credits
- While we carry the plans there is the original's extra 22% chance of a
  Thargoid in any system, because the Thargoids are trying to stop us
- The status byte is written back to the commander whenever it changes, so it
  saves and loads with everything else

Game:
- Docking settles mission business: collecting the plans, delivering them, or
  being offered the next mission, with A accepting

A galaxy generation bug found on the way, recorded in the roadmap: the
original hard-codes the Constrictor's system as galaxy 2 at (144,33), and no
system in any of this implementation's galaxies sits there — the nearest is
(145,29). Galaxy 1 matches the original exactly, so the fault is in the later
galaxies. Until it is chased down the mission resolves to the nearest system
so it stays playable, and ConstrictorTargetExists reports the discrepancy
rather than hiding it.

events.title: Fix the description fragments and show descriptions in the game
events.message:
Fix the description fragments and show descriptions in the game

Tools:
- The token definitions contain IF/ELIF blocks for the different versions of
  the game, and reading every branch spliced two versions of the same word
  together: an unconditional 'UNREMAR' followed by the NES branch's 'UNM...'
  gave 'unremarunremarkable'. The extractor now evaluates those conditionals
  for the disc version's docked build, which is the one that shows system
  descriptions
- Restricting token starts to the line after a previous token ends, and
  keeping the earlier fix, the extraction is now correct

Core:
- {single cap} takes precedence over {lower case}, so the system's name keeps
  its capital inside an otherwise lower case description
- The name is treated as a proper noun: capitalised wherever it appears, so
  'The planet Lave is ...' reads correctly

Game:
- Data on System now prints the description, wrapped to the 32-column grid,
  regenerated when the selection or the visit changes

The descriptions read as they should, misspellings and all:
  Lave is very fabled for its unusual tropical forests.
  The world Lave is an unremarkable planet.
  Lave is most famous for its vast parking meters and brandy.

One refinement is recorded in the roadmap: the article does not always agree
with the adjective, because the original pairs those choices by drawing a
single random number for both while this implementation draws them separately.

events.title: Add the extended token extraction and the description printer
events.message:
Add the extended token extraction and the description printer

Tools:
- EliteDataExtractor gains a 'tokens' command which walks the references from
  the original's description token (extended token 5) and emits every token it
  can reach: 191 tokens, following recursive tokens and the five-token runs the
  MTIN table gives for the random ones. The result goes to data/descriptions.json
  and is embedded like the other data

Core:
- TokenPrinter expands extended tokens the way the original's DETOK does:
  characters, two-letter tokens, recursive tokens, the MTIN random runs, and
  the jump tokens for case, the system name and line breaks
- DescriptionData generates a description for a system from the embedded table
  and a random number generator

The finding that matters: the original picks its phrases with the game's
random number generator, not with the system seeds, so a system's description
is not fixed. Look at the same system twice and you may be told something
different — which is what the original does, and why the famous Lave
description is what you get on a fresh start rather than a constant.

KNOWN BUG: some phrases repeat a fragment, giving text like 'an
unremarunremarkable planet'. The vocabulary and the structure are right and
the tests cover them, but the joining of fragments is wrong somewhere, so the
generator is deliberately NOT wired into Data on System yet. The roadmap
records the diagnosis to try first: the token extractor switching tokens
part-way through when a comment mentions another token number.

- CommanderSave captures everything the original's commander block holds:
  name, cash in tenths, fuel in tenths, galaxy, the system's seeds and
  index, legal status, kills, missiles, cargo capacity, every equipment flag,
  the four laser mounts and all seventeen cargo counts
- It is written as a small versioned JSON document rather than the original's
  76-byte block, because that layout is tied to BBC filing systems; the fields
  and their meanings are the original's
- What is loaded is validated rather than trusted: a file that is not JSON, a
  save from another version and a truncated hold are all rejected with a clear
  reason, and a missing file is reported rather than thrown
- GameSession gains Save, TryLoad and Load, and loading a commander moves the
  session to their system

- The game starts from the saved commander when one is present, as the
  original does, with --new-commander to ignore it
- CTRL-S saves from the market, equipment and status screens, and the result
  is reported on screen

Verified by test: a commander with cargo, lasers and equipment survives the
round trip through JSON and back from disk intact, saving is refused unless
docked, and damaged saves are rejected.

events.title: Add the Data on System screen
events.message:
Add the Data on System screen

- DataScene shows everything the original's TT25 prints about the selected
  system: distance in light years (green when a tank will reach it), economy,
  government, tech level, population, productivity, average radius and
  galactic coordinates, all generated from the system's seeds
- Lave comes out as Rich Agricultural, Dictatorship, tech level 4, 2.5 billion
  people, 2000 MCr productivity and a radius of 4116 km
- Reached with F3 from the market, the equipment shop and both charts, and
  H jumps to the system being shown

The description text is deliberately not faked. The original's phrases live in
its extended token table (TKN1, over six thousand lines) and are assembled by
its extended text system, so the screen says so plainly and the roadmap notes
the plan: extract the table as data, then port the printer and the selection.

events.title: Add the original's sound effects
events.message:
Add the original's sound effects

Core:
- Beeps carries the original's ten sounds with the exact four bytes from its
  SFX table: channel and flush control, amplitude or envelope, pitch and
  duration in twentieths of a second
- Pitch follows the BBC's divider, 125000 / pitch, so a high pitch number is a
  low note and zero is the chip's lowest
- The four sound envelopes are what give the sounds their character, and the
  synthesizer reproduces them: the laser is a short loud zap, the explosion is
  noise that dies away, the hyperspace drive sweeps upwards and the E.C.M. is
  a fast tremolo
- Every sound renders to samples, so the whole set is testable without an
  audio device: lengths match the table's durations, the E.C.M. switching off
  is silent, and the hyperspace sweep measurably rises in pitch

Game:
- SoundBank renders each sound to PCM once at startup and plays them through
  MonoGame, flushing the previous sound as a single sound chip does
- Sounds are triggered by the same events the original uses: firing, being
  hit, a kill, a missile launch, hyperspace and the E.C.M.
- The game still runs silently if there is no audio device

events.title: Add the short-range and long-range charts
events.message:
Add the short-range and long-range charts

Game:
- ChartScene draws both charts: the short-range chart centred on us with the
  systems within reach and the fuel circle, and the long-range chart of all
  256 systems with our position marked
- The fuel circle is the point of the short-range chart: a coordinate unit is
  four tenths of a light year, so a tank's reach in coordinate units is the
  fuel divided by four, which puts every system you can actually jump to
  inside the circle
- The crosshairs move with the cursor keys (eight coordinates at a time with
  shift) and snap to the nearest system, the selected system's economy,
  government, tech level, population and radius are shown underneath, and H
  jumps there
- The charts are docked screens, reached with F1 and F2 from the market and
  equipment shop, as the original puts them on its own function keys

events.title: Add hyperspace and the original's distance formula
events.message:
Add hyperspace and the original's distance formula

Core:
- Galaxy.DistanceTenths works out the distance between systems exactly as
  the original does: the squares of the coordinate differences are added and
  passed through its eight-bit restoring square root, then multiplied by four
- GameSession gains the selected system, the hyperspace countdown, the fuel
  check and the arrival, which rebuilds the market for the new system

The scale checks out against the original's own universe: from Lave, Leesti
is 5.6 light years away and reachable on a full tank, while Riedquat at 7.2 is
not — the classic opening decision of the game. Reaching those two names from
the seed generation is also a good independent check on the galaxy, since both
are built from the two-letter token table.

Game: H jumps to the nearest system within fuel range, counting down first and
then arriving with a fresh bubble, station, planet and sun, until the charts
arrive to choose a destination properly.

Core:

events.title: Add asteroids, cargo, mining and scooping
events.message:
Add asteroids, cargo, mining and scooping

Core:
- Debris holds the loose ends of a system: the original's 13% junk spawn
  chance with its three-bit limit, the tumbling rocks it fills with random
  roll and pitch bits, and the type split from one random byte (2% cargo
  canisters, 50% boulders, 48% asteroids)
- Destruction drops follow the laser: a mining laser shatters an asteroid
  into one to three scoopable splinters and a boulder into one half the time,
  while any other laser leaves a cargo canister behind
- Scooping collects canisters (carrying whatever their blueprint's scoop
  market item says) and splinters (which scoop as minerals), and needs fuel
  scoops and hold space
- Drops are spawned where the wreck was, and junk counts against the
  original's junk limit rather than the ship slots

Verified by test: the spawn rate and type split match the original's, mining
lasers produce one to three splinters from asteroids and one from boulders
half the time, scooping needs the equipment and the space, and flying at a
canister inside the scooping range collects it.

events.title: Populate systems with other ships
events.message:
Populate systems with other ships

Core:
- Spawner follows the disc version's main game loop: a 47% chance of
  spawning anything at all, anarchy systems always busy with the low bits of
  the random byte compared against the government so safer systems are
  quieter, then a 61% chance of pirates and otherwise a lone bounty hunter
- The ship tables are the original's: pirates fly one of the eight pack
  hunters from the Sidewinder to the Cobra Mk III pirate, and bounty hunters
  one of four from the Cobra Mk III pirate to the Fer-de-lance — which is why
  the Moray, sitting just after the Fer-de-lance, never spawns
- Spawned ships get the original's AI flag (AI and aggression bits set, with
  an E.C.M. about a fifth of the time), appear 9728 units ahead as the
  original fixes their position, and take a random heading — without that
  they spawn pointing away and simply fly off
- The extra-vessels delay spaces spawns out, and ships that drift beyond the
  bubble's range leave it, so the twelve slots do not silt up

Game: spawned ships are named and dressed from the extracted blueprints

events.title: Add shields, the damage model and death
events.message:
Add shields, the damage model and death

Core:
- Combat.TakeDamage is the original's OOPS: the attacker's z_sign chooses
  which shield was hit, the shield absorbs what it can, and the remainder
  comes off the energy banks. If the banks cannot take it, we die
- Shields recharge a point a frame from the energy banks, but only while the
  banks are above half full, as SHD does; the banks themselves recharge at
  ENGY + 1 a frame, so an energy unit doubles the rate
- Firing costs a point of energy a shot, which the recharge cancels out —
  which is exactly what the original does
- GameSession resolves death: an escape pod costs the cargo but saves the
  commander, and otherwise it is game over with a fresh commander standing in
  for the saved one until save and load arrive

Game:
- The dashboard's FS and AS bars show the real shield strengths
- ENERGY LOW flashes when the banks drop below 50, as the original's does

events.title: Add the ship AI, and the routine that lets ships turn
events.message:
Add the ship AI, and the routine that lets ships turn

Core:
- Tactics ports the structure of TACTICS: the aggression test that compares a
  random byte with bit 7 set against a ship's AI flag, steering towards us (or
  away, for peaceful ships) by setting the roll and pitch counters, and the
  aim and range test before opening fire
- MVEIT part 8: rotating a ship about its own axes from its pitch and roll
  counters. This was the missing piece — the counters the AI sets had nothing
  to drive until it was ported, which is exactly what the steering test caught
- Stations, cargo, asteroids, splinters and escape pods are left alone by the
  AI: the space station in particular must stay exactly where it is
- The counters take the opposite sign to the aim, as the original's TACTICS
  comment says they should

Verified by test: an enemy turns to point at us, opens fire at close range,
holds its fire beyond it, and cannot hit us without a laser fitted. Flying the
game for five seconds with a pirate in the system leaves our energy banks
empty, which is the AI doing its job.

events.title: Add lasers and combat
events.message:
Add lasers and combat

Core:
- Combat holds the original's laser constants: pulse 15, beam 15 with bit 7
  set, military 23 (Armlas), mining 50, with only the low seven bits doing
  damage. What separates a pulse laser from a beam laser is the rate: the
  original stores the power masked with %11111010 in LASCT and refuses to fire
  while it is non-zero, giving a pulse laser a ten-frame gap and letting beam
  and military lasers fire every frame
- Firing heats the laser by 8, cools it by 1 a frame and overheats at 242, and
  costs a unit of energy a shot, all as the original does
- HITCH's crosshair test: in front of us, a ship rather than the planet or sun,
  not exploding, within 256 units of the centre line and inside the targetable
  area from the blueprint
- Damage, destruction and the start of an explosion cloud

Game:
- Laser beams drawn from the two bottom corners of the view to the crosshairs
  with the original's random wobble, white when they are hitting something
- Explosion clouds as expanding soft discs
- The dashboard's laser temperature and energy banks now show the real values

events.title: Add the planet and the sun, and fix 24-bit coordinates
events.message:
Add the planet and the sun, and fix 24-bit coordinates

Core:
- Ship coordinates now use all 23 bits of their magnitude. SetCoordinate and
  GetCoordinate were truncating at 16 bits, which silently destroyed any
  position beyond 65535 units: the planet and sun both landed on the origin
- SystemArrival places the planet and sun by the original's SOLAR rules: the
  planet 3-7 x 65536 units to the upper right with its type from the tech
  level, the sun 1-7 x 65536 units behind us
- Bodies move by the equivalent of the original's MV40 routine, which works
  in wider arithmetic than the ship routine because the planet's coordinates
  need the extra bits; using the ship path collapsed the planet onto us
- The flight scene starts in Lave, so the station, planet and sun are all
  where the default commander would find them

Game:
- CelestialRenderer draws the planet and sun as discs of the original's
  angular size (radius 24576 divided by distance), with a softly shaded rim
  and a ringed variant for the second planet type

  which is how the coordinate bug was found

events.title: Amiga: the credit scroller reads a hires glyph whole
events.message:
Amiga: the credit scroller reads a hires glyph whole

W scrolls the version and score under the flight view. The scroller was built
around eight-pixel cells, one byte per plane with two characters to a word,
but in a 640 screen CHARSET_PTR names the sixteen-byte font. It indexed by
eight and read a byte a line, so it drew half of the wrong glyph, and it fed
a new character every eight pixels while the cell was sixteen wide, so what
did arrive was cut in half again.

A hires cell is now a whole word. SCROLL_CELL takes the cell's width as its
operand size, the way Q_PUSH does, so one line of pixels is written once
rather than once per screen width; the index steps by sixteen, a character
lasts twice as many scroll steps, and SCROLL_WORDS and SCROLL_STRIDE carry the
widths the loops and the buffer need. The 320 screens keep their layout.

events.title: Βήμα 14: η αποικία κινείται στην οθόνη
events.message:
Βήμα 14: η αποικία κινείται στην οθόνη

Η λίστα βρώμικων υπόσχεται ότι η οθόνη μετά από μεταλλάξεις είναι ταυτόσημη με
πλήρη σχεδίαση. Ως το βήμα 13 η υπόσχεση ήταν κενή: η προσομοίωση δεν έσπρωχνε
τίποτα μέσα της, και οι άποικοι μετακινούνταν στους πίνακες χωρίς να αλλάζει
ένα pixel.

Τα σπρωξίματα μπαίνουν στο ent_claim και στο ent_release — τα δύο σημεία που
ξέρουν και τον κόμβο και τη θέση. Περνούν από ΔΕΙΚΤΗ (wh_push) και όχι με
κατευθείαν κλήση, επειδή το tests/simtest.asm δεν συνδέει renderer: εκεί ο
δείκτης μένει μηδέν και η κλήση κοστίζει δεκατέσσερα T-states. Τα DK_* πήγαν
στο const.asm για τον ίδιο λόγο.

Ο πίνακας φιγούρων ξαναχτίζεται από τους ΠΡΑΚΤΟΡΕΣ, μία φορά ανά ριπή
σπρωξιμάτων: είναι κρυφή μνήμη, η προσομοίωση δεν την ξέρει, και μπαγιάτικη
ζωγραφίζει τη φιγούρα εκεί που έφυγε. Η σάρωση κοστίζει μετρημένα 9.984 us —
μισό frame — οπότε τρέχει μόνο όταν έχει σπρωχτεί θέση δακτυλίου.

Η δοκιμή είναι ισοδυναμία πάνω στον ΚΑΝΟΝΙΚΟ βρόχο: τρέχει ένα sol, παγώνει
την προσομοίωση, αδειάζει τη λίστα, και συγκρίνει με πλήρη σχεδίαση. Χρειάζεται
ολόκληρο sol γιατί οι ανάγκες πέφτουν ~20 ανά 1.500 frames και το NEED_LOW
είναι 64 — πριν από τα ~13.000 frames κανείς δεν σηκώνεται, και μια ισότητα
χωρίς κίνηση δεν αποδεικνύει τίποτα.

Και βρήκε σφάλμα που δεν είναι δικό της: ξαναζωγραφίζοντας ΑΔΕΙΑ θέση πάνω σε
φρέσκια πλήρη σχεδίαση αλλάζουν 2 ως 7 bytes, σε πέντε από τις οκτώ θέσεις.
ΔΕΝ φταίει η κενή παραλλαγή — δοκιμάστηκε να ξανασχεδιάζεται ολόκληρος ο θόλος
με κλιπ το ορθογώνιο 2x8 της θέσης, που εξ ορισμού πρέπει να ταιριάξει, και
έδωσε τα ίδια λάθος pixel. Το σφάλμα είναι στο κόψιμο του περάσματος
αντικειμένων σε παράθυρο δύο bytes στο αριστερό χείλος ενός sprite· το
test_object περνά με τέσσερα, γι' αυτό το σκρολάρισμα δεν το έδειξε ποτέ. Η
δοκιμή βάζει όριο 8 bytes ώστε να πέσει αν χειροτερέψει.

Δύο ακόμη:

Η μετάλλαξη του objtest έγραφε κατευθείαν στο dome_fig — κρυφή μνήμη, όχι
κατάσταση παιχνιδιού. Τώρα μετακινεί πράκτορα, που είναι αυτό που συμβαίνει
στ' αλήθεια.

Η αποικία εκκίνησης του §10.1 είχε ΑΠΟΘΗΚΗ και όχι κυλικείο. Το πέρασμα
αναγκών ψάχνει μόνο ιατρείο, κυλικείο και καταλύματα: κανείς δεν έπινε και δεν
έτρωγε ποτέ, και τα «δύο sols χωρίς να κάνεις τίποτα» δεν υπήρχαν. Το δωμάτιο
«αποθήκη» δεν το διαβάζει κανένα πέρασμα, οπότε ήταν το φθηνότερο να θυσιαστεί.

events.title: c64: a DMA byte costs what it costs on the board
events.message:
c64: a DMA byte costs what it costs on the board

The C64 memory window is a DMA master on the C64's bus: a byte steals a bus cycle and the RISC-V waits for the
handshake around it. The emulator charged nothing for that, only the firmware's own instructions, so a firmware
that polls over DMA ran through far more accesses per emulated second than the device ever could.

Measured on a real C64 Ultimate (firmware 3.15) over GET /v1/machine:readmem, which stops the machine and
memcpy's from the aperture (c64_subsys.cc:579). Between 256 and 32768 bytes the request time grows by 3.26 us
per byte, about three C64 cycles. The same measurement here read 1.61 us, all of it firmware instructions.

So `IoCtx` gains a `stall`, the wait state a device charges for an access; the bus collects it per instruction and
emulated time carries it (`Bus::stall`, `machine.rs`). The C64 window charges `time::DMA_BYTE_CLOCKS`, the
remainder that puts the total on the device's figure. Measured again afterwards: 3.25 us per byte, 3.2 C64 cycles.
Every other device charges nothing and is unchanged; the field is `stall: 0` at the construction sites.

What it fixes: the upstream cart tool's chip erase never completed here. The tool polls the status 6 000 000 times,
which is 20 s on the device -- long past the chip's 8 s erase -- and was under 3 s in this emulator, so the flash
was still busy every time it looked. With the access priced, the tool's own run reports

    [cartlib] erase roml 76s s=FF/FF done

and goes on to program the cartridge. The flash model and the clock were right all along; the bus access was free.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012ZrJ7fdcGMeQu8svPU5Xan
events.author: Jondalar

events.title: log: --log cart, the cycle a cartridge is handed
events.message:
log: --log cart, the cycle a cartridge is handed

The flash families in the expansion port schedule an erase off the cycle they are given and finish it only when a
later access carries a cycle at or after the due one (Flash040::catch_up_erase, VICE's lazy alarm). Nothing else
in the emulator shows that cycle, so a cartridge that looks stuck mid-erase cannot be told apart from one whose
time is not moving.

It settled exactly such a case. The upstream cart tool's chip erase never completed here: it polls the status
6 000 000 times over what it counts as 120 seconds, and the status kept reading DQ6/DQ3. The trace showed the
erase armed correctly and the cycle advancing -- just far too slowly, 0.48 C64 cycles per DMA access. Measured
against a real C64 Ultimate on 3.15 over the same REST path, a DMA byte costs 3.26 us, about three cycles; the
emulator charges 1.58 on that path and 0.48 on the tool's. So the tool's 6 000 000 polls are 20 s on the device,
where the chip's 8 s erase is long done, and under 3 s here, where it is not. The cartridge model and the clock
are both right; the bus access is too cheap. That is recorded, not fixed, by this commit.

Βήμα 13γ: η αλυσίδα κλείνει — τοποθέτησε, χτίστηκε, φάνηκε

Ο παίκτης βάζει ηλιακό με 30 μέταλλο και έξι δευτερόλεπτα αργότερα το HUD λέει
ALL SYSTEMS OK, χωρίς να έχει πατήσει τίποτα ενδιάμεσα. Τρία πράγματα έλειπαν:

1. Η ΕΡΓΑΣΙΑ BUILD ΔΕΝ ΕΧΤΙΖΕ ΤΙΠΟΤΑ. Το jb_arrive την έστελνε στο ja_operate.
   Τώρα η πρόοδος είναι η ΑΚΕΡΑΙΟΤΗΤΑ — η εγγραφή έχει ήδη ένα byte και το
   bd_commit το γράφει μηδέν — και στο 255 η κατάσταση γίνεται DS_ACTIVE.
   Μισοχτισμένο και μισοκατεστραμμένο είναι η ίδια κατάσταση, που είναι σωστό.

2. ΕΝΑ ΝΕΟ ΕΡΓΟΤΑΞΙΟ ΔΕΝ ΕΙΧΕ ΑΚΜΗ. Η δρομολόγηση το έβρισκε απρόσιτο, κανείς
   δεν ξεκινούσε ποτέ, και το κτίριο έμενε DS_BUILDING για πάντα. Το bd_link
   το δένει με τον κοντινότερο ζωντανό θόλο — «ακμή εξωτερικού χώρου» του §6.2,
   μια ακμή χωρίς διάδρομο να τη ζωγραφίσει.

3. ΤΟ HUD ΔΕΝ ΑΚΟΛΟΥΘΟΥΣΕ ΤΗΝ ΠΡΟΣΟΜΟΙΩΣΗ. Ξαναγραφόταν μόνο σε ενέργεια του
   παίκτη: το νερό έπεφτε 60 -> 0 με τη μπάρα ακίνητη. Τώρα μία φορά ανά
   περιστροφή τροχού. ΧΩΡΙΣ να πειράζει το φάντασμα — το πρώτο γράψιμο έσβηνε
   τον κέρσορα για τρία frames κάθε 320 ms και φαινόταν σαν τρεμόπαιγμα· το
   HUD ζει στις γραμμές 160-199 και δεν πατά το κάδρο.

Η ολοκλήρωση ξαναζωγραφίζει ΟΛΟ το κάδρο: 41 frames, 0,8 s, μία φορά ανά
κτίριο. Το §6.9 ζητά αποκάλυψη σε οκτώ κομμάτια και δεν γράφτηκε — αλλά η
λίστα βρώμικων ΔΕΝ είναι φθηνότερη εδώ, γιατί ένα tile κάτω από θόλο κοστίζει
99.840 us και ο μικρός θόλος έχει δεκαέξι.

Το tests/test_game.py τρέχει τον βρόχο και ελέγχει ολόκληρη την αλυσίδα.
Το DESIGN πήρε νέα §7.4 για τη σύμβαση σελιδοποίησης, ξαναγραμμένα §4.2, §6.9,
§10.1, και τρεις νέους κινδύνους — ανάμεσά τους ότι η βάση εξαφανίζεται πάνω
στο ίδιο της το θεμέλιο, γιατί το γκρι του σκυροδέματος είναι το γκρι του
δακτυλίου. Αυτό το βρήκε το κοίταγμα, όχι έλεγχος.

events.title: 68030 MMU: MOVES must use the _state accessors in the CE table too
events.message:
68030 MMU: MOVES must use the _state accessors in the CE table too

Table 35 (68030 MMU + caches + cycle-exact) never set xfc_postfix, so its
MOVES stores went through the plain dfc030c_put_* helpers instead of the
_state variants that record the data output buffer for the bus-fault
frame. A MOVES that page-faulted was then completed on RTE with the
PREVIOUS instruction's write data. Tables 32 and 34 already set it.

Seen with Atari System V (UniSoft SVR4) under Hatari: copyout() of the
first user page faulted, the retry stored the previous store's value over
the icode's `moveq #59`, and init's exec became a different syscall.

events.message:
68030 data cache: burst fill translates with the access's function code

dcache030_maybe_burst() translated the line address with regs.s, the
CPU's privilege level, rather than the function code of the access that
missed. A MOVES with SFC=user runs in supervisor mode: the supervisor
translation can match a transparent translation register, come back
untranslated, and the burst then fills a user-tagged line from PHYSICAL
memory at the logical address. Only visible when RAM exists there.

Seen with Atari System V under Hatari with 256 MB of TT-RAM: user data
at logical 0x1003xxxx read back as zeros through copyin() and every
dynamically linked program crashed in the runtime linker; 240 MB (no RAM
at that physical address) was fine.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Βήμα 13β: 96 κόμβοι αντί για 128, και 3.900 bytes κώδικα από το πουθενά
events.message:
Βήμα 13β: 96 κόμβοι αντί για 128, και 3.900 bytes κώδικα από το πουθενά

Η τράπεζα 0 είχε 61 ελεύθερα bytes και έμεναν ~3.000 να γραφτούν. Η απόφαση
(επιλογή του χρήστη ανάμεσα σε τέσσερις):

Οι δύο πίνακες δρομολόγησης είναι ΚΟΜΒΟΙ x 128 bytes. Με 96 κόμβους αντί για
128 πιάνουν 12 KB αντί για 16, και τα 4 KB που περισσεύουν στην τράπεζα 1
πήραν τα εικονίδια δωματίων m και l (3.936 bytes) — που με τη σειρά τους
ελευθέρωσαν ισόποσο χώρο ΚΩΔΙΚΑ στην τράπεζα 2. Ο κόμβος ενός θόλου είναι το
id του, μιας δομής MAX_DOME + id: 64 + 32 = 96, άρα οι δομές έπεσαν από 64 σε
32. Ο πίνακάς τους στην τράπεζα 6 μίκρυνε 256 bytes ως αγκαλιά.

Η τράπεζα 1 είναι η ΠΡΟΕΠΙΛΟΓΗ του παραθύρου, οπότε τα εικονίδια δεν κοστίζουν
σελιδοποίηση σε κανέναν εκτός από το πέρασμα αντικειμένων — που έχει την 6
μέσα και κάνει τώρα ένα out παραπάνω ανά θόλο.

Η εικόνα της τράπεζας 2 κόβεται πια στο χρησιμοποιημένο μέρος (11.264 αντί για
16.384): ένα incbin 16 KB θα έσβηνε τον κώδικα που μπήκε από πάνω. Εκεί
κάθονται το build.asm, το route.asm και το newgame.asm, μαζί με το ημερολόγιο
του φαντάσματος (ξαναέγινε 1.600) και τον πίνακα φιγούρων.

    τράπεζα 0   13.217 / 16.128   ελεύθερα 2.911
    τράπεζα 2   11.264 δεδομένα + 2.112 buffers + 2.850 κώδικας, ελεύθερα 158
    τράπεζα 1    3.936 / 4.096 πάνω από το DIST
    τράπεζα 6   15.840 / 16.384
    τράπεζα 7   15.944 / 16.384 (το G_text, 1.024, μένει ανέγγιχτο εφεδρεία)

events.title: Βήμα 13α: τα δύο μισά σε ένα binary — και τέσσερα που έσπασαν αμέσως
events.message:
Βήμα 13α: τα δύο μισά σε ένα binary — και τέσσερα που έσπασαν αμέσως

Ως τώρα το uitest.asm έδενε τον renderer με το build mode και το simtest.asm
την οικονομία με τον τροχό. Κανένα δεν έδενε και τα δύο, άρα καμία κλήση από
το ένα μισό στο άλλο δεν είχε ποτέ μεταγλωττιστεί. Το src/main.asm το κάνει.

Τέσσερα έσπασαν μόλις μπήκαν μαζί:

1. ΔΙΠΛΟΙ ΟΡΙΣΜΟΙ. Τα AG_* ορίζονταν και στο entity.asm και στο object.asm,
   τα R_* σε τρία αρχεία με διαφορετικά υποσύνολα. Μπήκαν στο const.asm, που
   γι' αυτό υπάρχει. Και μια σύγκρουση ετικέτας: gm_lp στο ghost και στο
   worldgen.

2. ΑΣΥΜΒΑΤΗ ΣΕΛΙΔΟΠΟΙΗΣΗ, και αυτό ήταν το αληθινό εύρημα. Ολη η προσομοίωση
   διαβάζει θόλους, δομές και πράκτορες κατευθείαν από το &4000 χωρίς να
   σελιδοποιεί — το simtest έβαζε την τράπεζα 6 μία φορά πριν τρέξει. Ο
   renderer αλλάζει τράπεζα δεκάδες φορές ανά frame και αφήνει πάντα την 1.
   Μαζί, η οικονομία μετρούσε τους πράκτορες μέσα στον πίνακα αποστάσεων: ο
   πληθυσμός έπεφτε στο μηδέν σε δέκα δευτερόλεπτα. Ο τροχός κρατά τώρα τη
   σύμβαση — μία σελιδοποίηση στην είσοδο, μία στην έξοδο.

3. ΤΟ rt_begin ΔΕΝ ΧΤΙΖΕΙ ΤΙΠΟΤΑ. Μηδενίζει τον μετρητή πηγών· αυτό που κάνει
   τον τροχό να τρέξει την ανοικοδόμηση είναι μια σημαία που το build mode δεν
   ήξερε καν ότι υπάρχει. Το «ο γράφος άλλαξε» μετακόμισε στο graph.asm ως
   rt_mark, γιατί το build mode δεν συνδέει τον τροχό.

4. Δεν υπήρχε ρουτίνα «νέο παιχνίδι». Το newgame.asm γράφει την κατάσταση του
   §10.1: τρεις μικροί θόλοι σε Γ, δύο διάδρομοι, πλατφόρμα, τέσσερις άποικοι,
   60 νερό / 40 τροφή / 30 μέταλλο / 10 βιοπλαστικό / 4 ανταλλακτικά — και τον
   πίνακα εργασιών στο 255, που είναι το άδειο.

Η αποικία ζει και διψά: το νερό πέφτει 60 -> 0 σε ~4.000 frames χωρίς ρεύμα,
που είναι ακριβώς ό,τι λέει το §10.1 ότι πρέπει να συμβεί.

events.title: Amiga: hold the blitter only while the clear runs
events.message:
Amiga: hold the blitter only while the clear runs

AMIGA_ENTRY took the blitter before the game started and kept it to the end.
Booting a fastdraw build from its ADF then hung with an empty screen on a
512 KB A500 under Kickstart 1.3. Holding it is what does it, not the call:
taking it and handing it straight back boots, and so does adding the WaitBlit
the documented sequence asks for while still holding it.

BEGIN_CLEAR takes it, waits for the system's last blit and WAIT_CLEAR hands it
back as the fill ends, so it spans the drawing and never a disk read. DISK.M68
reads a saved commander mid-game, which ownership held that long would hang
the same way.

events.title: board: --board c64u, the Bling Board's presence bit
events.message:
board: --board c64u, the Bling Board's presence bit

U2PIO_BOARDREV does not tell a C64U from an Ultimate 64-II Elite: 0x16 and 0x17 are one piece of hardware that
Commodore's branch labels one way and Gideon's the other, and a C64U running 3.15 writes "ULTIMATE 64-II" in its
own title bar. What differs is the Bling Board, the LED and keyboard controller the C64U carries, and a firmware
that wants to know asks BLINGBOARD_INSTALLED -- BLING_RX_FLAGS & 0x04 (u64.h:35-43) -- not the revision.

So `--board c64u` sets that one bit and nothing else; the revision stays 0x17 either way. The Bling Board's data,
get and irqen registers stay unmodelled, because 3.15 never reads them: its only consumer is
LedStrip::setup_config_menu (led_strip.cc:497), which picks a heading. Measured with --log io, once per boot:

    io R 0x10100802 0x04 blingboard+0x2 @0x000a37b4 LedStrip::setup_config_menu()+0x2c

The switch earns its keep against a firmware built from Commodore's branch, where the same bit decides
isCommodoreBoard(). That is what the 1541Ultimate session needs to exercise both labels against one emulator.
